articles.title: Synaptics Announces Astra SR200 Multimodal Edge AI Processors with Google Coral NPU
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 21st 2026
Synaptics Announces Astra SR200 Multimodal Edge AI Processors with Google Coral NPU
Synaptics Incorporated (Nasdaq: SYNA) today introduced the xMCU, a new class of microcontrollers that runs multimodal Edge AI, with the launch of the Synaptics Astra SR200 Series. Unlike conventional MCUs constrained by limited on-chip memory and compute, the xMCU combines heterogeneous, AI-native compute and acceleration with integrated high-bandwidth custom DRAM scalable to hundreds of megabytes, enabling larger AI models and richer multimodal workloads to run entirely on-device. The Astra SR200 Series of xMCUs is designed for the next generation of AI wearables, battery-powered sensing devices, connected cameras, streamers, and industrial vision and voice systems.
The SR200 Series is powered by the Synaptics Torq AI engine, which brings a standards-based hardware architecture and unified developer experience featuring the Coral NPU from Google Research. It also comes with the industry's first pairing of the Arm Cortex -M85 and Cortex -M52. Together with integrated vision and audio capabilities and hardware-rooted security, the SR200 Series brings unmatched system design efficiency and cost benefits to Edge and Physical AI designs.Setting a new standard for the industry, the Astra SR200 Series is engineered around the following core vectors: high-performance compute with extensible memory; transformer-ready AI acceleration; silicon-rooted security; multimodal integration; ultra-low-power architecture with tiered domains; and an open-source software ecosystem, offering developer choice and OEM design flexibility. 
The Synaptics Astra SR200 Series launches with three pin-compatible product lines, giving OEMs and developers a common hardware foundation and a shared SDK. The SR210 is designed to deliver 200 GOPS for power-optimized, always-on voice and sensing; the SR230 adds vision, display, and optional audio at 300 GOPS for mainstream multimodal devices; and the SR250 enables 400 GOPS with dual vision and display paths for premium, demanding edge applications. Developers can scale performance while preserving their software investment and system architecture.
In the SR200 Series of xMCUs, memory is the foundation, not an afterthought. A tiered architecture pairs up to 8 MB of SRAM with extensible, high-bandwidth, high-capacity custom DRAM that scales to hundreds of megabytes as AI models and workloads grow. Built around latency, retention, and power demands of Edge AI, this architecture runs workloads at one-third the power of typical system DRAM, eliminating the need for costly external memory in most applications at a fraction of the system power. 
At the heart of the family is the Synaptics Torq AI engine integrating the Coral NPU, optimized for low latency and high-efficiency execution of deep learning workloads, including CNN, transformer, and fully connected networks. Its open-source MLIR/IREE compiler supports industry-standard frameworks and model formats in place of proprietary vendor toolchains, extending Coral's Edge AI heritage into ultra-low-power, always-on IoT. 
A high-performance core, scaling to 800 MHz, tackles control, multimedia, and burst-compute workloads, while an efficiency core handles always-on sensor fusion, connectivity, and low-power inference. An optional Cadence Tensilica HiFi 5 DSP adds dedicated audio and acoustic ML processing, while an always-on domain manages voice activity detection, timekeeping, and wake-up. 
The SR200 Series integrates a multi-layered security engine that combines hardware isolation, cryptographic acceleration, anti-tamper detection, device lifecycle management, and secure boot. The implementation conforms to PSA Level 3 and CC EAL4+ certification targets, providing protection against software and physical attacks. 
The platform provides a broad peripheral and connectivity set, including high-speed octal SPI, SDIO and eMMC storage interfaces, UART, SPI, I2C, I3C, PWM, USB 2.0 and extensive low-power GPIO. Industrial variants add 1 Gb Ethernet with IEEE 1588 TSN support and two CAN-FD interfaces, supporting deterministic networking and real-time industrial control for Physical AI and Robotics applications. 
Supporting Zephyr RTOS and the open-source Torq NPU compiler, the SR200 Series brings groundbreaking performance and power efficiency to define a new category of MCU experiences for Edge and Physical AI.
Vikram Gupta, SVP and GM, Edge Compute & Connectivity Division, Synaptics"The next wave of AI will be defined by devices that understand their environment and act locally, while meeting tight power, cost, and form-factor requirements. With the Astra SR200 Series, we're introducing a new class, the xMCU, that brings applications-processor capability into the MCU domain, running multimodal AI workloads that traditionally require Linux and discrete DRAM. It gives customers a scalable foundation for everything from intelligent sensing to advanced Edge and Physical AI systems."
Yossi Matias, Vice President and Head of Google Research"Open technologies and strong partnerships are key to making Edge AI more accessible. Our ongoing work with Synaptics combines the Coral platform with Astra's scalable hardware and developer ecosystem to power next-generation, wearable-class devices. We share a vision of turning advanced research into reality through real-world products, empowering developers to create faster, more useful, and responsive experiences."

articles.title: PHP2Shell: Two Unpatched Critical PHP RCE Flaws (CVSS 9.2) Trigger Emergency Security Alert
articles.text:
This story is developing and was written before PHP's scheduled 14:00 UTC release on October 21. Once the release is out, the affected and fixed versions below are confirmed by the official advisory.
PHP will ship an out-of-cycle security release at 14:00 UTC today, October 21, for two critical vulnerabilities that its security team has rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale but has not described.
Security researchers at watchTowr say the two flaws allow remote code execution. Only the four supported PHP branches, 8.2 through 8.5, can receive the fix, and no exploitation has been reported so far.
The advance notice followed a leak. On October 20, a post on HN said two PHP remote code execution flaws, rated CVSS 10.0 and affecting versions from PHP 5 onward, would be disclosed on Thursday, October 22. The poster said they had "no evidence beyond 'source: trust me, bro'".
watchTowr then posted on X that the leaked information was real, that the two flaws were under embargo, that everyone had been supposed to wait until Thursday, and that it could not share more for now.
PHP published its notice that evening, at 19:33 UTC, with the release set for Wednesday, a day before the date watchTowr gave. The notice says PHP may release earlier "should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild."
The leak carried the flaws' existence, a score, a date, and two CVE identifiers, not how the flaws work. The CVSS 10.0 figure is the leak's. PHP's rating is 9.2 on version 4.0 of the scale.
The identifiers researchers are using, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, were also listed in the leaked post. PHP's notice names neither. The claim that every version since PHP 5 is affected is unconfirmed too: watchTowr's own FAQ on the flaws says that scope "has not been confirmed by an official vendor advisory" and that no configuration or feature requirement has been described.
PHP says "Full details, affected versions, and the fixed versions will be published with the release." Researchers have started calling the pair php2shell. The name is theirs, not PHP's.
Whatever the affected range turns out to be, PHP issues fixes only for its four supported branches, and records each branch's changes in its changelog. Versions 8.2 and 8.3 receive only security fixes, and 8.4 and 8.5 are in active support. Ahead of the release, several trackers, including Alpine Linux's and security researcher Kevin Beaumont, expect the fixes to ship as PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, the next point release of each branch, though PHP has not confirmed the numbers.
PHP2Shell: How to Reduce Your Risk Before the 14:00 UTC PHP Patch
Anything older, including 8.1, 8.0, 7.x, and 5.x, is end of life and gets no PHP fix. If the flaws reach those branches, installations on them will have no vendor patch.
| PHP branches that can receive today's fix |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Branch | Current release (September 24) | PHP support status | 
|---|---|---|
| 8.5 | 8.5.11 | Active support until December 31, 2027 | 
| 8.4 | 8.4.26 | Active support until December 31, 2026 | 
| 8.3 | 8.3.35 | Security fixes only until December 31, 2027 | 
| 8.2 | 8.2.34 | Security fixes only until December 31, 2026 | 
Security company Mallory counted about 884,000 internet-facing hosts whose HTTP banner reported a PHP version of 8.1 or older to the Shodan search engine on October 20, 59% of the roughly 1.5 million hosts that reported any version. The count covers banners, not confirmed affected systems, and a further 740,000 hosts reported PHP without a version.
PHP has published no workaround. Until the release lands, the preparation comes down to six steps, most of them drawn from a rapid-response post from Huntress, with CERT-EU's isolation advice added.
- Inventory every PHP install, including PHP bundled in vendor appliances, Windows software, and control panels such as cPanel and Plesk.
- Be ready to upgrade at 14:00 UTC. Patch internet-facing systems first, and check your Linux distribution and hosting provider for backported packages.
- On an end-of-life branch, upgrade, take the system off the internet, or put it behind a VPN or a web application firewall until you can.
- Where patching cannot be done at once, CERT-EU advises that you "consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available."
- Watch what PHP starts. Alert on php-fpm, php-cgi, httpd, or apache2 launching shells, interpreters, or download tools. On Linux servers without endpoint detection, Florian Roth's process-watcher logs every program a PHP process starts, with its command line. It sees a program only after it has started and, in Roth's words, "prevents nothing."
- If you find something, isolate the server, preserve the web server and PHP logs, and look for web shells, new files in the web root, new cron jobs, scheduled tasks, and accounts.
Huntress said it had not seen exploitation of the flaws in its partner environments as of October 20, had not built or reproduced a proof of concept, and was not aware of public exploit code. watchTowr's FAQ lists exploitation as none reported as of October 21 and the flaws as not in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
For comparison, when CVE-2024-4577, a PHP flaw in CGI mode on Windows, became public in June 2024, Akamai saw exploit attempts against its honeypot servers within 24 hours.
The release should clarify what the notice withheld: which versions are affected, which part of PHP is involved, whether an attack requires a particular way of running PHP, a configuration, or a login, and how PHP itself describes the flaws. At the time of writing, PHP had not released the fixes.

articles.title: Xbox ressuscite les dashboards Xbox 360 sur navigateur : vers une émulation à plus grande échelle ?
articles.text:
Créée le 13 octobre dernier, la division Xbox Labs commence déjà à faire parler d’elle. Sur X, Asha Sharma, patronne du gaming chez Microsoft, a relayé l’une des premières expérimentations de cette nouvelle entité : une démonstration du tableau de bord « Blades » de la Xbox 360… fonctionnant dans un navigateur web.
Lancer des jeux directement dans un navigateur web n’a rien de nouveau. Ces dernières années, les moddeurs s’en sont même donné à cœur joie en portant sur navigateur des titres iconiques comme DOOM, Quake III Arena, Diablo, Half-Life ou encore le premier Tomb Raider, via OpenLara, en utilisant des technologies telles que WebAssembly et WebGL, souligne VideoCardz. Encore plus récemment, un développeur a même réussi l’exploit de lancer GTA V sur un navigateur web.
C’est dans ce contexte que la (nouvellement créée) division Xbox Labs fait parler d’elle cette semaine avec la publication sur X d’une vidéo de démonstration faisant état de leurs travaux actuels, sur navigateur justement.
L’équipe Xbox Labs… Expérimente
On y voit une fenêtre Edge (lancée sur macOS plutôt que sur un PC Windows, ce qui mérite d’être mentionné) sur laquelle est lancé un programme permettant à l’utilisateur d’essayer les anciennes interfaces Xbox 360 : « Blades » et ses onglets verticaux, lancée en 2005 ; « New Xbox Experience » avec ses tuiles vertes pomme et son avatar apparent, utilisée à partir de 2008 ; et « Metro », déployée en 2011 avec un look approchant l’interface Modern UI de Windows 8.
Cette démonstration, qui n’est pas (encore ?) accessible au public, fonctionne directement via un navigateur web et fleure bon la nostalgie. Relayée par Asha Sharma, cette dernière toutefois pourrait augurer d’un projet d’émulation plus ambitieux.
Des observateurs attentifs, comme Kirby0Louise, sur X, ont en effet remarqué que la barre d’adresse du navigateur affiche « localhost:5173/play/FFFE07D1?dash=blades ». Une adresse qui comprend donc la mention « FFFE07D1 ». Or, cette dernière correspond à l’identifiant de titre (Title ID) attribué au tableau de bord de la Xbox 360. Le port 5173, quant à lui, est généralement associé au serveur de développement web Vite.
Vers une émulation officielle de la Xbox 360 sur navigateur ?
Cet indice pourrait (notez bien le conditionnel) suggérer que Microsoft exécute réellement le logiciel Xbox 360 via un émulateur (potentiellement avec son propre moteur Fission), dans ce navigateur… Plutôt que de se contenter de recréer de façon artificielle ces différents tableaux de bord.
Reste maintenant à savoir ce qui pourrait se cacher derrière ce projet, si Microsoft réfléchirait, pour une raison ou une autre, à émuler son ancienne Xbox 360 et éventuellement ses jeux dans les navigateurs. On sait que le moteur Fission est déjà employé à titre officiel pour l’émulation des jeux de la génération Xbox 360, donc le doute est permis. D’autant que Microsoft mise désormais sur une fonctionnalité Disc to Digital qui pourrait éventuellement être employée dans ce contexte.
Notons toutefois que la division Xbox Labs a été spécifiquement créée pour travailler sur les technologies logicielles expérimentales, sur la recompilation de jeux, les applications basées sur navigateur ou encore l’exécution de jeux existants sur du matériel pour lequel ils n’avaient pas été initialement conçus. L’aperçu partagé cette semaine s’inscrit donc pleinement dans ses missions… Sans que l’on sache à ce stade ce qu’il faut précisément en penser, ou en attendre.
Source : VideoCardz / X

articles.title: Google y Amazon lanzaron herramientas para que los programadores de IA dejen de depender de los chips de Nvidia
articles.text:
Google abrió el código de TorchTPU, la herramienta que permite llevar programas de inteligencia artificial escritos para los chips de Nvidia a sus propios procesadores sin reescribir una línea. El anuncio llegó un día después de que Amazon lanzara una herramienta similar y apunta al negocio que sostiene el dominio de la empresa tecnológica en la industria.
Las dos empresas atacan el mismo punto: PyTorch, el programa de código abierto con el que se construye la mayoría de los modelos de IA. Según datos que citó Amazon, el 85% de las aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial se escriben con PyTorch, que durante años trabajó mejor sobre las GPU, los chips gráficos que Nvidia diseñó para entrenar modelos.
Eso ocurrió porque Nvidia pasó años asegurándose de que su software, CUDA, encajara a la perfección con esa aplicación. El resultado, según describió TechCrunch, fue que sus chips quedaron integrados al estándar de la industria casi por defecto, aun cuando existen alternativas como las de AMD o Apple.
El software que ató a la industria a un solo fabricante
Amazon fue la primera en moverse. El lunes presentó TorchNeuron, una versión del programa adaptada a Trainium, su chip propio, que permite migrar una aplicación con un simple cambio de configuración. La empresa también anunció que enviará código al proyecto central de PyTorch para quitarle las partes que lo atan a un fabricante específico.
“Lo que de verdad importa es eliminar el bloqueo que le impedía a los desarrolladores tener una opción real”, dijo Colin Brace, vicepresidente de tecnología de software en Annapurna Labs, la unidad de Amazon que diseña sus chips. La compañía citó el caso de Deepgram, una firma de IA de voz que, tras migrar a Trainium, procesa 70% más audio por cada dólar que gasta.
Google responde con sus propios aliados
Un día después, Google presentó TorchTPU en la conferencia PyTorch 2026. La herramienta permite entrenar, servir y desplegar modelos sobre sus procesadores TPU (las unidades que la empresa diseña para IA) con las mismas herramientas que ya usan los programadores, entre ellas Hugging Face, vLLM y SGLang.
El proyecto se desarrolló junto con el equipo de PyTorch dentro de Meta, la empresa que creó el programa en 2016 antes de cederlo en 2022 a la fundación sin fines de lucro que lo administra. “No podemos quedar atados a una sola arquitectura de hardware”, afirmó Jana van Greunen, directora de ingeniería de PyTorch en Meta, según el comunicado de Google.
Hugging Face, la plataforma que aloja miles de modelos de IA de uso abierto, también se sumó al anuncio. Su vicepresidente de producto, Jeff Boudier, dijo que la colaboración busca que los programadores puedan elegir el hardware que mejor les convenga sin perder acceso a sus modelos favoritos.
Una pelea que recién empieza
Ninguna de las dos herramientas garantiza que los desarrolladores abandonen masivamente a Nvidia: cambiar de chip sigue implicando ajustes y pruebas, y la compañía conserva años de ventaja en rendimiento y en el ecosistema de software que construyó alrededor de sus procesadores.
Google dijo que ya puso a prueba TorchTPU entrenando modelos con hasta 8.000 procesadores de su serie Ironwood y que alcanzó una eficiencia de cómputo del 52% con la familia de modelos Qwen, una cifra que la empresa presenta como evidencia de que su alternativa ya funciona a gran escala.

articles.title: I asked ChatGPT to recreate 5 classic video games, including Snake, Pong and Tetris — then challenged it to make them even better
articles.text:
ChatGPT can now create games you can play right inside a conversation — I challenged it to recreate 5 classics, then gave them a crazy twist
Can ChatGPT really recreate my favorite retro arcade games?
OpenAI recently introduced GPT-6, a new model of ChatGPT. You've probably heard about a lot of its new features but one that I don't think has had nearly enough attention, especially considering how much fun you can have with it, is Intelligent UI.
It allows ChatGPT to generate interactive experiences directly within a conversation. OpenAI explains: “With Intelligent UI, responses can include graphics, tappable buttons, forms, charts, and interactive experiences you can use directly in your conversation.”
What's interesting is there isn’t a single format. Which means, depending on what you ask, ChatGPT might create an interactive diagram, a calculator, a mood board, a map or even a little gaming console.
There are some genuinely useful applications here, from making complicated subjects easier to understand to building simple tools on the spot. But I was particularly interested in something a little less practical — games.
ChatGPT can now create games you can actually play within the chat window. And while there are all sorts of possibilities for educational games, quizzes and entirely new creations, I wanted to see what would happen if I asked it to recreate some old favorites.
So I started with five classic games, including Snake, Pong and Tetris. I gave ChatGPT simple prompts to see how faithfully it could recreate them. I then asked it to reinvent each game with new aesthetics, unexpected gameplay mechanics and a few deliberately chaotic twists. Think Snake in a neon cyberpunk world and Tetris with rules that change every time you clear a line.
Here's what happened when I put ChatGPT's new game-making abilities to the test.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Snake gets a neon makeover
The prompt: "Create a playable version of the classic Snake game directly inside this conversation."
ChatGPT got the basics right straight away. The game was instantly recognizable, with responsive controls and even a slider to adjust the speed. It looked good and, importantly, it was actually fun to play for a couple of games.
I then asked it to give Snake a neon cyberpunk makeover, complete with moving obstacles, special power-ups and a speed increase every five points. Say hello to Neon Snake.
There was one small hiccup. Instead of creating the new game directly in the chat window, ChatGPT initially gave me the code. Which wasn't much use when the whole point was to play it there and then.
I tried another prompt asking it if it could make it directly playable in the conversation and that worked. The results of that experiment were fun. The neon aesthetic looked good, everything was color-coded and the new mechanics gave the classic (and, let’s be honest, sometimes boring) game an extra layer of challenge.
Tetris gets new rules
The prompt: "Create a playable game inspired by Tetris directly inside this conversation."
This one worked really well from the start. I’d just assumed it would be a bit buggy and glitchy because there’s so much going on compared to Snake, but the controls were intuitive and responsive, and the classic block-stacking mechanic was all there.
But what if Tetris changed the rules every time you cleared a line? That was the idea behind my follow-up prompt.
I asked ChatGPT to introduce unexpected twists, which could include rotating the board to adding unusual block shapes or special powers that could destroy part of the grid.
And it delivered. The changing rules introduced a fun element of unpredictability to a game that's usually all about getting into a rhythm. I also came away thinking about how much further you could take this. There are so many opportunities to experiment with different rules, challenges and power-ups.
Space Invaders becomes a First Contact situation
The prompt: "Build me a fully playable retro arcade game inspired by Space Invaders"
Again, ChatGPT recreated the classic arcade experience surprisingly well. It looked and played like the original, with straightforward controls and all the fun of shooting at waves of approaching aliens.
But I wanted to see whether it could do something a bit more imaginative than adding extra enemies or making everything move faster. So I asked it to introduce a choice: what if I could defend Earth by fighting the aliens or negotiating with them?
I wanted waves of pixel-art enemies, but also decisions between rounds that could unlock weapons, stop an invasion or make the next attack more dangerous.
ChatGPT called its reinvention First Contact, which I loved. Up until this point it was calling most of the games "chaos" or "chaotic" so this felt more inventive.
It was a fun way to introduce a new dimension to a familiar game. But did it work well? I don't know, I couldn't ever make it past the first level. This experiment really suffered with my poor alien-fighting abilities.
Haunted Pac-Man
The prompt: "Create a fully interactive retro maze game inspired by Pac-Man that I can play directly inside this ChatGPT conversation."
This was easily my favorite of the five, but I have always adored Pac-Man. ChatGPT's first attempt was a fun, responsive maze game with the familiar mechanics of moving around, collecting things and trying to avoid enemies. Bonus points for the fact it renamed it Maze Muncher.
For the reinvention, I decided to lean into Halloween. I asked it to turn the game into a haunted 1980s arcade, with me playing a little ghost hunter instead of Pac-Man.
I also wanted the maze itself to change. Every ten orbs collected would trigger a surprise, like shifting walls, new passages or an extra ghost. And I asked for temporary power-ups that would let me chase the ghosts for a change.
ChatGPT handled this well but didn't wait until I'd collected orbs. It was super fast-paced and there were new ghosts, secret passages and changing mechanics from the start. It was quick, easy to control and genuinely fun to play.
Pong reinvented
The prompt: Build me a fully playable version of Pong inside this conversation.
Pong might be the simplest game of the bunch, but ChatGPT made a really solid version. The controls were easy, the aesthetics were nice and it even offered easy, normal and hard difficulty settings.
I decided to ruin that simplicity and asked ChatGPT to create a more chaotic version where every point triggered a random modifier. The ball could split in two, the paddles could shrink, gravity could change or an obstacle could appear in the middle of the court.
The result definitely delivered on the chaos. The familiar back-and-forth gameplay was still there, but the changing rules made each rally a little less predictable. It was also a reminder of how much fun you can have with a simple idea. You don't need to reinvent every part of a game to make it entertaining.
I was genuinely impressed with how well all five games worked, especially considering how simple my original prompts were.
Yes, there were a few hiccups along the way, like ChatGPT deciding to give me code instead of a playable game a couple of times. But overall, the controls were responsive, the games looked good and the reinventions were more imaginative than I expected.
What I enjoyed most was how easy it was to experiment. You could take a game you already know, change the aesthetic, introduce an unexpected mechanic or come up with something completely ridiculous and see what ChatGPT made of it.
I can imagine this being a fun way to waste half an hour, especially if you loved these games growing up. Although, after all this experimenting, I do feel like I should remind you that the originals are still out there, and they're well worth revisiting too.

Becca is a contributor to TechRadar, a freelance journalist and author. She’s been writing about consumer tech and popular science for more than ten years, covering all kinds of topics, including why robots have eyes and whether we’ll experience the overview effect one day. She’s particularly interested in VR/AR, wearables, digital health, space tech and chatting to experts and academics about the future. She’s contributed to TechRadar, T3, Wired, New Scientist, The Guardian, Inverse and many more. Her first book, Screen Time, came out in January 2021 with Bonnier Books. She loves science-fiction, brutalist architecture, and spending too much time floating through space in virtual reality.

articles.title: MNT-Halan completes IPO as retail tranche attracts over 41,500 subscription orders
articles.text: Egyptian fintech MNT-Halan has begun trading on the Egyptian Exchange (EGX) under the ticker HALN.CA, following an initial public offering (IPO) that saw strong demand from institutional and retail investors. The IPO involved the sale of 320 million existing ordinary shares, representing 20% of MNT-Halan's issued share capital, by existing shareholder MNT Investments B.V. The offering comprised 272 million shares allocated to institutional and other private-tranche investors and 48 millshares allocated tos to retail investors. The private tranche was 11.2 times oversubscribed, rising to 19.4 times excluding cornerstone investors, while the public tranche was 43.6 times oversubscribed, attracting more than 41,500 subscription orders. Founded in 2018 by Mounir Nakhla, with roots dating back to 2009, MNT-Halan provides lending, payments, investment and e-commerce services through subsidiaries including Halan and Tasaheel. The group has served approximately 7.9 million customers and disbursed more than EGP 178 billion in financing since inception, as of June 30, 2026. The listing marks MNT-Halan's transition into a publicly traded company as it seeks to expand its financial services ecosystem, strengthen customer engagement and reach more customers through its technology platform. Press release: MNT Tech Holding for Financial Investments SAE (the “Company” or “MNT-Halan”) celebrated today the commencement of trading in its shares on the Egyptian Exchange (EGX), under the ticker symbol HALN.CA, following strong investor demand for its initial public offering (IPO). The milestone was marked by a bell-ringing ceremony attended by senior government officials, financial regulators, EGX leadership, MNT-Halan’s board members, executives and representatives of the banks, asset managers and advisors involved in the offering. The listing represents a significant milestone in MNT-Halan’s growth journey, opening a new chapter for the Company as a publicly traded business. Founded in 2018, with roots dating back to 2009, MNT-Halan has grown into a diversified financial services platform offering solutions across lending, payments, investments and e-commerce. Through the Company’s subsidiaries encompassing Halan and Tasaheel, amongst other subsidiaries (together the “Group”), the Group has served approximately 7.9 million customers since inception, with approximately 1.9 million active customers annually, and disbursed more than EGP 178 billion in financing as of 30 June 2026. Its technology-driven ecosystem and extensive distribution network enable it to meet a broad range of financial needs and expand access to financial services across Egypt. The IPO attracted strong demand from both institutional and retail investors. The Private Tranche was 11.2 times oversubscribed and 19.4 times excluding cornerstone investors, while the Public Tranche was 43.6 times oversubscribed, attracting more than 41,500 subscription orders. The offering comprised the sale of 320 million existing ordinary shares by MNT Investments B.V., representing 20% of MNT-Halan’s issued share capital prior to the closing of the subscription process. Of these, 272 million shares were allocated to the Private Tranche and 48 million to the Public Tranche. Omar Radwan, Chairman of the Egyptian Exchange (EGX), said, "MNT-Halan has demonstrated an inspiring model of how ambitious ideas and ventures can evolve into leading institutional entities capable of leveraging technology and innovation to serve millions of citizens. Today, through its entry into the capital market, the company reaffirms that the stock exchange offers the most efficient and equitable avenue for providing liquidity and financing future expansion through a diverse range of instruments, while strengthening its brand positioning and enhancing its corporate governance.” Radwan added that listing and offering shares on the capital market for major companies and institutions goes beyond merely raising capital and diversifying funding sources at the lowest possible cost. Rather, it serves primarily as a vital safeguard for ensuring their long-term sustainability and continuity across generations by institutionalising sound corporate governance practices, promoting transparency, and safeguarding shareholders’ wealth. Mounir Nakhla, Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of MNT-Halan, said, "We are proud to begin trading on the Egyptian Exchange, marking an important milestone in our journey. The strong demand for our IPO reflects investors’ confidence in Egypt, the financial ecosystem we have built, and our growth trajectory. As we enter this next phase, we remain focused on broadening our product ecosystem, deepening customer engagement and leveraging our proprietary technology to reach more customers and drive sustainable growth. We thank the Egyptian government, the CBE, the FRA, the EGX, our banking partners, asset managers and everyone who contributed to bringing this offering to fruition. We are also grateful to every international investor, family office, and individual who are helping us create a lasting, positive impact in Egypt.” Citigroup Global Markets Limited and EFG Hermes Promoting and Underwriting S.A.E. acted as Joint Global Coordinators and Joint Bookrunners for the Offering. Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP acted as U.S. and English legal counsel, and Matouk Bassiouny & Hennawy acted as Egyptian legal counsel, in each case to MNT-Halan and the Selling Shareholder. White & Case LLP acted as U.S. and English legal counsel, and MHR & Partners in association with White & Case LLP, acted as Egyptian legal counsel in each case to the Joint Global Coordinators and Joint Bookrunners.

articles.title: Attackers Abuse UpdraftCentral Keys to Plant Backdoors on WordPress Sites
articles.text:
Unknown threat actors breached TeamUpdraft's website and potentially gained unauthorized access to customers' connection keys for UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault, and UpdraftClone, using them to backdoor WordPress sites.
TeamUpdraft is the developer behind UpdraftPlus, a popular WordPress backup plugin with over four million active installations. The vendor also offers UpdraftCentral, a remote management service that's used for managing multiple sites remotely. A client component of UpdraftCentral is shipped within every copy of UpdraftPlus.
"Over the weekend of 17-18 October we identified unauthorized access to the teamupdraft.com website," TeamUpdraft said in a statement. "Our team responded straight away and worked through the night to contain it – we closed the access route, signed out every account and replaced the keys and credentials that could have been affected."
As a result of the incident, threat actors are believed to have accessed its customer database, which holds the following information -
- Names, email addresses, billing addresses and order history
- Account passwords, stored only in hashed (scrambled) form and never in plain text
- Two-factor authentication (2FA) settings
- Connection keys for UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault and UpdraftClone
TeamUpdraft said the database does not hold any financial information, and that they are handled by Stripe and PayPal. It also emphasized that the UpdraftPlus plugin, along with self-hosted versions of UpdraftCentral and backups sent to customers' own remote storage, are not impacted.
"However, if your site was accessed through UpdraftCentral, please also re-authorise your remote storage and change any storage access keys, as a precaution," it said.
In addition, TeamUpdraft said it deployed a fix to address the underlying issue, signed out every teamupdraft.com account and reset login security across the site, and released UpdraftPlus 1.26.13 (free) and 2.26.13 (Premium) to automatically disconnect every UpdraftCentral connection made before 10 p.m. BST on October 18, 2026, to prevent the old keys from working.
Other steps taken by the developer are listed below -
- Disconnected every site from UpdraftVault and issued new credentials
- Replaced every UpdraftClone client key
- Rotated its keys with payment providers and other connected services
- Implemented additional monitoring in place
- Reported the incident to the U.K. Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) and other relevant authorities
Users who have a teamupdraft.com account are advised to change their password with immediate effect (and elsewhere, if the same password has been reused), reset 2FA settings, and exercise caution when receiving unexpected emails claiming to be from TeamUpdraft.
TeamUpdraft is also recommending that cloud customers of UpdraftCentral follow the steps below as soon as possible, since the connection keys can send commands to the connected sites -
- Log in to the site's own WordPress dashboard, not through UpdraftCentral.
- Update UpdraftPlus to version 1.26.12 (free) or 2.26.12 (Premium) or later.
- Disconnect it from UpdraftCentral: go to Settings > UpdraftPlus > Advanced Tools > UpdraftCentral and delete the connection key.
- Go to Users and check for any administrator accounts you don’t recognise. Remove them.
- Go to Plugins, including the Must-Use tab if you can see it, and check for anything you don’t recognise. Remove it.
- Change the passwords for all administrator accounts on the site.
- If you find anything suspicious, consider restoring the site from a backup taken before 17 October.
- Reconnect the site to UpdraftCentral.
UpdraftVault users are being urged to reconnect their sites to the backup service, and UpdraftClone users who have created a client key are required to copy the new keys from My Account > UpdraftClone > UpdraftClone Key Management and share them with their clients.
The development comes as WordPress security company Patchstack said it observed an attacker holding valid UpdraftCentral dashboard keys issuing commands to install backdoor plugins on connected WordPress sites. The campaign is said to have run continuously through an 18-hour window on October 18 and 19, 2026.
"The attacker sends a signed plugin.upload_plugin command over the plugin's remote procedure call channel, which listens on ordinary POST requests to the site root. WordPress installs and activates the supplied plugin through its standard installer," Patchstack security researcher Dave Jong said.
Slovakia-based penetration testing company Nethemba, which first detected the attack in the wild, has described the rogue plugin as a backdoor that hooks into every request to the site to check if the URL contains the parameter "?_9f5696=" and compares it with a 32-character token.
If a matching token is detected, it creates a user "data-ops43" with the display name "Site Tools," assigns it the Editor role, and grants the account "manage_options" and "install_plugins" permissions, allowing the operator to upload arbitrary PHP plugins and open site settings.
"Enabling registration and setting the default role to administrator is enough for the attacker to create a full administrator," Nethemba said. "On a standard WordPress site, an Editor also has unfiltered_html, so the account can put JavaScript into posts that runs in the browser of every administrator."
"The backdoor has a second layer as well. The account it creates, with a known password, stays in WordPress even after the plugin is removed, and the attacker can log in with it through the normal login form unless two-factor authentication is enabled for that account."
Although an early version of the plugin suffered from a coding error that causes impacted sites to fail with error 500, Nethemba said the threat actor deleted the broken backdoor by sending a "plugin.delete_plugin" command and then uploaded a working version that creates a full administrator account or logs in as an existing administrator.
WordPress site owners are advised to check for the following indicators of compromise -
- Plugin names: Site Health Cache or Site Health 364F, Asset Forge 2, Content Helper, Wp Forge, Query Shelf, Style Bridge 8F5, Media Kit 183, Query Shelf, Post Dock 776, Nav Hub, Speed Desk, Speed Kit 300, Link Latch, Script Shelf, or Feed Case
- Account names: system_team850, web.tech988, cmseditor170, cms.tech644 or web_mgr684, with an email at @example.com and a display name such as System Team, Web Tech, System Staff, System Ops, or Cms Tech
- IP addresses: 43.250.53.42 and 2a09:bac5:4e21:2e3c::49b:9
In all, Patchstack said it observed 99 distinct backdoor plugin names, with each sample carrying the line "Small maintenance toolkit: keeps option storage tidy."
Wordfence, which published its own analysis of the incident, said a WordPress site may be affected if the below criteria are satisfied -
- The site had UpdraftPlus Free or UpdraftPlus Premium installed and active while the affected UpdraftCentral connection key was present.
- The site has, or had during the incident, an active connection key for TeamUpdraft’s cloud-hosted UpdraftCentral service.
"This is the second incident in this channel in five months," Patchstack warned. "In June 2026 the vendor fixed CVE-2026-10795 (CVSS 8.1), where an obsolete unsigned message format let an attacker forge UpdraftCentral commands with no keys at all. That was fixed in 1.26.5 and 2.26.5, but exploitation attempts continue, so sites below those versions face both problems at once."
The development comes days after the website of the Rank Math PRO WordPress plugin was hit by a software supply chain attack, causing users who downloaded version 3.0.123 between October 15 at 8:02 p.m. UTC and October 16 at 7:12 a.m. UTC to receive compromised versions that planted hidden backdoors.
The incident has been assigned the CVE identifier CVE-2026-111862 (CVSS score: 9.8). The issue was fixed in Rank Math PRO version 3.0.124.
"The malware may establish persistent access, communicate with rank1cdn[.]com, recreate hidden backdoors on page visits, and expose WordPress credentials, database credentials, API keys, and other secrets accessible to the web server," Wordefence said.
The findings also coincide with an advisory from PHP, which said it intends to ship a security release that fixes two critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, CVSS scores: 9.2), as information about the flaws leaked ahead of their scheduled disclosure. The flaws have been codenamed PHP2Shell.
According to watchTowr CEO Benjamin Harris, the vulnerabilities affect PHP versions 5, 6, 7, and 8, and were originally due for release on October 22 at 11 a.m. ET.
"PHP is everywhere. It quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," Huntress said. "When a critical bug lands in PHP itself, rather than in one app built on top of it, the number of places you have to go looking to identify vulnerable PHP versions gets very big, very fast."

articles.title: Promo Apple : Amazon casse le prix du MacBook Pro 16 M5 Pro, sous les 3000€
articles.text:
Depuis sa sortie en mars, le MacBook Pro 16 pouces a pris 400 € sur la boutique d’Apple, qui demande désormais 3 399 € pour sa version d’entrée. Amazon ramène la déclinaison M5 Pro avec 24 Go de mémoire et 1 To de SSD à 2 999,99 €, pour une machine que nous avons notée 9/10, à condition de choisir sa mémoire avec soin : elle ne pourra plus évoluer.
Le MacBook Pro 16 M5 Pro est le plus grand portable d’Apple, pensé pour celles et ceux qui retouchent, montent ou développent. Notre test lui a attribué la note de 9/10, en saluant le rendement de sa puce et l’endurance de sa batterie. Amazon le propose à 2 999,99 € au lieu de 3 399 € dans sa version argent avec 24 Go de mémoire unifiée et 1 To de SSD, soit 399,01 € d’économie sur le prix pratiqué par Apple. Elle vise les créatifs qui veulent la grande dalle sans payer la version 48 Go, affichée 3 759 €.
Le MacBook Pro 16 M5 Pro en 24 Go et 1 To passe à 2 999,99 € au lieu de 3 399 € sur Amazon, vendu et expédié par Amazon.
Pourquoi choisir le MacBook Pro 16 M5 Pro ?
- Un écran Mini-LED de 16,2 pouces : sa dalle de 3456 x 2234 pixels grimpe à 120 Hz, dépasse 600 cd/m² en SDR et affiche des couleurs très justes selon nos mesures.
- Une puce M5 Pro qui ne faiblit pas : ses 18 cœurs CPU et 20 cœurs GPU ont encaissé nos sessions Lightroom et nos exports vidéo 4K sans baisse de régime.
- Une autonomie de grosse journée : la batterie de 100 Wh a tenu un peu plus de 20 heures en lecture vidéo pendant notre test. En bureautique, comptez plutôt 12 à 13 heures.
Une station de création qui se déplace, à condition de la porter
La puce M5 Pro brille là où ce MacBook Pro est attendu : retouche photo, montage vidéo lourd et modélisation 3D. Dans notre test du MacBook Pro 16 M5 Pro, mené sur une version 64 Go et 4 To, son GPU de 20 cœurs devançait la RTX 5070 du Galaxy Book 6 Ultra dans les logiciels de création, en se contentant de 60 W. La connectique évite les adaptateurs au quotidien, avec trois ports Thunderbolt 5, un HDMI, un lecteur SDXC et le MagSafe. Elle accepte jusqu’à trois écrans externes 6K, de quoi en faire un poste fixe au bureau.
Cette configuration parle aux photographes, monteurs et développeurs qui veulent la plus grande dalle de la gamme. Ses 24 Go de mémoire unifiée, le point d’entrée du modèle, sont soudés comme le SSD : si vous manipulez déjà de très gros projets, visez plus haut dès la commande. Les joueurs passeront leur chemin : nous peinions à tenir 30 images par seconde sur Cyberpunk 2077 en QHD+ Ultra. Et avec 2,14 kg, ce n’est pas un compagnon de voyage léger.
Face aux 16 pouces Windows, un choix de rendement plus que de polyvalence
Le MacBook Pro 16 a désormais des rivaux sérieux, comme l’ASUS ProArt P16 et son écran OLED, ou le Razer Blade 16, bien plus à l’aise en jeu avec sa RTX 5090. Face à eux, la machine d’Apple garde l’avantage du rendement : en monocœur, les puces Panther Lake et Strix Point de ses concurrents restaient loin derrière dans nos mesures. Elle n’offre en revanche ni OLED, ni évolutivité, ni adaptateur secteur dans la boîte. Si vous hésitez encore entre macOS et Windows, notre comparatif des meilleurs PC portables situe ce MacBook face aux références de 2026.
✅ Les points forts
- Puce M5 Pro très efficace, sans baisse de régime sous la charge
- Écran Mini-LED 120 Hz lumineux et bien calibré
- Un peu plus de 20 heures en lecture vidéo dans notre test
- Connectique complète : Thunderbolt 5, HDMI, SDXC et MagSafe
- Six haut-parleurs parmi les meilleurs du marché sur un portable
❌ Les limites
- Mémoire et SSD soudés : les 24 Go sont définitifs
- Adaptateur secteur vendu séparément
- Wi-Fi 7 limité aux canaux de 160 MHz
- 2,14 kg et performances en jeu modestes
Le MacBook Pro 16 M5 Pro 24 Go reste à 2 999,99 € sur Amazon au moment où nous écrivons ces lignes : vérifiez la mémoire choisie avant de valider, elle ne pourra plus évoluer.
À 2 999,99 €, le MacBook Pro 16 M5 Pro retrouve le tarif d’entrée que nous relevions à sa sortie, alors qu’Apple le facture 3 399 € aujourd’hui. Pour qui veut un grand écran fidèle et une machine qui tient la charge, c’est la porte d’entrée la plus raisonnable du modèle. Notre 9/10 récompense justement cet équilibre entre puissance, discrétion et endurance.
Reste la question de la mémoire, à trancher maintenant puisqu’elle ne bougera plus. Si vos projets saturent déjà 24 Go, la version 48 Go à 3 759 € sera plus durable, et si vous cherchez une machine à emporter partout, le format 14 pouces vous encombrera moins. Prévoyez enfin un chargeur, absent de la boîte.

articles.title: Ni el calendario está a salvo: así son las falsas invitaciones y reuniones para robar datos y dinero
articles.text:
Los ataques de phishing a través de invitaciones de calendario se multiplicaron por más de diez entre julio y agosto de 2026, según datos de la firma de seguridad Sublime citados por Business Insider. Una modalidad sencilla en la que un evento aparece sin aviso en la agenda, con apariencia de reunión legítima, y basta un clic para comprometer contraseñas, datos de pago o la computadora entera.
La razón del crecimiento es, sobre todo, psicológica. Muchos usuarios ya desconfían de un correo con enlaces sospechosos, pero pocos sospechan de una cita que aparece directamente en su calendario de trabajo.
Cómo funciona el engaño en el calendario digital
El mecanismo es simple. El atacante envía una invitación a una reunión falsa o incluye mensajes sobre llamadas perdidas, facturas impagas o suscripciones por renovar. El evento trae enlaces maliciosos incrustados, listos para activarse con un clic.
Según el reporte de Microsoft, las invitaciones de calendario se procesan de forma distinta a los adjuntos de correo tradicionales: un enlace dañino puede llegar directamente a la agenda del usuario sin que este tenga que abrir ningún archivo adjunto.
Ron Kerbs, director ejecutivo de Kidas, empresa que desarrolla herramientas para detectar estafas y deepfakes en llamadas de voz, explicó que las invitaciones fraudulentas suelen adoptar dos formas. En la primera, el evento contiene un enlace de reunión comprometido o un formulario diseñado para robar credenciales o instalar malware.
En la segunda, la víctima ingresa a una videollamada que parece legítima y se encuentra con un impostor que se hace pasar por alguien de confianza, muchas veces con el nombre real de un empleado pero una dirección de correo falsa.
Es importante entender por qué este tipo de ataque resulta tan eficaz: la invitación llega directamente al calendario sin pasar por el filtro mental de “correo sospechoso” y algunas aplicaciones la muestran de forma automática aunque el usuario nunca la haya aceptado, lo que le da una apariencia de autenticidad inmediata.
Kerbs agregó que los estafadores recurren a tecnología de inteligencia artificial generativa para sumar realismo al engaño. “Están usando tecnología deepfake para parecerse al mismo tipo de soporte técnico”, señaló, en referencia al uso de audio o video generado por IA que imita a un empleado real de una compañía.
Casos que muestran el alcance del engaño
Aman Gairola, cofundador de la agencia de diseño india Say Design, creyó haber conseguido un cliente en junio cuando alguien reservó una reunión a través del sitio web de su empresa. La invitación incluía un enlace a lo que parecía una carpeta de Google Drive con un resumen de proyecto.
Gairola hizo clic y llegó a una página que imitaba a Google Drive, pero algo no cuadraba. Revisó la dirección del sitio, confirmó que era falsa y evitó abrir cualquier archivo. “Si tengo que calificar qué tan convincente es, le pondría un 9,5 sobre 10”, dijo, y agregó que su empresa evalúa eliminar la opción de agendar llamadas directamente desde su web y reemplazarla por un formulario.
Otro riesgo surge incluso cuando el remitente es una persona real y conocida. La montañista y oradora Jenn Drummond sufrió el robo de su cuenta de correo mientras abordaba un vuelo, y desde esa cuenta se envió a decenas de sus contactos una invitación de calendario que advertía sobre una supuesta citación judicial, con un enlace a un aviso legal falso que solicitaba datos financieros.
“¿Qué van a pensar? Que no soy confiable, y tu marca se construye sobre la confianza”, relató Drummond.
Cómo protegerse del fraude
Los especialistas recomiendan aplicar a los eventos inesperados el mismo nivel de desconfianza que a un correo sospechoso. En la práctica, eso implica no abrir enlaces ni llamar a teléfonos incluidos en invitaciones de remitentes desconocidos, y revisar la configuración del calendario para desactivar que las invitaciones entrantes se agreguen de forma automática.
Mathew Woodyard, director de inteligencia de amenazas en la firma de gestión de identidad Okta, sostuvo que la responsabilidad principal recae en las empresas que operan los servicios, más que en la capacidad del usuario para detectar una invitación falsa.
También señaló que las passkeys pueden resolver buena parte del problema, porque se crean para una página específica y solo funcionan en el sitio web auténtico, nunca en una copia falsa.
Eso elimina la necesidad de que la persona tenga que juzgar por su cuenta si un enlace es confiable. “Hasta que los factores resistentes al phishing como las passkeys se conviertan en el estándar por defecto, los ataques de phishing van a seguir funcionando”, concluyó.

articles.title: theQA raises over $550,000 to scale AI-driven consumer research in Kuwait
articles.text: Kuwait-based AI-powered market research startup theQA has raised more than $550,000 in a Pre-Seed funding round, backed by a Kuwaiti family office and strategic angel investors. Founded in 2025 by Ahmad Al Ebrahim and Hussain Ali AlNashaba, theQA provides a digital consumer research platform that enables businesses, agencies and researchers to create AI-assisted surveys, reach targeted audiences and collect consumer insights to inform business decisions. Since launching in April 2025, the company has built a panel of more than 20,000 verified participants and recorded revenue growth in every quarter of 2026, with revenue nearly doubling since January. The funding will support the expansion of its operations in Kuwait, the development of AI-powered research tools and enhancements to its consumer insights and data analysis capabilities. Press release: theQA, Kuwait’s first AI-powered consumer research platform, has raised over US$550,000 in a pre-seed round backed by a Kuwaiti family office and strategic angel investors. The funding will support scaling the platform in Kuwait. theQA enables businesses, agencies, and researchers to create surveys, target relevant audiences in Kuwait, and collect consumer feedback to inform their decisions. Its AI-assisted survey builder and workflows help turn research briefs into questionnaires, supporting studies on consumer preferences, brand perceptions, and new product concepts. Launched in April 2025, theQA has grown to over 20,000 verified panel members. Revenue has grown every quarter this year, almost doubling since January. Commenting on the investment, Ahmad Al-Ebrahim, Co-Founder and CEO of theQA, said: “We started theQA with a simple goal: to make it easier for businesses to understand the people they serve. Consumer research has traditionally required significant time, effort, and resources, and we saw an opportunity to make that process simpler and more accessible. Reaching over 20,000 participants in a short period has reinforced our belief in the need for this platform. This investment will help us build on that progress, strengthen our capabilities, and make consumer insights more accessible to businesses across Kuwait.” Hussain Al-Nashabah, Co-Founder and CTO of theQA, added: “Our focus has always been on simplifying the research process, from asking the right questions to reaching the right people and understanding the results. We’re continuing to develop tools that reduce the time and effort required to conduct research, including the practical use of AI where it adds value. This investment will allow us to improve the platform, introduce new capabilities, and help businesses turn consumer feedback into actionable decisions.” Ahmad Al Ebrahim and Hussain Ali AlNashaba are co-founders of theQA.

articles.title: 'There's a good chance RTX 6060 comes out in 2029': leaker believes Nvidia's next-gen budget GPU is a long way off, and that it'll fall short of the PS6's gaming performance
articles.text:
Nvidia's RTX 6060 GPU could disappoint for gaming performance compared to the PS6 — and it may not arrive until 2029
Leaker paints a gloomy picture for the next-gen budget GPU
- Nvidia's RTX 6060 may not arrive until 2029 a leaker claims
- They note that when there are supply issues (the current RAM shortage), Nvidia tends to drag out the release of lower-end GPUs
- They also believe it's unlikely the RTX 6060 will match the PS6 for frame rates
Nvidia's budget GPU for its next-gen range may not be released for three years yet, if a new rumor about the RTX 6060 turns out to be correct.
Wccftech spotted a post from leaker Kepler on the NeoGAF forums, who chipped in with speculation on Nvidia's graphics cards in a thread about the cost of the PlayStation 6.
Kepler was responding to a comment observing that the PS6 is going to go up against the RTX 6060 when it launches in terms of comparisons to PC gaming, and the leaker said — add seasoning with this as ever — that the "6060 will launch much later (and based on recent trends I doubt it will match PS6)".
In a further post, the leaker added: "When there's a supply shortage Nvidia tends to really drag the release of lower end cards. There's a good chance RTX 6060 comes out in 2029."
This would mean we're looking at an early-to-mid 2028 launch for the RTX 6090, 6080 and 6070, which lines up with more recent rumors. Of course, that's not a foregone conclusion, and Kepler is clearly speculating here.
Recent reports from analysts indicate that the PS6 will likely launch in 2028, though some have argued that Sony's next-gen console could appear late in 2027 (alongside other devices, perhaps).
Analysis: late, as well as short on performance?
Of course, what Kepler contends here is what Nvidia is supposedly planning right now, and just as with the PS6, a lot of the direction that Team Green goes in with its next-gen GPUs will depend on the memory crisis. Graphics cards do, of course, use video RAM (VRAM), and the next generation of GeForce products will be expected to up the ante on that score. (Gamers are already unhappy with Nvidia's current-gen VRAM configurations).
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The problem is that there's no shortage of predictions that RAM cost inflation is going to get even worse in 2027, after it has already spiked in a big way through the middle of this year. The theorizing then runs that 2028 is also going to be a difficult year, which lends weight to the argument that the RTX 6060 will indeed be late to the GPU party.
In short, I wouldn't rule out the possibility of a 2029 arrival for the RTX 6060 as suggested, which obviously isn't great news for those hoping to score a more wallet-friendly next-gen Nvidia GPU.
It's also interesting to note that Kepler believes the RTX 6060 won't be as powerful as the PS6 for gaming frame rates, but I'd take that claim with even more salt than the rumors around timing.
Gauging hardware capabilities at this stage is obviously a trickier task, but Kepler's assertion isn't an impossibility of course. Note that the current RTX 5060 matches the PS5 Pro's gaming performance (roughly, for rasterization as opposed to ray tracing), so if the RTX 6060 couldn't equal the PS6, that would be a clear disappointment for PC gamers on a budget (particularly if the VRAM loadout again turns out lean).

articles.title: Cómo saber qué dice un audio de WhatsApp sin tener que reproducirlo
articles.text:
Los mensajes de voz no siempre llegan en un momento adecuado para escucharlos. WhatsApp ofrece una herramienta integrada para convertirlos en texto y consultar lo que dicen directamente debajo del audio. No hace falta instalar otra aplicación ni reproducir el mensaje: basta con activar las transcripciones y seleccionar el idioma que se utiliza con mayor frecuencia.
La función también puede facilitar el acceso a las conversaciones a las personas sordas o con dificultades auditivas. Las transcripciones están desactivadas de forma predeterminada, así que es necesario habilitarlas desde los ajustes del teléfono antes de usarlas. WhatsApp explica que el texto se genera en el dispositivo y que los mensajes personales siguen protegidos con cifrado de extremo a extremo.
Cómo activar las transcripciones
El primer paso es abrir WhatsApp y entrar en Ajustes o Configuración. En Android, se accede desde el menú de tres puntos de la parte superior; en iPhone, desde la pestaña de ajustes o tocando la foto de perfil, según la versión de la aplicación.
Después, sigue esta ruta:
- Entra en Chats.
- Pulsa Transcripciones de mensajes de voz.
- Activa la opción.
- Toca Seleccionar idioma y elige el que hablas habitualmente en los audios recibidos.
- Si la aplicación lo solicita, descarga el paquete de idioma para completar la configuración.
La descarga prepara el reconocimiento en el dispositivo. WhatsApp indica que, por el momento, admite transcripciones en inglés, portugués, español y ruso; la disponibilidad puede depender del sistema operativo y la versión de la aplicación. En iPhone, la herramienta requiere iOS 16 o posterior y Siri activado.
Cómo leer un audio sin reproducirlo
Una vez activada la herramienta, abre el chat donde está el mensaje de voz y mantén pulsado el audio. En iPhone, selecciona Transcribir en el menú que aparece. En Android, mantén pulsado el mensaje, toca el menú de tres puntos y elige la misma opción.
WhatsApp procesará la nota y mostrará el texto en el propio chat, debajo del mensaje de voz. La transcripción puede tardar unos segundos en aparecer. Si el texto queda parcialmente visible, se puede tocar el mensaje para expandirlo y leerlo completo.
No es necesario que el remitente active nada: la transcripción se crea en el teléfono de quien recibió el audio. Tampoco se envía una notificación al remitente indicando que el mensaje fue transcrito. Según WhatsApp, el proceso se realiza localmente y la compañía no puede escuchar el audio ni leer el texto generado.
Qué hacer si la transcripción no aparece
Si no ves la opción Transcribir, comprueba que la función esté activada y que el idioma elegido coincida con el del audio. También puedes actualizar WhatsApp, verificar que el paquete de idioma se haya descargado o revisar los requisitos de iOS si utilizas un iPhone.
La herramienta no siempre reconoce todo con exactitud. El ruido de fondo, una grabación poco clara, los cambios de idioma, los nombres propios y las expresiones locales pueden afectar el resultado. Por eso, una transcripción sirve para entender el tema general de un audio, pero puede contener errores en palabras o frases concretas.
La función es distinta de la traducción: convierte la voz en texto en el idioma seleccionado, pero no necesariamente traduce lo que se dijo. Si el mensaje está en un idioma no compatible o la voz se entiende con dificultad, WhatsApp puede no generar una transcripción correcta. En esos casos, se puede cambiar el idioma desde Ajustes > Chats > Transcripciones de mensajes de voz o pedir al remitente que envíe el contenido por escrito.
Con la opción activada, basta con mantener pulsado el mensaje y elegir Transcribir para consultar su contenido sin reproducirlo. No elimina el audio ni lo convierte automáticamente al llegar: cada usuario decide cuándo solicitar el texto y qué idioma utilizar.

articles.title: Darmoshark Air28 Revealed As 28 G Wireless Fingertip Gaming Mouse
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 21st 2026
Darmoshark Air28 Revealed As 28 G Wireless Fingertip Gaming Mouse
Darmoshark, the Chinese mouse maker previously responsible for the Darmoshark M9, a flagship-spec gaming mouse for gamers with big hands, has come out swinging at the likes of the new Pulsar X2F CrazyLight and G-Wolves Lupine II with the Air28. The new asymmetrical fingertip gaming mouse packs flagship-tier specs into a small shape optimized for a fingertip grip. 
Much like the aforementioned G-Wolves Lupine II, the Darmoshark Air28 is an asymmetrical "ergo" fingertip mouse, and it comes in at a claimed 28 g, hence the name. Pricing is unclear as of the time of writing, but the brand has released the specs on its Bilibili page, revealing a PixArt PAW 3955 sensor and a Nordic 54L15 MCU, granting it 8 kHz polling, up to 30,000 DPI, 60 G acceleration, and 850 IPS tracking speed. The Air28 will also have optical mouse switches when it launches, although an exact launch date is as yet unclear. When it launches, it will feature both 2.4 GHz wireless and USB Type-C wired connectivity.The Bilibili teaser video also shows off the internals, which feature a lateral reinforcement strut to resist tight squeezing, suggesting the mouse will have a very thin side wall. It will also come with an NXP Dual 8K Display Receiver, which Darmoshark has long sold alongside its gaming mouse. This is likely the same receiver as the one sold with the Darmoshark M5 Air V2 mouse, which retails for around $80-119 on th Darmoshark official store, suggesting a similar price for the new Air28. Despite the ergonomic shape, and the lack of honeycomb cutouts, the new Air28 is still a claimed 3 g—or 10%—lighter than the aforementioned M5 Air V2

articles.title: U.S. Orders DeepSeek Removed From Federal Civilian Systems, Bans New Purchases
articles.text:
U.S. federal civilian agencies must remove DeepSeek products from their information technology systems, along with any third-party products or services "developed using DeepSeek implementations," under a Department of Homeland Security order.
They may also no longer buy information technology products or services from the Chinese AI developer or its affiliates
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin issued the order, dated July 24, 2026, under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018, and the department published it in the Federal Register on October 20. The notice does not define "DeepSeek implementations."
The order names Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd., the developer of the R1 and V3 models, and covers its affiliates as defined in federal acquisition rules. The company's privacy policy says it collects, processes and stores users' personal data in the People's Republic of China.
Under the 2018 law, the Federal Acquisition Security Council recommends exclusion and removal orders, and three officials may issue them: the Secretary of Homeland Security for civilian agencies, the Secretary of Defense for the Defense Department and national security systems, and the Director of National Intelligence for the intelligence community.
The DeepSeek order therefore covers only what civilian agencies buy and run. It does not restrict companies or the public.
The 2018 law was first used in 2025, when the Director of National Intelligence excluded Acronis, a Swiss cybersecurity and data protection company, from intelligence community procurement and ordered its products removed from intelligence community systems.
Executive agencies "shall comply with exclusion and removal orders," the law says. An agency can ask the official who issued an order for an exception, and under the council's regulations the request must be in writing and give a compelling justification.
DHS directs questions about the order to CISA's FASCSA Order Implementation Team at fascsa.orders@cisa.dhs.gov.
The order also reaches government contractors. A federal contract that carries FAR clause 52.204-30 bars the contractor from providing or using, in performing the contract, any product or service covered by an applicable FASCSA order, unless the issuing official has granted a waiver.
The clause also requires the contractor to:
- Search SAM.gov for the phrase "FASCSA order" at least once every three months
- Make a reasonable inquiry into its supply chain when a new order could affect it
- Report any covered product or service it has provided or used to the contracting officer within 3 business days of identifying it
- Send further information on mitigation within 10 business days of that report
- Include the clause in its subcontracts
An order issued after a solicitation applies to an existing contract only once the contracting officer adds it by amendment or modification.
The Federal Register notice gives no reasons for the order. The signed order is attached to the notice as four scanned pages and is posted on regulations.gov under docket DHS-2026-0628.
The order is dated July 24. DHS filed it for public inspection at the Federal Register on October 19, 87 days later, and it was published the next day.
The council's regulations leave public release of an order to the issuing official, who "May provide a copy of the order to other persons, including through public disclosure." They set no deadline for it.
The law requires the issuing official to notify the company named in an order and the appropriate congressional committees, and to review the order at least once a year.
Before the order, U.S. restrictions on DeepSeek were device bans adopted one body at a time. By February 2025, Congress, NASA, the Navy, the Pentagon and Texas had barred DeepSeek from government devices. Bills to bar DeepSeek on government devices were introduced in the House and Senate that month and had not advanced past committee as of October 21.
China's foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said at a briefing on October 20 that "China consistently opposes the overstretching of the concept of national security" and that Beijing will "resolutely safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies," the Associated Press reported. DeepSeek did not immediately respond to the AP's request for comment.

articles.title: NordVPN corrige une faille permettant à des pirates de désactiver des services Windows, mettez votre application à jour
articles.text:
Une vulnérabilité découverte dans NordVPN pour Windows permettait à un programme malveillant d'arrêter certains services système sans disposer des droits administrateur. Le fournisseur a déjà publié un correctif.
Le CERT Polska vient de communiquer sur une vulnérabilité dans l'application Windows de NordVPN. Référencée CVE-2026-106030 (CVSS 6.8), elle permet à un programme exécuté avec des droits limités d'arrêter certains services Windows ou de modifier leur configuration de démarrage, sans disposer des autorisations normalement nécessaires. Signalée par le chercheur Marcin Ressel, la faille a été corrigée fin septembre par le fournisseur VPN, mais les utilisateurs et utilisatrices qui n'ont pas mis à jour leur application peuvent encore y être exposés.
Des privilèges détournés pour agir sur les services Windows
Dans le détail, le problème résulte d'un défaut de contrôle des autorisations dans le système de communication interne de NordVPN sur Windows. L'application ne vérifiait pas correctement si les programmes qui lui transmettaient des commandes étaient autorisés à le faire. Un logiciel malveillant pouvait alors profiter des privilèges de NordVPN pour effectuer des opérations normalement réservées aux processus autorisés. Selon les services ciblés, l'attaque pouvait perturber le fonctionnement de Windows ou de certaines applications, voire empêcher leur démarrage automatique.
L'exploitation nécessitait toutefois l'exécution préalable d'un programme sur l'ordinateur visé. La faille ne pouvait donc pas être exploitée directement à distance. Les services bénéficiant des protections renforcées de Windows, comme Microsoft Defender, ne pouvaient pas non plus être désactivés de cette manière.
Nord Security avait déjà remédié au problème lorsque le CERT Polska a rendu ses conclusions publiques, au terme d'une procédure de divulgation coordonnée. Le correctif figure dans la version 8.12 de NordVPN pour Windows, publiée le 24 septembre, mais le fournisseur n'en a pas fait mention dans les notes de cette mise à jour. Les utilisateurs et utilisatrices disposant d'une version antérieure à la 8.12 doivent donc mettre leur application à jour pour ne plus être exposés à cette faille.
- storage9500 serveurs
- language167 pays couverts
- lan10 connexions simultanées
- moodEssai gratuit 30 jours
- thumb_upAvantage : sécurité polyvalente
NordVPN reste un service complet et solide pour le grand public, porté par un réseau étendu, d’excellents débits avec NordLynx et une gamme de fonctions qui dépasse largement le seul tunnel VPN. Meshnet, l’analyse des téléchargements, la protection contre le phishing et les arnaques, ainsi que la surveillance du Dark Web renforcent encore l’ensemble. L’application manque toutefois d’indicateurs pour comparer finement les serveurs et pousse assez clairement à laisser la protection active en permanence.
- Très bonnes performances avec NordLynx
- Réseau de serveurs très étendu
- Meshnet vraiment pratique au quotidien
- Politique no-log auditée régulièrement
- Support réactif, avec assistance en français
- Pas d’indicateur de charge ou de latence par serveur
- Interface qui pousse à garder le VPN activé en permanence
Une élévation de privilèges locale (LPE) permet à un programme déjà présent sur la machine, lancé avec des droits limités, d’effectuer des actions normalement réservées à des comptes plus puissants (administrateur ou SYSTEM). Dans Windows, ces actions passent souvent par des services, qui tournent avec des privilèges élevés et contrôlent des fonctions sensibles (réseau, sécurité, mises à jour). Contrairement à une attaque à distance, il faut d’abord parvenir à exécuter du code sur l’ordinateur (via un malware, une pièce jointe, un installateur piégé, etc.). L’impact typique est la désactivation de composants, la perturbation du système, ou la préparation d’étapes d’attaque plus graves. Le fait que ce soit “local” réduit la surface d’attaque sur Internet, mais reste sérieux si la machine est déjà compromise.
Les applications Windows utilisent souvent un mécanisme de communication inter-processus (IPC) pour dialoguer entre une interface utilisateur et un composant plus privilégié (service, agent, driver). Si ce canal IPC ne vérifie pas correctement l’identité du demandeur ni ses autorisations, un autre programme peut lui envoyer des commandes comme s’il était légitime. Le composant privilégié exécute alors la demande avec ses propres droits, ce qui contourne les restrictions normales imposées à l’utilisateur. Concrètement, cela peut se traduire par un arrêt de service ou un changement de “Startup type” (Automatique, Manuel, Désactivé) via les API de gestion des services Windows. C’est un schéma classique de “confusion d’autorité” : le contrôle est fait au mauvais endroit, ou pas assez strictement.
Un CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) est un identifiant public standardisé qui permet de référencer une faille de manière unique, quel que soit l’éditeur ou la source qui en parle. Le CVSS (Common Vulnerability Scoring System) donne un score de gravité sur 10 à partir de critères comme le vecteur d’attaque (local ou réseau), la complexité, les privilèges requis et l’impact sur la confidentialité, l’intégrité et la disponibilité. Un score de 6.8 se situe généralement dans une zone “moyenne à élevée” : ce n’est pas anodin, mais ce n’est pas non plus le niveau maximal associé à une prise de contrôle à distance sans interaction. Dans ce cas, le besoin d’exécuter d’abord un programme sur la machine pèse souvent sur la note, tandis que l’impact potentiel sur la disponibilité (arrêt de services) la fait remonter. Le CVSS sert à prioriser les correctifs, mais ne remplace pas l’analyse du contexte (poste critique, parc d’entreprise, protections en place).

articles.title: Many firms are still falling behind when it comes to getting their AI infrastructure up to speed
articles.text:
Many firms are still falling behind when it comes to getting their AI infrastructure up to speed
AI infrastructure is a major holdback
- Two in three IT leaders say their infrastructure isn't ready to handle AI and analytics
- Complex data regulations are giving them a major headache
- AI PCs also form part of the broader infrastructure considerations
According to a new report by Dell, UK businesses are struggling more than their EMEA counterparts when it comes to AI, with three in five (61%) British firms lacking a clear roadmap covering AI, data and security, compared with 46% across EMEA.
But one thing they have in common with their Europe and Middle East counterparts is that legacy infrastructure is likely one of the biggest factors slowing effective AI deployment.
Nearly two-thirds (64%) of IT leaders say their infrastructure is not yet fully prepared to support AI and analytics workloads at scale, noting substantial gaps between ambitions and reality.
Data foundations and IT infrastructure are still holding back AI
Having to coordinate compliance and regulatory factors across their entire stacks is also making it difficult for enterprises to lay out solid foundations, the report claims. More than half (55%) say security and compliance concerns have already slower or delayed their AI strategies, with 64% of leaders worried about regulation compliance when using their data for AI.
And it's not just complex IT infrastructure that's holding back widespread deployment, because even end-user devices need to be considered. Nearly all (92%) respondents agreed that modern devices help them in terms of productivity, but four in five (79%) are being held back by outdated devices.
To that tune, 86% of EMEA leaders now agree that AI PCs will play an important role in their strategies going forward. As of the beginning of 2026, AI PCs accounted for around 44% of all PC shipments (per Omdia tracking), marking a healthy ongoing rise.
"The focus is shifting from exploring what's possible to connecting the infrastructure, data, security and workplace technology needed to turn AI into real business value at scale," UK&I MD and Dell SVP Steve Young explained.

While IT leaders clearly understand some of the factors holding back effective AI deployments, at least two clear challenges are identified in Dell's report – complex regulatory environments and an expensive PC market driven by component shortages.
