articles.title: Databuddy Analytics raises $500,000 from Y Combinator
articles.text: US-based AI-powered analytics startup Databuddy Analytics has raised more than $560,000 in total funding, including $500,000 in Seed funding from Y Combinator, alongside investments from Maza Ventures and through the a16z Scout programme. Founded in 2026 by Palestinian entrepreneur Issa Nassar, Databuddy Analytics develops an AI-powered product analytics platform that helps businesses identify conversion drops, customer friction and product issues through automated investigations and actionable insights. The funding will support the development of more advanced AI investigation capabilities, additional integrations, targeted hiring and improved customer onboarding, as the company seeks to expand its user base. Press release: Databuddy Analytics, the AI-driven analytics platform, has raised $500,000 in Seed funding from Y Combinator as it launches its AI intelligence platform. With investment from Maza Ventures and through the a16z Scout programme, Databuddy has raised more than $560,000 to date. The company's new AI analytics platform investigates conversion drops, customer friction and product issues on a team's behalf and brings the findings to them. Unlike the traditional web analytics approach, the platform proactively shows what changed and why, without the need to dig through reports and filters. Databuddy has grown to serve more than 3,000 businesses in the first few months since launch. "Teams don't want more charts; they want to know what's broken and what to do about it," says Issa Nassar, Founder of Databuddy. "We built Databuddy so that the answer is one question away. Y Combinator's backing lets us move faster on that and put it in front of far more teams." Issa Nassar grew up in Palestine, started coding at age 11 and dropped out of university. He was accepted into Y Combinator at 20, becoming the youngest founder in the Middle East to be accepted into Silicon Valley’s iconic accelerator. Tambi Jalouqa, Managing Partner at Maza Ventures, shared, "Most founders start by explaining the market. Issa started by showing us what he had built. Databuddy is one of those products that looks deceptively simple, which is usually a sign that someone has spent a lot of time thinking about the problem. Issa has the combination we look for at Maza: he's deeply technical, moves unusually fast, and seems more interested in making something people want than in looking like a startup founder. Those are often the founders worth betting on early." The funding will support deeper AI investigation capabilities, additional integrations and targeted hiring. Databuddy will also invest in onboarding and migration support, helping more teams connect their existing data and put the platform to work.

articles.title: Dell CEO Says the Memory Shortage Will Get Worse in 2027
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Dell CEO Says the Memory Shortage Will Get Worse in 2027
Michael Dell doesn't think the memory shortage is anywhere near over. Speaking with The Wall Street Journal, Dell's chairman and CEO said things will get worse next year, as the AI data center buildout keeps soaking up DRAM and HBM supply. According to him, the bottleneck for Dell isn't demand, since the company is sitting on roughly $95 billion worth of AI server orders it hasn't delivered yet, the largest backlog in its history. Memory is what's holding those shipments back, as AI accelerators need plenty of HBM, while the servers around them still rely on conventional DRAM.
Relief also looks quite far away. New memory fabs take around four years to build, so Dell apparently doesn't expect meaningful new supply until 2029 or 2030. That aligns with Micron's CEO, who recently said supply will be much tighter in 2027 and 2028 than it is this year. Interestingly, SK hynix's CEO said something similar, expecting the memory shortage to last through 2030. Dell is reportedly coping by buying DRAM only when final assembly is close and by locking in long-term supply agreements, though there's no word on how much of that applies to its consumer products.PC buyers have been feeling the effects for months now. Memory prices have surged nearly 500% in the last 12 months and continue to be on the rise, affecting all segments of the DIY PC market. As for Dell, the company raised PC prices by 15-20% late last year and is reportedly raising monitor prices this month, too. It's reasonable to expect more hikes across the industry if the shortage does deepen in 2027.
Sources:

Even when DRAM would go down, it can not, TSMC and other material and manufacturing steps asks more as before the bitcoin bubble.
If you don’t lower the prices, I’ll execute the old man.
It’s barely running on XP as it is.
At least let him spend his final days in comfort.
The demand comes from the AI tech bros who still have yet to make a profit, hence it being an unsustainable bubble.
The basic principles of supply and demand instead work as follows in this context - demand is higher than supply, remaining "supply" in circulation (which is still not sufficient to meet demand) enters a spiral of rising prices, some stock is left on shelves, because retailers would rather sell more slowly at much greater profits with their remaining "supply" in stock, since resupply is a) at increased over MSRP prices, and b) not as available as it was prior to demand exceeding supply. Most of the new "supply" goes straight to the highest bidder, which, despite extreme prices for the consumer, is still not the consumer, it's the big companies that can make enough money from securing supply, that the price doesn't really matter anywhere near as much as it does to a consumer. A consumer who makes value judgements primarily based on want, not need. To clarify, the average gamer buying a GPU isn't doing so because that GPU is an investment, nor because they need it for their continued existence. Thus, their value judgement is want vs cost, and there is a much lower price level at which that cost becomes too much, for the want. For the average business/corporation that survives by making as much money off the same resources that go into making professional versions of that GPU, the value judgement is profit/cost. They project that they will, now or eventually, make more profit than the cost, so the price becomes borderline irrelevant.
It's very easy to understand that there is a shortage, because businesses that literally want to buy hardware, in many cases literally cannot, because there is a waitlist/queue, as prior contracts secured earlier are fulfilled first.
If you cannot or will not understand this, or choose to ignore it, your life will be filled with frustration and confusion, and putting forth objectively wrong statements like "there is no shortage", as emotionally attractive as those statements may be, become "reasonable". There, by definition, is a shortage, because demand is higher than supply. It's really a very simple economic concept.
Currently you can pick whichever projection you like (the big sellers/marketeers saying climbing prices all throughout 2027 or those user/buyer/manufactures claiming a bubble-pop much sooner than that) with something like a 50/50 chance of being right either way. Only time will actually tell. We'll know for sure in about 8 months (I think).
And then... there's bigger-better-bail-outs to consider from the incoming administration. "SI" is already being presented as an existential necessity! :P
On the "shortage" issue... There's definitely a shortage! I think what may be confusing others is exactly how much is managed and manufactured shortages as opposed to shortages created entirely from physical limitations on capacity. It's of course both to some degree or another - it's just not clear to most of us the ratios.
If I can produce 10 apples and people only want 5 the price of apples will drop in order for me to be able to sell my 10 apples. If suddenly the demand for apples goes up to 20 apples I still make 10 apples, it's just that the price will increase cause people are willing to pay more to get access to that commodity.

articles.title: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection ya se puede jugar en PC a 120 FPS
articles.text:
Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection ya puede ejecutarse de forma nativa en Windows gracias a un trabajo de ingeniería inversa asistido por inteligencia artificial. Los tres títulos que componen la recopilación (Uncharted: El tesoro de Drake, Uncharted 2: El reino de los ladrones y Uncharted 3: La traición de Drake) dejan así de estar limitados a las plataformas de Sony y llegan a ordenador con un rendimiento que alcanza los 120 FPS.
El responsable del proyecto es el desarrollador conocido como SuperMedo, la misma persona detrás de un port similar para Bloodborne. El avance resulta posible porque el hardware de las consolas no deja de ser, en esencia, hardware de PC encerrado en un ecosistema cerrado, una barrera que la inteligencia artificial ha ayudado a simplificar a la hora de portar títulos exclusivos de PlayStation.
Cómo funciona el port de Uncharted a PC
El sistema parte del código x86-64 original de los juegos de PS4, que se ejecuta de manera directa sobre la CPU del ordenador. Sobre esa base se añade una capa de compatibilidad que sustituye las funciones propias de la consola, de modo que el sistema operativo de Windows pueda interpretar correctamente las llamadas que originalmente estaban pensadas para PlayStation 4.
La parte gráfica se resuelve mediante un renderer basado en el emulador shadPS4, que traduce ese apartado visual a la API Vulkan. Este esquema es el mismo que ya se había utilizado en el port de Bloodborne, lo que confirma que la metodología empleada por SuperMedo puede extenderse a otros exclusivos de la plataforma.
No se trata de una emulación tradicional, sino de una ejecución prácticamente nativa del código original, con una capa intermedia que resuelve las diferencias de arquitectura entre consola y ordenador. Es ese punto el que explica por qué los resultados de rendimiento son tan superiores a los de un emulador convencional.
Rendimiento a 120 FPS y compatibilidad con DLSS y FSR
El launcher reúne los tres juegos de la colección y permite configurarlos para funcionar a 60 o 120 FPS, con la posibilidad de superar ese límite de forma experimental, aunque esta última opción puede generar problemas en el funcionamiento interno de los títulos.
El port incorpora, además, un conjunto de opciones gráficas propias de una edición pensada específicamente para PC. Entre ellas figura el soporte para NVIDIA DLSS y DLAA, AMD FSR 3.1 y FSR 4, así como generación de fotogramas mediante AMD FSR 3 Frame Generation y NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation. Los usuarios de tarjetas GeForce RTX 50 pueden recurrir también a Multi Frame Generation.
A nivel de controles, la recopilación admite teclado y ratón, compatibilidad con mandos y la posibilidad de reasignar por completo los controles, lo que incluye el manejo de la cámara mediante ratón en Uncharted 3.
Las primeras pruebas de rendimiento respaldan estas cifras. Una configuración con un procesador AMD Ryzen 5 7500F y una tarjeta NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER logró mover los juegos a aproximadamente 120 FPS en resolución 1440p nativa.
Otros usuarios reportaron haber completado Uncharted: Drake’s Fortune con una GeForce RTX 4060, con cifras de entre 100 y 120 FPS en 1080p con DLAA activado, aunque en las secuencias más exigentes el rendimiento podía descender hasta los 80 FPS.
Errores y problemas en esta fase temprana de desarrollo
El proyecto sigue en fase de desarrollo y presenta fallos propios de una versión sin pulir. Se han reportado cierres inesperados durante las partidas, y en un caso concreto un jugador informó de una partida guardada corrupta durante el capítulo 11 del primer Uncharted.
Uncharted 3, por su parte, puede mostrar de forma ocasional artefactos gráficos en determinados personajes. Son incidencias que, de todos modos, resultan menores si se considera que el port todavía no ha recibido ningún parche oficial que corrija estos comportamientos.
El ritmo de actualizaciones, sin embargo, es constante. La versión 0.3.6 ya solucionó varios errores gráficos y un bloqueo asociado a la secuencia del accidente de tren en Uncharted 2. Actualizaciones previas habían corregido, a su vez, problemas de texturas, fallos de renderizado y distintos cierres de los juegos.
Un segundo proyecto alternativo y cómo conseguir los juegos
Paralelamente al trabajo de SuperMedo existe otro port desarrollado por BilalReloaded, que ofrece resoluciones superiores, soporte para formato ultrapanorámico y otras funciones adicionales pensadas para PC. Este segundo proyecto también se encuentra en fase beta.
Como ocurre con el resto de ports de este tipo, ninguno de los dos incluye archivos del juego. Esto implica que cada usuario deberá volcar su propia copia legítima de Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection de PlayStation 4 para poder utilizarla en PC a través de estos sistemas.

articles.title: State Bank of India Confirms Data Leak After 3,897 Customer Records Found on Dark Web
articles.text:
State Bank of India has identified 3,897 customer records containing personal information in a set of about 375,000 records available on the dark web, and it does not yet know where the data came from.
The state-owned bank, India's largest, said in a stock-exchange filing dated October 21 that it "has experienced an incident involving the loss of certain data." The count is preliminary, and the bank has yet to establish whether the data is authentic, how far the exposure goes and what risk it poses to customers.
The exposed information "reportedly included customers' registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata associated with loan/lead records and other related files," in the filing's words. A CIF identifier is the customer information file number, the bank's internal ID for each customer.
The bank has not said whether the 3,897 records belong to 3,897 different people, or what the rest of the set contains. The 3,897 are roughly 1 in 100 of the records it examined.
Account numbers, balances, passwords, one-time passcodes, card details and government identity numbers such as PAN or Aadhaar are not among the categories the filing lists. The risk in the listed categories is impersonation: a caller or message that uses a customer's name, mobile number, date of birth, address, branch, and internal ID to appear to come from the bank.
The alert reached the bank on October 16 via its threat intelligence provider, CERT-In, India's national computer emergency response team, and the Defense Cyber Agency, the armed forces' cyber agency under the Ministry of Defense.
The bank activated its incident response and containment procedures and engaged an independent cybersecurity firm from CERT-In's panel of approved security auditors to assess what the filing calls "the alleged compromise."
The incident has no material impact on the bank's core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, the filing says. That covers the bank's business, not its customers.
The filing names no attacker, forum or dataset. The figure of about 375,000 matches a claim that the monitoring account CyberPulse56 flagged on X on October 16.
The account said a threat actor using the name Siriusim claimed to have leaked customer documents and personal data linked to SBI: 375,000 rows in CSV format and 2,722 PDF documents, said to include personal information, loan applications and supporting documents, account-opening forms and addresses.
The Free Press Journal examined the listing on BreachForums, a cybercrime forum used to trade stolen data, and found 4 sample records posted with the listing. The phone numbers in the samples were valid. The WhatsApp profile picture on one number matched the passport-size photograph on that person's KYC document, which the actor had also posted.
That check covers 4 records and does not show that the whole set is genuine or where it came from. The samples were mostly loan-related and carried KYC fields, and they did not show whether the data belonged to SBI itself, one of its subsidiaries, or a third-party provider that handles banking applications.
Nothing in the bank's filing ties its analysis to the listing, and the bank has not said whether the 2,722 PDF documents were part of what it examined.
Whether any SBI system was breached is an open question. The filing leaves the source of the data to the investigation and gives no date for when the data first appeared.
The filing does not mention whether affected customers have been or will be told. The bank's cyber security page, last updated in June, tells customers to report any cyber incident to report.phishing@sbi.co.in or the national cybercrime helpline, 1930. That is general advice, written before the incident.
Bank of Baroda, another state-owned bank, told the exchanges on July 27 about a cyber-security incident in nearly the same words, including "the alleged compromise," after receiving "a communication from an anonymous source claiming access to certain data." That filing named a preliminary cause, "potential business email compromise." SBI's names none.

articles.title: These 4 cheap headphones and earbuds will let you dodge the 'headphone dodger' penalty fare
articles.text:
4 cheap headphones and earbuds we've tested to avoid 'headphone dodger' fines — they're all cheaper than the £100 you'll pay if you're caught
Save a fine, buy an earbud
- UK government cracks down on people who annoy others with phone music
- Fines of up to £100 for those people
- It's cheaper to just buy these headphones
People who play music, TikTok videos or out-loud video calls on public transport probably aren't self-aware enough to know how annoying it is, but apparently the UK government does, because it's finally cracking down on so-called "headphone dodgers".
From next Monday, transport authorities will be allowed to fine rule-breakers by up to £100 if they're causing a nuisance. Prime Minister Andy Burnham is fronting the campaign, after previous governments toyed with the idea.
It's a good idea, but the success is dependent on enforcement, as transport safety officers and not drivers are expected to hand out the fines. Given how minimally-staffed most public transport services are, some (me) are dubious that the rules will make a difference.
However if you've been a 'headphone dodger' and you want to turn a new leaf (good on you), it'd make sense to buy a pair of headphones that cost much less than the £100 penalty fare.
And naturally, we've tested a few that we can recommend…
Sennheiser CX 80U
Starting with something nice and cheap, we've got some wired earbuds, which you can easily plug into the USB-C port on a phone and keep bundled up in your pocket the rest of the time. No Bluetooth dropouts, no losing a bud as you board the bus, no apps, none of that.
The Sennheiser CX 80U sound great, block surrounding noise quite well, and offer a nice simple design. We gave them 4.5 stars out of 5 in our review, only knocking them for some missing features of pricier buds.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Best of all, though, they're really cheap. They launched for $39.95 / £34.99 in January this year, but you can find them even a little cheaper than that on Amazon.
Sony WH-CH530 (or even the Sony WH-CH730N)
If you want great-value headphones, you can't go wrong with a pair from Sony, and its recently-released Sony WH-CH530N are really affordable at $69 / £50.
We haven't yet finished testing these on-ears, they're that new, but their predecessors the WH-CH520 got 4.5 stars in our review. We praised the balanced sound and long-lasting battery, and the newer pair will likely bring improvements.
As you can see in the picture, they come in a wide range of colors, and also have noise cancellation, which isn't something you can say about all options at this price point.
Prefer over-ears? Go for the just-reviewed, all-new Sony WH-CH730N: a solid four stars and they're just under that £99 (or equivalent, in your country of residence) fine line, if you'll pardon the pun…
JLab JBuds Mini ANC
Last, but not least, let's look at some standard wireless noise-cancelling earbuds, which we got to try earlier this year.
The JLab JBuds Mini ANC are tiny — you can even clip the case onto your keyring — so you've got no excuse for not having buds on the bus. At $49.99 / £49.99 they won't break the bank either.
We enjoyed the non-ANC JLab JBuds Mini too, when they came out three years ago, and they're ideal for people who want lightweight buds.

articles.title: Voitures thermiques après 2035 : le compromis européen se heurte déjà à un désaccord
articles.text:
Les négociateurs du Parlement européen pensaient avoir trouvé un compromis pour assouplir les règles sur les moteurs thermiques à partir de 2035. Mais les sociaux-démocrates n’ont pas encore validé cet accord qui doit encore franchir plusieurs étapes avant de devenir une réalité.
L’Europe semblait enfin avancer sur l’épineux dossier de la fin des voitures thermiques neuves en 2035. Dans la nuit du 19 au 20 octobre, les représentants des conservateurs du PPE, des sociaux-démocrates (S&D) et des libéraux de Renew Europe sont parvenus à un compromis pour assouplir les objectifs de réduction du CO2. Mais quelques heures plus tard, l’enthousiasme est retombé. Iratxe García Pérez, présidente du groupe S&D, a indiqué que ses députés devaient encore en discuter avant de donner leur feu vert.
Un sérieux contretemps pour les trois formations, qui disposent théoriquement d’une majorité au Parlement européen, à condition de parvenir à voter ensemble.
Le moteur thermique pourrait finalement survivre à 2035
Le compromis négocié à Strasbourg s’éloigne sensiblement de l’objectif actuel, qui impose aux constructeurs de réduire de 100% les émissions moyennes de CO₂ de leurs voitures neuves en 2035, par rapport à 2021.
Le nouveau texte ramènerait cette exigence à 95%, avec une souplesse supplémentaire pour les fabricants utilisant de l’acier bas carbone produit dans l’Union européenne. Grâce à ce mécanisme de crédits, la réduction effective pourrait descendre jusqu’à 87,5%.
De quoi permettre la commercialisation de voitures thermiques et hybrides neuves après 2035. Il ne s’agirait toutefois pas d’autoriser un pourcentage précis de véhicules essence ou diesel puisque les objectifs continueraient de porter sur les émissions moyennes des constructeurs.
Les négociateurs prévoient également davantage de flexibilité pour 2030, avec la possibilité de lisser les résultats entre 2029 et 2031. Les utilitaires bénéficieraient eux aussi d’objectifs assouplis, tandis que les petites voitures électriques abordables pourraient rapporter des crédits supplémentaires à leurs fabricants. Certains véhicules fonctionnant exclusivement avec des carburants renouvelables seraient également favorisés.
Paris et Berlin poussent leur propre compromis
La France et l’Allemagne avaient déjà ouvert la voie quelques jours plus tôt en s’entendant sur un objectif de 90% de réduction des émissions en 2035, sans obligation de compenser les 10% restants.
En échange de cet assouplissement, Berlin soutient les demandes françaises visant à privilégier les véhicules et composants fabriqués en Europe, notamment dans les dispositifs d’aide publique. Le gouvernement allemand obtient ainsi davantage de souplesse pour les motorisations thermiques et hybrides, tandis que Paris défend les intérêts de la production automobile européenne.
Avec la totalité des crédits liés à l’acier bas carbone, la réduction des émissions à l’échappement pourrait être ramenée à 87,5% contre 90% dans la proposition franco-allemande. Le compromis parlementaire offrirait donc davantage de souplesse aux constructeurs, sous réserve de remplir les conditions prévues.
Rien n’est encore décidé pour les automobilistes
Le désaccord au sein des sociaux-démocrates complique désormais le calendrier. Les commissions Transports et Industrie doivent se prononcer le 22 octobre avant un examen par la commission Environnement début novembre. Selon n-tv, un vote en séance plénière est envisagé en décembre
Même si le Parlement parvient à adopter une position commune, il faudra ensuite trouver un accord avec les États membres pour modifier la réglementation européenne.
Les divergences traversent également les familles politiques. Les conservateurs défendent l’assouplissement comme un moyen de préserver l’industrie automobile alors que certains sociaux-démocrates souhaitent maintenir une trajectoire favorable à l’électrique. Les écologistes redoutent, de leur côté, que ces changements fragilisent les investissements déjà engagés par les constructeurs.
À force de remettre en question l'échéance de 2035, l'Europe brouille un peu plus les perspectives des constructeurs et risque d'inciter les automobilistes à repousser leur achat. Électrique, hybride ou thermique, sur quelle motorisation miser quand les règles du jeu changent sans cesse ? Pour choisir leur prochaine voiture, les Européens vont finir par devoir allumer les antibrouillards.

articles.title: CapQuest closes $1 million pre-Seed funding to expand globally
articles.text: UAE-based fintech startup CapQuest has raised $1 million in a pre-Seed funding round, led by Oraseya Capital and AMKM Family Office, to accelerate product development and international expansion. Founded in 2023 by Antoine Bruna, Marco Banfi and Anvita Varshney, CapQuest operates an equity management platform that enables startups and established businesses to manage ownership structures, capitalisation tables, employee stock ownership plans (ESOPs), vesting schedules, fundraising transactions and shareholder communications. The funding will support product development, increased automation, enhanced equity management tools and commercial expansion, as the company seeks to grow its international customer base. Press release: CapQuest, a Dubai-based equity management platform, has announced the successful closing of its $1 million Pre-Seed funding round, led by Oraseya Capital and AMKM Family Office. Founded by Antoine Bruna, Marco Banfi, and Anvita Varshney, CapQuest is transforming how companies manage equity, ownership, and investor relations. The platform enables startups, scaleups, and established businesses to manage their cap tables, employee equity plans (ESOPs), vesting schedules, fundraising transactions, and shareholder communications through a single, centralised solution. Designed to replace fragmented spreadsheets and manual processes, CapQuest helps companies simplify complex equity operations, improve transparency, and maintain accurate ownership records throughout their growth. Growing International Traction Since its launch, CapQuest has established a growing international presence, serving companies across 11 countries, with a strong focus on the Middle East, Europe and emerging markets. Its client portfolio includes notable companies such as Holo, Erad, Avenia, and Teylor, reflecting increasing demand for modern equity management infrastructure among high-growth businesses. CapQuest's continued expansion highlights the growing importance of effective equity governance as companies navigate fundraising, employee ownership, and increasingly complex shareholder structures. Accelerating Growth and Product Innovation The funding will accelerate product development, expand CapQuest's commercial presence, and enhance its equity management capabilities through greater automation and more advanced tools. “This funding represents an important milestone for CapQuest and a strong validation of our vision,” said Antoine Bruna, CEO & Co-Founder of CapQuest. “Equity management remains unnecessarily complex for many companies, particularly as they scale and expand internationally. We’re building the infrastructure to make equity management more accessible, transparent, and efficient. With a growing international customer base and an expanding suite of products, CapQuest aims to become a leading platform for equity and investment management, connecting companies, shareholders, and investors within a unified ecosystem.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 Leaks Early, Brings Console Mods and Dual-Wielding Pistols
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 Leaks Early, Brings Console Mods and Dual-Wielding Pistols
CD Projekt RED's Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 isn't out until October 22, but most of its content has already leaked. YouTuber WesNemo apparently published a video covering the update too early, and while it has since been pulled, players on r/GamingLeaksAndRumours had already summarized it. According to WesNemo, CD Projekt gave him and other creators early access to the update ahead of its official presentation. The studio itself has only confirmed dual-wielding and cyberware customization so far, so treat the rest as unofficial until the patch notes go live.
Apparently, dual-wielding is limited to pistols and comes through a new "Double Trouble" perk in the Cool skill tree. The leak also lists a new Edgerunners 2 gig called "Clampdown," which reportedly acts as a prequel to the anime that premiered on Netflix on October 20, plus a mystery Night City tour sidequest. Glamdoc shops will let players change the look of arm cyberware like Mantis Blades and Gorilla Arms, and there are five new clothing sets, new hairstyles for both male and female V, Quadra skins through Twitch Drops, and a radio station playing Edgerunners music.The bigger news for console players is integrated mod.io support on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, along with a long-requested FOV slider. The Switch 2 is reportedly left out of mod support, although it's not clear if that changes later. CD Projekt will share full details during its livestream on October 21 at 5 PM CEST, so it's reasonable to expect a complete list of changes then.
Sources:
				WesNemo on YouTube, 				r/GamingLeaksAndRumours, 				via Notebookcheck			
	
	
	
		
	
		
3 Comments on Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 Leaks Early, Brings Console Mods and Dual-Wielding Pistols
i wish they would just add on a few side quests to keep it going until the cyberpunk 2 hits retail. no doubt in the very distant future.
The story literally mentioned that a new side quest is added that will serve as a prequel to Edgerunners 2.
And a new perk is also added in the talent tree for dual-wielding pistols. So for people that always wanted to use both Jackie's La Chingona Dorada guns, they can do so now.
You pick one handgun and one sniper rifle, and you can easily get through the entire game with just those two weapons. Once you've upgraded them, they all feel pretty much the same anyway, and you can even beat the game with a basic, run-of-the-mill weapon.
The same applies to pretty much every other game. It's the same story with the 71,678,126,387 cars you can buy in the game. They're completely pointless when it comes to progression! The same goes for skill trees and special abilities. In the end, they're often just different animations for killing enemies.
And the biggest joke of all is that you're practically invulnerable relatively early in the game. Apart from a few bosses, there are hardly any enemies that pose a real threat to you.
The game has so much potential because of its sheer size. The last thing it needs is more items and flashy animations. The city still feels lifeless!
I consider the story, including all the DLCs, to be one of the greatest things to happen in gaming over the last 10 years. That said, they could easily have made the map one-tenth of its current size without losing much.
Those little side quests kept me busy for weeks even after I'd completed everything else... You drive around for 10 minutes through a landscape where absolutely nothing happens, fire two or three shots at an enemy, and then drive another 10 minutes to your destination just to collect a reward that you have absolutely no use for.

articles.title: CISA Orders Federal Agencies to Patch Exploited Plex2Shell, Siemens, and SiteGuard Flaws
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Tuesday added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, including four vulnerabilities impacting Plex Media Server that's collectively called Plex2Shell.
The vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2026-96652 (CVSS score: 5.3) - Plex Media Server Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability
- CVE-2026-96654 (CVSS score: 6.9) - Plex Media Server improper neutralization of encoded URI schemes in a web page Vulnerability
- CVE-2026-96655 (CVSS score: 5.3) - Plex Media Server Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability
- CVE-2026-96656 (CVSS score: 8.6) - Plex Media Server external control of file name or path Vulnerability
According to security researcher Zach Main, who discovered and reported the vulnerabilities, a remote attacker could chain the four vulnerabilities to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. The issues were addressed in Plex Media Server 1.43.3.10861 released on August 3, 2026.
The addition of the four vulnerabilities to the KEV catalog follows a report from security researcher boredhackerblog, who found that threat actors are weaponizing the flaws to deploy cryptocurrency miners and proxy malware.
CISA has also flagged two other vulnerabilities as actively exploited. One of them is a DLL sideloading vulnerability in Siemens Software Center (CVE-2026-110936, CVSS score: 8.4) that has been abused in ClickFix attacks using a platform called Romulus.
The second security flaw is a command injection bug in EG Secure Solutions SiteGuard Server Edition (CVE-2026-106931, CVSS score: 8.5) that the Japanese company confirmed as being exploited. No additional details related to the exploitation activity are currently available.
CISA is urging Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to apply fixes for CVE-2026-106931, CVE-2026-96656, and CVE-2026-96654 by October 23, 2026, and the rest by November 3, 2026.

articles.title: Nueva herramienta de IA podría predecir supervivencia al cáncer con una selfie del paciente
articles.text:
Un equipo de médicos de Mass General Brigham, sistema de salud académico sin fines de lucro con sede en Massachusetts, desarrolló una herramienta de inteligencia artificial capaz de predecir las probabilidades de supervivencia de un paciente con cáncer a partir de una sola fotografía de su rostro.
El sistema, entrenado con datos de más de 40 millones de imágenes faciales de personas de distintas etnias y edades, representa una de las demostraciones más completas hasta la fecha sobre cómo el análisis de una selfie mediante IA podría ayudar a evaluar la salud de un paciente y orientar su tratamiento médico. Los detalles del hallazgo fueron publicados en la revista Lancet Digital Health.
El modelo calcula la edad biológica y el riesgo de mortalidad
A partir de la misma tecnología, los investigadores desarrollaron dos herramientas complementarias. La primera, denominada FAHR-FaceAge, estima la edad biológica de un paciente, es decir, la edad que aparenta tener según su rostro, y con ese dato predice su supervivencia frente al cáncer. La segunda, FAHR-FaceSurvival, predice directamente la supervivencia a partir de la fotografía facial, sin pasar por el cálculo intermedio de la edad biológica.
Aunque ambos algoritmos derivan del mismo modelo base, capturan información distinta y complementaria sobre el estado de salud del paciente. Cada uno analiza, además, zonas diferentes del rostro para realizar sus predicciones.
FAHR-FaceAge se centra en los surcos que van desde los costados de la nariz hasta las comisuras de la boca, la zona de la frente justo encima de las cuencas oculares y las sienes. FAHR-FaceSurvival, en cambio, evalúa la región debajo de los ojos y alrededor del puente nasal.
“FAHR-FaceSurvival avanza un paso más en el campo del reconocimiento facial de salud mediante IA, al aprender el riesgo de supervivencia directamente de fotografías faciales de pacientes con cáncer”, explicó Hugo Aerts, coautor principal del estudio, citado por The Guardian.
“Hasta donde sabemos, esta es la primera demostración de que un modelo de IA puede predecir directamente la supervivencia al cáncer a partir de una simple fotografía”, agregó.
Los pacientes que aparentan más edad enfrentan mayor riesgo
Entre los pacientes con cáncer tratados con radioterapia en Estados Unidos, quienes, según FAHR-FaceAge, aparentaban cinco años o más de los que realmente tenían, registraron un riesgo de morir un 21% más alto durante el período de seguimiento, que tuvo una duración promedio de cuatro años. En el extremo opuesto, los pacientes que aparentaban cinco años o más por debajo de su edad real mostraron un riesgo de mortalidad un 17% menor.
Según Aerts, el avance técnico central del sistema radica en que FAHR-Face aprende una representación general del rostro a partir de más de 40 millones de imágenes, que luego puede adaptarse a distintos resultados de salud, como la edad biológica y la supervivencia. “Este enfoque de modelo fundacional nos da una forma escalable de desarrollar múltiples biomarcadores faciales de salud, en lugar de entrenar cada modelo desde cero”, señaló el investigador.
Los resultados del estudio sugieren que las estimaciones de edad biológica de las personas están estrechamente vinculadas con su estado físico, lo que podría reflejar su capacidad para tolerar determinados tratamientos.
El hábito de fumar y el consumo de alcohol aceleran el envejecimiento facial detectado por la IA
Los investigadores hallaron que ciertos factores de estilo de vida se asocian con un envejecimiento facial más marcado según el análisis de la IA. El consumo elevado de alcohol, el uso de drogas y el tabaquismo se vincularon con una apariencia biológicamente más envejecida en las fotografías faciales analizadas por el sistema.
Raymond Mak, oncólogo radioterápico de Mass General Brigham, destacó que, a medida que la población envejece, los médicos necesitan mejores formas de estimar la reserva física y la fragilidad de un paciente antes de recomendar tratamientos intensivos como radioterapia, cirugía o terapia sistémica.
“Nuestro objetivo es hacer que la evaluación de salud basada en fotografías faciales sea más cuantitativa, consistente y escalable, de modo que pueda respaldar decisiones de tratamiento personalizadas, sin reemplazar el criterio médico”, afirmó.
Mak también señaló otro hallazgo inesperado: la consistencia de FAHR-FaceAge frente a variaciones habituales en las fotografías del mundo real, como la pose, la iluminación, la expresión facial y el maquillaje. El sistema se mantuvo estable incluso tras la mayoría de los procedimientos de cirugía plástica evaluados, con la excepción de un pequeño cambio observado después de una rinoplastia.
La herramienta podría facilitar decisiones médicas difíciles sobre el mejor camino terapéutico para los pacientes con cáncer y contribuir a predecir con mayor precisión el riesgo de muerte o de complicaciones tras una cirugía mayor u otros tratamientos oncológicos.
No obstante, los médicos que participaron en la investigación advirtieron que, si bien una sola fotografía facial podría ofrecer una vía sencilla y de bajo costo para respaldar decisiones de tratamiento personalizadas, se requiere más investigación antes de que la herramienta pueda emplearse de forma generalizada.

articles.title: When technology becomes part of the talent infrastructure
articles.text:
When technology becomes part of the talent infrastructure
AI-ready devices make workplace technology a talent advantage
Businesses invest heavily in attracting, developing and retaining talent. At the same time, many continue to view workplace technology primarily through the lens of procurement cycles, standardization and cost. Yet the technology employees use every day shapes how they experience the business and how effectively they can contribute.
As AI becomes embedded in everyday work, that connection becomes even more important. The organizations that realize the greatest value from AI will not simply introduce new tools. They will ensure employees have the technology, support and confidence to use them effectively.
CSG Director at Dell Technologies, UK.
The employee experience starts with technology
When workplace technology works well, it is largely invisible. When it does not, the effects are felt in everyday moments: a video call that starts late because something will not connect, a laptop that struggles through a day of meetings, or a workspace setup that is inconsistent from one location to the next. Individually, these are minor frustrations. Collectively, they influence productivity, engagement and perceptions of the workplace over time.
Employees do not judge technology by specifications or refresh cycles. Increasingly, they judge employers by the quality of the digital experience they provide and whether they can work without friction. As a result, organizations are increasingly looking beyond individual devices and considering the broader technology environment.
The PC, display, peripherals and collaboration tools all contribute to the employee experience, shaping how effectively people can collaborate, stay productive and adapt to changing business needs.
From access to enablement
This conversation is becoming more significant as AI moves from experimentation into everyday workflows. As these capabilities become more commonplace, organizations are recognizing that successful AI adoption depends on more than simply providing access to new tools. It requires the surrounding systems, processes and technology environments that enable employees to use them effectively.
This challenge is reflected in Microsoft's 2026 Work Trend Index, which highlights a growing "Transformation Paradox": employees are increasingly ready to work with AI tools, while many organizations are still adapting their systems, processes and operating models to fully support them.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
While AI is often discussed in terms of applications and platforms, employees experience it through the devices they use every day. For most employees, the PC remains the primary workspace: the place where meetings happen, content is created, decisions are made and work gets done. As AI is embedded in everyday business applications, the role of the PC is evolving.
It is no longer simply a gateway to information or a communication tool. Increasingly, it is becoming a platform through which employees interact with AI-powered capabilities as part of their daily work.
As these capabilities become embedded into everyday workflows, employees can spend less time summarizing meetings, searching for information or completing repetitive administrative tasks and more time on work that requires judgement, creativity and human interaction. The outcome is not simply productivity in the traditional sense. It is a better day-to-day experience of work.
The technology behind workforce readiness
Workforce readiness increasingly depends on whether employees have the tools and support required to make effective use of emerging capabilities. This is where device strategy becomes increasingly important. Ageing technology rarely creates a single catastrophic failure. More often, it limits potential through delays, workarounds and interruptions that make it harder for employees to take full advantage of new ways of working.
At the same time, AI is raising expectations about what employees should be able to accomplish. If organizations want people to embrace new ways of working, they need to consider whether the technology environment supporting them is fit for that purpose. That means looking beyond refresh schedules alone and considering the broader role workplace technology plays in enabling productivity and workforce readiness.
Why device strategy is becoming talent strategy
Organizations do not build successful workplaces through technology alone. Yet it is becoming increasingly difficult to separate workforce outcomes from the technology environment that supports them.
That is why the conversation around AI PCs is expanding beyond IT and procurement to include HR and business leaders. As organizations look for ways to improve employee experience, strengthen productivity and prepare people for AI-enabled work, device strategy is becoming part of a broader talent conversation.
In the past, technology was viewed as infrastructure that supported work. In the AI era, it is increasingly becoming infrastructure that supports talent. Organizations that recognize technology as part of their talent infrastructure will be better positioned to attract, empower and retain the people they need to succeed.

articles.title: Egyptian proptech Aqar Exit attracts investment at $2 million valuation
articles.text: Egypt-based proptech startup Aqar Exit has secured a $200,000 (EGP 10 million) investment from businessman Ayman Mamdouh Abbas, executive chairman of Intro Holding Group, in exchange for a 10% stake, valuing the company at approximately $2 million (EGP 100 million). Founded in July 2026 by Mahmoud Ammar, Aqar Exit operates a real estate platform that enables property buyers struggling with instalment payments to transfer their purchase contracts to new buyers, allowing sellers to recover payments and buyers to access units at their original contract prices. Since its launch, the company has reported EGP 9 billion in closed listings across 638 transactions, including 404 in its most recent reported month. However, its definition of closed transactions includes listings removed from the platform, rather than necessarily completed sales. The investment will support the launch of new products and expansion into international markets, particularly the Gulf region. Aqar Exit is targeting a $5 million funding round in 2027, with plans to attract local and international investors to support its regional growth. Press release: Egyptian proptech startup Aqar Exit has secured an investment of EGP 10 million (approximately $200,000) from businessman Ayman Mamdouh Abbas, executive chairman of Intro Holding Group, in exchange for a 10% stake in the company. The transaction values Aqar Exit at EGP 100 million (approximately $2 million) on a post-money basis, according to founder and chairman Mahmoud Ammar, who disclosed the investment in an interview with Al Arabiya Business. Founded in July 2026, Aqar Exit operates a platform for transferring property purchase contracts, targeting buyers who are struggling to meet instalment obligations on their real estate units. The platform connects these sellers with prospective buyers seeking properties at their original contract prices, without paying additional premiums, commonly known in Egypt's property market as overprice. Under the company's model, sellers can seek to recover the amounts they have already paid towards their properties without incurring contract assignment fees. The investment follows Aqar Exit's participation in the fifth season of Shark Tank Egypt, where it presented its business model to investors. According to Ammar, the company will use the new capital to develop additional products and support its expansion into international markets, with a particular focus on the Gulf. Aqar Exit has reported EGP 9 billion in closed listings since launching, covering 638 transactions, including 404 in its most recent reported month, compared with 233 in the preceding month. However, the company's definition of a closed transaction includes any listing removed from the platform, meaning the figures do not necessarily represent completed property sales or revenue generated by Aqar Exit. The platform has also registered 14,845 property assignment files submitted by 11,833 sellers, alongside 67,013 purchase requests from 32,870 prospective buyers. Average daily purchase requests increased by 58% to 1,060, from 671 in the preceding period, according to company figures. Looking ahead, Aqar Exit plans to pursue a funding round of approximately $5 million in 2027, targeting participation from Egyptian and international investors, businesspeople and investment funds. The planned financing would support the company's product development and regional expansion as it seeks to establish a broader market for transferring property purchase contracts.

articles.title: AWOL Vision Opens Pre-Orders for LuxVision: World's First Optical-Shift 4K 120Hz Projector
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
AWOL Vision Opens Pre-Orders for LuxVision: World's First Optical-Shift 4K 120Hz Projector
AWOL Vision, a global home entertainment brand delivering immersive audiovisual experiences through large-format displays, home cinema technology, and connected entertainment, announced that the AWOL LuxVision, first unveiled at IFA 2026, is now officially available for pre-order. Customers can reserve LuxVision with a $100 / €100 / £100 deposit to unlock exclusive Super Early Bird Benefits ahead of its official launch.
This world's first UST projector with optional lens shift is designed to adapt to the changing ways people use their big screens, delivering a tailored experience for every scenario. The big screen is no longer just for movie nights. Gaming is moving toward higher frame rates, sports fans are following multiple live events at once, and home theaters are becoming a more integrated part of everyday living spaces.Built for Every Big Screen Moment
Today's gamers expect a big screen to be just as fast and responsive as the games they play. Size alone isn't enough when the experience can't keep pace with the action. LuxVision delivers 4K at 120 Hz from input to output, bringing sharper, smoother motion to the giant screen. With 1 ms input lag at 4K 120 Hz, VRR and ALLM, gameplay stays fast and responsive. 6,000 ISO lumens help maintain vivid images even in real-home lighting, while Dolby Vision Gaming further enhances compatible titles. Together, these features bring the high refresh rates, brightness and low latency of modern gaming to a truly cinematic scale.
Bringing that big screen experience home means making it work with the space you already have. Lens shift has long given long-throw projectors more flexibility in installation, but UST owners haven't had the same option. LuxVision changes that with the industry's first vertical lens shift for UST, allowing users to move the image vertically within a 142-152% offset range without cropping, scaling, or sacrificing true 4K detail. This makes it easier to install, fine-tune, or upgrade a UST setup without having to reposition the screen or replace existing furniture. Combined with its 0.18:1 ultra-short-throw ratio, LuxVision can project a 120-inch image from just 7.5 inches away, bringing a giant screen into the room while taking up remarkably little space.
And all that big screen can do more than show one thing at a time. For sports fans, that means no longer having to choose between games when several big matchups are happening at once. With LuxVision's optional Multiview upgrade, users can connect multiple wired and wireless sources and enjoy up to four views simultaneously on one massive screen. Viewers can keep the main event front and center while following other matchups and key moments at the same time, turning the screen into a complete game-day hub.
Behind all of these experiences is AWOL's flagship imaging platform. LuxVision features an RGB triple-laser light source covering 110% of Rec 2020, along with a 10,000:1 native contrast ratio with IRIS, seven-level Dynamic IRIS and Enhanced Black Level (EBL) technology. It also supports Dolby Vision, HDR10+ and IMAX Enhanced. Anti-RBE Technology II is designed to reduce rainbow artifacts during both 2D and 3D viewing.
Price and Availability
LuxVision is available for reservation from September 14 through November 2 on AWOL's official website. Customers who place a $100, €100, or £100 deposit can lock in the LuxVision Cinema System Launch Offer, which includes the LuxVision Cinema System and one of two eligible screen options: a 100"-150" New Gen Fresnel ALR Screen ($999-$4,999) or a 100"-120" New Gen Floor-Rising ALR Screen ($1,999-$2,999). 
LuxVision will officially launch on November 3, with an MSRP of $5,999 / €5,999 / £4,999. 
LuxVision is offered in three standard finishes: Eclipse Platinum, Boreal Oak, and Champagne Walnut. Customers may also choose a Custom CMF (Color, Material, and Finish) option for an additional $1,000 or add 4-channel HDMI Multiview for an additional $500.

articles.title: Hackers Hid Vasilek Backdoor in VMware Tools During 2-Year Russian Healthcare Intrusion
articles.text:
A Belarus-aligned hacktivist group spent nearly two years within the network of a Russian healthcare organization.
According to a report published by Russian cybersecurity firm Solar, the activity has been attributed to a threat cluster dubbed Partisan Zmiy, which is also known as the Cyber Partisans.
Known to be active since at least 2020, the group has a track record of striking industrial enterprises and government agencies in Russia and Belarus with a backdoor called Vasilek that uses Telegram for command-and-control (C2) and data exfiltration.
Some of the attacks have also leveraged phishing lures to deliver an installer that simultaneously deploys the legitimate FortiClient VPN program on the system as well as an open-source program known as DNSCat2 that allows attackers to gain control of the infected host.
A notable aspect of the threat actor is their ability to stage destructive attacks with a wiper referred to as Pryanik, alongside taking steps to systematically clear Windows event logs using a utility dubbed Evlx.
The Rostelecom subsidiary said it discovered the intrusion in December 2025, although evidence suggests that the earliest signs of compromise date back to early 2024. The name of the targeted organization was not identified. The exact initial access vector used to breach the entity is also not known.
Unlike other attacks linked to Cyber Partisans, the threat actors remained on the network for an extended period of time without carrying out any destructive activity, marking something of a shift in modus operandi.
"The attacked organization possessed an extensive infrastructure and two-way trusted relationships with numerous subsidiary medical institutions," Solar said. "We hypothesize that the lack of infrastructure disruption is due precisely to the value of this access for further espionage and trusted relationship attacks."
Observed as part of the intrusion is a loader-scheduler service ("vmauad") that masquerades as a legitimate VMware component to maintain persistence and evade cursory inspection. To accomplish this, the attackers are said to have taken advantage of a trusted-but-unmonitored VMware Tools directory location to plant malicious executables or replace legitimate VMware DLLs with a malicious version ("vmtools.dll") containing the backdoor.
The primary responsibility of the Windows service is to launch the rogue binary "C:\Program Files\VMware\VMware Tools\authd.exe" that, besides launching a GOST tunnel every Saturday from 10 p.m. to 11 p.m., runs an updated version of Vasilek (version 1.5.8) once, eight hours after the service begins.
Once installed, Vasilek is equipped to collect information about an infected computer, execute Windows commands, launch and terminate processes, transfer files, capture screenshots, record keystrokes, and escalate privileges via runas. It can also prevent the machine from going into sleep mode, and update or remove itself.
One new addition is the "move_cursor" command that, as the name implies, allows the backdoor to move the cursor and simulate user input on the victim's screen.
"The group consistently invests in stealth and operational security, rather than new capabilities: hostname binding in two independent components, nightly scheduled payload launches, system proxy inheritance, disguise as legitimately installed but unused software, file rotation across the same paths, time-stomping, outgoing message suppression, and anonymous messages on behalf of the group in operator chats," Solar said.
"The backdoor's feature set has remained largely unchanged over four revisions. Due to Telegram being blocked in Russia by ISPs, communication between the Vasilek backdoor and C2 has become unstable."
The disclosure comes as Solar also disclosed details of a phishing campaign that employs JavaScript attachments mimicking business-themed documents, such as payments and purchase orders, to deliver a previously unreported malware family known as HypeAgent.
The Windows malware is a full-featured trojan designed to take complete control over infected systems, packing the ability to steal files, open a console, change desktop wallpaper, turn on a webcam, log keystrokes, launch hidden VNC and RDP sessions, control the mouse, and even deploy a cryptocurrency miner.
It's also capable of stealing cookies associated with Discord, Steam, GitHub, Instagram, Telegram, Binance, ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor, and tampering with the installed Exodus wallet app to inject JavaScript that can collect the victim's password, PIN, mnemonic phrase, and private key.
Earlier this June, Solar also observed legitimate infrastructure compromised by the ProxyCB proxyware botnet malware making automated requests to Russian websites and online platforms, while identifying possible overlaps between the botnet infrastructure and historical activity linked to TeamSpy, a threat cluster known for abusing TeamViewer to facilitate reconnaissance and data theft.
Last month, the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) charged Searzhudin Tamirlanovich Aktulaev, a 40-year-old Russian national extradited from Cyprus in May 2025, for exploiting an online messaging service of a well-known freelance employment platform to send malware-laced Excel attachments to about 80,000 of its users in 2016 and 2017 using 255 fake accounts.
The attacks led to the deployment of two types of malware, a variant of the TVRAT (aka Sheldor, SpyAgent, TeamBot, TeamSpy, and TVSPY) and DarkVNC, to harvest and send data from a victim computer to a remote server under the attacker's control. Thousands of computers are assessed to have been infected as a result of this scheme.

articles.title: Anthropic pidió al Congreso de EEUU una ley de IA que solo actúa si hay 50 muertes en juego
articles.text:
Anthropic, la empresa detrás del chatbot Claude, confirmó que está promoviendo entre legisladores de Estados Unidos un proyecto de ley de seguridad de inteligencia artificial que solo permitiría al gobierno bloquear el lanzamiento de un modelo si existe un riesgo inminente de matar a más de 50 personas o provocar más de 1.000 millones de dólares en daños.
El medio Politico reveló el borrador, y un vocero de Anthropic confirmó su existencia. Según personas que leyeron el texto, la propuesta solo activaría ese bloqueo si el riesgo proviene de la creación de un arma biológica, de que el modelo escape al control de sus desarrolladores o de un ciberataque.
El mecanismo previsto funciona así: evaluadores independientes, registrados ante el Departamento de Comercio, revisarían periódicamente a los laboratorios de IA y a sus modelos más avanzados. Esos evaluadores podrían recibir pago de las propias empresas que inspeccionan, siempre que el monto no dependa del resultado de la evaluación.
Si un evaluador detecta un riesgo catastrófico inminente, debe avisar al Departamento de Comercio dentro de las 72 horas. Recién entonces esa oficina podría pedirle a un juez federal en Washington que frene la distribución del modelo. Ningún otro organismo del gobierno tendría poder para actuar por su cuenta.
Los umbrales de 50 muertes y 1.000 millones de dólares replican los que ya exige la ley de seguridad de IA de California, conocida como SB 53, aprobada en 2025. “Este proyecto representa las propuestas de nuestro Marco de IA Avanzada, que venimos impulsando ante legisladores federales y estatales desde junio”, dijo el vocero de Anthropic a Politico.
SB 53 (abreviatura de Senate Bill 53, denominada formalmente Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act) es una ley de seguridad y transparencia para la IA avanzada aprobada en California. Su filosofía parte de que es prácticamente imposible predecir con certeza absoluta cada fallo, pero que la forma de proteger al público y a la vida humana es exigiendo transparencia total, auditorías obligatorias, rendición de cuentas y la obligación de reportar cualquier falla grave de seguridad.
Especialistas en seguridad acusan a Anthropic de retroceder
La reacción de especialistas en seguridad de IA fue dura. Nathan Calvin, de la organización Encode, escribió que aprobar el proyecto “nos dejaría menos protegidos frente a riesgos catastróficos que con la ley actual”, porque el juez solo estaría obligado a sopesar el daño que sufriría la empresa desarrolladora, no el daño al público de no frenar un modelo peligroso.
Calvin también objetó que el proyecto anularía leyes estatales como la SB 53 de California y le quitaría a los estados la capacidad de ordenar por su cuenta la suspensión de un modelo. Ketan Ramakrishnan, investigador de políticas de IA, calificó la propuesta de Anthropic como “asombrosamente mala”.
Scott Wiener, el senador estatal de California que redactó la SB 53, cuestionó si el borrador cumple con el propio estándar que Anthropic se había fijado: la empresa había dicho en junio que solo aceptaría que una ley federal reemplace a las estatales si esa ley nueva era “al menos tan fuerte” como su propio marco de seguridad.
Anthropic promete reescribir partes del texto
El 18 de octubre, Anthony Cimino, jefe de asuntos federales de Anthropic, respondió a las críticas en una publicación en la red social X. Reconoció que la empresa reescribirá la sección sobre anulación de leyes estatales para que los estados conserven un papel en los estándares de los evaluadores independientes y en la regulación de cómo se apaga un modelo.
Cimino también admitió que “probablemente sea momento” de revisar el umbral de 50 muertes, aunque defendió mantener un estándar judicial para bloquear un modelo: la medida es tan drástica, dijo, que necesita un control contra el abuso, pero “la barra no puede ser tan alta que el poder nunca llegue a usarse”.
El episodio ocurre semanas después de que el propio director ejecutivo de Anthropic, Dario Amodei, pidiera en septiembre que toda la industria de IA frenara el ritmo de desarrollo de sus modelos, al advertir que un grupo de agentes de IA podría tomar el control de “todo internet” en un plazo de seis a doce meses.
El proyecto de Anthropic compite además con la ley FRONTIER, presentada en julio por los representantes Lori Trahan y Jay Obernolte, que varios especialistas consideran más estricta. Chris Lehane, jefe de asuntos globales de OpenAI, publicó una respuesta que pareció apuntar a Anthropic: “ninguna empresa, incluida OpenAI, debería escribir sola las reglas de una tecnología con implicancias tan profundas para la sociedad”.
Cimino no dio una fecha para publicar la nueva versión del texto. El Congreso de Estados Unidos, además, está en receso hasta después de las elecciones legislativas de noviembre, lo que deja en pausa cualquier avance formal del proyecto mientras Anthropic revisa sus términos.

articles.title: Stop choosing the wrong Agentic AI use cases
articles.text:
Stop choosing the wrong Agentic AI use cases
Choose agentic AI use cases by measurable business value
Psychologist Abraham Maslow once warned: “It is tempting, if the only tool you have is a hammer, to treat everything as if it were a nail.” Agentic AI is becoming the enterprise version of that hammer.
Once people understand what agentic AI can do, the list of possible use cases grows quickly.
VP of AI transformation at Atos.
While that enthusiasm should be applauded, it can lead to strategies that are back to front “If AI is the answer, what’s the question?” By the time it comes to looking at results and whether the investment in AI has been fruitful, it’s hard to identify what’s been achieved and why achieving it was important in the first place.
Start with the value, not the agent
In the rush that followed ChatGPT, many organizations deployed AI tools to their workforces at large with no defined value or end goal. People started working differently almost immediately, but with no baseline captured, there was no way to know what had actually improved. Who knows how long it takes to write a coherent email and who knows what time is saved by having ChatGPT rephrase it for you!
This is what McKinsey calls the “gen AI paradox”. Its 2025 survey found just 39% of organizations reported any enterprise-level financial impact from their AI investment, despite mass adoption.
Organizations need to be precise about what they want to measure. There are three layers to this and most only capture the first.
- Adoption: are people using it?
- Behavior: are people doing their jobs differently?
- Outcome: revenue per salesperson, tickets closed per engineer, cycle time on a review gate.
Adoption and outcome together show a correlation; for example, people who use AI sell more. But it’s the, often missed, behavior layer in the middle that turns that correlation into causation, i.e. they sell more because they are now able to use AI to fill in more client reports, leaving more time to hit the phones.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Know your workflow
If organizations can’t see how work is really being done, two things happen. The baseline measures the wrong process, making any claimed improvement meaningless and an agent given the wrong steps cannot complete the job.
One procurement process at Atos looked like a four-step workflow on paper, but when we looked carefully and asked those doing it, it was closer to 10. People moved between Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), Outlook and spreadsheets, copying information, waiting for replies and re-entering data manually.
A baseline on four steps would have measured the wrong process and an agent given four steps couldn’t have completed a job that takes ten.
Not every problem needs an agent
Understanding the workflow also shows whether agentic AI is the right technology at all. If tasks follow fixed rules “if this happens, do that” the answer may be Robotic Process Automation (RPA), workflow automation or a process change.
Agentic AI is better suited to workflows where the system needs to interpret context, coordinate across tools, make recommendations or act within defined boundaries. Even then, it needs a clear measure of success and a credible business case. The economics of deploying Agentic AI are still in infancy, but this will act as a natural filter for only the most valuable cases.
Prove the value before building
Value is where the tough work of a clear business case comes in. Proving the value of Agentifying a process before any code is written.
This requires access to good data sets. Evidence on cost and business value before introducing Agentic AI is needed before budget is committed. Where the benefits are measurable and enough open data exists, it’s possible to build something real in a week. Where the data still requires work, it is always worth refining the data you have before attempting to justify a business case.
Work managed upfront will save cost and time and give you evidence of value.
Build a portfolio, not a queue
Once there is a shortlist of use cases, organizations can prioritize against financial impact, feasibility, process impact, technology requirements, human impact and risk. Scoring across multiple factors rather than ranking on ROI alone creates a portfolio instead of a queue. A lower-value use case with fast impact might prove value early and build credibility for agents that follow. A high-value use case with a two-year runway may need to wait.
Budget for a new mortgage
Even once the right case has been selected, many organizations still struggle to see impact because they focus on the build, then under-resource the work needed to make the change land.
Gartner calls this a “transition mortgage”, where AI adoption demands more support than traditional technology, often requiring 25% more training effort and up to 200% additional change management.
In our own organization, we were guilty of building independent tools in different regions and teams to solve the same business problem. We have now established clearer oversight of our use cases. The issue was not the quality of the tools, but duplicated effort, cost and resources.
Not every workflow needs a hammer
C-suite leaders should start with fewer use cases where the value and workflows are clear, the baseline is measurable, the data is available and the role of the agent is well defined. Then they should budget for communications, adoption, measurement and scale.
The value from agentic AI is not measured by the number of agents an organization deploys. It is measured by whether the work changed and whether the organization can prove it. Agentic AI is a powerful hammer, but success lies in understanding which problems are nails and which are not.

articles.title: Orange et Sosh en panne : le réseau mobile disparaît chez de nombreux abonnés
articles.text:
Décidément, après Revolut hier, c’est au tour d’Orange aujourd’hui. Une panne perturbe les services mobiles de l’opérateur et de Sosh ce mercredi 21 octobre en fin de matinée. Des abonnés rapportent une perte complète de réseau dans de nombreuses régions, avec, à l'heure d'écrire ces lignes, plus de 11 000 signalements sur DownDetector.
Mise à jour du 21/10 à 12 h 30 : Orange a reconnu les perturbations dans un message publié sur X : « Vous pouvez rencontrer actuellement des perturbations sur le réseau mobile Orange. Nos équipes sont pleinement mobilisées pour rétablir le réseau dans les meilleurs délais. »
Vous êtes concerné par cette panne ? N’hésitez pas à nous indiquer dans les commentaires votre ville, votre opérateur et les difficultés rencontrées : appels, SMS ou Internet mobile. Merci pour vos témoignages, qui nous aident à suivre l’évolution de la situation.
Plus de signal, plus de connexion Internet mobile, un téléphone qui affiche « aucun service » : les témoignages se multiplient autour de midi. Les remontées concernent des villes éloignées les unes des autres, de Paris à Toulouse, en passant par Lyon, Strasbourg ou Bordeaux. Elles dessinent un incident qui dépasse largement le cadre d’une antenne locale, même si son périmètre exact reste à préciser.
Des pertes de réseau signalées dans de nombreuses régions
De nombreux commentaires d'utilisateurs publiés en cette fin de matinée décrivent les difficultés à joindre le réseau d'Orange. « Plus de réseau à Clermont-Ferrand », écrit un utilisateur. « Coupure réseau mobile Orange à Paris », rapporte un autre. Des messages évoquent également des interruptions à Lille, Nice, Grenoble, Rouen, Orléans, Poitiers, Limoges, Biarritz ou encore Saint-Brieuc.
Certains abonnés décrivent des conséquences immédiates sur leur activité. À Saint-Genis-Laval, près de Lyon, une utilisatrice signale une box sans connexion et un téléphone hors réseau : « Impossible de travailler, très pénible ». À Strasbourg, un autre commentaire mentionne une perte de réseau sur le téléphone et une box 5G.
Ces témoignages rejoignent les indicateurs de Downdetector et Sosh apparaît également en difficulté.
Une origine et un délai de rétablissement encore inconnus
À l’heure de notre rédaction,Orange n'a pas encore communiqué sur les causes de ces perturbations ou un horaire de retour à la normale.
La météo officielle du réseau mobile ne nous a pas davantage permis d’obtenir un diagnostic : sa consultation nous a uniquement renvoyé la mention « Chargement en cours », avec une page qui tourne dans le vide. 
Les témoignages concernent principalement le réseau mobile. Les mentions de connexions Internet ou de box interrompues doivent être distinguées : une box 5G utilise elle aussi ce réseau. Elles ne suffisent donc pas à confirmer une panne générale de la fibre ou de l’ADSL.
Reste désormais à connaître l’étendue précise de l’incident, les services concernés et le délai nécessaire pour rétablir les communications des abonnés touchés.

articles.title: Warframe Alters Gameplay Metas Again with Riven Mod Rework and End of Infinite Ammo Builds
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Warframe Alters Gameplay Metas Again with Riven Mod Rework and End of Infinite Ammo Builds
When Digital Extremes introduced the powerful Riven mods system, the weapon-specific mods all had dispositions that would be adjusted quarterly as a balance for the resulting high damage output and subsequent popularity of specific weapons due to Riven mods, and the Riven system has seen a number of changes and reworks since it launched, mostly in an attempt to encourage build diversity and experimentation. However, metas have still emerged in the game, many of which came as a direct result of Riven mods. Now, Digital Extremes has decided to rework the Riven system again, doing away with Riven disposition entirely and capping ammo efficiency, resulting in what appears to be a more easily manageable and understandable system that should again encourage build diversity and be more new-player-friendly, to boot. 
The high-level overview of the change is that, with a few temporary exceptions, ammo efficiency will be capped at 75%, meaning the best-case scenario is that a weapon will only consume one ammo every four shots, and Riven mods will all be reset to new base values that would represent a disposition of 1.2 in the outgoing system. This means that all new weapons will start out with powerful mods available from the get-go, and existing Rivens may see significant swings in viability in the game. These changes will be introduced in an October 22 update, and Digital Extremes has also said that it will provide all Warframe players with an inbox reward in order to offset whatever impact this may have on builds that relied on those mods for high damage output. Players who used the Riven Splicers and Trait locking that was introduced earlier in 2026 will receive double the rewards as a thanks for testing the new system.The full write-up with the technical details of Warframe's new Riven mod changes and a full list of affected Riven mods, with their new stats, has been posted to r/ Warframe on Reddit. 
The game studio says that these changes have been implemented with the following goals in mind:
- Brand new weapons will have powerful Rivens available on day one
- All Rivens are guaranteed to offer a noticeable boost, including those for your favorite powerful weapons
- No more constant adjustments—your Rivens will not change unless you change them through rerolling
- All weapons get equal treatment, giving us more control when balancing old and new weapons
- Simplified system by removing Disposition as a factor when comparing and evaluating Rivens
Source:
				Digital Extremes on Reddit
