articles.title: Eight eMudhra CA Keys Compromised, Triggering Emergency Fixes Across Browsers and Software
articles.text:
The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority (CA) certificates are compromised, Mozilla and Google's Chrome Root Program confirms on October 20.
An intermediate CA signs the certificates that websites present, so anyone holding one of these keys could issue a certificate for any website that a browser would accept.
A researcher reported the compromise to the root programs on the evening of October 17, and Chrome and Firefox blocked the eight certificates within hours, after Chrome verified the findings.
No TLS certificate chaining to the six intermediates used for websites had been logged to Certificate Transparency (CT) before Chrome's block, so none could have been trusted by default in Chrome or any other browser that requires CT logging, the Chrome Root Program said.
The keys did not have to be stolen. They were generated with too little randomness, so anyone can compute them from the public certificates, Google's security teams said on October 20. eMudhra said on October 21 that a flaw in the April 2025 ceremony that created the certificates produced a second, weak set of keys alongside the intended ones, and that the weak set is what was published to the browser root stores.
Mozilla recovered the keys on its own within two hours of receiving the report, and researchers have since published them. Whether anyone exploited the flaw since the certificates were created is not known.
The keys are the ones Go blocked in its October 20 security releases without naming the CA, as The Hacker News reported earlier. The eight hash values in Go's code match the eight certificates. Go handled the fix on its URGENT track, which its security policy reserves for threats to the ecosystem's integrity or flaws being exploited in the wild, and neither the issue nor the release notes say which applied.
What Was Compromised
eMudhra is an Indian CA that sells certificates under the emSign brand through companies in India, the United States, and the Netherlands, and it has roots in the Mozilla, Chrome, and Apple root stores. The eight compromised certificates are:
- TLS, domain validated: EM DV TLS CA - G3B (eMudhra BV, Netherlands) and EM DV TLS CA - G3C (eMudhra Inc, United States)
- TLS, organization validated: EM OV TLS CA - G3B and EM OV TLS CA - G3C
- TLS, extended validation: EM EV TLS CA - G3B and EM EV TLS CA - G3C
- Code signing: EM OV CS CA - G3B and EM OV CS CA - G3C
The six TLS certificates were issued by emSign Root TLS CA - G3 and chain to emSign ECC Root CA - G3, a root in the Chrome and Apple stores and, until October 20, in Mozilla's.
Each of the eight also exists as a second certificate with the same public key, cross-signed by Sectigo under its AAA Certificate Services root, according to a certificate list published by Dennis Jackson, a Mozilla cryptography engineer.
Chrome did not need to block the two code-signing certificates, because its TLS verifier will not build a path through an intermediate restricted to code signing, the Chrome Root Program said.
Who Is Protected, and How
The Chrome Root Program received the report at 18:05 UTC on October 17 and had a CRLSet update blocking the six TLS intermediates in place by 19:45 UTC.
Mozilla received it at 20:06 UTC and finished pushing a OneCRL block to Firefox installations with standard settings at 22:59 UTC. CRLSets and OneCRL are revocation lists that the two browsers fetch on their own, so neither needed an update or a restart.
Chrome's block matches the public key rather than the certificate, so it also catches the Sectigo cross-signed copies. It is the same mechanism Chrome used earlier this month against rogue certificates for Google domains.
The researcher, credited by Mozilla only as Wayne, signed the message "We have a problem here - Wayne" with each of the eight keys and sent it to the root programs that day, according to Jackson, who published the signatures and certificates on a one-page site.
eMudhra has revoked the eight certificates. Apple blocked them on October 19, Microsoft on October 20, and other trust stores were notified on October 19, according to Jackson's site. Android devices received an equivalent block through Google Play Services at about 22:00 UTC on October 19, Google said.
The cross-signed copies did not widen the risk in Chrome or Firefox. Both stopped trusting Sectigo's AAA Certificate Services root for websites in April 2025, and Chrome's root store file does not carry it. Apple's root list for iOS 26 and macOS 26, published in December 2025, includes it.
Mozilla does not believe, for now, that the problem affects other CAs, Jackson wrote on Mozilla's policy list, and Chrome said it checked every other CA certificate in its store and "found no other instances of this failure mode."
What to Update
Browsers get revocation pushed to them. Many other programs that check TLS certificates, from Go binaries to anything using Python's certifi bundle, do not check revocation data and keep trusting a chain until their code or their root bundle changes.
Mozilla's advice to anyone who runs a trust store: nothing is needed where clients reliably check revocation and refuse connections when they cannot check, the eight intermediates should be blocked now where the software can block individual intermediates; and otherwise the operator should consider removing trust in the roots that signed them.
The fixes published so far, and what each one does:
| Software | Fixed in | What it does | Status | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Go | 1.27.3 and 1.26.10 | Rejects any chain containing one of the eight keys (CVE-2026-111943) | Released October 20, rebuild required | 
| Firefox | 158.0.1 , ESR 115.43.1 and ESR 153.5.1 | Carries the OneCRL block for installations that cannot receive Remote Settings ( CVE-2026-113470 ) | Released October 20 | 
| NSS | 3.131.1 | Removes emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from the trusted list | Released October 20 | 
| Python certifi | 2026.10.19 | Drops emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from the bundle | Released | 
| Rust webpki-roots | 1.0.10 | Drops emSign ECC Root CA - G3 | Released | 
| Homebrew ca-certificates | 2026-09-25_1 | Excludes emSign ECC Root CA - G3, emSign Root TLS CA - G3 and AAA Certificate Services by public key | Released | 
| Node.js | None yet | A draft change would block the eight keys | Pending | 
| Composer ca-bundle | 1.6.0 and 1.4.16 | Distrusts the eight compromised intermediates and refreshes its bundled root list | Released October 20 | 
Go's filter sits in the standard library and rejects any chain containing one of the eight keys, on Go's own verifier and on the macOS and Windows system-verifier paths, and the change adds no setting to turn it off. A program picks it up only when rebuilt with the new release; Go 1.25 and older are out of support and get no fixes.
Three of the fixes work by removing roots rather than blocking the keys. certifi, webpki-roots, and Homebrew's ca-certificates drop emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from their bundles, and Homebrew also drops Sectigo's AAA Certificate Services root and emSign Root TLS CA - G3.
That also cuts off every legitimate certificate that chains to those roots. Mozilla, which made the same change to NSS, said some servers will become unavailable to non-Firefox users of its trust list until those servers move to new certificate chains.
Jackson's site tracks a longer list, including the ca-certificates packages of Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch, Alpine and Gentoo, curl's CA bundle, pip, uv and Electron, with FreeBSD and Bun still pending, and it warns that the curl built into macOS still accepts the chain because it checks against a bundle file that Apple has not updated.
Cloudflare, which learned of the problem on October 19, has released fixed WARP and 1.1.1.1 clients and cloudflared 2026.10.2, and said customers who run their own origin servers, mutual TLS or containers may need to update trust stores themselves.
Firefox needs nothing unless Remote Settings is disabled by policy or blocked on the network. The October 20 releases carry the block list for those installations.
None of the sources provide a way to detect past misuse of the keys beyond Chrome's CT search, which covers only logged certificates.
What Happens to eMudhra
Mozilla removed emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from NSS on October 20. Chrome will remove the same root in version 43 of its root store and is reviewing the status of eMudhra's other root in its store, emSign Root CA - G1, the Chrome Root Program said, citing the seriousness of the incident. The removal is expected to reach every device that relies on the Chrome Root Store on the morning of Tuesday, October 27, Pacific time, and earlier on Chrome Canary and Beta, Google said, so website operators with certificates chaining to that root must install a certificate from another hierarchy before then to avoid breakage. eMudhra has committed to moving those customers off the root, Google said.
Mozilla said it is working with the CA, other root programs and downstream trust stores on the root cause and will post more when it can. eMudhra's trust-services repository carried no notice about the incident as of October 20. The company posted a statement on its corporate site that day and issued a press release on October 21, covered in the update below.
Go has not named the CA on its issue, where its release notes cite "specific security concerns around their operation", and a commenter asked for the hashes in the patch to be explained.
Filippo Valsorda, who maintains the cryptography packages in Go's standard library, replied that the keys are compromised and the certificates revoked, that Linux root stores are too poorly maintained for revocation to reach applications, and that putting the keys in code is the only option for now.
Roland Shoemaker of the Go security team later wrote on the issue that the team learned of the underlying problem on October 19 and kept the release notes deliberately vague, because the flaw was easy to exploit and the team expected it to become public that day. It became widely known only on October 20, he wrote.
Update: eMudhra Blames Flaw in April 2025 Key Ceremony
eMudhra Limited said in a press release filed with the BSE stock exchange on October 21 that the eight intermediates were created under its ECC root in a key generation ceremony on April 30, 2025, using hardware security modules certified to FIPS 140-2 Level 3, and that a flaw in that ceremony caused a key wrap and unwrap step, which packages a key for transfer and unpacks it again, to produce a second set of weak keys alongside the original strong keys. The weak keys were the ones published to the browser root stores, the company said, and it is still working to establish the root cause.
The company said an independent researcher found over the weekend of October 17 that the weak keys could be reverse-engineered, "possibly with AI-assisted techniques", and reported this to Apple, Google, Microsoft and Mozilla.
Scott Helme, a security researcher, wrote that he recovered all eight private keys from the public certificates on his laptop in under a second, that one of them is the number 4 and the rest are also whole numbers below 256, and that an AI agent did the same from a single prompt.
eMudhra said its infrastructure was not compromised, no data was breached and its physical and logical security controls remained intact. It said the roots and issuing CAs had passed independent audits two years in a row and had been in browser trust lists since mid 2025, and that the incident has no connection with its Indian digital signature certificate and eSign businesses, which run on separate infrastructure.
The global TLS business accounts for around 1% of the company's revenue, it said, while acknowledging a reputational risk it cannot quantify. It is giving affected customers replacement certificates and is continuing its root-cause investigation with the root programs.
In the statement on its website, dated October 20, eMudhra said the incident does not affect its root CA private keys or its other intermediate CAs, that only one of the eight intermediates had been deployed in production, and that none of the eight, including that one, had issued any end-entity certificate.
eMudhra's shares fell 20% in Mumbai on October 21, Business Standard reported.
(Corrected on October 21: an earlier version said it was not known how the keys left eMudhra. The keys did not need to leave the company, because they were generated with so little randomness that anyone can compute them from the public certificates. The passages on the cause have been revised.)

articles.title: El ‘modo espía’ de Spotify: aprende a ver la música de tus amigos en tiempo real
articles.text:
Spotify incluye una función conocida popularmente como ‘modo espía’, que en realidad se llama Actividad de tus amigos y permite ver, en tiempo real, qué canción está escuchando cada persona que sigues en la plataforma. No es un truco oculto ni una configuración secreta: es una herramienta oficial de la aplicación que muestra el tema actual o el último reproducido por tus contactos, junto con el tiempo transcurrido desde esa escucha.
Su funcionamiento depende de tres condiciones que deben cumplirse de forma simultánea para que la lista aparezca con información real.
Requisitos para activar el seguimiento entre amigos en Spotify
Lo primero es establecer el vínculo de seguimiento. Para que la actividad de una persona sea visible, es necesario entrar a su perfil dentro de Spotify y presionar el botón de “Seguir”.
Aunque no es obligatorio que la otra persona haga lo mismo, lo ideal es que el seguimiento sea mutuo, porque así ambos perfiles quedan habilitados para intercambiar esta información dentro del panel de actividad.
El segundo requisito depende exclusivamente de la otra persona. En la configuración de su cuenta, debe tener activada la casilla de “Compartir mi actividad de escucha”. Si esa opción está desactivada, o si el usuario decide reproducir música en una sesión privada, no habrá forma de ver qué está escuchando, sin importar que lo sigas o que ambos se sigan mutuamente.
El tercer punto tiene que ver con el dispositivo desde el cual se consulta esa actividad. La lista completa de reproducciones de los amigos solo está disponible de manera nativa en la versión de escritorio de Spotify, es decir, en la aplicación instalada en computadoras con Windows o Mac. Esto convierte al ordenador en el canal principal para acceder a esta función con todas sus posibilidades.
Cómo revisar la actividad de amigos desde la computadora
El proceso en la versión de escritorio es directo. Primero hay que abrir la aplicación de Spotify en la computadora y ubicar, en la barra superior o en el menú de vista, la opción para activar el panel de “Actividad de amigos”. Esta sección suele desplegarse como una barra lateral ubicada a la derecha de la pantalla.
Una vez activado ese panel, se despliega la lista de amigos junto con la canción que están reproduciendo en ese momento o, en caso de no estar conectados en ese instante, la última que escucharon y el tiempo que pasó desde entonces.
Esta vista permite monitorear en paralelo a varias personas sin necesidad de entrar a cada perfil de manera individual, algo que no ocurre en otros formatos de la aplicación.
Es posible ver la actividad musical de amigos desde el celular
A diferencia de la versión de escritorio, la aplicación móvil oficial de Spotify, tanto en Android como en iOS, no incluye una barra lateral que muestre en tiempo real la actividad de todos los amigos a la vez. Esta función está limitada a la versión de computadora.
Sin embargo, existe una alternativa parcial para los usuarios de celular. Ingresar directamente al perfil de Spotify de un amigo puede revelar información útil, siempre que esa persona tenga habilitada la opción de compartir sus artistas más escuchados o sus listas de reproducción.
En ese caso, es posible consultar desde el perfil los “Artistas escuchados recientemente” o acceder a las playlists que haya hecho públicas, aunque sin la actualización instantánea ni el detalle de la canción exacta que sí ofrece el panel de escritorio.

articles.title: Un chien robot pour surveiller les cultures et améliorer les rendements agraires
articles.text:
Un chien robot pour surveiller les cultures et améliorer les rendements agraires
En Espagne, le Centre technologique agroalimentaire d'Estrémadure (CTAEX) teste un robot à quatre pattes bardé de capteurs dans un vignoble de la Ribera del Duero et sous des tunnels de mûres. Il mesure la vigueur des plantes et la maturité des fruits afin d'aider les producteurs à planifier la récolte.
Chez Bodegas Familiares Matarromera, près de Valladolid, les rangs de vigne épousent des coteaux aux sols caillouteux et irréguliers. Un drôle d'arpenteur y fait ses premiers pas, des caméras sur le dos. Le 14 octobre 2026, il trottait également devant la presse sur la parcelle expérimentale du CTAEX, à Villafranco del Guadiana.
Robot AGRHOUND : des pattes plutôt que des roues pour arpenter les vignes
Le projet a été baptisé AGRHOUND, contraction d'agriculture et de hound, le chien de chasse en anglais. Lancé en juin, il réunit le CTAEX, Matarromera, le producteur de fruits rouges Social Berries 4.0, le spécialiste de l'imagerie spectrale SpectralGeo et la société informatique Soltel, avec l'appui de la fondation Prodti. L'Union européenne (via le fonds agricole FEADER) et le ministère espagnol de l'Agriculture assurent son financement. Le modèle exact du robot, lui, n'a pas été dévoilé.
Luis Muñoz, responsable du projet au CTAEX, parle de “mettre des pattes à l'agriculture de précision”. Un quadrupède grimpe les pentes et franchit aisément les sillons irréguliers. Dans la végétation dense, il passe là où un engin à roues peine. Sous les tunnels en plastique de Huelva, le signal GPS passe mal : le robot se repère donc en croisant un LiDAR et des caméras 3D, générant une cartographie en temps réel.
Capteurs et IA : lire la maturité du raisin dans la lumière
Ses capteurs multispectraux et hyperspectraux analysent la lumière renvoyée par les feuilles et les grappes sur bien plus de bandes que les trois couleurs d'une caméra classique. Des modèles d'intelligence artificielle en déduisent la vigueur et l'état hydrique des ceps, ainsi que la teneur des baies en sucres ou en anthocyanes. Grâce à cette estimation de la récolte en amont, le producteur peut organiser la main-d'œuvre et les vendanges, tout en préparant la commercialisation.
Les résultats s'affichent sous forme de cartes au sein d'une application intuitive destinée aux viticulteurs et techniciens. Celles-ci doivent aussi faire apparaître, pour une même parcelle, les zones qui mûrissent le plus vite. Le cépage “tempranillo” part avec une longueur d'avance : selon Luis Muñoz, un algorithme déjà très abouti existait pour cette variété. Pour la mûre, il a fallu presque tout reprendre de zéro.
Objectif 2029 : vers un chien-robot agricole 100 % autonome
Cette première année sert avant tout à collecter des données et à calibrer les algorithmes. Les campagnes de 2027 et 2028 devront ensuite les enrichir en conditions réelles, avant la conclusion du projet prévue début 2029. Viendront par la suite les cartes spectrales instantanées et un robot capable de choisir seul son trajet. L'ajout d'un bras articulé pour prélever des échantillons est également au programme.
“Notre objectif n'est pas de remplacer les professionnels”, insiste Luis Muñoz, qui souhaite avant tout couvrir davantage de parcelles en un minimum de temps. Reste encore à régler des défis très terre à terre : l'autonomie des batteries, la maintenance directement dans les champs, la couverture réseau en zone rurale… et la boue.

articles.title: Foldable phones could be hot – in more ways than one
articles.text:
Foldable phones could be hot – in more ways than one
How foldable phones highlight AI’s growing thermal management challenge
The most fascinating thing about Apple's new iPhone Duo – and others like it – may not be that it folds. It may be the innovation required to keep it cool. Because at a time when performance demands from edge AI continue to increase, we’ve now taken available smartphone real estate and – though not exactly halved it – constrained it more than ever. And that impacts heat. Which impacts performance.
What makes the Duo interesting isn't simply the engineering required to create a folding phone. It's that Apple is confronting the same challenge every edge device manufacturer now faces: AI capability is increasing faster than our ability to manage the heat it generates.
VP and GM of Thermal Management at xMEMS Labs.
That’s why I believe we’re entering a new phase of device innovation, with thermal design increasingly shaping what’s possible. In the edge AI era, managing heat helps determine what a device can do, how long it can sustain performance, and how small or thin it can be.
The iPhone Duo is just the latest reminder that smartphone manufacturers have run into a stubborn engineering problem: How to keep mobile processors cool when there’s almost nowhere left to put a cooling system.
For its part, with the Duo, Apple has packed its A20 Pro and other heat-generating electronics into an exceptionally thin, foldable design. It’s also created a custom vapor chamber to help dissipate heat and sustain performance in the new form factor.
The latter is more than an engineering footnote. It’s a glimpse at a challenge the edge AI industry is starting to confront. Thermal design and industrial design are inseparable. And new solutions to thermal challenges must be considered.
Foldables Make the Challenge Obvious
Foldable phones make the thermal management challenge easy to perceive. Conventional smartphone design gives engineers a relatively predictable enclosure in which to arrange the processor, battery, cameras, and thermal management system. A foldable must accommodate a hinge and two display sections while remaining thin enough to fold comfortably and fit in a pocket.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
At the same time, the processor and other electronics still generate heat – more, even, when we consider how people are starting to use mobile devices. Which means foldable designs necessarily concentrate significant heat-generating components into smaller and thinner portions of the device, precisely where space for thermal hardware is already constrained.
In general, vapor chambers remain one of the most effective ways to manage heat in a compact electronic device. They work by moving heat away from a concentrated source, such as a mobile processor, and spreading it across a larger area. But vapor chambers ultimately spread heat rather than remove it.
Sure, as processors become more powerful, manufacturers can increase the size and effectiveness of the vapor chamber. But eventually that thermal component itself becomes a design constraint, especially in foldable phones.
Agentic AI Makes the Challenge Urgent
In foldables, innovating around thermal management is itself an admirable design goal – if folding were the only technological advancement engineers had to tackle. But they’re pushing the envelope on physical design at the exact moment when smartphones are being asked to do much more. Namely, to process agentic AI workloads.
As agentic AI moves from the cloud to edge devices – AI-capable smartphones, wearables, glasses, and more – thermal management becomes the industry's most important challenge. Imagine a new foldable smartphone with its own specialized thermal management system, designed to accommodate an innovative new form factor. Now imagine asking that foldable to process vast amounts of data differently than before.
Unlike traditional mobile apps that perform discrete tasks, AI agents operate continuously. They sense their environment, preserve context, analyze streams of data, and act in real time.
In my view, the industry is still underestimating how significant this transition will be. Historically, a smartphone's thermal profile was defined by short bursts of activity: launching an app, streaming a video, capturing a photo. Agentic AI at the edge changes that model entirely. Devices are moving toward persistent intelligence, continuously sensing, processing, reasoning, and responding. With these sustained workloads, a device’s ability to manage heat becomes a defining constraint on its performance.
Passive thermal technologies remain indispensable. Vapor chambers, graphite, heat spreaders, and advanced materials will continue to play a critical role in future devices. The challenge is that Edge AI introduces thermal loads that increasingly benefit from more than heat spreading alone. As devices become thinner and workloads become more persistent, designers will need additional ways to not just to move heat away from sensitive components, but to move heat out of the system entirely.
Micro-Cooling Complements the Vapor Chamber
So here we are, with foldable smartphones capable of agentic AI processing. It’s a perfect storm of thermal design challenges. Engineers can continue enlarging or customizing the thermal systems they integrate into new and different form factors. Or they can find other ways to extract more thermal performance from available space.
The latter approach is where active, micro-cooling technology becomes a viable and important solution.
Unlike miniature rotary fans, which exist today and take up precious real estate of their own, MEMS-based piezoelectric actuators, fabricated in silicon, generate airflow inside extremely compact packages. Basically, it’s a fan on a chip, capable of precise active cooling that fits where conventional solutions cannot.
With micro cooling (µCooling), heat isn’t just spread out, it’s removed from the device entirely before it can sink into the case, delaying or eliminating thermal throttling. This hybrid approach to cooling in highly constrained spaces delivers better thermal performance in today’s AI-enabled smart devices.
It also creates greater design flexibility – a must as devices themselves become more physically flexible. If active µCooling can provide additional thermal performance, manufacturers may not need to maximize the physical dimensions of vapor chambers. A more appropriately sized, passive thermal system could be paired with localized active µCooling and thereby free up internal volume for other components and give designers more flexibility in how a device is assembled.
Put simply, with µCooling, thermal hardware wouldn’t have to consume as much of a device’s design envelope.
µCooling As Part of the Compute Architecture
The implications extend beyond folding smartphones. AI glasses, headphones, watches, robots, and other edge devices face the same fundamental problem, often with even tighter constraints on size, weight, and power.
The industry wants to put more intelligence into mobile devices while simultaneously making them smaller and more comfortable. That creates a physical contradiction. More compute generates more heat. Smaller devices provide less room to manage it.
µCooling offers a way to change the equation. Not by eliminating vapor chambers and other passive solutions, but by supplementing them with localized active cooling that provides additional thermal headroom while giving product designers more freedom.
As AI runs more continuously in the background, edge devices will spend more time computing and less time idle. Sustaining performance will matter as much as reaching peak capability. Foldable phones make this challenge acute, but it extends across the edge AI market as more intelligence and local processing place greater demands on compact hardware.
That intelligence has a thermal cost. Over the next decade, progress will depend as much on what physical devices can sustain as on what AI models can do. That’s why I believe thermal management is becoming a foundational technology of the edge AI era. The companies that solve this challenge will help define the next generation of intelligent devices.
Manufacturers already know this, which is why thermal management is so essential to product design. µCooling is the innovation behind the innovation – like smartphones that fold.

articles.title: Après ChatGPT, OpenAI veut révolutionner la création de vos médicaments
articles.text:
Le créateur de ChatGPT vient de s’offrir un spécialiste des logiciels destinés à l’industrie pharmaceutique. Une acquisition qui doit lui permettre de s’imposer dans le développement des médicaments, alors même que l’entreprise continue d’engloutir des milliards de dollars pour financer sa croissance.
Développer un médicament prend des années, et le moindre contretemps peut bouleverser tout un programme de recherche. C’est précisément sur ce terrain qu’OpenAI compte désormais avancer. Le 20 octobre, l’entreprise a annoncé le rachat d’Orchestra Bio, une société spécialisée dans les agents d’intelligence artificielle capables de coordonner les différentes étapes du développement pharmaceutique.
L'opération marque une nouvelle étape dans la diversification du groupe qui ne veut manifestement plus se contenter de fournir des modèles d’IA aux entreprises.
Des agents IA pour accélérer le travail des laboratoires
Un problème de fabrication, des résultats qui tardent ou un essai clinique repoussé peuvent rapidement entraîner des mois de retard. Orchestra Bio a justement développé des outils capables d’anticiper les conséquences de ces imprévus, de réorganiser les tâches et de proposer différents scénarios aux équipes scientifiques.
Les décisions restent entre les mains des chercheurs, mais une partie du travail de coordination peut être confiée à l'IA.
Les équipes d’Orchestra vont rejoindre Rosalind, l’offre d’OpenAI destinée aux sciences du vivant. Celle-ci repose notamment sur GPT-Rosalind, un modèle spécialisé en biologie et en chimie, ainsi que sur Workbench, un environnement permettant d’exploiter les données scientifiques et de préparer des expériences.
En associant ces outils aux agents d’Orchestra, OpenAI espère accompagner les laboratoires bien au-delà de la simple analyse de résultats. L’objectif est aussi commercial, puisque ce type de logiciel peut devenir indispensable au fonctionnement quotidien des équipes de recherche.
Mais avec quel argent OpenAI finance-t-il ses acquisitions ?
Le montant du rachat n’a pas été communiqué, pas plus que ses modalités de paiement. Impossible donc de savoir si OpenAI a utilisé sa trésorerie, ses actions ou une combinaison des deux.
L'absence de bénéfices ne l’empêche toutefois pas de poursuivre ses emplettes. Fin mars, l’entreprise a annoncé 122 milliards de dollars de capitaux engagés avec le soutien de poids lourds comme Amazon, NVIDIA et SoftBank.
De quoi financer une expansion particulièrement coûteuse, même si les investisseurs prennent un pari considérable sur l’avenir. Selon des projections révélées par le Financial Times et relayées par Reuters, OpenAI prévoyait encore de consommer 278 milliards de dollars de trésorerie entre 2026 et 2030.
Le groupe compte donc sur sa croissance future pour justifier des investissements qui dépassent aujourd’hui largement ses bénéfices, toujours inexistants.
Quand l’industrie pharmaceutique et l’IA s'attirent mutuellement
Le rapprochement entre intelligence artificielle et recherche médicale ne date évidemment pas de cette acquisition. En 2023, BioNTech avait racheté InstaDeep pour renforcer ses capacités en IA, tandis qu’AstraZeneca a plus récemment mis la main sur Modella AI afin d’accélérer ses travaux en cancérologie.
Le mouvement fonctionne désormais dans les deux sens. Les laboratoires s’offrent des spécialistes de l’IA pour améliorer leurs recherches, tandis que les entreprises technologiques cherchent à pénétrer un secteur où les besoins en calcul, en analyse et en automatisation sont considérables.
Anthropic avance également sur ce terrain avec son laboratoire de biologie, présenté en septembre, où des hypothèses élaborées avec Claude peuvent être confrontées à des expériences réelles.
- Chat dans différentes langues, dont le français
- Générer, traduire et obtenir un résumé de texte
- Générer, optimiser et corriger du code

articles.title: PlayStation Physical Game Share Still As High As 32%
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
PlayStation Physical Game Share Still As High As 32%
Since Sony announced that it would be ending physical media production for the PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 5 Pro, there has been much discussion about the value of physical games media in the modern gaming landscape. Some argue that physical media is invaluable for game preservation and access to content in some remote parts of the world, while others argue that its value is limited, because the physical media market share is small for most games, and it has limited preservation value, thanks to day-one patches. Alinea Analytics recently posted some data about physical media sales on PlayStation, putting more numbers to the impact of physical games media on PlayStation. 
Interestingly, despite the relatively high physical sales split of some games, like Resident Evil Requiem, with disc sales accounting for 30.2% of its sales, and Marvel's Wolverine, whose disc sales came to 32.3% of its total sales revenue, the total physical game sales revenue for games released in 2026 on PlayStation 5 and PS4 amounted to $655 million, which is less than 20% of sales revenue for the year. As the analytics firm explains, that revenue split itself is skewed by digital-only releases and pre-order bonuses, which are all digital sales. The data itself seems to tell a story of a split player base: those who buy first-party, single-player, narrative-driven games tend to skew more towards physical media, while sports and multiplayer gamers tend to buy digital more often.PlayStation's top-selling games for 2026 were FC27, Resident Evil Requiem, 2K27, 007 First Light, and Marvel's Wolverine, in that order. In that top-five list, three games had notably high physical sales splits. 
Physical sales share by game:
- Resident Evil Requiem: 30.2% or 1.3 million sales
- 007 First Light: 29% or 873,000 sales
- Marvel's Wolverine: 32.3% or 799,000 sales
Despite its low physical sales share, at just 8.9%, FC27 still sold 705,000 physical units, while games like Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced sold 613,000 physical units, and Crimson Desert sold 511,000. The revenue from physical sales of Requiem, First Light, Wolverine, FC27, Black Flag Resynced, Crimson Desert, Pragmata, and Onimusha Way of the Sword—Sony's games with the highest physical revenue—accounted for a total of $1.2 billion, with bigger titles, like Resident Evil Requiem accounting for as much as $92.3 million in physical revenue alone.At the end of the day, though, the revenue generated from physical games still pales in comparison to that of Sony's digital offerings, and, between the higher margins on digital media—shipping physical media is more expensive than digital distribution—players who are apathetic about the switch to digital-only games, and the revenue it may earn from players who would otherwise have bought a used copy on the second-hand market, Sony appears to be betting that it will come out ahead in terms of revenue and game sales if it sticks to its guns on the switch away from physical media.
Source:
				Alinea Analytics

articles.title: Critical FortiSIEM Flaw Gets Public Exploit PoC for Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have released a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit for a recently patched critical security flaw impacting Fortinet FortiSIEM that could result in arbitrary code execution.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-106173 (CVSS score: 9.4), is a critical path traversal flaw that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized code or commands via specially crafted packets.
Patches for the flaw were released last week by Fortinet in the following versions -
- FortiSIEM 7.5.0 (Upgrade to 7.5.1 or above)
- FortiSIEM 7.6 (Not affected)
According to Horizon3.ai, the issue involves an unauthenticated attacker connecting to the gRPC service listening on TCP port 27918 and exploiting the flaw to overwrite an existing file outside of the intended directory and turn the arbitrary-file-write primitive into remote code execution.
"The FortiSIEM gRPC QueryResultReq handler processes untrusted metadata without proper path validation," Horizon3.ai said. "By crafting metadata containing both path traversal sequences (../) and NUL-byte injection within gRPC's HTTP/2 and HPACK encoding layers, an attacker can write arbitrary files to the file system."
The problem stems from a case of unsafe path construction within a function named SendQueryResult(), which passes a user-supplied "query-id" parameter directly without sufficient validation.
In other words, an attacker can leverage this flaw to include directory traversal sequences such as "../" and escape that directory. However, this only allows an attacker to navigate to a directory of their choice and write to it, but not to opt for a file name because the program automatically adds its own file name "result-<source IP address>-0-0-<id>.dat," where <id> is a counter value controlled by the server.
That's where a second weakness enters the picture: a null byte ("\0") can be embedded in the "query-id" parameter, causing the operating system to interpret it as a string terminator and discard everything that comes after it. This, in turn, results in the appended file name suffix being ignored when the path is passed to the file-opening function.
An attacker could exploit this behavior to craft a "query-id" value with "\0" placed such that it's preceded by the actual file name to be overwritten – i.e., "../../../../../opt/charting/redishb.sh\0..." The file in question is a shell script that performs health checks on the Redis service and is run every 60 seconds by a cron job.
"The write lands on the exact path that preceded the null byte," Zach Hanley, Chief Attack Engineer at Horizon3.ai, said. "Pointed at an existing file, this overwrites it in place, keeping the original owner and permissions; a second variant uses two requests to create a brand-new file with an exact name."

articles.title: Du carrelage au canapé : ce que propose le nouveau Roborock
articles.text:
Roborock F25 Pro Turbo : le laveur de sol arrive en France avec ou sans option aspirateur-balai
Un duo qui frotte
On l'avait vu à l'IFA dans sa version Combo, le F25 Pro Turbo est désormais commercialisé en France sous deux formes.
Roborock F25 Pro Turbo
Roborock F25 Pro Turbo Combo
Après les annonces de septembre dernier et les arguments mis en avant récemment par la marque pour les déclinaisons du laveur de sol F25, voici les prix de deux nouveautés. Roborock commercialise le F25 Pro Turbo à 549 €, tandis que le F25 Pro Turbo Combo est affiché à 599 € jusqu'au 1er novembre, avant de passer au tarif conseillé de 699 €. L'écart entre les deux versions est donc provisoirement limité à 50 €.
Un coup de gâchette sur les taches
Les deux modèles partagent la fonction HyperScrub. En maintenant une gâchette enfoncée, l'utilisateur augmente le débit d'eau, l'aspiration et la vitesse du rouleau. Cela permet de concentrer les efforts sur une tache séchée ou des résidus de cuisine, puis de reprendre le nettoyage courant en relâchant la commande.
Roborock annonce une puissance maximale de 25 000 Pa et un rouleau tournant jusqu'à 550 tr/min en mode brossage. Selon la marque, le débit d'eau augmente de 245 % par rapport au mode automatique.
Le châssis peut se coucher à 180°, avec une hauteur limitée à 12,5 cm pour passer sous les meubles. Nous retrouvons également le système de raclettes destiné à limiter l'enroulement des cheveux, ainsi qu'une station qui nettoie et sèche le rouleau. L'autonomie atteint 60 minutes, mais en mode Éco.
Le Combo change de terrain
La différence se joue surtout au-delà des sols durs. Le F25 Pro Turbo Combo utilise un bloc moteur amovible pour passer du laveur à l'aspirateur-balai. Une tête dédiée permet alors d'aspirer les tapis et moquettes, tandis qu'une mini-brosse motorisée peut s'utiliser les surfaces textiles. Un accessoire 2-en-1 complète l'ensemble pour les recoins et les petites surfaces.

articles.title: Amazon se convierte en el primer proveedor de nube de la OTAN para información restringida
articles.text:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) se convirtió en el primer proveedor de servicios en la nube aprobado por la totalidad de los países miembros de la Organización del Tratado del Atlántico Norte (OTAN) para el manejo de información clasificada bajo el nivel “NATO RESTRICTED” (NR).
La aprobación permite que la Alianza, sus socios de la industria de defensa y cada uno de sus estados miembros utilicen los servicios de AWS para procesar cargas de trabajo con esa clasificación en cualquier región de la compañía ubicada dentro de un país de la OTAN.
Prolongado proceso de certificación
Para obtener la aprobación, AWS documentó su cumplimiento de la norma D32, la directiva técnica de la OTAN que fija los requisitos de seguridad para el manejo de información restringida en la nube pública. Como parte de ese proceso, el Centro Criptográfico Nacional (CCN) de España evaluó las capacidades de la compañía, antes de que la OTAN diera a conocer la aprobación a todos sus aliados.
David Appel, vicepresidente interino de Sector Público Global de AWS, calificó la certificación como “la culminación de un esfuerzo sostenido de varios años” y aseguró que refleja el compromiso de la empresa “de ayudar a los clientes y socios de los sectores de defensa, del sector público y afiliados a la OTAN a cumplir sus misiones críticas”.
El directivo agregó que “los gobiernos, y los ciudadanos, merecen tener acceso a la misma infraestructura y los mismos servicios que impulsan la innovación en el sector privado”.
La aprobación reduce tiempos y costos de acreditación
El visto bueno otorgado a AWS simplifica el camino que deben recorrer los países miembros y los socios industriales de la Alianza Atlántica para adoptar la nube comercial en proyectos con información restringida. Al contar ya con una base de seguridad común y evaluada previamente, los aliados pueden reducir el tiempo, el esfuerzo y el costo que implica cumplir con las obligaciones de seguridad y cumplimiento normativo que exige la OTAN.
Además, la certificación abre una vía acelerada para que cada país miembro acredite a AWS a través de su propio proceso nacional oficial, sin necesidad de repetir desde cero las evaluaciones técnicas que ya validó la organización a nivel central. Para la acreditación NR, la OTAN delega el proceso en un país miembro o en la Agencia de Comunicaciones e Información de la OTAN (NCIA), en su calidad de anfitrión.
La infraestructura disponible abarca 15 países de la Alianza
Actualmente, AWS opera 15 regiones de infraestructura en países miembros de la OTAN, siete de las cuales se encuentran en Europa continental. Todas esas regiones quedan habilitadas para el desarrollo de sistemas con capacidad para manejar información “NATO RESTRICTED”, de acuerdo con el alcance de la aprobación otorgada.
Dylan Browne, gerente general de la NCIA, destacó que “fortalecer la capacidad de la OTAN para aprovechar de manera segura la tecnología comercial es clave para construir una Alianza más resiliente y ágil”. Browne sostuvo además que la disponibilidad de productos comerciales que cumplen con los requisitos de seguridad de la OTAN amplía las opciones tecnológicas disponibles para la organización y respalda su capacidad de adoptar tecnologías modernas sin resignar seguridad ni resiliencia operativa.
El acceso se canaliza a través de una plataforma específica
La base técnica de este anuncio es AWS Trusted Secure Enclave – Sensitive Edition (TSE-SE), la solución a través de la cual los clientes de seguridad nacional y defensa pueden acceder a las capacidades ahora certificadas. Appel remarcó el compromiso de la compañía de “seguir trabajando para brindar la interoperabilidad que las naciones aliadas necesitan para fortalecer su resiliencia y proteger a sus ciudadanos”.
Los clientes interesados en implementar soluciones bajo este marco pueden coordinar con sus equipos de cuenta de AWS para evaluar cómo la aprobación y el TSE-SE se adaptan a sus casos de uso particulares dentro de los distintos países de la Alianza.

articles.title: Why enterprise AI needs real-time conversations, not just documents
articles.text:
Why enterprise AI needs real-time conversations, not just documents
The missing layer of the enterprise brain: how AI requires conversational context
The "enterprise brain" is a term featuring more and more prominently in the enterprise technology market and at the C-suite level. Technology vendors of all varieties are scrambling to connect internal documents, knowledge bases and structured data systems into a unified architecture.
The compelling goal is to provide AI agents with as deep organizational context as possible so they can reason, automate and assist with scarcely believable accuracy.
But as businesses pour resources into linking their databases, policy documents and CRM entries, a significant blind spot remains.
Efforts to build an enterprise brain often overlook the intelligence contained in the millions of conversations employees are already having with customers, colleagues and candidates across phone calls and messaging channels.
CEO and Co-Founder of Ringover.
Documents tell you what your policies are and CRM records can tell you what happened, but business conversations tell you why an incident happened.
For any company that is serious about building a true enterprise brain, conversations cannot remain a missing layer of organizational intelligence.
Beyond the confines of structured data
Standard business tools are excellent at tracking outcomes but terrible at preserving nuances. Structured systems may record instances of an enterprise deal stalled, an account at risk of churning or a candidate withdrawing from an interview process. But it of course can’t put its finger on the actual trigger.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
A deal doesn’t just stall, there will always be a key factor that changed the buyer's mind during a late-stage call. Similarly a candidate doesn’t just decline an offer, maybe a competitor introduced a work-from-home policy during a quick negotiation chat.
When organizations rely solely on static databases to train AI models or inform strategy, they are feeding their enterprise brain an incomplete diet. They receive the post-mortem without the symptoms, and AI needs the sometimes messy, real-time context found in human dialogue to understand the operational reality of a company.
Actionable context
Artificial intelligence has reached a level of maturity where analysing high-volume voice and chat interactions is no longer a nice to have or a bonus. But just recording every interaction and dumping raw transcripts into a data lake, which effectively hoards unstructured audio, solves absolutely nothing. To make conversational context truly useful, businesses must focus on a few core operational pillars.
First, conversational insights must automatically sync with existing enterprise systems rather than living solely within a VoIP dashboard, allowing real-time data from a support call to enrich the CRM and trigger automated alerts. Second, the extracted intelligence needs to be routed immediately to the teams equipped to act on it. For example, if sales calls routinely show that prospect friction stems from a specific pricing tier, that signal should flow directly to product strategy and marketing rather than remaining trapped in the revenue organization.
Finally, while AI should perform the heavy lifting of summarization, sentiment analysis and pattern recognition, human judgment must always remain the final filter for important decision-making. While this may seem obvious, it is amazing how overly reliant on AI many employees have quickly become, including using it for critical business judgement calls.
Breaking down knowledge silos
Knowledge silos continue to be huge challenges for many organizations. Sales teams learn what buyers want, support teams learn where the product fails, and recruitment learn how the market perceives employer branding. All is highly valuable information, but all too often these groups don’t share a unified intelligence pool.
When conversational context is ingested into the enterprise brain, these walls dissolve across every department. For instance, when a prospect mentions a niche feature gap during a sales demo, that insight can prompt product teams to prioritize the feature while sales updates its outreach messaging.
Similarly, if a customer casually mentions an upcoming corporate restructuring on a support call, account management can initiate proactive outreach to protect the account before contract renewal.
By connecting these conversational dots across departments, organizations shift from reactive firefighting to proactive alignment.
Value over volume
Now this is not to say that trying to capture, transcribe, and analyze every single internal interaction is the way forward. Because it goes without saying, this is borderline impossible. If attempted, it can lead to sky-high compute costs and even legitimate anxiety regarding employee monitoring.
To build a functional, trusted enterprise brain, organizations must prioritize value over volume. The focus should be on high-value workflows where conversation directly drives business outcomes, such as customer-facing revenue calls, critical support interactions or key talent acquisition touchpoints.
Focusing on these targeted areas minimizes data noise while delivering immediate ROI. Organizations must build trust by maintaining clear boundaries. Conversational analysis should focus on market trends, product feedback and operational blockers instead of micromanaging employee tone or enforcing rigid scripts.
The complete enterprise brain
A truly intelligent enterprise cannot run on paperwork and revenue tables alone. It requires the context and nuance that only human interactions provide.
As enterprise AI continues to evolve at rapid pace, having the largest static document libraries will count for nothing. The organizations that thrive will be the ones who successfully pair their structured business data with the rich, dynamic intelligence hidden inside their everyday conversations.

articles.title: Ce génial missile français voit sa cible avant même d’être tiré depuis l’hélicoptère Tigre
articles.text:
La Direction générale de l'armement a mené avec succès, il y a moins d'un mois, un nouveau tir d’essai du missile Akeron LP depuis un hélicoptère Tigre. Conçu par MBDA, il doit remplacer le Hellfire américain à partir de 2028.
Le 25 septembre 2026, sur le site DGA (Direction générale de l'armement) Essais en vol de Cazaux, en Gironde, un hélicoptère Tigre a tiré un missile Akeron LP qui avait déjà repéré sa cible avant de quitter son lanceur. C'est le quatrième tir de développement de ce missile conçu par le Français MBDA, et seulement le deuxième depuis un Tigre. Ce « verrouillage avant tir » n'est qu'une des cartes de l'Akeron LP, un missile très bien conçu, qui transmet ses images en direct à l'équipage, lui permet de corriger le tir ou de changer de cible en cours de vol, et doit l'exposer bien moins qu'avec le Hellfire américain.
Un missile Akeron LP qui ne lâche pas sa cible des yeux
Ce tir effectué avec succès le mois dernier vient couronner une série d'essais menés depuis début 2025 pour éprouver l'Akeron LP brique par brique, du sol jusqu'aux airs. En février 2025, un premier tir depuis le sol avait validé le comportement en vol, le guidage et la propulsion. Le mois suivant, un Tigre lançait pour la première fois l'Akeron LP, surtout pour vérifier que le missile se sépare sans danger de l'appareil. L'essai de Cazaux va plus loin avec le LOBL (Lock-On Before Launch). L'autodirecteur, l'« œil » du missile, accroche la cible en infrarouge alors que l'engin est encore sur son lanceur, puis doit garder cette prise une fois largué, malgré le souffle du rotor et les turbulences.
Cet œil en vaut trois, puisque l'autodirecteur conçu par Safran associe un capteur infrarouge, une caméra TV et un récepteur laser. Thales fournit la liaison de données, un canal radio dans les deux sens qui renvoie à l'opérateur les images captées par le missile pendant tout le vol. Le procédé avait déjà fait ses preuves le 24 mars dernier, lors d'un tir depuis le sol contre une cible mobile en mer, sur l'île du Levant. Selon la mission, l'équipage peut laisser le missile se débrouiller seul (le fameux « tire et oublie ») ou garder la main jusqu'au bout.
Et c'est là que tout change. L'opérateur peut corriger le point d'impact, basculer sur une autre cible, voire annuler la frappe en cours de route. Avec le Hellfire américain à guidage laser, la cible doit au contraire rester « éclairée » par un pointeur jusqu'à l'impact, ce qui contraint souvent l'hélicoptère à rester exposé. L'Akeron LP est aussi pensé pour verrouiller sa cible après le tir, ce qui permettrait à un drone de désigner l'objectif pendant que le Tigre reste caché derrière une colline. Ce scénario n'a pas encore été testé lors des tirs rendus publics.
L'Akeron LP vise le Tigre, puis le Guépard
Le missile français est né du programme MAST-F (Missile air-sol tactique futur), confié à MBDA en 2020 et géré pour la France par l'OCCAR, l'organisation européenne chargée de piloter des programmes d'armement en coopération. L'Akeron LP pèse environ 35 kg et mesure 1,80 m dans son tube. Sa double charge explosive serait capable de percer l'équivalent de plus d'un mètre d'acier de blindage, de quoi inquiéter les chars les mieux protégés, y compris ceux dotés de blindage réactif. Elle vise aussi les bâtiments légers et les petites embarcations, à plus de 8 km depuis un hélicoptère et jusqu'à 20 km depuis un drone. La première commande porterait sur 500 missiles et une centaine de lanceurs.
Ces missiles ne viendront pas seulement renforcer l'arsenal des Tigre français. Ils doivent surtout permettre à l'armée de se passer du Hellfire II, un missile américain soumis à la réglementation ITAR, qui encadre strictement l'usage et la revente des armements made in USA. Ici, les trois piliers du programme, MBDA, Safran et Thales, sont tous européens, et le développement est largement mené en France. Près d'un mois après l'essai d'ailleurs, dans un post LinkedIn publié mardi, Stéphane Reb, le directeur général de MBDA France, a encore salué un succès au service de la « souveraineté » et de l'industrie de défense nationale.
La prochaine étape, c'est celle de la qualification, avec une série d'épreuves qui devra prouver que le missile tient toutes ses promesses. Elle doit démarrer à partir de 2027. Les premières livraisons sont prévues pour 2028, et les Tigre modernisés au standard Mk3 doivent en être équipés à partir de 2029. Ce chantier de modernisation, mené avec l'Espagne, concerne 85 appareils, dont 67 français. Airbus Helicopters planche déjà sur l'intégration du missile au futur H160M Guépard, et l'Akeron LP a même été monté sur des robots terrestres lors d'un projet européen. Sous les cocardes françaises, le Hellfire peut commencer à préparer sa retraite.

articles.title: Qilin and INC Ransomware Groups Exploit Palo Alto Networks Flaw to Bypass MFA
articles.text:
Palo Alto Networks has disclosed that it's continuing to observe exploitation of a now-patched security flaw impacting PAN-OS and Prisma Access by ransomware actors.
The activity relates to CVE-2026-0257 (CVSS score: 7.8), an authentication bypass flaw that could be exploited by bad actors to set up unauthorized VPN connections. It was patched by Palo Alto Networks in May 2026 and was added by the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CSIA) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on May 13, 2026.
"Ransomware operators exploiting CVE-2026-0257 include Spikey Scorpius (aka Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (aka INC)," Unit 42 researchers said in an update shared on Monday. The development comes days after ReliaQuest said it detected both Qilin and Settra ransomware groups actively exploiting the flaw in financially-motivated attacks.
According to Unit 42, the threat actors are weaponizing the flaw to gain an initial foothold into corporate networks, and then bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA) controls to establish a VPN session.
Upon setting up a VPN session, the attackers have been found to engage in the following post-compromise activity -
- Conduct internal network reconnaissance using dual-use remote monitoring and management (RMM) tools.
- Move laterally across the network via RDP and SMB.
- Stage additional tooling for credential harvesting, data exfiltration, and ransomware deployment.
Attacks mounted by these groups are said to have targeted a wide range of sectors, including education, financial services, healthcare, high technology, hospitality, manufacturing, professional and legal services, government, transportation and logistics, utilities and energy, and retail.
"The most significant evolution in tactics, techniques and procedures (TTPs) following successful exploitation of CVE-2026-0257 is the direct pivot to the virtualization layer," Unit 42 said.
"In one notable case, attackers moved from the compromised VPN gateway to the vCenter management appliance. From there, they disabled security controls on ESXi hypervisors (execInstalledOnly) and used a custom tool to perform offline credential dumping directly against a domain controller's virtual disk (VMDK)."
This approach, the network security vendor added, circumvents in-guest endpoint detection and response (EDR) and security protections, allowing the threat actors to obtain domain-wide credentials.
Attackers have also been observed chaining the initial access method with other exploit tools, including efforts to target Veeam backup infrastructure by abusing known flaws (CVE-2023-27532) to inflict maximum damage.
It's worth noting that Qilin's exploitation of CVE-2026-0257 was previously flagged by Arctic Wolf in July 2026, with attacks ranging from rapid encryption-only operations to full double-extortion.
Besides applying the latest fixes, Palo Alto Networks is recommending that organizations proactively hunt for indicators of compromise and initiate appropriate incident response protocols if successful gateway-connected events are detected.

articles.title: NVIDIA Has January Discontinuation Dates Set for RTX 5090 and RTX 5080 16 GB, Claims Leaker
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
NVIDIA Has January Discontinuation Dates Set for RTX 5090 and RTX 5080 16 GB, Claims Leaker
Earlier this month, leakers claimed NVIDIA had stopped allocating GB202 silicon to the GeForce RTX 5090, effectively discontinuing the Blackwell flagship. NVIDIA denied it a few days later, with SVP Jeff Fisher saying the RTX 5090 hasn't been discontinued and will keep shipping. Now, Moore's Law Is Dead (MLID) says the plans are still in place, and the RTX 5080 is part of them too. In the latest Broken Silicon episode, MLID read out a message from what he calls one of his oldest sources, apparently a major retailer, saying NVIDIA has set discontinuation dates for both cards in the first half of January 2027. 
According to that source, the last RTX 5090 shipments arrived in September, while the final RTX 5080 batch should land by the end of October and sell through Thanksgiving. We recently reported that Micro Center has already marked its RTX 5090 listings as "Not Carried," which could be further evidence of the RTX 5090 leaving shelves. The retailer from MLID's video also says its system already has a placeholder SKU for an RTX 5080 24 GB, which aligns with BenchLife's earlier report of a Q1 2027 launch.Of course, this should be taken with a healthy dose of salt. MLID has a mixed reputation, and his leaks tend to be hit-or-miss. Just last month, he claimed NVIDIA was targeting the first half of 2027 for its Rubin-based RTX 60-series GPUs. Leakers like MEGAsizeGPU and Kepler_L2 disputed that almost right away, and multiple leakers now point to a 2028 window instead. NVIDIA also hasn't said a word about a 24 GB RTX 5080, but there have now been multiple reports of that card's existence from different leakers. If the timeline holds, it's reasonable to expect RTX 5080 16 GB stock to thin out after the holidays, with the 24 GB model likely costing more than the current card's $999 MSRP.

articles.text:
Panne réseau mobile : après Orange, SFR et Bouygues Telecom également en difficulté
Difficile journée que ce mercredi 21 octobre 2026. Après Orange, c'est au tour des réseaux mobiles de Bouygues Telecom et de SFR d'être possiblement en panne.
Depuis ce matin, le réseau mobile d'Orange est en panne avérée pour un bon nombre d'abonnés à travers la France. Alors qu'Orange a réagi et que les clients des autres opérateurs se pensaient à l'abri, il semblerait finalement que non.
Le réseau mobile de SFR et Bouygues Telecom également touchés ?
D'après DownDetector et des témoignages de plusieurs centaines de personnes depuis 11h30 ce matin, soit environ en même temps qu'Orange, SFR et Bouygues Telecom peineraient également à assurer le service mobile.
Ce n'est cependant rien comparé aux milliers de signalements à propos d'Orange, dont la panne semble beaucoup plus sévère. Sur X également, il est principalement question d'Orange, laissant à penser que les personnes concernées chez la concurrence sont beaucoup moins nombreuses.
Pour le moment, ni Bouygues Telecom ni SFR n'a communiqué sur ses réseaux pour évoquer cette panne. Reste donc à savoir les services réellement affectés et la cause de ces possibles pépins techniques.
Avec la faille PHP qui risque de mettre de nombreux sites web hors ligne aujourd'hui à 16h, ce mercredi 21 octobre 2026 risque définitivement d'être une journée noire dans la tech.

articles.title: Novedades de Pokémon GO para noviembre 2026: detalles del nuevo Pase de GO y eventos
articles.text:
Pokémon GO habilitará en noviembre de 2026 un nuevo Pase de GO mensual, un sistema de progreso con recompensas gratuitas y opciones de pago.
Entre los premios destacados habrá un encuentro con Groudon, Pokémonedas, Polvo Estrella, Caramelo raro XL y objetos para el juego.
El Pase de GO de noviembre estará disponible desde el martes 3 de noviembre hasta el martes 1 de diciembre, según la hora local de cada jugador.
Los Entrenadores recibirán el pase gratuito de forma automática y podrán sumar Puntos de GO para avanzar de rango y desbloquear recompensas.
También habrá dos opciones de pago. El Pase de GO Deluxe costará USD 7,99 e incluirá recompensas mejoradas y un avance más rápido. Por USD 9,99, estará disponible una versión que otorgará los Puntos de GO necesarios para llegar automáticamente al rango 11.
Las recompensas obtenidas deberán reclamarse antes del jueves 3 de diciembre, cuando caducarán.
Qué novedades trae Pokémon GO en noviembre de 2026
Durante el sábado 28 y el domingo 29 de noviembre no habrá un límite diario para conseguir Puntos de GO. Esta bonificación permitirá avanzar sin restricciones en el pase durante esos dos días.
El pase gratuito ofrecerá un encuentro con Groudon, 400 Pokémonedas, un Huevo Suerte, Caramelo raro XL y Polvo Estrella, entre otras recompensas.
Quienes compren el Pase de GO Deluxe podrán obtener 1.000 Pokémonedas adicionales, para un total de 1.400, una Superincubadora y encuentros extra con más Pokémon. Groudon podrá aparecer en su versión brillante.
Los jugadores que avancen en el pase desbloquearán bonificaciones según su rango.
Desde el rango uno recibirán un Caramelo adicional por intercambiar Pokémon; quienes tengan nivel 31 o superior obtendrán además un Caramelo XL garantizado.
A partir del rango 25, podrán abrir hasta 40 regalos al día, recibir hasta 125 al girar fotodiscos de Poképaradas y Gimnasios y guardar 10 regalos adicionales en la Bolsa.
Desde el rango 50, el Incienso de aventura diaria tendrá el doble de duración. A partir del rango 75, los jugadores recibirán más Polvo Estrella y EXP —los puntos de experiencia necesarios para subir de nivel— al eclosionar Huevos.
El Pase de GO Deluxe mejorará algunas de las bonificaciones del rango 25: permitirá abrir hasta 50 regalos al día, recibir hasta 150 regalos al girar fotodiscos de Poképaradas y Gimnasios, y guardar hasta 20 regalos adicionales en la Bolsa.
El Pase de GO Deluxe también podrá comprarse en la Tienda web de Pokémon GO. Quienes lo adquieran allí recibirán 10 Ultrabolas, cinco Revivir Máximo, un Pase de Combate Premium y cinco Pociones Máximas. La versión con 10 rangos añadirá un segundo Pase de Combate Premium.
Además, la Caja Ultraespecial del Pase de GO Deluxe de noviembre incluirá 20 Ultrabolas, 10 Revivir Máximo, cinco Pases de Combate Premium y 10 Pociones Máximas. Todas las opciones de compra estarán disponibles una sola vez y su disponibilidad podrá variar según la región.
Cómo empezar a jugar Pokémon GO
Para empezar, descarga Pokémon GO en tu celular y crea una cuenta. El juego utiliza la ubicación del dispositivo para mostrar un mapa basado en el entorno real. Al caminar, aparecerán Pokémon que puedes capturar al tocarlos en la pantalla y lanzar una Poké Ball con un movimiento del dedo.
Las Poképaradas son lugares del mapa donde consigues objetos, como Poké Balls y pociones.
Para obtenerlos, debes acercarte y girar el fotodisco, la imagen circular que aparece en cada punto. Puedes activar las notificaciones para conocer eventos cercanos.
Los Gimnasios te permiten combatir con otros jugadores y participar en incursiones, desafíos grupales contra un Pokémon. Al principio, lo más útil es capturar criaturas distintas, reunir objetos y completar tareas. No necesitas gastar dinero para avanzar.
Antes de salir, revisa la batería del teléfono, usa conexión móvil o Wi-Fi y presta atención al entorno.

articles.title: Microsoft continue de faire le tri dans Windows 11, de nouvelles commandes Copilot passent à la trappe
articles.text:
Microsoft poursuit le nettoyage des intégrations de Copilot dans Windows 11. Huit commandes d’intelligence artificielle vont disparaître de l’Explorateur de fichiers, sans que les fonctionnalités associées soient abandonnées.
En mars dernier, Microsoft promettait de simplifier Windows 11 et de se débarrasser des accès à Copilot jugés superflus. Après avoir supprimé ou rebaptisé plusieurs boutons dédiés à son assistant dans les applications natives du système, l’entreprise s’attaque désormais à l’Explorateur de fichiers. Dans une communication publiée le 19 octobre dans son centre d’administration Microsoft 365, elle annonce le retrait de huit commandes d’intelligence artificielle accessibles depuis le menu contextuel des fichiers OneDrive. Un coup de balai qui ne remet toutefois pas en cause les ambitions de Redmond en matière d’IA dans Windows.
Des raccourcis au rebut, des fonctionnalités toujours disponibles
Dans le détail, les huit commandes concernées se trouvent dans le sous-menu OneDrive, accessible d’un clic droit sur les fichiers compatibles pour les utilisateurs et utilisatrices disposant des accès Copilot nécessaires. Elles permettent de résumer un document, de générer une FAQ, de comparer plusieurs fichiers ou de poser des questions sur leur contenu. Pour les images, elles proposent également d’en analyser une ou plusieurs, de les comparer et d’en extraire le texte.
Leur suppression débutera à la mi-novembre et se poursuivra progressivement jusqu’au début du mois de décembre 2026. Seuls ces raccourcis sont concernés, puisque les fonctionnalités associées demeureront disponibles depuis le centre d’activité OneDrive.
Dans l’Explorateur de fichiers, il sera également toujours possible d’utiliser l’option « Demander à Copilot » du menu contextuel pour interroger l’assistant sur un fichier sélectionné, ou de passer par l’icône Copilot affichée au survol des fichiers dans la page d’accueil.
Moins de boutons Copilot, mais toujours plus d’intelligence artificielle
Cette décision prolonge les changements engagés au printemps dernier. Depuis, Microsoft a fait marche arrière sur le bouton Copilot flottant imposé dans Word, Excel et PowerPoint, tandis que le Bloc-notes a remplacé son bouton Copilot par une entrée « Outils d’écriture », plus explicite.
Mais comme nous l’expliquions déjà début septembre, ces ajustements ne traduisent aucun désengagement de Microsoft en matière d’intelligence artificielle. Le 7 octobre, le groupe présentait encore sa stratégie d’« intelligence hybride », destinée à faire travailler ensemble des modèles locaux et des services cloud. Parmi les nouveautés annoncées, Copilot pourra, avec autorisation, exploiter le contexte du PC pour réaliser des actions à la demande. Redmond prépare également une intégration facultative de son assistant dans la nouvelle recherche Windows, pour obtenir des réponses directement depuis la barre des tâches.

articles.title: Hackers Use Autonomous AI Agents to Breach Company Websites, Target Over 1,200 Sites
articles.text:
A Chinese-speaking criminal pointed autonomous AI agents at company websites and let them break in with almost no help, and a security researcher watched it happen because the operators left their control panels open on the internet.
The agents tried more than 1,200 sites and reached websites belonging to more than 100 companies, including farm-equipment maker Deere, appliance company SharkNinja and engine maker Cummins, according to Reuters, which reviewed the attacker's own records to identify them. How much data, if any, was taken is not known.
The researcher, Snorre Fagerland of the security firm NorForge, found the operations by scanning the internet for exposed copies of Cairn, an open-source AI tool popular with hackers.
Beginning around October 2, he found about two dozen Cairn instances being used maliciously, which let him read the attackers' work in real time. He set out the findings on Monday, and Reuters, which saw the report before publication, named the victims from its own review of the attacker's activity.
Cairn gives AI agents a starting point and a goal, then lets them work toward it step by step. The agents post what they find to a shared board, and the human operator can add hints along the way. It was built for authorized penetration testing and does other jobs too, but here it was pointed at online shops without permission.
Cairn's author, who posts as "le1xia0," told Reuters the tool was not designed for hacking attacks and that harmful use was not their intention.
What the agents did, and who was hit
NorForge grouped the exposed panels into three clusters and judged more than 20 of them likely to be malicious. The busiest cluster, which NorForge calls AIA0001, is Chinese-language and links 14 panels to more than 1,100 attack projects.
Its aim seems to be lasting access to shop and payment systems for later use, NorForge said, with targets in the United States, Japan and Australia.
A typical task told the agents to find a way to run code on a shop and then plant a web shell uploader. That is a form that saves uploaded files, not one that runs commands, and attackers can swap it for something worse at any time.
NorForge checked one claimed break-in, at a large hardware-parts vendor, and found the web shell live. It independently confirmed the compromise of one very large US retailer, in which the agents found the single cookie setting that selected a vulnerable backend server.
The three named companies told Reuters the damage was limited. Deere said it took steps to fix the problem and had no sign that sensitive information was accessed. SharkNinja said the attack hit a standalone product-support site and that it had contained the threat.
Cummins said it was investigating a report of a possible attack on a website run by one of its vendors. Two smaller businesses also told Reuters they were compromised.
One documented intrusion, by the agent's own account, worked through unauthorized write access to a memcached session store, unsafe handling of saved PHP objects, and a weakness in old Zend Framework code. The paths differ from victim to victim, so this is one chain, not a single method.
Cheap, fast, and largely unsupervised
The instructions were short. The Chinese-speaking operator sketched out preferred tactics in fewer than 100 Chinese characters, Reuters reported, and the agents went from there.
Successful break-ins took a little under 23 hours on average, NorForge found, and the overall success rate across the tools it saw was around 10%, though it cautioned the clusters chase different goals and are not directly comparable.
The cost was low, but the figures are rough. NorForge put the average at about $5 a task, counting attempts that failed or ended early, and said the uncertainty is considerable. Fagerland separately told Reuters the whole campaign had used about $5,000 worth of tokens, or roughly $50 per successful hack.
All the AIA0001 tasks ran under a worker named claudecode_deepseek-v4.1-flash, which could point to a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model driven by Anthropic's Claude Code. Neither the researcher nor Reuters confirmed the models, and Reuters said only that the campaign appeared to use DeepSeek and Claude Code.
The open panels leak the victims' secrets too
Leaving a Cairn panel open is a separate problem from the break-ins. The panels show who is being attacked, what weaknesses were found, and which credentials and keys were taken, so having your site tested on an open instance can expose your secrets, whatever the test's outcome.
NorForge ran the secrets scanner Trufflehog over the panel data and found hundreds of secrets, 11% of which it verified as still valid.
The panels also appear to expose the full set of the tool's controls, including the ability to start and stop projects, feed in new data, and point agents to different targets.
NorForge said it did not test whether those controls work without a login. A second, English-language cluster went further and exposed the operators' own SSH logins to their staging servers; NorForge said it did not log in.
The exposure is not only a criminal problem. NorForge also found apparently legitimate penetration-testing firms that had left real client tests on unsecured panels, putting their customers' data at the same risk.
What to check, and where this came from
Defenders can act on a few points:
- Exposed panels. Agent control panels of this kind often answer on port 8000, so an exposed one without a login is worth hunting for.
- Stray upload forms. An unexpected file-upload form sitting in a hidden directory is the foothold these agents aimed for.
- Magento patching. A worker directory NorForge browsed held a proof-of-concept for a critical Magento flaw, StyleSmuggler (CVE-2026-75650), and a test lab for it. There is no evidence it was used in these break-ins, but any shop still on an affected build should apply Adobe's hotfix for it: Adobe Commerce 2.4.4 through 2.4.9, or Magento Open Source 2.4.6 through 2.4.9.
NorForge's search followed a September report by Gambit Security, a separate campaign in which a criminal used Cairn alongside two other AI tools to steal credit cards; that report is what first flagged Cairn on an attacker's server. No source links the two operations.
NorForge said it is working with Reuters to warn victims and is asking hosting firms to take the panels down, an effort it said depends on how the hosts respond.
