articles.title: AI infrastructure management software startup ASI hits $3B valuation after raising $325M in funding - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI infrastructure management software startup ASI hits $3B valuation after raising $325M in funding
An artificial intelligence startup called ASI Inc., which builds complex models of air traffic and energy grids, said today it has scored $325 million in a Series C funding, bringing its valuation to a cool $3 billion.
The round was led by Spark Capital and joined by participants including Citadel Securities, Craft Ventures, Meritech Capital, Energy Impact Partners and Andreessen Horowitz.
The startup, which used to be known as Air Space Intelligence, is an AI company that develops frontier models designed to model physical reality and simulate future scenarios, so that its customers can plan and orchestrate how they operate critical infrastructure in real time.
It caters to companies in the aviation, defense and energy industries. For instance, it works with the Federal Aviation Administration and airlines such as United Airlines Inc. and Delta Air Lines Inc. to simulate and predict what’s happening in air space, so they can plan their flight operations. It gives pilots and air traffic controllers a way to plan ahead, reduce delays and increase flight safety and efficiency.
In addition, ASI works with the U.S. Army, U.S. Air Force and others, providing them with AI-driven command-and-control software that’s used to manage their daily operations. It also helps companies in the energy sector, including grid operators, enabling them to simulate their grid operations and plan for surges in demand.
ASI founder and Chief Executive Phillip Buckendorf (pictured) said he believes that future economic growth will be dependent on giving the people who run the country’s most critical infrastructure the ability to predict and forecast scenarios ahead of time, so they can avoid failures. “While the broader tech ecosystem spent hundreds of billions teaching AI to manipulate words and generate text, ASI is deeply focused on AI systems that can manage and control physical assets,” he stressed. “This capital ensures ASI scales as America’s engine: the automated nervous system keeping the country running.”
While hundreds of billions have been spent teaching AI to manipulate words and generate videos, ASI builds AI systems that can manage and control critical physical infrastructure – where there is zero margin for error.
Today we announced our $325M Series C to scale America’s… pic.twitter.com/l133h8H92E
— ASI (@AirSpaceIntel) October 20, 2026
The round follows a significant customer win for ASI. In June, it signed an $875 million multiyear agreement with the FAA to manage future air traffic across the U.S. with its AI platform. Impressively, it won the 12-year contract ahead of bigger and better known rivals such as Palantir Technologies Inc. and Thales SE, which both made aggressive bids, according to Bloomberg.
In air traffic scenarios, ASI’s system combines data from flight paths, real-time air traffic, weather and controller staffing to predict congestion and devise ways to get around problems and avoid delays. The FAA implemented the software at Dulles International Airport in Washington DC last month, and plans to expand it to all major U.S. airports in future.
The contract was a significant win for ASI, making the startup one of only four technology companies to land a federal contract of that size since 2000. Since then, ASI has secured another big contract with the U.S. Army. Earlier this month, it announced it had agreed a five-year deal worth $99 million to supply the military with AI software for its command-and-control program. Another big customer is National Grid USA Service Company Inc., which uses ASI’s software for planning purposes.
Going forward, ASI said the money from today’s round will help it expand further into the aviation, defense and energy sectors and also target new industries such as logistics. It’s also planning to grow its research and engineering teams with an eye to expanding the capabilities of its software.

articles.title: Iran threatens to attack undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz, calls them 'legitimate new targets' in future conflict — IRGC spokesman warns that a future 'third phase' in war with US could lead them to sever global data links
articles.text:
Iran threatens to attack undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz, calls them 'legitimate new targets' in future conflict — IRGC spokesman warns that a future 'third phase' in war with US could lead them to sever global data links
Trouble continues in the Strait of Hormuz
The Islamic Republic of Iran has described several undersea fiber cables that run through the Strait of Hormuz as "legitimate new targets." The area has become a hotbed of conflict since the start of military action by the United States, Israel and others in February. General Hossein Mohebbi, a spokesman for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, referred to the cables in comments at an event this week, The Telegraph reports.
"Seven large cables pass beneath the Strait of Hormuz, and all internet and commercial data pass through them," according to Mohebbi. He went on to describe the cables as "legitimate new targets" for future assaults. Meanwhile, another IRGC General, Yadollah Javani, who serves as the IRGC's political deputy, has since suggested that if Iranian infrastructure is attacked, Iran will respond by attacking the cables, according to comments reported by Iran International.
The conflict between the United States and Iran has cooled, but it isn't quite over yet. Mohebbi suggested that a "third phase" in the war would reveal a "new geography" that would include "new targets and new weapons." One particular cable referenced by the IRGC appears to match the Asia-Africa-Europe-1 cable, a cable stretching 15,050 miles from Asia to Europe, traveling through Oman, the UAE and Qatar. Both the UAE and Qatar share direct maritime borders with Iran.
Experts believe the threat is credible. Professor Alesso Patalano, a war and strategy professor at King's College London, told The Telegraph that "not only is it possible, but it's been a rather clear possibility for a long time," adding that divers could "go down to the seabed... and cut them or destroy them." Such attacks aren't "unheard of," going on to reference the Nord Stream 2 gas pipeline attack near Denmark in 2022, supposedly by Ukrainian agents, as an example.
Meanwhile, further comments, made to The Telegraph, suggest that Iran had considered cutting the cables several times since the war began. However, up until now, Tehran had avoided doing so, as it would mean "declaring war on the whole world and building new enemies," according to another unnamed Iranian spokesman, although stating that it would continue to be "an option if Trump escalates."
Iran isn't the only country that has taken a special interest in undersea infrastructure. A Russian ship, for instance, was chased from British waters by a Royal Navy attack helicopter earlier this year as it loitered for 14 hours less than a mile from five undersea cables that connect the UK with Spain, Portugal, Canada, and the U.S.

articles.title: Google Gemini arrive dans votre voiture avec un assistant IA beaucoup plus personnel
articles.text:
Google a démarré le déploiement d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité IA dans Android Auto. Son nom ? « Personal Intelligence ».
Android Auto évolue et l’intelligence artificielle y est pour beaucoup. Une récente version bêta du service a dévoilé les premières briques de la nouvelle interface personnalisable Cielo, qui donne à Gemini un accès plus large aux données Google Workspace. L’assistant, intégré à Android Auto depuis fin 2025, va, grâce à une nouvelle fonctionnalité, prendre encore plus de place dans le quotidien des conducteurs. On fait le point.
Gemini fournit désormais des réponses sur mesure dans Android Auto
Google vient de lancer une nouvelle fonctionnalité, qui relie Gemini à Gmail, Agenda, Photos, Maps, YouTube et à votre historique de recherche. Nommée Personal Intelligence, elle permet, si l’on en croit l’annonce, d’interroger l’IA et d’obtenir toutes sortes d’informations en conversant en langage naturel : une porte d’embarquement, l’état d’un vol, une suggestion de restaurant basée sur les habitudes alimentaires, un itinéraire vers un rendez-vous médical sans avoir à saisir d’adresse et bien plus encore.
La fonction Personal Intelligence est déployée dans un premier temps sur Android Auto et sera, par la suite, accessible dans les voitures équipées de Google. Elle aurait, selon le géant de la Tech, deux points forts : « la capacité à extraire des informations précises, par exemple d’un courriel, d’une photo ou d'un lieu enregistré dans Google Maps, pour répondre à votre question, et le raisonnement à partir de sources complexes ». Google n’en dit toutefois pas plus sur la fiabilité des réponses ou la manière dont seront gérées les erreurs.
Un copilote qui en sait un peu trop ?
Bien sûr Google se veut rassurant et indique qu’il a « conçu Personal Intelligence en plaçant la confidentialité au cœur de sa conception ». Dans les faits, aucune application ne sera connectée sans votre accord et la fonction pourra être désactivée à tout moment dans les réglages de Gemini. Sur les véhicules équipés de Google, les réponses ne seront disponibles que si vous êtes à bord et que votre téléphone est connecté.
La prudence reste, toutefois, de mise car on sait à quel point Google peut être gourmand en données personnelles : en accordant trop de permissions à Gemini, l’assistant aura accès à une grande partie de votre vie numérique. Il est donc essentiel de bien choisir les applications que l’on souhaite connecter.
Le déploiement de Personal Intelligence a démarré hier sur Android Auto. La fonction est réservée aux comptes personnels des plus de 18 ans : les comptes professionnels et scolaires n’y ont pas encore accès. Bien que Google parle d’une disponibilité globale, l’espace économique européen, la Suisse, le Royaume-Uni et le Nigéria ne sont pas dans la boucle pour le moment. Les français devront donc patienter avant de pouvoir tester cette nouvelle option.
- Multimodalité texte, voix et fichiers
- Intégration poussée aux services Google
- Applications Web, mobile et bureau
- Interface simplifiée et claire
- Intégration fluide des apps mobiles
- Commandes vocales efficaces

articles.title: Falha em certificados digitais coloca internet em alerta • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Falha em certificados digitais coloca internet em alerta
Chaves privadas fracas poderiam permitir a criação de certificados falsos para qualquer site.
A descoberta de oito certificados digitais comprometidos da autoridade certificadora eMudhra colocou empresas e pesquisadores de segurança em alerta. As chaves privadas eram tão fracas que poderiam ser recuperadas e usadas para emitir certificados falsos capazes de se passar por sites e serviços legítimos.
Seis dos certificados intermediários afetados eram usados para TLS, tecnologia por trás das conexões HTTPS, enquanto outros dois eram destinados à assinatura de código. Mozilla, Google, Apple e Microsoft receberam o alerta no sábado (17), e fabricantes começaram a bloquear os certificados comprometidos pouco depois.
O HTTPS usa certificados digitais para comprovar que o usuário está realmente conectado ao site que pretende acessar. Eles funcionam como uma espécie de documento de identidade reconhecido pelo navegador e ajudam a impedir que outro servidor se passe pelo original.
Com acesso às chaves privadas, alguém poderia criar certificados falsos para sites e serviços que seriam aceitos como legítimos por sistemas vulneráveis. Um pesquisador identificado como Wayne demonstrou ter acesso às oito chaves ao usá-las para assinar digitalmente uma mensagem enviada às empresas responsáveis pelos principais navegadores e sistemas. Segundo a Mozilla, seus engenheiros conseguiram recuperar as mesmas chaves pouco depois, confirmando a falha.
Isso não significa que um invasor poderia interceptar qualquer conexão pela internet. Segundo o Ars Technica, ainda seria necessário interceptar o tráfego entre a vítima e o serviço para explorar os certificados em um ataque.
A Mozilla afirma que concluiu o bloqueio dos certificados no Firefox menos de três horas após receber o alerta. A empresa também lançou o Firefox 158.0.1 para ampliar a proteção aos usuários. Chrome e outros navegadores também passaram a rejeitar os certificados comprometidos.
Havia uma exceção no momento da publicação: o Microsoft Edge no Windows 10 ainda conseguia estabelecer conexão com alguns servidores vulneráveis. A Microsoft foi questionada sobre o caso, mas não detalhou quando aplicaria o bloqueio nesse sistema.
Até o momento, não há relatos públicos de certificados fraudulentos utilizados em ataques. Esse tipo de medida já foi adotado em outras situações. O Chrome, por exemplo, deixou de confiar em certificados da Entrust após o Google apontar problemas na atuação da autoridade certificadora.
O principal problema agora está fora dos navegadores. Distribuições Linux, aplicativos e dispositivos conectados podem continuar confiando nas credenciais comprometidas até receberem atualizações. O engenheiro de criptografia Filippo Valsorda disse ao Ars Technica que o trabalho de limpeza pode ser maior do que o provocado pelo Heartbleed, grave vulnerabilidade descoberta em 2014, pela variedade de sistemas que precisam ser atualizados.
Para usuários comuns, a principal recomendação é manter navegador, sistema operacional e aplicativos atualizados. Serviços como Signal e WhatsApp não dependem do TLS para proteger o conteúdo das mensagens e, por isso, não são afetados da mesma forma.

articles.title: Corsair Updates Sabre V3 Pro Line-Up With New PureVector Ergo, Carbon Fiber, and Magnesium Gaming Mice
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Corsair Updates Sabre V3 Pro Line-Up With New PureVector Ergo, Carbon Fiber, and Magnesium Gaming Mice
Corsair has officially updated its Sabre V3 Pro mouse line-up with the PureVector series, a new partnership with Aimlabs that the brand claims can reduce aiming and correction time by as much as 33%. The PureVector nomenclature denotes a new tech developed by Corsair and Aimlabs that helps gamers optimize directional DPI to tune their mouse sensor for their own aiming style. The idea is that players would play through a calibration sequence inside Aimlabs while PureVector gathers data on their specific weak points and movement patterns, which the software will then use to build a custom DPI table based on movement direction, and then flash that directional DPI map to the mouse's firmware. 
The new tech comes preloaded on six new Sabre v3 Pro PureVector models, spanning three materials and two distinct shapes. The Sabre v3 Pro PureVector series offers both a symmetrical shape—measuring 122.9 (L) × 64.1 (W) × 38.8 mm (H)—which is based on the Sabre v2 shape that launched in late 2025, and a new right-handed ergonomic shape that measures in at 125 (L) × 67.5 (W) × 44 (H) mm. Both shapes are available from Corsair with a shell made of regular ABS (Ultralight model, $179.99), carbon fiber (CF model, $229.99), and magnesium (MG model, $199.99), with the latter featuring cutouts in the top of the shell for weight reduction.Internally, all of the Corsair Sabre v3 Pro PureVector mice are the same, packing a Corsair Marksman X sensor with 42,000 DPI peak sensitivity, 800 IPS tracking speed, and 70 G acceleration. The mice are also all capable of 8 kHz polling in both wired and 2.4 GHz wireless modes, and the built-in rechargeable battery has a claimed battery life of up to 200 hours at 1 kHz polling and 31 hours at 8 kHz polling rate. They also all use Corsair-tuned optical mouse switches for the left and right clicks. The mice are also all customizable in Corsair's Web Hub browser-based utility.The weights of the different versions of the Corsair Sabre v3 Pro PureVector mice are as follows:
- Sabre v3 Pro Pure Vector: 37 g
- Sabre v3 Pro PureVector Ergo: 41 g
- Sabre v3 Pro PureVector MG: 49 g
- Sabre v3 Pro PureVector MG Ergo: 55 g
- Sabre v3 Pro PureVector CF: 48 g
- Sabre v3 Pro PureVector CF Ergo: 54 g

articles.title: Ex-OpenAI Engineer Detained in Spy Device Case as Saudi Royal Contacts Emerge
articles.text:
A U.S. court on Monday granted the U.S. government's request to detain a former OpenAI engineer accused of planting a recording device in an executive conference room at the company's San Francisco office to allegedly steal sensitive secrets.
In a new court filing Sunday, prosecutors revealed that Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national, was "in frequent communications via WhatsApp with a member of the Saudi Royal Family" throughout 2025 and 2026. Alfozan is said to have communicated with the Saudi royal as recently as October 5, 2026, four days before he was arrested.
"Among other things, the individual told the defendant that an artificial intelligence initiative was being launched in Saudi Arabia and wanted the defendant to join it," the filing reads. "In May 2026, the individual told the defendant, 'Saudi needs you more then [sic] the US!' to which the defendant responded '100,' indicating he agreed."
The Saudi Royal Family member is said to have repeatedly attempted to recruit Alfozan and even asked when he planned to leave OpenAI, to which the defendant said he wouldn't do so until his stock vested.
Alfozan joined OpenAI as an engineer around July 2025 with an annual base salary of $385,000. Last week, the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) revealed that he had been arrested for allegedly inserting a stealthy audio recording device into a USB port on the back of a television in the executive conference room to capture sensitive conversations.
The defendant is also said to have modified the device to prevent data transfer between it and the television and encrypted the content stored on the device's microSD card. In addition, he used his wife's personal ChatGPT account to research how to "build a continuous audio recorder" to "captur[e] microphone audio and save compressed WAV recordings to an SD card."
"In the days and weeks before placing the device, the defendant (i) used an OpenAI productivity agent to ascertain which 'meeting rooms' OpenAI 'leadership and exec[utives]' used, and where they met with 'external partners'; and (ii) spent considerable time near the conference room where he later installed the device," the filing said.
Alfozan has been charged with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. If convicted, he faces a maximum possible sentence of five years in prison.
Prosecutors also argued that Alfozan is a flight risk, stating he has "ample resources... and what appears to be considerable support from a foreign government that has (i) no extradition treaty with the United States; (ii) limitless resources; and (iii) the ability to provide extraordinary travel assistance," according to the filing.
Shortly after details of his arrest became public knowledge, it emerged that the defendant had planned to depart to Riyadh with his wife and son on a one-way ticket on October 12, 2026. Although he was arrested three days prior, his wife and son are said to have already left the U.S. without him.
The day before her departure, Alfozan's wife allegedly told the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) agents that her U.S. visa was expiring and that she, along with her son, were permanently shifting back to Saudi Arabia.
"The defendant went to significant lengths to create customized, encrypted recording devices to secretly record highly sensitive meetings involving senior OpenAI personnel and executives, high-level business counterparts, and government officials, all while communicating with individuals of significance in Saudi Arabia and pursuing opportunities in – and making plans to travel to – Saudi Arabia," the filing said.
Stating the U.S. government's investigation is ongoing, prosecutors said a search of the defendant's residence and a "preliminary review" of his electronic devices, including his cellphone, uncovered several pieces of evidence -
- Several electronic components similar to those in the customized devices the defendant installed in the OpenAI conference room and had in his missing bag were identified in his residence.
- Photographs from his iPhone dated between September 22 and 28, 2026, that depict one additional concealed recording device, as well as what appear to be the input/output panels on TVs and other electronic devices in various locations in OpenAI buildings, including a second conference room where sensitive meetings took place.
- A deleted note on his cellphone from September 2026 included links to various recording devices, including those made by Seeed Studio, the same manufacturer whose devices were found in OpenAI's offices and his residence.
- Browsing history showed that the defendant accessed a folder called "Saudi Gov Docs" on October 4, 2026, and he used an OpenAI productivity agent to inquire about various Saudi-related business and government-related engagements from the Saudi Ministry of Communication and Information Technology (MCIT) between July 6, 2026, and September 21, 2026.
"The defendant leveraged his skills as a highly-educated engineer to create sophisticated recording devices that – the evidence strongly suggests – he intended to bring with him to Saudi Arabia," the filing said.
"Whether the defendant wanted to record OpenAI meetings to enrich himself by enhancing his own business prospects, or to provide aid a foreign government, or both, his conduct is criminal and it presents a danger to innovation in the Silicon Valley and a concern for the national security of the United States."

articles.title: Google unveils TorchTPU in a push to break Nvidia's stranglehold on AI compute - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Google unveils TorchTPU in a push to break Nvidia’s stranglehold on AI compute
Google LLC is striving to pry open Nvidia Corp.’s grip on the artificial intelligence computing industry with the launch of a specialized version of the open-source PyTorch framework, called TorchTPU, which is designed to eliminate a key advantage of its rival.
One of the reasons why Nvidia and its graphics processing units remain so dominant in the AI industry is that the vast majority of AI applications are written specifically to run on its GPUs, and it’s this reality that Google is trying to change with today’s release.
The PyTorch framework is a popular open-source toolkit that developers use to create, train and run AI models and neural networks. According to some accounts, more than 85% of all AI applications are created using PyTorch, which was created by Meta Platforms Inc. in 2016, long before anyone realized that large language models would come along to enable the AI boom.
Back then, Nvidia’s GPUs were already the preferred hardware used by developers for AI research, so Meta designed PyTorch specifically to work with that company’s chips. The focus on Nvidia’s hardware has continued, even after Meta open-sourced PyTorch in 2022, handing over stewardship to the nonprofit Linux Foundation.
With TorchTPU, Google has created an alternative version of PyTorch that makes it easier for developers to create models and applications that can run on its Tensor Processing Units or TPUs, which are specialized chips for AI workloads. TorchTPU also provides a simple way for developers to run existing apps and models on TPUs by making a few simple configuration tweaks, without having to rewrite any of the underlying code.
Google isn’t alone in trying to undermine the massive advantage Nvidia had thanks to PyTorch. In fact, it was just earlier this week that Amazon Web Services Inc. announced its own flavor of PyTorch, called TorchNeuron. Similar to TorchTPU, TorchNeuron makes it easy to run AI applications on different hardware, in this case Amazon’s Trainum chips. Amazon went even further, revealing that it has contributed code to the original PyTorch project that will decouple a number of key features from Nvidia’s GPUs, with the aim being to make it more compatible with any kind of hardware.
Google didn’t do that, but it may have gained an advantage over AWS in a couple of other ways. For one thing, the company said it collaborated closely with Meta, Hugging Face and a couple of startups called Inferact Inc. and RadixArk Inc., the developers of vLLM and SGLang, to ensure that various TorchTPU features and code libraries are compatible with their developer tools. With that, it has erased another advantage PyTorch brings.
Google also did something else that AWS didn’t. It revealed a new tool called the TPU agent suite that is meant to help developers move their AI applications to the Google Cloud platform and automatically fix any errors that occur during the migration process. Furthermore, it updated an existing tool called LiteRT, which is used to build AI applications that run directly smartphones, laptops and embedded devices rather than in the cloud. So it should now be compatible with PyTorch-based apps, Google said.
It’s clear that both cloud infrastructure providers are more eager than ever to win their fair share of AI workloads, and they understand that they need to cater to developers to get it, said Holger Mueller of Constellation Research. “Rebuilding PyTorch is one of the best ways to do that, because it makes it easier for developers to move their application code onto Google’s and Amazon’s respective compute platforms,” the analyst said. “It’s a win for developers and enterprises alike, because it means they have more choice about where to run their AI workloads, but it remains to be seen how much they can chip away at Nvidia’s strongly entrenched position.”
Of course, it will take more than this to convince millions of developers to drop Nvidia’s GPUs and rush to Google’s TPUs. But it does suggest that Google is confident it can chip away at Nvidia’s lead in the longer term.

articles.title: J'ai testé l'Ugreen Nexode 25000mAh : la batterie externe ultra-puissante de 200 W, idéale pour recharger votre PC portable
articles.text:
| Capacité nominale annoncée | 25000 mAh | 
| Capacité réelle annoncée | 18000 mAh | 
| Connectique | 2 x USB-C, 1 x USB-A | 
| Câble intégré | Non | 
| Charge sans-fil | Non | 
| Poids | 592 g | 
| Dimensions | 54 x 51 x 131 mm | 
Avec une capacité annoncée de 25 000 mAh et une puissance cumulée de 200 W, l'Ugreen Nexode ne compte pas se limiter à la recharge d'un smartphone. Cette batterie externe entend aussi prolonger la vie d'ordinateurs portables et autres appareils énergivores.
Ugreen poursuit le développement de sa gamme Nexode avec une batterie externe qui mise autant sur sa capacité que sur sa puissance. Affichant 25 000 mAh au compteur, soit une réserve énergétique de 90 Wh, ce modèle entend répondre aux besoins des utilisateurs en déplacement, loin de toute prise électrique, qu'ils soient équipés d'un smartphone, d'une tablette ou même d'un ordinateur portable.
Le fabricant annonce une puissance totale de 200 W, répartie entre trois ports USB, dont deux USB-C capables de délivrer respectivement jusqu'à 140 et 100 W. Un petit écran couleur se charge de communiquer les informations essentielles sur le fonctionnement de l'ensemble. De quoi séduire les utilisateurs qui aiment garder un œil sur les watts qui transitent dans leurs appareils.
Ugreen accompagne le tout de diverses protections électriques et revendique une capacité conservée supérieure à 80 % après 1000 cycles de charge. Une promesse de longévité intéressante, mais que notre protocole de test ne permet évidemment pas de vérifier.
Cette Nexode est commercialisée au tarif de 119 € à son lancement, même si le site officiel du constructeur l'affiche régulièrement autour de 75 €. Elle se frotte notamment à la PowerBank 25K 165W d’Anker.
Plutôt qu'un large rectangle aplati façon SSD, l'Ugreen Nexode adopte un format vertical aux angles arrondis avec une coque gris métallisé et une partie supérieure noire. L'ensemble affiche une certaine sobriété et ne déparerait pas sur un bureau, à côté d'un ordinateur portable.
Avec des dimensions de 13,1 x 5,4 x 5,1 cm, la batterie occupe un volume d'environ 361 cm³. Un encombrement plutôt contenu au regard de la réserve d'énergie embarquée, même si ses 592 g rappellent rapidement qu'il ne s'agit pas d'un accessoire à glisser dans une poche de pantalon. Un sac à dos est nettement plus indiqué pour transporter ce petit pavé. Sa forme lui permet néanmoins de tenir debout sur une surface plane, ce qui limite la place occupée lorsqu'elle est utilisée sur un bureau.
L'essentiel de la connectique est installé sur la tranche supérieure. On y trouve deux ports USB-C accompagnés d'un USB-A reconnaissable à sa languette violette. Cette disposition facilite l'accès aux connecteurs quand la batterie est posée verticalement. Les trois sorties permettent d'alimenter autant d'appareils simultanément, sous réserve de respecter la puissance totale disponible. En revanche, aucun câble n'est directement intégré à la batterie, pas plus qu'un système de recharge sans-fil.
La façade accueille un écran TFT couleur logé derrière une surface noire brillante qui contraste avec le reste du boîtier. Son intérêt dépasse le simple affichage du pourcentage de batterie restant ; il peut aussi renseigner sur les tensions, les courants et les puissances en entrée ou en sortie. Des indications appréciables pour vérifier qu'un appareil profite bien de la recharge attendue.
Un bouton placé sur la tranche permet d'interagir avec cet affichage. Seul bémol esthétique, la surface brillante se montre assez accueillante envers les empreintes digitales et rayures superficielles.
Enfin, avec ses 90 Wh, la Nexode demeure sous la limite habituelle de 100 Wh admise sans autorisation particulière en cabine d'avion. Il faudra néanmoins respecter les conditions de transport de la compagnie aérienne, les batteries externes au lithium n'étant pas admises en soute.
Avec 25 000 mAh annoncés sous une tension nominale de 3,6 V, l'Ugreen Nexode dispose théoriquement de 90 Wh d'énergie. Cette valeur la situe parmi les batteries externes de grande capacité, capables d'assurer plusieurs recharges avant de devoir elles-mêmes retrouver une prise de courant.
Reste que toute cette énergie n'est pas intégralement restituée. Les circuits de conversion, l'électronique embarquée et les pertes inhérentes au processus de recharge viennent nécessairement réduire la quantité réellement disponible. C'est précisément ce que nos mesures permettent d'évaluer.
Dans les conditions de notre protocole, nous avons relevé une capacité exploitable équivalente à 21 236 mAh sous la tension de référence de 3,6 V, soit environ 76,4 Wh. La Nexode restitue ainsi près de 85 % de sa capacité théorique, avec un écart d'environ 15 % par rapport à la valeur annoncée. Un résultat encourageant qui laisse une belle marge de manœuvre pour alimenter plusieurs appareils.
| Nb. charges Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra | Nb. charges Apple iPhone 15 Pro | Nb. charges Apple iPad Pro 13 (2024) | Nb. charges Nintendo Switch | Nb. charges Sony WH-1000XM5 | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4,25 | 6,49 | 2,06 | 4,93 | 17,7 | 
Pour donner une idée plus concrète de cette réserve, nos équivalences de capacité correspondent à 4,25 recharges d'un Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra, 2,06 d'un iPad Pro 13 pouces et 4,93 d'une Nintendo Switch. De quoi envisager plusieurs journées d'utilisation mobile sans devoir systématiquement chercher une prise. Ces estimations sont bien entendu théoriques : le nombre de recharges effectivement réalisées dépendra aussi des pertes propres à chaque appareil.
Si l'autonomie constitue l'un des arguments de l’Ugreen Nexode, c'est avant tout sa puissance annoncée qui attire l'attention. Le constructeur promet jusqu'à 200 W en sortie cumulée, une valeur destinée à répondre aux besoins d'appareils autrement exigeants qu'une simple paire d'écouteurs.
Le premier port USB-C peut théoriquement atteindre 140 W grâce au Power Delivery 3.1, avec un profil culminant à 28 V et 5 A. Le second USB-C se limite à 100 W, tandis que l'USB-A peut monter jusqu'à 22,5 W avec les équipements compatibles. Attention toutefois à ne pas additionner sans distinction les puissances maximales individuelles : la puissance globale reste plafonnée à 200 W, impliquant un partage entre les appareils branchés.
La batterie prend également en charge différents protocoles de charge rapide, une polyvalence bienvenue pour passer d'un smartphone Android à une tablette ou à un ordinateur portable sans nécessairement multiplier les chargeurs.
Lors de notre série de mesures, nous avons enregistré 13,05 W sous 5 V, puis 28,25 W à 9 V et 38,49 W à 12 V. La puissance grimpe ensuite à 48,69 W sous 15 V, pour finalement atteindre 65,69 W à 20 V. Une progression régulière qui traduit une intensité d'environ 3 A, légèrement supérieure sur les paliers les plus élevés.
Ces résultats témoignent d'une puissance déjà confortable pour la recharge rapide de nombreux appareils du quotidien. Ils ne suffisent cependant pas à confirmer les 140 W promis sur le premier USB-C, puisque nos relevés ne couvrent pas le profil 28 V nécessaire pour atteindre cette valeur. Le plafond cumulé de 200 W n'a pas non plus été vérifié par un essai de charge simultanée à pleine puissance. Impossible donc de valider ou d'infirmer ces deux annonces sur la seule base de nos résultats.
Quant à la recharge de la batterie elle-même, elle peut s'effectuer par l'un ou l'autre des ports USB-C, tous deux annoncés compatibles avec une entrée maximale de 65 W. Il faudra donc prévoir un chargeur suffisamment puissant pour profiter pleinement de cette possibilité.
L’Ugreen Nexode 25000 mAh (200W) séduit par sa capacité exploitable particulièrement généreuse, son rendement satisfaisant et ses trois ports USB adaptés aux usages intensifs. Son format vertical, sa connectique accessible et son écran couleur renforcent son ergonomie. En revanche, son poids élevé, l’absence de câble intégré et de charge sans-fil nuisent à sa praticité. Malgré ces réserves, elle constitue une solution polyvalente et convaincante pour les utilisateurs exigeants, surtout en période de promotion.
Face à l’Anker PowerBank 25K 165W, l’Ugreen Nexode se distingue par une meilleure endurance et un écran riche en informations. Sa connectique polyvalente constitue aussi un atout, mais l’Anker s'avère plus pratique grâce à ses câbles intégrés et s'est montrée plus performante lors de nos mesures de puissance.

articles.title: Investigadores hallaron más de 6.800 chats privados de la IA Muse de Meta expuestos en internet
articles.text:
Claroc, una firma de ciberseguridad encontró más de 6.800 conversaciones que usuarios compartieron con Muse, el asistente de inteligencia artificial de Meta, accesibles para cualquiera en internet sin que nadie les hubiera enviado el enlace.
La empresa, especializada en ciberseguridad, llegó a esas conversaciones mediante una búsqueda de DNS pasivo, una técnica que registra los nombres de dominio que ya circularon en internet. Abrió solo algunos cientos de los enlaces hallados y dejó el resto sin revisar.
El problema nace del propio diseño de Muse. Cuando un usuario pide compartir una charla con el asistente, Meta genera una página pública y arma la dirección web con el título que el usuario le puso a esa conversación. Ese nombre queda registrado en los servidores de DNS, visibles para cualquiera que sepa buscarlos.
Eso significa que no hace falta recibir el enlace para entrar a la página: alcanza con rastrear los nombres de dominio del servicio, algo que Claroc hizo con una sola consulta a una base de datos comercial. El sitio urlscan.io, que cualquiera puede usar, ya guardaba más de 75 capturas de esas páginas.
Qué se encontró en los datos de Muse
Entre los enlaces revisados, Claroc halló un documento con los apuntes de una persona que se preparaba para una entrevista confidencial con un laboratorio de inteligencia artificial, con el nombre del contacto interno y el horario exacto de la reunión.
Asimismo, encontró la revisión interna de ingresos de una empresa de marketing, dirigida a su director ejecutivo; una solicitud de préstamo con el monto pedido por su dueño; una lista de tareas con una alerta de fraude bancario y un número de cuenta parcial; y un informe de un inversor inmobiliario con direcciones de propiedades y cifras de rentabilidad.
Claroc también accedió al calendario anual de vacaciones de una empresa, con el nombre de cada empleado junto a la semana en la que estaría ausente. La firma aclaró que no identificó a ninguna de las personas ni empresas afectadas en su publicación.
No se trató de un ataque informático clásico. Muse respetó exactamente lo que cada usuario le pidió: compartir esa conversación puntual. El fallo está en que la dirección de esa página terminó siendo pública y fácil de reconstruir a partir de su propio título.
Claroc recordó un problema similar ocurrido en 2025, cuando conversaciones compartidas de ChatGPT aparecieron en los resultados de Google y OpenAI tuvo que retirar la opción que las hacía indexables. Después, Google ya había indexado más de 370 mil conversaciones de Grok, el chatbot de xAI.
Meta no respondió a los reclamos
La firma de seguridad informó el hallazgo al programa de recompensas por errores de Meta el 8 de octubre de 2026 y, según contó su cofundador y director de tecnología, Asaf Aproszper, no recibió ninguna respuesta de la empresa. Meta tampoco contestó las preguntas que le envió Ars Technica por correo electrónico.
Claroc dijo no tener pruebas de que alguien haya usado esa información de forma maliciosa, aunque aclaró que solo monitoreó un canal de búsqueda entre varios posibles.
El último día que revisó el sistema, aparecieron 27 páginas nuevas generadas por usuarios que seguían compartiendo conversaciones.
Muse se lanzó el 8 de septiembre de 2026 y rápidamente se ubicó entre las aplicaciones más descargadas de la tienda de Apple. El asistente puede completar formularios, hacer compras y gestionar cuentas de correo y calendario en nombre de sus usuarios.
La filtración se suma a una serie de tropiezos de seguridad que atravesó Muse desde su lanzamiento. A fines de septiembre del mismo año, un investigador descubrió una falla que permitía a cualquier aplicación instalada en la computadora tomar el control total de una cuenta de Muse, algo que Meta corrigió horas después de conocerse el caso.
Semanas más tarde, la revista Time reveló que Muse arma perfiles detallados sobre los contactos de cada usuario a partir de sus mensajes y correos, y un usuario denunció públicamente que el asistente compartió su dirección particular con un desconocido durante una venta en Facebook Marketplace.

articles.title: ‘Your TV should do what you paid for’: People are so sick of ads, trackers and bloat in their smart TVs that their using AI to vibe code them away
articles.text:
‘Your TV should do what you paid for’: People are vibe-coding apps to banish ads from their smart TVs and Android TV — and it’s catching on
Putting a stop to the madness
- Developers are stripping ads and tracking from smart TVs
- They’re using AI vibe coding to quickly spin up solutions
- Customers are growing increasingly frustrated with TV streaming bloat
If you’re sick of your smart TV being plastered with sponsored ads, slowed down with bloat, and infested with trackers, you’re not alone. But instead of putting up with the countless intrusions, some people are stripping the unwanted cruft from their TVs altogether — thanks to a little AI vibe coding.
As reported by TechCrunch, a number of developers have offered solutions in recent weeks. That includes one called dumbtv, which sets out its mission statement on its GitHub page: “Your TV should do what you paid for: your apps, your HDMI inputs, and nothing else. No ads from the TV itself, no watch tracking, no update you did not ask for.” To that end, dumbtv removes “Ads, telemetry, experiments and Alexa,” as well as any apps the user selects, from all manner of smart TVs.
Another option, this time called cleanyourtv, says it will “Strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, and replace the ad-filled home screen with a clean launcher that looks like an Apple TV. No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind.” Both projects claim to be fully reversible and say they do not touch the TV’s root directory.
You might not even need to download a GitHub project to debloat your smart TV. Posting on X, Ryan Doyle said they simply found a listing for their TV and asked Claude Code, “can you hack this?” The AI agent then walked Doyle through the steps to remove “ads, bloatware, spyware” and speed up the “laggy UI,” resulting in a far better user experience.
AI meets user frustration
At the other end of the spectrum from the simple solutions mentioned above is the ad-free Android TV setup created by a developer known as Cretezy. Instead of merely blocking advertising and tracking features in Android TV, it aims to replace many aspects of the operating system altogether. It includes an ad-free launch screen, a YouTube substitute, a media manager, and a remote control button remapper. Although it might sound complicated, Cretezy says that an AI agent can set the whole thing up for you and tailor it to your TV, demonstrating how AI can make removing bloat as simple as possible.
People have been getting their hands dirty with TVs for almost as long as they’ve existed. But what’s different this time is the power that AI has given people to quickly spin up a targeted solution in hours rather than days or weeks. That reduction in overhead has led to a proliferation of hacks and workarounds that remove annoying features many people would rather not have.
The timing plays a role in other ways. Right now, many consumers are growing frustrated with streaming TV providers, whose prices have risen and whose ads have become increasingly intrusive. Throw in rising awareness of the ways that Big Tech firms are tracking and monetizing their own customers, and you’ve got a recipe for answers like dumbtv and cleanyourtv.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
So, if you’re sick of how slow and bloated your smart TV has become, all it takes to fix it is a simple AI prompt and a little tinkering. The days of ensh*ttified TVs could be numbered.

articles.title: ChatGPT lance les conversations verrouillées : une nouvelle option de confidentialité très attendue
articles.text:
OpenAI déploie une nouvelle fonction permettant de verrouiller certaines conversations ChatGPT à l’aide d’un code PIN ou d’une authentification biométrique. Une protection bienvenue pour les échanges personnels, avec toutefois une précaution importante avant de l’activer.
On raconte désormais beaucoup de choses à ChatGPT. Des questions professionnelles aux problèmes personnels, en passant par des informations parfois confidentielles, nos conversations peuvent contenir bien davantage qu’une simple demande de recette de cuisine. Et lorsqu’on partage son ordinateur ou qu'on prête son téléphone, mieux vaut éviter que le premier venu puisse parcourir tout cet historique. OpenAI propose enfin une solution avec les conversations verrouillées, une fonction repérée cet été dans le code de l’application Android et désormais officiellement disponible. Mais attention : perdre son code pourrait coûter beaucoup plus cher que quelques minutes à chercher dans ses mots de passe.
Un code PIN ou Face ID pour protéger vos conversations ChatGPT
Dans ses notes de mise à jour du 20 octobre, OpenAI annonce le déploiement des conversations verrouillées sur ChatGPT.
Pour protéger une discussion, il suffit d’ouvrir son menu à trois points et de sélectionner l’option « Verrouiller la conversation ». L’utilisateur doit alors créer un code PIN à quatre chiffres, qui servira à retrouver ses échanges protégés depuis la rubrique « Conversations verrouillées » des Projets.
Ces discussions disparaissent de l’historique classique, des conversations épinglées et des résultats de recherche. Elles restent néanmoins enregistrées sur le compte, sans être supprimées. Sur iPhone, il est également possible d’utiliser Face ID ou Touch ID. Les smartphones Android compatibles peuvent recourir au système de déverrouillage de l'appareil.
La nouveauté concerne tous les abonnements ChatGPT, gratuits comme payants, sur le Web, iOS, Android et les nouvelles applications pour macOS et Windows. Le déploiement est progressif et aucune restriction géographique particulière n’est annoncée. La disponibilité immédiate sur l’ensemble des comptes français n'est toutefois pas garantie.
Un oubli du code peut entraîner la suppression définitive des échanges
Cette fonction avait déjà été repérée en août dernier, avant son officialisation cette semaine. Elle apporte une protection supplémentaire contre les regards indiscrets, mais ne transforme pas les discussions en coffre-fort numérique. OpenAI précise que le verrouillage ne repose pas sur un chiffrement de bout en bout spécifique et ne modifie ni la durée de conservation des données ni les paramètres autorisant leur utilisation pour améliorer ses modèles.
Autre limite : les informations déjà mémorisées par ChatGPT avant le verrouillage d’une conversation ne sont pas automatiquement effacées. Les liens de partage créés auparavant restent également accessibles tant qu’ils ne sont pas supprimés séparément.
Mais le principal avertissement concerne le code PIN. Selon la documentation officielle d’OpenAI, sa réinitialisation entraîne la suppression définitive de toutes les conversations verrouillées, ainsi que des fichiers et informations protégés uniquement par ce code. Même le support d'OpenAI ne pourra pas les récupérer. Il reste heureusement possible de modifier son code sans rien perdre, à condition de connaître l'ancien.
Une fonction donc particulièrement utile pour conserver certaines discussions, contenant des données particulièrement intimes ou sensibles, à l’abri des regards, notamment sur un appareil partagé. À condition de choisir un code que l’on n’oubliera pas au prochain changement de téléphone.
- Chat dans différentes langues, dont le français
- Générer, traduire et obtenir un résumé de texte
- Générer, optimiser et corriger du code

articles.title: Déploiement de la 6G : Apple met déjà le paquet pour s'y préparer
articles.text:
Pour rappel, Apple a longtemps eu recours à Qualcomm pour mettre au point ses modems. La firme a ensuite pris la décision de les confectionner elle-même, ce qui a abouti aux modems C1, C1X et plus récemment C2. Mais une révolution technologique arrive avec la 6G, qui commence à pointer le bout de son nez. L’entreprise à la pomme doit dès maintenant s’y préparer, et elle cherche la personne qui sera en mesure de tirer pleinement profit de cette technologie.
Apple recrute un ingénieur 6G
Apple vient de publier une nouvelle offre d’emploi, basée soit à San Diego, soit à Sunnyvale (Californie). Le titre de l’offre d’emploi laisse peu de doute quant à la fonction à exercer : ingénieur systèmes de modems cellulaires 6G. Le futur employé sera donc chargé de développer, avec ses équipes, les prochains modems Apple qui supporteront la 6G. La firme précise qu’il sera « responsable du cycle de vie complet des systèmes de modems cellulaires : de la définition des fonctionnalités et des capacités visant à améliorer l’expérience utilisateur de nos produits, en passant par la conception, le développement d’algorithmes, la mise en production et l’intégration sur silicium ».
Au niveau des qualifications minimales requises, il faut s’accrocher : un baccalauréat en génie électrique, en génie informatique ou dans un domaine connexe, accompagné de plus de 10 ans d’expérience pertinente dans l’industrie ; une solide connaissance des normes de communication cellulaire et des ensembles de fonctionnalités associés ; ainsi qu’une maîtrise de MATLAB, C/C++ et/ou Python. Apple précise aussi que l’employé doit avoir de l’expérience dans l’utilisation de l’IA générative et des outils basés sur les LLM « pour accélérer les flux de travail d’ingénierie ».
Enfin, côté salaire, Apple annonce une rémunération annuelle qui se situe entre 184 700 $ et 324 800 $, tout en précisant que le salaire de base peut varier en fonction de l’expérience, des compétences et des qualifications.
La 6G arrive en 2028, Apple doit s’y préparer dès maintenant
Aux alentours de 2028-2029, les premières spécifications techniques de la 6G devraient être finalisées, avec des essais précommerciaux dans la foulée. Les réseaux et les premiers appareils compatibles devraient quant à eux suivre autour de 2030, année visée pour le lancement commercial de la 6G.
Qu’attendre de cette technologie qui s’annonce révolutionnaire ? Cristiano Amon, le CEO de Qualcomm, estime que « la 6G va faire de nous tous des caméras ambulantes ». La prochaine génération de réseaux mobiles supportera par ailleurs massivement l’IA agentique, tout en étant intégrée à différents types d’appareils. Ceux d’Apple ne feront bien entendu pas figure d’exception.

articles.title: Galaxy S23 do Brasil recebe Android 17/One UI 9 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy S23 do Brasil recebe Android 17/One UI 9
Empresa libera update no modelo lançado em 2023. Software baseado no Android 17 tem expansão do Galaxy AI como principal novidade.
Donos de celulares Galaxy S23 vendidos no Brasil já podem atualizar o sistema operacional para a nova One UI 9, que tem o Android 17 como base. A linha faz parte da quarta leva de updates da Samsung, seguindo o cronograma obtido com exclusividade pelo Tecnoblog.
O software traz a expansão do Galaxy AI como principal novidade, além de suavizar a transição entre janelas e oferecer em detalhes informações sobre garantia e cuidados dos produtos registrados na sua conta.
Alguns usuários já receberam a notificação para baixar a One UI 9. Também é possível checar a disponibilidade nas Configurações do telefone. Como já é de se esperar, a novidade chega ao S23 depois de aparecer para donos de S24, S25 e S26, além dos dobráveis e modelos mais básicos, como o A57.
A expansão do Galaxy AI traz as principais novidades da One UI 9. A IA mantém recursos apresentados na One UI 8, como resumo de informações relevantes para o seu dia a dia com o Now Brief e sugestões baseadas na sua rotina via Now Nudge, a exemplo do que já acontecia com o Apple Intelligence nos iPhones desde o iOS 18. A Samsung garante que os trabalhos de IA terão melhores resultados com a atualização.
A fabricante também traz otimizações no app de câmera, com o Photo Assist, que realiza edições rápidas com IA a partir de prompts simplificados. O My FanCam também é um recurso recente da Samsung, permitindo separar cortes de vídeos feitos no celular de maneira automática.
A One UI 9 oferece melhorias na interface, com transições mais suaves ao alternar entre janelas abertas no smartphone. Outras atualizações menos visíveis também ficam disponíveis, como a seção de Garantia e Cuidados, onde usuários podem acompanhar o estado de saúde dos seus dispositivos Samsung. A privacidade também foi atualizada no sistema, mostrando em detalhes a atividade das suas IAs ao checar informações dos seus apps e contas.

articles.title: Samsung and SK Hynix are upgrading Chinese factories to produce advanced RAM chips as AI data center competition ramps up — big players move to fight off the threat from CXMT and co.
articles.text:
Samsung and SK Hynix are upgrading Chinese factories to produce advanced RAM chips as AI data center competition ramps up — big players move to fight off the threat from CXMT and co.
As Chinese rivals look to get in on the lucrative market, two chip giants are taking action to stay ahead of the game.
The two biggest NAND flash memory manufacturers on the planet, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, are reportedly working to upgrade their Chinese factories to produce more advanced chips for use in AI data centers, Reuters reports. The move comes as the two companies continue to fight off competition from the fast-growing Chinese memory makers like CXMT. Fierce competition in the lucrative AI RAM market has already seen manufacturers slash consumer-focused production to allow them to increase production capacity for the more advanced — and money-spinning — components.
Citing four people familiar with the companies' plans, the report claims that Samsung Electronics aims to switch its Xian plant to the production of 286-layer flash chips by the end of the year. SK Hynix has its sights set a little lower, targeting chips with 240 or more layers at its Dalian facility. That factory was taken over back in 2021, but a timescale for the new upgrades isn't clear.
However, while Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are well placed to deal with the growing threat from Chinese chipmakers, both are faced with additional complications in the form of U.S. regulations. Export controls on chipmaking equipment were applied in 2022, with the aim of slowing China's technological progress. Both companies, based in South Korea, must now get licenses in order to install U.S.-built hardware in Chinese factories. The report points to this as a reason for the recent growth of Chinese firms like Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. (YMTC). The company told investors at a recent IPO preparation meeting that it aims to become the world's largest NAND flash producer by the end of 2027.
While both Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix say that they are working in consultation with the U.S. authorities, there's little doubt that this extra step has hampered the companies' ability to upgrade their factories to better meet the new AI memory demand.
It's impossible to overstate just how key Samsung and SK Hynix are to NAND supply. Samsung's Xian factory produces around 40% of the company's global output. It currently produces chips that have around 200 layers, but Samsung's plans aim to boost that to 286 layers for V9 NAND chips. For its part, SK Hynix's Dalian plant currently produces chips with 192 layers, with the company's aim for 240-layer chips reportedly confirmed by three people familiar with the plans.
Meanwhile, CXMT, China's premier chipmaker, is looking to move beyond DRAM production. A report from September 2026 noted that it was eyeing production of 3D NAND memory for use in solid-state storage (SSD) products. The country's largest DRAM producer, CXMT, posted $22.41 billion in revenue and $11.57 billion in net profit in the first half of 2026 after years of losing money. But despite this purple patch, the company is still much smaller than the likes of Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Oliver Haslam has written about technology of all shapes and sizes for over 15 years, both online and in print. He's fascinated by how personal computing continues to change as tower PCs give way to foldable phones and beyond.

articles.title: SpaceX's stock soars as Elon Musk reveals crushing earnings and revenue beat - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
SpaceX’s stock soars as Elon Musk reveals crushing earnings and revenue beat
Shares of Space Exploration Technologies Corp., Elon Musk’s rocket developer and artificial intelligence company, gained more than 8% in late trading today after posting earnings results that revealed the strong momentum of its AI business.
The company, better known as SpaceX, reported third-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of 45 cents per share, crushing Wall Street’s forecast of 13 cents, while revenue soared 161% from a year earlier, to $14.6 billion, surpassing the $12.72 billion target with ease. That helped SpaceX to deliver a first-ever profit, with net income coming to $4.4 billion to reverse a loss of $1.1 billion in the same period one year earlier.
SpaceX also reported income from operations of $2.8 billion, compared with a loss of $273 million a year ago. Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization came to $8.8 billion, up 306%, while the company’s diluted income per share was 35 cents, up from a loss of 36 cents last year.
The company livestreamed its earnings call on its social media platform X, formerly Twitter, and it was a must-see for fans of Musk, who appeared alongside Chief Operating Officer Gwynne Shotwell and Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnson. The livestream began in dramatic fashion, with a video recap of the most recent Starship flight and orchestral music playing in the background.
It followed by a simulation of the company’s next upcoming flight, during which it will use a huge mechanical arm to try and grab both the rocket’s booster and the actual ship. The company has promised it will be a “profound technology milestone in the history of civilization and consciousness.”
The livestream then switched to a cinematic view of SpaceX’s products, before focusing on the three executives seated at a table in a room at the company’s Starlink factory in Bastrop, Texas.
“In order to understand the nature of the universe and all these fundamental questions, we must expand the scope of consciousness,” Musk said in a recording played against a video background of space and the moon. The event looked more like the opening of a science-fiction movie than a corporate earnings report.
Q3 2026 Financial and Operational Results https://t.co/Qrb0qeVG15
— SpaceX (@SpaceX) October 20, 2026
With the dramatic visuals out of the way, Musk got down to business, and quickly generated excitement when he stressed that he thinks a merger between SpaceX and Tesla Inc., his electric vehicle company, would be a “good idea.” He revealed the boards of both companies have created a special committee to examine the feasibility of a merger.
SpaceX is best known for its rocket-powered spacelift capability, but its most profitable business by far is Starlink, the satellite-based internet connectivity division, so those were some of the more interesting numbers that investors wanted to hear about. And what Musk said surely pleased them, as he revealed that Starlink’s subscriber base had grown to 13.6 million at the end of the quarter, up from 12 million in the prior period.
Meanwhile, Starlink’s total connectivity revenue soared to $5.25 billion in the quarter, up 69% from the $3.1 billion in recorded a year earlier and ahead of the Street’s forecast of $4.84 billion. Starlink’s consumer revenue came to $3.12 billion, while enterprise and government customers contributed $2.13 billion to the total.
SpaceX is also an AI company following its acquisition of xAI earlier this year. xAI is Musk’s AI startup, the developer of the chatbot Grok, and it also owns the X social media platform. XAI is now the company’s largest business, with revenue soaring to $7.56 billion in the quarter, up from just $813 million one year ago. Wall Street analysts had been looking for sales of just $6.47 billion there. The business is likely to get bigger in future too, for SpaceX wrapped up its $60 billion acquisition of the AI coding startup Cursor during the quarter.
The health of SpaceX’s AI business sparked a jump in the shares of companies such as Nvidia Corp. and Intel Corp., up 2% and 3% respectively, as well as neocloud providers like CoreWeave Inc. and Nebius Group N.V., which gained 5% and 6%, respectively.
“It seems as if Elon Musk is unstoppable right now, with all of SpaceX’s main business units growing,” said Holger Mueller of Constellation Research. “Starlink is growing fast and xAI, which was once a bit of a concern, is doing very well too. Buying Cursor was a smart move, because AI has changed the lives of developers. In fact, developer workloads are the easiest of all AI workloads to scale, and that’s exactly what xAI will be doing now.”
In the video, Musk laid out some ambitious goals for increasing the company’s data center capacity, saying he wants to grow it to 20 gigawatts by the end of 2027, up from just 1.7 gigawatts today. Though many investors have raised concerns about the sustainability of compute demand, SpaceX’s numbers and plans suggest that Musk does not feel the same way. On the contrary, Musk said SpaceX has been “hounded relentlessly by every hyperscaler and dozens of smaller companies to rent more of our compute.”
Musk also said that compute prices have increased to a point where the company can generate a return on its data center investments within 12 months, and he believes that this window could shorten to just six months by this time next year. But such a payback will be necessary, for the company revealed bold ambitions to grow its capital expenditure over the next year. SpaceX is planning to spend between $35 billion and $40 billion on data center infrastructure in the current quarter, up from $19.6 billion spent in the previous quarter.
Moving on to the forecast, Johnson took over, saying that the company is on track to hit a $100 billion annual recurring revenue run rate by the end of the year. That number could grow to as much as $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027, he said, thanks in part to the growing adoption of the company’s chatbot Grok.
For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, SpaceX is targeting revenue of between $33 billion and $37 billion, well ahead of the Street’s estimate of $22 billion.

articles.title: Hackers Use New ROMULUS ClickFix Platform to Deliver LegionLoader and Other Malware
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a ClickFix delivery platform called ROMULUS that's being used to distribute malware such as Legion Loader.
According to Forescout Research - Vedere Labs, ROMULUS is akin to a malware delivery service that employs ClickFix-style lures on bogus landing pages to trick unsuspecting users into running malicious commands and infecting their own machines.
"ROMULUS may be a privately operated panel, a commercial cybercriminal delivery service, an affiliate framework, or software that has been copied between operators," security researcher Sai Molige said in an analysis.
The cybersecurity company said it identified six IP addresses running ROMULUS -
- 96.62.224[.]81
- 86.109.75[.]7
- 151.240.151[.]223
- 23.94.145[.]224
- 93.152.224[.]118
- 2.27.248[.]127
Notably, the IP address "96.62.224[.]81" was identified as hosting a ClickFix script and an MSI installer file in connection with another campaign that has been found to leverage malicious ChatGPT Custom GPTs to direct victims to a fake URL responsible for serving the ClickFix lure.
Forescout's own analysis has since uncovered the same malware being delivered via another server, 86.109.75[.]7, that also hosted a panel codenamed ROMULUS. In addition, a separate chain triggered via ClickFix has been used to run a PowerShell script, which then delivers Legion Loader, a malware loader also called Satacom downloader, CurlyGate, and RobotDropper.
As of writing, it's not known who is behind the ROMULUS platform. However, it shares no overlaps with RomulusLoader, a malware family associated with Silver Fox (aka TA4922), a China-aligned threat actor known for repeatedly using tax-related pretexts to distribute remote access trojans like ValleyRAT (aka Winos 4.0), DcRAT, and potentially Venom RAT via DLL sideloading techniques.
The ROMULUS platform exposes two endpoints that are designed to download a PowerShell staging script, which decides the payload to be fetched next: a trojanized MSI installer carrying a malware loader or an encrypted archive containing Legion Loader that's inflated to nearly 1 GB with repetitive padding to bypass upload limits, sandbox budgets, or static-analysis thresholds. The loader, for its part, communicates with a remote server to fetch and run additional payloads.
The findings indicate how ClickFix is evolving beyond a social engineering technique into a highly effective entry point for malware. To mitigate the threat, it's essential to hunt for suspicious PowerShell commands and DLL sideloading events.

articles.title: AMD and Microsoft Bring FSR 4.1 to Xbox Series X|S, FSR Diamond Teased for Project Helix
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
AMD and Microsoft Bring FSR 4.1 to Xbox Series X|S, FSR Diamond Teased for Project Helix
AMD and Microsoft have confirmed that FSR Upscaling 4.1 is coming to the Xbox Series X and Series S. The news came in an AMD video presentation led by Jack Huynh, joined by Xbox CTO Scott Van Vliet and ASUS. The ROG Xbox Ally handhelds are getting it too, and it looks like they will be first in line, while the consoles are only listed as "coming soon." Neither company has shared a release date or a list of supported games. Both consoles use RDNA 2 graphics, the same architecture as the Radeon RX 6000 series, which AMD also announced FSR 4.1 for today, well ahead of the early 2027 target it set in May. Here's what Van Vliet said:
With FSR 4.1 coming to Xbox. Now, we've worked very closely with AMD to optimize this technology, giving developers another powerful tool for great performance and visual quality for players. Now, whether you're playing on an Xbox Ally handheld, as well as coming soon to Xbox Series X and Series S consoles. And this is just the beginning. Our teams are continuing to work together across hardware and software, and there's even more ahead with Project Helix, leveraging FSR Diamond to power what comes next.
The handheld side is a bit murkier. AMD said earlier this month that a lighter FSR model for APUs would arrive by the end of 2026, and it has reportedly listed both the Ryzen Z2 Extreme and Z2 A as targets. However, one report claims the base ROG Xbox Ally is left out, so owners are advised to wait for ASUS's driver update before assuming anything. Van Vliet also teased Project Helix, Microsoft's next-gen Xbox, which will use FSR Diamond with ML-based upscaling and multi-frame generation. Sony recently announced its own QSSR upscaler for the base PS5. The Series S probably stands to gain the most here, though a lot depends on how many developers actually adopt it.
Source:
				AMD			
	
	
	
		
	
		
16 Comments on AMD and Microsoft Bring FSR 4.1 to Xbox Series X|S, FSR Diamond Teased for Project Helix
RDNA 1-2-3-3.5 really paying for not having that RDNA 4 AI hardware FSR 4.x needs to run natively it seems. At least it can run, which wasn't the case not long ago.
For reference, the internal resolution is 50% that of native with Performance upscaling, for a 2x scale factor, whereas with Quality you're at 67% and 1.5x. Balanced is 59% 1.7x. UItra Quality is 77% 1.3x. Quality generally has a 20-30% performance bonus, with Performance being up to 70% bonus FPS due to literally rendering half of native. I'm honestly shocked that the raw FPS before frame gen on FSR 4.1 Performance is in the ~30 FPS range on hardware as on-paper powerful as an XSX. That's 540p internal resolution assuming output is 1080p, and it's only just holding ~30 FPS. Damn.
Can definitely see why that lighter model is required for handhelds. Lets hope that even with a cut down model the IQ improvements are still as notable as the jump from (typically not worth using as it's impossible to ignore the IQ issues) FSR 1-3.x to FSR 4.x (worth using and on par with DLSS 3.x). The Switch 2 had a pretty good result even with cut-down DLSS on obsolete handheld hardware, so in theory, it's possible. Fingers crossed. If not, at least there's still Intel XeSS, which even in compatibility mode is still much better than FSR 1-3.x, and works pretty well on those handhelds.
RDNA 4/5 handheld/console chips can't come soon enough, even if the raw raster is barely improved, these upscalers are essential in modern games, and struggling to hit 30 FPS before FG with the upscaler almost as low as it can go, internal resolution wise, isn't good.
Hey, at least MS/Sony are trying to eke out every last bit of oomph these consoles have. Kudos there.
Hopefully they'll implement it correctly and do a better comparison in the future. I'm no console user anymore, but still interested in the market.
Did you expect anything different? FSR 4.x was known to be heavier than FSR 3.x and would therefore yield lower performance on RDNA2 hardware. The question was simply whether FSR 4.x on performance/balanced settings would offer a better, more stable image compared to FSR 3.x on quality. And that was the whole point of releasing FSR 4.x for RDNA2 cards: to give the user more options—options that might offer image quality improvements that FSR 3.x couldn't deliver. In no way were we expecting higher performance out of RDNA2.
As has been said, this isn't tested on the base PS5 with its RDNA 1.5 esque GPU, this is full RDNA 2 on a fairly powerful config on the series X. Sure, it's not a PS5 Pro with a newer arch, but two quality levels? Damn.
While we knew it's a heavy model especially if the dedicated hardware isn't present (why wasnt it AMD/Xbox/Sony, you had both Turing and Ampere to learn from by the time the console chips shipped), I am quite surprised that the move from Quality to Performance is necessary to end up roughly at the same output FPS (considering the 9 improvement is after frame gen, the actual improvement is roughly half that). A whole 5 FPS gained at ~25 vs 30 base FPS while jumping down two quality settings is pretty nuts to me.
Anyway. Glad I've not really recommended any console besides the Switch 2 and PS5 Pro when I've been asked by friends what to pick if not going PC. Besides being roughly 2x the performance GPU wise of the base PS5, not being stuck in RDNA 1/2 hell is worth the premium.
Now, concerning the absence of corresponding hardware in RDNA 1/2 implementations that existed in Nvidia's GPUs, I imagine Nvidia didn't design that hardware in a month—let alone test it and build software and drivers for it. AMD would needed even more time, being something new to them. And of course, additional hardware means extra cost and potentially higher power consumption. With consoles being 6 years on the market already, the fact that the need for such hardware surfaced likely somewhere in their 4th, 5th, or 6th year of life suggests that choosing not to complicate the architecture with extra hardware—which would have increased both complexity and cost—was probably the right call.
Going from 25 fps to 30 fps is a 20% increase. Sounds good to me, maybe even better than good.
As for the last point, since you're a PC user who is deeply immersed in technology and its news, and since you're a PC enthusiast who finds themselves caring about things like "what technology is being used here", I think the wisest choice is to go for hardware that won't feel obsolete to you, because psychologically it won't sit well with you. It's like buying an RX 6950 today. It might still perform very well in games, but the moment you get it in your hands, you've already built a mental list of everything it can't do. This is a classic case of "ignorance is bliss".
Nvidia either refused to do dieshrinks or kept charging as much as before, harming Microsoft's first Xbox generation. There may have been technological dissatisfaction issues too (Sony dropped Nvidia after PS3 over those a generation later).You realize Xbox was Microsoft console? It was neither Nvidia console, nor joint Nvidia-MS project where Nvidia was in place to push some ideas or vision and be in position to mind alleged "enshitifications" or whatever. They were asked (and paid) to supply a GPU and a chipset.
This is the result of that decision making by both AMD/MS, and predictable (many people here on TPU have been talking about this for years). MS/Sony want to add non-shit upscalers, and it's a struggle, because to get good image quality you need AI, and if you need AI, it's going to be slow on anything without (decent) dedicated AI hardware. So, Pre RDNA 4 or Pre Turing. One of those debuted in 2018, the other in 2025. If you are making a console in 2019, which do you pick?
Obviously a last gen/two generation old combo you can get cheaply from AMD, right? Well here we are. 20-30 base FPS after upscaling from 540p. What can you do with that? Very little. They've boxed themselves in. Can't even sell the consoles cheaply to make up for it because of that same AI train they missed the boat on.
Only good thing I can say about the non-PS5P consoles is at least they weren't using the *shudder* Jaguar cores for CPU. That decision set back game dev what, 5 years? The Zen 2 cores in consoles are at least workable, even in 2026.
The question now becomes how many years using RDNA 1/2 GPU IP in the current gen of consoles set back the game dev industry.
Now we're at the point where the rumours are "next xbox is PC with UDNA 5", so, decent GPU/AI IP, presumably. Downside? ~1.5-2k "console". What's the alternative? PS5P (if you can find), or 20-25 FPS last gen console.
Good luck John Consumer, definitely some great choices set before you. Hope you built a PC a year ago, though you probably didn't.Given the GPU architecture the base PS5 and both XBOXes use, the only way to get both decent upscaling and decent performance is to run it on PS5P, it seems. Sony released a worse IQ and lighter upscaler for the base PS5 recently IIRC, to throw them a bone.

articles.title: Panne Orange : le réseau mobile perturbé ce mercredi, de nombreux abonnés privés d’appels et de données
articles.text:
[Mise à jour le 21 octobre à 14h15 : après une brève amélioration, la panne a repris de notre côté. Le réseau mobile d’Orange est de nouveau totalement indisponible. Et chez vous, le réseau est-il revenu ? N’hésitez pas à nous le dire en commentaire.]
[Mise à jour le 21 octobre à 13h26 : la panne semble en cours de résolution, et le réseau est de nouveau disponible chez certains abonnés, dont nous à la rédaction.]
Article orignal
Vous êtes un abonné Orange ou Sosh et votre smartphone affiche « Aucun service » ou refuse de se connecter à Internet ? Vous n’êtes a priori pas seul. Depuis 11h30 environ, le réseau mobile d’Orange connaît des perturbations dans plusieurs régions de France. Sur Downdetector, les signalements se sont multipliés pour atteindre près de 11 500 à 11h50, et de nombreux abonnés font part de leurs difficultés sur les réseaux sociaux.
Nous avons nous-mêmes pu constater la panne à la rédaction avec une absence complète de réseau mobile. Il est impossible d’effectuer un appel ou d’utiliser les données mobiles. Orange vient de confirmer l’incident sur X : « Vous pouvez rencontrer actuellement des perturbations sur le réseau mobile Orange. Nos équipes sont pleinement mobilisées pour rétablir le réseau dans les meilleurs délais. Veuillez nous excuser pour la gêne occasionnée ». Pour l’heure, l’opérateur ne précise pas l’origine de la panne ni le délai de rétablissement. Nous mettrons cet article à jour dès que nous en saurons plus.
 Bonjour, vous pouvez rencontrer actuellement des perturbations sur le réseau mobile Orange.
Nos équipes sont pleinement mobilisées pour rétablir le réseau dans les meilleurs délais.
Veuillez nous excuser pour la gêne occasionnée.
— Orange France (@Orange_France) October 21, 2026
Ce n’est pas la première fois que le réseau d’Orange flanche cette année. Le 29 juin dernier, une panne nationale avait déjà privé des milliers d’abonnés Orange et Sosh d’appels et d’Internet mobile dès l’aube, avant un retour à la normale vers 11 heures. Deux jours plus tard, le 1er juillet, une nouvelle vague de perturbations avait touché cette fois les réseaux fixe et mobile.
En attendant, si votre box le permet, les appels Wi-Fi peuvent servir de solution de secours pour téléphoner, à condition que l’option soit activée sur votre smartphone. Pour les appels d’urgence, le 112 reste joignable via le réseau d’un autre opérateur, même sans réseau Orange.
