articles.title: DLSS 5 Just Got a Lot Faster, but Is It Worth Using?
articles.text:
Nvidia has released a new version of DLSS 5 neural rendering, claiming it runs twice as fast as the previous model. This October update reduces the number of parameters in the DLSS 5 model by 24%, halving execution time and reducing VRAM usage by 20%. All of this has been achieved while maintaining comparable image quality, according to Nvidia.
We thought it was worth revisiting DLSS 5 in everyone's favorite title, NBA 2K27, which is once again the first game to officially ship with the latest model. Does the new version really run twice as fast across all RTX 50 series GPUs without compromising image quality? Does it address some of the issues we raised in our initial DLSS 5 analysis? And does this performance improvement make DLSS 5 worth using now?
 – WolfOfDarkness® (@WolfOfDarknesss) October 19, 2026
 – Sim Racing Esport (@SimRacingEspor) October 14, 2026
One thing to clarify before getting into the benchmarks... when Nvidia says the new DLSS 5 model is twice as fast, that doesn't mean games with DLSS 5 enabled will run at twice the frame rate. The improvement refers specifically to the rendering cost of DLSS 5, not everything else the game needs to render.
As a result, actual frame rates won't double after this update. However, Nvidia does claim a 1.4x performance improvement in NBA 2K27, so we'll see whether that holds up.
How the New Model Performs
Let's kick things off with Nvidia's gaming flagship, the GeForce RTX 5080 (see what we did there?). Previously, DLSS 5 was quite taxing on this GPU at 4K, dropping NBA 2K27 from 185 FPS with DLSS 5 disabled to just 53 FPS with the feature enabled.
As we showed in our previous investigation, performance doesn't change much when adjusting settings or increasing the level of upscaling, because the official DLSS 5 implementation operates on the output frame at the output resolution, rather than before upscaling is applied.
The new model improves performance considerably at 4K, increasing frame rates from 53 to 78 FPS, a 47% gain in this title. This makes 4K playable on this GPU to some degree, though there's still a 58% reduction in FPS compared to running without DLSS 5. Previously, that reduction was 71%, so the gap has narrowed somewhat.
At 1440p, we saw a 42% increase in frame rate with the new version of DLSS 5 compared to the old model, reducing the overall performance loss from 54% to 34%. Enabling the feature still significantly reduces in-game performance, just not to the same degree as before.
Meanwhile, at 1080p, the RTX 5080 is quite capable of running DLSS 5, though with neural rendering disabled, we run into CPU and game engine bottlenecks that cap performance.
RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5070: Big Gains at 1440p
The RTX 5070 Ti also benefits from the DLSS 5 model improvements. At 4K, the new model delivered 48% better performance, pushing NBA 2K27 above 60 FPS at this resolution for the first time. However, without DLSS 5 enabled, the game ran at 166 FPS, so the new model still comes with a massive 61% performance hit.
At 1440p, though, the situation is much better. The new model delivered 47% higher FPS than the previous version, cutting the performance loss from 62% to 44%. The game now runs above 120 FPS at this resolution with DLSS Quality upscaling enabled, which is very playable in this title. At 1080p, we saw a performance loss of 25% when enabling the new model, compared to 45% previously.
With the old DLSS 5 model, the RTX 5070 struggled at both 4K and 1440p. The new model provides a substantial boost in both scenarios. While this isn't enough to push 4K performance above 60 FPS, it does deliver 100 FPS at 1440p.
The overall performance loss compared to running without DLSS 5 is still pretty large, though. Frame rates were reduced by 60% at 4K and 54% at 1440p, although both are an improvement over the first model. At 1080p, the performance impact of enabling DLSS 5 on the RTX 5070 was around 39%.
RTX 5060 Ti and RTX 5060: More Playable, Still Costly
DLSS 5 was not usable on the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB at 4K with the old model, and that remains the case with the new version, despite a significant performance improvement.
Going from 24 to 35 FPS represents a 46% gain at 4K, but without DLSS 5, the game runs at 95 FPS. That's still a whopping 63% performance loss when enabling neural rendering.
At 1440p, the situation is better. The old model ran below 60 FPS at this resolution, while the new version pushes performance above 60 FPS, a welcome improvement for what used to be a mid-range GPU option. At 1440p, enabling DLSS 5 reduced performance by 55%, while at 1080p, we saw the frame rate cut in half.
On the RTX 5060, we're using Low settings to avoid VRAM issues. The new model delivers 57%, 54%, and 53% higher frame rates at 4K, 1440p, and 1080p, respectively. This makes 1440p gaming in particular a lot more pleasant, with the game now running at 71 FPS.
1080p also becomes more usable on the RTX 5060, with the new DLSS 5 model now capable of 112 FPS at this resolution. It technically exceeded our threshold for usability previously as well, but dropping from 240 to 73 FPS was a bit of a sting. The performance loss has now been reduced to 53% at this resolution.
RTX 5050: Playable at 1080p, with a Catch
Then we have the RTX 5050. This entry-level model was previously not fast enough to run DLSS 5 in our opinion, achieving just 33 FPS at 1440p and 53 FPS at 1080p with the old model.
The new version runs considerably faster on this GPU, delivering a 55% increase in FPS at both 1440p and 1080p. While this isn't enough to push performance above the 60 FPS threshold at 1440p, it does increase the frame rate to 82 FPS at 1080p. That's still a huge performance loss compared to running without DLSS 5, but at least it's playable.
One weird result we noticed with the RTX 5050 specifically, and not so much with the other graphics cards, is that 1% low performance didn't really improve with the new DLSS 5 model.
In some cases, it actually went backwards. It could simply be a testing quirk, but at 1080p, an 82 FPS average with 1% lows still in the 30s doesn't make for the smoothest experience.
RTX 5090: The Best Case for DLSS 5
Lastly, here's a look at Nvidia's RTX 5090. This was clearly the best GPU to use with DLSS 5, as even with the old model, it delivered playable frame rates at all resolutions.
The new model works quite well here. At 4K, frame rates increased by 45%, while the performance loss compared to running without DLSS 5 dropped from 60% to 43%.
At 1440p, the situation is even better, though performance without DLSS 5 enabled is again limited by other bottlenecks. The new model delivered a 35% higher frame rate, and the overall performance loss was relatively small at just 18%. So if you happen to be using an RTX 5090 to play NBA 2K27 at 1440p, you may as well enable DLSS 5 given the frame rates we're seeing here.
And of course, the RTX 5090 is also more than capable at 1080p, though we're not sure how many people are pairing a 5090 with a 1080p display.
Render Times: How Much Faster Is the New Model?
With this performance data in hand, we can calculate DLSS 5's render time across the entire RTX 50 series lineup and use those figures to estimate performance in various scenarios with neural rendering enabled.
For reference, let's revisit the results from our previous DLSS 5 performance analysis, using the original model. At 4K, many performance scenarios simply weren't possible. On the RTX 5070 Ti, for example, DLSS 5 had a render time of 17ms, meaning that no matter how fast the rest of the game ran, you'd never achieve a 60 FPS render rate on that GPU. The only way to achieve the visual smoothness of 60 FPS would be through heavy frame generation.
Measured DLSS 5 Render Times (previous model)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4K DLSS 5 Render Time (ms) | 7.9 | 13.7 | 17.0 | 22.1 | 31.1 | 37.8 | 53.1 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (120 FPS Game FPS) | 62 | 45 | 40 | 33 | 25 | 22 | 16 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (80 FPS Game FPS) | 49 | 38 | 34 | 29 | 23 | 20 | 15 | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 60 FPS | 114 | 332 | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 80 FPS | 217 | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | 
| 1440p DLSS 5 Render Time (ms) | 3.6 | 6.1 | 7.8 | 10.2 | 14.1 | 16.9 | 24.0 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (120 FPS Game FPS) | 84 | 69 | 62 | 54 | 45 | 40 | 31 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (80 FPS Game FPS) | 62 | 54 | 49 | 44 | 38 | 34 | 27 | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 60 FPS | 77 | 95 | 113 | 156 | 387 | n/a | n/a | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 80 FPS | 112 | 157 | 213 | 444 | n/a | n/a | n/a | 
At 1440p, more cards were capable of running DLSS 5 at acceptable frame rates, but there were still plenty of scenarios that we felt weren't particularly reasonable. The RTX 5070, for example, could achieve 60 FPS with DLSS 5 enabled, provided the game was already running at 156 FPS before switching the feature on. The RTX 5060 Ti and below weren't really capable of running DLSS 5 at this resolution.
The newer model is much faster, significantly reducing render times. On average, the model ran 83% faster at 4K in our testing and 94% faster at 1440p. These are averages across the RTX 50 lineup, so we're not quite at the doubling Nvidia claimed, but the improvement is substantial and close enough. An 83% increase in speed at 4K is massive.
Measured DLSS 5 Render Times (October model)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4K DLSS 5 Render Time | 3.8 | 7.4 | 9.3 | 12.0 | 17.9 | 21.5 | 30.6 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (120 FPS Game FPS) | 82 | 64 | 57 | 49 | 38 | 33 | 26 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (80 FPS Game FPS) | 61 | 50 | 46 | 41 | 33 | 29 | 23 | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 60 FPS | 78 | 108 | 136 | 216 | n/a | n/a | n/a | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 80 FPS | 116 | 196 | 312 | 2217 | n/a | n/a | n/a | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 120 FPS | 223 | 1076 | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | 
| 1440p DLSS 5 Render Time | 1.6 | 3.1 | 4.1 | 5.4 | 7.5 | 9.2 | 13.1 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (120 FPS Game FPS) | 101 | 88 | 81 | 73 | 63 | 57 | 47 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (80 FPS Game FPS) | 71 | 64 | 60 | 56 | 50 | 46 | 39 | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 60 FPS | 66 | 74 | 79 | 89 | 109 | 134 | 277 | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 80 FPS | 92 | 106 | 119 | 141 | 201 | 305 | n/a | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 120 FPS | 149 | 191 | 235 | 343 | 1231 | n/a | n/a | 
Interestingly, the speedup varies depending on the overall performance of the GPU. On the RTX 5090, for example, the new DLSS 5 model was slightly more than twice as fast at 4K. The RTX 5070 saw an 83% improvement, while the RTX 5060 was 76% faster. Even the RTX 5050 ran the new model 73% faster at 4K, which is an excellent outcome from a performance standpoint.
What Faster Render Times Mean for Gaming
These improvements make DLSS 5 a lot more usable across most of the GeForce RTX 50 series. Previously, the RTX 5080 took 13.7ms to render DLSS 5 at 4K, making it very difficult to hit 60 FPS unless the game was already running at a very high frame rate.
The new model takes just 7.4ms to render, meaning a game only needs to be running at 108 FPS before enabling DLSS 5 to still achieve 60 FPS afterward. For games previously running at 80 FPS, the new model now delivers 50 FPS, compared to 38 FPS with the old version.
There's also good news for the RTX 5070 Ti, which was largely unusable at 4K. The old model turned 120 FPS gaming into 40 FPS gaming. The new model is much more capable, with a starting frame rate of 136 FPS allowing the game to run above 60 FPS with neural rendering enabled. That's still a huge performance hit, but at least this configuration is realistic in games.
The news is even better at 1440p. With the old model, the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti were usable at this resolution, and both become considerably more practical with the update. On the RTX 5070 Ti, you previously needed a game to run at 113 FPS to achieve 60 FPS with DLSS 5 enabled. That requirement has dropped to just 79 FPS, meaning a game running at 79 FPS without DLSS 5 will only drop to 60 FPS with the feature enabled.
It's still a sizeable performance hit for a single visual feature, a 24% reduction in FPS in this example, but it's not that crazy. We're now within the realm of other performance-intensive graphics settings, rather than dealing with such a huge outlier.
The Performance Penalty Is Smaller, but Still Significant
With the new DLSS 5 model running ~80% to 90% faster than the original, the performance penalty has been reduced across the board. Take a game running at 120 FPS as an example.
Across the RTX 50 series lineup, enabling the old DLSS 5 model resulted in an average 71% performance loss at 4K. That's been reduced to 58% with the new model. At 1440p, the average performance loss has dropped from 54% to 39%.
In situations where you were enjoying a high frame-rate gaming experience, the performance loss remains substantial with neural rendering enabled. The RTX 5070 drops from 120 FPS to 73 FPS at 1440p. Essentially, you sacrifice those high frame-rates along with the latency benefits, to use DLSS 5 feature. But you don't have to sacrifice nearly as much as before.
For games running at 80 FPS, the impact of enabling DLSS 5 is smaller because its render time accounts for a lower proportion of the overall frame time. With the old model at 1440p, enabling DLSS 5 took games from 80 FPS to 44 FPS on average, a 45% performance loss. That penalty has been reduced to 31% with the new model.
Image Quality: Little Has Changed
Do these performance improvements come at the expense of visual quality? We're not going to do an exhaustive analysis here, but our general impression from using the new model in NBA 2K27, which features the official implementation, is that image quality is broadly the same, potentially slightly worse in some situations.
For a better representation of image quality comparisons, check out the HUB video below:
There are two ways to look at this. On the one hand, it's great that Nvidia has been able to improve performance while delivering largely similar visual output. That's a step in the right direction. On the other hand, DLSS 5's original model had quite a few visual issues, so stagnation or even a small step backward in image quality is not ideal. What we really need to see from DLSS 5 is performance and visual quality improving simultaneously.
The new DLSS 5 model still has noticeable issues with image stability, though it's difficult to say based on our testing whether these problems have gotten worse. Lighting flicker, where surfaces shift slightly in tone from frame to frame, is still very much present in the updated October model, and we noticed it in the same scenarios as in our original DLSS 5 analysis.
We also found with the original DLSS 5 model that neural rendering had a hard time keeping objects consistent at different distances from the camera.
This ugly effect also extends to skin tones. DLSS 5 is best equipped to enhance skin when a character is relatively close to the camera and occupies a large portion of the frame. As you zoom out or move farther away from a character, their skin typically becomes darker and shinier with neural rendering enabled, something that doesn't occur with the feature disabled. In our opinion, this can make human characters look a bit strange unless they're close to the camera.
Another major artifact we discovered was related to disocclusion. DLSS 5 had a tendency to create a halo-like effect around characters, and I think this has actually become slightly worse and more noticeable with the new model.
Has Nvidia Toned Down Neural Rendering?
Interestingly, while researching the new DLSS 5 model, we came across quite a few posts from people using modded versions who complained that the updated model appears toned down compared to the original. According to these reports, it produces a less intense effect and a smaller overall visual change, particularly with the sliders set to higher levels.
This is interesting because in NBA 2K27 (with the official DLSS 5 implementation), the effects of neural rendering look broadly similar to what they were before. Then again, NBA doesn't have an aggressive implementation. It mostly attempts modest visual improvements to avoid overcooking the image and generating an AI slop-like result.
DLSS 5 Got Faster, but It's Still a Work in Progress
The new DLSS 5 model is a step in the right direction toward making it a genuinely usable feature in games. The updated model runs much faster, while visual quality appears broadly similar. It's a decent level of optimization that makes neural rendering viable on more GPUs than it was at launch.
But doubling the processing speed is only one of many improvements this technology needs. Enabling neural rendering still comes with a high performance cost, even after this update. It's just that the penalty isn't nearly as massive as it used to be.
It's clear that performance was the focus of this DLSS 5 release and not visual quality. All of the artifacts and issues with the original release remain, and these need to be addressed. Otherwise, neural rendering will continue to produce worse image quality in some respects than traditional rendering. Whether Nvidia can improve both performance and image quality simultaneously remains to be seen.
I do find it bizarre that Nvidia didn't simply wait a few weeks and make this faster model the official release of DLSS 5. The tech has been integrated into a single game so far, and there has hardly been a rush of developers jumping on board (in contrast, modders appear to be all-in). How much optimization headroom remains is unclear, but it's an interesting jump in performance just weeks after launch.
Going forward, DLSS 5 titles will use the new model, so the original version is effectively going to be consigned to history. The upcoming Hogwarts Legacy update in November will use the new model, and we'll likely revisit DLSS 5 when that arrives.

articles.title: Rumor: NVIDIA RTX 6060 May Be Years Away, and Possibly Slower Than the PS6
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Rumor: NVIDIA RTX 6060 May Be Years Away, and Possibly Slower Than the PS6
Anyone holding out for an affordable next-gen NVIDIA card might have a long wait. Hardware leaker Kepler_L2 claims on NeoGAF that the GeForce RTX 6060 will "launch much later," adding that, based on recent trends, he doubts it will even match the PlayStation 6. He was replying to a forum member who argued the PS6 would compete with the RTX 6060, in the same thread where he claimed the console's RAM and storage alone cost over $680. Kepler didn't give an actual date, and the 2029 figure going around seems to be an extrapolation. Both Kepler and kopite7kimi have placed NVIDIA's Rubin-based RTX 60 series in 2028, and the x60 cards usually trail the flagship by a few months. The RTX 5060 arrived under four months after the RTX 5090, while the RTX 4060 took over eight months to follow the RTX 4090. 
With a flagship launch around mid-2028 or later, that could push the RTX 6060 into 2029. That said, the "much later" comment seems to be relative to the PS6, which is reportedly targeting late 2027, so the exact timing is still anyone's guess. Kepler didn't say why, but the ongoing memory shortage looks like the obvious suspect. NVIDIA reportedly postponed its RTX 50 SUPER refresh earlier this year to prioritize AI products that use the same GDDR7 memory, and the company recently admitted that RTX 5090 supply is tight. Of course, NVIDIA hasn't announced the RTX 60 series officially yet, so treat this as a rumor. Anyone looking to buy a new NVIDIA GPU should probably expect the current RTX 50 lineup to stick around for quite a while.

articles.title: Chez Xbox, on recrute un « Games Supply Strategist » pour gérer… les jeux en version physique
articles.text:
Alors que Sony prévoit toujours d’arrêter la production de disques pour les nouveaux jeux PlayStation en janvier 2028, Microsoft entretient encore le flou sur l’avenir des boîtes chez Xbox. Récemment, une offre d’emploi officielle vient de remettre le sujet sur la table…
Voilà quelques années maintenant que le jeu vidéo dématérialisé progresse à pas de géant, et Xbox n’a pas attendu 2026 pour prendre le virage. Game Pass, téléchargements, sorties multiplateformes… Chez Microsoft, le jeu se consomme de plus en plus sans passer par un magasin (et même sans passer par une Xbox). Pourtant, le fabricant recrute sur son site officiel un « Games Supply Strategist », un poste qui touche à la stratégie d’approvisionnement de son activité gaming.
Xbox cherche toujours à gérer ses jeux physiques
L’intitulé du poste est intrigant, mais c’est surtout la mission qui retient l’attention, puisque Microsoft évoque explicitement « le lancement de jeux physiques Xbox sur différentes plateformes », ainsi que la gestion des approvisionnements et de la distribution.
Autrement dit, le constructeur veut optimiser la manière dont ses jeux en boîte arrivent dans les rayons et répondent à la demande. Alors non, ce recrutement ne signifie pas pour autant que Xbox prépare un retour en force du physique. Il montre néanmoins que cette activité reste un sujet suffisamment concret aujourd’hui encore, pour justifier un poste dédié.
Et à l’heure où l’on s’interroge (plus que jamais) sur l’avenir des supports physiques, Microsoft ne semble pas avoir complètement tourné la page. Mais cette stratégie concerne-t-elle une offre limitée, les jeux Xbox distribués sur d’autres consoles ou des projets plus larges ? Difficile de savoir…
Des jeux Xbox de plus en plus rares en boutique
Sur le terrain, la tendance est pourtant difficile à ignorer. Les jeux Xbox occupent une place de plus en plus réduite dans les rayons de nombreuses enseignes, avec des stocks parfois très (très) limités. Ces dernières années, il n’était pas rare également de voir certains titres disponibles en boîte sur PlayStation et Nintendo Switch, sans équivalent physique sur Xbox donc.
Cette situation reflète la stratégie récente de Microsoft, qui a très largement misé sur le numérique, sans oublier les sorties de ses jeux sur les consoles concurrentes. Pour les collectionneurs et les joueurs attachés à leurs bibliothèques de boîtes, le constat est amer, et trouver certains jeux Xbox en magasin relève parfois du parcours du combattant.
Récemment, le géant américain a déployé une mise à jour visant à permettre aux joueurs de réclamer une licence numérique de leurs jeux physiques. Pour certains, c’est une manière de continuer à faire vivre le physique, pour d’autres, une manière de préparer l’avenir « tout numérique » que pourrait constituer l’écosystème Xbox Helix à venir.
Le disque va-t-il survivre chez Xbox ?
Contrairement à PlayStation, chez Xbox, et malgré des signaux qui témoignent d’un net recul, aucune annonce officielle ne permet aujourd’hui de conclure à un abandon du physique. Les jeux en boîte restent donc une réalité chez Microsoft (on l’imagine au moins jusqu’en 2028, comme son rival direct), et leur distribution nécessite toujours d’être organisée.
Dans ce contexte, le recrutement d'un « Games Supply Strategist » n’a rien d’illogique, puisqu’il s’agit de gérer une activité encore bien réelle, même si elle occupe une place de plus en plus réduite.
Faut-il y voir un signe encourageant pour les amateurs de boîtes ? Pas nécessairement. Cette annonce ne garantit en rien la présence de jeux physiques sur les futures consoles Xbox, ni même le maintien de l’offre actuelle au-delà des prochaines années. Elle rappelle simplement que Microsoft n’a pas encore tiré un trait sur le format. Mais pour combien de temps…
- La rétrocompatibilité au top
- Le Quick Resume, difficile de revenir en arrière
- Taillée pour l'avenir (HDMI 2.1, dolby vision/atmos, VRR)
- Niveau de finition exemplaire
- Grip généralisé sur les poignées
- Gâchettes et palettes plus abouties
- Finitions et ergonomie impeccables
- Très nets progrès de l'interface Xbox
- Puissance du Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme

articles.title: Edge AI MCU Features Multimodal Compute, Tiered Memory - EE Times
articles.text:
Microcontrollers, going through nonstop evolution, have reached their next inflection point: edge AI. A new MCU takes cloud-based models and brings them into the traditional MCU landscape to make sense of edge AI.
Unlike conventional MCUs constrained by limited on-chip memory and compute, Synaptics said its Astra SR200 Series MCUs combine heterogeneous, AI-native compute and acceleration with integrated high-bandwidth custom DRAM scalable to hundreds of megabytes. This enables larger AI models and richer multimodal workloads to run entirely on the device.
At Synaptics Tech Day held in San Jose on Oct. 20, 2026, CEO Rahul Patel called SR200 an xMCU because it offers multiple compute dimensions on a single piece of silicon. He also called Synaptics a processor company at the edge.
John Weil, VP and GM for IoT and Edge AI Processor Business at Synaptics, called SR200 a new class of microcontrollers. He pointed to three fundamental tenets that enable this design transition. “Synaptics went down this path to enable edge AI-capable devices with always-on low-power modes and a greater compute envelope found in entry-level microprocessor units,” he said.
Edge AI-tailored compute
SR200, the industry’s first pairing of the Arm Cortex-M85 and the Cortex-M52 cores, combines high-performance compute with up to 400 GOPS of AI acceleration, 256 MB of custom DRAM, vision and audio capabilities, and hardware-rooted security. The edge AI MCU incorporates Synaptics’s Torq NPU and Google Research’s Coral NPU to power CNN and transformer workloads.
Synaptics brings a variety of Arm cores from an ultra-low-power domain to a high-performance domain,” Weil said. “This allows engineers to pick exactly the compute level they want.” That, along with SR200’s tiered memory architecture, is crucial for combining modalities such as voice, vision, audio, motion and contextual sensing, and responding to them in real time.
“We have put a lot of time and effort into bringing high-performance and efficient compute to a low price point and low power point,” Weil said. “But we also invested heavily in memory architectures that were designed to feed CPUs and NPUs more efficiently.”
Multi-tiered memory
Memory architectures are traditionally designed to feed the CPUs and NPUs. However, a closer look at many AI applications shows they typically aren’t even pushing the compute element; instead, they are pushing the memory interface hard.
This is why the amount of memory that’s being procured and put into the cloud infrastructure is huge. In a traditional microcontroller, we used to have hundreds of kilobytes of memory. Then it became common to have megabytes of memory. And now we are referring to things in hundreds of megabytes of memory.
SR200’s tiered memory architecture builds high-performance compute around an on-chip memory architecture. It also includes a custom DRAM interface with in-package memory, bringing HBM-like high-performance memory to a microcontroller.
This tiered memory architecture solves two problems. First, it feeds compute cores efficiently. Second, this appropriate amount of memory supports ultra-low-power, always-on AI processing. The memory is custom-designed to handle processing for applications such as always-on listening and respond to them simultaneously.
“In this memory-constrained world that we live in right now, it offers design engineers the potential to build really differentiated edge AI devices,” Weil said. “No one else is talking about MCUs having this level of tiered memory architecture and going into the hundreds of megabytes of capacity.”
Fine-tuned power consumption
The SR200 microcontrollers blend high-performance compute with low-power consumption. That’s critical for developing battery-powered edge devices. The tiered memory architecture also plays a key role in enabling ultra-low-power operation. Moreover, if you feed the neural processors more efficiently, you can also reduce the power consumption of the device, Weil added.
The SR200 microcontrollers are available in three pin-compatible tiers. SR210 delivers 200 GOPS for power-optimized, always-on voice and sensing. SR230 adds vision, display, and optional audio at 300 GOPS for mainstream multimodal devices. SR250 delivers 400 GOPS with dual vision and display paths for demanding edge applications.
These MCUs are designed for the next generation of AI wearables, battery-powered sensing devices, connected cameras, streamers, and industrial vision and voice systems. According to Weil, their biggest traction so far is in body-worn electronics.

articles.title: Snapchat se paye Iron Man pour faire la promotion de ses lunettes connectées à 2 295 euros
articles.text:
Snap a officialisé le 20 octobre l’arrivée de Robert Downey Jr. chez Specs, sa filiale consacrée aux lunettes de réalité augmentée. L’interprète d’Iron Man y devient « directeur honoraire de l’expérience client », un intitulé créé pour l’occasion. Sa feuille de route couvre les contenus originaux, les Lenses, ces applications en réalité augmentée maison, et des collaborations sur le matériel comme sur des événements physiques.
Quarante secondes pour conquérir Iron Man
L’acteur assure avoir cédé vite : « Après avoir testé à peu près toutes les technologies portables sorties ces vingt dernières années, sans être vraiment impressionné, les Specs m’ont totalement conquis en quarante secondes ». Il file lui-même la référence à sa filmographie, en décrivant des lunettes qui « tiennent la promesse faite par un certain super-héros techno-optimiste » qu’il a incarné. Evan Spiegel, le patron de Snap, salue de son côté un partenaire qui « imagine ce que cette technologie pourrait devenir depuis près de vingt ans ». Le communiqué assigne à l’acteur une mission moins poétique : « guider les clients pour comprendre et imaginer ce qui est possible » avec l’objet.
Le recrutement s’accompagne d’une série d’épisodes publiés sur YouTube et le site de Specs : aménager son espace de travail, progresser au golf, suivre une série au lit ou apprendre à peindre, lunettes sur le nez. Un premier spot a été diffusé le soir même, pendant le match d’ouverture de la saison NBA entre les Knicks et les Sixers. Un épisode inédit accompagnera ensuite le premier match des World Series, le 23 octobre. Des expériences signées HBO et NBA figurent déjà au catalogue des Lenses.
2 295 euros chez Orange et 3,5 milliards déjà engloutis
Les Specs se précommandent aux États-Unis à 2 195 dollars en Wi-Fi, 2 395 dollars avec la 5G de Verizon, pour des livraisons attendues dans le courant de l’automne. La France suivra au même étage tarifaire : 2 295 euros, ou 2 495 euros en version 5G, avec Orange dans le rôle du distributeur. L’objet se veut autonome, sans téléphone ni boîtier externe : le calcul loge dans les branches, derrière deux verres à réalité augmentée. Les lunettes connectées de Meta, bien moins chères, jouent dans une autre catégorie, celle de l’accessoire arrimé au smartphone.
Présentées en juin à la conférence AWE, les lunettes ont d’abord récolté des moqueries pour leur gabarit, et l’action Snap a reculé d’environ 4 % le jour de la présentation. L’investisseur activiste Irenic Capital chiffre à plus de 3,5 milliards de dollars la facture du projet et réclame un examen de toutes les options, cession comprise. Evan Spiegel défend un « pari à long terme » et a filialisé l’activité, une structure qui ouvre la porte à des capitaux extérieurs. Le montant du contrat reste secret, mais une enveloppe d’environ 100 millions de dollars en actions circulait dès le mois de juin, sans jamais être confirmée par les deux camps.

articles.title: Fútbol Libre - Partidos de Fútbol y Canales Deportivos Online, es la búsqueda de Google que no aconsejamos
articles.text:
La búsqueda de “Fútbol Libre - Partidos de Fútbol y Canales Deportivos Online” se multiplicó en Google entre los aficionados que buscan ver gratis los cruces de la UEFA Champions League y la Copa Sudamericana. Sin embargo, esta consulta es una de las que los especialistas en seguridad digital desaconsejan con mayor insistencia.
Lejos de ofrecer una vía segura para disfrutar del torneo, la mayoría de los resultados asociados a ese nombre conducen a sitios clonados que ponen en riesgo la información personal y financiera de quien los visita.
El fenómeno responde a un patrón conocido. A medida que avanzan las fases decisivas de ambos certámenes, crece la presión por acceder a las transmisiones en tiempo real, y con ella, el tráfico hacia plataformas que prometen acceso instantáneo y sin costo. Esa demanda masiva es, precisamente, lo que explotan los operadores de estas páginas fraudulentas.
Por qué la búsqueda Fútbol Libre en Google es peligrosa
Durante los últimos meses, las autoridades y las grandes cadenas televisivas lograron bloquear buena parte de las páginas originales vinculadas a la red Fútbol Libre. La consecuencia directa es que, en la actualidad, casi todos los resultados que aparecen bajo ese nombre en los buscadores corresponden a clones maliciosos.
Estos sitios, en muchos casos, ya no están administrados por fanáticos del fútbol, sino por ciberdelincuentes que aprovechan el pico de visitas en los días de partido para lanzar campañas de estafa a gran escala.
El riesgo principal al ingresar a estas plataformas es la descarga forzada de extensiones o archivos APK. Bajo la excusa de mejorar la calidad de la transmisión, muchas páginas solicitan instalar programas o aplicaciones externas que en realidad contienen troyanos, virus espía o malware bancario capaces de robar credenciales y vaciar cuentas.
A esto se suma el peligro de aceptar permisos de notificación, que exponen al dispositivo a una avalancha de publicidad engañosa y mensajes de phishing diseñados para capturar contraseñas y datos sensibles.
También existen scripts ocultos para minado de criptomonedas: un clic en un falso botón de reproducción puede activar procesos que usan el hardware del teléfono o la computadora sin autorización, lo que sobrecalienta el equipo y acorta su vida útil.
En síntesis, buscar Fútbol Libre en Google para ver partidos de la UEFA Champions League o de la Copa Sudamericana expone al usuario a instalaciones de malware, robo de credenciales bancarias y minado oculto de criptomonedas, además de una transmisión de baja calidad con retrasos de hasta dos minutos respecto a las señales oficiales.
Fallas técnicas y tácticas de engaño en los sitios piratas
Más allá del riesgo informático, la experiencia de ver fútbol a través de estas plataformas piratas tiene fallas evidentes. Las transmisiones de Fútbol Libre suelen presentar un retraso de señal de hasta dos minutos respecto a las opciones legales, lo que implica spoilers de goles y jugadas clave para quienes siguen el resultado por otros medios.
A esto se agregan las caídas constantes del servicio en los momentos de mayor tensión del partido, producto de la sobrecarga de servidores clandestinos que no están preparados para sostener el tráfico de un encuentro decisivo. La calidad de imagen suele ser baja y las interrupciones, frecuentes, justo en los instantes donde más importa no perder la transmisión.
Los clones de Fútbol Libre y de plataformas similares se multiplican cada día y cambian de dominio de forma constante para evadir los bloqueos de las autoridades. Están diseñados para parecer legítimos y captar la urgencia de quienes buscan ver el partido a cualquier costo.
Entre las tácticas más frecuentes que utilizan estos sitios se encuentran los formularios falsos de “registro gratuito” que capturan datos bancarios, los anuncios que simulan ser controles del reproductor de video y redirigen a páginas de estafa, y las promociones falsas que ofrecen premios o acceso VIP a cambio de información personal.
Alternativas oficiales para ver los partidos de la Champions League y la Sudamericana
Frente a estos riesgos, la recomendación de los especialistas es recurrir a plataformas legales y autorizadas para seguir el torneo. Para los partidos de la UEFA Champions League o de la Copa Sudamericana existen varias opciones verificadas.
Entre ellas se cuentan los canales de televisión autorizados en cada país, la señal de DSports junto con su plataforma de streaming oficial DGO, y las señales abiertas y aplicaciones oficiales disponibles en distintos territorios.
Estas alternativas garantizan una experiencia estable, sin malware ni fraudes asociados, y protegen tanto los datos personales como la información financiera del usuario durante toda la transmisión.
Recomendaciones para cuidar tus datos al ver fútbol online
Para reducir el riesgo de caer en una estafa digital durante la temporada de partidos decisivos, los especialistas recomiendan evitar la descarga de archivos o extensiones fuera de las tiendas oficiales de aplicaciones.
También sugieren verificar siempre que la URL del sitio comience por “https” y pertenezca a una entidad reconocida, mantener actualizado el dispositivo con soluciones de seguridad activas para bloquear amenazas, y evitar compartir datos sensibles en plataformas que no cuenten con verificación.
Buscar Fútbol Libre en Google puede parecer una solución rápida para ver partidos de la UEFA Champions League o de la Copa Sudamericana, pero es una de las formas más sencillas de exponerse a fraudes y robo de datos financieros. Apostar por los servicios oficiales continúa siendo la única manera de disfrutar el torneo sin comprometer la seguridad digital.

articles.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, the inference framework behind its production services - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, the inference framework behind its production services
Chinese artificial intelligence startup Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Basic Technology Research Co. Ltd. today open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference framework behind its own production services.
The release takes on the cost of serving large models to the public. DeepSeek calls reaching a massive user base at a reasonable price “the core problem an inference framework has to solve” in a deployment Q&A posted with the code. One cluster now serves 155 trillion tokens a day, according to the same document, and revenue at off-peak pricing works out to $38 per graphics processing unit per hour.
For now DeepInfer supports a single model, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and by default it loads the updated 1017 version DeepSeek released over the weekend. Nvidia Corp.’s SM100 Blackwell GPUs can run the framework, as can Ascend 950 neural processing units from Huawei Technologies Co. Ltd. Hopper and other older Nvidia architectures are not on the list.
Two features that keep outputs identical from run to run work only on Nvidia hardware. All of the published performance benchmarks ran on Nvidia chips too, and the figures are DeepSeek’s own.
Speculative decoding in DeepInfer runs through DSpark, a system in which a draft model proposes five tokens at a time and a confidence head predicts which of them the main model will accept. Verification compute goes only to the likeliest candidates. That trims the number of draft tokens checked per step by about 30%, and DeepSeek estimated a 4% to 7% throughput gain at its production load. A second technique, which the company says nearly halves total prefill computation, runs only the last 128 tokens of each prompt back through the model’s decoder layers.
DeepSeek has not yet released its key-value cache management and load-balancing code, saying the two are tightly coupled to internal infrastructure. A blog post the company published on Zhihu lays out how both work. Splitting prefill and decode across separate machines is also left to operators, with the README noting that most of the engine work for it is already in place. The smallest deployment DeepSeek describes as efficient uses 64 GPUs for prefill and another 64 for decoding.
The same coupling kept DeepSeek from releasing its full engine in April 2025, when it described the software as an early fork of vLLM built around its cluster management tools. Maintaining a large open-source project was also more than “a small research team focused on developing better models” had bandwidth for, the company wrote at the time.
DeepSeek had already released components such as the FlashMLA, DeepGEMM and DeepEP kernel libraries, which DeepInfer now uses. The new README names vLLM as its original foundation.
DeepInfer’s Ascend support follows a Sept. 30 release in which DeepSeek brought the TileLang kernel programming language to Huawei’s chips with the chipmaker’s help. The startup plans to deploy at least 160,000 Ascend 950DT accelerators at a new data center in Inner Mongolia, Bloomberg reported in September.
The framework arrived a day after the U.S. Department of Homeland Security ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek products from their systems, including third-party services built on its technology.
DeepInfer is available on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license, and the companion deepseek-recipe library released with it converts requests into token sequences using the same logic as DeepSeek’s official application programming interface. DeepSeek said inference code for future models will go into the same repository.

articles.title: HPE says it will run the first supercomputer benchmarks on the Moon — GPU-powered fanless Spaceborne Computer-4 is slated to ride a rover to the lunar south pole to test AI and HPC benchmarks
articles.text:
HPE says it will run the first supercomputer benchmarks on the Moon — GPU-powered fanless Spaceborne Computer-4 is slated to ride a rover to the lunar south pole to test AI and HPC benchmarks
NASA will test coordination of three AI models trained on Earth, ISS, and lunar data.
A fanless compute module will head to the Moon for supercomputer benchmarking, AI testing, and additional experimentation by NASA and Deloitte, as detailed in a Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) release. The company’s Spaceborne Computer-4 will run what HPE calls “the first high performance computing (HPC) benchmarks on the surface of the Moon,” riding on an Astrolab FLIP rover to the lunar south pole. The launch is slated for late 2026 under NASA’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services initiative for a Moon Base program mission, in conjunction with a Voyager Technologies Griffin-1 lander.
Named benchmarks include High Performance Conjugate Gradients (HPCG), a supercomputing metric that complements High Performance LINPACK (HPL). AI testing will involve large language model (LLM) retrieval-augmented generation, vision inference, LiDAR processing, and an AI services container for AI app deployment. The LLMs “will deliver insights, analyze visual data, and support autonomous monitoring,” while the LiDAR processing involves mapping, navigation, terrain analysis, and infrastructure development.
Scott Wiest, HPE’s vice president, fellow and global sales chief technologist, said, “The next chapter of lunar exploration will depend on the ability to turn data into insights at the point of discovery.” HPE says “no other company or organization” has conducted such benchmarks on the Moon, with a presumption that no other parties’ planned HPC missions will get there first. HPE also assembled a software suite that handles the link to Earth-side systems and the secure delivery of results.
HPE’s “lightweight, self-contained, and fanless” advanced compute module is “built for space environments,” bringing AI and HPC “to the lunar edge,” as Wiest put it, or the “far-edge,” as HPE calls it. The computer blade is about 10 inches long and about 4 inches wide, about the size of a typical graphics card, and is made from two component cards, as HPE senior director Norm Follett explained on the company’s Technology Now podcast last year.
It includes 1TB of Kioxia storage, a low-power CPU, and a small GPU. The chassis is designed to shed heat into a rover plate, and the overall design is made for the Moon rather than being an off-the-shelf solution like International Space Station (ISS) units. Currently, HPE’s description of the unit lacks hard details on performance targets, power budgets, or chip vendors, but the eventual benchmark results will yield some information.
The original Spaceborne Computer launched in August 2017 on SpaceX’s CRS-12 to the ISS. It also ran HPL with HPCG, surpassing one teraflop, according to HPE. It was rack-installed and water-cooled; the fanless Computer-4 is quite miniaturized in comparison to the 124-pound original Spaceborne Computer. Spaceborne Computer-2, also on the ISS, is made of HPE Edgeline and ProLiant systems with Kioxia SSDs.
NASA will use the opportunity to run its Federated Learning for Unbounded and Intelligent Decentralization (FLUID) AI neural network, trained on data from the Earth, the Moon, and the ISS, coordinating three distinct models. The agency will also test a tuned LLM for semantic processing for handling onboard documents. Deloitte, for its part, will test its Silent Shield, “a new system to detect cyber intrusions” with near-real-time predictive analytics. Testing ideally occurs onboard, as the link to Earth is slow with low levels of bandwidth, Follett explained.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The launch is planned for the fourth quarter of 2026, using a SpaceX Falcon Heavy launch vehicle, SpacePolicyOnline reports. It will take several days for the lander to reach the Moon and its surface. The FLIP rover is designed to operate for one lunar day, or about 14 Earth days, before attempting to survive the night via hibernation, Follett said, making for a relatively tight benchmarking window.

articles.title: India’s GCCs move up the value chain to build products for global markets
articles.text:
India’s GCCs move up the value chain to build products for global markets
At TechSparks 2026, leaders from Mercedes-Benz Research and Development India, Siemens Healthineers and Lufthansa Systems India discussed how local problem-solving, product ownership, and innovation can help India build for global markets.
India has long been a global hub for technology services, but its growing engineering capabilities are opening up opportunities to develop products, create intellectual property (IP), and take ownership of innovation. As multinational companies expand their research and development (R&D) centres in the country, Indian teams are moving beyond executing assigned tasks to solving complex problems and building solutions for global markets.
At YourStory’s TechSparks 2026, Manu Saale, Managing Director and CEO, Mercedes-Benz Research and Development India; Kalavathi GV, Executive Director and Head, Global Development Centre, Siemens Healthineers; Luigi Celmi, CEO, Lufthansa Systems India; shared their perspectives on how India’s global capability centres (GCCs) can move up the value chain. The discussion explored the importance of localising products, building domain expertise, and fostering a problem-solving mindset.
For Kalavathi, the shift begins with recognising that healthcare solutions cannot simply be transplanted from one market to another. “What works in the US does not work in India,” she said.
“Our mantra is: Medtech is global, but healthtech is local,” she said, explaining how healthcare solutions must account for differences in lifestyles, disease prevalence, affordability, and access to care.
Previously, companies often adapted products designed for developed markets by removing features to make them suitable for India. But this approach did not adequately address the country's diverse healthcare needs, which span private hospitals, government facilities, and district clinics.
Kalavathi said that affordability and accessibility became essential, along with the needs of both patients and healthcare providers. So, the company began working with Indian clinics, hospitals, and customers to develop solutions tailored to local healthcare needs. “We started co-creating some of the ideas along with the Indian customers,” she said.
One example is a C-arm imaging system that was conceptualised, designed and manufactured in India to address local needs. The product now serves 40 other markets and has an installed base of 1,400 units, she said.
The company has also expanded its engineering capabilities in the country, with around 50% of Siemens Healthineers' software professionals based in India, according to Kalavathi.
For Lufthansa Systems, meanwhile, India's established engineering ecosystem and advances in automation offer an opportunity to build on the capabilities already available within the Lufthansa Group. Although Lufthansa Systems established its India operations only recently, the wider group already has more than 1,000 employees in India across its operations.
“We don't feel that we pay the price to be late. We feel that we can benefit and take the advantage rather of being late,” said Celmi, the company's India CEO, pointing to advances in automation and established industry partnerships.
Bengaluru's expanding aviation and aerospace ecosystem is another draw. In a sector where reliability is critical, engineers must bring deep domain expertise and focus on validating changes. “Engineers spend more time validating changes rather than creating them,” Celmi said.
At Mercedes-Benz Research and Development India, the evolution is from task-based execution to ownership of broader engineering challenges. While the car remains a global product, Manu Saale said, its head unit—the digital interface inside the vehicle—offers opportunities for customisation.
There was a time when India solved tasks based on what was told to them. Now is the time when India is asking, ‘What's the problem? Like, what's the big problem? Give me the big statement, and I try to solve it,’ he said.
Saale said this shift enables Indian teams to take responsibility for entire systems and subsystems rather than depend on daily instructions from global headquarters. As engineers accumulate product knowledge and systems expertise, they can engage with headquarters at a higher level and take ownership of more complex problem statements.
He also emphasised the need for India to move beyond its legacy of technology services and build products for domestic use and export markets. For him, the goal is not simply to connect different layers of technology but to develop the expertise needed to own the entire stack.
This ambition is reflected in the wider GCC ecosystem. Kalavathi cited Nasscom data indicating that 39% of GCCs in India are involved in product development, including product management, while around 9% are transformation hubs.
“We have reached a stage where, given the growth of the ecosystem, we can take ownership of complete products.”
Building original IP also requires companies to start with the problem they want to solve, rather than the technology they want to deploy. Kalavathi said organisations must draw on product expertise, clinicians, customer relationships, and partnerships with hospitals and startups to develop solutions that address unmet needs.
Saale echoed this view, emphasising that innovation begins when teams move from service-oriented thinking to identifying problems and developing solutions.

articles.title: tvOS 27.2 : votre Apple TV 4K va gagner trois nouvelles fonctionnalités
articles.text:
Apple prépare une mise à jour qui devrait rendre l’Apple TV 4K plus agréable à utiliser au quotidien. Au programme, des économiseurs d’écran plus variés, un choix plus précis des photos affichées et de nouvelles options d’accessibilité dans l’application Apple TV.
Prévue pour la semaine prochaine, tvOS 27.2 apportera trois nouveautés aux utilisateurs de l’Apple TV 4K. Apple s’attaque notamment aux économiseurs d’écran, avec davantage de liberté pour choisir ce qui s’affiche sur le téléviseur lorsque celui-ci n’est pas utilisé. L’application Apple TV évolue elle aussi, avec une option destinée à faciliter l’accès à certains films et séries.
Des économiseurs d’écran plus variés et personnalisables
Jusqu’ici, il fallait obligatoirement choisir parmi les catégories d’économiseurs d’écran de tvOS : les paysages aériens, les souvenirs et diaporamas, les portraits ou encore Snoopy. Avec la nouvelle option « Aléatoire », l’Apple TV 4K pourra dorénavant alterner entre toutes ces catégories au fil de la journée. Cela permettra notamment aux utilisateurs de varier les images affichées sur leur téléviseur sans devoir modifier manuellement leurs préférences.
La mise à jour donne aussi davantage de contrôle sur les photos personnelles. Dans les catégories « Souvenirs et diaporamas » et « Portraits », il sera maintenant possible de sélectionner directement les clichés à afficher depuis un iPhone ou un iPad. Jusqu’à présent, l’utilisation de sa photothèque comme économiseur d’écran impliquait de laisser l’Apple TV accéder à l’ensemble des photos.
La langue des signes arrive dans l’application Apple TV
La troisième nouveauté concerne les personnes sourdes ou malentendantes qui utilisent la langue des signes. Sur certains films et épisodes de séries compatibles, l’application Apple TV permettra d’activer cette option directement depuis les commandes du lecteur vidéo. Deux langues sont pour l’instant prises en charge : l’ASL (langue des signes américaine) et la BSL (langue des signes britannique).
D’autres évolutions sont prévues, mais elles ne font pas partie de tvOS 27.2. L’Apple TV 4K de quatrième génération, dont la sortie est annoncée pour le 13 novembre prochain, doit notamment prendre en charge Siri avec des fonctions d’intelligence artificielle, qui ne sont pas encore disponibles en France, ainsi qu’une configuration de son surround reposant sur quatre HomePod.
Source : 9to5Mac

articles.title: Surfshark One : VPN et antivirus réunis à prix réduit
articles.text:
VPN, antivirus et protection des données : Surfshark One casse ses prix, mais le pack vaut-il le coup ?
Avec 87 % de réduction et trois mois offerts, Surfshark One rassemble VPN, antivirus et outils de confidentialité dès 2,49 €/mois. Une offre pour simplifier sa cybersécurité à moindre coût.
VPN, antivirus et protection des données : que comprend Surfshark One ?
Un abonnement VPN, un antivirus et parfois un service de surveillance des données : la facture peut vite grimper. Surfshark One propose de regrouper ces protections dans une seule formule, actuellement affichée à 2,49 €/mois au lieu de 7,38 €/mois. La promotion annonce 87 % de réduction et jusqu’à trois mois offerts.
L’idée est simple : protéger ses appareils et renforcer sa confidentialité sans multiplier les abonnements. Une approche qui peut séduire les personnes souhaitant mieux sécuriser leur navigation tout en gardant un œil sur leur budget.
Surfshark One associe plusieurs outils complémentaires accessibles depuis une même application. Chacun répond à un besoin précis :
●VPN : masque l’adresse IP et chiffre la connexion pour renforcer la confidentialité en ligne.
●Antivirus : analyse les fichiers et les programmes afin de détecter les logiciels malveillants. Il propose également une protection de la webcam.
●Alert : avertit en cas de fuite détectée concernant certaines données personnelles, comme une adresse e-mail ou des informations bancaires.
●Search : propose un moteur de recherche conçu pour limiter les publicités et le suivi.
●Alternative ID : permet de créer une identité alternative et une adresse e-mail distincte pour certains formulaires.
●CleanWeb : bloque les publicités et les fenêtres intempestives.
L'intérêt du pack tient à cette complémentarité. Le VPN masque l’adresse IP, tandis que l’antivirus surveille les fichiers et les programmes à la recherche de menaces. En complément, Surfshark One propose des outils pour limiter les publicités et être averti en cas de fuite de données.
Surfshark One à 2,49 €/mois :une offre intéressante ?
Avec 87 % de réduction et jusqu'à trois mois offerts, Surfshark One affiche un tarif attractif pour réunir VPN et antivirus. Le service annonce aussi des connexions simultanées illimitées, pratiques pour protéger plusieurs appareils au sein d'un même foyer.
L'antivirus bénéficie par ailleurs d'une évaluation AV-TEST de 6/6 en protection, 4,5/6 en performances et 6/6 en convivialité.
Avant de souscrire, quelques points méritent attention :
●Le prix : vérifiez le montant total facturé et le tarif appliqué au renouvellement.
●La compatibilité : assurez-vous que vos appareils sont pris en charge.
●Le remboursement : une garantie de 30 jours est annoncée, selon les conditions applicables.
Au final, Surfshark One peut convenir aux personnes qui souhaitent réunir plusieurs outils de cybersécurité dans un seul abonnement. La promotion renforce son intérêt, à condition de tenir compte du prix après la période initiale. De quoi simplifier la gestion de ses protections sans confondre confidentialité en ligne et défense antivirus.

articles.title: Melhor TV Samsung em 2026: 10 modelos para comprar • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Melhor TV Samsung em 2026: 10 modelos para comprar
Encontre a melhor smart TV Samsung para comprar em diversos tamanhos e faixas de preço; lista inclui modelos 4K, QLED e OLED
Escolher uma TV Samsung em 2026 exige comparar modelos com diferentes tecnologias de imagem, como Crystal UHD, QLED, Neo QLED, OLED e Micro RGB, além da presença de recursos voltados a jogos, filmes e séries.
Cada linha atende a prioridades específicas, que podem fazer diferença na experiência de uso e no valor investido. Por isso, o Tecnoblog reuniu 10 TVs da marca disponíveis no varejo, apresentando pontos fortes e fracos de cada modelo. Confira a seguir.
A Samsung S95H é uma smart TV que entrega alta qualidade de imagem e recursos avançados para jogos. Sua tela OLED utiliza pixels autoiluminados, que podem controlar individualmente a emissão de luz, favorecendo contrastes elevados e a reprodução de pretos profundos. A linha inclui versões a partir de 55 polegadas.
Para jogos, a S95H oferece painel de até 165 Hz de taxa de atualização, VRR e compatibilidade com tecnologias como FreeSync Premium Pro e G-Sync. Esses recursos favorecem a fluidez com computadores e consoles compatíveis.
Um ponto de atenção fica pela ausência de suporte a Dolby Vision, que pode decepcionar alguns jogadores.
O sistema Tizen da Samsung reúne aplicativos de streaming, Gaming Hub, quatro entradas HDMI, Wi-Fi 6E e Bluetooth 5.3. Seu áudio integrado de 70 W diferencia o modelo de televisores com sistemas sonoros mais simples.
A Samsung QN90F combina retroiluminação Mini LED e alta taxa de atualização para atender a quem assiste a conteúdos variados em ambientes iluminados e também joga com frequência. Diferentemente da OLED S95H, ela utiliza um painel LCD com pontos quânticos e iluminação traseira.
Esses Mini LEDs permitem um controle mais localizado da luz, contribuindo para o contraste e reduzindo a dispersão de iluminação em determinadas cenas, embora ainda possa ocorrer “blooming” em situações de alto contraste. A linha está disponível em diferentes tamanhos, incluindo 43″ e 50 polegadas.
Nos jogos, a frequência nativa de 120 Hz pode chegar a 165 Hz, conforme o tamanho e a configuração. A TV conta com quatro entradas HDMI, VRR, ALLM e suporte a FreeSync Premium Pro, recursos úteis para equipamentos compatíveis com altas taxas de atualização e sincronização variável.
A Samsung S85H leva a tecnologia OLED a quem prioriza contraste e qualidade de imagem em filmes e séries, sem precisar recorrer aos recursos mais avançados da S95H. Como os pixels emitem luz individualmente, a tela consegue reproduzir preto sem depender de uma iluminação traseira.
Essa característica favorece cenas escuras e o contraste e a linha inclui versões de 48, 55 e 65 polegadas. O processamento fica a cargo do NQ4 AI Gen 2, que utiliza recursos de inteligência artificial para aprimorar a imagem e adaptar conteúdos de menor resolução à tela 4K.
A tela de 120 Hz com suporte a VRR também atende a quem pretende conectar consoles ou computadores via HDMI (são quatro entradas). No áudio, a configuração de 20 W e dois canais é mais simples que a da S95H.
A Samsung QN85F combina pontos quânticos e retroiluminação Mini LED para quem busca uma TV 4K com controle de iluminação mais preciso e recursos avançados para jogos. Essa tecnologia contribui para o contraste e a reprodução de detalhes em cenas claras e escuras.
O processador NQ4 AI Gen 2 oferece upscaling para 4K e recursos de processamento de imagem, enquanto o Neo Quantum HDR+ e o HDR10+ ajudam a ajustar brilho e contraste em conteúdos compatíveis. O modelo pode ser encontrado com tamanhos entre 55″ e 85 polegadas.
A taxa de atualização nativa é de 120 Hz, com suporte a até 144 Hz, conforme a versão. As quatro entradas HDMI 2.1 e os recursos para jogos permitem utilizar sinais de alta frequência com equipamentos compatíveis.
A configuração de áudio de 40 W e 2.2 canais, com suporte a Dolby Atmos, também é mais robusta em potência do que a encontrada em modelos de entrada.
A Samsung Q7F é uma opção de TV QLED 4K voltada ao uso cotidiano, com foco na reprodução de cores e no acesso a aplicativos de entretenimento. Ela está disponível em 50″, 55″, 65″, 75″ e 85 polegadas, e a tecnologia de pontos quânticos trabalha em conjunto com a iluminação LCD para ampliar o volume de cores.
Seu processador Q4 AI trabalha no aprimoramento da imagem e no upscaling para 4K, enquanto o Quantum HDR e a compatibilidade com HDR10+ permitem reproduzir conteúdos nesses formatos. O painel tem frequência nativa de 60 Hz, característica adequada ao consumo de programas de televisão, filmes e séries.
O sistema Tizen reúne os aplicativos de streaming e serviços da Samsung, incluindo o Samsung TV Plus, além de funções de espelhamento e conexão HDMI (tres portas). O áudio integrado tem potência de 20 W e dois canais, enquanto recursos como ALLM e VRR podem auxiliar em jogos compatíveis.
A Samsung QN70H utiliza Mini LED para controlar a iluminação da tela. Essa estrutura diferencia o modelo de uma QLED convencional, pois os LEDs menores permitem um controle mais localizado da luz, melhorando a separação entre áreas claras e escuras.
Você pode encontrar o modelo com tamanhos entre 55″ e 85 polegadas, todas com processamento de imagem com upscaling para 4K e funções de ajuste de contraste e cores. Em conectividade, são tres portas HDMI, duas USB, Wi-Fi 5 e Bluetooth 5.3.
O sistema Tizen, os aplicativos de streaming e a integração com o SmartThings completam a proposta para quem procura uma TV conectada. Seu painel tem taxa de 60 Hz, então não traz fluidez avançada para jogos.
A Samsung The Frame é voltada a quem deseja integrar a televisão à decoração, com uma tela que pode exibir obras de arte quando não está sendo usada para assistir a conteúdos. Seu principal diferencial está no formato e no acabamento, inspirados em um quadro.
A tela Matte reduz reflexos e ajuda a aproximar a aparência das imagens exibidas à de uma obra impressa, embora o resultado dependa da iluminação e da posição do aparelho. A linha é comercializada em tamanhos diferentes, incluindo versões de 50″ e 55 polegadas.
O painel QLED tem resolução 4K e utiliza pontos quânticos para reproduzir cores. O processador NQ4 AI Gen 2 oferece upscaling e recursos de processamento, enquanto a compatibilidade com HDR10+ atende a conteúdos que utilizam esse formato.
A taxa de atualização varia conforme o tamanho: a versão de 55 polegadas chega a 120 Hz nativos, com suporte a até 144 Hz, enquanto a de 50 polegadas tem painel de 60 Hz. Essa diferença é importante para quem pretende jogar.
A Samsung U8600F é uma TV Crystal UHD voltada ao entretenimento cotidiano. Ela utiliza painel LCD com iluminação LED convencional, diferentemente das linhas QLED, que acrescentam uma camada de pontos quânticos para aprimorar a reprodução de cores.
A linha está disponível em diferentes tamanhos, incluindo versões de 55 e 75 polegadas, e os recursos podem variar conforme a versão. O processador Crystal 4K oferece upscaling para adaptar conteúdos de menor resolução à tela, enquanto a compatibilidade com HDR10+ permite reproduzir materiais nesse formato.
A frequência nativa é de 60 Hz, o que atende ao uso com programas de televisão, filmes e séries, mas não oferece a mesma capacidade de atualização de modelos de 120 Hz ou superiores. Em conectividade, são tres portas HDMI, Bluetooth 5.2 e Wi-Fi 5.
A Samsung M75H combina uma tela 4K com retroiluminação Mini LED, voltada a quem procura controle de iluminação mais preciso em filmes, séries e transmissões esportivas. A linha inclui tamanhos como 55 e 85 polegadas, conforme a disponibilidade no varejo.
Seu chip interno reúne recursos de processamento, upscaling e ajuste de contraste, enquanto o Mini LED HDR e o HDR10+ permitem exibir conteúdos compatíveis com maior qualidade de imagem. A tecnologia Color Booster também atua no tratamento das cores.
O sistema Tizen reúne os aplicativos de streaming e funções inteligentes, com suporte a recursos de conectividade (tres portas HDMI, Wi-Fi e Bluetooth) e integração com dispositivos compatíveis. O áudio integrado tem potência de 20 W e dois canais, além de processamento virtual e áudio adaptativo.
A Samsung R85H utiliza a tecnologia Micro RGB, que traz LEDs microscópicos vermelhos, verdes e azuis na iluminação da tela. Diferentemente de uma QLED convencional, que utiliza pontos quânticos em um painel LCD com retroiluminação, o sistema Micro RGB trabalha com fontes de luz nessas três cores primárias.
A linha inclui versões de 55, 65 e 75 polegadas e o processamento fica a cargo do mecanismo de IA Micro RGB, que atua no controle das cores, no aprimoramento da imagem e no upscaling para 4K. A taxa de atualização nativa é de 144 Hz, com suporte a VRR, o que pode beneficiar o uso de videogames.
O sistema Tizen integra aplicativos de streaming, conectividade e funções de inteligência artificial, enquanto o controle remoto SolarCell pode ser recarregado por luz ambiente e energia solar, dispensando pilhas convencionais. Ao todo, são quatro portas HDMI, duas USB-A, Wi-Fi 6E e Bluetooth 5.3.
A escolha depende do ambiente e do orçamento. Antes de comprar, vale comparar os seguintes aspectos:
A Samsung M75H pode ser considerada uma das TVs com melhor custo-benefício para quem busca uma imagem 4K com recursos de aprimoramento por inteligência artificial sem precisar partir para modelos voltados a jogos de alto desempenho.
A tecnologia Mini LED permite um controle mais localizado da iluminação, enquanto o HDR10+ e o processamento de imagem ajudam a melhorar a reprodução de conteúdos compatíveis.
O tamanho ideal depende principalmente da distância entre o sofá e a tela, além do conforto visual de cada pessoa.
Como referência, TVs 4K de 43 polegadas podem funcionar bem a cerca de 1,3 a 1,8 metro; modelos de 50 polegadas, entre 1,5 e 2,1 m; e os de 55 polegadas, entre 1,7 e 2,3 m. Para distâncias maiores, vale considerar telas de 65 ou 75 polegadas.
A linha Crystal UHD refere-se às TVs de entrada da Samsung, com recursos mais básicos, enquanto as demais tecnologias presentes nas linhas QLED e OLED oferecem vantagens específicas de imagem. Em resumo:
As Smart TVs Samsung utilizam o Tizen, sistema operacional que reúne aplicativos como Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video e Disney+, além de recursos de conectividade e controle de dispositivos inteligentes.
Os modelos mais recentes adotam a interface One UI Tizen e podem incluir funções de inteligência artificial, comandos de voz e acesso a jogos em nuvem.
Samsung e LG oferecem opções para diferentes orçamentos, e a escolha depende da tecnologia e dos recursos desejados.
Enquanto a Samsung trabalha com Crystal UHD, QLED, Neo QLED e OLED, além do sistema Tizen e do HDR10+, o portfólio de smart TVs da LG se divide em LCD convencional, QNED e OLED, com o sistema webOS e suporte a Dolby Vision em determinados modelos.
Por isso, compare aparelhos de tamanho e preço semelhantes, considerando também taxa de atualização, formatos HDR, conectividade e prazo de atualizações.

articles.title: Barcelona corta la luz a los acampados en plaza Catalunya por un supuesto "enganche ilegal" que les ponía en "riesgo inminente"
articles.text:
Desde la tarde del martes, una parte de la plaza de Cataluña de Barcelona está a oscuras. No es una avería: el Ayuntamiento ha cortado el suministro eléctrico donde llevan tres semanas las tiendas de la acampada por la vivienda, nacida pocos días después de la que sigue activa en Sol. Lo justifica con un informe de los Bomberos: los acampados se habrían conectado de forma irregular a la red de la plaza, y eso, dice el consistorio, suponía un peligro inminente para las personas (un mal enganche podría producir un incendio, por ejemplo). Los acampados creen que les han quitado la luz para que se marchen.
Qué se sabe. El Ayuntamiento, en el cual actualmente gobierna el socialista Jaume Collboni, habla de proteger la integridad física de quienes duermen allí. Pero el informe no es público: lo conocemos por fuentes municipales. Tampoco está claro el alcance. Betevé habla de una parte de las farolas, mientras los acampados dicen que se han quedado sin iluminación en la plaza.
Bajo la lluvia. Para entender qué supone apagar la luz hay que mirar qué es hoy ese campamento. Según EFE, supera las 600 tiendas y ha aguantado las lluvias que inundaron varias y los vientos que dañaron un buen puñado de lonas. Hay normas de convivencia, con silencio a partir de las 00:30, y una comisión de cocina que prepara entre 300 y 400 platos al día. En el centro hay un espacio para personas sin hogar de la zona, entre quince y veinte cada día según sus cálculos, que reciben esterillas, sacos de dormir y comida.
León, uno de los portavoces, es monitor de escuela, vive en Nou Barris y compagina su trabajo con la plaza. "Estamos juntas, estamos organizadas, y seguiremos acampando", resumió a EFE. No es un campamento de fin de semana. Si bien les falta un concejal de urbanismo, sí es un barrio organizado donde hay quien trabaja, estudia y duerme fuera en octubre, pese a que las temperaturas anoche eran de 14ºC.
Qué pidieron el 7 de octubre. Ese día la acampada registró una solicitud formal al Ayuntamiento, a la que tuvo acceso EFE, para que se definieran protocolos y se garantizaran unos mínimos de agua potable, electricidad y alumbrado. Dos días antes, una manifestación por el derecho a la vivienda terminó con cargas de los Mossos d'Esquadra, contenedores incendiados y lanzamiento de objetos contra la policía. El balance policial fue de 13 detenidos y 28 agentes heridos leves. Los incidentes alcanzaron la plaza de Catalunya, donde algunos de los acampados reprocharon a los alborotadores que se refugiaran entre las tiendas y lanzaran objetos desde el monumento a Francesc Macià.
Trece días después, la respuesta pública que conocemos es el corte. La portavoz, Kiara Monrroy, cuenta que ha habido una reunión con representantes municipales y una visita a una oficina de atención ciudadana, sin acuerdos. "No nos responden", dice. Asegura además que nadie les advirtió de ningún riesgo eléctrico.
¿Seguridad o desgaste? El Ayuntamiento sostiene que cientos de tiendas, lluvia fuerte y una conexión precaria a mobiliario urbano son una mala combinación, y costaría explicar por qué no se actuó si ocurría algo. Los acampados tienen otra versión: según dicho informe, el enganche existía desde el principio, se toleró tres semanas y se cortó justo después de pedir garantías, sin alternativa.
Advierten de que cualquier incidente será responsabilidad del alcalde y temen que lo siguiente sea el agua de las fuentes. Este martes, según León, dos trabajadores municipales pidieron entrar para arreglar algo relacionado con el agua y no les dejaron pasar, precisamente por esa sospecha.
Y en Madrid, otras vías. Monrroy ha comparado con Madrid: ni siquiera allí, “gobernada por la derecha”, se ha visto un recorte así. En Sol la presión ha llegado por otros caminos, como el cierre durante horas de una estación de Metro por limpieza, que abrió después (si bien no descartan volver a cerrar si los análisis de niveles de amoniaco son superiores a los permitidos). O el censo de tiendas que pidió Almeida, como contamos ayer. En ambas ciudades el pulso se juega en el terreno administrativo: informes, suministros, mediciones.
Lo que viene. Los acampados dicen que seguirán al menos hasta la huelga general del 11 de noviembre y, si hace falta, hasta las elecciones del 29. El Ayuntamiento no ha aclarado, que sepamos, si la luz volverá ni si el corte es temporal. Anoche la zona ocupada continuaba a oscuras y acordonada con vallas, según CatalunyaPress. Por su parte, Albert Batlle, teniente de Seguridad, no ve pertinente un desalojo, ya que lo considera "desaconsejable y totalmente irresponsable".
Hay algo de déjà vu. Esta misma plaza fue en 2011 uno de los epicentros del 15-M, y quince años después la vivienda vuelve a ser la bandera. Entonces, un intento de “limpiar” la plaza acabó con miles de personas volviendo a ocuparla. Ahora la herramienta es otra, más silenciosa, y ha dejado la plaza más oscura que hace una semana. Y apagar la luz solo resuelve una cuestión física de cableados, pero no la cuestión humana de qué medidas se toman con esta plaza que ya funciona como un pequeño barrio, con cocina, normas y personas sin hogar durmiendo dentro.
