articles.title: The next Xbox could arrive in 2028 for $1,200 to $1,800, Xbox handheld may launch in 2027
articles.text:
What we know so far: Memory shortages from the AI boom have cast doubt on the release timing and pricing of Sony's and Microsoft's next-generation consoles. While rumors had pointed to a possible 2027 launch, a new report pushes that back another year and supports estimates that both devices could break the $1,000 barrier.
According to Fortune, Microsoft is aiming to launch its next-generation console, codenamed Helix, in time for the 2028 holiday season. As memory costs climb, its price has internally been projected at anywhere between $1,200 and $1,800, unless the company subsidizes the hardware.
Another new Xbox, a handheld, could arrive by the 2027 holiday season. It would presumably support digital Xbox console games, unlike Asus' Xbox-branded ROG Xbox Ally, which is little more than a Windows handheld.
The details come from the outlet's extensive profile of Xbox's CEO, Asha Sharma, who replaced Phil Spencer earlier this year. Sources also told Fortune that Sharma plans to overhaul the Game Pass subscription service into an à la carte model, where users pick specific add-ons and online features.
The CEO has previously said she wants to make the service more affordable, and Microsoft has already partially reversed its disastrous price hikes.
Helix could cost more than double, and possibly more than triple, the Series X's $500 launch price from 2020, because AI data centers have absorbed most memory and storage manufacturing capacity, quintupling DRAM and NAND costs. Microsoft, a major player in the AI boom, has already raised the Series X's price several times.
Rival console maker Sony is in a similar position. The PlayStation 5 Pro now retails for $900, and trusted leakers say the PlayStation 6's bill of materials is approaching $1,000. Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki recently confirmed that the PS6's launch window remains undecided, but the company's decision to stop manufacturing physical discs for new games in January 2028 suggests the transition is planned for that year.
Microsoft previously confirmed that developers will receive Helix development kits next year. Features such as ray tracing, path tracing, neural rendering, machine learning, upscaling, denoising, neural texture compression, and multi-frame generation will play central roles.
Microsoft's Helix console and the PlayStation 6 are expected to use AMD's Zen 6 CPU and RDNA 5 GPU architectures. According to leaks, Sony's console will feature eight CPU cores and 40 to 48 GPU Compute Units, while Microsoft's will increase the CPU core count to 10 with 20 threads, though its CU count remains unclear. Helix, which will also support PC games, could have a 40% advantage over the PS6 in some aspects of rendering performance.
Fortune's report also shed light on the remaining Xbox layoffs expected this year and next. Sharma has cut nearly 1,900 people so far as part of a plan to reduce headcount by 3,200 over the next year, with further rounds planned for October, November, and January. Across the company, Microsoft has laid off roughly 35,000 workers since 2020.

articles.title: Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor Comes to Steam and GOG.com on November 6th
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor Comes to Steam and GOG.com on November 6th
Boutique publisher SNEG, in collaboration with Wizards of the Coast, a subsidiary of Hasbro, Inc., are proud to announce the restoration of heritage Dungeons & Dragons title Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor will be available for the first time digitally on November 6th. You won't have to wait that long to play it, however, as a demo is available today through October 26th for Steam Next Fest - and your progress will transfer over into the full game!
Originally released in 2001 by Ubisoft and developed by Stormfront Studios, Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor is a turn-based party RPG set in the Forgotten Realms. It returns to the legendary Pool of Radiance, one of the most storied legacies in CRPG history - now updated to run smoothly on modern systems!Featuring the Dungeons & Dragons game rules with different species, classes and spells, Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor offers over 100 hours of gameplay. After a Pool of Radiance has been discovered in the Forgotten Realms, emanating a wave of pure evil cursing all it touches, the legendary wizard Elminster sends your party on a quest to find out what is behind this vile resurgence - and put a stop to it. 
Build a band of heroes, descend into the haunted elven ruins of Myth Drannor, and use tactical positioning, spellcraft and steel to stop an ancient evil from spreading across Faerûn. Players may choose between the genuine turn-based style of role-playing or focus on action with a timed-turn style of play.
This re-release features plenty of modern bells and whistles, including widescreen support up to 4K, upscaled background assets for sharper visuals, full controller support, and a reworked camera. The UI has also been improved with upscaling, a new action bar, and additional tooltips, while adjustable combat animation speeds let players fine-tune the pace of battles. For those who prefer the original experience, an optional "Legacy" mode preserves the classic gameplay and visuals. Steam Achievements, Cloud Saves, Steam Deck support, numerous bug fixes, and other quality-of-life improvements round out the package, giving players more ways than ever to enjoy this lost classic.
Features
- Features official Dungeons & Dragons rules
- Return to the legendary Pool of Radiance - back to where the legacy began
- Answer Elminster's call and face a new threat to Faerûn in the ruins of Myth Drannor
- Build a party of six: create up to four heroes and recruit two companions along the way
- Develop characters up to level 16, with powerful spells reaching 8th level
- Explore sprawling dungeons and battle through tactical turn-based encounters
- Use the optional turn timer to add extra pressure and a faster pace to combat
- Play comfortably on modern systems with widescreen support up to 4K, full controller support, and reworked camera controls
- Enjoy sharper visuals, an improved UI, adjustable combat animation speeds, and numerous bug fixes and quality-of-life improvements
- Choose how much you want to modernize the experience with granular settings and an optional "Legacy" mode that preserves the original gameplay and visuals
Artem Shchuiko, Director at SNEG"Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor was an ambitious game for 2001. It has its own place in Dungeons & Dragons gaming history, but for years it has been challenging to experience on modern systems. Our goal with this re-release is simple: preserve what made the original special, fix what needs fixing, and make it accessible again to both longtime fans and a new generation of CRPG players."

articles.title: The Acer Googlebook 14 is an excellent first attempt at a new type of laptop – but Google's software needs work
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Acer Googlebook 14 is a very good first attempt at a new breed of device: the Googlebook. Thanks to the lower starting price, 2-in-1 form factor and stylish design, it’s got a good chance of being the breakout Googlebook star. The powerful components allow Googlebook OS to run smoothly, on-device AI feels much better integrated than with Windows 11 laptops, and the screen looks fantastic. However, Googlebook OS feels a little underbaked at the moment, though some of the Android ecosystem features show promise. As long as Google remains commited to Googlebooks, and continues to improve the software, then the Acer Googlebook 14 will be an excellent investment for Android users looking for a slick MacBook Air-like experience. However, the limitations of Googlebook OS mean it might not be for everyone, and battery life is a little disappointing.
Reasons to buy
- + Premium design
- + 2-in-1 form factor
- + Excellent screen
Reasons to avoid
- - Googlebook OS needs work
- - Battery life is merely OK
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
At a glance: Acer Googlebook 14
What is it?
The Acer Googlebook 14 is one of the first Googlebook devices on the market. Unlike budget Chromebooks, Googlebooks are premium laptops that run Googlebook OS, an operating system based on Android, and Acer’s model is the most affordable variant and the only one that currently offers a 2-in-1 form factor.
What does it cost?
Googlebooks aren’t budget devices like Chromebooks — they come with premium price tags. That said, the Acer Googlebook 14 is the cheapest model you can get right now, starting at $899 / £999 (around AU$1,300). This entry-level model comes with an Intel Core Ultra 5 Series 3 processor, a 14-inch OLED screen, and 16GB RAM, and in some markets, you can also get it with a more powerful Intel Core Ultra 7 processor.
Alternatives
The Acer Googlebook 14 launches alongside four other Googlebooks: the Asus Googlebook 14, HP Googlebook 14, Lenovo Googlebook 15, and the Dell XPS Googlebook. These laptops all have superficially similar specs, such as starting with 16GB of RAM and 512GB storage, but each one has a different selling point, be it a larger screen, thinner design, or, in the Acer Googlebook 14’s case, a 2-in-1 design.
Acer Googlebook 14 scorecard
How the Acer Googlebook 14 scored in our review
| Group 1 Data |  |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Product | Value () | Design () | Performance () | Battery life () | Overall () | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acer Googlebook 14 | 4 | 4 | 3.5 | 3 | 4 | 
Acer Googlebook 14 review: Value for money
Starting at $899 / £999 (around AU$1,300), the Acer Googlebook 14 is the most affordable Googlebook in the initial lineup, with the Dell XPS Googlebook ($999 / $1,099 / $2,399) next. It’s around $200 / £200 cheaper than the HP Googlebook 14 and Asus Googlebook 14, the two most expensive Googlebooks.
The fact that the Acer Googlebook 14 is a 2-in-1 device, whereas the more expensive Googlebooks are simply traditional laptops, makes it, in my view, an even better value. The Acer Googlebook 14, as with all other Googlebooks, gives you 12 months of Google AI Pro (worth $249.99 / £220 / around AU$480), plus three months of YouTube Premium and a year of GeForce Now game streaming.
In the UK, Acer is also offering, for ‘a limited launch window’, an Acer Mega-Hardware Pack worth £144.96 which includes a compact 100W fast charger, 5-in-1 USB-C hub, Acer wireless mouse, three-year warranty — and it’ll plant 10 trees in the buyer’s name — a nice nod to Acer’s admirable focus on sustainability. This deal was supposed to end on October 19, 2026, but I have been informed by Acer that it’s been extended until the end of November.
This helps make the Acer Googlebook 14 an even better value, and I’ve asked Acer if similar bundles are being offered in the US, and will update this review when I hear back (the Acer Googlebook 14 isn’t currently on sale in Australia, which is a shame).
While the Acer Googlebook 14 is quite a bit more expensive than most Chromebooks, it’s a premium device with a gorgeous design and some powerful hardware, which does justify the higher price, somewhat. However, if money is tight, then a budget Chromebook will be a better buy.
Acer Googlebook 14 review: Design
- Only 2-in-1 Googlebook (so far)
- Sleek, premium design
- Lovely screen
When Google announced the first batch of Googlebooks, the company made it clear that these are premium laptops with designs to match. So, don’t think of the likes of the Acer Googlebook 14 as replacements for cheap and cheerful Chromebooks, but instead rivals to the MacBook Air, as well as Windows 11-powered ultrabooks.
That’ll be a disappointment to anyone who was hoping Googlebooks would be more affordable — perhaps rivalling the MacBook Neo when it comes to value for money. However, the Acer Googlebook 14 does look and feel like an expensive laptop, which goes some way to justifying the price.
With dimensions of 12.28 x 8.78 x 0.55 inches (312 x 222.9 x 13.9 mm), it’s slightly chunkier than the MacBook Air 13-inch (M5), though it comes with a slightly larger screen. It’s noticeably lighter than Apple’s laptop, weighing 2.51 lbs (1.14 kg), compared to the MacBook Air’s 2.7 lbs (1.24 kg).

Finger print scanner
The power button includes a finger print scanner for biometric login.
360-degree hinges
The hinges allow the screen of the Acer Googlebook 14 to flip back, turning it into a tablet-like device.
Keyboard
The keys are large and comfortable to type on.
It’s the second lightest Googlebook, only beaten by the Asus Googlebook 14, which weighs in at just 2.2 lbs (1 kg). The body of the laptop uses a magnesium-aluminium alloy, which feels robust without being too heavy, so while the Acer Googlebook 14 feels thin and light, it also feels durable. You certainly wouldn’t feel worried about damaging it when taking it out and about with you.
While it’s not the lightest laptop I’ve ever tested, it feels comfortable to hold in one hand, and shouldn’t hurt your back if you’re carrying it around. The thin design does come with some drawbacks, namely with the port selection — you just get three USB-C ports and an audio jack. One of the USB-C ports is Thunderbolt 4, while the other two are slower USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports, so that means you’ll want to pay attention to which port you plug things into, especially if transfer speeds are particularly important.
To Acer’s credit, three USB-C ports are an improvement on the two ports a lot of similarly-priced thin and light laptops offer (such as the aforementioned MacBook Air, though both those USB-C ports are Thunderbolt 4). If you need to charge the Acer Googlebook 14, however, one of those USB-C ports will need to be sacrificed.
The screen is a 14-inch OLED touchscreen with a sharp resolution of 2880 x 1800 and an aspect ratio of 16:10 (so it’s a little taller than standard widescreen displays). It looks fantastic, and really helps give the Acer Googlebook 14 a premium feel. As a touchscreen, it’s nice and responsive, and it also means that when using Android apps (which you can install directly onto the Acer Googlebook 14) designed to be used with a touchscreen, they work really well. The bezels on either side of the screen are nice and thin, which gives the Acer Googlebook 14 a modern feel, while also maximizing screen size without making the laptop too bulky.

At the top of the screen is a 5MP webcam with a physical privacy shutter that you can slide to turn off the camera, which is a reassuring feature. The keyboard feels nice and responsive, with a decent travel for each key when pressed. The keys are well spaced, so when typing quickly you can still accurately hit the keys you want. They are also backlit, so using the Acer Googlebook 14 in darker environments isn’t an issue.
There’s also a biometric fingerprint scanner included in the top-right corner of the keyboard for logging in quickly and securely. It works well, though it doesn’t feel quite as quick as the Touch ID button on modern MacBooks.
The Acer Googlebook 14 features a large glass touchpad that takes up around a third of the space below the keyboard, and it responds well to gestures.
On the back of the laptop lid is an understated Acer logo, along with the ‘Glowbar’, which is a thin horizontal line that lights up and changes color depending on what you’re using the Googlebook for. The Glowbar appears on all Googlebooks, though its placement on the lid varies (on the Acer Googlebook 14, it’s located in the corner opposite Acer’s logo).
When you plug in the Googlebook, the bar can display the battery level, and it flashes different colors when using the built-in Gemini AI helper. It adds a bit of interesting color to what would otherwise be a rather plain dark rectangle, and while I like the idea of the Glowbar showing the battery level when it charges, it only does so briefly. Also, when using the Acer Googlebook 14, the screen will be open, which means the Glowbar is facing away from the user, so I’m not quite convinced how useful this feature will be (this is an issue with all Googlebooks, not just Acer’s).
What really makes the Acer Googlebook 14 stand apart from the other Googlebooks it launched alongside is that it’s the only one that has a 2-in-1 form factor. Not only can it be used as a traditional laptop, but the screen can be folded back, turning it into a tablet-like device. Because Googlebook OS can run Android apps, both natively and streamed from your Android smartphone, this could be a big selling point for the Acer Googlebook 14. Thanks to the thin design, the Acer Googlebook 14 doesn’t feel too chunky when used in tablet mode, though it’s thicker and heavier than a regular Android tablet.
Android apps I tried on the Acer Googlebook 14 looked fantastic thanks to the OLED screen, with Netflix and Instagram adjusting themselves quickly depending on if I was holding the screen vertically or horizontally. Google Chrome, the default web browser, also worked well, and holding the Acer Googlebook 14 vertically meant I could read webpages with a lot less scrolling.
There is a slightly strange issue, however. While all the apps I tried did indeed change their orientation depending on how I held the Acer Googlebook 14, the desktop screen didn’t change — it stayed in its landscape orientation, and that meant launching apps either from the desktop or the App Drawer (essentially, Googlebook OS’ answer to Windows’ Start menu, and will be familiar to most Android users) was rather clunky — you either had to rotate the Acer Googlebook 14 back into landscape mode to comfortably launch an app, or just try to launch it with the user interface at the wrong angle.
It's a weird omission — Windows 11 has no issue with rotating its entire interface when you rotate the screen it’s on, and I had been expecting Googlebook OS to do the same. I mentioned this to Acer, and it shared the following:
"Acer Googlebook 14 is the first convertible device to run the new Googlebook OS. For the initial launch, Google has chosen to lock the app tray/taskbar in landscape orientation, as its usage data for convertible devices indicates that landscape is the most commonly used orientation. For additional information and support, please refer to the Google Help Center”
This is a bit of an odd decision by Google — sure, there’s only one 2-in-1 Googlebook at the moment, but that’s still 25% of the currently available Googlebook market. Hopefully this changes soon, as it does make the Acer Googlebook 14’s major selling point less enticing. If I were Acer, I wouldn’t be too thrilled about that.
The 2-in-1 abilities of the Acer Googlebook 14 are thanks to the robust 360-degree hinges that hold the two halves of the laptop together, and they feel sturdy and secure. I have no concerns about these handling thousands of openings and closings throughout the lifespan of the device.

Acer Googlebook 14 review: Performance
- Feels fast
- Screen looks great
- Googlebook OS needs work
Google has been keen to highlight that Googlebooks, like the Acer Googlebook 14, are not simply fancy Chromebooks, but an entirely new product category, and I have to say, from my initial impressions, the Acer Googlebook 14 and its fellow Googlebooks are certainly ambitious. The hardware is excellent, and the model Acer sent me to review features a cutting-edge Intel Core Ultra 5 325 processor and 16GB of LPDDR5X memory, plus a 512GB SSD.
That’s the kind of spec that would do well in a Windows 11 laptop, and Googlebook OS is supposed to be far more lightweight (being partially built on Android), so performance should be even better.
It certainly feels fast and responsive when opening apps and browsing the internet. Finding and installing apps via the Play Store is quick and easy, and familiar to anyone who’s used an Android device. Apps and games that have interfaces designed for desktop use (rather than simply being the Android mobile app in a window) have been tagged, so you should know if an app will work particularly well with the Acer Googlebook 14, which is a nice touch.
Benchmarks

That said, when I launched Monument Valley, a popular Android game that supposedly has been updated to work well on Googlebooks, I first had to map touch controls to the keyboard in a rather clunky and confusing manner (and as far as I know, all Googlebooks will come with touchscreens).
Skipping through the mapping process took me to the game, and I found using the touchpad and mouse cursor to interact with the game worked absolutely fine, so I’m not too sure what the point of the confusing mapping process is. Also, despite being labelled as being designed for desktop use, the game initially launched in a window in portrait orientation — so essentially, just showing the Android app. Even maximizing the app window didn’t make it go full screen.
I then tried the Acer Googlebook 14 in tablet mode (thinking that would be ideal for a mobile game), but for some reason, the auto-rotate function didn’t work, even when I toggled it on and off. Then, all of a sudden, it did work, though it asked me to restart the app ‘so that it looks better on your screen’. I did (luckily not losing any progress), and the Acer Googlebook 14 acted as it should. However, the game didn’t take up the entire screen, even in fullscreen mode — instead, it had the (admittedly larger) app in the middle of the screen, then large black borders around the edges. Restarting the app again did give me the full-screen experience, but this is far from a slick and premium experience.
Now, I want to be clear that these issues are related to the software, so it’s not really Acer’s fault. Googlebook OS is clearly still in its early days, and while I didn’t experience any major crashes, there’s still a lot of work to be done by Google, and unfortunately it means that the main selling point of the Acer Googlebook 14 — its 2-in-1 design — isn’t as impressive as it should be.
This also extends to some of the more interesting promises of Googlebook OS. The operating system is designed to be familiar for Android users, and aims to give a similarly slick experience that iPhone users get when using a Mac, such as screen mirroring, seamless switching between devices, and seeing messages your phone receives on your laptop’s display.
When Google launched the Googlebooks a month or so ago, I was shown how the apps on a connected Android phone could be opened on a Googlebook without any installation. Another demo showed someone using an app on their phone, then quickly switching to their Googlebook to continue using the same app where they left off. It was impressive, and something that, as an Android user, I’d been wanting for years. Only Samsung came close, and even that was a bit clunky (and you needed to have a Samsung phone and Samsung laptop).
So, I was disappointed when I just could not get the Acer Googlebook 14 to show the apps on my Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra. Instead, I was given a QR code to scan, which opened up the ‘Cross-device services’ settings on my smartphone. These were already enabled, and it wasn’t clear what I needed to do. Again, it was far from the slick experience I (and other Android users) had been promised.
After speaking to Acer, I was pointed to a Google support page which announced that Googlebook OS support for Samsung phones has now begun to roll out, and that phones need to run Android 17 (and in the case of Samsung smartphones, also run One UI 9.0). My phone was actually on a slightly older version, but the One UI 9.0 update was waiting to be installed, which I did. I was then prompted (after scanning the QR once again) to update Cross-Device Services. Progress!
It took a while, but I was then able to see my phone’s apps on the Acer Googlebook 14. Clicking on an app brought it up on the screen with a desktop-like interface, though it took a few seconds. This is because the Acer Googlebook 14 is streaming the app wirelessly from your phone, so there’s a little delay, but then you get the app in the exact state you left it on your phone.
With the phone properly connected, you can also view its files within the file explorer app on the Acer Googlebook 14, as well as files saved on the Googlebook’s internal drive, and any Google Drive accounts you have as well. This is another nice bit of interaction between Googlebook OS and your Android device, though again there’s a bit of a delay as the Googlebook streams files from your phone.
Having your Google Drive folders within the file explorer (called ‘Files’) app is another nice touch — as long as you use Google Drive. As an Android user, there’s a good chance that you do use Google Drive, especially as new owners of Googlebooks get a year’s subscription to Google AI Pro for free, which includes 5TB of storage. I actually mainly use OneDrive, and I was pleased to see that once I had logged into the OneDrive app on the Acer Googlebook 14, the files I store on Microsoft’s rival cloud storage service also appeared within the Files app.
So, the Googlebook OS and Android ecosystem feels like it needs tightening up a bit, as this is still early days, but there’s a lot of potential here, and if Google can nail it, it will make Googlebooks like the Acer Googlebook 14 very attractive to people who use Android smartphones.
On-device AI is a big selling point of Googlebooks, and with the included Google AI Pro subscription, you get access to Gemini Argon, Google’s latest AI model. I had a play around with it on the Acer Googlebook 14, asking it to help me code a complex musical plugin for Ableton Live 11, and it was quick and helpful, explaining its process and offering suggestions and advice. Even with Google AI Pro, I did use up my current allowance in around 10 minutes. At least it resets every five hours.
The ’Magic Cursor’ feature is another key selling point (according to Google) of the Googlebook OS. Once you’ve turned it on, you can shake the mouse cursor, and Gemini can view what’s on your screen. You can highlight parts of the screen and ask Gemini questions about it. I tried it while I had a photo open, and it offered to generate digital art based on the photo, or come up with gift ideas for the people pictured.
It is similar to the ‘Click to Do’ feature of Windows 11, but that takes a screenshot of your screen, then offers limited ways to interact with it. The Magic Cursor feature feels much more flexible, as you’re interacting with live elements of the screen, and highlights the benefits of Googlebook OS being built from the ground up to support AI, rather than having AI awkwardly pasted onto an existing operating system, as with Windows 11.
Overall, the day-to-day performance of the Acer Googlebook 14 was very good, though the early nature of Googlebook OS means some features aren’t quite as slick as I’d have hoped.
That said, there’s a lot of potential here, and the integration for Android smartphones shows a lot of promise. Hopefully Google will continue to update Googlebook OS regularly — though there’s always the worry with Google that it will abruptly drop support and lose interest in any product that it feels isn’t selling well.
Acer Googlebook 14 review: Battery Life
Battery life results
How long does the battery last?
| Versus Comparison Data |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Attribute | Acer Googlebook 14 | Samsung Galaxy Book6 Pro | Dell XPS 14 (2026) | Samsung Galaxy Book6 Ultra | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Battery life video test | 11.2 | 14.866666666666667 | 12.316666666666666 | 15.183333333333334 | 
Because Googlebook OS has been designed as a lightweight operating system, similar to Chrome OS, I was expecting very good results from the Acer Googlebook 14’s battery.
Acer suggests that it will last up to 14 hours for local video playback and up to 16 hours of web browsing. In our battery benchmark tests, which replicated moderate web browsing activity, the Acer Googlebook 14 in fact lasted for just under 10 and a half hours. In our video playback benchmarks, which loops a 1080p video, the Acer Googlebook 14 lasted 11 hours and 12 minutes.
This is below what Acer claims, but it’s not bad — expect the Acer Googlebook 14 to last well over a single work or school day on battery, and with some tweaks you should be able to get a few more hours out of the battery.
However, we’re increasingly seeing laptops with battery lives hovering around 20 hours these days, so the 10 hour battery life of the Acer Googlebook 14 isn’t as impressive as it would have been a few years ago.
Should I buy the Acer Googlebook 14?
Buy the Acer Googlebook 14 if...
✅ You have an Android smartphone and need a new laptop
The Acer Googlebook 14 works really well with Android smartphones thanks to some great features of Googlebook OS, such as streaming apps from your phone to the laptop. Just check compatibility before you buy.
✅ You were thinking of buying an Android tablet as well
Thanks to its 2-in-1 design and ability to run Android apps natively, the Acer Googlebook 14 offers a great way to save a bit of money and have a device that can act as both a laptop and an Android tablet.
✅ You’re all-in on Google’s AI ambitions
Google’s Gemini AI is tightly integrated into the Googlebook OS software, so if you already use it a lot, then you’ll love the Acer Googlebook 14.
Don't buy the Acer Googlebook 14 if...
❌ You rely on a certain Windows or macOS app
While Googlebooks can run web apps and thousands of Android apps, it can’t run Windows or macOS apps. In the future, devs might make Googlebook OS-compatible versions, but that’s not guaranteed, so if there’s a critical app you rely on, you should look elsewhere.
❌ You have an iPhone
So many of the Acer Googlebook 14’s benefits are tied to having an Android phone, and while there are some features that work with iPhones, you’ll be missing out on a lot — and you’d be much better off getting a MacBook, anyway.
Also consider
Pros
- Exquisite design
- Glorious large display
- Respectable graphical performance
Cons
- Not the lightest
- Lacks ports
- Heavy keys
Pros
- Great all-round performance
- Good display for a Chromebook
- Premium build quality
Cons
- Small lid opening angle
- Not convertible
- Typing can feel cramped
How I tested the Acer Googlebook 14
- Used as main work laptop for several weeks
- Travelled with it
- Connected it up to my Android smartphone
I used the Acer Googlebook 14 for several weeks, for all manner of tasks, including writing some of this review on it. During that time, I also connected my Android smartphone to it to make full use of the ecosystem. I ran a variety of apps and games on the Acer Googlebook 14 during my time testing it.
I also attended Google’s launch event in London, as well as Acer’s own event, for deep dives into the technology and features. I’ve been reviewing laptops, including Chromebooks, for nearly 20 years, and have used that experience to inform my review.

articles.title: Three workers killed, one in intensive care after fall at TSMC’s 2nm fab construction site — accident marks at least nine construction deaths since 2024, broken bolt on a steel connection plate suspected as cause behind tragic accident
articles.text:
Three workers killed, one in intensive care after fall at TSMC’s 2nm fab construction site — accident marks at least nine construction deaths since 2024, broken bolt on a steel connection plate suspected as cause behind tragic accident
Four contract workers fell with steel parts during Phase 4 hoisting work, which is now halted.
Three contract workers died, and one more is in intensive care after an accident at the construction site for TSMC’s 2nm Fab 22 in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, reports Taiwan’s Central News Agency. The Southern Taiwan Science Park (STSP) Bureau suspects the cause was a broken bolt on a steel connection plate that sent the workers and steel components tumbling. Steel hoisting on the project has been halted, and the STSP has sent labor inspectors to investigate. The accident is not the first of its kind but rather follows at least a half dozen others since September 2024 at TSMC construction sites in Taiwan, according to local reports. Each of those earlier accidents killed one worker.
Local police said that the men were welding a steel beam on an upper floor and fell with it, while the STSP said the workers were performing steel-structure hoisting and installation when a third-floor connection-plate bolt apparently broke.
10 emergency vehicles were sent to the site with 22 personnel, and all four men involved in the incident were taken to the hospital. On-site medical staff gave first aid, but three of the workers died despite resuscitation efforts, and the fourth was moved to intensive care. The workers were employed by a contractor working on the fourth phase of the complex’s construction, and TSMC said the area was within that contractor’s scope of work.
According to the report, TSMC stopped the related construction work on its own and is working with authorities and supervising the subcontractor’s follow-up.
The Fab 22 complex, located in Kaohsiung’s Nanzi District, is part of the science park and is being built to accelerate 2nm manufacturing. TSMC entered high-volume 2nm, or N2, manufacturing in the fourth quarter of 2025, including at Fab 22. The complex has five phases planned, with a total investment TSMC puts at more than NT$1.5 trillion, or about $46 billion. The accident happened on the construction side, not in a producing fab. Kaohsiung’s deputy mayor said construction on Phase 4 began in August 2025, with operations expected in the fourth quarter of 2027.
Business Today reports that TSMC fab construction has increased, from four fabs a year in 2017–2024 to nine a year in 2025 and 2026. The deaths come as the company plans for 13 new leading-edge and advanced-packaging fabs in Taiwan, with company-wide capex of $60 billion to $64 billion this year.
The faster pace has encouraged the addition of a contractor’s safety record as a weight in selection and a plan for a Taiwan Semiconductor Construction Engineering Safety Association with construction partners. TSMC Chairman C.C. Wei said at last year’s shareholders meeting that safety cannot be compromised, and the company’s 2025 annual report said it will keep investing in fabs across several locations in Taiwan “with a strong emphasis on construction site safety.”
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Cliff Hou, TSMC senior vice president and deputy co-COO, told Business Today that increased worker count and overlapping construction have raised the risk, requiring careful supervision, and that TSMC’s contractor lost-time injury rate had fallen about 42% from last year’s high as of late May, when the publication toured the Nanzi site to see the overhaul. It’s too early to call the program a failure, with the cause as yet unknown.
The accident comes less than a week after an explosion killed two people at Intel’s chip plant in Israel, though that was an operating fab rather than a construction site. Both accidents come as chipmakers race to meet demand, with global chip sales passing $1 trillion through August, according to the Semiconductor Industry Association.
The STSP’s findings will determine what penalties, if any, will fall under Taiwan’s Occupational Safety and Health Act, while it assists the victims’ families. No date has been given at this time for that or for the Phase 4 steel hoisting restart. Nor has TSMC commented on any schedule impact.
Follow Tom’s Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Inception says Mercury 3 beats GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 at up to 8x the speed - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Inception says Mercury 3 beats GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 at up to 8x the speed
Diffusion language model startup Inception AI Inc. today released Mercury 3, its new flagship model.
In the company’s own benchmarks, Mercury 3 beat OpenAI Group PBC’s GPT-6 Luna and Anthropic PBC’s Claude Haiku 5.5 on eight of 12 tests at four to eight times their speed.
The release takes on the main doubt about Inception’s approach. Co-founder and Chief Executive Stefano Ermon said the question the company has heard most since Mercury 1 “is whether diffusion can scale.” As he sees it, the limits come down to “compute and data, not fundamental algorithmic barriers.”
GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 write their answers the conventional way, one token after another. A Mercury model drafts the whole response up front, then refines every position in parallel over a few passes. Inception clocked Mercury 3 at 1,068 tokens per second on Nvidia Corp. graphics processing units, with Haiku 5.5 reaching about 240 in the same comparison and GPT-6 Luna about 130.
Inception has not disclosed a parameter count for Mercury 3, saying only that it is more than 40 times the size of Mercury 1. The context window grows to 1 million tokens, up from the 260,000 that Mercury 2.5 handled. Ermon said training on Mercury 3’s successor is already under way.
Across the benchmark results, Mercury 3’s widest lead over GPT-6 Luna came in coding, where it scored 51.1 on SWE-Bench Atlas against 33.3 for the OpenAI model and 32.3 for Haiku 5.5. The new model trailed Haiku 5.5 on DeepSWE, a second coding benchmark, by 46.3 to 51.6, and on one long-context test. GPT-6 Luna won two more by less than a point each. No outside group has published its own results on the model yet.
Early customers are putting Mercury 3 into products where users notice every delay. Kuan Zou, founder and chief executive of real-time search startup Octen AI, said that on smart glasses “an answer that takes five seconds feels broken.” Median generation time in Octen’s tests was 0.9 seconds. At tutoring app RevisionDojo, co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Michael Tong said hints and marked answers now come back in about a second.
Mercury 3 lists at 20 cents per million input tokens and 70 cents per million output tokens, with cached input 90% cheaper. A launch promotion halves both rates for now. GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 each list at 10 cents and 50 cents for typical prompts. Developers can reach the new model on Inception’s own platform or through OpenRouter Inc., Baseten Labs Inc. and Vercel Inc., and software already written for OpenAI’s application programming interface needs only minor changes to call it.
Inception is a venture capital-backed startup that Ermon founded in 2024 with fellow computer science professors Aditya Grover and Volodymyr Kuleshov. Microsoft Corp.’s M12 venture arm was among the backers when Menlo Ventures led a $50 million round in the company last November.
Microsoft was in talks to acquire Inception as of May, according to a Reuters report that said the startup wanted more than $1 billion. Space Exploration Technologies Corp. had also approached the company, Reuters said. No deal with either suitor has been announced.

articles.title: El fin de la libreta de bocetos: la evolución tecnológica que jubilaría al papel en el diseño gráfico
articles.text:
El olor a grafito y el sonido de las hojas al pasar solían ser la banda sonora inconfundible de cualquier estudio de diseño. Durante décadas, las mesas de los creativos estuvieron dominadas por montañas de libretas, marcadores desgastados, libretas de recortes y gomas de borrar.
Era un ecosistema enteramente táctil, nostálgico, pero también físicamente limitante y poco amigable con la preservación del medio ambiente. Hoy, ese paisaje de papelería abarrotada empieza a desvanecerse silenciosamente para dar paso a escritorios despejados, donde un solo rectángulo de cristal encierra las herramientas de todo un taller.
La diseñadora gráfica peruana, Abril Belmonte, en declaraciones a Infobae, demostró ser consciente de esta realidad. Ya no busca su viejo cuaderno cuando llega la inspiración: ahora sus manos se deslizan sobre una pantalla con un lápiz digital que no requiere tajador. Aunque la celulosa ha sido reemplazada por luz dinámica, la fricción, el flujo de la idea y el nacimiento del trazo siguen intactos.
Esta transformación está impulsada por el desarrollo de tabletas de gama alta orientadas a la creatividad y la productividad. Dispositivos como la Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra buscan replicar la precisión del soporte físico mediante pantallas de bajo grosor, integración de estilete y funciones de inteligencia artificial. De este modo, la transición del formato impreso al digital se plantea como una optimización del flujo de trabajo.
La simulación del trazo físico: sensación táctil y ergonomía
El mayor reto de la digitalización siempre ha sido convencer a la memoria muscular de los artistas. Sin embargo, el desarrollo del lápiz óptico ha logrado replicar con exactitud el comportamiento de las herramientas tradicionales.
“Para mí, se siente muy similar a dibujar sobre una hoja de papel. Lo que más me gusta es la sensibilidad a la presión del S Pen de Samsung: cuando presionas más, el trazo sale más oscuro y grueso, y cuando lo haces más suave, se vuelve más fino”, detalla Abril Belmonte.
Técnicamente, el S Pen cuenta con un diseño ergonómico que ofrece una entrada precisa e intuitiva para tomar notas y esbozar conceptos sin esfuerzo. “Dibujar directamente con el S Pen es mucho más intuitivo que hacerlo con un mouse, porque tienes un control más directo sobre cada trazo”, añade la diseñadora.
Este nivel de detalle se potencia en aplicaciones de nivel profesional como Clip Studio Paint —que ahora llega con herramientas de pintura de precisión y beneficios exclusivos en el ecosistema—, permitiendo que el lienzo digital reaccione de la misma forma que un papel de alto gramaje absorbería la tinta.
Sostenibilidad y digitalización: de la libreta al ecosistema ecológico
Más allá de la experiencia de dibujo, la transición busca reducir la dependencia de insumos físicos. Migrar a un formato completamente digital transforma el flujo de trabajo, eliminando la necesidad de arrumar decenas de cuadernos a lo largo del año.
“Personalmente, prefiero bocetar directamente en la tablet porque es súper ligera y la llevo a todos lados. Además, tener nuestros proyectos digitalizados nos permite compartir las ideas rápidamente con el equipo”, afirma Belmonte.
Este nivel de portabilidad se apoya en un diseño de ingeniería delgado, con apenas 5,1 milímetros de grosor en su versión tope de gama. El reemplazo del papel se completa a través de plataformas nativas como Samsung Notes y herramientas de Galaxy AI, como Note Assist.
Autonomía y colaboración en cualquier lugar
El entorno de una agencia exige respuestas rápidas y soluciones integrales. Para Belmonte, la capacidad de avanzar con agilidad en proyectos complejos de marcas, empaques e ilustraciones directamente desde una tablet portátil, sin estar atada a una computadora de escritorio, es importante para el ritmo de Enigma Brand Studio.
Este rendimiento ininterrumpido en exteriores o reuniones se sostiene sobre especificaciones técnicas de vanguardia. La nueva serie de tablets incorpora resistencia al agua y al polvo con certificación IP68, lo que permite bocetar al aire libre o en ambientes exigentes sin temor a accidentes.
A nivel de autonomía, los dispositivos han sido diseñados para largas jornadas de inspiración lejos de un enchufe, ofreciendo baterías masivas que brindan hasta 23 horas de uso continuo en su modelo de 14,6 pulgadas y 21 horas en la versión Plus.
Cuando el ritmo de trabajo exige energía, la batería pasa del 0% al 100% en aproximadamente 95 minutos. Todo esto es impulsado por un procesador de 3 nanómetros que aumenta la capacidad de la CPU y GPU, refrigerado por una cámara de vapor 3D de nuevo diseño para que, al renderizar proyectos complejos bajo el brillo de 1.600 nits de su pantalla Dynamic AMOLED 2X, el equipo mantenga un rendimiento óptimo sin sobrecalentarse.

articles.title: Nouvelle cyberattaque en France : les données de propriétaires de chiens et chats ont encore été volées
articles.text:
Il y a quelques jours, un pirate qui se fait appeler ChimeraZ a revendiqué un nouveau vol de données d’envergure sur un forum. Le hacker a mis en vente plusieurs bases de données sur une plateforme criminelle. Ces annonces ont été rapidement repérées par le site spécialisé FrenchBreaches.
 🔴 Alerté par FrenchBreaches, le LOOF confirme une cyberattaque et le vol de données ! Noms, adresses, e-mails, identifiants de chats et dates de naissance potentiellement exposés. L’organisme annonce avoir identifié l’origine de l’attaque et suspendu certains services. https://t.co/jqATim9kWd
— FrenchBreaches (@Frenchbreaches) October 20, 2026
Le répertoire le plus volumineux appartient à l’I-CAD, le fichier national d’identification des chiens, chats et furets. Selon le hacker, 2,9 millions de propriétaires et 50 000 vétérinaires sont concernés par cette fuite. Le pirate revendique aussi le piratage des données de 1,4 million de personnes recensées dans la Société Centrale Canine (SCC), l’organisme de référence pour les chiens de race. Enfin, le hacker prétend également avoir compromis le Livre officiel des origines félines (LOOF), l’organisme qui gère les pedigrees des chats de race. Environ 654 000 enregistrements ainsi que plus de 90 000 documents (48 Go) ont été volés. Au total, ce sont plus de 4 millions de personnes qui auraient été touchées.
Dans les échantillons analysés par le média spécialisé, on trouve des noms et prénoms, des coordonnées, des numéros de puce électronique, des noms d’animaux, voire des pedigrees et des tests ADN. Il y a suffisamment d’informations pour relier précisément un animal à son maître, ce qui ouvre la porte à toutes les dérives et abus. Avec le nom d’un animal, sa race ou son numéro de puce, un escroc peut rendre un faux message très crédible. Il peut notamment se faire passer pour un vétérinaire ou un organisme officiel afin de réclamer un paiement. Les éleveurs, dont les coordonnées professionnelles ont été volées, sont particulièrement visés.
À lire aussi : Cyberattaques en France : les dernières fuites de données et entreprises touchées
Le LOOF confirme rapidement la cyberattaque
La fuite a été rapidement confirmée par le LOOF. Dès le 20 octobre, l’organisme a confirmé avoir été victime d’une cyberattaque. Selon le communiqué, des individus se sont introduits dans le système informatique pour récupérer des données. L’organisme confirme que des noms, prénoms, adresses postales et e-mail, noms et numéros d’identification des chats, et dates de naissance, ont été subtilisés. Le Livre officiel des origines félines précise par contre n’avoir identifié « aucune donnée sensible » ayant été compromise. Par précaution, le LOOF a coupé l’accès à plusieurs de ses services. Ensuite, l’origine de l’attaque a été découverte, et la brèche a été colmatée.
Entre les lignes, l’organisme confirme qu’une même entité s’est attaquée à l’I-CAD et à la SCC. D’autres structures ont été ciblées par des attaques du même type. Celles-ci ont été revendiquées par « le ou les mêmes individus », indique le LOOF. Ce n’est pas la première fois que les données de l’I-CAD se retrouvent entre les mains de cybercriminels. Cet été, des pirates étaient déjà parvenus à pénétrer dans le système d’Ingenium animalis, la société qui gère le fichier I-CAD. Les intrus avaient volé les adresses e-mail de millions de propriétaires de chats et de chiens. Ces attaques s’inscrivent évidemment dans l’explosion des fuites de données en France. Pays le plus touché d’Europe, la France recense plus de 40 millions de comptes piratés en six mois.

articles.title: La voiture la plus vendue du monde va passer à l'électrique
articles.text:
Toyota s’apprête à faire un grand pas pour sa gamme de voitures électriques. Le constructeur japonais va donner à son best-seller, figurant régulièrement comme la voiture la plus vendue au monde annuellement, une version électrique. Voici ce que l’on peut attendre de la future Toyota Corolla électrique, qui pourrait ne pas être fabriquée au Japon.
Une Corolla électrique à l’horizon 2028
Selon les informations venant du média japonais Nikkei, Toyota aurait l’ambition de lancer cette Corolla électrique à l’horizon 2028 en s’appuyant sur la Chine. En effet, pour préparer cette berline électrique très importante pour le constructeur japonais, l’aide de la coentreprise FAW Toyota est à envisager. C’est déjà le cas pour le Toyota bZ3X commercialisé en Chine, qui représente une bonne part des ventes de voitures électriques dans le monde pour Toyota.
Cette berline électrique portant le nom de Corolla devrait être la première Toyota à utiliser la plateforme nommée « multipathway », mais celle-ci serait multiénergie.
Adapter la Corolla au monde entier
La Toyota Corolla est un modèle essentiel pour Toyota, car elle est distribuée dans le monde entier. Mais c’est aussi un exercice difficile de proposer un même véhicule sur tous les marchés du monde. Il y a bien sûr quelques adaptations pour les différents marchés, mais une Corolla vendue aux États-Unis, au Japon ou en Europe est, dans les grandes lignes, identique.
De ce fait, Toyota doit être prudent, car il est très difficile de concilier les besoins des marchés américain, japonais, chinois ou européen dans un même et unique véhicule. C’est pour cela que Toyota ne va pas proposer qu’une version électrique de la prochaine Corolla, mais bien un véhicule multiénergie pour s’adapter aux différents marchés.
On attend donc des motorisations électriques, mais aussi des hybrides et des essence sur la future génération de Corolla. De ce fait, elle pourrait être vendue uniquement en électrique en Chine, en électrique et hybride en Europe pour répondre à nos contraintes réglementaires, et avec toutes les énergies aux États-Unis. Ce qui devrait assurer une belle réussite encore à la prochaine génération de Corolla, car Toyota ne met pas tous ses œufs dans le même panier.

articles.title: Eternal Q2 net profit rises 92% in FY27, revenue up 78%
articles.text:
Eternal Q2 net profit rises 92% in FY27, revenue up 78%
Blinkit remained a key contributor to Eternal’s revenue, reporting Rs 19,152 crore in revenue in Q2 FY27.
Eternal, the parent company of Zomato and Blinkit, reported a 92.3% year-on-year (YoY) rise in net profit in the second quarter of FY27, while revenue grew 78% YoY. However, the company missed analysts’ estimates, which had projected a net profit of Rs 250 crore.
Eternal’s net profit for the second quarter of FY27 stood at Rs 125 crore, compared with Rs 65 crore in the same period a year ago. Revenue rose to Rs 24,138 crore from Rs 13,590 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year.
The quick commerce segment, Blinkit, continued to be a key revenue contributor, with revenue reaching Rs 19,152 crore in the second quarter of FY27.
According to Eternal, Blinkit’s net order value (NOV) grew 79.3% year-on-year (YoY). The quick commerce platform added 308 new stores, taking its total store count to 2,751. Its adjusted EBITDA improved for the sixth consecutive quarter, reaching 0.9% of NOV and translating into a profit of Rs 184 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 156 crore in the year-ago period.
Eternal said it expects Blinkit’s store count to exceed 3,500 by March 2027 and potentially reach 5,000 by March 2028.
On the quick commerce business, Eternal Group CEO Albinder Singh Dhindsa said, “How we grow matters as much as how fast. Each of our stores has a finite capacity to serve. A customer who shows up only for a deep discount uses the same capacity as one who orders every week across categories. We could add customers much faster by leaning on price, but those customers usually leave when the discount ends.”
The food delivery business Zomato saw its NOV grow by 21.5% YoY and the company said growth acceleration is now continuing for five consecutive quarters.
On the performance of the food delivery business, Eternal Founder Deepinder Goyal said “We're happy with how the business is doing right now. That said, we try not to read too much into any single quarter. Our long-term expectation for food delivery has always been 20%+ annual growth, and the last two quarters have brought us back to that range. This view didn't change last year when growth slowed, and it doesn't change now that it has picked up.”
Edited by Megha Reddy

articles.title: Thermostat réglable et connexion Wi-Fi : le chauffage d’appoint Dreo 316S est à 47,49 €
articles.text:
Le chauffage soufflant connecté Dreo 316S de 1 500 W est à 47,49 € (-21 %)
Le chauffage soufflant Dreo 316S de 1 500 W associe connexion Wi-Fi, thermostat réglable et minuterie de 12 heures dans un format compact.
Amazon propose le chauffage soufflant Dreo 316S en blanc à 47,49 €, contre un prix conseillé de 59,99 €. L’économie atteint 12,50 €, soit environ 21 %. Par rapport au prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, de 49,99 €, la baisse représente 2,50 €, soit 5 %. Cette version équipée du Wi-Fi est vendue et expédiée par Amazon, avec la livraison gratuite proposée.
Un chauffage céramique de 1 500 W avec thermostat
Le chauffage d’appoint Dreo 316S utilise une résistance céramique PTC et un ventilateur pour diffuser l’air chaud. Sa puissance maximale atteint 1 500 W. Son format compact et sa poignée facilitent les déplacements entre les pièces, pour apporter ponctuellement de la chaleur dans un bureau ou une chambre.
Le thermostat permet de choisir une température entre 5 et 35 °C, par paliers de 1 °C. En mode ECO, l’appareil arrête automatiquement la chauffe lorsque la température demandée est atteinte. L’intérêt est de réguler le fonctionnement selon le besoin, sans garantir un pourcentage fixe d’économies : la consommation dépend notamment de la consigne et de l’isolation de la pièce.
Des commandes à distance et une minuterie de 12 heures
Cette déclinaison bénéficie d’une connexion Wi-Fi, en complément des commandes sur l’appareil et de la télécommande fournie. Une minuterie allant jusqu’à 12 heures permet de limiter la durée de fonctionnement. Le chauffage propose aussi plusieurs niveaux de chauffe, un mode ventilation seule et une fonction mémoire des réglages.
Le Dreo 316S intègre une protection contre la surchauffe et un dispositif anti-basculement, ainsi qu’un verrouillage enfant des commandes. Ces équipements accompagnent son usage comme chauffage d’appoint. L’appareil doit rester installé sur une surface stable, avec les entrées et sorties d’air dégagées.

articles.title: Otter.ai raises $320M in funding for its AI meeting assistant - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Otter.ai raises $320M in funding for its AI meeting assistant
Otter.ai Inc., the developer of a popular artificial intelligence meeting assistant, today announced that it has raised $320 million in funding.
The capital came entirely from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund. The investment vehicle provides startups with financing for sales and marketing initiatives. General Catalyst doesn’t take a stake in portfolio companies, but instead receives a share of the revenue that it helps them generate.
Otter.ai’s AI assistant is accessible through desktop and mobile clients. Users can launch it before a call to access information about the topics on the agenda. If a salesperson is preparing for a product pitch, Otter.ai might flag features in which the prospect expressed interest during previous meetings. The platform also pulls relevant data from external services such as HubSpot.
Otter.ai transcribes meetings with the help of an AI-powered speaker recognition engine. The feature organizes transcripts in a format that shows who said what. Furthermore, Otter.ai adds in information from any slides or screen sharing sessions that may have appeared on users’ screens.
The platform pairs every transcript with a one-page summary that outlines the topics the meeting covered and key action items. Otter.ai organizes the files that it generates by topic, team, project to make them easy to find. A built-in search engine enables users to retrieve specific items with natural language prompts.
The service can sync the data that it generates to external services via a set of ready-to-use integrations. It supports more than a dozen popular cloud services including Snowflake, Jira and OneDrive. An MCP server enables users to make Otter.ai files available to chatbots such as ChatGPT.
Otter.ai offers its core feature set alongside role-specific tools. Salespeople can generate follow-up emails to leads and automate the task of booking product demos. Teachers, in turn, have access to a tool that generates study guides based on lecture transcripts.
The company offers its service in a free tier and three paid editions. The top-end Enterprise version includes dashboards that enable managers to track trends across customer conversations. A sales executive, for example, could use Otter.ai to monitor how often leads mention a competitor. The Enterprise version also includes an expanded set of access controls and a single sign-on feature.
Otter.ai says its platform has more than 40 million users worldwide, including employees at more than 86% of the Fortune 500. Reuters reported that the company hopes to at least double its enterprise business over the next year. Otter.ai plans to achieve that goal by tripling its sales and marketing budget.

articles.title: Accident d’un Mirage 2000D de l’armée de l’Air, un corps retrouvé et un aviateur toujours recherché
articles.text:
Un Mirage 2000D de l’armée de l’Air et de l’Espace a été victime d’un accident mardi soir en Meurthe-et-Moselle. Un corps a été retrouvé, tandis que les recherches se poursuivent pour localiser le second membre d’équipage.
Il était environ 22h40, mardi 20 octobre, quand un Mirage 2000D de l'armée de l'Air et de l'Espace a été accidenté dans le secteur de Rogéville, en Meurthe-et-Moselle. L'appareil de l'escadron de chasse 2/3 « Champagne », basé à Nancy-Ochey, rentrait de mission avec deux aviateurs à son bord. Mercredi matin, le ministère des Armées a dressé un premier bilan, encore incomplet, et précisé que des enquêtes étaient en cours.
À bord du Mirage 2000D, deux aviateurs aux rôles bien distincts
Pour mener ses frappes au sol, de jour comme de nuit, le Mirage 2000D mise sur un duo assis l’un derrière l’autre. À l’avant, le pilote de chasse tient les commandes. À l’arrière, le navigateur officier systèmes d’armes, ou NOSA, joue le rôle de copilote tactique, en ce qu'il trace la route, surveille les capteurs, comme la nacelle qui pointe un laser sur la cible, et guide les bombes jusqu’à leur objectif. Hier soir, c’est ce tandem qui rentrait de mission.
Selon le ministère, un corps a été retrouvé et attend d’être formellement identifié, tandis que le second membre d’équipage est toujours recherché. Aucune identité n’a été rendue publique.
Deux enquêtes sont menées en parallèle, avec des buts différents. L'enquête de sécurité, qui relève du Bureau enquêtes accidents pour la sécurité de l'aéronautique d'État (BEA-É), cherche à comprendre pour prévenir, sans désigner de coupable. L'enquête judiciaire, elle, établira d'éventuelles responsabilités. Le ministère n'avance aucune piste, et il faudra sans doute des mois avant d'y voir clair.
Un Mirage 2000D tout juste remis à neuf
Dérivé du Mirage 2000N, qui portait l'arme nucléaire, le Mirage 2000D est en service depuis 1993 et s'est fait une spécialité des frappes au sol, en journée ou en pleine nuit. On rappelle qu'à la mi-juin, la Direction générale de l'armement (DGA) livrait le cinquantième et dernier exemplaire rénové à mi-vie, au terme d'un chantier lancé en 2015.
Jusqu’ici dépourvu de canon intégré, l’avion a reçu un canon de 30 mm logé dans une nacelle sous le fuselage, pour tirer sur des cibles au sol et épauler directement les troupes au combat. Pour se défendre face à un chasseur ennemi, il troque ses vieux missiles Magic II contre des Mica IR, qui se guident sur la chaleur dégagée par l’appareil adverse. Son électronique a enfin gagné un module qui traite davantage de données et les fait mieux circuler entre les équipements de bord, de quoi lui permettre de voler au-delà de 2030 aux côtés du Rafale.
Ce n'est en tout cas pas le premier drame pour les Mirage de l'armée de l'Air. Le 9 janvier 2019, un 2000D de Nancy-Ochey s'était écrasé dans le Jura en plein vol à très basse altitude, causant la perte de ses deux membres d'équipage. Le BEA-É avait ensuite pointé des erreurs humaines liées à un manque d'entraînement. En août 2024, deux Mirage 2000 entraient en collision près de Colombey-les-Belles, faisant deux morts. Mercredi, les recherches, elles, se poursuivent toujours pour retrouver le second aviateur.

articles.title: Câmeras do Smart Sampa foram expostas em vazamento; MP investiga • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Câmeras do Smart Sampa foram expostas em vazamento; MP investiga
Informações do sistema de videomonitoramento da Prefeitura de São Paulo ficaram disponíveis por cerca de 11 meses em um repositório público.
Dados de acesso ao Smart Sampa, sistema de videomonitoramento da Prefeitura de São Paulo, ficaram expostos por cerca de 11 meses em um repositório público na internet. O material permitia acessar transmissões de parte das mais de 58 mil câmeras do programa e continha informações de milhares de agentes de segurança.
Segundo apuração do portal UOL publicada nesta terça-feira (20/10), entre os arquivos encontrados estavam 181 combinações de login e senha, dados cadastrais de mais de 6 mil agentes e informações sobre reprodução de funções da plataforma.
A reportagem afirma ter conseguido acessar imagens ao vivo de vias públicas e de equipamentos municipais, como escolas, unidades de saúde e hospitais. A Prefeitura confirmou o vazamento ao Tecnoblog, mas nega que houve falha de segurança. Segundo a nota da gestão do município, os dados foram divulgados ilegalmente por um servidor, que já foi identificado, afastado e está sob investigação da Corregedoria da Guarda Civil Metropolitana (GCM).
Os arquivos encontrados no repositório continham informações que permitiam reproduzir funções da central em outros dispositivos e realizar consultas usando dados como nomes, CPFs e placas de veículos, de acordo com o UOL.
Essas informações permaneceram disponíveis em um repositório aberto por cerca de 11 meses. Parte das credenciais permitia acessar a plataforma da Sentinelx, empresa responsável pelo software usado pelo Smart Sampa.
A reportagem afirma que as credenciais possibilitavam visualizar transmissões de equipamentos conectados em locais como escolas e hospitais. Em um dos testes, um repórter foi até uma rua do bairro Campos Elíseos, no centro de São Paulo, e acenou diante de quatro câmeras. A equipe conseguiu acompanhar os movimentos em tempo real.
Foram identificadas:
Inaugurado em julho de 2024, o Smart Sampa reúne câmeras públicas e câmeras privadas conectadas a uma central de monitoramento da Prefeitura de São Paulo. O programa é operado pela Sentinelx em um contrato estimado em R$ 588 milhões ao longo de cinco anos.
O Ministério Público de São Paulo abriu um procedimento para apurar o vazamento. Segundo o jornal Folha de S.Paulo, ainda não se trata de uma investigação formal, mas de uma Notícia de Fato instaurada pela secretaria da Promotoria.
A Prefeitura de São Paulo afirma que um servidor que já possuía autorização para acessar o Smart Sampa divulgou informações do sistema ilegalmente. O funcionário foi afastado e sua conduta está sendo investigada pela Corregedoria da GCM.
Em nota ao Tecnoblog, a gestão do prefeito Ricardo Nunes (MDB) afirma que “não há nenhuma fragilidade nos mecanismos de segurança” do Smart Sampa e acusa o UOL de agir “com irresponsabilidade”.
A administração municipal declara que o programa é fiscalizado pelo Tribunal de Contas do Município e conta com mecanismos de supervisão e auditoria previstos em contrato. Segundo a Prefeitura, as câmeras instaladas em equipamentos públicas ficam em áreas de circulação comum e não abrangem consultórios, salas de atendimento ou outros ambientes assistenciais.
“O repositório de dados disponibilizado ilegalmente na internet foi retirado do ar pela Pasta e não havia nele menção a senhas de acesso”, diz a nota.

articles.title: Millions of routers can be hijacked over Wi-Fi thanks to a 16-year-old bug
articles.text:
Why it matters: Chipmakers ship buggy code all the time, that alone isn't news. What makes WPSplinter stand out is that Broadcom apparently did issue a fix eight years ago, but that fix never reached the routers sitting in people's homes. Furthermore, the lack of a CVE kept the problem invisible to the advisories and patch pipelines that router makers and ISPs rely on.
Security researcher Quentin Kaiser detailed the flaw at the Hexacon conference in Paris on October 16. He calls it WPSplinter, a name he only gave it because Broadcom refused to issue an official identifier.
The bug sits in Broadcom's old code for WPS, the feature that lets you connect a device by pressing a button on the router instead of typing a password. That code mishandles how certain messages are exchanged and with the right sequence of them, it lets an attacker read the router's memory or run external code on the device.
The attacker doesn't need the Wi-Fi password or a completed WPS pairing. Being within radio range is enough. This also isn't the WPS PIN weakness that made headlines in the early 2010s. The problem is Broadcom's code, not WPS itself.
Kaiser's demos make the risk concrete. On an Askey TCG3000 gateway supplied by Orange Belgium, his exploit pulled the Wi-Fi key out of the device's NVRAM, sent it back over the air, and then used it to join the network. On a different device, a Proximus BBOX3V+ made by Sagemcom, he got a remote shell running entirely over Wi-Fi, with no internet connection needed on his end. He says the attack works over long distances.
One detail that won't surprise anyone at this point... Kaiser says AI helped him find the bug in less than a week, work that would have taken months by hand. Router firmware used to be protected partly by obscurity and by how tedious it was to dig through. That's no longer the case, for researchers or attackers.
Kaiser confirmed the bug on gateways from three of Belgium's four major ISPs: Proximus, Orange and VOO. By his count, that's about 1.5 million vulnerable devices in Belgium alone. But routers built on the same Broadcom chips are sold worldwide. His list of affected models, which he says is incomplete, includes gear from Cisco, TP-Link, Netgear, Sagemcom, Nokia, ZTE and Zyxel, deployed by ISPs like Movistar, Optus, KPN and Türk Telekom. That tally would put a closer global estimation in the low hundreds of millions.
When Kaiser reported the bug in July, Broadcom said it had known about it since 2018, had since replaced the old WPS code in its software, and that he should take it up with device makers. Kaiser says the 2018 patch to the old code was incomplete anyway. Broadcom also declined to request a CVE, calling the code obsolete and outside its support window.
On Hacker News, some argue that the blame is on router makers and ISPs for never updating. Kaiser's counterpoint is that without a CVE, the warning likely never made it down the supply chain.
Changing your Wi-Fi password won't help, since the attack happens before login. Turning off WPS is (always) worth doing, but Kaiser warns it may not fully disable the vulnerable code. If in doubt about your ISP's router firmware, it's best to switch off the gateway's Wi-Fi, put it in bridge mode, and use your own up-to-date router. Kaiser has also posted a detection script on GitHub for anyone who wants to check their hardware.
One last detail that won't surprise anyone at this point. Kaiser says AI tools helped him find the bug in under a week, work that would have taken months by hand. Router firmware used to be protected partly by obscurity and by how tedious it was to dig through. That's no longer the case, for researchers or attackers.

articles.title: OpenAI quiere crear medicamentos con IA: comprar una startup biotecnológica es su primer paso
articles.text:
OpenAI quiere llevar la inteligencia artificial al desarrollo de medicamentos y dio un paso en esa dirección con la compra de Orchestra Bio, una plataforma que ayuda a las empresas biofarmacéuticas a ordenar y seguir el largo camino que lleva a crear un nuevo tratamiento.
La adquisición permitirá unir la tecnología de Orchestra Bio con Rosalind, las herramientas de OpenAI para investigadores de biología y química.
La apuesta es usar IA no solo para analizar datos científicos, también para coordinar el trabajo que hace falta para que un descubrimiento llegue a convertirse en un medicamento.
Desarrollar un fármaco puede llevar, en promedio, entre 10 y 15 años desde la identificación de un objetivo hasta la aprobación regulatoria en Estados Unidos, según OpenAI. En ese período intervienen científicos, áreas de fabricación, equipos de ensayos clínicos y socios externos.
El desafío no está únicamente en encontrar una molécula prometedora. Consiste en evitar que los problemas de organización, los datos dispersos o una demora en una etapa frenen todo el programa.
Qué significa esta adquisición para OpenAI
La compra de Orchestra Bio acerca a OpenAI a una de las partes menos visibles, pero más complejas, de la industria farmacéutica: la coordinación diaria de los proyectos que buscan desarrollar nuevos tratamientos.
Orchestra Bio ofrece una plataforma en la que las personas pueden trabajar junto con agentes de IA.
Esos sistemas pueden seguir estudios, campañas y cronogramas, además de reunir información de distintas áreas para detectar posibles retrasos.
La empresa incorporará también a un equipo con experiencia en biotecnología, software e inteligencia artificial. La idea es combinar ese conocimiento con Rosalind, el conjunto de herramientas que OpenAI ya desarrolla para las ciencias de la vida.
Dentro de esa iniciativa, GPT-Rosalind puede ayudar a los científicos a analizar preguntas de biología y química. Rosalind Workbench, en tanto, conecta esos modelos con datos y herramientas científicas para revisar resultados y planificar experimentos.
Para qué sirve incorporar IA en el desarrollo de medicamentos
La inteligencia artificial puede ayudar a los equipos a encontrar antes los obstáculos que amenazan con retrasar un proyecto. Un problema en la fabricación de un lote, por ejemplo, puede postergar el inicio de un ensayo clínico y afectar otras tareas previstas.
Los agentes de Orchestra Bio pueden identificar qué actividades y plazos están comprometidos, reunir la información relacionada y mostrar distintas alternativas para responder. La decisión final sigue en manos de científicos y responsables del programa, pero con más datos disponibles y menos tareas manuales.
OpenAI mencionó sus alianzas con Novo Nordisk y Moderna. Según la compañía, la IA puede transformar información científica compleja en planes de trabajo y experimentos concretos.
El objetivo es acompañar todo el proceso: desde explorar una idea y diseñar un experimento hasta interpretar los resultados y coordinar los pasos necesarios para que los tratamientos prometedores lleguen antes a los pacientes.
Sam Altman confiesa su temor con ChatGPT
Sam Altman, director ejecutivo de OpenAI, afirmó que no ha dormido bien desde el lanzamiento de ChatGPT por la responsabilidad de definir cómo responde la herramienta.
El directivo explicó que cada límite, advertencia o rechazo implica decidir qué información puede ofrecer el sistema, cuándo debe intervenir y cómo equilibrar la libertad de uso con la prevención de daños.
En una entrevista con The Tucker Carlson Show, Altman señaló que OpenAI consulta a filósofos morales y expertos en ética tecnológica, aunque reconoció que la decisión final corresponde a la empresa.
Según explicó, una norma puede evitar un perjuicio, pero también restringir una consulta válida para educación, salud o investigación.
Le preocupan, sobre todo, los ajustes pequeños: el tono, el detalle de una explicación o la forma de rechazar un pedido.
El ejecutivo defendió que ChatGPT debe tratar a los adultos como adultos, con protecciones frente a solicitudes que faciliten daños graves, como instrucciones para fabricar armas biológicas o desarrollar síntesis virales.

articles.title: Jensen Huang Nvidia GTC keynote disrupted by Greenpeace protest over chips in Russian drones — 'What are you doing about that?' heckler demands before being thrown out
articles.text:
Jensen Huang Nvidia GTC keynote disrupted by Greenpeace protest over chips in Russian drones — 'What are you doing about that?' heckler demands before being thrown out
"What are you doing about the environmental destruction?"
Protesters disrupted Jensen Huang's Nvidia GTC keynote in Berlin on Wednesday morning. Just minutes into the CEO's customary address, the broadcast was interrupted by a heckler from the crowd demanding the CEO answer claims that the company's chips were found inside Russian drones, and charges of environmental destruction more broadly. While the incident wasn't fully picked up by Nvidia's livestream, footage filmed by attendees shows protestors standing on chairs with a large banner that reads "Nvidia, clean up your dirty business!"
Multiple videos and images shared to X show protestors brandishing a large banner with a Greenpeace logo. "Jensen, what about the technology that was found in Russian drones? Those were Nvidia chips. What are you doing about that?" one of the protestors called out across the auditorium. "What are you doing about that? What are you doing about the environmental destruction?" the heckler demanded.
Huang can be heard on the broadcast and in the video stating, "It's okay, go easy," as security rushed to escort the protesters out of the hall. "I'll talk to you later," Huang stated as the individuals were removed from the premises.
The complaint raised by the protester appears to relate to recent reports that Nvidia Jetson chips have been found in Russian cruise missiles used against Ukraine, as well as in AI drones. Reports indicate Russia's S-71 'Monochrome' weapon has autonomous targeting capability powered by Nvidia's consumer-grade Jetson Orin chip. "Our Jetson Orin modules are consumer-grade products sold to students, developers, and startups for a wide range of beneficial applications," Nvidia told Tom's Hardware at the time. The company reiterated that the chips are not available in Russia and are not designed for military purposes, but admitted it cannot track the resale of pre-owned Jetson chips after they are sold.
A report in August claimed that a Russian AI drone killed three civilians in Ukraine, the first documented case of civilian deaths caused by a Russian drone using fully autonomous targeting. Images of the recovered drones confirmed they contained Jetson Orin modules. "All important issues, but let me get through my keynote," Huang quipped before continuing his presentation.
Huang is in Berlin for Nvidia's three-day GTC event, taking place from October 20-22. The customary keynote, given this morning, also includes fireside chats and talks for developers and business leaders.
