articles.title: Asus' ROG XBOX Ally X20 is a big step forward, but not in performance
articles.text:
I’m writing this a few days after my MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ review went live on MobileSyrup, and as much as I enjoyed my time with the mean $2,200 gaming machine, it did have its share of cons, including its LCD display. Now, I have Asus’ latest 20th anniversary ROG Xbox Ally X20 in front of me, and it addresses some of the new Claw’s limitations head-on.
The Claw had several appealing features, but its biggest selling point was undoubtedly Intel’s new Arc G3 Extreme chip. With XeSS thrown into the mix, the custom handheld chip proves just how far handheld gaming PCs have come in terms of raw performance. Look beyond the processor, though, and the new Claw loses some of its appeal, especially considering its hefty price.
This is where I feel that Asus can fill the gap. The original Xbox Ally X, released last year, is a more direct rival to the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+, at least when it comes to display technology, since both feature dated LCD panels. However, 2026 marks Asus’ 20th anniversary of its Republic of Gamers (ROG) brand, and the company has gone beyond simply slapping a decorative logo onto an existing product.
The new ROG Xbox Ally X20 swaps its predecessor’s LCD for an OLED panel, paired with other refinements to the handheld gaming experience. Most importantly, at C$1,899, it costs $300 less than MSI’s latest offering. But is it truly a better handheld?
The OLED upgrade
Let’s start with the most glaring improvement, no pun intended. The ROG Xbox Ally X20’s OLED display is a delight to look at, especially in more vivid and colourful games like Ninja Gaiden 4 and Dragon Ball: Sparking! Zero. The latest Steam Deck and the Lenovo Legion Go 2 both feature OLED panels, and it’s nice to see the rest of the industry heading in that direction. The first two are limited to 1,000 nits of peak HDR brightness, while the new X20 pushes that to 1,400 nits.
For reference, the original Xbox Ally X’s IPS-level panel could only achieve 500 nits. This makes the new X20’s advertised HDR max almost three times brighter. Even though the two figures aren’t directly comparable, the spec bump is definitely noticeable in practice, with high-contrast scenes looking particularly striking. It’s one of those upgrades that’s difficult to appreciate from a spec sheet alone, and much more evident when you try it yourself.
And even when you’re not playing HDR-supported titles, the X20 has an advantage over its predecessor. Its SDR brightness is rated at 600 nits, which is 100 nits brighter than its predecessor and even the new Claw 8 EX AI+. The 20% improvement, too, is very noticeable, and arguably more important for everyday use. That’s because the Windows interface renders in SDR, so even if you’re not necessarily gaming, you should see improvements during everyday Windows navigation, browsing, and general use. Is that a big enough reason to upgrade from last year’s Xbox Ally X? In my opinion, no. Should you upgrade if you’re holding onto an even older handheld? Paired with other upgrades, there’s definitely a case there.
Asus has also given the new handheld a bigger 7.4-inch display while retaining its predecessor’s 1,920 x 1,080 pixel resolution. The Xbox Ally X offered a 7-inch display, and although the extra 0.4 inches don’t sound like much on paper, the extra screen real estate is always welcome, especially when navigating through Windows menus that aren’t really optimized for the small screen experience.
Elsewhere, another practical screen-based upgrade comes in the form of a Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) change. For reference, the original Xbox Ally X also featured VRR, albeit in the 48Hz to 120Hz range. The X20 supports VRR between 30Hz and 120Hz, which makes a lot more practical sense for a gaming handheld. Most modern PC games offer built-in frame rate caps that start at 30fps, followed by 60fps, and higher options. With the older Ally X’s 48Hz lower limit, a game capped at 30fps would fall outside the display’s native VRR range. The X20, on the other hand, can synchronize its display directly with frame rates as low as 30fps, which should result in less screen tearing. This is particularly useful in demanding titles that struggle to maintain 60fps — a consistent 30fps is better than fluctuating below 60.
And 30 fps is still a very real target in 2026. For reference, GTA VI will be limited to 30 fps on the PlayStation at launch, and my testing with Black Myth: Wukong (more on that below) shows that even today’s powerful handheld PCs can struggle to maintain 60fps in demanding games.
Rounding off the main display-based upgrades is support for Dolby Vision HDR and a new anti-reflective coating.
More than a simple anniversary makeover
At first glance, the new Ally X20 doesn’t look significantly different from its predecessor from the outside. It retains the controller-like look with the Xbox-style ABXY button layout that makes the Ally line instantly recognizable. However, a closer look reveals more.
The entire body features a translucent layout that looks straight out of Nothing’s playbook, with the front adorned with the familiar Xbox and ROG lettering repeated across the surface. It’s not a huge change, but it sure does offer the X20 its own identity while retaining the familiar Ally design.
There are black and gold anniversary accents all over the front and back that I’m not necessarily a huge fan of, but I can appreciate Asus trying out something new. Thankfully, the design changes aren’t all cosmetic.
Compared to its predecessor, the X20 offers better rubberized grips that make holding onto the handheld more secure in hand, especially during extended gaming sessions. The device weighs in at 756g, and although the rubberized grips help, they don’t outright eliminate grip fatigue. I had this issue with the Claw 8 EX AI+, and even though the X20 is slightly lighter than MSI’s latest, the same issue prevails. This is an inherent drawback of handheld gaming PCs, which, in part, is exacerbated by my poor wrist health.
That being said, grip fatigue shouldn’t take away from other improvements packed into the new handheld. The X20 now features TMR joysticks, which use Hall Effect-like magnetic sensing to detect movement instead of relying on physical contact between components. This should make the joysticks much less susceptible to stick drift, a must on a $1,900 device.
The D-pad has received a quiet upgrade too. You can lift and rotate the X20’s traditional D-pad to switch between four-way and eight-way directional inputs.
Before I tried out the handheld, I had imagined this to be a finicky experience, though that wasn’t really the case. Lifting and rotating the D-pad is seamless, and the eight-way directional controls feel just as solid as the traditional four-way configuration, with no noticeable wobbling or stray movement. If you like fighting games where diagonal inputs are essential, the added flexibility should definitely come in handy. This isn’t a make-or-break addition, but it sure is a welcome one that doesn’t feel gimmicky.
The rest of the layout remains familiar, including two rear buttons, shoulder triggers, a power button that doubles as a fingerprint reader, a headphone jack, two Type-C ports, and a microSD Express card reader.
Like the Claw 8 EX AI+, the X20 also uses an M.2 SSD, which should make future swaps a lot more straightforward. It’s worth noting, though, that unlike the Claw, you will need to disconnect the X20’s battery to reach the SSD.
Compared to last year’s Xbox Ally X, that’s everything that Asus has changed. The Xbox Ally X starts at $1,300. The X20 starts at $1,900. You’re essentially paying a $600 premium for a better display, improved controls, and a handful of design refinements.
New look, same old power
Yep, that’s about it. That premium doesn’t get you more power, nor does it get you more performance. The X20 retains its predecessor’s AMD Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme chip with integrated AMD Radeon Graphics.
Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme isn’t a bad processor by any means. When we used the Ally X last year, we found it to be a very capable performer, and that hasn’t changed at all. What has changed, however, is the competition. What was once the best handheld PC chip on the market is now facing stiff competition from Intel’s new Arc G3 Extreme, which powers the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+.
In my testing, the Intel-powered handheld delivered impressive performance in demanding games, though the performance results varied depending on the power configuration and whether upscaling and frame generation were enabled. I ran the same tests on the X20 on comparable power levels to see how AMD’s chip holds up against Intel’s latest and greatest, and the results were surprising.
I started with a relatively well-optimized title that runs well on most modern handhelds: Forza Horizon 5. With the game running at 1,920 x 1,080 resolution, high settings, no frame generation, and at the X20’s sustained power limit of 35W, I recorded 82fps. Dropping the power limit to a more modest 17W brought the frames down to 64fps.
With a slightly higher in-game resolution of 1,920 x 1,200 and otherwise comparable graphics settings, and the same sustained power limit of 35W, the Claw 8 EX AI+ benchmarked at 110fps. The same benchmark at 17W returned 78fps.
Intel’s new chip clearly seems to have an upper hand here, even though the X20’s results are nothing to scoff at. The overall Horizon 5 experience was smooth and perfectly playable, and paired with the OLED, I’d argue that it was actually better than the Claw 8’s experience. But that’s mainly because the performance difference wasn’t huge.
Naturally, I turned to a more demanding title to really put the X20 through its paces.
With Black Myth: Wukong running at 1,920 x 1,080, high settings, the X20’s max sustained power limit set at 35W, and no frame-gen, I recorded between 26 and 31fps. Enabling FSR 3 frame generation pushed that up to 44–50fps.
Reducing the power limit to 17W also dropped fps to 22-26 with no frame generation. Enabling frame-gen pushed that to a perfectly playable 34-42fps run. I’d still recommend running demanding titles at medium settings. At 35W, the X20 offered 45–50fps without frame generation, which increased to 56–63fps with the feature enabled. At 17W, I recorded 31–35fps without frame generation and 48–52fps with it.
I recorded all these figures across a repeated area in the game with the same enemies and surroundings, so they should give you a good idea of how different power settings affect performance on the X20.
Now, how do those figures compare to the Claw 8 EX AI+? Terribly.
With the same repeated area on high settings, the Claw managed 50-60fps at its 35W sustained power without frame generation. Enabling XeSS frame generation pushed that figure to 85–110fps. At 17W, the Claw managed 29–37fps without frame generation and 46–58fps with it. That’s already comparable, if not better, to the figures the X20 offered on medium settings.
| Device | Graphics | Power mode | Frame gen OFF | Frame gen ON | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 | High | 35W sustained | 26–31 FPS | 44–50 FPS | 
| Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 | High | 17W | 22–26 FPS | 34–42 FPS | 
| MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ | High | 35W sustained | 50–60 FPS | 85–110 FPS | 
| MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ | High | 17W | 29–37 FPS | 46–58 FPS | 
The Claw leveraged Intel’s XeSS tech, while the X20 relied on AMD’s FSR 3, so this test wasn’t necessarily a perfect apples-to-apples comparison. Still, it’s easy to point out how Intel’s latest chip has a significant performance advantage. It’ll be interesting to see how AMD responds with its next-generation Ryzen AI Z3 Extreme chip, though that’s a conversation for another day.
I think it’s important to mention here that the X20 losing to the Claw in raw performance doesn’t necessarily make it a worse handheld. It’s just worse in that one specific category. In fact, I’d argue that the X20 offers an overall better gaming experience thanks to its OLED display. My main issue is that Asus is charging $1,900 for what is essentially last year’s performance. The X20 is the best handheld I’ve tried, but it’s not the best at everything. Both of those things can be true.
Elsewhere, there’s nothing particularly revolutionary about the software experience compared to last year’s Xbox Ally X, and the same goes for battery life.
Who should spend $1,900 on this?
If you’re in the market for your first PC gaming handheld, and you’re deciding between MSI and Asus’ latest offerings, I’d suggest going for the Ally X20. The Claw is undoubtedly more powerful, but the X20’s OLED display, paired with slightly inferior performance, is a better value proposition. Spending $2,200 on the Claw 8 EX AI+ makes absolutely no sense unless raw performance is your absolute priority, or if you’re rolling in cash.
If you already own last year’s Xbox Ally X, I wouldn’t recommend upgrading. Sure, the OLED and the design changes are tempting, but they’re not worth spending $1,900 when almost everything else is essentially the same. You’ll be better off holding onto your handheld for now.
If you’re still using an older handheld, like the original Steam Deck, or even the 2023-released ROG Ally, there’s a much stronger case for upgrading if you’re in the market. You’ll definitely appreciate the OLED display, though the more apparent upgrade will likely be the performance bump, especially in more demanding titles. The X20’s controller-like layout should also be a welcome improvement over the flatter designs of older handhelds.
And if you’re someone who’s expecting to replicate a proper gaming PC experience with the X20, I’d suggest saving up more and investing in a gaming laptop or potentially even a PC instead. As impressive as modern handhelds are getting, they’re still handhelds that are held back by the very thing that makes them appealing in the first place: their compact size. There’s only so much performance you can squeeze into a portable device before you need to plug in, and at that point, you might as well be playing on a more powerful gaming laptop.
The Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 is priced at $1,899 in Canada. There’s also a special anniversary bundle that includes gold-accented ROG XREAL R1 Edition 20 augmented reality (AR) glasses, a dbrand Killswitch Case, and a hard-shell Pelican Protector Case. The bundle will set you back $3,499.

articles.title: Enterprise work management at Elevate - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
What to expect during monday.com’s Elevate event: Join theCUBE Oct. 29
Enterprise work management is entering a new phase as artificial intelligence agents move beyond assisting employees to executing business processes.
Platforms once designed to organize projects and track assignments are becoming environments where people and autonomous agents collaborate, raising questions about application development, productivity and governance. That transition is a central theme of monday.com’s Elevate conference, taking place Oct. 28–29 at the Javits Center in New York City. The event brings together business leaders, developers and technology professionals to examine how AI is changing enterprise operations. SiliconANGLE and theCUBE will provide exclusive interviews and analysis, with special coverage airing Oct. 29. (* Disclosure below.)
“Monday.com Elevate signals a broader shift in application development: from building software that helps people manage work to building AI-powered applications and agents that execute work,” said Paul Nashawaty, principal analyst at theCUBE Research. “For AppDev leaders, the promise of AI-assisted app creation is compelling, particularly as business teams seek to build tailored solutions faster and reduce their dependence on constrained engineering resources.”
The opportunity is substantial, but so are the challenges of deploying autonomous systems within established enterprise environments. As monday.com expands its AI capabilities, theCUBE will examine whether organizations can translate faster application development into measurable business outcomes while maintaining oversight of increasingly independent agents.
AI-powered application development moves beyond traditional work management
The growing use of AI agents is changing expectations for enterprise work management software. Rather than simply coordinating assignments, these platforms are beginning to execute the work itself, automating processes and giving employees new ways to create applications without extensive coding expertise.
The shift is already evident in enterprise software development, where AI adoption has accelerated significantly.
“The momentum behind events like Elevate is unmistakable. According to theCUBE Research, 92% of organizations now report AI capabilities integrated into at least one stage of their software delivery lifecycle, up sharply from 71% in early 2024,” said Sam Weston, analyst at theCUBE Research.
The company’s monday AI ecosystem brings together several capabilities intended to support that shift. Agent Factory allows organizations to create specialized AI agents, while monday sidekick provides contextual assistance within the workspace. Meanwhile, monday vibe enables users to build custom business applications through natural-language prompts, reducing the technical expertise traditionally required for software development.
These capabilities could help businesses address application backlogs and automate processes that span departments. Sales teams, for example, could use agents to qualify leads and update records, while service organizations could automate ticket routing and resolution. The broader opportunity is to connect these activities within a shared operational environment.
The Elevate 2026 agenda includes hands-on sessions focused on building AI agents, creating applications with vibe coding and integrating automation into enterprise workflows. The emphasis on practical implementation reflects a growing industry challenge: moving beyond experimental AI applications to systems that deliver consistent results.
The anticipated expansion of autonomous agents adds urgency to these efforts, particularly as enterprises consider how human employees and AI systems will share responsibility for business processes.
“With 79% of organizations anticipating widespread AI agent adoption within three years, Elevate26’s focus on building with AI agents and human-agent collaboration arrives at a pivotal moment for enterprise leaders,” Weston said.
The real test, however, is whether organizations can move beyond rapid prototyping to production-grade applications with measurable business value, maintainability and enterprise controls, according to Nashawaty.
“Elevate’s significance will ultimately be determined not by how quickly an app can be generated, but by how reliably it can be deployed, governed and scaled,” he said.
AI agent governance becomes essential as autonomous workflows expand
Giving AI agents greater responsibility across business applications also introduces new security and governance challenges. Agents that can access sensitive information, modify records or initiate transactions require clearly defined permissions and oversight mechanisms, particularly when their activities cross organizational boundaries.
For enterprises adopting AI-powered work management, the challenge extends beyond protecting individual applications. Organizations must establish how agents authenticate, what information they can access and which activities require human approval.
“The security question gets more difficult as AI agents move deeper into enterprise workflows. An agent may be acting on behalf of a person, but its access can span applications, data and business processes. Enterprises need a clear way to establish whose authority the agent is operating under, what it is allowed to do, and when a human needs to get involved,” said Krista Case, principal analyst and practice lead of cybersecurity and cyber resilience at theCUBE Research.
These considerations become particularly important as business users gain the ability to create applications and automated workflows independently. Faster development can reduce pressure on IT teams, but it can also introduce inconsistencies in security policies, access controls and operational accountability if organizations lack centralized governance.
The Elevate agenda addresses these concerns through sessions dedicated to AI governance and guardrails, offering a broader discussion about what enterprises need to consider before expanding agent deployments.
“Platforms such as monday.com are becoming places where people and AI agents coordinate work together,” Case added. “That puts governance directly in the flow of work. Companies need visibility into what agents are doing, controls around the data and actions available to them, and an audit trail that lets teams understand how work moved from a request to an outcome.”
For monday.com and its enterprise customers, the next stage of AI adoption will depend on balancing easier application creation with the security and governance requirements of production environments. TheCUBE’s coverage will examine how that balance shapes the company’s platform strategy and what it means for organizations preparing to give AI agents a more active role in everyday business operations.
TheCUBE event livestream
Don’t miss theCUBE’s coverage of monday.com’s Elevate event on Oct. 29. Plus, you can access theCUBE’s exclusive content on demand after the event.
How to watch theCUBE interviews
We offer you various ways to watch theCUBE’s coverage of monday.com’s Elevate event, including theCUBE’s dedicated website and YouTube channel. You can also get all the coverage from this year’s events on SiliconANGLE.
TheCUBE podcasts
SiliconANGLE’s “theCUBE Pod” is available on Apple Podcasts, Spotify and YouTube, which you can enjoy while on the go. During each podcast, SiliconANGLE’s John Furrier and Dave Vellante discuss the biggest trends in enterprise tech, including AI, cloud, cybersecurity and infrastructure, with context and analysis.
SiliconANGLE also produces our weekly “Breaking Analysis” program, where Vellante examines major developments in enterprise tech, combining insights from theCUBE with spending data from Enterprise Technology Research, available on Apple Podcasts, Spotify and YouTube.
Guests
During monday.com’s Elevate 2026, theCUBE will feature interviews focused on the company’s AI strategy, Agent Factory, monday sidekick and vibe coding. Discussions will address how AI agents are changing enterprise workflows, the business implications of AI-powered application development and the security and governance challenges of deploying autonomous systems at scale.

articles.title: Building AI in India? Privacy is now a valuation issue: Shivaarti Bajaj
articles.text:
Building AI in India? Privacy is now a valuation issue: Shivaarti Bajaj
At TechSparks 2026, Shivaarti Bajaj of RSD Bajaj Global Law Firm explains why consent, data mapping, and breach readiness under India’s DPDP Act now shape how investors value AI and data-driven startups.
As India’s startups race to build AI-first products, the way they handle personal data could decide what those companies are eventually worth.
Speaking at TechSparks 2026, YourStory’s annual flagship summit, Shivaarti Bajaj, Founding Managing Partner of RSD Bajaj Global Law Firm, argued that privacy can no longer be an afterthought. Founders, she said, are not just shipping products but creating assets: assets that can be valued, bought, sold, devalued, or even taken away if they are not built and complied with correctly.
“When we are creating products, we are creating companies, an asset,” Bajaj said.
Intellectual property remains the first line of defence. Trademarks protect the brands that D2C companies are building, patents matter for deep tech innovation, and copyrights and design protection cover creators, semiconductors, and IoT hardware. But Bajaj noted that IP law in India is well established. The newer and less understood risk lies in the data sets companies collect and create.
To illustrate the stakes, she pointed to Verizon’s acquisition of Yahoo’s operating business. The deal was originally agreed at $4.83 billion, but after Yahoo disclosed two major data breaches, the price was cut by $350 million, and Verizon took on a share of the related litigation.
Buyers and investors, Bajaj said, now factor remediation costs into pricing. Whether a company is in D2C, edtech, deep tech, or AI, it can expect a valuation discount if it has no data map, cannot prove consent, works with vendors who handle data without contracts, or has no breach response plan.
In India, these questions are becoming urgent. The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules are being phased in over an 18-month window that began on November 13, 2025, with full obligations taking effect by May 2027. Once fully in force, penalties under the law can go up to Rs 250 crore for security lapses, and up to Rs 200 crore each for failures in breach reporting or in handling children’s data.
“We are not talking about a few thousands,” Bajaj noted. “These are very serious things which require a lot of compliance.”
She also showed how quickly regulation can move. After the misuse of AI-generated images through Grok on X in January this year, the government brought in synthetic media rules by February. The rules require AI-generated content to be labelled and to carry metadata that identifies the tool used, which means the gap between incident and regulation was barely a quarter.
India does not yet have a dedicated AI law, but its AI governance guidelines set out seven guiding “sutras” centred on trust, consent, and accountability. For Bajaj, the most important takeaway for builders is privacy by design. That means getting compliance, data alignment, and consent mechanisms right at the code, design, and supply chain level from day one.
Consent itself must be specific. Data collected for one purpose, such as facial recognition, cannot be repurposed to train a model. Withdrawing consent must also be as easy as giving it. And unlike many global regimes that set the age of digital consent between 13 and 16, India treats anyone under 18 as a child who needs verifiable parental consent.
She cited the US case of Everalbum, a photo app that used customers’ images to train facial recognition models without proper consent. The company was ultimately ordered to delete not just the data but the models built on it.
“Your training data carries rights, the rights of privacy, the rights of IP,” Bajaj said.
Accountability cannot be outsourced either. Under the DPDP framework, responsibility stays with the data fiduciary, and breaches must be reported to the Data Protection Board within 72 hours. Platforms acting as intermediaries face even tighter timelines and must act on deepfakes and other misused AI content within hours.
Bajaj urged founders to map their personal data, disclose what goes into model training, name every vendor in their user notices, and take specific consent. Done right, she said, privacy by design protects a company’s valuation and helps India build IP for the world.
“You build a company for money, but you build for value in the end,” she concluded.

articles.title: La dernière grille de Free TV ne passe pas, des chaînes thématiques déplorent une plongée des audiences
articles.text:
L'ACCES, qui représente les chaînes du câble et du satellite, a saisi l'ARCOM au sujet de la nouvelle numérotation des chaînes de Free. Elle reproche à l'opérateur d’avoir mis en avant les chaînes FAST, au détriment de leur audience.
La nouvelle numérotation des chaînes de Free TV, en place depuis le 25 août, ne passe toujours pas auprès de certains éditeurs. L'ACCES qui fédère les chaînes du câble et du satellite, vient de saisir le régulateur de l'audiovisuel et du numérique, l'ARCOM, en brandissant des chiffres de Médiamétrie. L'association des chaînes conventionnées éditrices de services explique que les canaux qui ont reculé dans la grille auraient perdu en moyenne plus d'un cinquième de leur couverture auprès des abonnés Free. Moins visibles, elles disposeraient aussi de moins de moyens pour financer leurs programmes, prévient-elle, comme l'a rapporté le média spécialisé Écran total mardi 20 octobre.
Free TV a rangé ses chaînes… mais dérangé leurs éditeurs, qui demandent des comptes
Le 25 août, près de 700 chaînes ont changé de numéro sur les Freebox et dans l’application Free TV. Free les range désormais par thème, et chaque thème démarre à une centaine ronde, facile à retenir. Il y a le cinéma et les séries au canal 100, le sport au 200, la jeunesse au 300, l’info au 600, les chaînes locales et régionales au 900, et les chaînes étrangères au-delà du 1000. Les chaînes gratuites de la TNT, elles, gardent leurs numéros habituels, TF1 en tête sur le 1. Certaines chaînes payantes, dites premium, apparaissent même deux fois, à leur nouvelle place thématique et dans un raccourci en début de liste, entre les canaux 32 et 56. beIN SPORTS 1 est par exemple accessible à la fois sur le 36 et sur le 245. Des bandeaux affichés à l’écran annonçaient le changement depuis le 11 août.
On comprend l'idée. Chaque famille de chaînes a son quartier, avec une chaîne mosaïque pour en faire le tour d'un coup d'œil, et aucune chaîne n'a disparu. Mais l'ACCES retient autre chose. Free a placé en tête plusieurs univers de chaînes FAST (pour Free Ad-supported Streaming Television), qui sont des chaînes gratuites diffusées en streaming et financées par la publicité, ainsi que d'autres chaînes 100 % numériques. Pour l'association, cette organisation modifie très concrètement les conditions d'accès du public aux chaînes conventionnées.
Pour mesurer ce que ce grand déménagement coûte vraiment à ses chaînes, l’ACCES s’est tournée vers Médiamétrie, l’institut de référence de la mesure d’audience en France. Selon les premiers retours, les chaînes dont le numéro a reculé ont perdu en moyenne 22 % de couverture mensuelle chez les abonnés Free de 4 ans et plus, par rapport à septembre 2025. Ce chiffre est à manier avec prudence, car avancé par une partie prenante, et la comparaison remonte à plus d'un an, période pendant laquelle d'autres facteurs ont pu peser.
L’ACCES demande à l’ARCOM de passer la grille de Free au crible
Pour défendre ses membres, l’ACCES affirme que ses chaînes ne jouent pas avec les mêmes règles que les chaînes FAST. Car les chaînes conventionnées, liées à l'ARCOM par une convention, doivent respecter des règles éditoriales et de protection des publics. Selon leur régime, elles sont aussi tenues de diffuser des œuvres françaises et européennes et de participer au financement de la création. Les FAST, souligne l'association, n'ont pas ces contraintes. Cette dernière réclame donc que la mise en avant dans la grille tienne compte des obligations effectives de chaque service et de sa contribution réelle à la création.
L'association déplore aussi le timing. Les chaînes thématiques subissent déjà l'éclatement des usages et la pression sur leurs revenus. Moins exposées, elles risquent de s'affaiblir davantage et de réduire les moyens qu'elles consacrent aux programmes. L'ACCES rappelle enfin que, depuis quarante ans, les chaînes payantes ont rendu attractives les offres du câble, du satellite puis des fournisseurs d'accès à Internet, en aidant à recruter et fidéliser les abonnés. Les opérateurs qui ont grandi avec ces « partenaires historiques » doivent, selon elle, préserver leur visibilité.
L'ACCES demande désormais à l'ARCOM d'examiner rapidement le plan de services de Free. Elle appelle aussi l'opérateur à ouvrir le dialogue avec les éditeurs, pour corriger les positions qu'elle estime insuffisamment justifiées et rendre aux chaînes de découverte et de documentaire une place facilement identifiable. On attend de voir quelle suite le régulateur et l'opérateur, qui misait sur un zapping simplifié, donneront à cette demande.

articles.title: Alors que l'Europe rêve d'IA souveraine, l'Allemagne signe avec un géant américain
articles.text:
Début octobre, le moteur de recherche allemand Ecosia claquait la porte de Mistral après cinq mois de partenariat, troquant le champion français de l’IA contre des modèles ouverts, chinois pour partie. Le 19 octobre, le chancelier Friedrich Merz scellait sur scène, à Berlin, une coopération stratégique avec l’américain Nvidia. En deux semaines, le récit d’une IA européenne autosuffisante a sérieusement vacillé.
À Berlin, des puces, des start-up et une déclaration d’intention
L’annonce a ouvert le sommet Invest in Germany, qui réunit depuis lundi près de 200 dirigeants d’entreprises dans la capitale allemande. Aux côtés de Jensen Huang, le patron de Nvidia, Friedrich Merz a officialisé une coopération entre son gouvernement, le fabricant de puces et un groupe d’industriels. Une déclaration d’intention porterait notamment sur des modèles d’IA taillés pour l’industrie. Le rendez-vous se poursuit ce mardi, avec la moitié du cabinet allemand autour du chancelier.
Nvidia a aussi annoncé des prises de participation dans quatre start-up allemandes : Agile Robots dans la robotique, Avelios Medical dans la santé, Mirelo dans les médias et Reflex Aerospace dans le spatial. Les montants restent confidentiels. Le tout pioche dans une enveloppe de près de 10 milliards de dollars promise par le groupe aux entreprises, universités et laboratoires européens.
« Ouvrez vos portes à l’IA pour qu’elle exploite vos données », a lancé le chancelier aux entreprises du pays, PME en tête, en citant l’industrie manufacturière, la construction mécanique et l’automobile. Berlin mettrait de son côté plusieurs centaines de millions d’euros sur la table, notamment pour louer de la puissance de calcul chez Deutsche Telekom. Le dispositif s’articulerait autour de SOOFI, le programme allemand de modèles ouverts dits souverains, avec les robots et les véhicules autonomes en ligne de mire. Huang a salué en retour l’expertise industrielle et mathématique du pays, promettant une IA qui renforcera ces capacités au lieu de les remplacer.
Une souveraineté à géométrie variable
Christian Kroll, le fondateur d’Ecosia, juge les modèles de Mistral en retard d’environ un an sur la concurrence et pointe des serveurs régulièrement saturés. Il reproche aussi à la start-up son électricité d’origine nucléaire, incompatible selon lui avec les engagements climatiques de son moteur, et la présence d’investisseurs non européens à son capital. Parmi eux figure… Nvidia.
Pour le remplacer, le moteur de recherche s’est tourné vers des modèles ouverts, dont les chinois Qwen, GLM et Kimi, à l’heure où Mistral dévoilait son nouveau grand modèle, Large 4. L’entreprise allemande invoque la qualité et les coûts, quitte à écorner au passage son propre discours sur l’indépendance européenne.
En novembre 2025, Deutsche Telekom et Nvidia lançaient déjà à Munich un centre de calcul à 1 milliard d’euros, fort de 10 000 GPU. Google a pour sa part promis 5,5 milliards d’euros d’investissements en Allemagne d’ici 2029. Jensen Huang enfoncera le clou dès mercredi, lors de sa conférence GTC organisée cette semaine dans la capitale allemande.

articles.title: A judge lets Denuvo subpoena Discord, Reddit, and Steam to unmask the cracker Voices38
articles.text:
Connecting the dots: Denuvo has spent the past few weeks trying to uncover Voices38's true identity. The mysterious cracker has been wreaking havoc on the company's notorious DRM and anti-tamper technology, and Denuvo is now turning to lawyers in a bid to unmask the skilled coder.
Denuvo's first attempt to uncover Voices38's real identity was unsuccessful because the company tried to obtain too much data at once. Now, a California federal judge has granted the Irdeto-owned DRM maker's revised subpoena requests. Several internet companies will soon have to respond to Denuvo's lawyers, but Voices38 could still remain a John Doe in the end.
Denuvo's latest legal assault began earlier this month, when the company asked a judge to help identify the unnamed cracker operating under the "Voices38" moniker. The request was part of Denuvo's lawsuit against Voices38, which centers on the cracker's alleged violations of the DMCA's anti-circumvention provisions.
Denuvo initially asked the judge to approve 46 separate subpoena requests targeting Discord, Valve, Reddit, and other internet companies. The subpoenas sought potential names and email addresses, along with additional data related to payments and financial transactions, login logs, comment histories, and more.
According to Judge Haywood S. Gilliam Jr., Denuvo's requests went too far. Although the company was seeking to uncover Voices38's identity, the subpoenas extended well beyond the information needed to identify the individual or individuals involved. Given the potentially significant privacy implications, the judge decided to narrow the scope of the requests.
Denuvo was given two options: revise its subpoenas or provide detailed explanations justifying each request. The DRM maker chose the former, reducing the number of requests from 46 to nine. Judge Gilliam has now approved the revised requests, allowing Denuvo to serve subpoenas on Discord, Valve, and Reddit.
Specifically, the company is seeking identifying information associated with the "voices38" Discord account, Reddit user voices38, and seven different Steam profiles. So far, Denuvo has been able to target only an online pseudonym. The subpoenas could help the company obtain further information about Voices38's identity, including names, government-issued identification documents, email addresses, phone numbers, and physical addresses.
Despite being targeted by a company known for pursuing DRM crackers, Voices38 recently indicated that things would be fine regardless. The coder released their latest crack just a couple of days ago. However, over the past few hours, Voices38 has reportedly deleted their official Reddit account, one of the main channels the cracker used to share releases and updates.
Could Voices38 become the next Voksi, the cracker whom Denuvo successfully forced into early retirement several years ago? The developer was instrumental in removing Irdeto's anti-tamper technology from recent games, including Doom: The Dark Ages and Resident Evil Requiem.

articles.title: Samsung y SK hynix tienen un problema en China: necesitan modernizar sus fábricas chinas para frenar a YMTC
articles.text:
YMTC (Yangtze Memory Technologies) está creciendo como la espuma en China. Este fabricante de chips NAND ha alcanzado una cuota de mercado del 38,5% en su país de origen durante el segundo trimestre de 2026, según la consultora Omdia. Durante 2025 su cuota fue aproximadamente del 28%, lo que refleja una tendencia al alza muy marcada. Sin embargo, Samsung y SK hynix, las compañías que lideran el mercado mundial de los semiconductores NAND Flash, se están desangrando en China.
Durante el segundo trimestre de este año Samsung ha retrocedido a una cuota del 33,5% en China. Y SK hynix al 17%. YMTC ya vende más chips NAND Flash en China que Samsung y SK hynix. Y este mercado es demasiado grande y demasiado importante para pasar esta tendencia por alto. De hecho, estas dos compañías surcoreanas están planeando modernizar sus fábricas chinas para competir con YMTC, que ya las ha alcanzado desde un punto de vista estrictamente tecnológico.
Este último fabricante de semiconductores produce sobre todo chips NAND de 160 y 232 capas, pero también fabrica una pequeña cantidad de chips de 294 capas. Y planea superar las 300 capas a medio plazo. Incrementar el número de capas de estos semiconductores es importante porque permite almacenar más información en el mismo espacio, así como reducir el coste por bit. Las plantas que tienen Samsung y SK hynix en China, sin embargo, ya no tienen la capacidad de competir de tú a tú con las de YMTC.
UN VISTAZO A...
Samsung y SK hynix tienen un problema con las sanciones de EEUU
La planta que tiene Samsung en Xi'an, en el noroeste de China, es la responsable de aproximadamente el 40% de su capacidad de fabricación mundial de chips NAND. Actualmente está produciendo circuitos integrados de unas 200 capas, y los directivos de Samsung planean modernizar estas instalaciones para conseguir que sean capaces de fabricar chips NAND V9 de 286 capas. Además, según Reuters, este proyecto de modernización aspira a incrementar la capacidad de fabricación hasta las 40.000 obleas mensuales en diciembre de 2027.
Para Samsung y SK hynix la única forma de competir con YMTC en China y frenar su avance en el mercado mundial pasa por modernizar las fábricas que tienen en este país
SK hynix se encuentra en una posición similar a Samsung en China. Su fábrica de Dalian, en el noreste de este país, produce circuitos integrados NAND de 192 capas, y aspira a mejorar estas instalaciones para iniciar la fabricación de chips de 240 capas, y, más adelante, de más de 300 capas. Para Samsung y SK hynix la única forma de competir con YMTC en China y frenar su avance en el mercado mundial pasa por modernizar las fábricas que tienen en este país. Y no lo tienen fácil.
Las restricciones que el Gobierno de EEUU ha impuesto a la exportación de equipos avanzados para fabricar semiconductores a China son un obstáculo para Samsung y SK hynix. Para incrementar el número de capas de sus chips NAND Flash necesitan forzosamente instalar máquinas de litografía más avanzadas en sus plantas de Xi'an y Dalian, así como equipos de procesamiento de obleas y grabado de vanguardia. Y las restricciones estadounidenses dificultan la introducción de estas máquinas en China y obligan a ambas compañías a obtener las licencias necesarias.
Este escenario tan complejo plantea una paradoja muy interesante. EEUU quiere ralentizar el desarrollo de la industria china de los semiconductores, y por este motivo está impidiendo que los equipos más avanzados que utilizan patentes estadounidenses lleguen a China. Además, quiere contener el avance de YMTC en el mercado mundial, pero, y aquí llega la paradoja, sus sanciones a China impiden a Samsung y SK hynix modernizar sus plantas en este último país. Y si no equipan adecuadamente sus fábricas de Xi'an y Dalian, seguirán perdiendo competitividad frente a una YMTC que cada día es más fuerte. Veremos cuál es el desenlace final de este conflicto.

articles.title: Une première : coincé 491 jours au milieu des mines, ce soldat ukrainien a été sauvé par un drone géant
articles.text:
Une première : coincé 491 jours au milieu des mines, ce soldat ukrainien a été sauvé par un drone géant
Les jambes déchiquetées, terré seul au milieu des mines pendant 491 jours, Kostiantyn Vlasenko semblait condamné. Ni fantassins ni robots terrestres ne pouvaient l'atteindre. Pour l'arracher à ce piège, l'armée ukrainienne a tenté un pari qu'elle présente comme une première mondiale : le suspendre sous un hexacoptère lourd et le faire voler au-dessus des lignes russes.
Le 19 octobre, la 92e brigade d'assaut ukrainienne a publié sur Telegram des images saisissantes : un fantassin amputé, harnaché sous un drone à six rotors, survole le front de Koupiansk, dans la région de Kharkiv.
Menée le 4 octobre avec la 30e brigade mécanisée et le fabricant Gurzuf Defence, l'opération a permis de rapatrier Kostiantyn "Magura" Vlasenko, originaire de Kryvyï Rih. Ce soldat tenait la rive gauche de l'Oskil depuis juin 2025. Le 14 février 2026, une munition larguée par un drone russe lui a broyé les deux jambes, au point qu'il a dû s'amputer lui-même. Ravitaillé par les airs tous les quatre ou cinq jours, il a tenu jusqu'au bout.
🔴 HISTORIC FIRST: Ukrainian forces completed the first-ever aerial evacuation of an injured soldier from the frontline using a drone.
Soldiers from the 92nd Assault Brigade and 30th Mechanized Brigade used a heavy Gurzuf Defence hexacopter to rescue the wounded infantryman from… pic.twitter.com/sgKIyeexos
— UNITED24 Media (@United24media) October 19, 2026
Heavy Shot Ayudag-6 : Starlink, treuil et leurres pour un vol à haut risque
D'après le média ukrainien Oboronka, qui a recueilli les témoignages des protagonistes, la mission a demandé six mois de préparation. La veille, un drone a largué au blessé un harnais d'alpinisme et un téléphone contenant un tutoriel vidéo. Au petit matin, l'Ayudag-6, capable d'emporter jusqu'à 130 kg, est venu le cueillir au bout de son treuil.
Des bombardiers lourds Vampire ont saturé les secteurs voisins pour détourner l'attention russe, et l'un d'eux a été abattu. Piloté via Starlink, l'appareil volait escorté d'un intercepteur Lucky Strike prêt à percuter tout engin hostile.
	
Je savais qu'il y avait un homme en dessous : je voulais l'amener le plus vite et le plus sûrement possible.
Sur cet itinéraire de 16 km, l'hexacoptère a dû faire escale pour changer de batteries avant de rejoindre le blessé, puis l'a déposé à ce point relais. Gurzuf Defence chiffre la mission complète à 62 km, bouclée en 1 h 14 min 36 s. Un robot terrestre a ensuite convoyé le soldat sur 8 km jusqu'à une zone sûre.
Évacuation des blessés par drone : un dernier recours, prévient le fabricant
Le rescapé est désormais hors de danger et a été proposé au titre de Héros de l'Ukraine. Gurzuf Defence refuse pourtant d'y voir le début d'une routine. Son cofondateur, Pavlo Feldblium, juge les risques trop élevés pour un blessé suspendu dans les airs. Selon lui, les promesses de milliers de missions "renvoient pour l'instant davantage à Ray Bradbury ou à Stanisław Lem".
	
La voie aérienne reste le dernier recours, quand il ne reste plus aucune autre chance de sauver un homme.
D'autres industriels avancent malgré tout sur ce terrain. Quelques jours plus tôt, SkyFall envoyait au front le StarGate, premier drone ukrainien conçu spécifiquement pour l'évacuation des blessés, capable de porter 150 kg sur 15 km.

articles.title: Xbox ya despidió a 1.868 empleados y prepara tres rondas más de recortes hasta enero de 2027
articles.text:
Xbox despedirá a más empleados este mes, en noviembre próximo y en enero de 2027, según confirmó su CEO, Asha Sharma, en una entrevista con la revista Fortune. La división de Microsoft ya recortó 1.868 puestos de los 3.200 que planea eliminar en un año.
Sharma asumió el cargo en febrero pasado, designada por el CEO de Microsoft, Satya Nadella, para revertir el declive de la marca de videojuegos tras la salida del histórico ejecutivo, Phil Spencer. Desde entonces lidera lo que varios empleados describen como la reestructuración más profunda en la historia de Xbox.
Los próximos recortes se suman a los que ya comenzaron cinco meses después de la llegada de la nueva CEO, cuando la compañía anunció el plan de eliminar el 20% de su plantilla. Entre los despedidos hay empleados que trabajaban en Xbox desde hace décadas, lo que implica, según fuentes citadas por Fortune, la pérdida de conocimiento acumulado dentro de la empresa.
La forma en que se ejecutaron los recortes, repartidos en varias tandas a lo largo de un año, generó además desgaste interno: parte del personal se siente bajo una amenaza constante sobre si su puesto será el próximo en desaparecer.
“No estamos aquí para hacer lo mínimo necesario y tener solo un buen negocio”, dijo Sharma a Fortune. “Estamos acá para ser la empresa de entretenimiento número uno.”
Xobx, un negocio de USD 21.000 millones con márgenes bajos
Xbox es un negocio de USD 21.000 millones que combina hardware, estudios creativos y miles de títulos de videojuegos. Pese a esa escala, su margen de ganancias ronda el 3%, entre un tercio y un décimo del nivel que manejan sus competidores.
Las consolas de la generación actual de Xbox vendieron apenas un poco más de un tercio de las unidades que vendió la PlayStation 5, de Sony, de acuerdo con estimaciones de terceros citadas por Fortune. El costo de los componentes de hardware también subió por la escasez de chips de memoria.
La compra de Activision Blizzard por USD 69.000 millones en 2023 convirtió a Xbox en el tercer negocio de Microsoft por ingresos, pero también, complicó su operación. Matt Booty, director de contenidos de Xbox, reconoció que la empresa “no conectó los puntos” entre sus distintas apuestas en los últimos cinco años.
La sospecha de una venta o escisión de Xbox
La magnitud de los recortes alimentó versiones, entre empleados actuales y exempleados, de que Microsoft prepara a Xbox para una eventual venta, escisión o conversión en una subsidiaria independiente.
Judson Althoff, a cargo del área comercial de Microsoft, negó esa posibilidad: “Asha es una de las mejores líderes que tenemos en toda la compañía. No la hubiéramos puesto al frente de un negocio que pensamos vender”, afirmó, aunque reconoció que “habrá mucha especulación” sobre el futuro de la división.
Joost van Dreunen, profesor de la Universidad de Nueva York especializado en videojuegos, planteó un escenario distinto: a medida que Microsoft destina más dinero a infraestructura de inteligencia artificial, podría verse obligado a desprenderse de negocios que no generan esos retornos.
“Si ese es el futuro que se viene, Xbox se volvería cada vez más atractivo para una venta que financie el futuro de la IA en la empresa”, dijo el profesor.
Una consola nueva de Xbox con Microsoft para 2028
Sharma impulsa además un rediseño de Game Pass con planes a la carta y prepara el lanzamiento de un dispositivo portátil de nueva generación para fines de 2027, además de una consola sucesora para fines de 2028. El proyecto interno, conocido como Helix, tiene un costo proyectado de entre USD 1.200 y USD 1.800 para el consumidor, según estimaciones preliminares de la compañía.
Xbox tiene hoy unos 100 millones de usuarios activos por día, lejos de la meta de mil millones que fijó Sharma para la plataforma. El uso de consolas repuntó interanualmente tras la caída del año anterior, y la ejecutiva dijo que espera que las mejoras financieras se reflejen a partir del año fiscal 2027 de Microsoft.
El próximo punto de control será el informe trimestral de resultados de Microsoft, previsto para este mes, que mostrará si la reestructuración empieza a traducirse en números. Sharma, por su parte, dijo que no tiene un plazo definido para su gestión al frente de la marca.

articles.title: Como ativar e cadastrar um chip da Vivo (físico ou eSIM) • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Como ativar e cadastrar um chip da Vivo (físico ou eSIM)
O processo de registro e ativação dos chips da Vivo é feito totalmente digital por meio do portal da operadora ou configurações do sistema do smartphone
Ativar e cadastrar o chip da Vivo é um processo prático que pode ser feito diretamente pelo celular, tanto usando o chip físico quanto o virtual (eSIM). Para o modelo tradicional, basta inserir o cartão no aparelho, aguardar o recebimento do SMS e acessar a página de registro da operadora.
Quem prefere a praticidade do eSIM conta com uma ativação totalmente digital, sem a necessidade dos cartões plásticos. Para isso, basta escanear o QR code fornecido pela Vivo nas configurações do Android ou iPhone para baixar o perfil digital e liberar a linha.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog mostra o passo a passo para cadastrar um SIM card e um eSIM da Vivo.
Antes de começar: o que você precisa para cadastrar o chip da Vivo
Ativar um chip da Vivo é um processo simples que exige apenas alguns documentos e preparativos básicos no aparelho. Veja o que você precisa ter em mãos para concluir o cadastro com sucesso, seja com um chip físico ou um eSIM:
- CPF e documento oficial: número do CPF do titular da linha e documento com foto (RG ou CNH) para a validação de identidade;
- Dados pessoais completos: data de nascimento, endereço residencial com CEP e o código de área (DDD) desejado para o número;
- Celular desbloqueado: smartphone sem restrições de operadoras e conectado a uma rede Wi-Fi estável, requisito importante ao configurar o eSIM junto a compatibilidade da tecnologia do chip virtual;
- Chip SIM Vivo ou QR Code: o chip físico inserido na gaveta do aparelho ou o código de ativação fornecido pela operadora para baixar o perfil digital.
Como cadastrar o chip físico da Vivo
O processo para cadastrar o chip da Vivo Pré-Pago no celular é simples e totalmente digital. Siga o passo a passo para ativar a linha usando o chip físico em um smartphone desbloqueado.
Atenção!
A ativação dos chips dos planos Vivo Controle ou Vivo Pós é feita de forma diferente. Basta inserir o SIM card no aparelho e, em seguida, fazer uma chamada para qualquer pessoa para ativar a linha.
1. Insira o chip físico da Vivo no celular
Com o smartphone desligado, insira o SIM card na gaveta do dispositivo. Em seguida, ligue o aparelho para ele reconhecer o chip e estabelecer conexão inicial com a rede móvel.
2. Selecione o DDD da sua região
Após o smartphone detectar o chip, surgirá uma notificação na tela para a escolha do DDD. Selecione o código de área da sua região para definir o prefixo do número e confirme a seleção para avançar.
3. Aguarde o SMS com o número Vivo e link de cadastro
A operadora enviará uma mensagem de texto com seu novo número e, em seguida, outra mensagem trará um link de cadastro da linha Vivo Pré. Caso o SMS não chegue, abra o navegador do celular e acesse o site cadastro.vivo.com.br.
Importante: a rede móvel precisa estar ativada ou o dispositivo conectado a uma rede Wi-Fi para avançar para o próximo passo.
4. Preencha os dados pessoais do cadastro Vivo
Ao acessar o portal de registro e ativação do chip Vivo, preencha os dados pessoais solicitados, como o número do CPF.
5. Valide sua identidade
Siga as orientações da tela para tirar uma selfie nítida e aguarde a confirmação de identidade.
6. Envie a foto de um documento de identidade
Na próxima etapa, toque em “Continuar” e tire uma foto do seu documento oficial com foto ou envie uma imagem salva na galeria do dispositivo.
7. Conclua o cadastro e ativação do chip
Após a checagem automática dos documentos enviados, confirme a finalização do processo no sistema. Em poucos instantes, o plano estará liberado para realizar chamadas e navegar na internet.
Como cadastrar um eSIM da Vivo no celular Android
Para cadastrar um eSIM da Vivo em um smartphone Android, você precisa de um aparelho compatível com a tecnologia, conexão Wi-Fi e o QR Code gerado pela operadora. Veja o passo a passo para ativar o chip virtual:
- Abra o menu de Configurações do seu aparelho Android.
- Toque em “Conexões” ou “Rede e Internet”, dependendo do modelo do aparelho.
- Entre na opção “Gerenciamento de chip” ou “Rede móvel” para gerenciar os perfis digitais.
- Toque na função “Adicionar eSIM” ou “Baixar novo chip” para iniciar o cadastro.
- Escolha a opção para escanear o código QR fornecido pela operadora.
- Aponte a câmera do celular para o QR Code da Vivo.
- Toque em “Adicionar” ou “Configurar” para autorizar o download das credenciais da linha.
- Mantenha o Wi-Fi conectado durante o download do perfil até o sistema confirmar o perfil da Vivo como ativo.
Como cadastrar um eSIM da Vivo no iPhone
Configurar o eSIM da Vivo no seu iPhone apenas precisa de um aparelho compatível com o chip virtual, conexão Wi-Fi e o QR Code da operadora em mãos. Confira o caminho para cadastrar o chip da Vivo:
- Abra o menu “Ajustes” do iPhone.
- Toque na aba “Celular” e selecione “Adicionar eSIM” ou “Configurar Celular”.
- Escolha o método “Usar QR Code” para habilitar o leitor da câmera.
- Aponte a câmera do iPhone para o código QR fornecido pela operadora.
- Quando surgir o aviso “Plano Celular Detectado” ou “Ativar o eSIM”, toque em “Continuar”.
- Selecione “Adicionar Plano Celular” e digite o código de confirmação, caso a Vivo solicite.
- Aguarde a conclusão do download do perfil digital e defina o uso padrão da linha móvel.
Posso ativar o chip da Vivo por SMS?
Não é possível cadastrar o chip da Vivo por SMS diretamente, pois a mensagem de texto serve apenas como suporte na ativação. A operadora utiliza o canal para enviar o número da nova linha e o link para concluir o registro no site oficial.
Se o SMS não chegar, verifique se o SIM card está bem encaixado no smartphone e reinicie o aparelho. Caso o problema persista, ligue para a central de atendimento no número 1058 para obter suporte para ativar o chip Vivo.
É possível cadastrar um chip da Vivo pelo WhatsApp?
Sim, dá para iniciar o cadastro Vivo no WhatsApp oficial pelo número (11) 99915-1515 para receber suporte direto da operadora. O assistente de IA facilita as orientações iniciais, sendo ideal para quem usa eSIM e precisa cadastrar o chip da Vivo com praticidade.
Para sua segurança, confirme se a conta possui selo de verificação antes de solicitar o QR Code de ativação. Nunca compartilhe dados pessoais sensíveis, como o seu CPF ou códigos de confirmação, com números não oficiais.
Problemas comuns durante a ativação do chip da Vivo
Alguns imprevistos de rede ou de hardware podem ocorrer ao cadastrar um número Vivo. Confira os problemas mais frequentes durante a ativação do chip físico ou do eSIM e como resolvê-los:
- Falta de sinal ou chip não reconhecido: reinsira o cartão SIM na gaveta do smartphone e confirme se o Modo Avião está desativado;
- Bloqueio de segurança por PIN/PUK: digite a senha PIN solicitada na tela. Se errar três vezes, consulte o código PUK impresso no cartão de suporte original do chip para evitar a perda definitiva do acesso;
- Atraso no recebimento do SMS: reinicie o telefone para forçar a reconexão com a rede de telefonia. Caso a mensagem com link de cadastro não chegue, envie a palavra “NUMERO” via SMS para 8300;
- Falha ao ler o QR Code do eSIM: verifique se o dispositivo está conectado a uma rede Wi-Fi estável durante o escaneamento e solicite um novo código de perfil digital se o anterior tiver expirado;
- Divergência de dados cadastrais: confira se o CPF, o nome e a data de nascimento informados conferem exatamente com os registros oficiais do titular da linha para evitar recusas automáticas do sistema.
Como identificar um problema no chip
Identificar falhas no seu SIM card exige testes práticos para isolar a origem do problema de sinal. Conheça os testes recomendados para verificar o estado do seu chip físico com rapidez:
- Limpeza e reinicialização: desligue o aparelho, remova o cartão e limpe os contatos metálicos com um pano seco. Reinicie o celular ou alterne o modo avião para forçar uma nova varredura de rede;
- Teste cruzado de aparelhos: insira o seu chip físico em outro smartphone compatível. Se o final normalizar, a falha está no leitor do seu telefone; caso o erro persista, o problema é no próprio SIM card;
- Teste de outro SIM ativo: coloque um chip diferente e ativo no seu dispositivo. Se a conexão móvel for estabelecida imediatamente, o SIM card anterior precisa ser substituído na operadora;
- Verificação de rede e pendências: confirme nas configurações se a linha móvel está habilitada. Cheque também se há bloqueios de segurança por PIN/PUK ou irregularidades no cadastro Vivo.
O que fazer se eu digitar alguma informação errada durante o cadastro?
Errar os dados durante o cadastro Vivo pode impedir a validação da identidade e causar o bloqueio preventivo da linha. Se o formulário já foi enviado, é fundamental corrigir as informações imediatamente pelo aplicativo Meu Vivo ou ligando para *8486.
Caso o erro envolva o CPF, o nome ou a data de nascimento, procure o atendimento da operadora ou uma loja física com um documento oficial com foto. Já para ajustes de endereço e meios de contato, utilize os canais digitais.
Por fim, é importante estar atento aos prazos: novos clientes de linhas pré-pagas podem validar os dados em até 5 dias nos três primeiros meses e em até 1 dia depois desse período para evitar o bloqueio do chip. A Vivo pode dar até 30 dias para regularizar a pendência cadastral antes de suspender ou bloquear o serviço.

articles.title: Salesforce to acquire marketing automation provider Braze for $5.66B - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Salesforce to acquire marketing automation provider Braze for $5.66B
Salesforce Inc. today announced plans to acquire Braze Inc. for $5.66 billion in cash.
The deal values the marketing software provider at $47.5 per share, which is about 58% higher than its last closing price. The steep premium is a reflection of Braze’s strong finances. The company’s revenue grew 26% year-over-year last quarter, to $227.2 million, while its adjusted operating income nearly quadrupled.
Enterprises often spread their customer records across multiple systems, which makes them difficult to analyze. Braze offers a cloud platform that can aggregate customer data into a centralized repository to ease processing. It collects the information using more than 190 pre-packaged connectors.
The platform organizes the data that it ingests into a standardized format using user-created scripts. From there, it groups customers with similar interests into segments. An electronics retailer, for example, could create a segment that includes all the shoppers who have bought smartphones via its website.
Braze enables companies to create personalized marketing campaigns for every customer segment. A set of built-in artificial intelligence features, BrazeAI, automatically creates campaign materials such as promotional emails. It customizes the content based on parameters such as product availability and a customer’s purchase history.
A feature called Agentic Standards enables users to create guardrails for AI-generated campaigns. For example, a marketing team could specify the maximum number of times an ad can be displayed to a shopper. From there, Braze automatically sorts out details such as the best time of day to send a promotional message.
Braze can distribute promotional messages via a company’s website, mobile app, SMS, WhatsApp and several other channels. A set of observability dashboards enables marketers to monitor the performance of each channel. Braze displays metrics such as the percentage of recipients who clicked a shopping link inside a sales email.
Salesforce will use the company’s technology to enhance its Marketing Cloud platform. Like Braze, the platform enables companies to combine customer data from different sources and use it to personalize their marketing campaigns. Built-in AI agents automate repetitive parts of the workflow. Salesforce says that the acquisition will improve Marketing Cloud’s ability to personalize campaigns across multiple outreach channels.
“Salesforce shares our commitment to marketers, and we’ll continue building as Braze and investing in the Braze community of customers and partners who built this company with us,” said Braze co-founder and Chief Executive Bill Magnuson. “Salesforce’s platform will help us innovate faster.”
Salesforce expects to close the acquisition in its 2028 fiscal year, which starts next February.

articles.title: PHP warns it plans to release 2 emergency patches imminently
articles.text:
Website admins, brace yourselves. Fixes for what are believed to be uncommonly severe vulnerabilities are scheduled to drop in a little more than 12 hours for PHP, a programming language that powers websites and Web applications everywhere.
PHP maintainers said Monday that they planned to release patches for two vulnerabilities, both with severity ratings of 9.2 out of a possible 10.
Waiting for PHP2Shell
“All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available,” the advisory stated. “We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild.”
The maintainers published the advisory following the leaking of purported details, which have yet to be confirmed. The report showed a video of an exploit tool dubbed PHP2Shell executing code on webservers running:
- WordPress 7.1.3
- MediaWiki 1.46.2
- phpBB 3.3.17
- Magento 2.4.9
- Joomla 6.2.0
- Laravel 13.36.0
- Laravel 8.83.29
- Symphony 8.1.9
- Drupal 11.4.10
- WHMCS 9.0.9
All of the above use PHP. A video depicting the tool has been reposted here.
Attempts to locate the unconfirmed report were unsuccessful, but security firm watchTowr said it claimed to affect every PHP version from PHP 5, released in 2004, onward. The security firm went on to say it has confirmed that the vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are real.

articles.title: DeepSeek AI tools banned from US government agency systems as rift with China grows
articles.text:
DeepSeek AI tools banned from US government agency systems as rift with China grows
Federal civilian agencies are no longer allowed to use DeepSeek and must remove it from their tech stack
- US civilian agencies have been ordered to stop using DeepSeek and remove it from government systems
- DHS cited data security, user tracking, and potential national security risks tied to the AI model
- The move expands broader US restrictions on Chinese technology across government infrastructure
The Donald Trump administration has banned Chinese Artificial Intelligence model DeepSeek from all civilian government agencies and ordered them to stop using it and remove it from its tech stack immediately.
Earlier this week, the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) issued a new notice, notifying government agencies of the change:
“The Department of Homeland Security is publishing notice of the Secretary of Homeland Security’s issuance of an order (1) excluding information technology products and services developed by Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd (DeepSeek), to include affiliated entities as defined in applicable regulations, from federal civilian agency procurements; and, (2) removing all DeepSeek and DeepSeek-affiliate products, and third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations, from civilian agency information technology.”
Multiple threat vectors
Apparently, this is not the first time the Trump administration made moves against Chinese AI tech. According to CNBC, the order was originally issued in late July this year, and applies to federal civilian agencies including the Treasury, State and Justice departments, but excluding the Department of Defense. The publication also said the US Congress restricted the use of DeepSeek in intelligence community systems late last year, and even earlier - in March - the US Commerce Department told its staff not to use DeepSeek. The Defense Information Systems Agency banned it in January 2025.
In the latest DHS order, it was said that DeepSeek’s models “present multiple threat vectors”. To use the tool, users need to provide all sorts of data - from personally identifiable information (PII) to other business or proprietary information, which the company can use to “track and digitally fingerprint users”. Furthermore, China’s laws allow the government to easily access and collect the data created and stored by private companies, meaning information on US citizens can easily fall into the government’s hands. That, in turn, “could produce actionable intelligence on US persons and/or government programs,” the DHS explains.
“The models themselves may contain malware or other security vulnerabilities,” it stressed. “Indeed, open-source security research has found that the DeepSeek iOS mobile application contains multiple critical vulnerabilities.”
When asked for a comment, China’s foreign ministry told the Reuters news agency it would safeguard the rights of its companies: “China consistently opposes the over-generalization of national security as well as the politicization of science, technology and trade issues,” Mao Ning, a ministry spokesperson, told the agency.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
China trade war
US President Donald Trump has openly talked against using Chinese technology and has banned multiple companies and solutions already. In his first term, he blacklisted hundreds of Chinese companies and affiliates, including telecommunications giants Huawei and ZTE, semiconductor manufacturer SMIC, drone maker DJI, and surveillance technology firms Hikvision and Dahua Technology. ZTE almost went bankrupt over it, and Huawei ended up building its own mobile phone operating system, Harmony OS, after losing access to Google and Android. At the time, the US was upgrading its mobile network to 5G, something Chinese companies were interested in working on. However, Trump argued that the Chinese government could force these companies into installing backdoors, which could allow China to eavesdrop on US communications.
In August 2026, during his second term, Trump signed an executive order declaring a national emergency and banned all foreign bulk-power systems from being imported, installed, or used in the country. He also said the government would analyze existing systems to isolate and remove any foreign-built hardware or software. The same ban was issued during his first term but was revoked by the Biden administration.
Later this month, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) will vote to prevent all Chinese labs from testing hardware used in the US, Reuters reported. Last year, four in five (82%) of all US electronics were tested in China.

articles.title: SpaceX and Tesla boards form special committees to review merger | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The boards of SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees to review a possible merger. The special committees, which consist of independent directors, were created at the request of shareholders, according to Elon Musk, CEO and the largest individual shareholder of both companies.
“Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees, so it’s this sort of a … It’s an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking, and I can’t be in the conversation,” Musk said in response to a question during SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call.
Musk didn’t name the members of these special committees, only noting that they were independent directors. Tesla has seven independent board members under Nasdaq’s listing standards, including board chair Robyn Denholm; Ira Ehrenpreis, who is also a committee chair; former Tesla CTO JB Straubel; Joe Gebbia; Jack Hartung; James Murdoch; and Kathleen Wilson-Thompson, according to the company’s October 19 proxy filing.
Neither Musk nor his brother Kimbal Musk is independent. Denholm, Gebbia, Ehrenpreis, Hartung, Murdoch, and Wilson-Thompson sit on a variety of established committees overseeing audit, compensation, and corporate governance.
SpaceX lists six independent directors, including Ehrenpreis, who is also the chair of the company’s compensation and nominating committee. Randy Glein, Donald Harrison, Steve Jurvetson, Luke Nosek, and Roelof Botha are also considered independent directors.
Antonio Gracias, Musk, and SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell are also on the board, but not considered independent. Gracias, who once sat on Tesla’s board, founded and leads Valor Equity Partners, which has a 3.4% stake in SpaceX. Gracias’ firm also financed SpaceX’s AI hardware purchases through leaseback arrangements.
Musk said he supports the idea of the merger but cautioned that it is not a guaranteed outcome.
“I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla Motor is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” he said, adding that he thinks it would be a good idea. “At the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this.”
The special committees have not reached agreement on the terms of any transactions, he said.
The SpaceX IPO cemented Musk’s grip on the company — he has more than 50% voting power — which would make it easier to garner support for a merger from SpaceX shareholders. It is a much bigger hurdle over at Tesla, where the company would need a 50% vote from all shareholders, not just those who vote, Musk noted.
“I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity,” Musk said, adding there was a lot to be gaining from cooperating on developing AI software, robotics, SpaceX’s orbital AI data center project Starmind, and Terafab, the joint chip manufacturing project between Tesla and SpaceX.

articles.title: Axiomtek Launches MANO330 Compact Thin Mini-ITX Industrial Motherboard
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Axiomtek Launches MANO330 Compact Thin Mini-ITX Industrial Motherboard
Axiomtek, a world-renowned leader relentlessly devoted to the research, development, and manufacture of innovative, highly efficient, and reliable industrial computer products, proudly introduces the MANO330, a compact Thin Mini-ITX motherboard powered by the Intel Processor N97 or N150 and DDR5 memory. Designed for space-constrained systems that require flexible connectivity and expansion, the MANO330 combines multi-display capability, dual LAN connectivity, versatile M.2 expansion, and industrial I/O in a compact platform. With a wide 12-24 VDC power input, the MANO330 provides system developers with a flexible foundation for smart manufacturing and industrial automation, digital signage, smart retail, and POS applications.
Compact Performance for Space-Constrained Systems
The MANO330 combines a compact Thin Mini-ITX design with Intel Processor N97 or N150 and DDR5-4800 memory support. The N97 supports up to 32 GB of memory, while the N150 supports up to 16 GB. Measuring just 170 x 170 mm, the MANO330 provides the essential computing performance and I/O capabilities needed for embedded systems, helping developers build space-efficient solutions for a wide range of industrial and commercial applications.Rich Visuals and Reliable Network Connectivity
Designed for information-rich applications, the MANO330 supports multiple independent display outputs through HDMI, VGA, LVDS/eDP interface, and USB Type-C with DisplayPort support. This display flexibility allows system developers to configure multiple screens for applications such as digital signage, retail displays, and industrial monitoring. The board also integrates 2.5GbE and GbE LAN, providing reliable network connectivity for connected systems and industrial applications.
Flexible Expansion to Fit Different Applications
The MANO330 provides flexible expansion options for storage and wireless connectivity. Its M.2 Key M 2280 slot supports SATA/NVMe storage, while M.2 Key E 2230 supports wireless connectivity. The M.2 Key B 3042/3052 interface provides an additional expansion option and is paired with a Nano SIM slot for wireless applications. These options allow customers to configure storage and connectivity according to their application requirements, helping simplify system development and integration.
Built-In I/O for Easier System Integration
The MANO330 integrates commonly used industrial interfaces directly on the board, including RS-232, RS-422/485, USB, SATA, and GPIO, helping reduce the need for additional interface hardware. Two RS-232 ports support jumper-selectable RS-422 or RS-485, while four additional RS-232 ports provide further serial connectivity for industrial devices. Combined with the board's 12-24 VDC power input, these built-in interfaces provide system developers with greater flexibility and help simplify system integration.
Tina Tu, Product Manager at Axiomtek"Today's embedded systems need to balance compact design with flexibility for different application requirements. With versatile display, connectivity, expansion, and industrial I/O options, the MANO330 gives system developers greater freedom to configure and integrate solutions for a wide range of industrial and commercial applications"
Advanced Features of MANO330
- Intel Processor N97/N150
- DDR5-4800 SO-DIMM, up to 32 GB with N97 and 16 GB with N150
- Dual LAN ports
- M.2 Key B 3042/3052
- M.2 Key E 2230
- M.2 Key M 2280
The MANO330 is now available.
