articles.title: TP-Link proposes $1 billion US Wi-Fi router manufacturing alliance with Key Tronic — potential deal seeks to end ongoing saga blocking its Wi-Fi 8 products from American homes
articles.text:
TP-Link proposes $1 billion US Wi-Fi router manufacturing alliance with Key Tronic — potential deal seeks to end ongoing saga blocking its Wi-Fi 8 products from American homes
You scratch my back, I’ll scratch yours
TP-Link is fully determined to get in the good graces of the U.S. government to break free from a total ban on newly developed routers manufactured outside of the country. Although TP-Link is incorporated in the U.S. with a headquarters in Irvine, California, the company has been under pressure from the full weight of the U.S. government because of its historical Chinese roots. However, in an effort to appeal to the Trump administration’s zeal for creating jobs and touting American manufacturing, TP-Link this week announced that it has signed a letter of intent to assemble routers in the U.S. through a crucial partnership with Key Tronic.
How did we get here?
The ongoing saga started back in late 2024, when the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party requested that the Department of Commerce investigate TP-Link. At the time, the committee warned that “TP-Link products are also found on U.S. military bases, with the Army and Air Force Exchange and the Navy Exchange selling these devices to members of the military and their families,” and claimed TP-Link routers were sending user data back to China.
The select committee implored the Department of Commerce to use its broad powers to investigate TP-Link and take any necessary action to mitigate threats to national security. The campaign against TP-Link ramped up in mid-2025, with 17 members of Congress petitioning the Commerce Department to ban the sale of the company’s hardware in the U.S. due to alleged deep ties to the CCP. In late 2025, 23 U.S. House members and Senators again asked the Commerce Department to investigate TP-Link’s actions, including adding the company to the Covered List, investigating any threats to national security, and informing the public about potential risks associated with using the company’s devices.
The situation reached a boiling point in March 2026, when TP-Link and other router manufacturers were added to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Covered List, forbidding the sale of foreign-made routers in the U.S. that hadn’t already been approved. At the time, the FCC noted, “Recently, malicious state and non-state sponsored cyber attackers have increasingly leveraged the vulnerabilities in small and home office routers produced abroad to carry out direct attacks against American civilians in their homes. From disrupting network connectivity to enabling local networking espionage and intellectual property theft, foreign-produced routers present unacceptable risks to Americans.”
Since that time, several things have changed, with none of them being positive developments for TP-Link. Over the past six months, Amazon, Asus, and Netgear have all gained conditional approvals from the FCC to sell new wireless products in the U.S., while TP-Link has been stonewalled (conditional approvals are valid for 18 months from the date of issuance). Considering that TP-Link has been the world’s largest provider of Wi-Fi routers and associated devices for over a decade, losing access to the U.S. market for its new line of Wi-Fi 8 devices is a significant blow. This was readily apparent in late September when TP-Link opened preorders for its Archer 8 Ultra Wi-Fi 8 router. The company announced that the router would be available in the United Kingdom, Germany, and Australia. However, the U.S. was conspicuously absent from that list because of the ongoing ban.
Adding insult to injury, earlier this month, multiple states (including Florida, Montana, Iowa, and Nebraska) sued TP-Link Systems, alleging that the company has made false and misleading claims about the security capabilities of its products and continued ties to China.
“TP-Link’s conduct has placed Montana consumers at risk of harm by making their home and small-office networks vulnerable to exploitation and intrusion by foreign actors with a proven track record of nefarious conduct. That risk is ongoing: many consumers keep their routers for years, and many of the compromised TP-Link models in Montana homes do not support automatic firmware updates and no longer receive security support at all,” stated Montana Attorney General Austin Knudsen.
Knudsen further claimed that while TP-Link touts that it employs 300 people in the U.S., the bulk of its workforce (numbering over 11,000 employees) conducts development and manufacturing operations in China. “Further, TP-Link claims to manufacture its U.S.-market products in Vietnam, but less than one percent of the components by value are sourced in Vietnam, and the rest are imported from or through China,” Knudsen added.
“Iowans’ sensitive data and our national security is at risk because of TP-Link and their connection to the communist Chinese government,” stated Iowa Attorney General Bird. “TP-Link tells Iowans its routers are safe, our personal data is secure, and that they have no ties to China. They are not telling the truth. It’s time to hold China and China-backed companies accountable.”
TP-Link barks back
Up until this point, TP-Link has vehemently denied any ties to the Chinese government and has refuted similar allegations from one of its primary competitors, Netgear. However, on October 13, the company issued its sharpest rebuttal yet in a letter to the FCC. TP-Link touted its “America-first” strategy and chastised the state lawsuits brought earlier this month.
“A group of 21 state-level officials recently raised a scattershot barrage of baseless and previously debunked allegations relating to TP-Link’s confidential, non-public application,” TP-Link exclaimed. Rather than seeking to advance legitimate public policy objectives, the letter appears aimed primarily at encouraging federal officials to apply a heightened standard to TP-Link’s pending application that would be unattainable to TP-Link or any other router manufacturer in the world.”
TP-Link stated that its innovation in the router space earned its position as the market leader in the U.S., and that the constant barrage of legal fights and war of words is undermining fair competition and is an actual threat to national security and critical infrastructure given the broad proliferation of its products.
To that end, TP-Link reiterated that it has officially filed for conditional approval from the FCC, so that it can specifically sell two next-generation Wi-Fi 8 routers in the U.S. The company noted, “As the United States positions itself as a leader in wireless technology, a Conditional Approval would guarantee American consumers access to the same cutting-edge wireless equipment that will soon be available in other parts of the world."
TP-Link proposes $1 billion investment in the U.S.
With its back against the ropes, TP-Link is appealing to the U.S. government in the best way it knows how: with money and jobs. If there’s anything that the U.S. government likes, it’s investment in manufacturing on its own soil and high-paying jobs to bolster local economies. To help push the U.S. government along in approving a conditional approval to sell Wi-Fi 8 hardware, TP-Link has signed a letter of intent with Key Tronic to manufacture routers in the U.S. instead of importing them from Vietnam. More specifically, the routers would be assembled in Corinth, Mississippi.
“This LOI with Key Tronic demonstrates our firm commitment to expanding domestic advanced manufacturing, and establishing America as our base for delivering secure, reliable connectivity solutions to households and businesses around the world,” said TP-Link Systems Inc. CEO Jeffrey Chao. “By choosing to assemble cutting-edge products here at home, we are thrilled to support U.S. high-tech job growth and empower a new generation of American innovation and innovators.”
TP-Link hopes that the investment will cut through most of the red tape that is currently preventing it from selling its latest products stateside. However, it remains to be seen if these latest sweeteners will be enough to sway President Trump and the agencies under his purview. As the company notes, it was the first to deliver Wi-Fi 7 routers in the U.S., and it wants to continue that leadership position by offering the first Wi-Fi 8 routers. The hardware is ready to go, as evidenced by the opening of preorders; it’s just currently being held up by roadblocks at the federal level, along with added pressure from state governments.
Until that time, Wi-Fi 8 products like the Archer 8 Ultra and Deco 8 Ultra will remain off-limits to Americans, which have given TP-Link a reported 65 percent share of the U.S. consumer router market.
Brandon Hill is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware. He has written about PC and Mac tech since the late 1990s with bylines at AnandTech, DailyTech, and Hot Hardware. When he is not consuming copious amounts of tech news, he can be found enjoying the NC mountains or the beach with his wife and two sons.

articles.title: Next Xbox console could cost as much as US$1800 without subsidies
articles.text:
Yesterday, we wrote about the increasing likelihood that the PS6 will have an eye-watering price tag of at least US$1,000 (about C$1,400). Now, we’re learning that Microsoft’s rival console, the PC-like Project Helix, could cost well above that.
In a big new feature from Fortune focusing on recently appointed Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, we get a better idea of Xbox’s hardware plans for the next two years. Part of this reportedly includes a handheld device coming by the 2027 holiday season, as well as Project Helix the following year. Fortune also reports that a “major overhaul” of Xbox Game Pass is planned that would introduce a tiered system through which players choose features à la carte, including console-only games, cloud gaming and multiplayer.
But the biggest revelation from Fortune‘s piece is rumoured price for Helix, which the publication pegs at anywhere between US$1,200 and $1,800 (around C$1,650 to $2,500) unless Xbox subsidizes the cost. Naturally, this staggering price cost is the result of AI-driven component shortages brought about by the likes of Microsoft itself.
However, that is an obscene price range even if Microsoft does indeed eat some of the cost. It’s also unclear how much this handheld may cost. Interestingly, Fortune noted that its development recently sparked a “rekindling of an old turf battle between the Xbox and Windows teams.” In particular, Windows leaders wanted the upcoming handheld device to use a “trimmed-down” version of Windows Home, while Xbox was pushing its own software for peak performance. Tensions supposedly “ran high enough” that a senior Xbox exec threatened to scrap the handheld entirely, but ultimately, Xbox is now “largely controlling” the direction of the OS.
But all of these console and handheld rumblings honestly feel besides the point. Frankly, it begs the question, even if pricing was much lower, of why anyone would buy an Xbox device right now, anyway. Even before the so-called RAMmageddon, substantially fewer people have been buying Xbox consoles over the past several years, and nothing the company has done lately has exactly instilled much confidence.
Above all else, Microsoft has been gutting the Xbox brand through thousands of layoffs at the likes of Obsidian, Halo Studios, Zenimax Online, id Software and Vancouver-based The Coalition, as well numerous studio closures, divestitures and consolidations. It’s been doing these reductions in waves, too, which Fortune notes has naturally left staff “demoralized, feeling as if they are sitting under a year-long cloud, waiting to see if there their roles will be eliminated next.” Per the publication, Xbox is eyeing more layoffs this month, November and January, although it noted that these plans could change.
Among these layoffs, we’ve seen veterans who have been in the industry for decades on the likes of Doom being axed, causing Xbox to lose invaluable institutional knowledge. Other examples of the company’s callousness and short-sightedness include promoting Halo Studios’ cinematic director and laying him off in the same week, axing Gears of War: E-Day‘s story director only a few weeks before the game’s launch and letting go of one of the key driving forces behind backwards compatibility and Xbox Cloud Gaming.
Meanwhile, Sharma wants to focus on bigger franchises like Call of Duty, Fallout and Minecraft as part of a wildly ambitious goal of reaching one billion people daily. To be clear, that figure includes console, PC, mobile and adaptations like the Fallout TV series, and Xbox even formed a new division focused on this multimedia Hollywood approach. Nonetheless, getting rid of thousands of the people who made Xbox what it is certainly isn’t a good way to help reach such a lofty goal.
All of this has led to rampant speculation that Microsoft is simply “cleaning up” Xbox to make it more appealing to potential buyers. In particular, Fortune noted that several current and former staff members do believe that Xbox is being prepared “for an eventual sale, spin-off, outside investment or conversion into a subsidiary,” also citing a high-level internal presentation with Sharma exploring these very scenarios that The Information had previously reported on.
Naturally, Microsoft denies looking to offload Xbox, claiming it has a long-term vision for gaming. And speaking to Fortune, Judson Althoff, who leads Microsoft commercial business, said Xbox is valuable to the company’s wider operations because its low-latency demands stress-test Microsoft’s cloud, it helps maintain retail relationships with the likes of Walmart and it connects the company to creators through Minecraft.
Time will tell how this all pans out, but one thing’s for sure: Xbox is a mess right now.

articles.title: Jio Platforms IPO oversubscribed in less than two hours led by QIBs
articles.text:
Jio Platforms IPO oversubscribed in less than two hours led by QIBs
The qualified institutional investors showed strong interest for the IPO of Jio Platforms with subscription crossing 4x.
Jio Platforms’ initial public offering (IPO) was oversubscribed in the qualified institutional buyers (QIB) category within two hours of opening on Wednesday, signalling strong demand from institutional investors.
However, the issue remained undersubscribed in the non-institutional investors (NII) and retail investor categories. As of 12:50 pm, data from the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) showed that the QIB portion was subscribed 4.86 times, while the NII and retail portions were subscribed 0.61 times and 0.46 times, respectively.
The IPO opened on October 21 and will close on October 23. Jio Platforms aims to raise Rs 30,213 crore through the issue, which is priced in the range of Rs 1,065–1,119 per share.
This is one of the largest public issues in India exceeding that of Hyundai Motor India’s Rs 27,870 crore issue in 2024.
Jio Platforms is valued at around $108 billion at the upper band of the IPO price.
The issue is a fresh offering of up to 27 crore shares, and no offer-for-sale component implies that existing shareholders are not selling.
On Monday, the company allotted shares worth about Rs 8,110 crore to 212 anchor investors at Rs 1,119 apiece. Bids for the anchor allocation exceeded Rs 2.5 lakh crore, more than 30 times the amount available.
Jio Platforms is betting that its technology, artificial intelligence and cloud ambitions will drive growth beyond telecom, Managing Director Akash Ambani said on Tuesday, pitching the Reliance Industries unit as a technology company ahead of what is set to be India's biggest-ever initial public offering.
"There is no either-or at Jio: the network is our technology," Ambani said in an interview with PTI, highlighting the company's in-house 5G core, cloud-native radio access network and software platform serving 533.3 million customers.
“Connectivity was the first product we built on that platform. Digital services, AI and cloud are what we are layering on top of it now," he said.
The IPO comes as investors assess whether the country's largest telecom operator can convert its vast customer base into higher-margin revenue from digital services, enterprise technology and AI, as subscriber growth alone becomes a less powerful driver of expansion.
(With inputs from PTI)

articles.title: Nvidia wants AI factories built in real factories
articles.text:
Nvidia wants AI factories built in real factories
Nvidia wants new AI capacity to show up at the data center fully built. At its GTC Berlin conference on Wednesday, the company introduced DSX POD, a reference design for shipping containers that partners fill with Vera Rubin racks, networking, and liquid cooling before they leave the factory.
Installing and wiring up racks in a conventional data center can take months, Nvidia says. But a DSX POD can be ready to deliver tokens in as few as 14 days, as long as the site already has the necessary power, cooling, and network connections (which are, to be fair, often bottlenecks, too).
The idea here is for data center operators to get to value faster, because, as Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement, “An AI factory creates value when it starts producing tokens — not when construction is complete.”
What’s in the box
Each container holds seven Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, or 504 Rubin GPUs. Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, said in a press briefing ahead of the announcement that a single unit packs about 10 million components and weighs around 28 metric tons.
The containers also come with roughly 20 kilometers of copper cabling and 17 kilometers of scale-out networking preinstalled and tested. Once a container arrives, crews set it in place, connect it to its neighbors, and run the final burn-in tests, Buck said.
Water use
Buck also noted that Nvidia designed the system to use no water for cooling. Vera Rubin can run on coolant as warm as 45 degrees Celsius, Nvidia says, so dry coolers, which work pretty much like a car’s radiator, can do the work instead of the evaporative cooling towers that are still the standard for many data centers today.
In a separate DSX announcement, Nvidia explains that operators in some climates may still need chillers on the hottest days. For a 2-gigawatt deployment, the company estimates that dry cooling can save about 54 million liters of water a day compared with cooling towers.
Data centers in a box
This server-in-a-container may feel a bit familiar, and indeed, tech companies do love to use containers, even if it’s sometimes more of a publicity stunt than a solution to a real problem.
Back in 2006, Sun Microsystems unveiled Project Blackbox, a data center in a 20-foot container, for example. A decade later, then-AWS CEO Andy Jassy ended his re:Invent 2016 keynote by having an 18-wheeler drive Snowmobile, a 45-foot container that could haul 100 petabytes of data, onto the stage.
Microsoft and AWS have since built containerized data centers for disaster zones and military missions.
All of those, however, are different from what Nvidia is doing here. DSX PODs are basically prefab parts that can be slotted into a data center. Buck described them as the building block for new AI factories.
Armada, which already sells containerized edge data centers, is one of 17 partners building them, alongside Bull, Dell, HPE, Schneider Electric, and Vertiv.
Nvidia says partners will start delivering DSX POD systems worldwide in early 2027.

articles.title: TikTok accusé de mettre des enfants en danger et de faciliter le blanchiment d’argent
articles.text:
« Je me bats depuis des mois pour régler ça avec des gens qui ne trouvent pas les dégâts assez graves », écrivait une responsable de la sécurité de TikTok à un collègue. Avec d’autres salariés, elle a raconté sous serment comment la direction de l’application a laissé traîner leurs alertes sur l’exploitation sexuelle d’adolescents.
La radio publique américaine NPR a pu consulter ces témoignages, versés en mars 2026 au dossier d’une procédure fédérale où sont regroupées, depuis 2022, des centaines de plaintes contre TikTok, Meta, Google et Snap. Les plaignants accusent ces entreprises d’avoir conçu des plateformes nocives pour les mineurs et caché les risques qu’elles connaissaient. Aucun jury n’a encore examiné ces dépositions, et TikTok a évité plusieurs procès en signant des accords amiables, dont l’un avec l’Alabama, en septembre, contre 100 millions de dollars. Dans une déclaration envoyée après la publication de l’enquête, Nathaniel Brown, porte-parole de TikTok, a dénoncé des citations « triées sur le volet à la demande des avocats des plaignants ». Les salariés entendus ont surtout parlé de l’argent que TikTok tirait de lives où apparaissaient des mineurs, et de protections que les adolescents contournaient à l’insu de leurs parents.
Des cadeaux virtuels dont TikTok gardait une part
Les spectateurs de TikTok Live achètent des cadeaux virtuels qu’ils offrent aux personnes qui filment en direct. Ces dernières les échangent ensuite contre de l’argent, et TikTok garde une commission au passage. Reagen Maher, qui a occupé entre 2021 et 2024 des postes de responsable dans les équipes de sécurité et d’enquêtes de TikTok, a mené pendant des mois une « croisade » afin de faire remonter ses constats jusqu’à V Pappas, qui dirigeait alors les opérations. D’après elle, l’entreprise savait que des mineurs se déshabillaient sur Live avant qu’une enquête de presse ne le révèle en 2022. TikTok limitait depuis 2021 la diffusion en direct des 13-17 ans, mais ses enquêteurs internes ont trouvé, rien qu’en janvier 2022, des adolescents de 13 à 15 ans dans 112 000 vidéos en direct. Dans leur rapport, ils ont relevé des risques de pédopiégeage et des « revenus importants » tirés de cadeaux envoyés à des lives contraires au règlement.
Silvija Krupena dirige la cellule de renseignement financier du cabinet britannique RedCompass Labs. Pour elle, l’argent issu de l’exploitation d’enfants peut constituer le produit d’un crime, et les entreprises qui le traitent sciemment risquent des poursuites pour blanchiment. « Un adulte a payé. Un enfant a été exploité. La plateforme a pris sa part », résume-t-elle. Elle ajoute que les alertes adressées aux dirigeants pèsent lourd, car la responsabilité pénale dépend de ce que l’entreprise savait. TikTok assure appliquer un programme anti-blanchiment conforme aux standards internationaux. La loi américaine oblige les plateformes à déclarer les contenus pédocriminels au Centre national pour les enfants disparus et exploités (NCMEC). Interrogé par NPR, TikTok n’a pas dit s’il avait signalé ces lives, ni ce qu’il avait fait de l’argent encaissé.
Des parents tenus à l’écart, selon d’anciens salariés
TikTok a lancé en 2020 la Connexion famille, avec laquelle les parents peuvent limiter le temps d’écran de leur adolescent et filtrer certains contenus. L’année suivante, des salariés ont repéré un lien caché dans les comptes d’adolescents. Il suffisait de l’utiliser pour sortir du contrôle parental. « Ça rend la fonction un peu inutile », a écrit Jordon Furlong, alors chef de produit chargé du bien-être numérique, dans une discussion interne. Si vous avez activé la Connexion famille, TikTok assure aujourd’hui prévenir votre compte quand votre enfant la quitte.
Reagen Maher a signalé une autre faille dans sa déposition. En s’inscrivant avec un compte Google, Facebook ou Instagram, un enfant pouvait accéder à la version de TikTok réservée aux plus de 18 ans, et la direction le savait, assure-t-elle. Les dirigeants ont même évité de connaître l’âge de leurs utilisateurs. Après le rachat de Musical.ly en 2018, Adam Wang, qui dirigeait TikTok Live, et Alex Zhu, président de TikTok, ont préparé un sondage auprès des utilisateurs américains. Ils ont écarté toute question sur le niveau scolaire, de peur de révéler des enfants de moins de 13 ans, dont la loi COPPA protège les données. « Si la FTC apprend l’existence de ce sondage, elle pourrait nous en demander les résultats », notait Adam Wang sur la messagerie interne, à propos de l’autorité américaine de protection des consommateurs. Eric Han, responsable de la sécurité de TikTok entre 2019 et 2023, a signalé en interne, dès 2020, un « effet de contagion » des contenus liés au suicide. Il a indiqué dans sa déposition que TikTok n’avait pas averti les parents des dangers de l’application.
La Commission européenne a accusé TikTok en juillet de mal protéger les comptes des mineurs, après avoir estimé en février que ses contrôles parentaux demandaient trop de temps et de connaissances techniques à la plupart des parents. Ses conclusions sont préliminaires, mais si Bruxelles les confirme, TikTok risque une amende jusqu’à 6 % de son chiffre d’affaires mondial.

articles.title: Spotify quiere que pagues por tus podcasts favoritos: este es el nuevo servicio de Membresías
articles.text:
Spotify presentó Membresías, una herramienta para que los podcasters reciban ingresos recurrentes directamente de sus seguidores. La propuesta amplía las opciones de pago más allá de los episodios adicionales: cada creador decide qué ventajas incluir y cuánto costará cada nivel de acceso.
La función se está desplegando en 34 mercados, entre ellos España, Estados Unidos, Reino Unido, Canadá, Australia y varios países europeos. No es necesario tener Spotify Premium para pagar la membresía de un podcast: tanto los usuarios gratuitos como los suscriptores Premium pueden encontrar las ofertas en la página del programa y acceder al contenido exclusivo desde Spotify.
Episodios extra, menos anuncios y acceso anticipado
Las ventajas cambian según el podcast. Los creadores pueden ofrecer audio o vídeo exclusivo, episodios adicionales, menos anuncios, acceso anticipado a nuevos programas o a su archivo de contenidos. También pueden combinar varios beneficios y proponer distintos niveles de precio para atraer tanto a oyentes ocasionales como a sus seguidores más comprometidos.
Spotify añade opciones para reforzar la relación entre los creadores y sus comunidades. Los miembros pueden mostrar una insignia al comentar episodios, mientras que los podcasters pueden darles la bienvenida con vídeos. La plataforma también ofrece herramientas de promoción, pruebas gratuitas y análisis para que los creadores sepan qué beneficios ayudan a conseguir nuevas suscripciones.
El contenido de pago se ofrece desde la página del programa. Una vez que el oyente se suscribe, puede acceder a los episodios exclusivos en Spotify. Según el servicio, la membresía es independiente del plan Premium: pagar por un podcast no exige contratar una suscripción general a la plataforma, y tener Premium tampoco incluye automáticamente los beneficios de pago de cada programa.
Qué necesitan los podcasters para participar
La herramienta está disponible para programas elegibles alojados en Spotify for Creators o Megaphone. Para activarla, el podcast debe tener al menos tres episodios publicados, 100 oyentes o espectadores y un mínimo de 100 horas de consumo en Spotify durante los 30 días previos. Los creadores que cumplan los requisitos pueden configurarla desde Spotify for Creators o Megaphone.
Spotify afirma que los creadores conservarán el 90 % de los ingresos generados por las membresías. La empresa presenta el sistema como una fuente de ingresos recurrentes que se suma a la publicidad, los patrocinios y el Programa de Socios de Spotify. El servicio no fija un único precio para todos los podcasts: cada creador puede elegir sus tarifas y estructurar sus niveles.
Los primeros podcasts que ofrecerán membresías
Entre los programas que activaron la función desde su lanzamiento están The Adam Friedland Show, Making Sense with Sam Harris, The Shawn Ryan Show, The Sculpt Society y Two Hot Takes. YMH Studios, por su parte, ofrecerá membresías en 12 programas de su red. Cada uno definirá sus propios contenidos y ventajas.
La herramienta fue anticipada durante el Día del Inversor de Spotify, celebrado en mayo, junto con otras iniciativas para creadores, como funciones apoyadas por inteligencia artificial y opciones para gestionar patrocinios. El anuncio encaja con la estrategia de la compañía de ampliar su oferta de podcasts y vídeo, mientras busca atraer a más productores y competir por la atención de las audiencias.
Las membresías no sustituyen las opciones gratuitas de los podcasts ni obligan a los creadores a reservar todo su contenido para quienes pagan. La decisión sobre qué episodios quedan abiertos y cuáles se ofrecen como beneficio exclusivo corresponde a cada programa. Así, los oyentes podrán seguir escuchando los contenidos gratuitos y elegir si pagan por ventajas adicionales en los podcasts que más les interesan.

articles.title: Vuelve a bajar de precio el Google Pixel 10 Pro: es el móvil Android compacto que me compraría ahora mismo
articles.text:
Tenemos varias opciones interesantes si buscamos un móvil Android de gama alta que sea, sobre todo, compacto. Ahora bien, los que se han lanzado este año 2026 tienen precios elevados, incluso con alguna oferta que ha ido apareciendo. Por eso mismo, calidad-precio, merece la pena echar un vistazo a la generación anterior, que es donde se sitúa este Google Pixel 10 Pro, disponible en Amazon por 668,88 euros. Son más de 400 euros de diferencia con respecto al Pixel 11 Pro, lo que hace que me parezca más recomendable ahora mismo.
Google Pixel 10 Pro - Smartphone Android Libre con Gemini, Sistema de cámara Trasera Triple, batería de más de 24 Horas y Pantalla Super Actua de 6,3" - Obsidiana, 128GB
Un móvil compacto de gama alta a un gran precio
Es cierto que hemos visto este móvil de Google algo más barato en el pasado, pero es un buen precio si tenemos en cuenta lo que ofrece. Con el Pixel 11 Pro en las tiendas, apostar por el modelo del año pasado va a hacer que tengamos un móvil compacto de gama alta a un precio muy inferior. Es cierto que el nuevo modelo tiene novedades y mejoras, pero no son tan sustanciales para la diferencia de precio actual que hay entre ambos dispositivos.
Estamos ante un dispositivo con una pantalla OLED de 6,3 pulgadas que utiliza panel LTPO (algo que no está presente en el Pixel 10 base) y 120 Hz. También cuenta con un brillo máximo de 3.300 nits, lo que es ideal para exteriores. A nivel de rendimiento, podemos esperar un buen desempeño gracias al chip Tensor G5 y a sus 16 GB de RAM. Es un móvil pensado para durar que, de hecho, llegó con siete años de actualizaciones garantizadas (aunque ya habría consumido uno de ellos).
Otro punto a destacar del mismo es su batería, que, pese a estar lejos en cifras de los teléfonos de otros fabricantes (tiene 4.870 mAh), está bien optimizada. Para el final, nos hemos dejado uno de sus puntos clave: las cámaras. articles.title: « J’ai un peu de cyberpsychose » : ce que cache l’étrange confidence d’Elon Musk
articles.text:
« J’ai un peu de cyberpsychose. Peut-être beaucoup, en fait. » La phrase est d’Elon Musk et elle a été prononcée lors de l’X Takeover, le rassemblement annuel des fans de Tesla, auquel il participait à distance. Le patron de Tesla, SpaceX et xAI y a ajouté avoir vécu une « psychose IA ou SI » « probablement une demi-douzaine de fois » au cours de l’année, rapporte Business Insider. Le « SI » renvoie à la « super intelligence », le nom que Donald Trump veut désormais donner à l’intelligence artificielle.
À quoi faisait-il référence ? Sans doute à sa conviction que l’IA peut avoir du goût. Juste avant son aveu, Elon Musk s’extasiait sur des clips musicaux générés par intelligence artificielle. « Vous vous dites : ‹ Waouh, l’IA peut avoir bon goût ? C’est dingue › », a-t-il raconté. Rien dans ses propos ne ressemble à une confidence sur sa santé mentale : le milliardaire reprend surtout une expression devenue à la mode dans la Silicon Valley.
 Elon Musk at @theXtakeover: “At various points this year, I’ve had AI or SI psychosis probably like half a dozen times.” @elonmusk https://t.co/iu0PqpcGTm
— Tesla Owners Silicon Valley (@teslaownersSV) October 15, 2026
Une boutade dans la Silicon Valley
Dans les milieux de la tech, la « psychose IA » est en effet devenue un signe de ralliement, presque un badge d’honneur pour ceux qui utilisent l’IA de manière intensive. En mars, Garry Tan, le patron de l’incubateur Y Combinator, plaisantait : « J’ai la cyberpsychose, mais je crois qu’un tiers des PDG que je connais l’ont aussi. » Et lors d’une fête organisée en mai à New York, les participants scandaient « Un, deux, trois, psychose IA ! ». Même la musicienne Grimes, mère de plusieurs enfants d’Elon Musk, s’en amusait en décembre dernier sur X : « Le truc avec la psychose IA, c’est que c’est plus drôle que de ne pas l’avoir ».
Un phénomène bien réel pour les psychiatres
La plaisanterie tranche avec ce que décrivent les soignants. La « psychose IA » n’est pas un diagnostic médical reconnu. L’expression désigne des cas où des conversations prolongées avec un chatbot alimentent ou renforcent les idées délirantes d’une personne, l’IA validant ses croyances au lieu de les contredire. « Ce n’est pas aussi simple que de tracer une ligne entre l’IA et la psychose, mais nous voyons des cas de psychose mêlés à l’usage de l’IA », explique Julia Sheffield, professeure adjointe de psychiatrie au Vanderbilt University Medical Center, dans la revue de l’American Psychological Association. « Pour ces patients, l’IA semble renforcer les pensées délirantes et amplifier l’expérience du délire. »
Son équipe a passé au crible les dossiers médicaux de l’hôpital entre décembre 2022 et avril 2026. Elle a identifié 28 patients dont les troubles psychotiques étaient liés à l’usage d’un chatbot, ChatGPT dans plus de la moitié des cas. Pour six sur dix d’entre eux, il s’agissait d’un tout premier épisode psychotique, selon cette étude publiée en juin, qui n’a pas encore été relue par d’autres chercheurs. Ragy Girgis, professeur de psychiatrie clinique à l’université Columbia, considère l’IA comme une source de renforcement « plus puissante » que les autres, parce qu’elle répond et s’adapte à chacun.
Le phénomène reste rare en proportion, mais pas en volume. En octobre 2025, OpenAI estimait que 0,07 % des utilisateurs actifs de ChatGPT sur une semaine montraient des signes possibles de psychose ou de manie, soit des centaines de milliers de personnes à l’échelle du service. Le même rapport indiquait que plus d’un million d’utilisateurs évoquaient chaque semaine des pensées suicidaires avec le chatbot. Depuis, OpenAI a aussi déployé un système qui estime l’âge de ses utilisateurs afin d’appliquer automatiquement des protections aux mineurs, actif en Europe depuis la fin août.
Concernant Elon Musk, il est bien sûr impossible de tirer la moindre conclusion médicale. Cette sortie de l’un des patrons les plus influents de l’IA ravive néanmoins le débat sur un phénomène que les psychiatres prennent de plus en plus au sérieux.
Si vous traversez une période difficile ou avez des pensées suicidaires, le 3114, numéro national de prévention du suicide, est joignable gratuitement 24 heures sur 24.

articles.title: GTA 6 is on track to smash records as pre-orders exceed 6 million copies
articles.text:
Forward-looking: Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to be the biggest video game launch of 2026 and, quite possibly, the most successful entertainment launch in history. With one month to go before its November 19 release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles, market intelligence firm Sensor Tower has shared its estimates for the game's pre-orders.
As of October 20, Rockstar has pre-sold an estimated 6.45 million copies of the game – earning roughly $630 million in the process. According to Sensor Tower, most – 74% – are buying the game for PlayStation 5. Broken down another way, it works out to 4.8 million copies sold for PS5 and 1.66 million on Xbox.
An earlier estimate from Piper Sandler suggested Rockstar might sell north of 45 million copies of GTA VI come launch.
GTA VI is the highly-anticipated sequel to Grand Theft Auto V, which arrived way back in 2013. It is set in the fictional state of Leonida, which is based on Florida, and looks to be more immersive and interactive than anything we have seen from the franchise to date. Rockstar has been working on the game for over a decade, so to say it has big shoes to fill would be a huge understatement.
GTA VI is priced at $79.99 for the standard edition, or $99.99 for the ultimate edition. Rockstar is also offering a premium collector's set that includes several game-themed goodies for $399.99. Oddly enough, this edition doesn't actually include a copy of the game itself.
Gamers and other major industry players are preparing accordingly. In August, we profiled several gamers that plan to take off from work on launch week in order to binge play the new crime sim. Competing game studios, meanwhile, have adjusted their launch schedules to avoid dropping new games in the same window as GTA VI. Even the military is getting in on the frenzy, with solders at one base reportedly offered time off to play the game in exchange for reenlisting.

articles.title: “Plus probable que ça réussisse” : en novembre, SpaceX tentera une folle double capture du Starship en plein vol
articles.text:
“Plus probable que ça réussisse” : en novembre, SpaceX tentera une folle double capture du Starship en plein vol
SpaceX s'apprête à tenter un double rattrapage inédit du Starship avec les bras mécaniques de sa tour de lancement. Une étape aussi risquée que cruciale pour diviser les coûts de l'exploration spatiale et préparer le retour sur la Lune.
On y est. Ceux qui ont vécu la première capture historique en plein vol du premier étage du Starship en octobre 2024 se rappellent avec émotion de leur sidération. SpaceX nous prépare un événement de même ampleur. Plus fou encore : cette fois-ci, ce sont les deux étages qui devraient être saisis par les Chopsticks de Mechazilla, le Super Heavy et le Ship. Lunaire. Martien.
C'est Elon Musk lui-même qui vient d'en faire l'annonce officielle lors de la conférence des résultats trimestriels de SpaceX. Comme il aime à le dire, quoi qu'il en soit – résultat ou échec – ça sera du spectacle. Et concernant les chances de succès, Musk est assez confiant :
	
Je dirais qu'il est plus probable que l'inverse que cela réussisse.
Le vol 15 tentera de marquer l'histoire
Le vol 14 marqua l'entrée du Starship dans la cour des lanceurs orbitaux. Ce fut globalement une réussite (malgré quelques moteurs récalcitrants). Mais le vol 15 doit être l'une des étapes cruciales qui validera en partie les espoirs fondés sur ce lanceur sans équivalent. La réutilisation intégrale, Super Heavy plus Ship, est une condition sine qua non du projet. Projet de remplacer les Falcon 9 par des Starship, projet de l'envoyer vers la Lune et vers Mars.
Les tentatives auront lieu en novembre, même si aucune date n'est fixée. L'autorité de régulation des vols (FAA) devra donner son accord, comme à chaque fois. Ensuite, l'autre grande étape sera le ravitaillement en plein vol, que la société spatiale prévoit pour début 2027.
Pour Elon Musk,qui prétend vouloir rendre l'humanité multiplanétaire : “C'est un jalon technologique profond dans l'histoire de la civilisation et de la conscience”.
Beaucoup plus risqué que le rattrapage du Super Heavy
On pourrait croire qu'après avoir réussi trois rattrapages du Super Heavy par la tour, puis des amerrissages en douceur du Ship, l'opération suivante ne serait qu'une belle conjugaison des deux. C'est en réalité bien plus complexe. Voici pourquoi :
- Le Ship aura réalisé au moins une orbite, soit une heure trente de vol, et non quelques minutes comme le Super Heavy.
- Sa vitesse sera environ 6 fois plus élevée que celle du Super Heavy (28 000 km/h contre 4 500 km/h).
- Les contraintes sur les tuiles thermiques sont énormes à une telle vitesse. Le Ship sera enveloppé de plasma qui fera monter la température du bouclier thermique à plus de 1500 °C.
- La précision nécessaire pour atteindre une tour de lancement n'est pas comparable à celle nécessaire pour amerrir dans l'océan.
Le futur du spatial suspendu à un double bottle flip challenge
Pour la NASA et son programme Artemis, qui compte sur le Starship pour ramener les astronautes sur la surface lunaire, cette maîtrise technique est une condition absolue. Sans un lanceur entièrement réutilisable, l'établissement de bases permanentes sur la Lune ou l'exploration de Mars restera économiquement hors de portée.
	
La seule façon d'étendre la conscience au-delà de la Terre sur une base durable est d'avoir un lanceur orbital entièrement réutilisable.
Bien sûr, la réussite du vol 15 ne résoudrait qu'une minuscule partie des problèmes qui attendent SpaceX et la Nasa pour leur retour habité sur la Lune. Il restera à réussir le ravitaillement envol, à se poser sur un pôle sud très accidenté, en redécoller, etc. Et pour Mars, c'est encore pire, les défis technologiques et physiologiques sont d'un autre ordre de grandeur. Ce vol 15 n'est pas une condition suffisante à ces projets, mais c'est une condition nécessaire.

articles.title: Nvidia bets open models can give enterprise AI agents the context they’re missing
articles.text:
Nvidia bets open models can give enterprise AI agents the context they’re missing
Every enterprise company is currently trying to figure out how to have its AI tools work with its data. Meanwhile, every major enterprise vendor that works with those enterprises (think SAP, Microsoft, Salesforce, Workday, etc.) is making a claim on becoming the central hub for managing and securing that data.
But what about the companies that want to do it themselves?
Nvidia, on Wednesday, announced how it wants to provide enterprise AI agents with the data they need to make sense of company data — all without competing with the data platforms that already store it.
At its GTC Berlin conference Wednesday, the company added Agent Knowledge Foundation to its Agent Toolkit. This new collection of open-source components bundles the company’s Nemotron Retriever models, a new Auto-Ontology library, the Kumo family of models for structured data, and its CUDA-X data processing libraries.
With this system, Nvidia says, the data can stay where it is and remain managed under the access rules these companies already have in place.
Today, as Adel El Hallak, Nvidia’s vice president of product for agentic AI, tells The New Stack, enterprises may be able to connect an agent to a vendor like Snowflake, but that doesn’t help the agent understand the overall enterprise context.
“I wish it was as easy as connected to my Snowflake system, connected to my email exchange, connected to my knowledge base, and then all of a sudden, magically, the AI understands all the data. But the reality is different,” he says.
Large language models are “great at predicting next tokens,” El Hallak argues, but when presented with a single spreadsheet that has “a whole bunch of tabs,” the agent will have a hard time finding something specific. “It’s gonna struggle,” he says.
Better retrieval, fewer lookups
“In the world of agents, you want the most accurate embedding models or reranking models,” El Hallak says, even if that adds a bit of latency to each lookup. The agent then gets “much more pertinent information. So the number of lookups at the end, the overall latency actually goes down.”
Nvidia says its Nemotron Retriever embedding model raised search relevance by 65% in tests on an open source OpenSearch setup, needing fewer search steps and adding hardly any latency. SAP’s fine-tuned version of the reranker ran nearly three times faster, Nvidia says, and ServiceNow got better reranking quality with close to 25% less latency.
From RAG to ontologies
“RAG was awesome, but is it good enough?” El Hallak asks. Knowledge graphs, he says, represent concepts and the relationships between them better than retrieval-augmented generation, which pulls in chunks of text based on similarity.
Nvidia’s Auto-Ontology library builds those graphs from a company’s own tables and maps raw data to business concepts like customers, products, and orders. Its listing in Nvidia’s NGC software catalog shows a REST API and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that agents can use to query it.
“You and I, it’s easy for us to understand. A tier is the same thing as a plan when you’re looking at a mobile carrier,” El Hallak says, but LLMs “mess those up.”
Nvidia bought Illumex, an Israeli startup that automated the creation of semantic layers and ontologies for enterprise data, for a reported $75 million in February. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told Globes that the team’s ontology expertise would help it build “libraries and models that will enable the adoption of Agentic AI in organizations.”
Predictions from tables
Kumo, the startup Nvidia bought in June in a deal The Information valued at more than $400 million, built foundation models for relational data. Nvidia has since released several Kumo models as open weights on Hugging Face, including Kumo Tabular in September.
El Hallak says those models replace the per-task pipelines data teams used to build “for every classification, for every churn, for every sentiment analysis.”
“The whole point of the ontology … is to bring harmonization as you create those knowledge graphs, so there’s [consistency] across the tables, and then you could use Kumo to drive predictive analytics,” he says.
Partners, not rivals
“I’m not looking to compete with, for example, a Snowflake. On the contrary, I want to partner with them,” El Hallak says.
Nvidia’s own supply chain team uses Agent Knowledge Foundation through Palantir’s Foundry platform, building on earlier work between the two companies. Databricks is pairing a Kumo anomaly detection model with Genie Ontology, the context layer it introduced in June, and Snowflake customers can run Kumo models in Snowflake Notebooks.
“I’m not thinking about ACLs and data access and all those things. That’s why I need the partners,” El Hallak says, referring to access control lists and other security features that its enterprise partners offer.
Owning the stack
Not every vendor is taking that route. SAP closed its acquisition of Prior Labs, the company behind the TabPFN tabular models, in July and committed more than €1 billion to it over four years. It now offers TabPFN-3.5 Plus in SAP AI Core alongside its own RPT models.
Nvidia, meanwhile, distributes its models through Hugging Face, which it agreed to buy for $12.9 billion in September. “We just build little weights and models, and we publish them on Hugging Face,” El Hallak says.
That leaves Nvidia building the models, while the likes of Snowflake and Databricks keep control over the data and the permissions around it.

articles.title: Claro coloca 54 milhões de pessoas em novo programa de fidelidade • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Claro coloca 54 milhões de pessoas em novo programa de fidelidade
Claro Clube passa por reformulação e passa a contar com quatro categorias. Clientes ganham descontos e internet adicional.
A Claro lança nesta terça-feira uma nova versão do programa de fidelidade Claro Clube, que agora fica disponível para mais de 54 milhões de clientes, segundo a empresa revelou com exclusividade ao Tecnoblog. A novidade são os clientes do pré-pago do Prezão, que também terão acesso ao programa. A transição será feita a partir de janeiro de 2027.
O novo modelo acaba com o acúmulo de pontos. Em vez disso, os benefícios dependem da categoria do cliente, que é definida a partir dos serviços contratados. Ele lembra mais os programas usados por companhias aéreas. São quatro categorias: Claro Clube, Prata, Ouro e Rubi.
Confira abaixo a tabela com as quatro categorias do Claro Clube, os clientes contemplados e os benefícios de cada uma delas.
| Benefício | Claro Clube | Prata | Ouro | Rubi | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Contemplados | Prezão | Fibra, TV+ ou pós-pago | Claro Multi e outros combos | Múltiplos serviços para família | 
| Desconto e cashback em mais de 300 parceiros | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | 
| Bônus de internet móvel (20 GB) | ❌ | ✅ 1x por ano | ✅ 2x por ano | ✅ 4x por ano | 
| 50% de desconto em cinema e teatro | ❌ | ✅ 2 ingressos por mês | ✅ 4 ingressos por mês | ✅ 8 ingressos por mês | 
| Pré-venda e desconto em ingresso de futebol | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | 
| Desconto em celular 5G (no plano Multi) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ R$ 100 | ✅ R$ 500 | 
| Ingressos em eventos patrocinados | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | 
O cashback pode ser resgatado em Pix ou vale-compras, com parceiros como Natura, C&A e Riachuelo, além dos restaurantes Outback e Bob’s. O desconto em ingressos de cinema é feito em parceria com a Cinépolis, e a pré-venda de futebol vale para jogos de 14 clubes brasileiros. As experiências do Rubi incluem eventos apoiados pela Claro, como os campeonatos de tênis Rio Open e SP Open.
O Claro Clube funciona dentro do aplicativo Minha Claro, onde o cliente consulta a própria categoria, resgata as ofertas e vê as marcas parceiras. A operadora afirma que o app também recomenda as vantagens mais relevantes para o perfil de cada pessoa.
A categoria é definida por uma pontuação de relacionamento, calculada a partir dos produtos contratados num mesmo CPF. Esses pontos não são acumulados nem trocados por prêmios, mas servem para enquadrar o cliente em uma categoria. Cada produto vale uma quantidade de pontos:
O Claro Clube é a categoria de entrada, exigindo 0 ponto. O Prata vai de 1 a 5 pontos, o Ouro de 6 a 15 e o Rubi começa em 16. Um exemplo dado pela Claro: um cliente com Claro Fibra em casa (4 pontos), outro Claro Fibra na casa de praia (4), uma linha Claro Pós (4) com duas linhas adicionais (2 x 2 pontos) e um Claro TV+ (4) soma 20 pontos. Portanto, é reconhecido como cliente Rubi.
Os pontos ficam no CPF do titular do contrato. Dependentes não pontuam no próprio CPF, e os benefícios só podem ser resgatados pelo titular, segundo a documentação visualizada pelo Tecnoblog.
Quem acumulou pontos no Claro Clube atual não perde o saldo de imediato. Os resgates continuam disponíveis normalmente até 31 de dezembro de 2026, pouco mais de dois meses depois do lançamento do novo programa. Já a transição ocorre em 1º de janeiro de 2027.
Segundo a Claro, o novo modelo foi desenhado a partir de pesquisas com consumidores nos últimos meses, que apontaram preferência por benefícios de uso imediato, por poder escolher a vantagem e por parcerias ligadas ao dia a dia. “Criamos um programa mais simples, mais abrangente e mais conectado ao dia a dia das pessoas”, afirmou o diretor de marketing da Claro, Marcio Carvalho, em comunicado.

articles.title: Mysterious AMD Zen 6 APU with 24GB of LPDDR5 memory appears in benchmarks — chip may be for next-gen Steam Deck or gaming handhelds
articles.text:
Mysterious AMD Zen 6 APU with 24GB of LPDDR5 memory appears in benchmarks — chip may be for next-gen Steam Deck or gaming handhelds
A mysterious AMD chip points to a possible Steam Deck successor.
An AMD engineering sample has made an appearance in a listing on OpenBenchmarking. According to a report by TechPowerUp, the chip could potentially be a part of AMD’s upcoming Gainsborough family and a possible candidate for the next-generation Steam Deck handheld console. As per the OpenBenchmarking listing, the chip comes with a six-core, 12-thread processor paired with 24GB of high-speed LPDDR5 memory.
The engineering sample with part number 100-000001930-12_Y was tested on an AMD GBR-FF6-SKT validation board, with the CPU running at clock speeds of 2.4 GHz. The system also features four 6GB SK Hynix memory packages, resulting in 24GB of LPDDR5 memory running at 9,600 MT/s. That’s a big jump when compared to the current Steam Deck, which comes with 16GB of LPDDR5 memory running at 6,400 MT/s, alongside a four-core, eight-thread AMD Zen 2 processor.
The benchmark listing also provides some clues about the processor’s underlying architecture. As per Notebookcheck, the sample’s CPU microcode revision corresponds to AMD’s Family 1Ah, model DCh. Linux kernel changes indicate that this model falls within the range reserved for newer Zen 6 processors, suggesting that Gainsborough could use AMD’s next-generation CPU architecture. However, there is no clarity or any confirmation whether it will use standard Zen 6 cores or the denser Zen 6C variant.
The integrated GPU is listed with a clock speed of 2,400 MHz, although its architecture and compute unit count remain unknown. The sample was tested using the GpuTest benchmark suite on Ubuntu 24.04 at 1024 x 768 resolution, resulting in scores of 3,871 in GiMark, 3,508 in FurMark, and 9,319 in TessMark. While the FurMark score is comparable to the original Stam Deck, we can’t really come to any conclusions at this point, as the tests were conducted on an engineering platform using development software rather than a finished handheld. For now, the results do not establish how the chip would perform in games, as power limits, cooling, driver maturity, and the final GPU configuration all contribute to the performance in a compact gaming device.
If these specifications carry over to a future Steam Deck, the additional CPU cores along with the larger and faster memory would provide a meaningful hardware upgrade. That being said, neither AMD nor Valve have confirmed a connection between the Gainsborough family and a future Steam Deck. Thus, it is best to take this with a grain of salt and wait until there is more concrete information in the future.

- usertests DS426 said:Fair point on mem prices but Zen 2 -> 6 is already a big jump, especially when you factor in 50% more cores.
2x Z6 + 4x Z6d would about be the most ideal setup IMO for a handheld except for the die-to-die latency penalty and added cost of using two dies, even if they are recycled semi-defective ones (some cores weak or dead, etc.).I'm not worried about the CPU performance which would be great with that setup (I suppose even all/mostly LP cores would be fine, which is why I mentioned them). Rather, Zen 7 cores could be delivering an additional large power efficiency increase over Zen 6 at low power draw (source is MLID):
https://www.igorslab.de/en/zen-7-aka-grimlock-at-a-glance-big-gaps-at-amd/ The energy efficiency is particularly impressive: at just 3 watts per core, performance increases by 30 to 36% compared to Medusa (Zen 6). 
Ideally, the CPU in a handheld rarely needs a lot of power, and extra power is diverted to the GPU in a higher wattage scenario.
But more importantly, RDNA5 or later should blow away what is an RDNA3.5 derivative.
I understand that 12 CUs RDNA4m would be a decent improvement over the original, but I'm not sure it's transformative enough to meet Valve's past statements about the Steam Deck 2. Having full fat FP8 FSR4 may not even make much of a difference now that a lightweight version of FSR4.1 is officially being made available to "Z2-series", which presumably includes the "Z2 A" which is the Steam Deck 1 SoC.
24 GB is the minimum viable memory for a Steam Deck 2, and should be fine for many games. 32 GB would be better, and I wonder if they would be willing to bifurcate the lineup and offer more RAM in the top model(s).
I don't think die-to-die latency is a problem. The Zen 6 family will include smaller monolithic APUs, and Gainsborough seems like it would be one of them. The products that do use chiplets should be using the "sea of wires" InFO-oS interconnect like Strix Halo, which would eliminate latency.
Future APUs will be more expensive as wafer costs keep going up for new nodes, which is an argument against Just Wait-ing for Zen 7, etc., but a tiny SoC's silicon cost doesn't matter compared to memory/storage, at least at this moment. Reply

articles.title: Russia drafted plans for AI that could block 95% of VPNs — but the idea has quietly vanished from its national roadmap
articles.text:
Russia drafted plans for AI that could block 95% of VPNs — but the idea has quietly vanished from its national roadmap
The machine-learning filter it would have relied on is funded separately
- A draft of Russia's national AI plan proposed using AI to analyze 70% of blocked VPN services and lift blocking effectiveness to 95%
- The Digital Development Ministry says the measure is absent from the current draft, but Roskomnadzor's separately budgeted and arguably crucial ML filtering project remains
- The 95% is an effectiveness target, not accuracy, and sources expect AI to raise false positives, with corporate VPN, cloud and voice traffic most exposed
Russia's Digital Development Ministry considered using artificial intelligence to push the effectiveness of its VPN blocking to 95%, according to a front-page report in Kommersant.
The measure appeared in a draft of the country's national plan for implementing AI through 2030; the ministry now says it is not in the current version.
This isn't the first time such a move has been reported, but some earlier coverage might have been overzealous, to say the least, when it reported that "Russia Eyes AI-Powered VPN Crackdown With 95% Blocking Accuracy." The problem with that headline is that not only was that proposal dropped, but the 95% accuracy figure was never actually in play.
A draft that proposed AI use
None of the above reporting should reassure an estimated 57 million Russians who rely on circumvention tools.
Roskomnadzor (the Federal agency tasked with "Supervision of Communications, Information Technology and Mass Media") has its own machine-learning filtering project budgeted outside the national AI plan, and the money for Russia's blocking infrastructure is set to double next year.
Kommersant, which reviewed the draft, reports that the ministry wanted AI to analyze the characteristics of 70% of all the VPN services Russia blocks. The drafters reckoned that would lift blocking effectiveness to 95%.
Asked about it, the ministry said the current draft of the plan "contains no such information," in Meduza's translation. A source familiar with the discussions told Kommersant that agencies had pitched a range of measures for the plan, some of which may never be implemented, and that the traffic-analysis algorithms already in service are a form of intelligent analysis but do not count as AI.
An AI layer would behave fundamentally differently; rather than matching known signatures, models would weigh packet sizes and timing, session length, and the balance of inbound to outbound traffic, then flag likely VPN servers from indirect clues: how a node behaves, which host it sits on, and what its neighboring IP addresses look like. The payoff is speed, catching new servers before they reach any blocklist.
Kommersant uses the word effectiveness, and the distinction matters: a blocking-effectiveness figure describes how much targeted traffic it stops. It says nothing about how much legitimate traffic gets stopped with it, and that is what the catch is; the solution proposed does not account for any mistakes, just how effective it would be at its job of blocking out VPN traffic.
The 95% target is also less of a leap than some headlines suggest, because Russia already has 92% on paper, at least by its own estimates. A Roskomnadzor subsidy decision for its Main Radio Frequency Center (GRChTs), dated January 2025 and surfaced in May 2026 by journalist Maria Kolomychenko, sets an "average level of effectiveness" of 92% for restricting VPNs via signatures by the end of 2030. Verstka reports that the AI proposal was meant to lift that same indicator to 95%.
The more consequential point is that striking a line from a draft strategy does not strike the capability. Forbes Russia reported in January 2026 that Roskomnadzor planned to spend 2.27 billion rubles (around $29 million) in 2026 on a machine-learning-based traffic-filtering mechanism, a project we flagged when Windscribe saw a roughly 90% drop in its Russian traffic that same month.
The false-positive risk is not hypothetical in Russia, because the government has already learned how hard it is to separate good VPNs from bad ones. When the ministry ordered major platforms in April to block users with VPNs switched on, its guidance promised a whitelist for corporate VPNs.
Telegram founder Pavel Durov claimed the crackdown had "triggered a massive banking failure," and outage-tracking data showed bank disruptions on April 3 2026. A source told RBC at the time that no reliable technical method existed to tell permitted corporate VPN traffic from the rest.
For now the picture on the ground is unchanged: blocking is intensifying with or without an AI mandate. At least 10 VPN providers reported tighter restrictions in the week after September's State Duma elections, and VPN Guild chairman Alexey Kozlyuk described it to Meduza as "a continuation and gradual intensification" of a campaign that began in August.
The Kommersant report also landed a day after RBC revealed a draft ministry order requiring phones on Russia's 5G networks to support the FSB-developed Kuznyechik cipher from March 1, 2032.
Providers keep adapting. "In Russia, VPNs face pressure almost every month; it is a new norm," an Amnezia VPN spokeswoman told TechRadar Pro. But Sarkis Darbinyan of RKS Global and the VPN Guild warned TechRadar that for users, the end result is "an ever-shrinking number of services that actually work."
The 95% target may be gone from one document. The infrastructure, the money, and the intent behind it are not.

articles.title: Philips Monitors Introduces the 27E3C2500 and 32E3C2500
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Philips Monitors Introduces the 27E3C2500 and 32E3C2500
The Philips Monitor line-up expands with the 27E3C2500 and 32E3C2500, two curved monitors designed for home and office users and casual gamers. Both feature a QHD resolution and 1500R curved VA panel, combining detailed visuals for everyday tasks with smooth motion for gaming. They are designed for people who use the same monitor for work and entertainment, from reviewing documents to watching a movie or playing a game.
With a QHD resolution of 2560 × 1440, both monitors provide more detail than Full HD and sufficient space to view documents and applications side by side. The curved screen adds a sense of immersion when watching movies or exploring game environments. The Philips 27E3C2500 offers a 27-inch (68.6 cm) screen for users who prefer a smaller display. The Philips 32E3C2500 provides a larger 31.5-inch (80 cm) viewing area, with the same QHD resolution and refresh rate. The choice allows users to select a size that suits their desk and viewing preferences.Both models support HDR10 for compatible HDR content. Philips SmartContrast analyses the displayed content and adjusts the backlight to enhance contrast.
Smooth motion for everyday tasks and casual gaming
A 144 Hz refresh rate makes scrolling and on-screen movement look smoother than on a conventional 60 Hz display. During gaming, Adaptive-Sync matches the display's refresh rate to the output of a compatible graphics source, helping reduce screen tearing and stuttering.
Both monitors also offer 0.5 ms MPRT for reduced perceived motion blur during gaming. This helps keep moving images clearer during fast-paced scenes.
Features for the home desk
SoftBlue technology reduces blue light emissions, while Flicker-free technology reduces screen flicker during everyday use. Both monitors also include an EasyRead mode for on-screen reading.
HDMI and DisplayPort inputs provide connections for compatible sources. Two built-in 2 W speakers let users listen to videos and games without adding separate speakers to the desk, while an audio output offers an additional listening option.
The stand allows users to tilt the screen to suit their viewing position. Both monitors support 100 × 100 mm VESA mounting for use with a compatible monitor arm or wall mount.
Full HD options in the same range
The range also includes the Philips 27E3C2200 and 32E3C2200, with 27-inch and 31.5-inch screens respectively. Both offer a Full HD 1920 × 1080 resolution with a 1500R curved VA panel, 144 Hz refresh rate, and Adaptive-Sync. 
Prices and availability
The Philips 27E3C2500 and 32E3C2500 combine curved QHD viewing with features for home working and casual gaming. Two screen sizes and built-in audio give users a choice of display for a desk shared between work and downtime.
The Philips 27E3C2500 will be available for purchase in November, at an MSRP of £129.99. 
The Philips 32E3C2500 will be available for purchase in November as well, at an MSRP of £169.99.
