articles.title: 50 morts : Anthropic veut réglementer l’IA, mais fixe des seuils qui font froid dans le dos
articles.text:
Selon les informations du média Politico, des représentants d’Anthropic, l’entreprise derrière Claude, se sont rendus au Capitole afin de présenter un projet de loi à des élus, visant à réglementer le développement de l’intelligence artificielle. Aussi surprenant que cela puisse paraître, les seuils fixés par Anthropic pour permettre aux autorités de faire suspendre un modèle d’IA sont particulièrement élevés : une menace pouvant provoquer plus de 50 morts ou blessés graves, ou plus d’un milliard de dollars de dommages.
50 morts ou un milliard de dollars de dommages : les seuils surprenants fixés par Anthropic
Ce projet de loi élaboré par Anthropic établit trois cas où une IA de pointe pourrait être bloquée : le développement d’une arme biologique, une cyberattaque et un modèle échappant au contrôle de son concepteur. Il s’agit donc de cas souvent évoqués et particulièrement redoutés. Mais nous arrivons au point le plus surprenant : le blocage d’une IA ne pourrait être déclenché par le gouvernement américain que si l’un de ces deux seuils risque d’être atteint. Le premier seuil serait atteint si une IA pouvait provoquer plus de 50 morts ou blessés graves. Le second seuil est quant à lui atteint lorsque plus d’un milliard de dollars de dommages sont enregistrés. Ce faisant, Anthropic fixe donc un prix à une vie humaine. en deors de toute question éthique posée par ce genre de calculs une autre question s’impose : pourquoi attendre de tels dégâts avant de stopper une IA ?
Précisons aussi que la surveillance des modèles d’IA serait confiée à des évaluateurs indépendants, enregistrés auprès du département américain du Commerce. Les laboratoires pourraient les rémunérer, à condition que leur paiement ne dépende pas des conclusions de leurs évaluations. Si un risque imminent est identifié, les évaluateurs devront le signaler au département du Commerce dans les 72 heures suivant la fin de leur évaluation. Un juge fédéral du district de Columbia serait par ailleurs le seul habilité à ordonner la suspension d’un modèle d’IA, à la demande du département américain du Commerce.
Pourquoi des seuils aussi élevés ?
Si l’on résume l’actualité récente : Anthropic appelle à ralentir le développement de l’IA et annonce la création d’un fonds destiné au bien public, tout en proposant de limiter le blocage d’un modèle d’IA aux cas où il risque de provoquer plus de 50 morts ou blessés graves, ou plus d’un milliard de dollars de dommages. À première vue, il est difficile d’y voir une logique.
En réalité, Anthropic devrait continuer à encadrer en interne le développement de ses IA, sans attendre que l’une d’entre elles risque de provoquer plus de 50 morts ou blessés graves. Avec ce projet de loi, l’entreprise cherche surtout à définir les conditions dans lesquelles le gouvernement américain pourrait bloquer un modèle d’IA, tout en limitant les possibilités d’intervention des autorités.

articles.title: Financial transformation: Why slow AI adoption is the top risk - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Dell’s security chief warns AI is lowering the barriers to sophisticated cyberattacks
Financial transformation powered by artificial intelligence now runs as two races at once. Banks and other financial institutions are racing to turn data into action with AI, while their security teams scramble to prepare for a wave of agentic AI-driven threats.
That second race is being shaped by how cheaply attackers can now obtain advanced capabilities. Agentic AI hasn’t erased the old hierarchy of hacktivists, criminal gangs and nation-states, but it has handed lower-tier actors tools once reserved for the top, according to John Scimone (pictured), president and chief security officer of Dell Technologies Inc.
“I think the pyramid still exists, but undoubtedly the cost of entry and the barriers to entry have crumbled,” Scimone said. “Said another way, the least sophisticated attack tomorrow is more sophisticated than the world will have ever seen a year ago.”
Scimone spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante at the Dell Technologies New York Symposium, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed financial transformation and using AI to defend against AI threats. (* Disclosure below.)
Securing financial transformation in the agentic era
Dell is already putting frontier models to work on its own defenses. The company is a partner in Anthropic PBC’s Project Glasswing, which gives vetted organizations access to powerful AI tools to secure critical systems, Scimone noted. The program has drawn in new members and was recently folded into a broader verification program. The fundamentals of identity, access management and detection still apply, but attacks now arrive at a speed and scale that make yesterday’s practices insufficient, he explained.
“We as cybersecurity professionals are going to have to use AI to defend against AI,” Scimone said. “There’s a huge opportunity really to be able to leverage this capability for good.”
That opportunity could matter most to organizations that have never been able to staff a full security team. Agents can deliver scale and expertise that smaller companies could never hire or build on their own, according to Scimone.
“Our future security program might be a security program of one person, but it might have 10,000 agents, all of which are the best security practitioners in the space and the roles in which they’re assigned,” Scimone added.

articles.title: CNIL, DeviantArt, OBS : des sites ferment à cause des failles PHP — Frandroid
articles.text:
Ce mercredi 21 octobre, vers 12 h 30, le site de la CNIL est passé en maintenance, a constaté Next. Le gendarme français des données personnelles a coupé son site par précaution, en attendant le correctif que PHP doit publier à 16 heures.
PHP fait tourner une grande partie du Web, et ses deux failles permettent de prendre le contrôle d’un serveur à distance, comme nous l’expliquions lors de l’annonce. Plusieurs administrations et grandes plateformes ont fait le même choix. Pour les internautes, ça veut dire plusieurs heures sans accès à des services publics ou à des sites très fréquentés.
Aux Pays-Bas, la Tweede Kamer, la chambre basse du Parlement, a mis son site hors ligne par précaution, a confirmé un porte-parole. D’après la NOS, l’audiovisuel public néerlandais, la coupure touche aussi MijnOverheid.nl, le portail où les citoyens reçoivent leur courrier administratif. Même chose pour DigiD, l’identifiant qui sert à se connecter aux services de l’État, un peu comme FranceConnect chez nous. Des services publics finlandais ont pris la même décision.
Plusieurs grandes plateformes privées ont suivi. 4chan, le célèbre forum anonyme, se dit « temporairement en lecture seule en attendant une mise à jour de sécurité urgente de PHP ». DeviantArt, la plateforme de partage d’illustrations, a annoncé sa maintenance dans un message publié sur X, et le site Dev-Null a fait de même.
L’équipe d’OBS, le logiciel libre de streaming et d’enregistrement vidéo, a aussi prévenu sur X que « certaines parties » de son site seraient indisponibles en attendant la publication des détails de la faille. Elle précise que le streaming via les comptes connectés ne devrait pas être touché.
Le CERT-EU conseille lui-même de couper
Mardi 20 octobre, l’équipe de PHP a annoncé deux failles critiques et un correctif pour ce mercredi. Elles sont référencées CVE-2026-109618 et CVE-2026-109619 et notées 9,2 sur 10 en gravité.
Le même jour, le CERT-EU, le service de cybersécurité des institutions européennes, a publié une fiche sur ces failles. Il y conseille aux organisations qui ne peuvent pas corriger tout de suite d’isoler leurs applications connectées à Internet jusqu’à la mise à jour.
Pourtant, la page « maintenance » intégrée à WordPress ou Magento ne suffit pas. PHP lit chaque requête avant même que l’application vérifie si elle est en maintenance. Il faut donc arrêter PHP sur le serveur et afficher une page statique à la place, ce qui revient à fermer le site.
Des attaques déjà en cours ?
Cloudflare, dont le réseau filtre le trafic de nombreux sites, dit en voir les premières. Dane Knecht, son directeur technique, a écrit sur X que l’entreprise observe « des attaques qui commencent à émerger ». Cloudflare a déployé des règles de pare-feu contre les méthodes d’attaque déjà connues, y compris pour ses clients gratuits. Par contre, Dane Knecht présente ces règles comme une solution temporaire. De son côté, watchTowr, une société de cybersécurité qui dit avoir reproduit l’une des failles, confirme qu’elles sont bien réelles. Elle garde pourtant les détails jusqu’à 16 heures, pour que les pirates ne prennent pas de vitesse les administrateurs.
Des preuves d’exploitation circulent aussi sur les réseaux sociaux, mais personne ne les a confirmées à l’heure où l’on écrit. Aux Pays-Bas, le NCSC, l’agence nationale de cybersécurité, n’avait encore constaté aucun abus ce mercredi. Si une exploitation se confirme, PHP s’est réservé le droit de publier les détails et le correctif plus tôt que prévu.
Node.js, l’outil qui fait tourner du JavaScript sur les serveurs web, publie lui aussi des correctifs de sécurité ce mercredi, pour ses versions 22, 24 et 26. Aucun lien n’a été établi entre les deux alertes. Node.js avait programmé ces mises à jour dès la semaine dernière, et sa faille la plus grave est classée « élevée », un cran sous « critique ».
Le correctif de PHP est attendu à 16 heures, heure de Paris, avec le détail des deux failles et la liste des versions touchées. Les abonnés Free peuvent déjà souffler, leur Freebox n’est pas concernée.

articles.title: Cuándo se debería automatizar con bots el servicio al cliente y cuándo debe hablar un ser humano
articles.text:
La inteligencia artificial (IA) en la atención al cliente ya forma parte de sectores tan diversos como la banca, las telecomunicaciones, el comercio y los servicios públicos.
Los bots de voz y texto pueden responder consultas, identificar datos de una cuenta, resumir conversaciones y derivar pedidos. Aun así, la expansión de estas herramientas no elimina la necesidad de una persona al otro lado de la línea.
La decisión ya no pasa por elegir entre automatización o atención humana, sino por asignar cada instancia al recurso adecuado. Las consultas repetitivas pueden resolverse con rapidez mediante sistemas automatizados; los casos complejos, sensibles o de alto impacto requieren escucha, criterio y capacidad de decisión. El desafío consiste en transferir la conversación a tiempo y sin obligar al cliente a repetir su historia.
Qué consultas conviene automatizar con un bot de IA
Los asistentes de IA resultan útiles para gestiones simples y previsibles: consultar un saldo, verificar el estado de un trámite, actualizar datos, enviar una factura o responder preguntas frecuentes.
Durante el Tech Day 2026 de BPrO, Diana Lemus, Regional Sales Director de Five9, ubicó entre esos usos la guía inteligente, las transcripciones, los resúmenes de llamadas, el control de calidad automático y la predicción de demanda.
“La tecnología amplifica el talento, no lo sustituye”, sostuvo Lemus. Su visión apunta a que los sistemas asuman tareas administrativas y de clasificación para que los agentes dediquen más tiempo a resolver problemas que necesitan contexto.
Cómo puede una IA detectar qué necesita el cliente
En una llamada entrante, el primer objetivo es identificar el motivo del contacto sin llevar al usuario por largos menús de opciones. Sergio Antolínez, AI Product Owner de Ipcom, dijo que el sistema debe aprovechar los datos disponibles y, luego, escuchar. “Tenemos que saber qué necesita el usuario, saber por qué me está llamando”.
Esa interpretación incluye palabras, frases y confirmaciones breves. Un “sí”, “claro” o “ajá” puede validar una información; una frase como “me cobraron dos veces” revela una posible incidencia de facturación.
Para Antolínez, el bot debe presentar el contexto que ya posee, orientar la conversación con una pregunta y adaptar el recorrido según la intención detectada. El objetivo es evitar que el usuario navegue por un árbol de opciones que no responde a su necesidad.
Cuándo debe la IA transferir la llamada a un humano
La derivación debe activarse ante situaciones complejas, de riesgo financiero, con excepciones no documentadas o con señales de vulnerabilidad.
En esos casos, el bot puede considerar atributos de la conversación para elegir al asesor más adecuado. No siempre debe recibir el caso quien está disponible antes: puede requerirse un agente con mayor capacidad de empatía o experiencia.
Además, la transferencia es necesaria cuando aparecen emociones, cansancio, incertidumbre o decisiones que exceden una respuesta predefinida. Lemus señaló: la IA puede clasificar, sugerir y acelerar; el agente humano debe “escuchar, resolver, dar confianza, construir decisiones con contexto humano y crear conexión genuina”.
Por qué el trabajo de la IA es clave para la asesoría del humano
Derivar una llamada no debería equivaler a reiniciar el proceso. Si el bot ya validó la identidad, identificó el motivo del contacto y recogió antecedentes, esa información debe llegar al asesor. De lo contrario, el cliente enfrenta una segunda entrevista para explicar lo que ya dijo, una de las causas más frecuentes de frustración en la atención telefónica.
Antolínez advirtió que repetir validaciones y preguntas “daña totalmente la experiencia y la interacción”. La integración entre canales, bases de datos y sistemas de gestión de clientes permite que el asesor continúe desde el punto en que falló la automatización.
La IA debe ceder la conversación con un resumen claro, los datos verificados y la intención detectada. Así, la persona asume el caso con elementos para resolverlo, no para reconstruirlo.

articles.title: Cops raid office of RFK Jr. allies planning “unethical” vaccine trial on babies
articles.text:
Police in Guinea-Bissau raided the offices of Danish researchers on Monday, seizing doses of hepatitis B vaccine intended for a vaccine trial for newborns. International health experts have called the trial “unethical,” but anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has attempted to fund it with US taxpayer dollars.
Under Kennedy, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention announced in December that it had awarded the Danish researchers—led by married couple Peter Aaby and Christine Stabell Benn of Bandim Health Project—an unsolicited $1.6 million grant to run the trial. Aaby and Stabell Benn are controversial vaccine researchers who claim vaccines cause overlooked harms. They have been repeatedly praised by Kennedy but are currently under investigation by Danish authorities for alleged scientific misconduct.
Plans for the trial were halted in January as widespread condemnation erupted over the trial’s design, which would potentially expose thousands of newborns in the country to hepatitis B, risking a lifelong infection that can lead to liver cirrhosis, cancer, and premature death. Outrage flared again after a Rolling Stone story earlier this month claimed the CDC set aside another $1.6 million in funding in late September and planned to move forward with the trial.

articles.title: Une recharge en 5 minutes pour 10 000 € : BYD dévoile sa nouvelle Seagull en Chine
articles.text:
BYD a lancé ce mardi 20 octobre en Chine la deuxième génération de la Seagull, sa voiture électrique la moins chère. La présentation s’est tenue sur le circuit de Zhengzhou, dans la province du Henan. Comme cela était attendu depuis cet été, la nouvelle génération grandit. Elle mesure 4,21 m de long, soit 42,5 cm de plus qu’avant, ce qui la rapproche de la Dolphin, la compacte de la marque. Elle passe de quatre à cinq places, gagne un coffre avant de 94 litres et devient une propulsion. Enfin, sa puissance grimpe à 115 ou 129 ch selon les versions, contre 75 ch auparavant.
Pour mémoire, la Seagull pèse lourd chez BYD, avec environ 1,55 million d’exemplaires vendus depuis avril 2023. Ses ventes s’essoufflent pourtant. D’après les chiffres compilés par CnEVPost, elles ont reculé de 33 % sur les neuf premiers mois de 2026, à 265 901 unités. Sur toute l’année 2025, BYD en avait écoulé 529 537.
Des prix hallucinants en Chine pour la BYD Seagull
Le prix d’appel est en baisse comparé à la génération précédente : 65 900 yuans, soit environ 8 800 €, contre 69 900 yuans, environ 9 300 €. Surtout, la nouveauté phare de la citadine est l’arrivée de la technologie Flash Charging, qui promet de passer de 10 à 70 % de batterie en seulement cinq minutes. Pour l’avoir, il faut toutefois viser les versions à partir de 75 900 yuans, l’équivalent de 10 100 €.
| Caractéristique | Vitality | Freedom | Comfort | Flying | Smart | 
| Puissance | 116 ch | 116 ch | 129 ch | 129 ch | 129 ch | 
| Batterie | 30,1 kWh | 30,1 kWh | 39,2 kWh | 39,2 kWh | 39,2 kWh | 
| Autonomie (CLTC) | 320 km | 320 km | 420 km | 420 km | 420 km | 
| Recharge Flash | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | 
| Prix* | 8 800 € | 9 700 € | 10 100 € | 11 100 € | 13 300 € | 
*Prix en yuans converti à l’euro actuel
Quand les deux premières versions se contentent de 30,1 kWh et n’ont pas droit à la recharge Flash, les trois modèles les plus huppés adoptent un accumulateur de 39,2 kWh cette fois compatible avec la recharge ultra-rapide.
Attention aussi aux autonomies, mesurées selon le cycle chinois CLTC, plus généreux que la norme européenne WLTP. En convertissant, on se retrouverait avec des autonomies respectives d’environ 262 km et 344 km. Des valeurs comparables à la Renault Twingo E-Tech ou une Citroën ë-C3… pour un prix près de 10 000 € moins cher.
La recharge en cinq minutes a ses conditions
Zhang Zhuo, directeur commercial du réseau BYD, a indiqué que la marque comptait 12 165 stations Flash le jour du lancement, et en vise 20 000 d’ici à la fin de l’année. Début octobre, ces bornes ont d’ailleurs fait parler d’elles quand des enfants ont été filmés en train de se balancer à leurs câbles à Nanning. Pour convaincre, BYD offre un an de recharge Flash gratuite aux particuliers qui achètent l’une des trois versions compatibles.
Dans le cas de la nouvelle Seagull, pour passer de 10 à 70 % sur la batterie de 39,2 kWh, il faut y faire entrer environ 23,5 kWh en cinq minutes, soit une puissance moyenne d’environ 280 kW. Du jamais vu sur une citadine.
Pas chère et bien équipée, la BYD Seagull
D’après le dossier d’homologation déposé auprès du ministère chinois de l’Industrie (MIIT), la batterie LFP vient de FinDreams, la filiale batteries de BYD. Cette chimie lithium-fer-phosphate coûte moins cher, car elle se passe de nickel et de cobalt. Le moteur, lui, sort de l’usine BYD de Zhengzhou.
En revanche, la marque n’a pas rogné sur l’équipement. On trouve un écran central de 15,6 pouces avec l’IA chinoise DeepSeek, des sièges avant chauffants et ventilés, et un massage pour le conducteur. Les versions hautes peuvent recevoir un lidar, un capteur laser posé sur le toit qui cartographie les alentours, pour une aide à la conduite en ville et sur autoroute.
Les commandes sont ouvertes sur le site chinois de BYD. La marque n’a pas dit si cette deuxième génération arrivera en Europe, où la première est vendue sous le nom de Dolphin Surf. En France, le modèle vient justement de gagner une cinquième place et les services Google.

articles.title: Cette fois, le satellite russe Kosmos 2612 s’approche à 500 mètres d’un satellite américain en orbite
articles.text:
Le satellite militaire russe Kosmos 2612 a passé cinq jours à tourner autour d'un satellite radar américain que l'armée ukrainienne utiliserait pour son renseignement. Au plus près, les deux engins n'étaient plus qu'à 500 mètres l'un de l'autre d'après LeoLabs, et d'autres observateurs parlent de quelques dizaines de mètres.
Nous avons laissé Kosmos 2612 à 5 kilomètres d'ICEYE-X36, le 16 octobre. L'engin russe a continué à manœuvrer jusqu'au 19, en passant tour à tour devant et derrière le satellite radar, selon LeoLabs. Cette entreprise américaine suit les objets en orbite basse grâce à un réseau de radars au sol. « C'est l'approche non coopérative la plus avancée et potentiellement la plus dangereuse que nous ayons observée », a déclaré Adam Marsh, vice-président de LeoLabs. Jamais un satellite n'avait approché ainsi un autre satellite actif en orbite basse sans l'accord de son propriétaire, d'après l'astrophysicien Jonathan McDowell. Les spécialistes ne sont pas d'accord sur la distance minimale, et une panne d'ICEYE-X36 serait presque impossible à imputer à Moscou.
Une distance impossible à mesurer au mètre près
Les spécialistes cités par l'AFP évoquent moins d'une centaine de mètres au matin du 18 octobre, et le média ukrainien Militarnyi 26 mètres. Marco Langbroek enseigne la surveillance optique de l'espace à l'université de technologie de Delft, aux Pays-Bas, et suit Kosmos 2612 depuis le printemps. Il a mis en garde contre ces valeurs trop précises, dans un message publié sur X. « Des valeurs comme "26 mètres" citées par certains ont très peu de valeur réelle », a-t-il écrit.
Les observateurs indépendants calculent la position des satellites à partir d'éléments orbitaux publics, diffusés par l'armée américaine. Pour le chercheur, la marge d'erreur de ces calculs est nettement supérieure à 26 mètres. Si un satellite allume son moteur entre deux mises à jour, la position calculée est fausse, et Kosmos 2612 a justement multiplié les petites poussées autour du moment où il s'est le plus approché. Les équipes de LeoLabs ont relevé ces corrections de trajectoire répétées pendant toute l'opération, car l'engin russe cherchait à rester près du satellite radar au lieu de le croiser une seule fois.
Dans les calculs de Marco Langbroek, l'orbite d'ICEYE-X36 n'a pas bougé. Aucune collision n'est donc visible dans ces données, mais seuls les utilisateurs du satellite radar peuvent dire s'il fonctionne toujours.
Washington muet sur un satellite lancé depuis la Californie
ICEYE est née en Finlande, mais ICEYE-X36 est exploité par sa filiale américaine, ICEYE US, et a décollé en mars 2024 de la base de Vandenberg, en Californie. Les États-Unis sont donc l'État de lancement du satellite au sens du droit spatial, rappelle Victoria Samson, directrice de la sécurité spatiale à la Secure World Foundation. Marco Langbroek ajoute que des Ukrainiens pourraient aujourd'hui posséder ou louer l'engin. ICEYE a élargi en janvier sa coopération avec le ministère ukrainien de la Défense, sans jamais dire quels satellites travaillent pour Kiev. Si ICEYE-X36 tombait en panne, la coïncidence serait très suspecte, mais il serait difficile de prouver la responsabilité de Kosmos 2612, prévient le chercheur néerlandais.
Les manœuvres de mai, quand plusieurs satellites lancés avec Kosmos 2612 ont rejoint le plan orbital d'ICEYE-X36, sont mentionnées dans un document de la Force spatiale américaine sur les menaces spatiales. Le secrétaire de l'US Air Force, Troy Meink, a reconnu en septembre que les États-Unis disposaient d'armes de contrôle spatial en orbite pour défendre leurs intérêts. Aucun responsable américain n'a en revanche commenté la poursuite d'ICEYE-X36, et Victoria Samson ne comprend pas ce silence. « Je me demande pourquoi le gouvernement américain est resté silencieux sur cette affaire », a-t-elle confié.
Le CSIS est un centre de réflexion américain consacré aux relations internationales. Clayton Swope, directeur adjoint de son programme de sécurité aérospatiale, a appelé les États-Unis et l'Europe à décider dès maintenant de leur réponse si Moscou attaquait un satellite occidental. Comme le rapporte l'AFP, il a précisé qu'il était impossible de confirmer la présence d'une arme à bord de Kosmos 2612.
L'engin russe a ensuite pris ses distances, jusqu'à une centaine de kilomètres d'ICEYE-X36 d'après Jonathan McDowell. Marco Langbroek a repéré une nouvelle manœuvre de Kosmos 2612 le 18 octobre, et il n'exclut pas qu'elle prépare un nouveau rapprochement.

articles.title: ‘You are all born artists’: Prakash Belawadi on surviving the AI age
articles.text:
‘You are all born artists’: Prakash Belawadi on surviving the AI age
At TechSparks 2026, actor and theatre artist Prakash Belawadi reflected on AI’s impact on creativity and jobs, urging people to reconnect with their inner artist and find purpose beyond what technology can replace.
Actor-theatre artist Prakash Belawadi began his session at TechSparks 2026 with a simple question: “Any artists out there?”
He went on to answer his own question with a profound reflection: “This is a trick question. You are all born artists. But the formal education system and corporate life crushed the artist in you. Reconnect with the artist in you; it will help you survive in this AI age,” he said.
Belawadi spoke on “The last human advantage: What AI cannot replace”, discussing how technology is changing creativity, work, culture, and public life.
Responding to a question about whether AI challenges artists and whether they need to upskill to remain relevant, Belawadi distinguished between art created for personal fulfilment and art produced for commercial or practical purposes.
To illustrate his point, Belawadi asked how many people in the room had tried writing poetry. While few had identified themselves as artists, several hands went up in response to the question about poetry.
“Why would you want to write poetry? You don’t think you’re going to make money out of it. You don’t think it’s going to be a career. Why did you try to write?” he asked.
For Belawadi, the answer lies in the impulse to create something for oneself, without necessarily seeking commercial value or external validation. In such cases, he argued, AI isn't a challenge because the act of creation is the point.
“You write it because you felt like it. You don’t take AI’s help to write poetry,” he added.
However, the equation changes when creativity becomes a professional assignment with a deadline and a specific outcome. For instance, a lyricist tasked with writing a song within four hours could use AI to generate lyrics based on the scene's characters, setting, language, and context.
In these cases, AI becomes a tool for accomplishing a defined objective. As more people turn to it for similar tasks, competition for artists intensifies.
“If you want to do something with art that is useful, I think AI is more than a challenge. We’ll have to look for another occupation, I would say,” Belawadi said.
He acknowledged that actors could also be replaced in certain roles as the technology advances.
“For me as an actor, for instance, at the present level of AI, I can give my persona and charge royalty only for my persona. You can make a non-fungible token of my persona, then just lend it, and AI will do the rest. I don’t need to go to shoot, for instance. I can be replaced,” he said.
Belawadi believes AI cannot easily reproduce a dimension of human experience: the ability to respond to the world through lived experience.
While AI may replicate an actor's appearance and deliver a convincing performance, he believes replacing a person in a conventional screen role could be far easier than replicating the complexity of an individual shaped by lived experience.
“But if you are doing a hero role in a movie, it’s very easy to replace, I think,” he said.
Belawadi pointed out that young people today face a difficult double whammy: climate change and a slew of new technologies.
“There’s a third that’s related to both: you will need two and a half times more energy than you need now when AI is fully deployed, and that is going to make climate change worse. And the new technologies won’t give you jobs.”
Belawadi did not argue for holding back the technology. Asked which human skills beat AI, he turned the question around. “AI can replace many things humans are doing. The question is: what are you doing? Do you need to do that? What are you doing, and why are you doing it?”
He then offered a list of things he thinks AI could take over. It included:
- Courts: With around 54 million cases pending, he said AI could begin deciding them within seconds. Human judges could retain appeals.
- Primary health care: Diagnosis and minor procedures at village clinics, with remote guidance for complex surgery, delivered “without prejudice” of caste, gender, skin colour or geography.
- Elections: If people trust their phones with payments, he asked, why not trust an OTP with a vote?
- Accounting: He had told his daughter, a chartered accountant, that she was already out of a job.
- Traffic: He suggested a million driverless vehicles for Bengaluru would give the city back its streets.
Belawadi urged AI developers to use their skills to improve the lives of people around them, arguing that building ethical AI requires a sense of responsibility towards one's community.
“If you are building ethical AI, I think you need to rebel and make a better India. There is no other country that is as good for you as India is, if you have self-respect,” he said.
Emphasising that this responsibility begins with the people in one's immediate surroundings, he added, “When I say India, I don't mean you talk for 1.5 billion people. I'm saying you talk for yourself: whether you can be useful and make lives better for the people around you.”
He cautioned that developers who fail to bring this sense of purpose to their work risk being made redundant by the very technology they create. “Otherwise, I'll talk to AI. I may not need you, I'm saying,” he said.

articles.title: Stocker le surplus solaire pour l’utiliser plus tard : le kit Zendure SolarFlow 2400 AC est à 959 €
articles.text:
Le kit Zendure SolarFlow 2400 AC avec batterie de 2,88 kWh est à 959 € (-20 %)
Le kit Zendure SolarFlow 2400 AC associe un module de conversion à une batterie AB3000X de 2,88 kWh pour stocker l’électricité et la restituer selon les besoins.
Amazon propose le kit Zendure SolarFlow 2400 AC avec une batterie AB3000X à 959 €, contre un prix conseillé de 1 199 €. L’économie atteint 240 €, soit environ 20 %. Le prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours est également indiqué à 1 199 €. L’ensemble est vendu et expédié par Zendure_Europe, avec une livraison annoncée entre le 3 et le 6 novembre.
Une batterie de 2,88 kWh pour compléter une installation solaire
Le système de stockage domestique Zendure SolarFlow 2400 AC fonctionne en couplage AC, sur le réseau électrique du logement. Il permet de récupérer le surplus d’une installation photovoltaïque existante pour le restituer ultérieurement. Les panneaux solaires ne se branchent donc pas directement sur ce module.
La batterie AB3000X incluse offre une capacité de 2,88 kWh. Le système accepte jusqu’à six batteries compatibles, vendues séparément, pour atteindre 17,28 kWh. Cette dernière valeur correspond à la capacité maximale après extension, et non au stockage fourni dans ce pack.
Une gestion connectée avec un compteur compatible
Le SolarFlow 2400 AC prend en charge une puissance bidirectionnelle pouvant atteindre 2 400 W selon la configuration. L’application Zendure permet de suivre son fonctionnement et de gérer les périodes de charge et de décharge. Il peut également stocker de l’électricité du réseau pendant les périodes à tarif réduit.
Pour adapter automatiquement les échanges à la consommation du logement, un compteur intelligent compatible est nécessaire. Cet accessoire n’est pas indiqué dans le contenu du pack : il faut le prévoir séparément si l’installation n’en possède pas déjà un. Une sortie dédiée permet aussi d’alimenter des appareils directement raccordés en cas de coupure, après activation de cette fonction dans l’application.

articles.title: De nombreux HomePod victimes d'un bug fantôme : Apple corrige enfin le tir, mais n'assume pas
articles.text:
Il y a quelques années, certains HomePod se sont mis à dérailler. Sur les réseaux sociaux et sur les forums d’Apple, on trouve des milliers de témoignages de personnes dont l’enceinte s’est tout à coup mise à faire n’importe quoi. Concrètement, la musique démarre seule en pleine nuit, Siri s’active sans raison, le volume grimpe d’un coup. Le phénomène a été baptisé « ghost touch », ou toucher fantôme, par les victimes. Celui-ci survient lorsque la surface tactile située sur le dessus de l’enceinte enregistre des pressions qui n’existent pas, comme si un fantôme appuyait dessus pour vous tourmenter.
Un bug récalcitrant sur de nombreux HomePod
On a rencontré le problème il y a un peu plus d’un an sur notre HomePod mini, acheté dans le sillage de la sortie en 2020. L’enceinte a plusieurs fois lancé des playlists sur Apple Music au beau milieu de la nuit et s’est mise à répondre à des demandes qui n’existent pas. Dans les cas les plus graves, le HomePod est persuadé qu’on appuie en permanence sur la surface tactile. De facto, il finit par entrer dans une boucle de redémarrage. Le voyant rouge est impossible à éteindre. L’enceinte devient alors inutilisable. La défaillance touche surtout le HomePod mini et le HomePod 2. Il s’agit d’un problème au niveau du matériel.
Pendant des années, Apple n’a jamais reconnu officiellement le problème, pourtant massivement épinglé par ses clients. Les utilisateurs devaient se débrouiller tout seuls pour trouver une solution. Sur Reddit, on a trouvé plusieurs témoignages qui recommandent de modifier les réglages d’accessibilité de l’enceinte. L’un des réglages d’accessibilité impose en effet d’appuyer plusieurs secondes pour valider une commande sur la zone tactile. L’opération doit théoriquement empêcher le bug fantôme de se produire. Sans succès de notre côté. Parfois, il s’écoulait néanmoins plusieurs heures ou plusieurs jours avant que le HomePod ne recommence à devenir fou. Pour tenter de corriger le tir, on a aussi plusieurs fois réinitialisé l’enceinte. Là encore, cela n’a servi à rien.
Une deuxième option, bien plus radicale, est aussi apparue sur la toile. Elle consiste à ouvrir l’enceinte pour débrancher physiquement les connecteurs de la surface tactile. De facto, la zone n’est plus utilisable. Il faut impérativement passer par Siri pour la moindre commande. Ayant deux mains gauches, et aucune patience, nous avons renoncé. On a fini par débrancher l’accessoire et à le glisser dans un tiroir, dans l’espoir qu’Apple trouve un beau jour une solution.
À lire aussi : Apple dévoile le HomePod mini 2 : voici ce qui change
Un correctif qui ne s’assume pas
Bonne nouvelle, Apple s’est enfin penché sur le problème. Le géant de Cupertino vient en effet de déployer la mise à jour iOS 27.2 sur tous les HomePod, y compris les premiers modèles commercialisés il y a huit ans et sur le tout nouveau HomePod mini 2. Attention, il s’agit de la version release candidate, soit une itération presque définitive de la mise à jour. La version finale ne devrait pas tarder. Elle est attendue avant la fin du mois.
La mise à jour ajoute une fonctionnalité intitulée « Verrouiller les commandes » dans l’application Maison. Disponible sur tous les HomePod, ce réglage va tout simplement désactiver tout le pavé tactile du HomePod mini. Le toucher, le toucher prolongé qui appelle Siri et le réglage du volume seront totalement hors service. Évidemment, le capteur restera défectueux, mais il ne déclenche plus rien tout seul, ce qui permet de se servir à nouveau de l’enceinte. Toutes les autres fonctionnalités continuent de fonctionner normalement.
Officiellement, Apple ne présente pas cette option comme un correctif du bug des touches fantômes. Pour le moment, Apple ne reconnaît pas de défaut matériel sur ses enceintes. La mise à jour ne signifie pas que la marque reconnaît une défaillance massive. Apple présente plutôt le réglage comme une nouvelle option pour les parents de jeunes enfants ou les propriétaires de chats. Elle vise à éviter que les bambins ou les chats appuient sur la surface tactile du HomePod. De notre point de vue, elle rend surtout la vie à un appareil qui prenait la poussière, et qu’on avait presque condamné.

articles.title: ChatGPT activa PIN o huella digital en los chats para evitar que tu pareja o amigos los vean
articles.text:
OpenAI anunció que los usuarios de ChatGPT ya pueden bloquear conversaciones individuales con un PIN de cuatro dígitos, Face ID o Touch ID, para evitar que otra persona las vea al tomar prestado el teléfono o la computadora.
La función, llamada Locked Chats, mueve cada conversación protegida a una sección separada del historial regular, de los chats fijados y de los resultados de búsqueda dentro de la aplicación. Según la empresa, está pensada para quien habla de temas personales o planea una sorpresa y no quiere exponer esa charla al mostrarle otra cosa a un familiar o amigo.
A diferencia de los Chats Temporales, que generan una sesión aparte que desaparece y no queda guardada en el historial, los chats bloqueados se conservan y pueden volver a abrirse en cualquier momento con la misma autenticación.
OpenAI aclaró que bloquear un chat no equivale a cifrarlo de punta a punta ni crea una bóveda encriptada aparte. Tampoco cambia cuánto tiempo la empresa conserva esa conversación, ni borra la información que ChatGPT ya había incorporado a su memoria antes de activar el bloqueo.
La compañía explicó además que la opción no modifica la configuración de “mejorar el modelo para todos”, con la que algunos usuarios autorizan que sus conversaciones se usen para entrenar el sistema.
Cómo funciona la memoria en los chats bloqueados
Cuando la función de memoria está activada, los chats bloqueados comparten entre sí un registro propio, separado del que usa el resto de la cuenta. Los mensajes nuevos que se envían dentro de esa sección pueden actualizar esa memoria interna, pero no se filtran hacia las conversaciones comunes.
OpenAI también advirtió que restablecer el PIN borra de forma permanente todos los chats bloqueados, junto con los archivos y el resto del contenido que estaban protegidos bajo ese código anterior.
La función no está disponible para los Chats Temporales, los chats archivados, las conversaciones grupales, los chats creados a partir de un enlace compartido, los que tienen tareas programadas ni los que incluyen grabaciones de reuniones.
Locked Chats comenzó a desplegarse este martes para las cuentas Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise y Edu. OpenAI precisó que, por ahora, no llegará a ChatGPT for Healthcare, la versión pensada para el sector salud.
Una función de privacidad para un producto masivo
ChatGPT superó los 1.000 millones de usuarios activos por semana, según la propia OpenAI, una escala que convirtió al chatbot en una herramienta donde millones de personas comparten información médica, laboral o económica junto con consultas cotidianas.
Esa masividad explica por qué otras plataformas de inteligencia artificial conversacional enfrentaron esta misma semana cuestionamientos de privacidad: The Verge reportó que Meta pausó la posibilidad de compartir conversaciones de su asistente Muse después de que investigadores encontraran chats privados accesibles en internet.
Por el momento, OpenAI no detalló si prevé extender alguna variante de Locked Chats a sus herramientas empresariales ni si planea sumar cifrado de punta a punta en el futuro. El despliegue sigue en curso y, según la compañía, podría tardar días en llegar a todos los usuarios de las cuentas habilitadas.

articles.title: Microsoft says October updates didn’t actually fix VPN issues
articles.text:
Microsoft says it mistakenly flagged a bug causing Always On VPN connection issues as fixed in the October 2026 Windows 11 cumulative updates.
Always On VPN replaced the legacy DirectAccess technology and supports domain-joined, non-domain-joined, and Microsoft Entra ID–joined devices running Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server.
It runs in the background and establishes secure tunnels back to the user's corporate network whenever their device connects to the internet.
Microsoft first acknowledged the issue in a service alert sent to IT administrators in late September, saying it was triggered on systems running Windows 11 24H2 and later after installing the September 2026 security updates when the initial Always On VPN connection failed (e.g., when using automatic protocol selection with IKEv2 and SSTP).
"When automatic protocol selection or protocol fallback was configured, affected VPN connections could remain stuck in a Connecting state or fail to connect after an initial connection attempt failed," it said. "In some cases, subsequent connection attempts could display the error, 'The specified port is already in use.'"
Mistakenly marked as resolved
After releasing the October 2026 Patch Tuesday Windows 11 cumulative updates, Microsoft marked the bug as resolved, but in a Tuesday update it said the issues weren't actually addressed and that a fix would ship later.
"This disclosure was mistakenly updated to Resolved status on October 13, 2026. We have returned its status to Mitigated," it said in a service alert sent to IT admins. "A resolution for this issue is planned to be included in an update to be released in the coming weeks. We apologize for any inconvenience or confusion."
While Microsoft continues working on a permanent solution, it shared a temporary fix that requires affected customers to choose one of two VPN tunneling protocols to work around the issue.
"IT administrators can mitigate this issue by changing the Always On VPN profile from automatic protocol selection to a single protocol, either SSTP only or IKEv2 only, depending on their environment and configuration," it said. "Organizations should select the protocol based on their environment, security, and deployment requirements."
The September cumulative updates have been linked to multiple other problems affecting both home and enterprise Windows users. Days after last month's Patch Tuesday, Microsoft released emergency out-of-band updates to fix Hyper-V issues, Remote Desktop Services failures, and USB audio problems.
It also shared a temporary workaround for an issue that blocked some Windows 11 users from logging in with valid domain credentials and announced that it is working to address another bug that broke the Windows built-in File History backup feature.

Mise à jour à 14H00 : le réseau Orange est en panne depuis 2 heures et 40 minutes. L’opérateur a indiqué travailler à la résolution du problème, mais n’a toujours pas indiqué d’explications. Une panne de cette longueur est assez rare.
En quelques minutes, ils étaient plusieurs milliers à signaler une panne complète de réseau chez Orange et Sosh. L’origine des signalements est datée de mercredi 21 octobre autour de 11h20. On ne connaît pas l’origine de la panne pour le moment.

Je voulais sortir faire des courses mais je n’ai aucun moyen d’être joignable si je m’enlève de la wifi ? » écrit Georgia Sarah.
Orange vient de poster un message sur son compte X où il confirme qu’il y a bien un problème technique. L’opérateur évoque des perturbations sur le réseau mobile.

articles.title: “We are not forking TypeScript”: Cloudflare spearheads Rust port written by agents, for agents
articles.text:
“We are not forking TypeScript”: Cloudflare spearheads Rust port written by agents, for agents
Cloudflare is going all-out to ensure that AI coding agents can check their work without exhausting available computing resources, leading a new effort to bring Microsoft’s TypeScript compiler to Rust.
But whatever you do, don’t call it a fork.
Taking to X, Cloudflare’s director of engineering Christoph Nakazawa confirmed that the company is taking ownership of tsrs, a Rust port of TypeScript that it claims is up to eight times faster, and uses 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0.
Microsoft’s own TypeScript compiler is reaping the benefits, too, with the teams sharing optimizations as they work to keep the two implementations in sync.
“We are not forking TypeScript — we are working with the TypeScript team and as a result 7.1 is already ~2.5x faster, too,” Nakazawa writes.
That “port vs fork” message runs throughout the accompanying blog post, co-authored by Nakazawa and fellow Cloudflare engineers Boshen Chen and Dimitri Mitropoulos, who go to great lengths to explain that they very much see TypeScript as Microsoft’s to continue steering.
“To be clear, we are not forking TypeScript. We believe the TypeScript team should remain in full control of the language’s design and direction.”
“To be clear, we are not forking TypeScript,” they write. “We believe the TypeScript team should remain in full control of the language’s design and direction. They have maintained a long-term vision while guiding TypeScript’s adoption across the JavaScript community. We do not want to change that.”
Why Rust, when Microsoft already has Go?
Developed and released by Microsoft back in 2012, TypeScript extends JavaScript with a type system that helps developers catch errors before their applications run. However, checking those types can consume considerable computing resources, particularly in large projects where multiple AI agents may be writing and validating code simultaneously.
Microsoft addressed some of those performance problems in July with TypeScript 7.0, replacing its JavaScript-based compiler with one written in Go and delivering roughly tenfold speed improvements.
As The New Stack previously reported, Microsoft had considered Rust for the rewrite, but concluded that reproducing TypeScript’s existing architecture in Rust would introduce significant complications around memory management and compatibility.
The performance gains reported for tsrs make for an interesting comparison with Microsoft’s own Go implementation. Commenting in a Hacker News discussion about the Rust port, Daniel Rosenwasser, Microsoft’s principal product manager for TypeScript, notes that “a lot of the speed does not just come down to language choice,” adding that “some of what is going to make TS 7.1 faster and leaner… actually comes from optimizations discovered in tsrs.”
“Some of what is going to make TS 7.1 faster and leaner… actually comes from optimizations discovered in tsrs.”
Separately, Rosenwasser announced TypeScript 7.1 beta earlier today, detailing substantial speed and memory optimizations.
Cloudflare, for its part, sees another opportunity in Rust, particularly its compatibility with WebAssembly (Wasm). Go can compile to Wasm, but it has to bring its garbage collector along. Rust offers more direct control over memory, reducing the overhead of running development tools in resource-constrained environments. For Cloudflare, that could make it easier to run complete development environments inside browsers and isolated Workers sandboxes, where AI agents can write, check, and build applications.
The move also fits into Cloudflare’s growing JavaScript ecosystem. As The New Stack reported last week, the company has been assembling an extensive collection of JavaScript tools and expertise, including through its acquisition of VoidZero in June and the recent release of Void, an open-source platform for deploying and managing AI-built applications.
With that in mind, it’s the Cloudflare and VoidZero teams who are are now developing tsrs as part of Oxc, VoidZero’s Rust-based JavaScript toolchain, with plans to integrate it into other developer tools.
Owner and operator: A tsrs origin story
It’s worth noting that the tsrs project began just last month at restaurant software company Owner.com, where head of AI developer experience Max Schwenk says he faced a 37,000-file TypeScript backend. Writing in a blog post published on Monday, he notes that Microsoft’s Go compiler consumed 19 GiB of memory and took 80 seconds for a single-threaded check, restricting how many coding agents could work concurrently.
With multiple agents generating code simultaneously, the resource demands made it difficult for each to check its changes independently, forcing Owner.com to experiment with cloud-based development environments and other compromises.
“For a coding agent to be maximally productive, it needs to be able to validate its work in the tightest possible loop,” Schwenk writes.
After running into limits while trying to improve the Go compiler’s memory usage, Schwenk tried something somewhat more ambitious: use Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 to recreate the compiler in Rust. He would direct the experiment and evaluate the results, leaving the implementation entirely to AI agents.
“I wrote zero code,” Schwenk writes. “Not ‘barely any’. Zero.”
“I wrote zero code. Not ‘barely any’. Zero.”
And the results came remarkably quickly. Schwenk says he deployed more than 20 AI subagents in parallel, waking the following morning to a functioning typechecker. Further optimizations brought Owner.com’s typechecking time down to roughly seven seconds in CI, and across more than a dozen public projects, Schwenk reports tsrs running 2.5 to five times faster than Microsoft’s newer Go compiler nightly, while using about a third as much memory.
Agentic rewrites in Rust
In truth, the tsrs project is just the latest example of AI agents being enlisted for substantial Rust migrations. As The New Stack reported last month, GitHub used its own Copilot agents to rewrite its coding-agent runtime in Rust, while Anthropic had previously used Claude agents to help migrate its Bun JavaScript runtime from Zig to Rust.
Elsewhere, Meta has also used AI to help port the React Compiler to Rust, while in September OpenAI revealed two engineers used Codex and GPT-5.5 to rebuild its Habitat storage service in Rust.
But such rapid, AI-assisted rewrites raise questions about how developers verify that the resulting software behaves as intended. For a TypeScript compiler, that means ensuring it catches the same errors as Microsoft’s implementation. Schwenk says the project uses TypeScript’s conformance tests, deliberately introduces errors into real projects and runs Miri, a tool for detecting memory-safety problems in Rust. Those checks have already uncovered a memory bug that appeared only in an optimized build.
“A faster compiler that finds fewer errors is a broken compiler with good marketing.”
“A faster compiler that finds fewer errors is a broken compiler with good marketing,” Schwenk writes.
Maintaining compatibility, it’s fair to say, will be an ongoing challenge. Cloudflare plans to borrow the AI-assisted approach behind Vinext, its Vite-based reimplementation of the Next.js web framework, where agents monitor Next.js for changes, run compatibility tests, and propose fixes when differences emerge. Some discrepancies remain in tsrs, including the order in which diagnostic messages are displayed.
“We will apply the same process to TypeScript, taking extreme care that we don’t introduce diverging behaviors from upstream TypeScript,” the Cloudflare authors write.

articles.title: Article Series: Agentic AI Architecture
articles.text:
The IT industry is changing before our very eyes. With AI entering the software architecture and development landscape, whether we like it or not, we are set to be taken on a roller coaster, the likes of which we haven’t seen since the advent of microservices and cloud-native computing. If the last decade was spent mostly on mastering and optimizing the cloud and micro- or nano-scale service-oriented architecture, the next decade will likely be spent figuring out how to master AI for building a new generation of IT systems.
These new systems will harness the power of AI in ways that, even today, are perhaps not fully comprehensible, as this space is moving forward at a neck-breaking pace, and last year’s best practice is this year’s antipattern. This rapid pace of innovation comes with many challenges, but can also be exciting for those willing to join the ride.
In this series, we try to establish agentic AI architecture as a new type of software architecture that will likely dominate the industry for years to come. The articles, written by industry experts, cover various elements and aspects of agentic AI architecture. We aim to present the latest trends and developments shaping the new type of architecture as it enters the mainstream.
While it’s impossible to characterize the new type of software architecture fully at this point, we hope this series offers useful insights into how the agentic AI space will shape the future of the IT industry in the coming years. Agentic AI Architecture is still in its infancy, but we hope to track how it evolves and matures and cover all key milestones and breakthroughs in the future.
You can download the entire series collated in PDF format, in the associated eMag.
Series Contents
From Microservice to Agents: The Next Evolution of Distributed Systems
This article discusses the shift in distributed systems architecture, driven by large language models (LLMs) and reasoning systems. Mallika Rao argues that agentic AI architectures focus on decomposing decisions, much like microservice architectures decompose functionality. Additionally, the author shares initial architectural patterns and failure modes introduced by the new paradigm, highlighting the increased importance of observability and reliability in these new types of agentic systems.
The Evolution of Agentic Harnesses: From Chains to Graph to Code
Karthik Ramgopal describes how building agents that interact with large language models has evolved in recent years from ad hoc experiments to resilient, production-grade architectures. Karthik also shares best practices and battle-tested advice for robust agentic AI architectures, drawn from his experience building several agentic solutions.
Systemic Approach to Memory, Knowledge, and Context in the Agentic AI Architectures
Adi Polak delves into the knowledge layer of agentic AI and introduces context engineering as a new discipline that has emerged in the agentic AI space. Adi argues that context management should be tuned to the system it supports and discusses key elements and mechanisms for incorporating high-quality context data into LLM prompts to reduce or eliminate hallucinations.
Agentic AI Architecture Framework for Enterprises
In this article, Subash Natarajan and Ahilan Ponnusamy describe a three-tier framework for designing and delivering agentic AI systems, covering many distinct elements, solutions, and patterns. The authors then offer industry-specific examples and share implementation strategies and guiding principles required for successful adoption.
Agentic AI Architecture: Current Challenges and Future Opportunities
Finally, Rafał Gancarz wraps up the eMag's overarching topic by examining how agentic AI architecture, as a new generation of software architecture, will change the IT industry as we know it today. Rafał connects the dots and covers a broad range of areas and architectural aspects that will need to adapt to address the challenges posed by agentic AI.

articles.title: AI-assisted vibe coding brings Thunderbolt 4 support to Windows 98 SE
articles.text:
The takeaway: Vibe coding is viewed negatively by many, but when dedicating resources to a specific project isn't feasible, few alternatives exist. Microsoft, for example, doesn't have the time or resources to create modern drivers for operating systems they've long moved on from… but AI has no problem crafting code for legacy versions of Windows.
A developer by the name of Yeo Kheng Meng recently commissioned AI to create a driver that enables generic USB 3.x, USB4, and Thunderbolt 3/4 host controllers to work on ancient operating systems including Window 98 SE, ME, 2000, XP, Vista, and 7.
Dated versions of Windows barely make a blip on the OS market share radar, so why should anyone even care about something like this? Well, despite the low percentage of overall users, there are still lots of retro computing enthusiasts out there actively using older computers running legacy hardware and software. Being able to take advantage of modern connectivity is just icing on the cake for them.
Even if you aren't interested in this particular driver, there's a lot to take away from a story like this. Vibe coding gets trashed in the mainstream as a lazy way to approach a coding problem but as mentioned, not everyone has the time or resources to devote human programmers to every project. Tasks are often tackled based on priority, and making a driver for retro computing fans likely isn't going to rank high on that list.
One can also argue that vibe coding is a great way to explore ideas without having to be an expert in the field of programming. Every day, people come up with new and creative ideas that could help others but don't have the technical skills to turn them into a practical application. If vibe coding can get them a step closer and teach them something about the process along the way, I'm all for it.
Those interested in learning more about the vibe-coded driver for Win98 are encouraged to check out Meng's deep dive over on his blog.

articles.title: Grafana Labs leans on AI agents to automate AI agent observability - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Grafana Labs leans on AI agents to automate AI agent observability
Observability software pioneer Grafana Labs Inc. is flexing its muscles in the rapidly emerging market for artificial intelligence monitoring tools with a swath of updates to its Grafana Cloud platform announced at ObservabilityCON 2026 today.
The startup announced a new suite of AI agents, including Assistant Watchers for monitoring AI workloads and autonomous agents, and Grafana Cloud Agents for remediating problems, in addition to various broader enhancements focused on monitoring and understanding AI telemetry data.
Grafana first made a name for itself in traditional observability with its open-source Grafana platform, and since the turn of the year has aggressively pivoted to focus specifically on AI observability. The original Grafana stack was built to monitor cloud infrastructure and the software applications of yesteryear, and the startup was one of the first to recognize that generative AI applications behave very differently.
Because traditional apps work so differently, legacy observability tools struggled to provide much insight into AI models and agents, making them difficult to debug. Grafana’s solution is to treat agent sessions and large language model conversations as standard telemetry signals, similar to the logs, metrics and traces associated with traditional applications. That way, customers can monitor the performance of these systems in the context of their broader information technology infrastructure.
With the rise of autonomous agents that perform increasingly complex tasks on behalf of humans, Grafana is responding with the launch of highly specialized AI agents that are specifically designed to observe the behavior of those systems. The company said it’s pushing towards “agentic operations,” and a key part of this push is its new Assistant Watchers, which are always-on agents designed to observe and learn the normal telemetry patterns of other agents and flag anomalies in their behavior before bigger problems arise.
Alongside the Assistant Watchers, it’s also launching Grafana Managed Sandboxes in preview, which provide a controlled environment where AI can analyze code in the context of its production behavior and prepare software fixes that can be reviewed by humans. Meanwhile, Pages is a new capability that enables teams to build customized, app-like visualizations of AI workloads that provide deeper insights than its standard dashboards.
Grafana Senior Director of AI Mat Ryer said enterprises want AI agents to take over more work from humans, but if they’re going to do this, they need both evidence and control at each step. “Watchers surface emerging problems, investigations help diagnose them, and Grafana Managed Sandboxes prepare fixes for human review,” he said. “Together they make Grafana Cloud more autonomous, bringing detection, diagnosis and proposed action into one workflow, grounded in the team’s own telemetry.”
Grafana’s agents might be quite sophisticated, but the company recognizes that observability needs to do more than just secure AI workloads. One problem it’s seeking to address is the cost of running AI in the cloud. To do this it’s introducing query performance enhancements in Grafana Cloud Logs, based on technology it obtained through its recent acquisition of Logline. This enables faster full-text search across low-frequency data such as specific request IDs at no additional cost, Grafana said.
Another update is the new Adaptive Logs Archive within Grafana’s Adaptive Telemetry Suite, which allows enterprise users to route logs to their own object storage buckets using open data formats so they can retain observability data at lower cost for future investigations and compliance checks.
Finally, Grafana said, it’s trying to address full-stack visibility across both AI and traditional cloud workloads with the introduction of its new Knowledge Graph and Digital Experience Monitoring capabilities. Knowledge Graph can connect infrastructure and application dependencies with real user experiences, so that both AI agents and human engineers can view a shared runtime context when investigating problems. This capability is augmented by new Mobile Observability and Session Replay tools that enable teams to see issues from the user’s perspective.
“Most teams do not have a monitoring problem,” said Director of Product Richard Lam. “What they have is a technology debt problem: telemetry from every layer and no way to connect it to the customer it affects. Putting a knowledge graph in every Grafana Cloud stack and extending it from the infrastructure to the user makes unified observability foundational instead of something every team has to assemble on its own.”
Today’s announcements indicate that Grafana has a clear vision for what is fast becoming confusing future, in which AI is used for observability and observability is a must for AI.

articles.title: Reino Unido propõe abrir NFC do iPhone a rivais do Apple Pay • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Reino Unido propõe abrir NFC do iPhone a rivais do Apple Pay
Proposta da autoridade britânica prevê acesso mais barato à tecnologia para bancos e carteiras digitais concorrentes.
A Autoridade de Concorrência e Mercados do Reino Unido (CMA) propôs, nesta terça-feira (20/10), novas regras para ampla a concorrência nos pagamentos por aproximação no iPhone. O órgão quer reduzir as taxas cobradas pela Apple e facilitar o acesso de bancos, fintechs e outras carteiras digitais ao chip NFC dos aparelhos.
As medidas incluem taxas de acesso mais baixas e a possibilidade de uso de tecnologias alternativas ao sistema atualmente oferecido pela Apple para pagamentos por aproximação, diz a Reuters. A proposta ficará em consulta pública até 17 de novembro.
Assim como na União Europeia, que regulou as carteiras digitais nos aparelhos da Apple em 2024, um dos mecanismos previstos é o Host Card Emulation (HCE). A tecnologia permite que os apps processem pagamentos sem depender do componente físico, conhecido como Secure Element. A Apple já permite atualmente integrações de terceiros ao NFC no iPhone através de APIs.
Apesar de seguir um caminho parecido, a proposta do Reino Unido é menos restritiva para a Apple do que as regras implementadas no bloco europeu. Por lá, a empresa se comprometeu a permitir o acesso gratuito de terceiros ao NFC do iPhone para pagamentos por aproximação.
A CMA britãnica, por outro lado, não propõe essa gratuidade. O órgão quer reduzir os valores cobrados e ampliar as formas de acesso ao NFC. A autoridade ganhou poder para intervir nesse tipo de prática após classificar Apple e Google como empresas com status de mercado estratégico no setor de plataformas móveis.
Segundo dados citados pela CMA, transações por aproximações representam atualmente 39% de todos os pagamentos realizados no Reino Unido, ante 3% há uma década. Mais de 60% dos adultos no país utilizam alguma carteira digital, segundo a autoridade, e o Apple Wallet é o mais usado entre os britânicos.
“Ouvimos que taxas altas, termos rígidos e restrições relacionadas à tecnologia sem contato da Apple tornam difícil demais para os concorrentes inovarem e competiram”, afirmou a diretora-executiva da CMA, Sarah Cardell.
O NFC faz parte de uma série de tecnologias e serviços presentes em aparelhos da Apple que estão na mira de análises regulatórias, especialmente na Europa. Recentemente, a empresa teve de abrir mão da exclusividade de ferramentas proprietárias em alguns casos, como:
A empresa entrou em acordo com o Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade) para implementar parte dessas mudanças, incluindo a abertura da Apple Store e pagamentos externos, no Brasil.
A possível medida recebeu apoio de empresas do setor financeiro na região, mas desagradou a Apple. A empresa argumenta que desenvolvedores já dispõem de mecanismos para oferecer pagamentos por aproximação no iPhone por meio do NFC e do Secure Element e ampliar o uso de outras tecnologias pode reduzir as proteções do sistema atual.
“Não acreditamos que a CMA deva exigir que a Apple adote uma abordagem com menores proteções de privacidade e segurança”, afirmou um porta-voz da empresa. A CMA deve avaliar as contribuições recebidas na consulta pública antes de decidir se transforma as propostas em exigências formais.

articles.title: Modder Builds "Slurptop" Cyberdeck with Full Height Keyboard, Swappable Tool Batteries, and Trackball
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Modder Builds "Slurptop" Cyberdeck with Full Height Keyboard, Swappable Tool Batteries, and Trackball
The concept of a cyberdeck is to customize hardware to better suit your specific needs and use cases, and a modder who goes by "Slurp Burgers" online has taken the concept to something of an extreme, with their take on a laptop, the Slurptop. Unlike many DIY cyberdeck builds, which are based on Raspberry Pi computers, the Slurptop uses a full-fat AMD Ryzen 7 7730U in the motherboard from a GMKtec M5 Ultra mini PC. As a result, it has somewhat better I/O than a traditional laptop, although the mini PC's three front USB Type-C ports were all used to connect the display and peripherals internally. 
The modder took the GMKtec innards and built a custom 3D printed shell around them, replete with a columnar-stagger ergonomic keyboard using MX-style switches and SA profile keycaps, a central num pad, and a trackball mounted at the bottom of the cyberdeck. Perhaps more interesting, the modder designed custom circuitry to be able to run the device off a 24 V Kobalt power tool battery, which is swappable in the event that you need an emergency charge. The modder says that, with light productivity use, like word processing, the battery lasts around five hours, but that could be increased with a bigger 8 Ah battery.There are a few nice touches that bring the whole cyberpunk/utilitarian aesthetic together, like the rugged handle with a built-in OLED display and the bright green dual-pole single throw toggle switch used to turn on the Slurpdeck. In addition to the trackball—whose PixArt PMW3360 sensor was harvested from a mouse and unique, hand-wired keyboard, the Slurpdeck also features a built-in hinged panel that contains an XP Pen drawing tablet in the lid. The full write-up is available on the Slurp Burgers blog.The charging mechanism is rather interesting. In an attempt to avoid the headache and potential hazards of designing custom charging circuitry, Slurp Burgers opted instead to use the stock charging hardware from the power tool battery. That means charging happens externally from the device, but it has a built-in, off-the-shelf, high-speed UPS switch that automatically switches the mini PC from the wall charger to battery power when wall power is removed. When you plug it back in, the cyberdeck automatically switches back to wall power, allowing you to remove the battery and charge it on the tool battery charger.

articles.title: Microsoft reportedly projects $1,200 to $1,800 price for 2028 Project Helix
articles.text:
We haven’t heard many details about Microsoft’s upcoming “Project Helix” gaming hardware since the company announced it in March as a device that will “play your Xbox and PC games.” In a new wide-ranging profile of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, though, Fortune alludes to a dual release strategy for upcoming Microsoft gaming hardware, with “a next-generation handheld device” planned by the end of next year and a 2028 holiday season console release that could cost between $1,200 and $1,800.
That future console price range is based on what has “internally been projected” at the company, according to Fortune. But the price for consumers could come down if “Microsoft decides to subsidize the cost,” the outlet says, as many console makers have done in the past.
While a $1,200 starting price would be historically high for the game console market, even accounting for inflation, it also reflects a new normal: The slowdown in Moore’s Law and AI-driven component shortages means cutting-edge gaming hardware just isn’t as cheap as it used to be. This year, the Steam Machine broke the $1,000 starting price, while the 2-year-old technology in the PlayStation 5 Pro is now going for $900, and the 6-year-old Xbox Series X now starts at $750.
Internal clashes and sell-off rumors
Fortune also reports that Microsoft is beset by internal clashes over whether its upcoming Helix handheld will run a “trimmed-down version of Windows Home”—akin to last year’s ROG Xbox Ally—or a bespoke operating system built and controlled by the Xbox group. Fortune cites “people briefed on the clash” in reporting that one high-level executive threatened to cancel the handheld altogether if they were forced to use Windows.

articles.title: SpaceX's AI business is beating expectations | TechCrunch
articles.text:
SpaceX’s data centers and Grok agents were more profitable than investors expected in the third quarter of the year, as the company leaves its roots as a space company behind to focus on artificial intelligence, which now makes up 52% of its income.
CEO Elon Musk’s deep tech conglomerate reported $14.6 billion in third-quarter revenue on Tuesday, according to its regulatory filing.
That number was driven by growth in all segments, but especially its renamed “Super Intelligence” business line, which generated $7.5 billion in revenue from the recently acquired Cursor coding tool, Grok bot, and most importantly, the company’s burgeoning neocloud business, which now boasts 1.7 GW of compute. The AI business generated $431 million in profit, which would have been higher without $1.2 billion in one-time stock-based compensation expenses related to the Cursor acquisition.
The top-line revenue number was also boosted by about $1 billion in income related to the recovery of Bitcoin prices and unspecified related-party income that might be attributed to a SpaceX investment in another company.
The growing revenue is balanced against total capital expenditures of $19.6 billion, as SpaceX continues to build out a second data center project, Colossus II, and increase investment in Starship, the heavy-lift rocket it sees as vital to deploying a new generation of Starlink satellites and developing orbital data centers. CFO Bret Johnsen said the company would spend $35 billion to $40 billion on new capital investments in the fourth quarter.
During a livestreamed discussion of the results with investors, Musk said he was spending four days a week in Memphis, Tennessee, the site of Colossus II, working to bring the data center online.
“People are starting to realize [that] the constraint on deployment of super intelligence is more in power and cooling and infrastructure than it is in chips,” Musk argued, saying that he had tasked a team of SpaceX engineers to solve that problem. “This is a bit like the New York Yankees playing in Little League. It’s not fair, but the net result is being able to deploy power cooling infrastructure at a rate that is vastly faster than any anyone else.”
In one example, Musk noted that manufacturers of turbines to power data centers are facing 12- to 18-month delays in obtaining the metals that blades and vanes required for those machines. Now, SpaceX is using the metal casting capabilities developed for SpaceX to make those components and obtain turbines more quickly.
Musk also said that the next test flight of the Starship rocket, expected in November, would see SpaceX attempt to recover both the first-stage booster and the second stage. Recovering both segments of the vehicle would be a “massive technology milestone,” Musk said, but the true milestone will be reflying both stages.
SpaceX also saw growth in subscribers to its Starlink space internet network, reaching 13.6 million consumers, with Musk predicting that the growth of AI agents would lead to more demand for connectivity.
Despite those capital expenditures, the company’s revenue boost was substantial enough to push it back into profitability. SpaceX reported net income of $4.4 billion, a turnaround from the $1 billion loss in the same quarter last year. It will still have some catching up to do if it wants to remain profitable for the year, however. In the first nine months of the year, SpaceX still had a net income loss of $413 million.
Musk took a particularly bullish stance on the company’s Super Intelligence business segment, predicting that SpaceX’s annual recurring revenue by the end of 2027 will be “somewhere between $500 billion and $1 trillion.”
More concretely, Johnsen forecast total revenue for the first quarter of 2027 in the range of $33 billion to $37 billion.
This is a developing story. TechCrunch will update.

articles.title: Oblivion gamer uses Claude AI to boost average FPS gains up to 48%, stutters slashed by 90% — performance mod doesn't change game assets or alter visuals
articles.text:
Oblivion gamer uses Claude AI to boost average FPS gains up to 48%, stutters slashed by 90% — performance mod doesn't change game assets or alter visuals
Yes, this mod is just about 100% vibe-coded.
The revelation that there was a ton of performance lying on the table in the remastered The Elder Scrolls Part IV: Oblivion won't be a surprise to people who have played the game, which is notorious for its hitching and stuttering. The reason primarily lies in its poor utilization of hardware, and that's a big part of what LTSharpe and Claude have addressed in the new Oblivion Remastered Performance Fix that changes nothing about the game's visuals yet increases performance by as much as 68% in the worst case. (h/t to ComputerBase)
Yes, this mod is just about 100% vibe-coded, and yet, rather than hacking Minecraft into GTA V on iPhone, or hacking CoD Black Ops 2 maps into Minecraft, this mod is a binary code modification for Oblivion Remastered that seeks to improve performance and stability considerably, and according to numerous jubilant and thankful posts on NexusMods, it seems to do exactly that, with one user proclaiming that the performance increase was "dramatic" and that the overworld stuttering that plagues the game is "completely gone."
The story goes like this: gamer and mod creator LTSharpe has a slightly older system with a Ryzen 7 5800X CPU. Not the newest chip on the block to be sure, but Zen 3 isn't so old that it should be crumpling under the weight of games just yet. Frustrated with the verifiably awful performance of the remaster of The Elder Scrolls Part IV: Oblivion, he paid for a subscription to Anthropic's Claude AI agent and started working with the assistant to diagnose and fix the performance problems.
"Diagnose" is a critical keyword here, because it isn't like Claude was hallucinating an engine.ini tweak somebody else published for the original game 20 years ago. The partners, with Claude doing the hard work and LTSharpe directing, reverse-engineered the game to the point that they were able to build a repeatable benchmarking framework. That allowed them to systematically diagnose the causes of the performance problems and then test fixes against the real behavior of the game with modified machine code.
That's the thing; this was done without source code. Neither TES4 Oblivion nor the remaster's Unreal Engine is open-source software. The sheer magnitude of the task would be incredibly daunting to a team of human engineers, much less a single person. According to LTSharpe, over the course of two weeks Claude successfully diagnosed and fixed bugs in not only the Remaster's Unreal Engine code, but also in the underlying Gamebryo original engine, in AMD's frame generation code, and even in the Unreal Engine itself, improving performance and avoiding crashes.
The developer—or perhaps we should say, coordinator?—is careful to acknowledge that the performance tweaks were created with his system specifically in mind and that they may not work well for others. Indeed, he has a Radeon graphics card, which puts him within a surprisingly small minority of PC gamers, and some portion of his fixes were aimed at making sure AMD's FSR upscaling and frame generation remain in effect despite a long-standing game bug that disables them when you task-switch (Alt+Tab) out of the game. The good lieutenant invites other gamers to try out the fix and report back, and he's even helping out with support requests on NexusMods, too. Head over there if you're keen to grab the fix and try it for yourself.
