articles.title: Meta Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations
articles.text:
Muse, the new general-purpose AI agent from Meta, can expose sensitive information when users share conversations through web links, researchers reported Monday. In response to questions from Ars about the behavior, Meta said it’s suspending the sharing feature while the company reviews it and considers making changes.
Like many online services, Muse has allowed users to share searches, conversations, images, and similar content with other people. Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. To keep potentially sensitive information from being accessible to unintended people, the URLs typically contain a long sequence of text that can’t be easily guessed.
A single query is all that’s required
Muse, which Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said last month was “built from the ground up for privacy and security,” seems to take the same precautions. But a central design decision for constructing URLs has made the links easy to discover. As a result, researchers from security firm Claroc said they were able to enumerate 6,800 links Muse users created for sharing conversations with others. After opening a few hundred of them, the researchers found information that was clearly not intended to be publicly available, including:
- a candidate’s notes preparing for a confidential executive-search call with a frontier AI lab, naming the lab’s internal contact and the meeting time
- a national marketing company’s internal revenue review, marked for its CEO
- a small-business owner’s loan application, with the amount requested
- a to-do list that included a bank fraud alert, with a partial account number and a transaction amount and time
- a real-estate investor’s internal performance report, with two property addresses and exact return, income, and mortgage figures
- a workplace’s full-year staff vacation calendar, listing dozens of employees against the week each one would be away
“If you had asked us beforehand, we would have guessed that gathering these would take real effort,” the researchers wrote. “It took one query.”
In an emailed statement responding to questions from Ars, Meta said:
We opened the Muse bug bounty program so researchers could raise different scenarios and help us continue improving the product. People have the ability to share specific Muse artifacts, which creates a page that can be accessed by those with the link. However, we’ve paused this functionality while we review this report and consider changes to how these links can be discovered.
Asaf Aprozper, the co-founder and CTO of Claroc, said he reported the findings through Meta’s bug bounty program on October 8 and also tried reaching people at Meta on LinkedIn, but got no reply either way.
The easiest way to discover the URLs is to perform a passive DNS search through one of many available commercial services. Passive DNS records store the historical resolution of domain names to IP addresses, as well as nameserver, and mail-server records over time. Passive DNS systems typically collect DNS responses from sensors positioned at recursive DNS resolvers or other infrastructure. A passive DNS record is generally created when a monitoring system observes a DNS response. In the case here, once the intended party clicks on the share link, the DNS information is recorded in a searchable database.
And look! They call it superintelligence on that page, just like Trump.
Oh boy…

articles.title: NVIDIA Confidential Computing Expands, Enabling Frontier Model Builders to Securely Scale Across Global Infrastructure
articles.text:
NVIDIA builds tools to enable safe agents across the stack. The NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, announced today, is part of NVIDIA’s growing portfolio of technologies that enables organizations to safely deploy agents at scale. NVIDIA Confidential Computing is the infrastructure layer that protects the models and data those agents depend on while running.
Today, NVIDIA is expanding that layer with Confidential Bare Metal, a new deployment option with NVIDIA Confidential Computing that enables frontier model builders to run sensitive workloads on dedicated third-party infrastructure while retaining control of their models and data.
NVIDIA is introducing new platform security controls that protect data in transit, measure platform integrity and enforce hardware-level access restrictions. These new controls let frontier model builders use bare-metal instances to own and operate their bespoke software stack, including host and platform infrastructure software, when operating on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure across third-party cloud, neocloud and enterprise infrastructure.
NVIDIA Confidential Computing now offers a converged security architecture with three deployment options:
- Confidential Bare Metal for bare-metal infrastructure
- Confidential Containers for Kubernetes environments
- Confidential Virtual Machines for virtualized environments
Organizations can match the right model to their trust boundaries and operating requirements.
NVIDIA Confidential Computing is also expanding across NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Rubin systems and will integrate with NVIDIA DSX OS as a reference architecture for cloud providers building AI factories.
Model Builders Tap Global Capacity
Confidential Bare Metal gives supported providers a path to serve high-value workloads that require strong model and data privacy protections. For model builders, the expanding ecosystem offers more geographic, sovereign and operational options for scaling training and inference worldwide.
Cohere plans to integrate Confidential Bare Metal into Cohere Model Vault, using NVIDIA Confidential Computing trusted execution environments to extend hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU — protecting models and data in memory and across interconnects during execution.
“Enterprises trust Cohere to provide a secure and confidential platform for inference,” said Phil Blunsom, chief technology officer at Cohere. “With NVIDIA Confidential Computing in Cohere Model Vault, we’re extending hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU, protecting customer data in memory and across interconnects during execution.”
Google Cloud is extending support for  Confidential Bare Metal to A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems. These will combine non-virtualized NVIDIA accelerated computing with cryptographic protection for training data and model intellectual property.
“Google Cloud introduces Confidential Bare Metal to provide AI labs with hardware-isolated, non-virtualized compute environments and end-to-end cryptographic protection. Our A4X instances, built using NVIDIA Confidential Computing, preserve the privacy of user data, protect model IP, provide top-line serving performance,” said Andrés Lagar-Cavilla, distinguished engineer and AI infrastructure security lead at Google Cloud.
Confidential Computing Expands Across the NVIDIA Platform
NVIDIA Confidential Computing uses hardware-rooted isolation and cryptographic attestation to help protect models and data during execution.
Support now extends to NVIDIA Grace Blackwell NVL72 — bringing Confidential Computing to NVL72 rack-scale systems — as well as x86-based NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 and NVIDIA DGX Rubin NVL8 systems.
CoreWeave, Firmus, GMI Cloud, Google Cloud, IREN, Lambda, Microsoft Azure Infrastructure, Nebius, Nscale and Vultr support NVIDIA Confidential Computing deployments. Global systems partners including Cisco, Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo, Supermicro and Bull will support these capabilities with NVIDIA-Certified Systems.
NVIDIA DSX OS will support all NVIDIA Confidential Computing modes, giving cloud providers a software foundation for building and operating AI factories that support confidential workloads.
Learn more about NVIDIA Confidential Computing.

articles.title: Streaming guide JustWatch becomes a streamer itself | TechCrunch
articles.text:
JustWatch, a company offering a search engine and guide for streaming movies and TV shows, is now moving directly into the streaming business itself. On Tuesday, the company behind the popular guide that’s used by 50 million people is launching JustWatch TV. The new streaming service will feature content from 30 partners and will offer both free and paid tiers, as well as a movie rental store.
The media and entertainment company behind the streaming guide, the JustWatch Group, initially announced its plans to venture into streaming last month. At the time, it said partners like Paramount, New Regency, Fremantle, Bleecker Street, and Vortex Media were on board. The company has since announced other content partners, including Cineverse in the U.S., LEONINE Studios in Germany, SND in France, and Altitude in the U.K.
The 12-year-old company has long been known for its online guide to movies and TV. Essentially, it’s a “TV Guide” for the streaming era, helping users navigate a landscape where movies and shows move from one service to another, making it harder to keep up with what’s streaming where.
Available in 140 markets globally, the guide provides streaming options for more than 500,000 movies and shows across more than 1,500 service providers worldwide. This “where to watch” information and streaming chart data are also used to power some 1,400 partner websites and apps and are valuable to studios, distributors, streamers, and agencies that use the data to target their campaigns across social media platforms like Meta, YouTube, TikTok, and others.
Now the company believes there’s an even bigger opportunity to grow its audience data and insights by running its own service.
“At a time where there is so much choice, yet with so many people constantly searching for a place to find their favourite film, the series they just heard about, or something exciting that fits them, it is a great moment to be a hub for all things entertainment,” said Quentin Carbonell, JustWatch SVP of Global Content Acquisitions and Strategy, in an email shared with TechCrunch. “By having our own service with titles to watch directly on JustWatch TV, we can grow our already massive audience, while continuing to direct them to all our streaming partners. This is a natural continuation of our mission to contribute to the entire ecosystem, from the big screen to the small one.”
The new streaming service will be available within JustWatch’s existing apps and website across 12 markets, including the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Ireland, Germany, Austria, France, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, Australia, and New Zealand.
Its free tier will offer a selection of ad-supported titles, while the ad-free version, JustWatch TV Plus, will offer more than 300 ad-free titles in the U.S., as well as other exclusive features, like advanced filters and the option to hide previously seen or disliked titles in the guide.
A movie rental store will also initially be available in the U.S., U.K., Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand, with more markets to follow in time.
While the ad-supported tier competes with free streamers like Tubi and Plex, the Plus tier will compete with low-cost streamers like Roku’s $2.99 per month ad-free service, Howdy. It will be similarly priced at $3.99 per month or $49.99 for a lifetime subscription. (The latter is an interesting way to price streaming, given the evolving content costs, but JustWatch believes there will be additional value in the data collected.) Paid subscribers will also be able to take 10% off on hundreds of rentals in the JustWatch TV Store, the company noted.
Like most low-cost services, JustWatch’s content lineup focuses on older movies and shows, as well as more indie content.
Another unique feature is that users will be able to influence the service’s content to some extent. JustWatch says users will be able to request titles they want to see to help shape what comes to the service.

articles.title: A critical PHP vulnerability may take websites down today
articles.text:
Security patches for the PHP programming language, widely used to build websites and web apps, are expected to roll out today, with the goal of fixing two critical vulnerabilities that could wreak havoc on the internet if left unchecked. In an advisory published on Tuesday, PHP developers said the vulnerabilities have a severity rating of 9.2 out of a possible 10, with some cybersecurity agencies encouraging websites to temporarily take their systems offline if they’re unable to apply the fix immediately.
A critical PHP vulnerability may take websites down today
A patch is about to roll out, but the exploit affects more than 40 percent of the internet.
The security patch is expected to drop today at 10AM ET — though the developers say they may release it earlier if the vulnerability details become public or there’s evidence of the exploits actively being used — and PHP users are being urged to “upgrade as soon as the release is available.” According to cybersecurity firm watchTowr, the vulnerabilities are Remote Code Execution exploits that reportedly impact every PHP version from PHP 5 onward, and could enable attackers to run their own code on affected servers, allowing them to maliciously alter websites, steal data, and more.
The impact of these vulnerabilities could be vast, with one security researcher estimating that more than 1.3 million internet-connected hosts are likely affected. WordPress security plugin provider Wordfence also warned that every WordPress site will be vulnerable because they all run on servers that use PHP, which is no small number given WordPress reported last year that it powers more than 40 percent of the internet. Wordfence also warned that the fix can’t be installed using automatic updates, so site owners need to find out who is responsible for updating PHP to apply the patch manually.
The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team and the UK National Cyber Security Centre have both issued advisories that encourage any companies who can’t immediately patch their platforms to instead isolate their internet-facing apps from public networks or take them offline entirely until the vulnerabilities can be fully mitigated. Mobile operating system developer GrapheneOS says they’ve temporarily taken their user discussion forum offline because proof of concept exploits are already being developed and they “don’t want to take the risk.” According to PHP developer Gina Peter Banyard, patching is the only mitigation, and otherwise turning servers off “might be the most sensible thing to do.”
Multiple cybersecurity organizations have also prompted PHP admins to prepare, with threat researchers at Sansec saying they expect to see “mass attacks within 15 minutes of the release.” That doesn’t mean attackers are waiting around, however. Cloudflare chief technology officer Dane Knecht says “we are seeing early attacks emerging” against the platform’s PHP sites, and that Cloudflare is temporarily updating its firewall rules as a stopgap until the fix is available.

articles.title: Q&A: Why CoLab is in the “sweet spot” of engineering software | BetaKit
articles.text:
The small but mighty St. John’s, Nfld. tech scene has garnered attention in recent months for being an “unlikely” hub for startups, and rapidly scaling companies such as CoLab Software have helped build that reputation.
“That’s a huge Newfoundland advantage… the connections are so rich between people that people want to be here and they want to come back.”
CoLab makes an AI-powered engineering design platform that helps engineers plan out complex products before they are manufactured. The scaleup was founded in 2017 by two Memorial University graduates who did co-ops in Silicon Valley and later went through Y Combinator before returning to build in Newfoundland. Since then, it has raised more than $100 million USD ($140 million CAD) from local and US investors, grown its team to roughly 250 people, and was reportedly last valued at around $500 million USD. It has also landed big-name clients like Bombardier and Ford.
As CoLab’s chief strategy officer, Taylor Young works side by side with co-founders Adam Keating and Jeremy Andrews to guide the company’s direction, orchestrate partnerships, and lead corporate development. BetaKit sat down with Young to learn more about CoLab’s business journey and the advantage of running the business from Newfoundland.
The following conversation has been compiled from BetaKit’s interview with Young, as well as her on-stage remarks at the techNL conference on Tuesday. It has been edited for clarity and length.
CoLab has been around for nine years now and has a mature product. What’s the landscape like for engineering software and AI?
The engineering software landscape has gotten almost no attention over the past 30 years. When you compare it to almost any other B2B (business-to-business) realm, from life-saving medical devices to airplanes to rocket ships, they are still using 30-year-old technology.
You have the incumbents—the computer-aided design and product life-cycle management companies—then you have thousands, lately, of very small technology startups that were not around when CoLab started, and then you have a small group of us that have been doing this for 10 years or so.
For our customers who are desperately trying to understand how they transform in the age of AI, and who face increasing pressure to do everything faster, who do they bet on? There’s no one right answer, but we are getting chosen a lot as that partner, I think, because we’re in a real sweet spot of maturity.
In a fast-growing startup, how do you prioritize what to work on and what to put aside?
Sometimes, some things feel good to solve because they’re easy or actionable, but that doesn’t mean they’re the things you should work on. In the early days of getting a company off the ground, you have to train yourself to say no to most things.
We needed to pick a market that was small enough that we could win, but referenceable enough to other markets that it could help us tap into that growth. For us, it was industrial equipment and HVAC—not the most exciting technology in the world. We had to do that for a long time and focus on a small subset of use cases until we earned the right to do more.
How do you follow where the market’s heading versus leveraging feedback from customers?
Customers show you the problems and, generally, we show them potential solutions. I think that was simpler before AI-driven product development. We used to be able to identify problems and build solutions specific to a use case, and it was very clear for a customer to wrap their heads around if they wanted it or not. Now we can build things a lot faster that are a lot broader.
We’ve gotten into a mentality of trying more and putting more in front of the user. We work with very large companies—that means the person who is buying the tool, and the people who will use it, could be several layers removed, with hundreds of people between them. So you have to put stuff in front of them and wait and see.
What would you say is the biggest benefit of building a company in St. John’s?
I think we are subject to a lot less noise than your average Silicon Valley startup. What that forces us to do is focus on our customers, use that as the most important source of information for what we’re going to do, and to pay a little bit less attention to what everybody else is doing.
“I think we are subject to a lot less noise than your average Silicon Valley startup.”
Obviously we need to understand what’s changing, but our customers are often fairly removed from that, and there’s an enormous amount of noise and distraction if you spend too much time concerning yourself with the startup ecosystem.
We have an amazing team based here that intends to be a part of CoLab the whole way. They have an emotional connection to CoLab and they want to see it through. From what I understand, that’s unusual in other parts of the world where people are focused on growing a career more than they’re focused on growing a company.
I was going to ask about challenges with talent retention, but it sounds like you have a loyal core.
That’s a huge Newfoundland advantage. I’m sure it’s not specific to this province, but it’s an advantage that we’ve found. I think the connections are so rich between people that people want to be here and they want to come back. Obviously, some people are dying to get to Toronto or New York or Montréal, but by and large, we see that going away is a short-term decision. They’re going to go work in the Bay Area, and then they’re going to figure out how to get back.

articles.title: Spotify se sube al modelo Patreon con sus nuevas membresías para podcasts
articles.text:
Spotify acaba de incorporar una nueva vía de monetización para podcasts, de la mano de membresías. En adelante, los usuarios podrán comprar suscripciones de pago para apoyar a sus creadores de contenido favoritos, recibiendo contenidos exclusivos y otros beneficios a cambio.
A través de las membresías, los realizadores de podcasts contarán con una nueva opción para generar dinero a través de Spotify. De esta manera, ya no dependerán de la publicidad como fuente de ingresos y podrán fortalecer la conexión con su público y forjar una comunidad más estrecha.
Los requisitos de Spotify para ofrecer membresías a través de los podcasts son bastante accesibles. La plataforma exige que las producciones estén alojadas en Megaphone o Spotify for Creators, y que tengan al menos 3 episodios publicados, 100 oyentes/espectadores y 100 horas de consumo en Spotify en los 30 días previos.
Otro detalle interesante es que los creadores podrán quedarse con el 90 % de los ingresos que sus podcasts generen a través de las nuevas membresías de Spotify. Sin dudas, una opción muy atractiva para ampliar la monetización del material y fidelizar todavía más a su audiencia.
Los podcasts de Spotify adoptan el modelo Patreon a través de membresías
A través de las membresías de Spotify, los creadores de podcasts podrán ofrecer contenidos exclusivos y otros beneficios a quienes les apoyan económicamente. La plataforma de streaming se ha inspirado en el modelo de Patreon, aunque no es la primera en hacerlo. Otros servicios de distribución de contenidos llevan tiempo brindando soluciones similares, como YouTube.
Es importante mencionar que para comprar la membresía de un podcast no será necesario pagar por Spotify Premium. Esta nueva función estará disponible tanto para los usuarios de pago como para quienes tienen una cuenta gratuita en el servicio.
Respecto de los beneficios que se pueden brindar a través de las membresías, Spotify indica que los podcasts podrán dar acceso temprano a nuevos episodios, entregas exclusivas o menos anuncios, por citar algunos ejemplos. También será posible implementar distintos niveles de apoyo, con precios y perks diferentes para cada uno. La nueva vía de monetización incluso admite pruebas gratis por 7 días.
Quienes compren las membresías para los podcasts de Spotify recibirán insignias que se podrán mostrar junto a su perfil al momento de comentar publicaciones. Una iniciativa interesante y que ya se está poniendo en marcha con títulos seleccionados (y bastante populares) como The Shawn Ryan Show, Two Hot Takes y The Adam Friedland Show.
Eso sí, las nuevas membresías no llegarán a todos los países de inmediato. Spotify está ofreciendo esta herramienta para podcasts en 34 mercados, entre los que se encuentra España. Por lo pronto, Latinoamérica no aparece entre los territorios contemplados. Seguramente se expandirá a más lugares con el correr del tiempo, aunque no hay precisiones en tal sentido.

articles.title: Google rollt Personal Intelligence für Android Auto aus: Warum deutsche Autofahrer leer ausgehen
articles.text:
Google rollt Personal Intelligence für Android Auto aus: Warum deutsche Autofahrer leer ausgehen
Viele Autofahrer:innen, die Android Auto für ihre Reisen nutzen, dürfen sich über zahlreiche Neuerungen freuen. Nicht nur, dass sich schon Android Auto 18 als großer Versionssprung am Horizont abzeichnet. Jetzt hat Google schon vorab ein KI-Upgrade für seinen Dienst ausgerollt. Wie das Unternehmen in der Ankündigung schreibt, zieht damit Personal Intelligence von Gemini in Android Auto ein.
Personal Intelligence in Android Auto – aber nicht für jeden
Die schlechte Nachricht für deutsche Autofahrer:innen, die sich auf KI-Features in Android Auto gefreut haben, vorweg: Wie Google im Kleingedruckten in der Ankündigung verrät, wird Personal Intelligence in allen Regionen außer der EU, der Schweiz, dem Vereinigten Königreich sowie Nigeria ausgerollt. Ob und wann die KI-Funktionen auch hierzulande nachgereicht werden, ist nicht bekannt.
Dementsprechend bleibt deutschen Android-Auto-User:innen vorerst nur zu hoffen, dass die Neuerungen auch in ihren Fahrzeugen landen. Sollte das zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt passieren, gibt es einige praktische Features durch Gemini und Personal Intelligence. Dadurch kann Googles KI auf weitere Google-Dienste und die darin befindlichen Daten der User:innen zugreifen, um noch persönlichere und präzisere Antworten zu liefern.
Zu den verknüpfbaren Apps zählen der Google Workspace samt Gmail und dem Google-Kalender, Google Fotos, Google Maps sowie Youtube und die Suchmaschine des Konzerns. Wie nützlich das im Alltag sein kann, zeigt das Unternehmen an mehreren Beispielen. Wer sich etwa auf der Fahrt zum Flughafen befindet, kann Gemini per Spracheingabe fragen, ob der gebuchte Flug noch pünktlich startet und von welchem Gate er abhebt. Die KI durchforstet dann die Mails mit den Ticketinformationen und gleicht die Daten im Netz mit den aktuellen Abflugzeiten ab.
Ferner können User:innen einfach sagen, dass Gemini sie über Android Auto zu ihrem Termin lotsen soll. Die KI schaut im Kalender nach, was als Nächstes ansteht, und sucht die Adresse heraus. Durch die Verknüpfung mit Google Fotos können User:innen etwa sagen, dass sie zu dem Ort wollen, den sie letzte Woche an einem bestimmten Tag fotografiert haben. Gemini scannt die Bilder im Ordner, sucht die gewünschte Adresse heraus und legt es als neues Ziel in Android Auto fest.
Standardmäßig ist Personal Intelligence dabei deaktiviert. Erst wenn User:innen in den Einstellungen der Gemini-App die Freigabe erteilen, kann die KI auf die jeweiligen Google-Dienste zugreifen. Alle herkömmlichen Funktionen wie das Navigieren, Abspielen von Musik und Tätigen von Anrufen funktionieren auch weiterhin ohne Personal Intelligence unter Android.
Gerade weil das KI-Feature (noch) nicht in die EU kommt, fände ich es interessant, ob und welche Neuerungen sonst noch in der neuen Version stecken. Leider verrät der Artikel dazu nichts außer der Versionsnummer. Schade.

Bring better speeds to your home network with this Wi-Fi 7 router
There's no point upgrading your internet connection if you've got a bad Wi-Fi router slowing you down. If the ISP-provided router isn't up to the task, and you're ready to banish the lag, you'll want to pick up this TP-Link router, on sale for a limited time only. The TP-Link Archer BE9700, also known as the BE600, is down to $189.98 right now, giving you a 24% saving on its list price.

With the BE9700, you're getting a tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router with six external antennas, enough to give you coverage for up to 2,600 sq. ft. with up to 120 different devices connecting to it. TP-Link reckons you can expect to see speeds of up to 5,765 Mbps on the fastest 6 GHz band, with 2,882 Mbps at 5 GHz, and 1,032 Mbps at 2.4 GHz. MLO, or Multi-Link Operation, support means you're able to connect using these different bands at the same time, giving you even faster speeds and better protection against congestion.
The TP-Link Archer BE9700 router has six antennas and adds Wi-Fi 7 support for your network, with one 10Gb WAN port and four additional 2.5 Gb Ethernet ports for high speed wired connectivity.
Our TP-Link BE9700 review shows this is a serious option for your network. This is a good value router with solid Wi-Fi 7 support, with speeds that make it a competitive option, especially at this price point. Our review shows that it comes with class-leading 6 GHz performance, with decent enough speeds at 5 GHz and 2.4 GHz. It's the top choice in our best Wi-Fi router shortlist, too.
While Wi-Fi 7 support is the big deal here, the wired connections aren't bad, either. You get a 10Gb WAN port to hook this router up to your super-fast modem, giving you max speeds. Aside from the speeds, you get a USB 3.0 port on the side, which you could use to hook up a printer or external hard drive as a basic NAS. EasyMesh support, meanwhile, means you can use this as a wireless node in a mesh network. It also has Quality of Service controls to help you prioritize traffic for your core devices, such as your gaming PC, so you don't lose out when you're gaming.
The $189.98 sale price for this TP-Link Archer BE9700 router is a good one, even if it has yo-yo'd in price over recent months. That said, this is a solid discount off the $249.99 list price that it was at a few weeks ago, and one that'll give you an ultra-fast upgrade to your local network.

articles.title: PSG – Barça ce soir : comment suivre le choc du Parc des Princes en direct
articles.text:
Un an après leur duel à dans la citadelle Montjuïc, le PSG et le FC Barcelone se retrouvent ce mardi 20 octobre au Parc des Princes pour la 3e journée de la phase de ligue. Diffuseur officiel de la rencontre, CANAL+ propose son offre CANAL+ Sport à 29,99 €/mois pendant 12 mois, avec beIN SPORTS, Eurosport et Apple TV inclus.
Le coup d’envoi de ce PSG - FC Barcelone sera donné à 21 h, heure de Paris, dans le cadre de la troisième journée de la phase de ligue de la Ligue des Champions. Les Parisiens, qui ont remporté la compétition deux saisons de suite, abordent cette édition dans la peau d’un des grands favoris et retrouvent pour l’occasion l’adversaire qu’ils avaient déjà croisé la saison passée, à domicile cette fois.
En France, c’est le groupe CANAL+ qui détient les droits de la rencontre. Pour celles et ceux qui ne sont pas encore abonnés, l’offre CANAL+ Sport reste le moyen le plus direct et le plus légal de suivre le match en direct, que ce soit devant la télé ou en streaming sur mobile.
Profiter de CANAL+ Sport à 29,99 €/mois au lieu de 39,99 € sur CANAL+

- BeIN SPORTS et Eurosport sont inclus dans le même abonnement, sans avoir à cumuler les services

Paris - Barça, le genre de soirée européenne qu’on ne regarde pas en différé

Avec le format de la phase de ligue, chaque point compte pour accrocher le top 8 et éviter les barrages, ce qui donne à ce choc d’octobre un enjeu bien réel au-delà du prestige. Pour le suivre, il faudra en revanche passer par le groupe CANAL+, qui n’est pas une chaîne en clair : sans abonnement, il n’existe pas de solution légale pour voir le match en direct en France. Le coup d’envoi étant fixé à 21 h, mieux vaut régler la question de l’accès avant le début de l’avant-match, plutôt qu’à la dernière minute.
Du canapé au smartphone : le match vous suit partout

articles.title: Former international boxer’s LegalTech startup EstateMin raises €1 million to scale in the US | EU-Startups
articles.text:
EstateMin, an Irish-founded LegalTech startup helping trust and estate law firms manage estate values with its AI-powered platform, has secured €1 million in pre-Seed funding.
The funding round saw participation from NDRC, First Port Syndicate, and Enterprise Ireland, which invested through its High Potential Start-Up programme. Angel investors Mike Hanrahan, Moira McKenna, and Conor Stanley also participated alongside other Irish angels.
“The real benefit for our clients is how much easier EstateMin makes it to get us information. Executors and family members can complete their intake right from the portal, on their own time, instead of juggling calls and paperwork during an already difficult process. That means their matter moves faster and they spend less time chasing us for updates,” said James Greenwood of Greenwood Law in Illinois.
Founded in Ireland in 2024 and now headquartered in Brooklyn, New York, EstateMin was built to solve a problem its co-founder and CEO, Isabella Hughes, experienced firsthand. A law graduate and former international boxer, Hughes spent time working as a legal executive, manually retyping client information into legal documents, a time-consuming process that she describes as unnecessary.
To solve this problem, she teamed up with Oisín Dolphin, a machine learning expert with over eight years of experience, who was drawn to the same problem after going through probate following the death of his father. The two met at an NDRC founder weekend at Dogpatch Labs in 2024. John Noonan, who brings more than four years of experience across product and consumer success at legal technology company Clio, subsequently joined as the third co-founder.
“What Oisín was describing was something I was doing every day. You don’t necessarily question it when it’s simply part of your job. Then somebody points out that you’re taking information a client has already provided and typing it all over again, and suddenly you realise how much time is being lost,” said Hughes, co-founder and CEO of EstateMin.
EstateMin’s AI-powered platform helps attorneys manage estate planning, estate administration and trust matters by digitising client intake, organising estate information, extracting data from documents and supporting form preparation. Its AI Case Reviewer scans files to flag missing fields, inconsistencies, or additional forms needed before a submission is finalised.
The platform integrates with existing legal case management systems, including Clio, and the company says it can become operational in about two minutes with minimal configuration. The platform is already helping trust and estate law firms manage more than €686 million ($770 million) in estate values across 777 matters.
Law firms reportedly save five to seven hours on each estate planning matter and five to ten hours on estate administrations. The platform is active across all 50 US states, and EstateMin is reporting 20% month-on-month revenue growth.
The journey to this point hasn’t been easy, with Hughes recounting a pivotal moment where they had to decide between the US and the UK. After initially building for Irish law firms and seeing slower adoption than expected, Hughes said they didn’t have the money to try everywhere and choose between the UK or take the bigger risk and expand to America.
“The response we’d had in New York was completely different, so we decided to go for it,” she explained.
The pre-Seed funding is earmarked for customer acquisition in the US, scaling EstateMin’s go-to-market operations, and expanding its engineering and product teams. The company has already hired two software engineers and added US business development capacity as part of its US push.
“EstateMin started with a very simple problem: why are highly trained legal professionals spending so much time retyping information? We’ve gone from working on that problem in Dogpatch Labs to building specifically for firms across America. Now we want to see how far we can take it,” Hughes added.

articles.title: Cleaning up PFAS
articles.text:
Cleaning up PFAS
Ridding the world of forever chemicals could address a range of health and environmental and health woes.
Scrubbing Earth of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances—a.k.a. PFAS or forever chemicals—could eliminate a list of woes for people and planet. Used for decades in everything from nonstick pans to firefighting foams, PFAS have been linked to increased risks of fertility challenges, developmental delays, cancer, and reduced immune response. They are known for a strong bond between carbon and fluorine, which the environment struggles to break down.
The sticking points
PFAS are everywhere: They spew from factories and slough off products and into water with normal use. Scientists have found them in everything from human blood to Antarctic snow. One 2022 report found that 89% of the US population had PFAS in excess of two nanograms per milliliter of blood plasma, a common threshold for potential adverse health effects, and 9% of the population had passed the riskier level of 20 nanograms per milliliter.
The PFAS monster is also a moving target. New compounds are still being created and used. There are more than 12,000 of them, and much of the cleanup research focuses on only a small handful.
The progress
Cleansing PFAS-contaminated soil is a project in its infancy, but it is possible to prevent more buildup by pulling the chemicals out of water systems. There are two ways to handle this: trap or destroy. Some scientists have found reverse osmosis—a process that pushes water through supertight filters—useful in point-of-use cases, like water filters at kitchen sinks.
Other techniques in the pipeline might be more suitable for large-scale removal—for example, at water treatment facilities. One, called foam fractionation, generates bubbles that capture PFAS. More approaches, like ensnaring the chemicals in nanothin layers of charged metal, are also under investigation.
Trapping, though, is imperfect. You’re left with PFAS-filled brine, which if not properly destroyed (an expensive and energy-sucking endeavor) can still end up in the environment.
Jack Huang, a professor of crop and soil sciences at the University of Georgia, is working on destruction. He’s testing a method called electrochemical degradation, which uses electrodes to break down the bonds that hold PFAS together. The product destroyed more than 90% of PFAS mass in tests and has already been licensed by the engineering consulting firm AECOM.
Ridding life of PFAS is also a policy challenge. There are alternatives; we just need the push to use them. And we’ve had success before: The EPA’s 2010/2015 PFOA Stewardship Program has helped slash the release of water-repellent perfluorooctanoic acid by 95%. More recently, Minnesota, Maine, and New Mexico have passed bans on PFAS in products like cookware and dental floss.
Progress meter ............ 6
Scientists are making strides toward removing and destroying PFAS—but it’ll be all for naught if we don’t turn off the tap.

articles.title: Digitaler Ausweis auf dem Smartphone: Was Banken an d-you kritisieren
articles.text:
Digitaler Personalausweis ab 2027: Warum Banken vor Sicherheitslücken in der d-you-Wallet warnen
Die staatliche Wallet „d-you“ soll im Januar 2027 starten. Nutzer können sich damit per Smartphone ausweisen, amtliche Dokumente speichern und elektronisch unterschreiben.
Grundlage dafür ist die EU-Verordnung eIDAS 2.0, die jeden Mitgliedstaat verpflichtet, seinen Bürgern eine solche Wallet anzubieten. Die Bundesregierung plant dazu entsprechende Regeln im Digitale Identitätengesetz (DIdG), über den Gesetzentwurf stimmt der Bundestag voraussichtlich am Donnerstag ab.
Die Deutsche Kreditwirtschaft (DK), als Interessenvertretung der Banken und Sparkassen, fordert nun Nachschärfungen im Gesetz. Zwar begrüßen die Banken, dass Kunden sich künftig per Wallet geldwäscherechtlich identifizieren können, wenn sie ein Konto eröffnen. Die Institute fordern jedoch, klar festzulegen, dass es ausreicht, die vom Wallet–Verfahren bereitgestellten Daten zu speichern, also dass eine Ausweiskopie weder erforderlich noch technisch umsetzbar ist. Ohne diese Präzisierung könnten Banken sonst vorsichtshalber zusätzliche Nachweise verlangen, wodurch der Vorteil einer schnellen, papierlosen Kontoeröffnung verloren gehen könnte.
Außerdem müsse das Gesetz klarer regeln, wann Banken eine fremde Wallet akzeptieren müssen, wer bei technischen Fehlern haftet und welche Daten ihnen zur Betrugsabwehr zur Verfügung stehen.
Authentifizierung und Autorisierung
Den Banken geht es dabei unter anderem um die Trennung von Authentifizierung (als Sicherheitsabfrage) und Autorisierung, also die Freigabe von Zahlungen.
Grundsätzlich sind sie offen dafür, die Wallet beim Onlinebanking und beim Bezahlen als Sicherheitsabfrage zu akzeptieren, ähnlich wie heute eine TAN-App, allerdings nur dort, wo eine solche Prüfung ohnehin vorgeschrieben ist. Die Banken befürchten, das Gesetz könne sie zur Akzeptanz verpflichten, ohne dass sie die nötigen technischen Nachweise und eine eindeutige Haftungsregelung bekommen. Die DK fordert deshalb eine Klarstellung im Gesetz.
Keine Annahmepflicht
Grundsätzlich unterstützt die Bank die Idee, die Wallet auch für Zahlungen nutzbar zu machen. Eine Verpflichtung der Banken, Zahlungen direkt über die Wallet anzubieten, lehnen sie aber ab.
Jedes Institut soll selbst entscheiden dürfen, mit welchem Verfahren Kunden ihre Zahlungen freigeben. Auch eine pauschale Annahmepflicht im stationären Zahlungsverkehr sehen die Banken kritisch. Kartenzahlungen, Girocard und Bargeldabhebungen dürften nicht durch die Hintertür an die Wallet gekoppelt werden. Bestehende Systeme umzubauen, wäre aus Sicht der Banken technisch, rechtlich und wirtschaftlich sehr aufwendig.
Kunden sollen ihre Bankkarte künftig in die Wallet laden können, ähnlich wie heute bei Apple Pay oder Google Pay. Ob eine Bank das anbietet, soll aber ebenfalls ihre freie Entscheidung bleiben. Die DK wünscht sich auch hier eine eindeutige Formulierung im Gesetz. Außerdem soll eine Einbindung nur mit einem Vertrag zwischen Wallet-Anbieter und Bank zulässig sein.
Neben der staatlichen Wallet können auch Unternehmen künftig eigene Wallets anbieten. Laut Entwurf entscheidet darüber aber das Digitalministerium, und zwar mit der Möglichkeit, seine Entscheidung später zu ändern. Für Investoren ergebe sich daraus Planungs- und Investitionsrisiken, warnen die Banken. Sie fordern daher, private Wallets direkt im Gesetz zu erlauben, bestehende Angebote zu schützen und einen klaren Zeitplan festzulegen.
Streitpunkt Haftung
Eine weitere offene Frage berührt die Haftung in Betrugsfällen oder bei technischen Pannen. Zahlungsdienstleister wollen nicht für Fehler einer Wallet haften, die sie nicht selbst bereitgestellt haben oder kontrollieren können.
Die Banken fordern deshalb: Wird eine Wallet zur starken Kundenauthentifizierung genutzt, soll der Wallet-Anbieter nachweisen müssen, dass die Authentifizierung ordnungsgemäß lief, korrekt protokolliert wurde und nicht durch einen Fehler der Wallet beeinträchtigt war.
Außerdem wollen die Banken ein gesetzliches Recht auf die Informationen, die sie zur Prüfung von Erstattungs-, Haftungs- und Betrugsfällen benötigen. Dazu zählen standardisierte Protokolle, Transaktionsdaten, Angaben zum Wallet-Anbieter und Risikosignale. Bei bekannten Sicherheitslücken oder Zertifizierungsproblemen wollen sie außerdem das Recht haben, eine Wallet abzulehnen oder vorübergehend sperren zu dürfen.
Bedenken zur EUID-Wallet hatten zuletzt auch Sachverständige in einer Anhörung des Digitalausschuss angemeldet. Anfang Oktober bemängelten Daten- und Verbraucherschützer etwa, dass sich die Wallet zum Start nicht pseudonym nutzen lässt. Anbieter könnten mehr Daten abfragen als nötig und aus den Daten Profile bilden.
Die IT-Sicherheitsforscherin Jiska Classen von der Universität Potsdam kritisierte, große Teile der Sicherheitsarchitektur seien noch nicht öffentlich und nicht bewertet. Smartphones blieben ein hohes Risiko, weil viele Geräte keine Sicherheitsupdates mehr erhielten. Über ein kompromittiertes Handy könnten sich unbefugte Nutzer im Namen eines anderen ausweisen, Hotels buchen oder Kredite aufnehmen. Auch sie forderte daher eine eindeutige Haftungsregelung im Gesetz.
Das braucht kein Mensch. Es dient ausschließlich nur der totalen Kontrolle von uns allen. Wacht doch endlich auf! Macht ihr es trotzdem, dürft ihr später nicht meckern.

articles.title: En 2010, dejó su trabajo en Estados Unidos para dedicarse a la agricultura; hoy su empresa factura millones por año.
articles.text:
Shashi Kumar abandonó en 2010, tras una carrera dedicada al sector tecnológico en Estados Unidos, el camino tan habitual en favor de un campo más agreste para echar raíces: la India. Su empresa, Akshayakalpa Organic, que cofundó en 2010, declaró una facturación de 5.560 millones de rupias en el ejercicio 2025-2026. Eso equivale a unos 52,2 millones de euros.
La exitosa “vuelta a casa” tenía su complejidad familiar: Kumar había crecido en una familia de agricultores en Tiptur, Karnataka, y su padre quería que estudiara para encontrar un trabajo fuera del campo. Según relató el propio Kumar, dejaron de hablarse durante ocho años.
Kumar cursó ingeniería en Bangalore y un máster en el Illinois Institute of Technology de Chicago y, según la biografía de su empresa, se dedicó a las telecomunicaciones durante cerca de diecisiete años antes de emprender su iniciativa, trece de ellos en Wipro Technologies. Su interés por la agricultura se despertó en la universidad, cuando visitó al agricultor Cherkady Ramachandra Rao, quien le enseñó a combinar cultivos y a vender el excedente de producción de una pequeña explotación.
Así nació la idea de contar con una iniciativa que ayudara a los jóvenes a percibir la agricultura como una actividad lucrativa. Partieron de la ganadería lechera para diversificarse posteriormente. Según su recuerdo en el pódcast de Prime Venture Partners, el negocio llegó a estar a punto de quebrar en varias ocasiones. También ha contado que en septiembre de 2016, tras fracasar en su búsqueda de capital, su esposa, Shilpa, aportó tres millones de rupias procedentes de los ahorros familiares y su tío aportó un millón más.
La empresa de Kumar, que según el pódcast genera 600 millones de rupias al mes y trabaja con un total de 2.800 agricultores, tendría unas ventas anuales de 7.200 millones de rupias si se mantuviera el mismo ritmo durante doce meses.
Tecnología para organizar la producción
El acercamiento de Kumar a la agricultura había empezado antes, ya que, según la biografía de ATREE, una organización de investigación ambiental, ya estaba experimentando con cultivos orgánicos en 2004 mientras seguía trabajando a jornada completa en tecnología. Shilpa se encargaba de la gestión diaria de la pequeña parcela en Ramanagara. Kumar cofundó Akshayakalpa en 2010 con el veterinario GNS Reddy.
Sus conocimientos de ingeniería encontraron su aplicación en el sector agrícola. Kumar afirma que utilizan análisis predictivo para anticipar la producción y detectar posibles problemas. Con la suscripción y el comercio electrónico, añade, el negocio anticipa la demanda y ajusta las compras de leche a los agricultores. Según explica, pueden rastrear cada litro hasta la granja de origen.
Esta empresa, al igual que muchas otras, tuvo que aprender a vender su producto. Por eso, tal y como afirma Kumar en la misma entrevista, los primeros nueve años fueron una lección; no habían comprendido la importancia del acceso al mercado. Lok Capital invirtió en la empresa en 2019 y se retiró en 2024, y en su página web se describe cómo las ventas anuales pasaron de 290 a 3.000 millones de rupias durante el periodo de inversión. Además, explican que el negocio no se centró únicamente en vender productos, sino que la creación de marca y la captación de clientes constituyeron un pilar fundamental.
No es la primera vez que alguien pasa de una carrera profesional en el ámbito tecnológico a algo tan diferente como criar animales. En otro artículo ya contamos la historia de Feng Yuan, que fue despedido de Microsoft tras 22 años y se dedicó a criar gansos. En su perfil de LinkedIn también anunciaba servicios de optimización de sistemas.
Los recortes para mantener la empresa
Las dificultades financieras, tal y como relató Kumar en una publicación de LinkedIn sobre los años 2016 a 2019, requirieron una reestructuración. Hicieron algunos ajustes: cerraron operaciones en dos ciudades y suspendieron la incorporación de nuevos empleados durante tres años.
Kumar dejó de cobrar y la plantilla no tuvo subidas salariales. Así, Kumar concluye su relato con una nota sobre esos años críticos: “No se puede replicar esa locura”.
Los sistemas tecnológicos de gestión siguen presentes en la empresa agrícola. Kumar explica el uso de datos e inteligencia artificial, incluido el seguimiento digital de miles de animales.

articles.title: Spotify eliminó más de 50 millones de canciones spam o ‘basura’ hecha con IA
articles.text:
Spotify retiró más de 50 millones de canciones identificadas como contenido basura o spam generado con inteligencia artificial de sus recomendaciones durante este año, como parte de la idea de frenar la avalancha de música creada en masa con herramientas automatizadas.
La cifra, publicada en el blog oficial For the Record, se suma a los más de 75 millones de temas que la empresa eliminó por completo de la plataforma tras infracciones graves o reiteradas de sus reglas contra el spam.
Según el comunicado, a comienzos de este año Spotify analizó qué canciones los oyentes saltaban, ignoraban o reportaban como no deseadas y encontró un patrón: esos temas coincidían sistemáticamente con los clasificados como basura o spam.
Durante los últimos seis meses la compañía modificó su sistema de recomendaciones para sacar ese contenido y darle más lugar a artistas humanos verificados. Sus editores aplican el mismo criterio y no incluyen en listas ese tipo de material, afirmó Spotify.
Spotify tiene una combinación de señales contra el spam
Spotify explicó que ninguna señal por sí sola identifica contenido basura, por lo que combina el comportamiento de los oyentes, los patrones de carga, los metadatos de cada tema y herramientas externas de detección de inteligencia artificial.
La empresa reconoció que la tecnología de detección de IA tiene límites y que la tarea se volverá más difícil a medida que la inteligencia artificial generativa avance. Por eso dijo que rastrea tácticas como cargas masivas, duplicados, manipulación de buscadores, redes de listas de reproducción fraudulentas y canciones artificialmente cortas.
Spotify obliga a los artistas a aclarar qué tiene IA de sus canciones
Desde abril de 2026, Spotify habilita que los artistas declaren qué partes de una canción se hicieron con inteligencia artificial a través de un sistema llamado AI Credits. La empresa dijo que recibe decenas de miles de esas declaraciones por día.
Más de 300.000 artistas, que representan más del 99% de lo que los oyentes buscan en la plataforma, cuentan hoy con la verificación Verified by Spotify, un sello que certifica que detrás del perfil hay una persona real. Siete de cada diez de esos artistas son independientes.
La plataforma también etiqueta a miles de perfiles como AI Persona cuando la identidad del artista fue generada con inteligencia artificial. Esos perfiles quedan excluidos de las recomendaciones editoriales y algorítmicas, salvo que un oyente decida seguirlos. Spotify dijo ser el único gran servicio de streaming que aplica ese tipo de etiqueta.
Un grupo de artistas participa además de una prueba piloto que les permite revisar y bloquear lanzamientos que los mencionen sin su autorización antes de que aparezcan en su perfil. La empresa prometió extender esa herramienta a todos los artistas antes de que termine el año.
Desde 2024, Spotify exige un mínimo de 1.000 reproducciones para que un tema empiece a generar regalías. Según la empresa, las canciones con indicios de haber sido generadas con inteligencia artificial tienen diez veces más probabilidades de no alcanzar ese umbral, lo que dificulta que los infractores cobren regalías destinadas a artistas reales.
La compañía ya había advertido sobre el problema en septiembre de 2025, cuando dijo que había retirado 75 millones de temas spam en los doce meses anteriores. En ese momento explicó que los pagos totales de regalías en la plataforma crecieron de 1.000 millones de dólares en 2014 a 10.000 millones de dólares en 2024, un volumen que, según la empresa, atrae a actores que buscan explotar el sistema con contenido masivo.
El anuncio llega mientras otras plataformas de streaming refuerzan sus propias reglas frente al contenido generado con inteligencia artificial. YouTube Music comenzó la semana pasada a etiquetar las canciones hechas con IA y se sumó así a Apple Music y Tidal, que además impide que esas canciones generen ingresos.

articles.title: Hijacked Developer Account Used to Plant Stealer in OVHcloud CLI
articles.text:
French cloud computing and web hosting company OVHcloud says a hacker used the GitHub account of one of its developers to plant a secret-stealing binary in its official command-line interface (CLI) tool.
The supply chain incident occurred on October 19, and OVHcloud lists versions v0.11.0 through v0.15.0 as compromised. Version 0.10.0 and the newly released version 0.16.0 are clean.
“The hacker used the GitHub account of one of the developers and added a binary whose job is to retrieve secrets from the disk. The quality of the binary is poor but it can go all the way,” OVHcloud founder Octave Klaba said on X (translated from French).
Klaba said the compromised version appeared at 14:47 Paris time and was blocked at 16:21, after a customer reported the issue. According to OpenSourceMalware, a user flagged the tampering publicly on GitHub after an automated hash check failed.
The CI/CD pipelines were not impacted, Klaba noted in a different post, as the issue stemmed from GitHub’s release immutability option not being enabled.
“As a result, a user with the appropriate permissions could directly modify existing releases on GitHub without any checks from our CI/CD,” Klaba said. The option has since been enabled.
OpenSourceMalware says the attacker uploaded the binary over the original files of already published releases. Only builds for the most common platforms were replaced, which the researchers believe points to credential harvesting on developer and operations workstations.
The account belongs to a legitimate OVHcloud contributor. According to the researchers, it had been compromised since at least March 2026, when four of its personal repositories were rewritten, three of them to include a hidden loader.
The loader’s next stage queries the Solana blockchain for the location of a further payload, using a wallet that is a known GlassWorm indicator.
However, the researchers could not confirm that the same actor was behind the March account compromise and the October attack. “Whether the same actor did both is our inference,” they said. OVHcloud has not mentioned GlassWorm in its statements.
OpenSourceMalware could not obtain a sample of the payload for analysis before OVHcloud deleted the malicious files.
Users who installed or updated the CLI on macOS, 64-bit Linux, or Windows x86_64 via the official install script, Homebrew, or a direct GitHub download during the roughly 94-minute window are affected. Those who built from source, used Go’s install command, or pulled the official Docker image are not.

articles.title: NVIDIA Agent Toolkit Expands, Grounding Enterprise Agents in Company Data
articles.text:
Agents are only as useful as what they know, and only as trustworthy as the boundaries they run within.
Leading enterprises are using the open source NVIDIA Agent Toolkit — now expanded with new tools — to customize and control agents, use company data to inform their answers and actions, monitor what they do and govern how they operate.
NVIDIA Agent Toolkit comprises:
- The new NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation with NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries
- NVIDIA open models including Nemotron Retriever and the new Kumo family
- NVIDIA OpenShell secure agent runtime
- NVIDIA NemoClaw secure agent blueprints
- Tools and skills, like NeMo Relay and NeMo Compass
To develop agents that accomplish real work and are trustworthy from development to deployment, builders need an open agent stack that brings together the models, harness, runtime, data and tools.
NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation helps enterprises turn data into company intelligence agents can use. Agents can find relevant information, understand what it means for the business and use it to make predictions and help people decide what to do next. Companies can use Agent Knowledge Foundation without moving data, rebuilding existing workflows or changing governance controls.
The foundation features NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuDF, cuGraph, cuML, cuOpt and cuVS, and the new Auto-Ontology library, which translates raw company data into familiar business concepts — like customers, products and orders — and maps how they relate.
It also includes NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever and Kumo Structured open models — Kumo Tabular, Kumo Relational, Kumo Time Series and Kumo Forecast — which help agents find relevant company information to answer questions and make predictions.
OpenShell provides the secure runtime boundary, giving enterprises control over what agents can access and do. NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints provide reference designs for building secure, specialized agents. The newest NemoClaw blueprint for agent optimization provides a step-by-step starting point for improving agent intelligence — making them better at their jobs over time.
Enterprises Adopt NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation
The new NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation is already at work across enterprises.
With Palantir, NVIDIA’s supply chain organization is using Agent Knowledge Foundation through Palantir Foundry, Ontology and AIP to deploy specialized agents, create actionable intelligence from proprietary data, predict outcomes and optimize decision-making.
Databricks pairs NVIDIA Kumo Anomaly with Databricks Genie Ontology to power context-aware agents.
Snowflake is enabling customers to use the NVIDIA Kumo Engine and Kumo Relational open models in their Snowflake Notebook environments to unlock more predictive capabilities.
NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models make search faster and more accurate. Using the embedding model, Amazon OpenSearch Service improved relevance with fewer search steps and virtually no added latency. SAP’s fine-tuned reranker ran nearly 3x faster. ServiceNow improved reranking quality while cutting latency by nearly a quarter. Zoom is using Nemotron Retriever models to improve document understanding, search relevance and context retrieval for Zoom AI Services.
Amazon Web Services (AWS), ClickHouse, Cloudera, Cohesity, Dassault Systèmes, Dell, Elastic, Exa, IBM, NetApp, Oracle, Perplexity, Starburst and VAST Data are also among those building on Agent Knowledge Foundation.
Learn more by joining this GTC Berlin session on building, deploying and optimizing specialized agents in production.

articles.title: Exclusive: Plants can speak using electricity, so this startup built an AI model to decipher their language | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Justin Mast’s life was changed by a cyborg plant.
A few years ago, Mast was reading through some scientific literature when he stumbled upon research about a houseplant wired to a motorized stand. When the plant wanted more light, electrical signals flowed through the living tissues. A control board sensed the current and wheeled the plant closer to the light source.
“I’m like, what the heck?” Mast told TechCrunch. “That was the entry to the rabbit hole for me.”
Mast wound up partnering with Lee von Kraus, a neuroscientist who has worked with DARPA, to found Electric Plant, which has been spending the past three years collecting data to build a large language model, Bombadil, capable of interpreting the subtle electrical signals coursing through a plant’s stem and relaying details about the plant’s needs to growers.
The founders believe their model could one day lead to a tool that would let people “speak” to plants. “We’re listening more than we’re speaking, but listening’s the first step,” said Mast, co-founder and CEO of Electric Plant.
To bring its sensors and Bombadil to market, Electric Plant recently raised an $11.2 million seed round led by Onto Ventures and Climactic, with participation from Ponderosa, Endeavor Catalyst, Ludlow, Michigan Rise, The Fund, Schox VC, and Dug Song.
Even in the most controlled greenhouses, farmers and growers don’t have full visibility of what their plants require, Mast said. Traditionally, farmers, growers, and foresters have relied on coarse tools that react to plants’ demands for water, nutrients, or light. And tools like soil probes, handheld spectroscopes, and satellite imagery work well enough, but they leave much to be desired, Mast said.
“That technology is sophisticated, but its ability to get at the inside of the plant isn’t very sophisticated. Most of that stuff still lags quite a bit behind the real-time needs of the plant,” he said.
Electric Plant had to start somewhere, though, so it used those devices to train its Bombadil model, which is capable of interpreting electrical signals in about 125 different species. “We know the model will surpass a lot of that equipment,” Mast said.
The startup’s sensors are also significantly cheaper than existing tools, which generally cost thousands of dollars. “This is tens of dollars,” he said.
The sensors, about the size of a regular iPhone folded lengthwise, are attached to a plant using stainless steel screws. The screws must penetrate the cambium — the layer of living tissue just under the bark — to connect to the microvolt changes occurring within the plant. Data collected from these sensors is sent to a base station via a low-power wireless network.
Electric Plant only needs a couple sensors per acre for accurate results, Mast said. The data gets interpreted by Bombadil in the cloud, and the results are sent back to the customer, who can use it to, for example, adjust their watering or fertilizer schedules. Mast claims such a system can boost yields while reducing water use by 20% or more.
Mast wouldn’t disclose who Electric Plant’s initial customers are, but it’s easy to imagine applications in agriculture and forestry.
Bombadil’s first hundred-plus species runs the gamut of plant forms, from ferns, redwoods, and tomatoes to dahlias, Mast said.
“This is the most diverse model ever created on biological electrical signals,” he said. “No one’s ever done anything equivalent to this in the animal world.”

articles.title: Revolut sufre una caída masiva y no se puede ni usar la app ni pagar... o acceder a tu dinero
articles.text:
Revolut ha confirmado una caída masiva de sus sistemas que está impidiendo a los usuarios poder acceder a la app (y por tanto a sus cuentas) o poder pagar. Desde esta mañana, múltiples usuarios han reportado que no podían pagar con las tarjetas de Revolut, ni tampoco a través de sistemas de pago de terceros.
Ahora la compañía ha confirmado que ha sufrido una caída generalizada de sus sistemas que afecta a varios de sus servicios, aunque están trabajando en ello. Se desconoce cuándo volverán a estar operativos o qué nivel de disrupción está experimentando la compañía, así como las causas de la misma:
Actualmente estamos experimentando una interrupción en el servicio que afecta a varias funcionalidades, lo que podría hacer que algunos servicios no estén disponibles. Nuestro equipo de ingeniería está trabajando activamente para restablecer el servicio por completo a la mayor brevedad posible. Agradecemos su paciencia y pedimos disculpas por cualquier inconveniente que esto haya podido causar.
Actualmente, la web de servicio de la compañía confirma que 31 de sus instancias están afectadas o no disponibles, incluyendo los sistemas de registro, inicio de sesión, transferencias o pagos con tarjeta, sin que haya trascendido cuándo volverán a estar disponibles.
Si eres usuario de Revolut, te recomendamos estar atento al estado del sistema de la compañía y, mientras tanto, usar otros servicios bancarios alternativos.

articles.title: YouTube might be testing hiding the dislike button
articles.text:
YouTube appears to be testing hiding the dislike button on videos, as reported by 9to5Google. At least two users on X have recently shared screenshots of the dislike button now being placed in the three-dots submenu, and a user on Reddit also shared an image of the dislike button being absent for them.
YouTube might be testing hiding the dislike button
Some users have reported that their YouTube dislike button has been moved to the three-dots menu.
Right now, for me, the dislike button sits right next to the like button under a video. Moving it to a submenu would make it considerably more of an effort to access, meaning that fewer people would likely use it.
It’s unclear how widely this apparent test may be rolled out, and Google didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.
YouTube has shown a willingness to make changes to the dislike button. In 2021, it hid the public dislike count on videos to help “protect creators from harassment,” though creators can still see dislike counts. Earlier this year, YouTube removed the dislike button from YouTube Shorts, suggesting instead that users take advantage of options in the three-dots menu.

articles.title: University of Alberta partners with Silicon Valley VC firm to help commercialize research | BetaKit
articles.text:
The University of Alberta (U of A) is enlisting the help of a US venture capital firm to guide its staff in moving deep tech research from the lab to the marketplace.
The news: The U of A announced a partnership with Celesta Capital on Oct. 14. The aim is to bring Celesta’s expertise to the U of A’s students and staff with training on entrepreneurship, patents, commercialization, intellectual property, and more. The partnership will also include industry and venture capital summit events held at the university.
From the source: “The U of A produces research with global reach, and our job is to move that work into the world where it creates companies, jobs, and impact,” associate vice-president of innovation, knowledge, mobilization, and partnerships Darren Fast said in a statement. “Partnering with Celesta gives our researchers and founders direct access to investors and operators who have built deep tech companies at a global scale.”
The context: Celesta’s partnership with the U of A comes at a time when Edmonton’s startup ecosystem is betting on deep tech as the city’s next flashpoint. The news comes on the heels of an announcement by Edmonton Unlimited that it will launch a Deep Tech Foundry program early next year with the specific goal of meeting the unique demands of commercializing deep tech.
Programming under the Celesta-U of A partnership will launch later this month with Scientific Entrepreneurship Day. Coordinated between Edmonton Unlimited, Celesta, the Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute, and the U of A, the day will feature a curriculum designed to cover fundraising, intellectual property strategy, market validation, team building, and more.
Final thought: Celesta partner Charles Lespérance said Alberta broadly has the ingredients needed to develop a world-class deep tech ecosystem, including research expertise, technical prowess, and ambitious founders. But deep tech has historically faced unique hurdles to commercialization, including greater technical risk, high capital costs, and long research and development cycles.
That has created trepidation for some investors. Speaking at the NACO Summit this past summer, Émilie Boutros of TandemLaunch said deep tech companies often fail not on their technology, but due to a lack of business coaching. Celesta’s partnership with the U of A brings that coaching together with the resources Edmonton’s deep tech community already has.
BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.

articles.title: Pour laisser tomber la voiture en ville, ce vélo cargo électrique Fiido T2 avec 500 € de remise est une bonne idée — Frandroid
articles.text:
Avec le Fiido T2, vous avez un vélo électrique conçu pour la mobilité urbaine. Il est tout indiqué pour vous si vous habitez dans une grande ville et que vous n’avez pas besoin d’une voiture pour vos déplacements quotidiens. Ou, si vous êtes à la campagne et que vous souhaitez partir en promenade, en camping ou à la pêche avec tout votre matériel sur le porte-bagage. Ce modèle présenté ici peut porter 200 kg et vous accompagner théoriquement sur 136 km sans que vous ayez à fournir de gros efforts. Il se retrouve en plus en promo sur le site officiel de la marque avec 500 euros de réduction.
Pourquoi choisir le Fiido T2
- Pour sa capacité de charge de 200 kg (dont 80 kg sur le porte-bagages), de quoi transporter un ou deux enfants
- Pour sa batterie de 998,4 Wh et ses 136 km d’autonomie annoncée
- Pour son équipement de série complet avec béquille, garde-boue, éclairage et carénage de roue arrière
Sur le site de Fiido, le modèle longtail T2 dont il est question ici est affiché à 1 799 euros. Il est en promo à 1 499 euros et une fois dans le panier, il passe même à 1 299 euros.
Un design robuste et sécurisant pour un poids conséquent
Le Fiido T2 est un vélo électrique qui s’appuie sur un cadre en aluminium renforcé qui peut encaisser une charge utile de 200 kg : 120 kg sur la selle et 80 kg sur le porte-bagages arrière rallongé. Pour la sécurité des passagers, Fiido a intégré des flasques en plastique de chaque côté de la roue arrière, qui évitent que les pieds, les lacets ou les vêtements se coincent dans la roue. En parlant des roues, ce sont des modèles monobloc de 20 pouces, à bâtons, en alliage de magnésium selon Fiido. Pas de rayons à casser ni à retendre, donc. La contrepartie de cette robustesse est inévitable : le vélo pèse 39,5 kg et ça se sent au démarrage ou quand on le manipule à l’arrêt. Heureusement qu’il y a une béquille centrale pour faciliter son stationnement et une poignée d’assistance à la marche (jusqu’à 6 km/h) pour faire avancer le vélo à côté de soi sans effort.
Plutôt que d’opter pour un moteur pédalier onéreux, la marque a choisi un moteur moyeu placé dans la roue arrière, d’une puissance de 250 W pour 55 Nm de couple. Avec, et c’est une bonne surprise, un capteur de couple Mivice qui analyse l’effort appliqué sur les pédales en temps réel pour distiller l’assistance en douceur, de façon réactive, pour garder un pédalage naturel. Sur du plat ou du léger faux plat, le couple est suffisant pour avancer fluidement et un petit coup de mode Turbo permet un démarrage rapide quand le feu passe au vert. Mais si vous vous lancez dans une pente un peu abrupte, il va falloir fournir un certain effort musculaire, surtout si le vélo est chargé.
Un confort de fatbike avec un bon freinage
Pour pallier l’absence de suspension arrière, le T2 utilise des pneus CST ultra larges de 4 pouces. Avec un tel volume d’air, le vélo filtre bien les irrégularités de la route et les pavés, pour offrir du confort au conducteur et aux passagers. La fourche suspendue de 60 mm de débattement à l’avant se charge d’absorber les gros chocs. Comme le vélo porte des charges lourdes, Fiido se devait d’assurer côté freinage et c’est le cas : il est équipé de freins à disque hydrauliques avec des étriers à quatre pistons. Le freinage est ainsi puissant et mordant, ce qui est rassurant, surtout en ville. Le feu arrière intègre aussi une fonction feu stop, pratique pour prévenir les autres usagers d’un ralentissement.
Pour ce qui est de la batterie, il faut là aussi pouvoir tenir la route : Fiido intègre une batterie amovible généreuse de 998,4 Wh insérée verticalement derrière le tube de selle. Avec une telle capacité, la marque annonce une autonomie maximale de 136 km. Ce chiffre sort d’un test maison en mode Eco, avec 85 kg de charge (cycliste et équipement), sur terrain plat et à 27 °C. En mode Turbo et dans les mêmes conditions, Fiido descend déjà à 102 km. Le relief, le vent ou deux enfants à l’arrière feront encore baisser la note. Même chargé et avec une assistance au maximum, vous pouvez l’utiliser sur plusieurs dizaines de kilomètres sans vous inquiéter.
Si vous cherchez un vélo électrique d’une autre envergure, vous pouvez consulter notre guide sur les meilleurs modèles du moment, établi par nos experts en la matière.
