articles.title: How a blockchain marketplace is unlocking clean gas production in Kenya - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
African technologists and entrepreneurs are applying blockchain in innovative ways, creating a new financial infrastructure for the continent with wide-ranging benefits, including for the humanitarian sector.
Through its Blockchain Ventures investment programme, supported by the Ethereum Foundation and GSR Foundation, UNICEF Office of Innovation provides funding and technical assistance to emerging market startups building innovative blockchain-based solutions.
Kenya-based Autonomous Systems Research (ASR) began by exploring how drones could support disaster response, wildlife and environmental conservation. Working in remote areas led founder Moses Gichanga to investigate another challenge: generating electricity without transporting fuel into the field. ASR is developing ways to turn waste plant material into gas and electricity, and using blockchain to track traceability of biomass, payments to suppliers as well as applications in mobile money and disaster response.
How did a hobby building drones turn into Autonomous Systems Research?
Back in 2011, my daughter was two and a half and needed amusing, so I made her a kite. When the kite got boring, I built a small aeroplane out of paper bags. One early version had an eight-foot wingspan, with a laptop strapped to it and car wiper motors working the controls. Then I asked myself what would happen if I strapped a camera to one and flew it in a national reserve. That was when I started flying drones in Tsavo National Park.
I began asking how we could use this technology to help elephants and other wildlife, and to conserve ecological areas. That grew into Autonomous Systems Research. Later, ASR received its first grant from UNICEF Office of Innovation. We used it to explore whether drones could be useful for disaster response planning, ecological conservation, wildlife and agriculture, and what data would come out of that work. Since then, we have flown missions with government agencies, including Kenya Wildlife Service.
How did conservation work lead you from drones to producing energy from plant material?
Some of the places where we work are very remote and have no electricity. Our drones need charging, so we used a generator. But it became unsustainable to keep carrying fuel into the wilderness. We looked at solar panels, but they took up space and time. So we thought about modifying a generator to run on gas made from biomass. Later, people in communities saw that we had electricity in places without a supply and asked where we got it. We began thinking about making gas and electricity available to them too.
Where would the biomass come from, and what could the gas and electricity be used for?
We still use drones to look for potential sources of biomass. Once we identify some, we send someone to find out whether we can purchase it or otherwise acquire it. We want waste biomass. We do not want to cut down trees, and we do not want people planting biomass to sell to us instead of growing food. Coffee bushes, for example, produce material when they are pruned. We can turn that into gas.
We have developed equipment that converts biomass into gas, which we can use to run an engine. Gas is the primary thing we produce, but we can generate electricity as well. We have a site near our rural office where we are working with people who provide biomass and receive gas. We are also in the process of bringing local primary schools into the project. We are also in the process of brining local primary schools into the project. We want to see whether – with the right safety checks, ventilation and supervision – the gas could be used to cook meals and heat water, as an alternative to open fires.
You began using blockchain to track biomass. What does it record, and where else might you use it?
We wanted an audit trail that someone else could inspect. For the biomass, we record where it comes from, what type it is, the quantity, who gave permission to clear it, what they were paid, if anything, and how much gas we produced from it. We also have a payment mechanism for people who provide biomass, connected to mobile money platforms, M-Pesa and Airtel Money. We are interested in carbon credits in the future, and for that we would need a record people can trace.
We are looking at other applications too. Through our work on payments, we have engaged a local bank and are building a platform intended to offer mobile money services using blockchain. We also do volunteer work in emergencies, and we have developed a ledger system that can record where survivors are and what help they need after a disaster, though we have not applied that in a real-world setting yet.
What is holding the gas project back from operating at a larger scale?
We can produce the gas, but we have not reached the point of liquefying it efficiently. At the moment, we store it without liquefying it, which takes up more space. If we could liquefy it, we could fit more into a cylinder and look at selling it on a larger scale. We have tried some basic methods, but they use too much energy to work commercially. Finding a better way to do it would require substantial investment.
ASR began with drones, but you are now developing energy and other technologies. Is the idea to test solutions at ASR, then build separate businesses around the ones that work?
Yes. ASR does research into systems that can run themselves. That includes the drones and, eventually, the gas plant. When we develop a project, we intend to incorporate it as its own company, with its own governance structure, while ASR continues doing research.
We do not plan for ASR itself to become the gas supplier. The gas business could sell the product and make money as its own company, although we would still expect to have a role in its governance. We want to take an idea through the research and testing stage and then allow it to become something that can stand on its own.
ASR is a for-profit company, but you describe social good as central to its work. How do those aims fit together?
Social good is front and centre in what we do. Our tagline is “tools for transformative change”. We are structured as a limited liability company and we intend to make a profit, but we engage in projects that have a social good component.
We hope to make a lot of money. We want to do it in a way that helps our neighbours make money too. The more money they make, the less they need from us or from donors. There is a limit to how long someone can keep holding your hand. At some point, you need to become self-sustaining.
Take the gas project. We intend to sell the gas, but I also think about children collecting twigs for firewood. If we can make gas affordable to their households, they would not have to do that. I do not see a conflict between the social purpose and the business: we want to produce the gas cheaply enough that we can sell it at a price people can afford. As we see it, it is easier to get a shilling each from a million people than a million shillings from one person.
UNICEF was ASR’s first backer. Beyond the grant, what did its support make possible?
The first grant let us explore whether drones could be used for disaster response planning, conservation, wildlife and agriculture. Later, when we approached other organizations, we could show them what we had done and what we had learned. We have since received grants from other organizations, including Kenya’s National Commission for Science, Technology and Innovation, and done business with local government organizations.
We have also remained part of UNICEF’s alumni community since its investment. UNICEF organized a session for us with Google for Startups, and we later graduated from that programme. They organized seminars and workshops and supported our attendance at the World Economic Forum’s Annual Meeting of the New Champions. Those opportunities helped us think differently about what we could do.

articles.title: SpaceX sort une vidéo qui dévoile la future acrobatie du Starship
articles.text:
On savait l’ambition, on a maintenant une vidéo promotionnelle. Au détour de la présentation des résultats du troisième trimestre de SpaceX, un clip a été diffusé le mardi 20 octobre 2026 pour montrer à quoi devrait ressembler le prochain vol du Starship. Celui-ci est prévu au cours du mois de novembre, à une date qui reste à déterminer.
Ce quinzième test de la fusée géante de l’entreprise américaine doit être un jalon dans son développement, puisque c’est à cette occasion qu’un essai de capture de l’étage supérieur (le Ship) par une tour de lancement est attendu. Le premier étage (Super Heavy) doit aussi être récupéré de la même façon, grâce aux bras mécaniques de la tour, surnommée Mechazilla.
« Pour le vol 15, qui devrait avoir lieu le mois prochain, nous allons tenter d’attraper à la fois le propulseur et le vaisseau. Si nous réussissons, ce sera la première fois qu’un lanceur orbital aura été entièrement récupéré », a déclaré Elon Musk, CEO de SpaceX, à cette occasion, dans un extrait qui tourne depuis parmi les passionnés de SpaceX.
À quoi doit ressembler le vol 15 du Starship, idéalement
Elon Musk avait déjà évoqué plus tôt en octobre cette manœuvre aérienne, en prophétisant un vol dans quatre à six semaines. En réalité, cette acrobatie avec le Ship est dans les tuyaux depuis longtemps, notamment en 2025 ou courant 2026. Elon Musk l’annonçait même pour le vol 14. Le planning n’a pas cessé d’être remis à plus tard.
SpaceX rattrape déjà ses boosters Super Heavy avec la tour depuis octobre 2024, mais ce n’est pas systématique : cela dépend des objectifs recherchés et des conditions météorologiques. Lors du 14e vol, le 28 septembre, le propulseur avait fini sa course en mer, dans le golfe du Mexique. Le Ship, lui, a réussi son premier vol orbital.
Le but de SpaceX est de faire de Starship une fusée entièrement réutilisable. Avec la Falcon 9, sa fusée actuelle qui assure l’essentiel des lancements, cet objectif n’est que partiellement atteint. Seul le premier étage est récupéré et réutilisé, jusqu’à 37 fois pour le propulseur le plus utilisé. Le second étage, en revanche, est perdu à chaque vol.

articles.title: Hacker gets 8 years for stealing $3.3 million from taxpayers
articles.text:
A Nigerian national was sentenced to eight years in prison for his involvement in a series of spearphishing attacks targeting US tax preparation businesses since 2019.
40-year-old Chukwuemeka Victor Amachukwu (also known as Chukwuemeka Victor Eletuo and So Kwan Leung) has pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit computer intrusions and wire fraud after being extradited from France to the United States in August 2025.
"Chukwuemeka Amachukwu believed he was operating safely offshore when he targeted his victims, but he has now been held to account and now faces a serious sentence for his crimes," said US Attorney Jamie McDonald in a Monday press release.
"Amachukwu took part in sophisticated schemes to hack into US businesses, steal and use stolen identity information of victims, and commit fraud. These crimes imposed significant harm on the victims and the public, and so it is only appropriate that the crimes also come with a significant sentence for the defendant."
According to court documents, Amachukwu and his accomplices stole more than $3 million after filing fraudulent tax and loan applications with the Internal Revenue Service and state tax authorities using their victims' stolen personal data.
Together with co-defendant Kingsley Uchelue Utulu and other Nigerian co-conspirators, Amachukwu launched spearphishing attacks against tax preparation businesses in New York, Texas, and other US states between 2019 and 2021, gaining unauthorized access to their targets' computers and stealing the tax and personally identifiable information (PII) of at least 800 customers.
In total, he allegedly obtained about $2.5 million in fraudulent tax refunds (after filing for $8.4 million in refunds) and another $819,000 through fraudulent loan applications with the Small Business Administration's Economic Injury Disaster Loan program.
Amachukwu was also involved in a fake investment scheme that offered potential US victims investments in what the scammers described as valuable standby letters of credit. However, these investments did not exist, and the fraudsters stole more than $7 million from multiple victims.
In addition to the prison term, the court sentenced Amachukwu to one year of supervised release and ordered him to pay $3.6 million in restitution and forfeit nearly $11 million.

articles.title: Ver online Millonarios vs. Once Caldas con Fútbol Libre, Roja Directa o Xuper TV: el truco gratuito que podría entregar datos personales y financieros
articles.text:
Ver Millonarios vs. Once Caldas por enlaces de Fútbol Libre, Roja Directa, Xuper TV u otras plataformas no oficiales puede exponer datos personales, contraseñas e información financiera.
La expectativa por el partido, programado para este martes 20 de octubre, incrementa la circulación de páginas que prometen una señal gratuita, pero que pueden ocultar archivos maliciosos, formularios falsos y permisos que no corresponden a una transmisión deportiva.
El encuentro de la jornada 13 de la Liga BetPlay II-2026 se disputará a las 20:30, hora colombiana, en El Campín de Bogotá. Millonarios llega con 25 puntos y busca afianzarse en la pelea por los cuadrangulares, mientras que Once Caldas tiene 19 unidades y necesita sumar para mantener opciones de clasificación. La transmisión oficial estará disponible en Win Sports y Win+, incluidas sus señales básica y HD.
Las páginas gratuitas pueden pedir permisos que una transmisión no necesita
Las búsquedas para seguir partidos en directo suelen mostrar sitios que imitan servicios conocidos o cambian de dirección tras bloqueos. Algunos portales solicitan descargar una APK, instalar una aplicación o añadir una extensión al navegador antes de habilitar el supuesto vídeo.
Una plataforma destinada únicamente a reproducir fútbol no requiere acceso a contactos, mensajes, cámara, ubicación, archivos privados o funciones de accesibilidad. Si un enlace asociado a Fútbol Libre, Roja Directa o Xuper TV reclama esas autorizaciones, existe un riesgo de que el archivo contenga software ajeno a la transmisión.
El Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad de España advierte que las aplicaciones maliciosas se distribuyen con frecuencia mediante repositorios externos, enlaces directos y páginas que no cuentan con controles verificables. La descarga de una APK fuera de las tiendas oficiales facilita que circulen versiones modificadas, copias falsas y programas con funciones ocultas.
Un archivo instalado puede permanecer activo después del partido
El peligro no termina cuando concluye la transmisión. Una aplicación instalada desde una fuente desconocida puede ejecutarse en segundo plano, cambiar configuraciones del teléfono, abrir ventanas emergentes o redirigir la navegación hacia otros dominios.
También conviene desconfiar de extensiones que prometen eliminar anuncios, desbloquear partidos o mejorar la calidad de imagen. Algunas pueden registrar actividad de navegación, insertar publicidad o llevar al usuario a portales diseñados para obtener datos. El contenido deportivo funciona en esos casos como un reclamo para instalar programas que no tienen relación con el partido.
Las señales de alerta incluyen anuncios persistentes, aplicaciones que aparecen sin explicación, cambios en la pantalla de inicio, consumo inusual de batería y una reducción del rendimiento. El daño puede no ser inmediato: una transmisión puede reproducirse con aparente normalidad mientras un programa mantiene actividad durante varios días.
Los permisos pueden facilitar el robo de contraseñas
Una APK fraudulenta puede incorporar un keylogger, un programa capaz de registrar las pulsaciones realizadas en un teclado o una pantalla. Si, después de instalarlo, el usuario accede al correo electrónico, a una red social o a una aplicación bancaria, el software puede capturar nombres de usuario, contraseñas y otros datos sensibles.
El riesgo aumenta si la aplicación obtiene autorización para leer mensajes SMS. Muchas entidades financieras envían códigos de un solo uso para confirmar transferencias, recuperar claves o validar un inicio de sesión desde un dispositivo nuevo. El acceso a esos mensajes puede dejar expuestos códigos bancarios, verificaciones de correo y claves temporales de redes sociales.
Los permisos de accesibilidad requieren especial cautela. Estas funciones pueden permitir que una aplicación observe el contenido que aparece en pantalla o interactúe con otras herramientas instaladas. Una app para ver fútbol no necesita acceder a mensajes, contactos, ubicación ni accesibilidad para mostrar una señal de vídeo.
El ransomware puede bloquear fotos y documentos del teléfono
Otro riesgo asociado a las transmisiones piratas es el ransomware, un tipo de software malicioso que puede cifrar fotografías, documentos y otros archivos del dispositivo. Después, los responsables pueden exigir un pago a cambio de una supuesta recuperación de la información.
El uso de enlaces no oficiales expone tanto a teléfonos como a tabletas, TV Box y computadores. Si alguno de esos equipos está conectado a una red doméstica, el problema puede afectar otros dispositivos vinculados, como cámaras, sistemas de almacenamiento o equipos donde permanecen abiertas sesiones de correo y navegación.
Para seguir Millonarios vs. Once Caldas sin instalar archivos externos, la opción disponible es la transmisión de Win Sports y Win+. Si una página exige descargar una APK, desactivar protecciones del dispositivo o conceder permisos ajenos a la reproducción, la medida recomendable es cerrar el sitio.

articles.title: PS6 : et si la manette permettait de rendre les jeux plus fluides ?
articles.text:
L’optimisation des performances graphiques des jeux vidéo passe aujourd’hui par des algorithmes de plus en plus poussés que Sony compte bien utiliser pour sa PS6. Un nouveau document officiel déniché sur le web détaille justement une méthode de génération d’images qui va permettre d’améliorer la fluidité des images affichées sur votre TV ou votre écran de PC.
Anticiper vos mouvements grâce à la manette
Contrairement au DLSS qui récupère uniquement les données de mouvement depuis le moteur du jeu, le modèle imaginé par Sony intègre un paramètre supplémentaire qui exploite les informations de la manette pour anticiper avec plus de précision vos déplacements d’une image à l’autre. Avec cette approche, Sony cherche à limiter le décalage qui peut exister entre ce que vous faites avec la manette et ce qui s’affiche à l’écran (ce que l’on appelle l’input lag).
Le brevet mentionne également la prise en charge potentielle de la génération de plusieurs images, un procédé que l’on connait déjà sur PC avec les cartes graphiques haut de gamme comme la RTX 5090. Le brevet précise que « Dans certaines configurations, les prédictions ne se limitent pas à l’image qui suit immédiatement dans le flux », soulignant que le système de décodage peut être entraîné pour prédire un nombre variable d’images situées avant ou après l’image d’entrée. On peut se poser la question de l’utilité d’une telle option sur un téléviseur classique dont la fréquence se limite généralement à 120 Hz, même si le fait d’avoir le choix est toujours bon à prendre.
La PS6 prépare ses armes
Si la technologie en elle-même est intéressante, on espère que les studios ne l’utiliseront pas comme une béquille pour masquer une piètre optimisation de leurs jeux qui tourneraient, par exemple, à 20 images par seconde. Une telle pratique risquerait d’introduire des artéfacts visuels, même si l’intégration des commandes du joueur grâce à la manette pourrait en partie corriger ces défauts.
Découvrez : Notre test de la PS5 Pro : très fluide, trop chère
Cette trouvaille ne représenterait qu’une des briques technologiques de la PlayStation 6, Sony ayant récemment racheté une technologie d’IA pour encore plus de photo-réalisme. Il faudra bien ça pour justifier le prix de la PS6 qui s’annonce extrêmement salé.

articles.title: Llega a Lidl, el viernes 30 de octubre, la freidora de aire tipo Ninja Crispi que cuesta menos de la mitad y tiene más capacidad
articles.text:
Lidl acaba de renovar su catálogo de ofertas y lanzamientos, con un nuevo folleto cargado de novedades de lo más interesantes. Y si tuviéramos que destacar una, sin duda lo haríamos con su freidora de aire superventas con recipientes de cristal, la cual recuerda en diseño a la popular Ninja Crispi. Una freidora agotada online desde hace días pero que llega al fin a tiendas físicas de Lidl el próximo viernes, 30 de octubre.
Una alternativa low cost al modelo de Ninja
Hablamos de la Silvercrest »SHFDG 1500 A1«. Una freidora de aire que, tras ese nombre difícil de pronunciar, ofrece unas características muy parecidas al modelo de Ninja pero en versión low cost. El PVP de la Ninja Crispi es de 179,99 euros (aunque habitualmente suele estar rebajada), mientras que esta otra de Lidl se queda en 69,99 euros: algo menos de la mitad de su precio.
Donde más destaca esta de Lidl es en su buena relación calidad precio y en su diseño. Cuenta con doble cesta independiente de 2 y 4 litros (cada una, algo mayor en capacidad que las de la Ninja), ambas transparentes, que permiten retirarlas de la propia freidora y almacenarlas en la nevera (con las tapas que incluyen) o servir directamente en la mesa.
También cuenta con cuatro programas preestablecidos, una temperatura ajustable entre 60 y 200 grados y una potencia de 1.500 W. En conjunto, una estupenda opción si andábamos tras la pista de una freidora de aire con ese diseño tan característico y cada vez más extendido que permite ver lo que cocinamos en tiempo real. Sobre todo, si queremos gastar lo mínimo posible y la Ninja se sale del presupuesto.

articles.title: Inma y Jesús, españoles trabajando en Noruega: “Hemos ahorrado 10.000 € en tres meses; en España, con suerte, ahorrábamos 400 € al mes”
articles.text:
Inma y Jesús se van a trabajar durante algún tiempo a Noruega para ahorrar dinero y poder seguir viajando por Asia. “Hemos ahorrado 10.000 euros en tres meses; en España, con suerte, ahorrábamos 400 euros al mes”, comentan sobre su experiencia. En España antes ejercían como trabajadores sociales.
Antes de marcharse, los dos probaron a cortar gastos para poder ahorrar cada mes algo más. “Pensábamos que el problema era que gastábamos mucho”, afirman. Dejar de salir con amigos y de comprar ropa les parecía una forma rápida de acumular ahorros, pero apenas consiguieron un incremento con el que quedar satisfechos.
El proceso para encontrar trabajo llevó varios meses hasta que lograron dar con una oportunidad en el extranjero para trabajar en Noruega durante la temporada de verano. Llegaron a dedicar “cinco o seis horas diarias” a buscar empleo. Además de ello, el trabajo que consiguieron es temporal.
Ahorrar para seguir viajando
El cálculo a partir de las cifras que da la pareja es sencillo. Si ahorraran 400 euros al mes, les llevaría 25 meses ahorrar 10.000 euros. Suponiendo, claro está, que consiguieran mantenerse ahorrando esa cantidad todos los meses, ya que era lo que podían guardar en España en el mejor de los casos.
La pareja tampoco hace hincapié solo en el dinero, precisamente porque le gusta viajar y quiere poder elegir adónde va y cuándo. El alojamiento en Noruega es de pago, aunque la empresa para la que trabajan les proporciona una vivienda en un lugar remoto. Los dos aprovechan para explorar el entorno. Según Inma, esto les permite gastar menos en ocio.
El vídeo recoge una experiencia personal que puede ser muy diferente para otras personas. El mensaje advierte de que otros podrían ahorrar más o menos que ellos. Para valorar una oferta concreta, hay que tener en cuenta el sueldo neto y el coste del alojamiento.
 @elviajedejein Esta es una experiencia personal y no significa que todo el mundo en Noruega pueda ahorrar eso! Jajaja Quizás puedas ahorrar más o menos! En nuestro caso ha sido una decisión maravillosa que nos está permitiendo acercarnos más a la vida que de verdad queremos ❤️ #trabajarennoruega #noruega #españolesennoruega
♬ sonido original - Inma & Jesús
Buscar trabajo en Noruega
En primer lugar, hay que buscar ofertas de trabajo en Noruega. La búsqueda en plataformas como EURES, la red europea de servicios de empleo, nosotros ya te la hemos contado.
Por supuesto, las condiciones de cada oferta pueden ser diferentes, pero una forma de acotar la búsqueda es filtrarlas por el idioma de trabajo. Según el servicio público de empleo noruego Nav, al utilizar su buscador de empleo Arbeidsplassen, hay que elegir “Engelsk” dentro de “Arbeidsspråk” para mostrar los puestos que indican el inglés como idioma de trabajo. Esto es importante debido a las condiciones específicas de los puestos en lo que respecta al idioma.
Antes de solicitar un puesto, hay que fijarse bien en los requisitos de los puestos en los que uno esté interesado, ya que cada puesto puede indicar su propio nivel de dominio del idioma.
Cuando se llega a trabajar en Noruega, hay que revisar los términos del contrato, que debe proporcionar el empleador. Según la Inspección de Trabajo noruega, todos los trabajadores deben tener un contrato escrito. Para periodos laborales de más de un mes, debe estar firmado y listo lo antes posible o, a más tardar, siete días después del inicio del trabajo. Para periodos de un mes o menos, o si una empresa de trabajo temporal cede al trabajador a otra, debe estar listo el mismo día en que comienza el trabajo.
El salario mínimo y los impuestos
Como regla general, en Noruega no hay un salario mínimo garantizado por ley para todos los sectores. La Inspección de Trabajo noruega publica salarios mínimos para determinadas actividades, y es responsabilidad del empleador respetar los que correspondan.
Si la oferta de trabajo no se ajusta a un mínimo obligatorio, debe corregirse. Si una persona encuentra una oferta de trabajo concreta, tal vez incluso con el mismo salario que otra, eso no significa necesariamente que vaya a ahorrar la misma cantidad de dinero si trabaja allí. El importe del sueldo neto no podrá calcularse solo con el salario bruto anunciado, sin tener en cuenta la tributación aplicable.
En Noruega existe un sistema específico de tributación salarial para los extranjeros que gestiona la Administración tributaria. Se llama PAYE, es voluntario y aplica un tipo general del 25 %, con requisitos y excepciones. El trabajador puede optar por las reglas generales de tributación, tal y como explica la Administración tributaria sobre PAYE.
La Administración tributaria menciona que la mayor parte de los trabajadores extranjeros que llegan se incorporan al sistema PAYE al solicitar su tarjeta de retención fiscal. Esta tarjeta es un documento electrónico obligatorio para quienes trabajan en Noruega, no solo para los que están en PAYE, y, si no se dispone de ella, los empleadores deben retener el 50 % del salario.
Según la Administración tributaria, esta retención es un anticipo y puede no coincidir con la cantidad total de impuestos que se deberán. Aunque el asunto pueda resultar complicado, esa retención reduce el dinero disponible mientras se tramita la tarjeta, algo que afecta al ahorro con el que se pueda contar durante una estancia corta.

articles.title: Une panne handicape les abonnés Free, surtout dans le Sud de la France
articles.text:
Les signalements de panne Free sont assez nombreux ce mardi après-midi. Le réseau de l’opérateur tient à l’échelle nationale, mais c'est surtout dans le Sud de la France que l'internet fixe fait des siennes.
On imagine volontiers que Free s'en passerait bien, toujours est-il que l'opérateur est frappé par de petits incidents multiples dans plusieurs endroits de France. Ce mardi 20 octobre 2026, les signalements se multiplient et font état d'une coupure bien réelle, qui prive d'internet depuis ce matin des abonnés de Free, notamment dans les Bouches-du-Rhône, un département assez sévèrement frappé par les intempéries depuis cette nuit, avec d'ailleurs un décès à déplorer.
Votre Freebox ne marche plus ? La panne est bien réelle, mais surtout en Provence
Alors que se passe-t-il chez Free, en panne ce mardi comme le nos collègues de Frandroid le rapportent ? Sur Downdetector, deux signalements sur trois concernent la connexion Internet fixe, loin devant le Wi-Fi (17 %) et le réseau mobile (11 %). Pour savoir si les box sont réellement en cause, Clubic a essayé de se faire une idée de l'état du réseau Free. La plateforme Free-reseau.fr, qui justement interroge les équipements de l'opérateur toutes les quinze minutes, livrent des chiffres intéressants.
À 16h38 par exemple, seuls 27 équipements sur près de 23 700 ne répondaient plus, soit à peine 0,1 % du réseau. Le compteur affiche bien 202 incidents depuis minuit, mais la plupart sont survenus en pleine nuit, entre 0h30 et 4 heures, et ont été rapidement résolus. Vers 14 heures, rien de très important ne s'est produit.
Comment expliquer alors cette avalanche de signalements ? Free-reseau ne voit que les équipements de Free, pas un éventuel blocage plus loin sur la route des données. Pour faire le tri chez soi, le plus simple est d'ouvrir les mêmes sites en 4G. Si seule la connexion de la maison coince, le service technique répond au 3244, un numéro non surtaxé depuis une ligne Free. L'opérateur n'a, pour l'heure, fait aucun commentaire.
Dans les Bouches-du-Rhône, la fibre Free a par endroits décroché
Chez Free ce mardi après-midi, le problème se situe surtout en Provence. Le département des Bouches-du-Rhône concentre à lui seul 19 des 27 équipements hors service, et Salon-de-Provence figure d'ailleurs parmi les villes les plus citées sur Downdetector. Salon-de-Provence a été touchée dès le matin, puis la panne s'est étendue en fin de matinée à Miramas, Istres, Grans, Lançon-Provence, La Fare-les-Oliviers et Eyguières. Entre 14h30 et 15h10, elle a gagné Fos-sur-Mer et Port-Saint-Louis-du-Rhône. À 16h38, aucun de ces équipements n'était revenu. Ailleurs, quelques coupures isolées persistent, comme à Paris (rue Saint-Luc), Villeneuve-Saint-Georges, Villeneuve-sur-Lot, Colombey-les-Belles, et Marsillargues, dans l'Hérault, où un équipement ADSL ne répond plus depuis 2h45 environ.
La journée avait déjà mal commencé pour les clients Revolut, avec des cartes refusées, des virements bloqués et une application inaccessible dès le début de matinée. La néobanque britannique, qui assure que l'argent et les données de ses clients sont en sécurité, est hébergée chez Google Cloud, qui de son côté est touchée par un incident. D'autres banques européennes, britanniques surtout, ont également été touchées. D'après un site spécialisé, la région londonienne du géant américain aurait subi un incident électrique. Rien ne relie officiellement cet épisode aux soucis de Free, bien entendu. Mais pour ceux qui seraient clients Revolut et Free en même temps, et on imagine qu'ils sont des milliers, ce mardi est un vrai mardi noir.

articles.title: Boudées en Chine malgré Xpeng, les nouvelles électriques de Volkswagen pourraient finir en Europe — Frandroid
articles.text:
Il y a encore quelques années, les marques européennes cartonnaient en Chine. C’était notamment le cas des constructeurs allemands, tels que Volkswagen ou encore BMW et Mercedes. Mais tous ont subi de plein fouet l’offensive des marques chinoises, qui leur a fait perdre de très nombreuses parts de marché.
Les livraisons du groupe Volkswagen en Chine ont chuté de 36,6 % au deuxième trimestre 2026 sur un an, bien plus que le marché chinois, en recul d’environ 20 % selon le constructeur. Elles ont encore plongé de 38,5 % au troisième trimestre. Une enquête de Reuters publiée ce lundi 20 octobre montre que l’alliance nouée avec Xpeng pour inverser la tendance n’a, pour l’instant, pas tenu ses promesses.
Pour contrer ces difficultés, Volkswagen avait fait le choix en 2023 de nouer un partenariat stratégique avec Xpeng. Le but ? Profiter du savoir-faire de Xpeng en matière de voitures électriques, mais aussi de son expérience sur le marché chinois. Cette alliance a donné naissance à deux modèles, le SUV ID. Unyx 08 et la berline ID. Unyx 09. Volkswagen visait d’ailleurs haut, puisque ses documents internes, consultés par Reuters, tablaient sur 3 622 ventes mensuelles de l’Unyx 08 en Chine dès 2026.
Ce n’est pas la première alliance chinoise de Volkswagen : le groupe produit depuis des décennies dans le pays avec ses partenaires FAW et SAIC. D’autres constructeurs étrangers ont pris le même chemin, à l’image de Stellantis, qui s’est associé à Leapmotor en 2023. Volkswagen avait d’ailleurs lui aussi sondé ce constructeur la même année, selon deux sources de Reuters.
Mais trois ans après la signature avec Xpeng, le bilan est particulièrement décevant, comme le rapporte l’agence de presse Reuters. Entre son lancement en avril et la fin du mois d’août, l’ID. Unyx 08 ne s’est vendu qu’à 267 exemplaires par mois en moyenne en Chine, selon le cabinet ThinkerCar, soit à peine 7 % de l’objectif. Plus largement, Volkswagen perd beaucoup de terrain sur ce qui a longtemps été son marché le plus stratégique.
La Chine, qui a longtemps pesé près de 50 % des bénéfices du groupe, n’en représente plus qu’environ 10 % aujourd’hui. En 2019, Volkswagen Group China se disait capable de livrer 1,5 million de voitures électrifiées (100 % électriques et hybrides rechargeables) dans le pays en 2025. Le groupe n’y a finalement livré que 115 500 voitures 100 % électriques l’an dernier.
Plusieurs explications à cette crise
Selon l’association chinoise des constructeurs automobiles (CPCA), la part de marché du groupe Volkswagen en Chine est passée de 20 % en 2019 à 10 % sur les huit premiers mois de 2026. Comment expliquer un tel échec ? Il y a plusieurs raisons.
D’abord, le tarif. L’ID. Unyx 08 a été lancé en avril à environ 34 260 dollars (environ 30 500 euros). Au même prix, ses rivaux chinois offrent davantage de technologie, comme le Xiaomi YU7 et ses capteurs avancés ou le Zeekr 7X et sa recharge rapide. Entre avril et août, Xiaomi a vendu près de 57 000 YU7 et Zeekr plus de 21 000 7X, contre environ 1 300 Unyx 08, d’après ThinkerCar. Le tout dans un contexte de guerre des prix toujours très forte.
Volkswagen a d’ailleurs dû revoir sa copie. Depuis quelques semaines, le constructeur affiche l’Unyx 08 avec une remise de 17 % sur son prix de lancement d’avril. En interne, il avait déjà abaissé dès le début de l’année sa prévision de ventes pour 2026 de 32 600 à 12 300 exemplaires, soit plus de 60 % de moins, selon les documents consultés par Reuters.
Par ailleurs, les concurrents chinois sont également plus rapides pour dégainer de nouveaux modèles, plus modernes et avancés. Volkswagen peine donc à rivaliser, malgré un temps de développement raccourci. Volkswagen assure que la nouvelle architecture électrique développée avec Xpeng, qui doit servir de base à ses modèles fabriqués localement, a été conçue en 18 mois seulement, un record selon le constructeur.
Les ID. Unyx 08 et 09 en sont des retombées. Mais comme le résume Pedro Pacheco, vice-président de la recherche chez le cabinet Gartner, « les clients chinois se demandent : pourquoi acheter une voiture allemande chère s’ils peuvent obtenir la même technologie à un prix bien plus abordable ? ».
Le groupe allemand pâtit aussi de son réseau de distribution. La gamme ID. Unyx est surtout vendue par Volkswagen Anhui, une coentreprise dédiée à l’électrique, qui compte aujourd’hui 166 points de vente. Elle ne profite donc pas des plus de 3 000 concessions que Volkswagen exploite avec ses partenaires FAW et SAIC. Selon deux sources de Reuters, beaucoup d’acheteurs potentiels ignoraient même l’existence de l’Unyx 08.
En parallèle, Volkswagen se prépare à vendre en Europe une ou plusieurs de ses voitures électriques conçues pour la Chine. L’entreprise pourrait même les produire sur place, afin de faire tourner des usines actuellement en sous-activité.
La suite se jouera avec l’ID. Unyx 09, la berline issue de la même alliance, attendue dans les concessions chinoises ce mois-ci. Volkswagen n’a pas revu ses ambitions à la baisse pour autant : ses documents internes tablent sur près de 4 900 ventes par mois en moyenne, et plus de 90 000 par an d’ici 2034, selon Reuters. Après les 267 ventes mensuelles de l’Unyx 08, ces objectifs semblent pour le moins optimistes.

articles.title: AI startup Vectorial lands $3M in funding to simulate human behavior for consumer research - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI startup Vectorial lands $3M in funding to simulate human behavior for consumer research
Consumer research is a slow and cumbersome challenge that few companies do well, but if Vectorial AI Inc. is successful, they’ll never have to worry about doing it again.
The startup today said it has raised $3 million in seed funding to propel the launch of its new artificial intelligence-driven platform that simulates human behavior to generate valuable feedback for product development and marketing teams. Today’s round was jointly led by Smilegate and SenseAI Ventures, with additional funding coming from the ecosystem funds of the University of California at Berkeley and Stanford University. Angel investors from Meta Platforms Inc., Mastercard Inc. and Shopify Inc. also contributed to the round.
Vectorial believes it has identified a critical bottleneck in technology development. These days, virtually every company is using AI tools to generate massive amounts of code, accelerating the development of new software products and applications.
But consumer research is still stuck in the dark ages. Most firms still rely on outdated surveys of real audiences, which can take weeks to compile and complete, and are usually very limited in scale, with perhaps only 50 to 100 participants.
According to Vectorial co-founder and Chief Executive Taranveer Singh, many smaller startups simply avoid doing user research altogether, and just assume or hope they know what consumers actually want. But that’s hit-and-miss at best, and it leads to hours of wasted time and money spent on products no one needs.
“We believe AI is creating two distinct frontiers,” Singh told SiliconANGLE. “One focuses on reasoning and solving complex problems, while the other focuses on simulations and decoding human behavior.”
Rather than gather up real humans to test new products, Vectorial has built a platform that uses AI to simulate thousands of users within specified target demographics. It’s based on the concept of a “living model” of target customers that continuously updates itself to take into account emerging trends and behavioral shifts.
Singh says the feedback generated from these simulated audiences is extremely accurate, and he’s convinced that this method will become the standard for all new consumer products within the next four years or so. “Two pieces are missing,” he said. “The ability to simulate many scenarios, and the ability to bring your users into the same room as you build.”
Several other startups have tried to use AI to solve the consumer research conundrum before, but Singh believes that all of them have fallen short, because none of them actually models human behavior. One solution that’s been tried repeatedly is AI-moderated interviews, but these still take multiple days to organize because they’re still reliant on real humans, and they usually involve small sample sizes. Another popular approach is to use synthetic agents, but Singh says these lack grounding in real consumer behavior, which means their outputs can’t be trusted.
So how does Vectorial improve on these methods? Its solution is to embed its simulated audiences directly into companies’ development workflows, so developers receive a continuous flow of feedback that informs all of their decisions. Vectorial’s platform is powered by a behavior model called SAPIENS, which is continuously being trained on latent socio-demographic, psychographic and behavioral traits across a mammoth database of more than 2.5 million real consumers.
This makes SAPIENS 30% more accurate than general-purpose models when it comes to predicting consumer behavior, said Chief Product Officer Rahul Garg. It should get better too, for Vectorial will use the funds from today’s round to expand its behavioral dataset and build a more advanced model called SAPIENS 2.0.
“We continue to invest in our behavior model, but a model alone doesn’t solve the problem,” Garg said. “That’s why we put behavior models to work inside the product development loop. We believe this fundamentally changes how products are designed and built, because it puts users in the room where you build.”
The early results have been pretty good. Vectorial’s platform has already been put to use by e-commerce, gaming and healthcare firms such as GoodRx Inc., Boat, Everkind Inc. and Concrete Software Inc. Those customers run an average of 600 simulations per month, meaning they’re constantly getting feedback on every design change, feature implementation and so on. Vectorial has compared the findings of its simulated audiences with real user studies, and it typically achieves accuracy of around 86%.
This level of accuracy is one of the reasons why Rahul Agarwalla of SenseAI Ventures decided he had to back the startup. He said most companies struggle to understand their user’s needs, which means they’re hardly benefiting from the accelerated development times AI enables.
“Vectorial replaces the slow theater of surveys with millions of simulated humans using the product and providing insights,” he said. “This is a new class of AI designed to predict human behavior, and not just the next work like LLMs do.”

articles.title: NCC device verification questions Nigeria's phone imports
articles.text:
Nigeria’s telecom regulator launched a device verification tool that lets buyers check whether a phone is approved for use on local mobile networks. But enforcing compliance across an import-dependent market could test the agency’s technical reach.
With 99% of smartphones imported into Nigeria and an estimated 63 million mobile devices sold annually, the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) faces a market structured around multi-layered supply chains, informal distribution networks, and varied entry routes.
Launched on October 7, 2026, the NCC’s Device Checker requires consumers to dial *315# to verify whether a phone meets Type Approval requirements—the NCC’s mandatory regulation that all communication equipment must meet before connecting to local networks.
The regulator says the tool is part of a broader effort to enforce its Device Management System (DMS) under Section 132(2) of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003.
The checker uses a phone’s International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI), a unique 15-digit identifier, to verify its status against the NCC’s approved equipment records. By linking device records to import declarations, the regulator says it can investigate whether a phone was properly declared to the Nigeria Customs Service and trace the business responsible for importing it.
However, the stakes are substantial in a market that imports an estimated ₦50 billion ($30 million) worth of mobile devices every month. Its near-total reliance on imports creates a complex supply chain that could hamper enforcement.
As a result, a consumer whose phone gets flagged risks navigating an informal multi-tier supply chain with no clear recourse, no standard refund procedure, and no guarantee of compensation.
How device verification works across categories
Consumers can check a mobile device’s status by dialling *315#. Selecting “Check this device” on the menu displays whether the handset is NCC Type Approved and verified for use. Alternatively, buyers can retrieve the 15-digit IMEI code by dialling *#06# and entering it on the NCC’s online portal.
These verification methods enable buyers to detect non-compliant devices before completing a transaction rather than discovering issues after payment.
For personally imported devices, the workflow differs. Individuals bringing phones into the country for use with local SIM cards must contact the NCC via its 315 helpline for guidance on individual verification.
Foreign visitors roaming on international SIM cards do not need to register their devices. Devices connected to a local network before October 7 are automatically allowed. However, new, unverified handsets imported by visitors are subject to a cumulative 30-day grace period per year before registration becomes mandatory.
Commercial entities importing SIM-enabled hardware—including smartphones, tablets, connected laptops, smart meters, and point-of-sale (POS) terminals—must verify compliance with type approval before distribution.
Regulatory responsibility lies upstream: original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), commercial importers, and primary distributors are legally required to obtain Type Approval before offering hardware for sale.
The distinction between consumer verification and enterprise registration is critical: consumers verify network eligibility, whereas supply-chain entities bear the burden of regulatory compliance.
Through the DMS portal, the regulator states it can track SIM-enabled devices back to primary importers, log total import volume, and initiate sanctions against non-compliant entities.
However, backend traceability does not guarantee immediate redress for consumers when an unapproved device is flagged post-purchase.
Enforcement challenges in a fragmented market
Sellers in Abuja’s GSM Village support the regulator’s initiative, yet there are concerns that structural complexities within Nigeria’s device distribution networks could impede implementation. Elsewhere at Banex Plaza in Abuja, TechCabal‘s findings from sellers were not different.
Nigeria records an estimated 63 million mobile device sales annually. Trade data from Volza shows mobile phone imports totalled 4,886 shipments between July 2024 and June 2025, involving 11 international exporters and 12 registered major buyers in Nigeria.
While import metrics do not quantify grey-market volume, the NCC’s enforcement partnership with the Nigeria Customs Service highlights lingering vulnerabilities around grey-market imports and border smuggling.
In 2024, the Nigeria Customs Service reported 3,555 contraband seizures. Although specific device counts were omitted, persistent illicit inflows indicate that unapproved hardware continues to enter retail channels, creating post-purchase compliance risks for consumers.
Regularising upstream accountability
The NCC states that approximately 231 million active devices registered before October 7, 2026, have been automatically onboarded into the DMS database without requiring subscriber intervention. However, the commission did not disclose the number of devices flagged or pending clearance.
Merchants holding inventory imported before that date can regularise their stock by registering their business documentation and uploading batch IMEI records to the NCC enterprise portal. Support is available via the 315 desk.
This transition window aims to protect compliant trade vendors from regulatory penalties on legacy stock.
Traders contend that regulatory enforcement must target primary importers rather than downstream micro-retailers who lack the technical means to evaluate upstream Type Approval status.
Secondary retailers rarely receive customs documentation or Type Approval certificates from distributors. While this does not absolve vendors knowingly trading in illicit goods, it creates operational friction when stock is acquired in good faith.
The NCC’s digital ledger could help trace undeclared devices to sellers and suppliers. But as Ogoh suggests, having “empirical data” is only the first step; turning that evidence into accountability and consumer refunds remains the bigger test.
The commission indicates that these audit trails help regulators distinguish between deliberate contraband trading and inadvertent distribution by secondary vendors.
However, audit trails alone do not determine financial liability or resolve refund disputes once non-compliant hardware has passed through multiple intermediaries to reach end users.
Enforcement and consumer protection
Consumer protection underpins the rationale for the Device Checker. Yet the tool’s impact will depend on whether enforcement mechanisms can penetrate multi-tiered supply chains to guarantee consumer indemnification.
Although the regulator maintains that automated verification prevents erroneous network blocking, dispute resolution remains complex. Nigeria’s Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018 grants rights to repair, replacement, or refund for non-compliant goods, but practical enforcement across informal markets remains difficult.
The Device Checker’s ultimate success hinges on converting technical detection into actionable consumer safeguards. Identifying unverified IMEIs offers little relief to buyers left holding deactivated hardware without a clear, enforced refund path in informal trade hubs.
To scale sustainably, the NCC must strengthen inter-agency coordination with the Nigeria Customs Service to stop unapproved hardware at entry ports rather than at retail points of sale. Without stringent primary-importer enforcement and structured consumer indemnities, digital verification risks transferring systemic supply-chain failures onto consumers.

articles.title: Accenture, Dragos, SANS Launch $10M Initiative to Defend Small US Utilities
articles.text:
Accenture, Dragos and the SANS Institute on Tuesday announced the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation, which aims to help under-resourced US water, electric and natural gas utilities protect their operational technology (OT) environments.
They are putting up roughly $10 million to start, a mix of funding and services. The first phase will cover up to 500 utilities, which will get free security tools, equipment, deployment help and training.
To qualify, a water, wastewater, electric or natural gas utility must be based in the US and bring in under $100 million a year. The companies estimate that this bar covers more than 50,000 organizations, or over 97% of US utilities.
Each participant gets the Dragos Platform and related services, with Accenture handling setup, integration and continued support. SANS will train utility staff in ICS/OT security so they can run their defenses internally.
The foundation will also fund the hardware needed to deploy and run the Dragos Platform. It will connect participants to a peer network of utilities that share operational experience.
The companies say many small utilities struggle with limited funding, workforce shortages and aging technology, especially those serving rural or underserved communities. They also cited recent attacks on more than 100 US water systems across over a dozen states.
“Adversaries are aggressively targeting utilities, attacking the operational environments that provide life-sustaining services to millions of Americans. Yet many small operators lack the capacity to defend against these threats,” said Dragos CEO Robert M. Lee.
The foundation builds on the Dragos Community Defense Program, which gives more than 100 utilities free access to the Dragos Platform. Dragos launched that program in December 2023 for US utilities with less than $100 million in annual revenue.
The announcement comes four months after Accenture agreed to acquire a majority stake in Dragos. The deal was part of an OT cybersecurity push valued at roughly $4.1 billion.
Related: Siemens Software Center Vulnerability Exploited in ClickFix Malware Attacks
Related: Supermarket Refrigeration Attack Widens to Copeland, Dixell Controllers
Related: AI Agents Navigate Unfamiliar OT Systems and Move Equipment in Minutes, Booz Allen Finds

articles.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
articles.text:
AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.
How Scientists Tested Perceptions of AI Consciousness
Published in the journal Cognition, the study was led by Dr. Louis Longin of LMU's Chair of Philosophy of Mind, working alongside Dr. Bahador Bahrami, Professor Ophelia Deroy, and other researchers.
"Whereas previous studies have typically asked general questions about whether AI actually has mental states, our study is the first to directly compare how people attribute the same mental states to AI and humans behaving in exactly the same way, under identical circumstances," says Longin.
"We may be using mental terms to refer to AI, but this may only be because we lack better words," says Ophelia Deroy, philosopher and a senior author of the study. "After all, AI is trained to act and speak like a human, so these descriptions seem natural."
To investigate how people judge consciousness, the researchers conducted experiments involving nearly 1,100 participants. One group read brief descriptions of artificial agents that showed different levels of responsiveness to their environments. For example, some agents reacted to sounds or recognized the emotional states of others.
Another group encountered the same situations, except the characters were described as humans rather than AI systems. Participants then evaluated how conscious or aware each character seemed to be of its surroundings.
A Surprising Gap Between Human and AI Consciousness
The experiments revealed that responsiveness influenced how participants judged both humans and artificial intelligence. Characters that reacted more actively to their surroundings were generally considered more conscious and more aware.
However, a striking difference emerged when participants evaluated consciousness specifically. Even the most responsive AI was rated as less conscious than the least responsive human. In other words, identical behavior did not lead people to assign the same level of consciousness to humans and machines.
The results changed considerably when participants were asked about awareness instead. For this characteristic, judgments of humans and AI followed largely similar patterns, suggesting that people interpret awareness and consciousness in fundamentally different ways.
"There is a growing worry in public discussion that people will see AI behaving in a human-like way and start treating these systems as if they had human-like mental states," says Longin, lead author of the study. "We found something much more nuanced: People are quite willing to say that an AI notices things and is aware of its surroundings. But they clearly draw a line when it comes to the term 'consciousness'. People consistently attribute less consciousness to AI than humans -- even when their behavior is identical."
Although people sometimes describe AI as conscious when discussing its actions, the findings indicate that they still distinguish between artificial systems and human minds.
Why One Word Changes How We Perceive AI
The researchers believe the difference between consciousness and awareness offers an important insight into how people understand artificial intelligence.
Awareness is a relatively neutral term that can describe an agent's ability to detect and respond to information in its environment. Consciousness, however, carries deeper implications about subjective experience and what it means to have an inner mental life.
Because awareness focuses more directly on observable behavior, people appear comfortable applying it to both humans and AI. Consciousness carries a different meaning, leading people to judge the two much less similarly.
The findings also highlight why the language used to discuss artificial intelligence matters, particularly as AI systems become increasingly capable of producing convincing human behavior.
"Our study teaches us lessons for how we communicate about AI," says Bahador Bahrami, who is also a senior author of the study and an expert in social neuroscience. "Companies and journalists often reach for hyped descriptions of AI models, and credit them with intentions, plans, or even moral conscience and hesitation. What our study shows is that everyday judgments are much more discriminating: People do not simply put AI and humans on the same mental scale. But the boundary also depends on which terms we use. For more neutral descriptors such as 'awareness', the distinction can largely disappear. That makes our choice of language important."
Story Source:
Materials provided by Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Louis Longin, Jurgis Karpus, Nadine Meertens, Bahador Bahrami, Ophelia Deroy. AI is not as conscious as humans: Essentialism in mental state attributions to artificial systems. Cognition, 2027; 278: 106733 DOI: 10.1016/j.cognition.2026.106733
