articles.title: TikTok staff raised child safety concerns, but executives reportedly failed to act | TechCrunch
articles.text:
TikTok was repeatedly warned by employees about the risks the social media platform posed to children, according to court records obtained by NPR. The documents say employees were frustrated with how executives responded to their concerns about risks to children, including sexual exploitation and exposure to suicide-related content.
Depositions of employees filed in March 2026 are shedding new light on TikTok’s child safety practices.
According to NPR, TikTok employees warned that minors were appearing in sexual content that was available for purchase on TikTok, raising concerns that the company could profit from potentially illegal activity. They also flagged that minors were exploiting loopholes to access age-restricted content and hide their activity from parents.
Additionally, the court documents show that TikTok didn’t conduct surveys to determine the age of its users out of concern that it would have to share the results with the Federal Trade Commission.
“These citations and claims are clearly cherry-picked at the behest of trial lawyers and used to inaccurately rewrite our history and mislead the public about our commitment to youth safety and how our platform works,” a TikTok spokesperson said in an emailed statement to TechCrunch. “It’s unfortunate that NPR has chosen to ignore the numerous documents and resources we have provided that demonstrate how these claims mischaracterize our record and platform features.”
The statement continues, “We have invested billions of dollars in Trust & Safety and rolled out more than 50 preset safety, privacy, and security settings for teens, including Family Pairing, which helps parents and guardians customize the experience for their teens. We remain steadfast in our commitment to the well-being of our community.”
TikTok, in addition to Meta, Google, and Snap, faces hundreds of lawsuits consolidated in federal court. The lawsuits allege that these companies’ platforms harm minors and that they failed to disclose known risks to young users.
TikTok has reached settlements in several of these cases before they went to trial, including one in Los Angeles where a jury found that Meta and YouTube had designed their platforms to be addictive to young users.
Update 10/20/2026 10:00 a.m. PT: The article was updated to include a statement from TikTok.

articles.title: NVIDIA Open Models Advance Europe’s Sovereign Intelligence Across Industries
articles.text:
NVIDIA is expanding its family of open models across language, robotics, biology, and quantum computing, giving developers, researchers and enterprises what they need to build applications tailored to local languages and industries
The portfolio includes the new NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt models; new NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models for embedding, reranking and document parsing; the new NVIDIA Kumo family open weight foundation models and libraries for structured business data; NVIDIA Cosmos 3.5 world models; NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge for autonomous vehicles; NVIDIA BioNeMo for healthcare and scientific discovery; and NVIDIA Ising for quantum computing.
The open models give organizations a foundation they can customize with local data and deploy on infrastructure they control.
NVIDIA Nemotron Powers Post-Training Across Industries
NVIDIA Nemotron brings open language models, datasets and recipes to developers building agents. The models support text and images, helping agents orchestrate workflows, reason through complex problems and complete specialized tasks at a lower cost. Nemotron models are built with data, research and expertise from the NVIDIA Nemotron Coalition, including European partners Black Forest Labs, H-Company and Mistral.
Nemotron provides a foundation for enterprises to build applications based on their own knowledge and expertise. Dassault Systèmes, Domyn, Dream, Palantir’s customers, Salesforce, SAP, Shopify, Synopsys and WPP, as well as professional services providers like Accenture and EY, are working with Nemotron models and datasets to create custom models and build domain-specific agents.
A broad ecosystem of post-training partners, including AfterQuery, AgileRL, AI21, Alice, Applied Compute, Baseten, CoreWeave, Distil Labs, EON, Fastino, Fireworks, Google Cloud, Mercor, Multiverse Computing, Nebius, Handshake AI, Plurai, Prime Intellect, River.AI, Scale AI, Trajectory and TNG, is helping enterprises customize Nemotron for domain-specific workloads.
NVIDIA Kumo Speeds Agents’ Work With Structured Enterprise Data
NVIDIA Kumo open foundation models, libraries and tools help agents and applications forecast outcomes, score fraud risk and recommend actions from structured business data. Part of NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation, Kumo shortens time to prediction and reduces the cost and complexity of building a separate machine learning pipeline for every task.
Developers can use pretrained Kumo models to bring predictions to more applications quickly, then fine-tune them using proprietary data when higher performance is critical. The portfolio includes NVIDIA Kumo Structured, with models for relational and tabular prediction, forecasting and anomaly detection, and NVIDIA Kumo Engine, an open library stack for developing and deploying structured data foundation models.
Cognite, Coinbase, Databricks, DoorDash, Revolut and Tubi are among the first to work with Kumo models to accelerate development. Snowflake customers are already using Kumo models to accelerate AI development in industries including advertising, energy, financial services and retail.
NVIDIA Cosmos Accelerates Robotics Training and Simulation
NVIDIA Cosmos is a family of open world foundation models that helps developers build robots, autonomous vehicles and vision agents that understand and interact with the physical world.
NVIDIA is introducing new Cosmos post-training and optimization tools to help developers improve world models using less compute, along with simulation checkpoints for evaluating behavior in interactive driving and robotic manipulation scenarios before real-world testing.
NVIDIA is also introducing Cosmos Data Factory — comprising blueprints and core agent skills — to help developers curate, label, generate and evaluate training data for driving scenarios, product defects, image augmentation and event generation. Developers can use complete workflows or individual capabilities with agents coordinating the process.
Porsche with Voxel51, ANYbotics with Encord, Zalando and CEVA Logistics with Sereact, and Siemens are using Cosmos Data Factory to create high-quality, diverse training datasets and improve model precision.
NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Brings Real-Time Reasoning to Autonomous Vehicles
NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge is a compact reasoning model that brings real-time scene understanding and motion planning directly into autonomous vehicles. Built on NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge’s Nemotron-based foundation and optimized for the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor platform, it helps developers bring advanced driving capabilities into vehicles with lower computing requirements.
NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina Advances Protein Design
NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina is an open protein design model from NVIDIA and the Baker Lab at the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design.
The model generates protein sequences and 3D structures to help researchers design proteins that bind to difficult targets, assemble into complex structures and bind to small molecules.
NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina delivers leading performance across more than 10 protein design tasks and generates designs about 13x faster than RFdiffusion3 in a benchmark of 200 amino acid proteins. Researchers can use the model through agents to generate and evaluate candidates against design goals and molecular constraints, then choose which designs to test in the lab.
NVIDIA Ising Accelerates Quantum Development
The NVIDIA Ising family of open models provides a common, extensible foundation to speed the breakthroughs needed to develop useful quantum supercomputers, from real-time hardware calibration to error correction, across different qubit modalities and tailored to individual hardware needs.
IQM Quantum Computers is using Ising to calibrate its quantum processors, showcasing how specialized open calibration models outperform large general-purpose models. SEEQC is combining the NVIDIA NVQLink platform and Ising with its unique Digital Link to meet the low-latency requirements needed for real-time quantum error correction.
AWS is making NVIDIA Ising readily available to researchers by integrating the model family into AWS Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS). While decoding is typically performed on classical hardware colocated with the quantum processor due to latency requirements, the AWS PCS integration lets researchers build on Ising prior to deployment.
Availability
- NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is available on Hugging Face, ModelScope, OpenRouter and build.nvidia.com as an NVIDIA NIM microservice, as well as through NVIDIA cloud, post-training and inference partners. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is expected to be available on Friday, Oct. 23.
- NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever open models are available on Hugging Face, various partner platforms, and as an NVIDIA NIM microservice on build.nvidia.com.
- NVIDIA Kumo open models are available on Hugging Face and optimized and packaged as an NVIDIA NIM microservice for production inference on build.nvidia.com.
- NVIDIA Cosmos is now openly available on Hugging Face and GitHub, and through select inference partners.
- NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge will be available for download on GitHub and Hugging Face later this month.
- The NVIDIA BioNeMo open model RFD4-Proteina is available on build.nvidia.com and as an NVIDIA NIM microservice, as well as on GitHub, Hugging Face and through select inference partners.
- NVIDIA Ising is available on GitHub, Hugging Face and build.nvidia.com.

articles.title: Solid-state batteries
articles.text:
Solid-state batteries
Batteries that swap liquid electrolytes for solid materials promise to charge faster, last longer, and (crucially) run cooler.
The rise of the lithium-ion battery, which powers everything from the smallest personal electronics to gargantuan energy storage systems, has been nothing short of revolutionary. But as anyone who’s boarded a plane in the last decade could tell you, storing and pumping out energy by moving charged lithium ions through a liquid electrolyte soup has its drawbacks, not least that the batteries have a troubling tendency to catch fire. Enter the solid-state battery, which swaps liquid for a solid ceramic or polymer, creating power packs that charge faster, last longer, cram more energy into smaller spaces, and (crucially) run cooler. A new generation of companies aim to bring such batteries to market, and if their bets pan out, the tech could substantially ease the shift away from fossil fuels.
The sticking points
Solid-state batteries have been “just a few years away” for more than a decade now. In laboratories, the technology works. But there have been challenges. In designs that pair the solid electrolyte with a lithium-metal anode (the side of the battery that releases electrons into an electrical circuit), needlelike filaments called dendrites tend to grow during charging, and they eventually push through the electrolyte and short the cell. Solid electrolytes are supposed to physically block the formation of dendrites, but many of them crack as the treelike projections break through like roots in a concrete foundation.
Then there’s the problem of manufacturing at scale. Mass production requires large quantities of defect-free sheets of ceramic-like material to make the electrolytes as well as dry rooms for assembly, since those electrolytes have a tendency to react with water. Would-be manufacturers quote a range of potential prices for solid-state batteries, but most expect them to fall in line with lithium-ion packs sometime in the mid-2030s.
The progress
Nascent as the technology is, solid-state batteries have already seen high-profile missteps. But one of America’s most advanced solid-state-battery companies says it’s closing in on being able to bring its product to market. The Bill Gates–backed QuantumScape launched in Silicon Valley in 2010 and built its battery around a class of ceramic materials that it says is compatible with lithium—meaning no dendrite formation. “We spent, then, like 10 years learning how to process it to satisfy all of the other requirements,” says Tim Holme, QuantumScape’s cofounder and chief technology officer. In 2025, the startup announced a proprietary, large-scale manufacturing method for quickly producing and heat-treating the ceramic electrolytes used in its batteries. “Nobody has ever done this in the field of ceramics before,” Holme claims. For 10,000 years, producing ceramics has involved slowly cooking the starting materials in an oven over the course of days. “We figured out a way to shorten that down to several minutes,” he says.
Plenty of other companies are pushing the tech forward as well. Toyota, the world’s biggest automaker, launched a research program on solid-state batteries way back in 2010. It’s now partnering with the global energy and petroleum company Idemitsu Kosan on a pilot plant, promising cars that can travel up to 745 miles after charging 10 minutes or less—a huge leap, if it works out. In China, CATL, the giant behind roughly 40% of the global battery market, is aggressively pursuing solid-state batteries too, pumping nearly $2.6 billion into a research program in 2024 alone. Mercedes, meanwhile, equipped one of its EQS sedans with solid-state batteries last fall; after driving nonstop for 750 miles, the car still had some range to spare.
Will the tech gain traction? Investing in vehicle batteries makes sense given the size of the potential market. But any little uptick in cost typically gets passed on to buyers, so the first solid-state EV batteries will inevitably be more expensive.
Grid storage buyers, who are working to meet the increasing demands posed by data centers, may also hesitate to purchase new technologies that still haven’t come down the cost curve. Then again, the promise of energy storage that lasts longer than lithium-ion’s typical eight hours could make them easier to persuade.
Some companies are taking a page from a playbook employed by outfits pursuing fusion: Focus on near-term markets with better margins to help fund development and bring down costs. Solid-state firms including California-based Solid Energies and Arizona-headquartered Sion Power are looking at selling batteries to the aviation industry or the military. “Those are sectors that are less sensitive to cost, and they typically require lower volumes as well,” says Evelina Stoikou, head analyst for battery technologies and supply chains at the consultancy BloombergNEF. “It’s a good way to prove your concept, then go through and fund the pilot plant where you can make that and eventually scale up.”
Progress meter ............ 7
The technology works, the capital is there, and demand is not far behind. But as with anything in manufacturing, unknown unknowns remain.

articles.title: SpaceX und Tesla sprechen über Fusion – angeblich ohne Musk
articles.text:
Die von Tech-Milliardär Elon Musk geführten Unternehmen Tesla und SpaceX prüfen einen rekordträchtigen Zusammenschluss. Der Autobauer und die Weltraumfirma hätten dafür auf Wunsch von Aktionären spezielle Ausschüsse gebildet, sagte Musk in einer Videokonferenz zu den Quartalszahlen von SpaceX. Er sei wegen möglicher Interessenkonflikte nicht Teil davon. Musk ist Großaktionär beider Firmen – und diese Anteile sind die Basis seines Vermögens von geschätzt rund 920 Milliarden Dollar (820 Mrd. Euro), das ihn zum derzeit reichsten Menschen der Welt macht.
Über eine Fusion von Tesla und SpaceX wird schon lange spekuliert, Musk äußerte sich dazu bisher ausweichend. Jetzt sagte er, er persönlich finde, ein solches Zusammengehen sei eine gute Idee. Es wäre aber „übertrieben“ zu sagen, dass es „mit Sicherheit“ dazu kommen werde, schränkte er ein. Musk verwies unter anderem darauf, dass für einen solchen Schritt die Zustimmung von mindestens 50 Prozent aller Tesla-Aktionäre notwendig wäre.
Billionen-Bewertungen für SpaceX und Tesla
SpaceX ist an der Börse aktuell mehr als 1,9 Billionen Dollar wert und Tesla rund 1,48 Billionen Dollar. Es wäre damit die bisher gewichtigste Fusion zweier Firmen.
In beiden Fällen sind die hohen Bewertungen in hohem Maße eine Wette darauf, dass Musk seine Versprechen künftiger Erfolge einlösen kann. Er will Tesla vom Verkauf von Elektroautos auf selbstfahrende Robotaxis und humanoide Roboter umstellten. In beiden Bereichen trifft die Firma auf starke Konkurrenz. SpaceX fing mit Raketenstarts an, verdient das Geld inzwischen aber vor allem mit dem Satelliteninternet-Dienst Starlink und KI‑Rechenzentren. Musk stellt für die Zukunft auch Rechenzentren in der Erdumlaufbahn in Aussicht – allerdings gibt es Zweifel, ob das machbar ist.
Mehr Macht für Musk
Bei SpaceX hat Musk bereits die volle Kontrolle dank Aktien mit mehr Stimmrechten. Bei Tesla folgt die Mehrheit der Aktionäre zwar auch seinen Wünschen – aber Musk will schon seit Jahren seine Führungsposition mit einer höheren Beteiligung absichern. In Erinnerung blieb etwa sein Spruch, er wolle keine «Roboter-Armee» bei Tesla bauen, solange ihn jemand vom Chefposten verdrängen könne.
Vergangenes Jahr gewährten ihm Tesla-Aktionäre die Aussicht auf ein riesiges Aktienpaket. Allerdings müsste Tesla dafür hochgesteckte Zielmarken erreichen, die aktuell nicht sehr realistisch wirken. Bei einer Tesla-Übernahme würden die Vorgaben aber hinfällig. Und Musk bekäme die Kontrolle, die er immer haben wollte.
Multimilliardär mischt in der Politik mit
Musk ist für seine rechten politischen Ansichten bekannt. Er spendete 2024 mehrere hundert Millionen Dollar für den Wahlkampf von Donald Trump und wurde zeitweise zu einem der engsten Vertrauten des US-Präsidenten. Aktuell gibt er wieder in großem Stil Geld für den Parlamentswahlkampf von Trumps Republikanischer Partei aus. Im Präsidentenauftrag sollte Musk im vergangenen Jahr die US-Regierungsausgaben kürzen und erntete dabei viel Kritik für sein rabiates Vorgehen.
Das politische Gewicht des Multimilliardärs und seiner Unternehmen in Washington ist weiterhin groß. Die SpaceX-Raketen sind aktuell unverzichtbar für die US-Raumfahrt – militärische Programme inklusive. Auf Starlink ist die Ukraine zur Verteidigung gegen russische Attacken angewiesen – und Musk soll laut Medienberichten eine Rolle bei der jüngsten Drosselung des Dienstes dort gespielt haben. Er ist auch Co-Chef eines Gremiums, das das Pentagon zur Kriegsführung der Zukunft beraten soll, zu der nach US-Gedankenspielen auch Roboter wie Teslas Optimus gehören könnten.
Tesla-Aktionäre erwarten nicht viel
Nach der Ankündigung legte die Tesla-Aktie im nachbörslichen Handel um gut zwei Prozent zu. Das ist ein Zeichen dafür, dass sich Anleger keinen großen Aufpreis bei einem Zusammenschluss mit SpaceX erhoffen. Musk hatte bereits seine KI-Firma xAI, die nicht an der Börse notiert war, in SpaceX aufgehen lassen.
Der Investor und langjährige Branchenanalyst Gene Munster verwies zugleich darauf, dass ein Zusammengehen wirtschaftlich Sinn ergeben könne. Tesla habe, was SpaceX bisher fehle: die Möglichkeit, Künstliche Intelligenz über Fahrzeuge und Roboter mit der realen Welt interagieren zu lassen, argumentierte Munster im Wirtschaftssender CNBC. Deswegen gehe er von einer Zustimmung der Aktionäre aus. „Es wäre in jeder Hinsicht das einzigartigste Unternehmen der Welt.“
Tesla und SpaceX kooperieren bereits bei der gewaltigen Chipfabrik Terafab, die Musk in den USA bauen will. Bisher wird dafür erst noch das Grundstück freigemacht. Ein weiteres Produkt der Zusammenarbeit sind Kaltgas-Raketendüsen von SpaceX zumindest auf einigen Varianten eines neuen Tesla-Sportwagens, der laut Musk 2028 in die Produktion gehen soll.
Zwei Starship-Starts pro Woche?
Musk machte in der Videokonferenz wie so oft weitreichende Versprechen. So sagte er, dass die große SpaceX-Rakete Starship, die bisher erst 14 Mal testweise flog, gegen Ende kommenden Jahres zweimal pro Woche starten solle. Vor drei Monaten hatte er allerdings noch von täglichen Starts gesprochen. Auch kündigte Musk an, dass die Zahl der Starlink-Satelliten binnen drei Jahren auf 100.000 steigen werde. Nach jüngsten Angaben waren es etwas mehr als 10.000.
SpaceX: Schwarze Zahlen nach langer Durststrecke
Im vergangenen Quartal verbuchte SpaceX nach langer Durststrecke einen Milliardengewinn. Auslöser waren vor allem kräftige Zuwächse im Geschäft mit Internet aus dem All sowie mit KI-Rechenzentren.
Unterm Strich verbuchte SpaceX schwarze Zahlen von 4,4 Milliarden Dollar (3,9 Mrd Euro). Im dritten Quartal des Vorjahres hatte es noch einen Verlust von gut einer Milliarde Dollar gegeben. Der Umsatz sprang von rund 5,58 Milliarden Dollar vor einem Jahr auf 14,58 Milliarden Dollar. Analysten hatten im Schnitt mit rund 12,7 Milliarden Dollar gerechnet.
Beim Internet aus dem All mit dem Satelliten-Dienst Starlink stieg der Umsatz im Jahresvergleich um 69 Prozent auf 5,2 Milliarden Dollar. Zum Stichtag 30. September kam Starlink auf 13,6 Millionen Kunden. Der Dienst ist unter anderem in 3.800 Flugzeugen verfügbar.
Die KI-Erlöse schossen von 813 Millionen Dollar vor einem Jahr auf 7,56 Milliarden Dollar im vergangenen Quartal hoch. Musks KI-Firma, die nun SpaceXSI heißt, baute große Rechenzentren auf, die inzwischen zum Teil für Milliarden-Gebühren an KI-Rivalen wie Anthropic und Google vermietet werden. Die KI-Sparte warf einen operativen Gewinn von 431 Millionen Dollar ab – nach roten Zahlen von 1,7 Milliarden Dollar ein Jahr zuvor.
Der Umsatz im Geschäft mit Raketenstarts legte im Jahresvergleich um sechs Prozent auf 1,77 Milliarden Dollar zu.
Auf und Ab für SpaceX-Aktie
SpaceX war Mitte Juni mit einem Rekorderlös von 75 Milliarden Dollar an die Börse gegangen. Mit dem Ausgabepreis von 135 Dollar gab sich Musks Unternehmen zum Debüt eine Bewertung von fast 1,8 Billionen Dollar. Das stand in krassem Kontrast zum aktuellen Geschäft – aber SpaceX rechtfertigte die Bewertung mit großen Plänen bei Künstlicher Intelligenz.
In den ersten Wochen nach dem Börsengang stieg der Kurs – angetrieben unter anderem vom Interesse von Privatanlegern – bis auf gut 225 Dollar. Danach rutschte die Aktie zwischenzeitlich unter den Ausgabepreis. Im nachbörslichen Handel legte der Kurs um mehr als neun Prozent auf über 160 Dollar zu.

articles.title: Families of Wes Hall, Patsy Anderson make $3-million donation to SickKids’ AI initiative | BetaKit
articles.text:
The self-proclaimed “King of Bay Street,” Wes Hall, and philanthropist Patsy Anderson are supporting the Hospital for Sick Children’s (SickKids) AI program.
The news: SickKids announced on Friday that Hall and Anderson joined forces to make a $3-million donation to the SickKids Artificial Intelligence (SKAI) program, which focuses on deploying “responsible AI” across clinical care, research, education, and operations, according to the hospital’s foundation.
The donation also establishes the SickKids Artificial Intelligence Innovator in Child Health award, with its inaugural recognition going to Dr. Devin Singh, the co-lead of SickKids’ SKAI Service.
From the source: In a statement, Hall said the donation “backs a visionary team helping to ensure Canadian innovation shapes the future of health care.”
“SickKids has world-class AI researchers and clinicians positioned to transform health care,” the Dragons’ Den star added. “We should be doing everything in our power to foster and keep their breakthrough undertakings here in Canada.”
The context: SickKids launched SKAI in March 2025 as a flagship initiative of the SickKids 2030 strategy. SKAI’s three major components include an in-house service to develop and support AI systems, a research arm with scientists using AI for medical discovery, and an AI literacy and knowledge-sharing component. Before Hall and Anderson’s donation, SKAI had received investments of $1 million or more from approximately a dozen backers.
In his own statement, Singh said the donation provides the SKAI team with a runway to develop and scale machine learning algorithms safely, from research validation to everyday clinical operations.
Final thought: This isn’t the only recent tech news tied to SickKids. On Tuesday, the pediatric hospital announced a five-year partnership with Microsoft Canada. The agreement will expand the use of Microsoft Azure as SickKids’ primary cloud platform, and include Azure credits so the hospital can, among other things, “build the AI capabilities needed to support the future of care.”
Feature image courtesy Wes Hall via Facebook.

articles.title: Judge dismisses Sam Altman’s sister’s sexual abuse lawsuit
articles.text:
On Tuesday, US District Judge Zachary Bluestone dismissed the lawsuit Ann Altman filed last year alleging that her brother, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, had sexually abused her throughout her childhood. As reported earlier by The Guardian, the judge wrote that over the past year, Ann had failed to appear for an independent medical examination or meet other deadlines despite warnings that it would result in the case being dismissed.
Judge dismisses Sam Altman’s sister’s sexual abuse lawsuit
Ann Altman’s lawsuit against her brother was dismissed with prejudice, meaning it can’t be refiled.
When the case was filed last year, a statement shared by Sam Altman, his mother, and his brothers said, “Annie has made deeply hurtful and entirely untrue claims about our family, and especially Sam… All of these claims are utterly untrue. This situation causes immense pain to our entire family.”
Bluestone granted Sam Altman’s motion to dismiss the case with prejudice, meaning it can’t be refiled in that court, while denying Sam’s request for attorney fees and costs. Santos Perez, a lawyer who had represented Ann until withdrawing this month, told The Guardian in a statement that “I am no longer authorized to comment on this case but I continue to believe in Annie.”

articles.title: Samsung-Smartphone beim Discounter: Wie gut ist dieses Aldi-Angebot?
articles.text:
Samsung-Smartphone beim Discounter: Wie gut ist dieses Aldi-Angebot?
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Smartphones könnten in den kommenden Monaten immer weiter zu Luxus-Gadgets avancieren. Als Reaktion auf die Speicherkrise haben in den vergangenen Wochen viele große Hersteller die Preise für ihre Modelle erhöht. Betroffen sind vor allem die Top-Modelle. Wer da nicht mitgehen will – und zu Abstrichen bereit ist –, fährt mit einem Einsteiger-Smartphone günstiger. Ein solches bietet Aldi in Form des Samsung Galaxy A18 ab dem 29. Oktober 2026 in seinen Filialen reduziert an. Kostenpunkt: 219 statt 279 Euro.
Diese Abstriche müsst ihr beim Galaxy A18 in Kauf nehmen
Selbst bei der unverbindlichen Preisempfehlung wird schon klar: Raketentechnik gibt es hier nicht zu kaufen. Entsprechend liest sich das Datenblatt. Mit dem Exynos 1610 ist Samsungs eigener Einsteiger-Prozessor an Bord. 5G unterstützt er nicht. Ihr surft unterwegs maximal mit LTE‑Geschwindigkeit. Dazu gibt es magere vier Gigabyte Arbeitsspeicher. Zum Vergleich: Das etwa 150 Euro teurere Galaxy A56 bietet acht Gigabyte RAM. Mit der Funktion RAM Plus soll das Smartphone auf bis zu vier Gigabyte virtuellen Arbeitsspeicher zugreifen können. Dabei greift das Gerät dann auf 128 Gigabyte großen Datenspeicher zu. Einen sehr großen Leistungsschub sollte man sich davon nicht erwarten.
Abstriche müsst ihr außerdem beim Gehäuse machen. Das ist nach IP64 nur gegen Spritzwasser, aber nicht gegen dauerhaftes Untertauchen geschützt. Wie gut die Dreifachkamera auf der Rückseite performt, lässt sich nur schwer einschätzen. Mit teureren Modellen können die Systeme in günstigen Smartphones in der Regel aber nicht mithalten. Immerhin: Der Speicher lässt sich per microSD-Karte erweitern. Das ist heutzutage längst nicht mehr selbstverständlich.
Wie gut ist der Aldi-Deal?
Wer sich für das Smartphone dennoch interessiert, muss nicht zwingend bis zum 29. Oktober warten, bis es bei Aldi in den Regalen steht. Die üblichen Online-Shops bieten das Gerät derzeit schon jetzt für 219 Euro an. Mancher Ebay‑Händler ist hier sogar noch etwas günstiger, berechnet allerdings zusätzliche Versandkosten, sodass ihr mit den Angeboten von Amazon, Saturn und Mediamarkt insgesamt besser fahrt.
Einziger Vorteil beim Discounter: Aldi legt noch ein Starter-Set von Aldi-Talk mit einem Guthaben in Höhe von 10 Euro bei. Das fehlt bei den Elektronikriesen und Versandhändlern natürlich.

An analytics-driven approach leveraging integrated industry leading technologies targeting advanced node devices.
								October 21st, 2026 - 
								By: Synopsys
								
							
Achieving the requisite target yield as early as possible during silicon ramp is a lead indicator of product success. Delays in reaching yield entitlement can impact time-to-market, increase manufacturing costs, and reduce overall product competitiveness—particularly at advanced nodes where complexity and cost continue to rise. As a result, incorporating a solution that can rapidly identify and resolve systematic yield limiters has become essential to enabling efficient ramp to high-volume production.
Such a solution requires analytics-driven volume diagnostic and failure analysis capabilities to reverse engineer test failures captured on automatic test equipment (ATE). These capabilities identify the precise failing location within the chip, rank failure candidates based on yield impact, and provide the highest-priority candidates to the failure analysis lab for final root-cause confirmation. Corrective action can then be performed on either the design or the silicon process to correct and improve the yield of your chip and ultimately enable you to go to high volume production and into the market ahead of the competition.

articles.title: Developing an AI Factory Digital Twin with an Agent-Assisted Workflow | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
Building an AI factory digital twin requires developers to bring site plans, equipment assets, and engineering requirements into a consistent model that teams can inspect, revise, and prepare for simulation. Connecting these inputs into an editable workflow helps teams explore design alternatives and incorporate engineering feedback as the design evolves.
The NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint, part of NVIDIA DSX Sim, provides reference digital twin assets, sample scripts, and workflows for developing AI factory digital twins. Built on OpenUSD and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, the blueprint gives developers a foundation for assembling facility and equipment models with SimReady assets, and connecting them with engineering simulation tools.
Frontier AI models can help developers work with this foundation through agents and connected applications and tools, as explained in Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations with Frontier AI Agents. Developers guide agents to bring together design inputs, assemble and revise OpenUSD scenes, and inspect the results. The blueprint supplies reusable assets and workflows, and the agents help developers apply and adapt them to specific design requirements (Figure 1).
This post demonstrates an agent-assisted workflow for turning reference assets, site data, and design requirements into an editable OpenUSD campus model. Developers can use this approach to explore layouts, revise equipment placement, and prepare designs for engineering review and downstream simulation. Developers connect tools and guide changes, while engineers review results to inform the next iteration.
Providing agents with a design foundation for AI factory modeling
Consider a practical question: How should an AI factory hall be configured when the available power is fixed? Changing the compute configuration can impact equipment quantity, placement, electrical distribution, and cooling. Evaluating the alternatives requires those disciplines to work from consistent requirements and design data.
An agent needs context before it can make a useful design proposal. Given only photos or renderings, it can produce a model that looks plausible but may have incorrect dimensions and proportions. Reference assets and project documents help ground the proposal, but the resulting model still requires dimensional checks and engineering review.
A grounded workflow starts with the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint and reference design, then incorporates the project’s requirements, drawings, equipment information, and site constraints. Each source has a different role: existing geometry supplies reusable buildings and equipment while architectural references inform appearance; aerial imagery and elevation data provide geographic context; project drawings and equipment information establish dimensions and placement; requirements define the conditions the design must satisfy.
For example, the team used the NVIDIA Santa Clara Headquarters building, Voyager, as design inspiration for an AI factory campus site based on the DSX reference design. The inputs included:
- DSX 3D models: Data hall, central utility buildings, substations, generators, cooling equipment, vehicles, and vegetation.
- Architectural references: Images of Voyager from various aerial and on-the-ground views to inform the roof, facade, solar canopies, and landscaping.
- Site plans (DSX Reference Design): PDFs describing the campus arrangement and a more detailed first phase, including buildings, roads, utility areas, and access areas.
- Requirements documents: An indexed collection of architectural drawings, form-factor studies, Basis of Design documents, room layouts, and other records.
- Geographic data: USGS aerial imagery and elevation data of the selected site used to place the campus in the surrounding terrain.
Together, these sources provide a starting point for an agent-assisted workflow and basis for reviewing its output. They help teams trace design choices to their sources—for example, building placement to a site plan and facade styling to an architectural reference. That traceability supports review; dimensional accuracy still depends on checking the model against the applicable drawings, specifications, and site constraints.
Building an OpenUSD campus site model using an AI agent
To implement this workflow, a frontier AI model runs in an agent harness: software that manages context, instructions, and tool calls. Skills encode repeatable tasks and AI factory domain knowledge. Developers connect modeling and analysis operations through tool interfaces, including the Model Context Protocol (MCP), where supported, and define which changes the agent may propose or apply.
In the campus model example, existing DSX reference designed buildings from the DSX Blueprint and equipment supplied the starting geometry, while the site plans guided placement and first-phase details. The team supplied photographs and the architectural references from the NVIDIA Voyager campus to guide the architectural additions.
For the solar canopy, the frontier AI agent used USD Content Agents to help generate its geometry and materials, then refined the design using the Voyager references. This gave the team an editable architectural element to review alongside the existing buildings and equipment. The canopy remained a conceptual design where an engineering team could check for dimensions, structural properties, and suitability for simulation.
The team then combined the reused assets and new architectural geometry in additive USD layers, keeping changes separate from the source assets. In the Omniverse RTX viewport, the team could inspect the canopy in the context of the campus, review its appearance and placement, and revise the model as design decisions change. USGS aerial data was used for the landscape and elevation plan.
Extending the campus model to evaluate a fixed power budget
The campus model could support a subsequent capacity planning study: How should an AI factory hall be configured within a fixed power budget? The proposed extension would connect the modeled layout with compute, electrical, and cooling requirements to evaluate alternative configurations.
One starting point is an illustrative NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 inference comparison. It contrasts a baseline using MaxP—the highest static GPU-level power setting—with DSX MaxLPS, an AI factory design and operating framework that coordinates facility design, dynamic power allocation, and performance-per-watt optimization. Applying this comparison to a hall would require evaluating the support power, cooling, and networking infrastructure.
Normalized to a 1 MW power basis, assuming a power usage effectiveness (PUE) of 1.1, the illustrative scenario shows a DSX MaxLPS capacity of 400 GPUs and aggregate token throughput of 1.35x the MaxP baseline (Figure 4). These figures are reference assumptions for the proposed study, not results generated by the campus model.
In the proposed workflow, developers would connect the agent to project data and engineering tools so it could help identify equipment and design assumptions requiring review. The reference comparison would inform capacity targets. Engineers would evaluate feasible configurations using complete racks, including their placement, electrical distribution, cooling connections, and network resources.
Using Systems Modeling Language (SysML), teams can represent requirements and link them to system elements. A project team could use these relationships to organize requirements drawn from source documents. If the modeling tool exposes those relationships through an API, MCP, or other supported interface, the agent could query them to flag potentially affected dependencies affected by the proposed change. Drawings and CAD would provide dimensions and placement references, while equipment catalogs would supply the parameters for engineering analysis.
The handoff would be a proposed design revision, accompanied by the requirements, equipment, and follow-up engineering studies. After engineering reviews, the agent could help update the OpenUSD scene to reflect the selected rack configuration and layout. Preparing the scene for a specific simulation would require additional checks and configuration, including geometry, equipment properties, system connections, and boundary conditions.
Assembling the digital twin with OpenUSD and SimReady
After the team reviews a proposed configuration and its affected requirements, the next step is to prepare the design for analysis. This requires more than geometry: engineers need equipment properties and connection data to evaluate power and cooling. OpenUSD brings building geometry, equipment assets, and associated data into a shared scene. USD attributes and custom schemas can preserve links to engineering records and requirements, keeping changes traceable across applications.
The DSX system architecture connects asset preparation, data storage, simulation services, and the digital twin application. For the fixed-power scenario, this provides a framework for bringing the revised layout together with the equipment information needed to evaluate its power and cooling implications.
SimReady Foundation describes the asset data needed for particular simulation uses. While OpenUSD provides the shared scene, SimReady specifications help teams assess whether its assets contain the required data needed for the intended analysis, select the requirements and supported validators appropriate to the equipment and analysis, then check the geometry, properties, and connection data they cover. The agent can help surface missing information and associate it with the affected equipment for the team to review.
Developers can also source equipment assets from the SimReady Central Library on Hugging Face, a free, ungated library of more than 2,000 simulation-ready OpenUSD assets. For AI factory digital twins, teams can discover and reuse OEM-provided racks, power and cooling equipment, reducing asset preparation.
The AI factory pipeline samples provide examples for CAD conversion, optimization, metadata, and validation. Through connected tools, an agent can help invoke these preparation steps and collect their reports.
The resulting handoff is an assembled scene tied to the proposed design revision, with its supporting data, completed checks, and remaining gaps visible. This gives the simulation team the context needed to prepare the study and evaluate how the configuration behaves within the fixed power budget.
Evaluating power and cooling simulations to guide design revisions
With the revised scene assembled and the data gaps identified, prepare the studies needed to evaluate the configuration. In the fixed-power scenario, electrical loading and cooling analysis help determine how the proposed equipment arrangement behaves under the specified operating conditions. The application uses the geometry, equipment properties, and system connections, with additional solver preparation where required.
Where developers have implemented supported solver connections, an agent can submit studies, retrieve results, and associate findings with the affected equipment and requirements. Engineers review the assumptions and results to determine whether the design supports the proposed configurations or needs further revision. Each finding should identify the tested design revision and distinguish calculated results from stored results or AI approximations.
The capacity question now becomes a basis for making design decisions: which equipment configuration to pursue, what supporting infrastructure it requires, and where further analysis is needed. Those decisions feed back into the editable design, enabling the team to refine the proposal and repeat the affected studies.
Selecting compute for agent development, visualization, and simulation
For a workflow like the campus example, select hardware around the task: developing the agent tool connections, editing the scene, or running the engineering studies.
- NVIDIA DGX Spark for personal agent development: Prototype agents, test compatible local AI models, and connect engineering tools. Pair with an RTX system for DSX visualization and simulation.
- NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell Workstation Edition GPU for interactive design and simulation: Prepare OpenUSD assets, review digital twins, and run supported engineering simulations.
- NVIDIA DGX Station for larger local AI workloads: Develop and run larger AI models and agents locally. Add an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition GPU for visualization and supported simulation applications.
- NVIDIA RTX PRO Server for shared development and simulation: Follow the NVIDIA RTX PRO AI Factory reference architecture, which specifies eight RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs per server and groups four servers into a scalable unit. Size the deployment for inference, visualization, and supported simulation workloads based on scene complexity, solver requirements, and concurrent users.
Connecting applications to the engineering decision
Extending the campus model into an engineering study requires applications that manage requirements, supply equipment data, and calculate physical behavior. Application providers are addressing these scenarios across the workflow:
- Dassault Systèmes addresses the challenge of keeping system requirements and design decisions consistent with CATIA Magic. Its SysML tools let engineers model system elements and interfaces, check model consistency, and evaluate designs against the architecture. Within an agent-assisted workflow, simulation findings can inform proposed updates to the SysML model configuration, subject to engineering review, keeping requirements and the systems model connected throughout design iterations. Dassault Systèmes also supports the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol for agent-to-agent integration, complementing MCP-based access to tools and data.
- PTC is working to keep digital twin studies connected to the product data they represent through Windchill and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Windchill manages version-controlled Creo and other CAD data; the announced integration is intended to bring that data into a shared 3D environment for engineering review and simulation. This addresses the handoff from the managed equipment design to the AI factory digital twin.
- Cadence Reality Digital Twin Platform answers the fixed-power question: how many GPUs can run, and can they be cooled? It couples equipment and power models with computational fluid dynamics to simulate MaxP, MaxQ, and DSX MaxLPS. Stakeholders see the impact on power, cooling, and token throughput before a single rack is installed and continues through the life of the AI factory. Built on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, SimReady assets, and OpenUSD, the Cadence Reality Digital Twin allows collaborative and agentic optimization of AI factory performance.
- Siemens supports detailed evaluation of fluid flow and heat transfer with Simcenter STAR-CCM+, where engineers calculate how a proposed design behaves under specified conditions. For AI factory infrastructure, Siemens has also developed DSX-aligned reference architectures that combine power distribution, automation, and simulation-ready assets. These address the need to represent supporting infrastructure alongside compute equipment in the factory design.
Get started with the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint
Choose one engineering question, connect the required data and tools, assemble the digital twin with OpenUSD, and use SimReady requirements to prepare assets for the intended analysis. Review the result before expanding.

articles.title: The cash cost of a 60-day customer (Sponsored) | EU-Startups
articles.text:
A bigger UK contract can consume runway before it creates cash. Put the payment terms into the funding plan before signing.
A large UK customer offers a scale-up a contract with 60-day payment terms. The revenue looks attractive. The less visible question is how much cash the startup must find before the customer pays.
Before signing, put the collection date into the cash forecast and compare it with when wages, suppliers and taxes must be paid. Then test what happens if payment takes longer. A profitable contract can still need funding, and a revenue target does not supply it.
This matters particularly for founders selling services or software to larger organizations. The customer may have enough money to pay. It may also have a procurement process that requires a purchase order, an approved invoice and a particular payment run. Winning the account and financing the account are different jobs.
Thirty more days can tie up nearly £400,000
Start with a simple illustration, not an actual company. Assume annual UK credit sales of £4.8 million, spread evenly through the year, with invoices issued as sales occur. Ignore VAT, seasonality, bad debt and other changes for now.
At 30 days from invoicing to cash, average receivables would be roughly £395,000. At 60 days, they would be about £789,000. The extra 30 days ties up approximately £395,000 in invoices, without adding a pound of annual revenue.
The calculation is annual credit sales divided by 365, multiplied by the extra days to payment. Here that is £4.8 million ÷ 365 × 30, or £394,521 rounded to the nearest pound. If only part of the customer base changes terms, use that part’s sales, not the whole company’s turnover.
This is an estimate of additional receivables, not a precise funding requirement. Cash already held, supplier terms, deposits and the timing of delivery costs affect the amount the company must finance. Fast growth can also make a steady annual average misleading. Model the actual expected invoices and receipts month by month before deciding how much liquidity is needed.
The distinction is important: the £395,000 has not necessarily been lost. It is unavailable for payroll or the next product release while the business waits. The British Business Bank makes the same underlying distinction in its cash-flow guidance: rising profit does not prevent a shortage of cash when growth requires working capital.
Price the timing as well as the product
Payment terms are part of a commercial offer, not a minor line for finance to discover after the sale. If winning a contract requires financing the customer for longer, make that cost visible alongside gross margin and acquisition cost.
Using the illustration, an assumed annual funding cost of 10% on the additional £395,000 would be about £39,500 a year. That rate is a modeling assumption, not a financing quote. Fees, eligibility, concentration limits and the available facility could change the actual cost substantially.
The answer need not be a higher headline price. A setup fee payable before work starts, milestone billing or a deposit may reduce the amount financed. These are commercial options to negotiate, not terms every enterprise buyer will accept. They must fit the product and the customer’s purchasing process.
An early-payment discount also has a cost. Compare that cost against the cash released and the number of days gained, rather than assuming that faster payment is always worth any discount. The aim is to win a contract that the company can afford to deliver.
Check the customer’s record, not just its policy
Sixty-day terms and late payment are not the same thing. A customer paying exactly on day 60 has used the agreed credit period. A customer paying on day 75 has introduced another 15 days of uncertainty.
For many large UK companies, founders can check published payment-practices reports through the government’s reporting service. The reports show measures including average time to pay and the proportion of payments not made on time. Check the contracting legal entity, not merely the group’s familiar brand name.
Those reports are evidence to question, not a guarantee about one invoice. A company-wide average may not describe the startup’s business unit or contract. Use the information to ask concrete questions before signing: when does the clock start, which purchase-order details are mandatory, who accepts delivery and what happens if an invoice is rejected?
Ask the sales team to resolve those questions while the customer still wants the contract signed. Otherwise, an apparent 60-day deal may include weeks of avoidable administration before the agreed period even begins.
Do not fund growth with an assumed recovery
Keep a distinction between invoices expected to pay normally and overdue balances whose timing is uncertain. Repeated promises should not become fresh, certain cash dates in the board forecast.
For a UK receivable that has genuinely become overdue, establish whether the issue is administrative, a dispute or an inability to pay. Reconcile the balance and set a decision point for seeking local collection or legal advice, whether directly or through a platform such as Debitura. That is a recovery decision, not a substitute for funding the next month’s operating costs. Neither an instruction to collect nor a legal claim makes the money immediately available.
The useful board conversation comes before a cash crisis: how much growth can current liquidity support if customers take the time already allowed in their contracts? Run a second version with plausible delays and identify the point at which hiring or delivery commitments would need to change.
A prestigious customer can be a good investment. But its logo does not pay wages. The payment terms belong in the funding plan on the day the contract is evaluated, not on the day the first invoice goes overdue.

articles.title: Eliminating traffic deaths
articles.text:
Eliminating traffic deaths
Deploying simple, proven methods for making our roads safer could save more than 1 million lives worldwide each year.
Every year, traffic crashes kill more than one million people, and they’re the leading cause of death for children and young adults. In the US, 100 people a day lose their lives this way, in many cases not on highways but on rural and local streets. “Traffic deaths are a leading cause of preventable death, yet we treat it like it’s inevitable,” says Leah Shahum, founder and director of the Vision Zero Network, a nonprofit focused on making streets less deadly.
The sticking points
The causes of a crash can be muddy. Drivers make mistakes like speeding or getting distracted, but infrastructure fails them too: Perhaps they were on a road built for speed and not safety, in a screen-filled vehicle, or at an intersection where pedestrians, cyclists, and other cars aren’t visible.
Cheap and proven traffic-calming opportunities abound—from using planters to tighten intersections to lowering speed limits—but government logjams and red tape can be speed bumps. “There’s so many moving parts,” says Laura Sandt of the University of North Carolina Highway Safety Research Center. “On the flip side, it shows that we have so many opportunities for injury prevention.”
The progress
The total number of traffic deaths has increased over the last century. And though the US rate has dipped from a peak of 30.8 deaths per 100,000 people in the 1930s, the past decade has seen a concerning jump in deadly pedestrian incidents. At the same time, communities are waking up to the essential role of traffic safety policy, Shahum says.
One success story is Hoboken, New Jersey, which hasn’t had a traffic fatality since 2017. This is due to a combination of efforts like boosting investment in public transit, promoting walkability by extending curbs, and using cameras to identify crash-prone intersections in need of a redesign. But even there, obstacles remain. If an intersection hasn’t been proved to be deadly, for example, it can be an uphill battle to argue for removing parking spaces to widen curbs. “You’re kind of selling insurance through these improvements, and that’s not always easy,” says Greg Francese, the city’s acting director of transportation and parking.
There’s also no silver bullet that will work everywhere. Situated directly across the river from New York City, Hoboken is a highly transit-oriented city of less than 60,000 people. Success there might not translate to traffic-death hot spots like Memphis or Dallas. But it’s not impossible. Take Edmonton, Alberta, a sprawling, car-centric Canadian city of around one million people: Between 2015 and 2020, it cut traffic fatalities by 63% and serious injuries by 40% by adjusting speed limits and improving signals at crosswalks.
Progress meter ............ 6
We know how to tweak intersections and adjust traffic signals. Getting the funding and will to roll out those changes is the big red light.

articles.title: Streaming überholt erstmals Fernsehen und Radio in Deutschland: Wer von dem Medienwandel wirklich profitiert
articles.text:
Streaming überholt erstmals Fernsehen und Radio in Deutschland: Wer von dem Medienwandel wirklich profitiert
Streamingangebote werden in Deutschland in diesem Jahr einer Prognose zufolge erstmals mehr Umsatz erzielen als klassische Medienangebote wie Fernsehen und Radio. Nach Berechnungen des Verbands Privater Medien (Vaunet) werden die Erlöse aus Streamingdiensten 2026 auf rund 8,6 Milliarden Euro steigen. Damit würden sie erstmals mehr als die Hälfte (52 Prozent) des gesamten Audio- und audiovisuellen Medienmarktes ausmachen. Im Jahr 2019 lag ihr Anteil noch bei 26 Prozent.
Insgesamt rechnet der Verband für das laufende Jahr mit einem Umsatzwachstum von 1,8 Prozent auf 16,3 Milliarden Euro, wie aus der Herbstprognose hervorgeht. Das Wachstum wird demnach ausschließlich von steigenden Einnahmen aus Video- und Audiostreaming getragen.
Während Streamingangebote weiter zulegen, stehen die klassischen Medien unter Druck. Die Werbeumsätze im Fernsehen dürften in diesem Jahr um sechs Prozent auf rund 3,1 Milliarden Euro sinken. Auch bei der Radiowerbung erwartet der Verband einen Rückgang um sechs Prozent auf 636 Millionen Euro.
Ganz anders sieht es beim Streaming aus: Die Werbeerlöse im Videostreaming sollen um 15 Prozent auf rund 2,5 Milliarden Euro steigen. Auch die Einnahmen aus Audiostreaming-Werbung wachsen der Prognose zufolge um zehn Prozent auf 147 Millionen Euro.
Große Tech-Konzerne profitieren besonders
Von der Entwicklung profitieren allerdings vor allem große internationale Technologieunternehmen. Nach Angaben von Vaunet entfallen bereits 72 Prozent der Werbeumsätze im Videostreaming auf die vier großen Anbieter Alphabet, Amazon, ByteDance und Meta. „Der Werbemarkt wächst jedoch zunehmend an ihnen vorbei“, sagte Vaunet-Geschäftsführer Frank Giersberg mit Blick auf die privaten Medienanbieter. Die steigende Bedeutung des Streamings zeige, wie stark sich der Medienmarkt verändere.
Auch bei kostenpflichtigen Angeboten setzt sich der Trend fort. Die Einnahmen aus bezahlten Video-Abrufangeboten wie Streaming-Abonnements sollen um 4,5 Prozent auf rund 3,7 Milliarden Euro steigen. Für kostenpflichtige Audioangebote erwartet der Verband ein Plus von fünf Prozent auf rund 2,2 Milliarden Euro. Die Umsätze im klassischen Pay-TV dürften dagegen um vier Prozent auf 1,9 Milliarden Euro zurückgehen.

articles.title: SA’s Injini launches EdTech for Employment incubation programme - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African ed-tech incubator Injini has launched a new two-year programme that will support 10 early-stage South African edtech startups building solutions that create or support employment pathways for young people.
Founded in 2017, Injini, which is a member of the UVU Africa Group, is a registered non-profit company that exists for the sole purpose of improving educational outcomes in Sub-Saharan Africa. Its programmes and research via the Injini Think Tank contribute towards its mission to increase the quality, accessibility, and relevance of education in the region. It announced its latest cohort earlier this year.
The EdTech for Employment Incubation Programme, which is financed by Zurich-based Leopold Bachmann Foundation, will run from October 2026 to September 2028, and targets startups whose solutions serve youth aged between 15 and 30.
The programme comes against the backdrop of a South African youth unemployment rate that stood at 46.1 per cent in the first quarter of this year, according to Stats SA, which is among the highest in the world. Injini said the figure reflects a structural shortage of quality vocational and work-readiness pathways connecting young people to the economy.
A growing number of edtech startups are building solutions in this space, including teacher training platforms, tutoring and mentorship tools, and technologies that prepare young people for economic participation. However, Injini said these companies often lack the structured support, market access and proof-of-concept evidence they need to scale.
“South Africa’s youth aren’t short on ambition or ability. What they need are structured pathways into work,” said Krista Davidson, executive director at Injini. “We’ve spent years watching talented edtech founders build real solutions to this problem, without the support to test what works, prove it, and scale it. This programme is designed to close that gap.
The programme will run two cohorts of five startups each. Each cycle begins with a recruitment and selection process, followed by a six-month incubation period built around four pillars: product foundations, business sustainability, market access, and impact measurement.
Participating startups will receive hands-on support from Injini’s team, as well as access to a network of specialist consultants matched to their needs. Founders will also have opportunities to network and engage with the wider ecosystem and potential users.
Over its two-year run, the programme aims to reach 20,000 underserved youth, help up to 2,000 of them access work or income-generating opportunities, and create 20 direct jobs within the cohort companies.
“We’re looking for ed-tech companies that are already doing the hard work of connecting young people to skills and income,” Davidson said. “Over the next two years, we want to give ten of them the structural support, proof points and market access they need to grow.”
Both non-profit and for-profit edtech startups with a clear social impact mandate are eligible, with priority given to those working in work-readiness and digital skills, teacher training and professional development, and tutoring or peer-learning models that generate income and employment opportunities for young people.
Interested startups can apply here.

articles.title: Tesla Roadster moins cher : la marque annonce un 4e bolide plus « abordable »
articles.text:
Le 15 octobre dernier, Elon Musk a dévoilé le Tesla Roadster. Pour rappel, le modèle est décliné en trois versions : le Roadster Performance (une version routière classique, deux places, avec aérodynamique active et système d’aspiration sous la voiture), le Roadster Thrust (une version deux places ajoutant des propulseurs à gaz froid à l’arrière pour améliorer l’accélération) et le Roadster Rocket (une version monoplace, avec des propulseurs répartis autour du véhicule et des capacités de décollage). La présentation du 15 octobre était centrée sur ce dernier modèle, particulièrement impressionnant, il faut le dire. Ces trois modèles sont présents sur le site de Tesla, et une quatrième version pourrait prochainement les rejoindre.
Une Tesla Roadster standard
Franz von Holzhausen, designer en chef de Tesla, a confirmé l’information auprès du magazine MotorTrend : un quatrième modèle de Tesla Roadster rejoindra prochainement les trois autres. Concrètement, il est question d’une version standard, placée juste en dessous de la Roadster Performance, et donc moins performante, mais aussi plus « abordable ».
Selon Top Gear, ce modèle Standard atteindrait 1 090 ch, contre 1 360 ch pour la Performance. Il serait dépourvu du système d’aspiration multimode et pourrait également faire l’impasse sur l’aérodynamique active. Le véhicule pourrait donc être moins performant sur les accélérations, tout en offrant une meilleure autonomie. Les matériaux haut de gamme au sein de l’habitacle et le revêtement doré sur les vitres teintées pourraient aussi être remplacés par d’autres matériaux afin de faire baisser le prix. En revanche, ce modèle standard devrait bel et bien intégrer une propulsion, avec deux moteurs installés à l’arrière.
Quel prix pour ce modèle standard ?
Pour l’instant, Tesla ne présente pas ce modèle standard sur son site. Étant donné que nous ne disposons pas de fiches techniques, toutes ces informations devront être confirmées. En revanche, l’existence de ce modèle « plus accessible » semble actée. À ce titre, il reste aussi à connaître son prix. Ce modèle standard devrait afficher un prix plus bas que celui de la Roadster Performance, mais il devrait tout de même coûter un bras.
Pour rappel, Tesla demande un acompte de 50 000 € pour la Roadster Performance. En ce qui concerne le modèle Roadster Thrust, l’acompte s’élève à 250 000 €. Les prix de ces deux modèles sont toujours inconnus à l’heure où nous écrivons ces lignes, et il n’y a aucune garantie de livraison.

articles.title: Windows Server 2025 gets support for quick machine recovery
articles.text:
Microsoft announced that IT administrators can now use quick machine recovery on Windows Server 2025 after installing the October 2026 security update.
Quick machine recovery (QMR) lets IT admins fix critical boot failures with targeted Windows Update fixes without physical access to affected systems.
When enabled, it boots into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) and launches the QMR Tool if Windows fails to start because of a configuration change or a new driver. It then sends crash data to Microsoft, which can remotely fix issues by adjusting settings or removing problematic drivers or updates.
"With the October 2026 security update, quick machine recovery extends to Windows Server 2025," the company said in a message center update.
"Quick machine recovery is designed to help restore devices experiencing widespread boot issues by using the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to search Windows Update for applicable remediations."
On Windows Server 2025, cloud remediation is disabled by default, but admins can enable it via Group Policy under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Quick Machine Recovery to retrieve and apply cloud-sourced remediation.
For local configuration, admins must sign in to the target server with administrator permissions and use the Local Group Policy Editor. In domain configurations, they can use Group Policy Management on a Windows Server or an administration computer, but they also need permissions to edit the GPO and link it to the intended organizational unit (OU).
To disable QMR through Group Policy, admins have to explicitly turn off 'Enable Cloud Remediation' to prevent cloud-sourced remediation and disable 'Enable Auto Remediation' to block automatic application of local remediation packages.
This can be done by going through the following steps:
- Open the local policy or domain GPO that manages the target Windows Server 2025 computers.
- Go to Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Quick Machine Recovery.
- Open Enable Cloud Remediation, select Disabled, and select Apply, then OK.
- Open Enable Auto Remediation, select Disabled, and select Apply, then OK.
- (Optional) Verify the effective configuration.
Microsoft introduced quick machine recovery in November 2024 as part of its Windows Resiliency Initiative at Ignite 2024, in response to a July 2024 outage caused by a buggy CrowdStrike Falcon update that rendered millions of Windows devices unbootable.
It began testing in late March 2025, rolling it out to Windows Insiders in the Beta Channel. In November, it also began testing a faster version that now runs a single scan to fix systems with boot problems, rather than looping through solutions.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

Nedbank clears the final hurdle to take control of NCBA
Nine months after putting R13.9 billion ($855.5 million) on the table, Nedbank is finally at the end of its NCBA takeover.
The South African lender’s offer to acquire 66% of NCBA Group, one of East Africa’s largest banking groups, is now unconditional after clearing the remaining regulatory approvals.
Settlement begins this week, with the transfer of shares to Nedbank expected from early November. NCBA will become a Nedbank subsidiary, but keep its name, Nairobi headquarters, management, and Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE) listing, according to its Monday filings.
Catch up: Nedbank first announced the deal in January. In February, Kenya’s capital markets regulator allowed it to buy 66% without making an offer for the entire company. The tender opened in May, and by July, shareholders had offered 79.9% of NCBA’s shares, more than Nedbank wanted. Those offers had to be scaled back to 66%.
Shareholders who sell will receive 80% of their payment in newly issued Nedbank shares and 20% in cash. The remaining 34% of NCBA will stay in public hands.
Between the lines: Nedbank is buying more than a Kenyan bank. NCBA already operates across Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and Rwanda, with digital businesses in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Its digital business accounted for 32% of group profit in 2025, and it disbursed KES 1.4 trillion ($10.8 billion) in digital loans.
The deal also shows how Nedbank’s Africa strategy has changed. In 2025, it sold its 21% stake in Ecobank and shifted towards markets where it can control the banking operation rather than remain a minority investor. NCBA gives it that control, plus customers, licences, and infrastructure across East Africa, without building them country by country.
What to watch: Nedbank has previously talked about using NCBA as a springboard into Ethiopia and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Now it has the platform to try.

Fintech
Why Onafriq shut down its Nigerian agent banking business
In hindsight, it is not hard to see the play Onafriq, the pan-African payments company, was making when it expanded into Nigeria by acquiring Baxi in 2021.
Nigeria still relied heavily on cash, and Baxi already had more than 90,000 agents. Onafriq could enter with a ready-made distribution network instead of spending years building one.
The timing looked good, too. OPay and Moniepoint had begun building large agent networks in 2019, while PalmPay entered agent banking later. In 2021, Baxi was already one of Nigeria’s biggest independent agent networks, giving Onafriq an early lead over some newer competitors.
But the lead did not hold. By the end of 2024, PalmPay reportedly had more than 700,000 agents, while Moniepoint had over 800,000 point-of-sale (PoS) terminals. But as of 2025, Baxi had just over 460,000 agents, paling in comparison. In October, it finally decided to shut down the business, months after trying to sell Baxi.
Between the lines: Agent banking became a scale game. Rivals poured money into terminals, agent recruitment, and incentives, making it easier to close the distribution gap. At the same time, agents could work with several providers, making a large network less defensible than it first appeared.
The economics also changed. More terminals entered the market much faster than transaction volumes grew, so providers competed over the same payments.
Meanwhile, account-to-account (A2A) transfers—direct bank payments—gave customers another way to move money without visiting an agent.
Onafriq’s attempt to sell Baxi before shutting it down shows that the problem was bigger than one bad year. The company had already decided the agent business no longer fit where it wanted to put capital.
Zoom out: Onafriq bought Baxi partly because physical distribution was scarce. Five years later, the market had plenty. Being early gave Baxi a head start, but it did not stop competitors from catching up and, eventually, passing it.

South African union want Shein and Temu banned to protect local jobs
Behind the low-cost tops you see on Shein and Temu is a dispute over how foreign shopping platforms compete with local businesses, and what that means for the people who make and sell clothes in South Africa.
What happened? The Congress of South African Trade Unions (COSATU), the country’s largest trade union federation, wants South Africa to ban Shein and Temu. It backed a proposal from the Southern African Clothing and Textile Workers’ Union (SACTWU), which says the platforms hurt local jobs by undercutting domestic retailers and manufacturers.
Explain like I’m new here: Shein entered South Africa in 2020, while Temu followed in 2024. Both sell directly to consumers online, offering a wide range of clothing and other goods at prices that traditional retailers can find hard to match. A 2025 study by the Localisation Support Fund (LSF), a South African organisation focused on strengthening local production, estimated that Shein and Temu generated R7.3 billion ($444 million) in South African sales in 2024, equivalent to roughly 3.6% of the country’s retail market.
Can South Africa ban them? South Africa has already taken steps to narrow the tax advantage to benefit some low-value imports. Previously, goods worth less than R500 ($30.41) were cheaper to bring into the country. In 2024, the South African Revenue Service (SARS), the country’s taxman, introduced value-added tax (VAT) on low-value imports and subsequently ended their special customs-duty treatment.
However, COSATU’s proposal goes further than changing tax rules. If both platforms are banned, some consumers could pay more without automatically creating new jobs in local factories. South Africa still has to work out how to protect local jobs while allowing competition and preserving affordable choices for shoppers. Closing tax loopholes is one part of that effort; making local manufacturers more competitive is another.

Cameroon wants to put more Internet on its electricity poles
Building a fibre-optic network requires a place to lay the fibre, permission to use the land, and a lot of money. But what if the poles that already carry electricity could also help carry the Internet? Cameroon is exploring that option.
What happened? On October 16, Camtel, Cameroon’s state-owned telecoms operator, and Socadel, the country’s electricity provider, signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to explore sharing infrastructure for fibre deployment.
How would it work? Camtel has the fibre network and telecoms expertise, and Socadel has electricity infrastructure, such as utility poles and rights-of-way. Instead of Camtel building entirely new infrastructure to carry fibre cables, it could attach overhead cables to suitable electricity poles and use existing routes to reach more locations. The two companies will now study whether they can combine those assets for faster Internet access.
Cameroon has tried this before: In 2023, the government transferred about 812 kilometres (km) of overhead fibre that Eneo, Socadel’s predecessor, had installed on electricity poles along Cameroon’s southern interconnected grid to Camtel.
That network served major cities including Douala and Yaoundé, its capital, and added to Camtel’s fibre infrastructure, which stood at about 12,000km. The latest agreement focuses on closer infrastructure sharing, including the possibility of incorporating fibre into future electricity infrastructure projects.
What happens next? The companies have not yet announced a nationwide rollout or a specific number of new kilometres. Their immediate job is to determine where the arrangement makes sense and identify pilot sites. If the model works, Camtel could expand fibre routes without building every supporting telecom structure from scratch, reducing deployment costs.

articles.title: Amazon duplica su apuesta por la nuclear y anuncia una nueva central en Indiana para sus centros de datos
articles.text:
Amazon ha acordado ayudar a pagar el desarrollo de una central nuclear de 960 megavatios en Indiana, y sería el primer cliente en comprar su energía. El proyecto, anunciado el lunes junto a la empresa X-energy y American Electric Power (AEP), instalaría 12 pequeños reactores modulares (SMR) en los terrenos de una antigua central de carbón. Eso sí, nadie ha dicho cuándo podría producir electricidad realmente.
Energía nuclear para la IA. El apetito de las grandes tecnológicas para proporcionar energía a sus centros de datos no cesa, y está llegando a puntos insostenibles para la red eléctrica. Estos centros colosales donde se almacena toda la infraestructura necesaria para echar a andar la IA necesitan muchísima electricidad durante las 24 horas del día, y la energía nuclear es una de las pocas fuentes libres de carbono que puede proporcionarla.
Amazon afirma que quiere poner en marcha más de 5 gigavatios de nueva capacidad nuclear en EEUU para 2039 con X-energy, e Indiana es el segundo proyecto dentro de ese plan. El primero es la Cascade Advanced Energy Facility en el estado de Washington. TechCrunch señala que el acuerdo de Indiana es tres veces mayor que el primer acuerdo entre las dos empresas.
Los detalles. La planta utilizaría 12 reactores Xe-100 de X-energy, cada uno con una potencia nominal de 80 MW. Estaría ubicada donde se encontraba antes la antigua central eléctrica Breed Generating Station en el condado de Sullivan, justo al sur de Terre Haute, según Amazon. AEP, cuya filial Indiana Michigan Power ha operado una central nuclear durante más de 50 años, se encargaría de su funcionamiento.
UN VISTAZO A...
A diferencia de muchos otros proyectos energéticos nuevos vinculados a centros de datos, la planta se conectaría a la red pública. Amazon afirma que daría servicio tanto a la red regional como a sus propias instalaciones. La empresa también señala que el proyecto podría crear más de 1.000 puestos de trabajo en la construcción y más de 100 empleos permanentes.
Amazon afirma que el Xe-100 utiliza helio como refrigerante y combustible TRISO. Además, la empresa asegura que el diseño previene una fusión nuclear solo a través de sus principios físicos, sin sistemas activos ni intervención humana. Amazon también indica que los reactores pueden ser refrigerados por aire, por agua o mediante una combinación de ambos.
El dinero. Amazon no ha revelado cuánto está aportando. Un portavoz declaraba al medio The Register únicamente que la empresa está "invirtiendo miles de millones en proyectos de energía nuclear" en general. Amazon invirtió una buena cantidad de dinero en X-Energy en una de sus rondas de financiación, aportando 700 millones de dólares en 2024. El papel de la gran tecnológica aquí es ser tanto inversor como primer cliente de X-Energy. Eso sí, Amazon afirma que no participará en el proceso de aprobación regulatoria.
Lo que no se dice. Tal y como cuenta The Register, EEUU aún no ha construido ni un solo SMR comercial operativo, y X-energy no ha construido un reactor operativo de ningún tamaño. El Xe-100 todavía se encuentra en fase de desarrollo y concesión de licencias.
Los permisos en EEUU añaden otro obstáculo, pues según cuenta el medio, los permisos de construcción para estos proyectos están vinculados a un emplazamiento específico. X-energy afirma que su primer proyecto, cuatro reactores en una planta de Dow Chemical en Seadrift (Texas), se encuentra en las fases finales de revisión por parte de la Comisión Reguladora Nuclear, pero dicha aprobación no se aplicaría automáticamente a Indiana.
TechCrunch añade que el emplazamiento de Seadrift está en el centro de una demanda en Texas que alega un "incumplimiento habitual" de las normativas sobre agua y residuos en la instalación de Dow, y que X-energy aún no ha comenzado las obras allí.
Cuánto tardará. Un portavoz de X-energy declaraba al South Bend Tribune que la planta podría estar terminada "tan pronto como a mediados de la década de 2030", pero que el calendario "podría cambiar" a medida que el proyecto avance. Por otro lado The Verge señala que no se espera que la construcción de Cascade, la primera planta anunciada por Amazon, comience hasta finales de esta década.
