articles.title: US Agencies Detail Incident Response Practices for Rogue AI Agents
articles.text:
Effective and efficient use of complex agentic systems is important for all organizations, but recognizing, preventing and recovering from them going rogue could be an existential necessity.
NIST, the NSA, and CISA recognize the increasing potential for AI agents to behave in an unexpected and potentially harmful manner, and has responded with a list of key practices for both preparing for and responding to such behavior. The report (Key Practices for Incident Readiness and Response in Super Intelligence Training and Evaluation) uses the term super intelligence (SI) rather than artificial intelligence (AI) in line with presidential executive order 14434.
In the report, the ten key practices are grouped into five stages: prepare, detect, respond, recover, and report. For clarity, the report also includes three useful terminology definitions covering AI agents, AI control incident, and AI control near-miss.
“The practices are intended to help the frontier SI industry prevent, prepare for, and respond rapidly to incidents in which SI systems do not act as intended or authorized,” the agencies explain.
Preparation includes activities such as asset and risk inventories, defense-in-depth, least privilege, zero-trust controls, credential management, supply chain risk management and more.
Detection requires continuous monitoring for correct behavior, and anomalous activity and indications of compromise.
Response entails isolating affected systems, revoking credentials, rebuilding compromised environments, determining the blast radius, and conducting root-cause analysis that looks past the specific vulnerability exploited.
Recovery requires testing restoration procedures in advance and documenting recovery decisions along with any residual risk accepted.
Reporting requirements are three-fold: report incidents to all affected parties, wherever required by law, and publicly and widely.
None of the stages or practices is given any greater weight over the others. Instead, the five stages should be treated as a single target. Complex agents all have the potential for misbehavior bordering on rogue and dangerous. These ten practices combine to help organizations develop a stable and effective environment for complex agentic systems, where problems can be detected early and effective operation maintained.
Only the final two practices (#9 and #10 in the Report stage) go beyond the more technical steps of incident readiness and response.
The first of these, ‘Notify Government’, may be a legal requirement, including: “Adhere to any applicable legal reporting requirements, including cybersecurity incident reporting obligations to CISA, law enforcement, and/or cyber-defense organizations.”
The last, Share Information Publicly, is mainstream good behavior throughout cybersecurity that will benefit everyone: “Share details with the public, where appropriate, as early as feasible,” and “Identify and publicly report key practices, takeaways, or improvements adopted in response to the incident or that could benefit other actors in the ecosystem.”
The value of this document is not in providing any new or unrecognized information for AI agent governance, but in providing a very clear and thorough checklist for use by security professionals to maximize the use of agents while minimizing or recovering from agentic incidents.

articles.title: GTC Berlin 2026: Live Updates From NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s Keynote
articles.text:
Founded in a tent near the Berlin Wall in 1980, the Tempodrom moved several times before settling near Anhalter Bahnhof in 2001. Its permanent home has since hosted concerts, galas and political events.
Today, it hosts a different kind of spectacle.
GTC Berlin runs three days, with more than 100 sessions on agentic AI, robotics, physical AI, open models and accelerated computing underway at STATION-Berlin down the road. Here, journalists, analysts and partners have gathered for the main event: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s keynote.
Huang Takes the Stage
Huang opened with a question: What do L’Oréal, Revolut, Spotify, Merck, Vodafone, Zara, Porsche, Nestlé and HSBC have in common? They’re all European companies and they’re all working with NVIDIA on AI, he said.
The keynote comes on the heels of NVIDIA’s weeklong road across Europe — Paris, London, Stockholm, Dublin — with the company committing nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem across Europe and working with 12,000+ partners.“After decades of advancement in the computer industry, we are now at the beginnings of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said.
AI is a five-layer cake, Huang explained. Energy powers advanced computers that are part of an AI factory, which generates tokens and digital intelligence from the models that run on it, which are then integrated into every application.
“Long before the AI models emerge, the infrastructure has to exist,” he said, highlighting how, similarly, the internet first needed networking, and electricity first required the grid.
“To be part of this AI economy, you don’t want to just be consuming the AI; you want to be producing the AI,” Huang said. “We could do all of that here in Europe, and in fact, we’ve already started.”
The AI Factory Gets a New Form Factor
Huang framed NVIDIA’s full-stack AI factory — spanning hardware, system software, CUDA-X libraries and models — as a broad platform for building and operating AI infrastructure.
“This now represents the breadth of technology necessary to create the AI factory,” Huang said. “This is what NVIDIA builds today, and this is the foundation by which we can enable Europe to be part of the AI ecosystem, the AI economy.”  
He said Vera Rubin, in full production, extends NVIDIA’s computing platform beyond models and large language models to process the entire AI agent. He also showed several of NVIDIA’s latest rack-scale hardware offerings.
Next, Huang announced NVIDIA DSX POD, a reference design for complete NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery. With DSX POD, onsite deployment can shrink from six months to just 14 days once site utilities are ready.
“This is a complete transformation of the world supply chain,” Huang said. “This will change the way that people install and build data centers, and hopefully, as a result, velocity goes up.”
The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform enables companies to reduce water consumption for cooling by up to 100% and generate the same AI output with up to 30% less power.
Agents Are the New Computing Platform — and Safety Is an Engineering Problem
Huang said agents think, reason, iterate and use tools, driving token consumption as they become more useful.
He described an agent as comprising five elements: a model, a harness that orchestrates its work and memory, a sandbox that isolates the harness, knowledge and tools. In that framing, an agent is more than a model answering questions; it can draw on knowledge and act through tools.
“The most important thing is to make sure the agent is secure,” Huang said. The autonomous agent can access files, resources, networks and tools, so its privileges should be minimal and it should be monitored.
NVIDIA’s answer is the new NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for Safe AI Agents, a full-stack design built on NVIDIA OpenShell — an open source, policy-controlled runtime with kernel-level sandboxing that sits between an agent and the systems it can affect.
 
That means privileges, policy enforcement and monitoring must adapt dynamically. “Every single time an agent is launched, the privileges are different,” Huang said.
Open Models Turn Expertise Into an Advantage
Huang presented NVIDIA’s open models as a starting point for building AI tailored to specific needs.
NVIDIA’s frontier, open models are available for use across industries: Nemotron for language, Cosmos for world foundation models, GR00T for humanoid robotics, Alpamayo for autonomous vehicles, Ising for quantum-classical computing and Earth-2 for physics AI.
“We are the frontier,” Huang said. “So in all of these different areas, we offer you all of the models, and we’re continuously working on it. We’ve been working on it for a decade, and we’ll continue to work on this forever.”
NVIDIA provides the models, data and scripts to reproduce them, and companies can post-train a model on their own data for a particular use case — turning proprietary data into what he called “sovereign intelligence.”
“You could start with an open model, something that’s incredibly good like Nemotron, and with your own data, post-train it for your use case and achieve, of course, super intelligence,” Huang said. “That is a very sensible thing to do, and all the technology exists today.”
NVIDIA Gives Agents a Knowledge Layer
Huang then introduced the NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation as a set of models and libraries for connecting agents to enterprise data, whether it’s unstructured information in documents or structured data in databases.
He highlighted Nemotron tools for parsing documents, embedding queries and reranking relevant information, along with new NVIDIA Kumo models for making predictions from structured data.
“Ultimately, what turns these super agents, these agents into super agents, is that you give them access to your company’s knowledge,” Huang said.
NVIDIA CUDA-X — Accelerated Tools for Agents
Huang then described NVIDIA CUDA-X as a collection of accelerated libraries used across science, engineering, research and creative work.
NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform has more than 11 million developers building on it.
Huang said those libraries can accelerate simulators, solvers and data-processing engines — the kinds of tools agents may draw on to do useful work.
“CUDA-X tools are what gives agents the tools of the trade,” Huang said. 
Agents Go to Work in Labs, Factories and Engineering
A video showcased NVIDIA Agent Toolkit bringing company knowledge, models and tools together in three industry examples:
At Lila Sciences, agents help design a potential B-cell lymphoma therapy, using virtual experiments to guide work in an automated lab.
At Siemens’ Erlangen factory, agents help prepare new products for production, testing plans in a digital twin before changes reach the factory floor.
And at Dassault Systèmes, engineering agents adapt vehicle design, using simulation to identify a problem and refine the design.
“And [all this] knowledge and tools belong to you,” Huang said after the video rolled. “That’s your expertise, and so all of this is now possible to do.”
Telcos as Distributed AI Infrastructure
Huang said AI is transforming telecommunications, improving spectrum efficiency and turning cell towers into distributed AI infrastructure.
He cited 100,000 sites and about 100 gigawatts of distributed data centers, and said NVIDIA has made its first commercial phone call on T-Mobile’s network with Nokia after nearly eight years of work.
“Now CUDA makes phone calls,” Huang said. “AI will revolutionize the way we do telecommunications. It will enhance our spectrum efficiency tremendously.” 
AI Moves Into the Treatment Room
Healthcare and life sciences leaders are building on NVIDIA technologies to advance drug discovery and expand patient care.
For example, NVIDIA and Siemens Healthineers are developing AI-enabled radiation therapy.
Nemotron agents coordinate treatment planning, the Isaac for Healthcare platform and Omniverse libraries create a digital twin of the device and patient anatomy to simulate tumor targeting. Holoscan with IGX Thor connects live imaging and sensor data to enable real-time adaptive delivery as the patient moves.
Huang described adaptive radiotherapy as a physical-AI application: as the patient’s body and tumor change during treatment, the system must track the changes and adjust the radiation targeting.
“The tumor is changing in shape. The physical body is changing while you’re in therapy,” Huang said. “The robot, this radio adaptive radiotherapy system, has to perceive the changing environment, understand where the tumor is, segment it just perfectly and direct the radiotherapy accordingly.”
The Road Ahead: Mobility Leaders Join NVIDIA’s Automotive Ecosystem
Huang said the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform is being designed into more vehicle fleets, with autonomous-driving software connecting robotaxis to ride-hailing services.
Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride are showcasing selected autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform, demonstrating potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles as well as future robotaxi fleets.
In addition, Volvo Cars is adopting Hyperion and NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack software for safe automated driving. NVIDIA also introduced new AI and safety technologies to help developers build, validate and deploy autonomous vehicles at scale.
Volkswagen’s van, JLR, Volvo and Mercedes-Benz’s next-generation vehicles will be Hyperion-compatible, Huang announced, saying, “Welcome to Hyperion.”
A Reference Humanoid for Robotics Researchers
Huang then announced Agile ONE SN, a reference humanoid built on Isaac GR00T — a 31-degree-of-freedom body, expected to be available next year, designed to cut researcher setup time from weeks to days.
The platform is modular: researchers can use the full workflow or pull in selected components. 
“This is a great starting point,” Huang said. 
It builds on NVIDIA’s open physical AI stack — Isaac Capture for data collection, GR00T models for robot intelligence, Isaac Lab for simulation-based training, Isaac OS for runtime — and NVIDIA’s open physical AI dataset. Partners including Agility Robotics, Figure, KUKA and NEURA Robotics are already building on the same platform.
Personal AI Gets a New Machine
Huang closed by discussing RTX Spark laptops, which launched last week, bringing together RTX graphics and NVIDIA’s full-stack AI platform in slim, premium Windows PCs for accelerated creation, immersive gaming and powerful local AI.
He compared its 1 petaflop of performance and 128GB of memory with the DGX-1 he delivered to OpenAI in 2016 — then made the difference in size the punchline:
“In the year 2016, I delivered 1 petaflop and 128GB … to a small company called OpenAI,” Huang said, holding up the compact machine in front of the audience. “This is 1 petaflop and 128GB. The only difference, of course, is that I can hold this like this, and DGX-1 took two people to carry upstairs.”
Huang then showed a video of an agent helping train Hugging Face’s Microduck: it set up a course and simulated the robot in Isaac Sim, sent training jobs to the cloud, then brought the learned policy back to RTX Spark for evaluation before deploying it to the physical robot.
A flock of four Microducks joined Huang onstage, sitting down, standing up and even taking a nap on cue. He explained that they were created on RTX Spark, trained in the cloud and learned their skills in simulation.
“You were created on RTX Spark … [we] trained you in the cloud on a whole bunch of NVIDIA supercomputers, and you learned your skills right here on RTX Spark and the digital twin,” Huang told them.
The Full Lineup
With the Microducks gathered around him, Huang recapped the keynote: Europe is building its AI economy, AI factories are evolving to run agents and physical AI is the next frontier.
“So that’s it,” Huang said. “Everybody can build agents. Every company in Europe will become an AI company … and we’re going to have a thriving AI economy here in Europe.”
To close, Huang had one more surprise: a Eurovision-style musical send-off that turned the keynote’s themes into a comic recap.
The lyrics raced from OpenShell’s guardrails — “No credentials. Access dismissed” and “Sentry on BlueField never clocks off” — to physical AI, where robot training was likened to “college for robots without student loans.”
The punchline: “You can’t spell fungible without fun.” A saxophone solo led into a rousing “We are Europa” chorus.
“Let’s work together to build Europe’s AI economy and put AI to work,” Huang said, closing out his talk. “Have a great GTC.”

articles.title: Japan launches mission to bring home a piece of the Martian moon Phobos
articles.text:
Japan launched a $578 million mission Monday on a five-year expedition to land on the largest moon of Mars and retrieve samples for return to Earth, a daring international project that could yield new insights into the formation of the Solar System.
The robotic Martian Moons eXploration mission, known as MMX, lifted off at 3:41 pm EDT Monday (4:41 am Japan Standard Time Tuesday) from Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan.
The MMX spacecraft rode into orbit atop a 207-foot-tall (63-meter) H3 rocket, Japan’s flagship launch vehicle. The rocket assigned to MMX debuted a new souped-up configuration with four strap-on solid rocket boosters, full-throttle main engines, and an extended payload shroud to accommodate the demands of Japan’s heaviest and most ambitious interplanetary mission to date.
The rocket’s upper stage accelerated the MMX spacecraft to a top speed of more than 24,000 mph, fast enough to break free of Earth’s gravitational pull for the 10-month voyage to Mars. The nearly 9,900-pound (4.5-metric ton) spacecraft—two-thirds of its mass comprised of propellant—separated from the H3 rocket about 71 minutes after liftoff.
Hiroshi Yamakawa, president of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), declared the launch a success. “A long journey of five years has just started,” Yamakawa said.
MMX established contact with ground controllers, unfurled its solar panels, and was in a “very stable condition” soon after separating from the H3 rocket, according to Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, the mission’s project manager at JAXA. “So far, so good.”
“The MMX [mission] we launched today is a challenging mission aiming for the world’s first sample return from the Martian moons,” said Yoshihiro Seki, Japan’s science minister. “We hope that the results obtained through this mission will contribute to the development of our nation’s space science and exploration technology.”
Building on a legacy
The mission to the Martian moons builds on Japan’s success in leading the Hayabusa and Hayabusa 2 missions, the world’s first two spacecraft to bring back pristine specimens from asteroids. Scientists believe Phobos could itself be an asteroid that was captured into orbit around Mars billions of years ago. One of MMX’s science goals is finding out if that theory is correct.

articles.title: Figma co-founder Dylan Field thinks MCP is not a perfect protocol | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Despite Figma co-founder Dylan Field’s concerns about MCP (model context protocol), which standardizes how AI agents connect to external data sources and tools, the company is expanding its support for the open source standard.
At the design company’s first Config conference held in India, the company announced 20 new MCP partners, including Amp, ClickUp, Dia, Junie by JetBrains, Linear, Meta Muse, Mistral, Notion, OpenCode, and Sarvam Agents.
Field has expressed his misgivings about MCP before. Days before this announcement, one of MCP’s co-creators complained about Figma not supporting the open source tool Pi. As part of his response, Field made a comment about Anthropic not making its various resources available via MCP.
“I find it interesting that Anthropic (creators of MCP standard) do not expose artifacts/other cloud resources created via MCP,” he wrote on X. “The debate is framed as open vs closed. Everyone always prefers open … obviously. And meanwhile issues of asymmetric context sharing are ignored.”
(Field later added that Figma plans support Pi.)
At a media briefing, I asked Field about this debate. The co-founder explained that while Figma wants to be open, he doesn’t think MCP is a perfect protocol.
“I’m really excited about what we’re doing in terms of opening up our ecosystem. I also think that MCP is not a perfect protocol. And I think that it is something that has tons of room for improvement,” the co-founder responded. “It is advantaged more to frontier labs. Also, I understand everyone online who just wants a protocol that they can use when they want to use their Figma data, and I want them to use it, too.”
Figma’s CEO said that the reason the company doesn’t want to be fully open is that the more data the company exposes through MCP, the higher the chance of abuse.
He also clarified that while most users don’t intend to use MCP or Figma data in a malicious way, the company still has to think about those potential risks.

articles.title: Trump is giving Nick Shirley $10,000 and launching a $25 million fraud bounty program
articles.text:
Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance said on Tuesday that the Trump administration was giving right-wing YouTuber Nick Shirley $10,000 and launching a $25 million bounty program for members of the public to report fraud.
Trump is giving Nick Shirley $10,000 and launching a $25 million fraud bounty program
In December 2025, Shirley published a viral video alleging fraud at daycares in Minnesota that were operated by members of the local Somali community. Shirley lingered in parking lots and asked to enter childcare centers, taking refusals as evidence that the centers weren’t actually caring for children. The video quickly went viral, triggering a massive governmental response: Federal immigration agents descended on the Minneapolis area, and the Trump administration froze Minnesota’s federal funding for childcare. Shirley has since visited other states in the US under similar pretenses, showing up unannounced to grocery stores and hospice centers in search of evidence of fraud. Vance and others in the administration publicly praised Shirley, who has since become a mainstay in the MAGA-aligned content creator ecosystem. He’s helped popularize a genre of so-called independent journalism popular on the right in which content creators and influencers confront businesses or people they suspect of fraud or crime as the basis for their online content. Harassment — or even immigration crackdowns — often follow.
The administration told Fox News that it was also launching the Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program (WHIP), a pool of $25 million open to anyone who believes they’ve witnessed fraud. A “particular emphasis” is placed on fraud in hospice, home healthcare, daycares, and special services, a government website says. A chatbot collecting responses instructs the reporting party: “Briefly describe what you saw, heard, or read. A few sentences are enough. Include names, dates, amounts, or records if you have them, and how you know. Note any details you’re unsure about.”
According to Fox News and the reporting portal, members of the public who flag fraud are eligible to get up to $30,000 if a tip submitted leads to a conviction or significant federal action. But speaking on Tuesday, Trump contradicted the $30,000 ceiling.
”If you turn somebody in and … you find $1 billion, we are giving a commission to that person of 1 percent,” Trump said today. (One percent of $1 billion would exceed the $30,000 cap.) “And if it’s $10 billion, $200 billion, $400 billion, we’re giving a 1 percent commission to that person,” Trump continued.
The White House didn’t immediately clarify how the $10,000 payment to Shirley was calculated or how the program is being funded in the first place.
Shirley’s methods have been criticized particularly in Minnesota, where sweeping fraud investigations were already taking place before he arrived to make content. He accused businesses of faking childcare services based on little more than being denied entry to facilities, and — to the frustration of many — acted as if his video was the first fraud investigation in the state. Subsequent state official visits to the centers Shirley featured found them operating “as expected.”

articles.title: Repeat tech entrepreneur Ryan St. Germaine joins Raven as partner | BetaKit
articles.text:
Vancouver’s Raven Indigenous Capital Partners has bolstered its investment team as it prepares to raise its next fund.
The news: Ryan St. Germaine has joined the impact-driven venture capital (VC) firm as a general partner (GP). He and Raven announced the news on LinkedIn last week, when he officially assumed the role. Raven, which claims to be North America’s only Indigenous-led and owned VC firm, backs Indigenous-led tech businesses across the continent, from seed to Series A rounds. Its portfolio includes AdvancedAg, Animikii, CruxOCM, and PLATO Testing, among others.
From the source: “We talk about wanting more Indigenous folks in venture, and if we want to do that, we’ve got to take bets on the people that we believe can get it done,” St. Germaine told BetaKit in an interview. “I think people recognize my abilities. I’ve founded and led and exited companies on the other side, and it’s not that different.”
The context: In VC, moving straight to GP is rare, as most people gradually work their way up the ranks. But St. Germaine and Raven are confident that he has the chops to excel in this position. The Métis serial technology entrepreneur behind BCjobs.ca, Jobcast, and Indigenous Tech Circle had sat on Raven’s investment committee for its $100-million CAD second fund and served as an entrepreneur-in-residence since early 2024, where the firm said he has played “an important part” in its work.
St. Germaine joins existing Raven GPs Althea Wishloff and Sean McCormick under managing partner Stephen Nairne. He said there are no other immediate changes to Raven’s leadership. Raven plans to begin raising its next fund in late 2025 or early 2026. For now, he’s supporting existing Raven companies from Fund II and its $25-million predecessor. The firm is also deploying a $32-million Indigenous Outcomes Fund that’s geared toward supporting climate and health initiatives that improve outcomes for Indigenous communities.
Final thought: The new Raven GP said Indigenous companies don’t receive enough early-stage risk capital. St. Germaine is excited by the chance to help create “more equitable outcomes” for the community. He is also looking forward to working more closely with the startups he previously pitched on participating in Indigenous Tech Circle, where he plans to transition out of the CEO role but stay involved on the board.
Feature image courtesy Raven Indigenous Capital Partners.

articles.title: Cogumelo pode ajudar a reduzir o sal da comida sem perder sabor
articles.text:
O aumento do sódio nos alimentos tem se tornado um problema cada vez maior na saúde humana. Levantamentos da OMS apontam que em 2023, cerca de 1,7 milhão de mortes no mundo estiveram diretamente ligadas ao alto consumo de sódio. Isso é acompanhado por outros dados da instituição que apontam que 1,4 bilhão de adultos possuem hipertensão e problemas relacionados ao excesso de sal.
E esses problemas podem estar perto de serem mitigados. Pesquisadores da Universidade Médica de Gannan, na China, identificaram um peptídeo derivado do cogumelo Hypsizygus marmoreus, mais conhecido como Shimeji-branco, capaz de aumentar em 70,59% a percepção de sabor salgado em testes. O estudo foi publicado na revista Nature em sua seção de “ciência da comida” no início deste mês.
Para quem tem pressa:
- Pesquisadores da Universidade Médica de Gannan, na China, identificaram peptídeos derivados do cogumelo shimeji-branco capazes de aumentar a percepção do sabor salgado em testes;
- Entre os compostos analisados, o peptídeo ASHGEGF apresentou o maior resultado, aumentando a percepção de salinidade em até 70,59%. Os outros dois peptídeos selecionados tiveram aumentos de 49,02% e 47,06%;
- A pesquisa busca desenvolver alternativas para reduzir o sódio nos alimentos sem comprometer o sabor. Os próximos testes vão avaliar o desempenho dos peptídeos em alimentos e soluções com baixo teor de sódio.
Extração de diversos peptídeos
A seleção do Hypsizygus marmoreus não foi aleatória. Sua rica presença de bioativos e realçadores de sabor tornou o shimeji-branco o favorito para a pesquisa.
Para identificar os peptídeos presentes no alimento, os autores do estudo misturaram o cogumelo em pó, água e algumas enzimas para quebrar as proteínas. Os resultados mostraram mais de seis mil peptídeos.
Com auxílio de ferramentas de IA e sistemas computacionais, os pesquisadores identificaram e reduziram o número de compostos relevantes e estáveis para apenas cinco. Produzidos sinteticamente, os peptídeos passaram por testes primários, nos quais três se destacaram: ASHGEGF, GDDWT e LDDGF.
Entre eles, o que mais se mostrou significativo foi o ASHGEGF. O peptídeo em questão potencializou a sensação de salinidade da solução de NaCl a 3 mg/mL, em até 70,59%, enquanto o LDDGF apresentou um aumento de 49,02% e por fim o GDDWT com 47,06%.
Os testes foram feitos primeiramente com humanos que indicaram o aumento do sabor salgado. Em seguida, os compostos passaram por uma “língua eletrônica” que apontou resultados mais específicos. A vantagem do experimento com o equipamento também foi relevante para evitar erros causados pela possível fadiga sensorial humana.
Leia mais:
- Sal demais faz mal — mas será que pouco sal também é perigoso?
- Não é só cortar o sal: estudo mostra alimentos para combater hipertensão
- Dois ingredientes comuns são inimigos do seu estômago!
Teste prático na alimentação
Os próximos passos da pesquisa visam analisar a performance dos peptídeos em alimentos e soluções com baixo nível de sódio.
Esse processo busca explorar a reação dos compostos com pouco sódio, entendendo mais a fundo sua capacidade de potencialização e se eles podem ser uma solução relevante para a substituição dos altos níveis salinos nos alimentos, sem que eles percam o sabor.
Ana Figueiredo é editora de tecnologia do Olhar Digital. É formada em Jornalismo pela Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU).

articles.title: Jamie Dornan sur Aragorn : « Pas une seule seconde je ne cherche à faire mieux que Viggo »
articles.text:
Contrairement à plusieurs acteurs de la trilogie Le Seigneur des anneaux initiale (Ian McKellen, Elijah Wood, Andy Serkis), Viggo Mortensen ne fera pas son retour dans The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum, spin-off qui se situe entre les événements des films Le Hobbit et La Communauté de l’anneau. Aragorn, son personnage, sera pourtant au cœur du récit. Il sera incarné par Jamie Dornan, 44 ans, soit 24 ans de moins que Viggo Mortensen.
Pour beaucoup de fans, le départ de Viggo Mortensen, ô combien charismatique dans le rôle d’Aragorn, passe mal. Jamie Dornan en a bien conscience. Il s’est exprimé pour la première fois sur cette succession à l’occasion d’un entretien accordé à L’Officiel USA, paru ce lundi 19 octobre. Les comparaisons seront difficiles à éviter, mais Jamie Dornan prévient qu’il ne cherche pas à faire oublier Viggo Mortensen.
Le nouvel Aragorn rend hommage à l’ancien Aragorn
Jamie Dornan ne minimise pas la difficulté. Il confie : « Il y a de la pression quand on essaie d’emboîter de tels pas. On m’a demandé d’interpréter un rôle hyper iconique, et je ferai de mon mieux. Mais pour moi, Aragorn sera toujours et à jamais Viggo. Son interprétation est l’une de mes préférées de tous les temps et je suis honoré d’essayer de retrouver au moins une partie de l’énergie qu’il a apportée à l’origine au personnage. Pas une seule seconde je ne cherche à faire mieux que lui. »
Jamie Dornan nourrit donc un immense respect pour Viggo Mortensen. Attention quand même à ne pas se sentir trop écrasé sous la pression, au risque de s’effacer totalement. Par le passé, on a vu d’autres acteurs éprouver des difficultés à passer après un autre. On pense à Alden Ehrenreich, qui a incarné un jeune Han Solo dans Solo: A Star Wars Story, après Harrison Ford.
L’histoire de la saga a de quoi le rassurer : Viggo Mortensen n’était pas le premier Aragorn. Peter Jackson avait d’abord confié le rôle à Stuart Townsend, avant de le remplacer par Viggo Mortensen. Le personnage a donc déjà changé de visage une fois, avec le succès que l’on connaît.
Jamie Dornan est en tout cas déjà applaudi par Leo Woodall, qui interprète Halvard, un rôdeur dúnedain compagnon d’Aragorn. « Je peux le dire maintenant, mon Aragorn est Jamie Dornan », assure-t-il dans ce même entretien croisé.
Dans The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum, dont la sortie est prévue le 15 décembre 2027 dans les salles françaises, Gandalf (Sir Ian McKellen) charge Aragorn de traquer Gollum (Andy Serkis, également réalisateur du film) afin de garder Bilbon Sacquet et la Comté à l’abri de Sauron. Outre Andy Serkis et Ian McKellen, Elijah Wood retrouvera le costume de Frodon avec une présence modeste, et Lee Pace celui de Thranduil. Le casting est complété par de nouveaux arrivants, comme Kate Winslet et Anya Taylor-Joy.

articles.title: Cuáles son las cinco prácticas que hacen que la computadora dure menos de uno o dos años
articles.text:
Muchos usuarios creen que un computador se vuelve lento o se avería por simple antigüedad, pero en la mayoría de los casos el desgaste prematuro responde a hábitos cotidianos que pasan desapercibidos.
Desde bloquear la ventilación hasta instalar programas sin control, existen prácticas que deterioran tanto el hardware como el software del equipo, y que son evitables con cuidados básicos.
Hábitos que afectan el tiempo de vida de un computador
- Bloquear la ventilación y acumular polvo
El calor es el principal enemigo de cualquier equipo. Los ventiladores integrados en la carcasa cumplen la función de ingresar aire fresco y expulsar el calor interno, un proceso que se ve comprometido cuando se usa el portátil sobre superficies blandas, como una cama, un sillón o las piernas.
El polvo y las pelusas que se acumulan en las entradas de aire también atascan el interior y empeoran la circulación. Esto genera un recalentamiento progresivo que puede dañar los componentes.
Por eso conviene usar el equipo siempre sobre una mesa rígida, limpiar los puertos externos cada mes y abrir el chasis cada tres meses para eliminar el polvo interior con aire comprimido.
- Dejar que el equipo se sobrecaliente
Cada componente de un computador está diseñado para funcionar dentro de un rango de temperatura específico. Superarlo acelera su degradación o provoca averías directas.
Un exceso de calor puede derretir soldaduras y desplazar componentes, además de secar la pasta térmica de la CPU, lo que reduce su capacidad de refrigeración y agrava el recalentamiento general. La acumulación de polvo también puede derivar en “thermal throttling”, una reducción forzada de la velocidad de los componentes para evitar daños irreversibles.
El sobrecalentamiento constante perjudica directamente a la batería: pierde capacidad de forma acelerada hasta un punto en que el equipo necesita estar siempre conectado a la corriente para funcionar.
- Maltratar la batería con cargas extremas
Dejar el portátil enchufado de manera permanente con el 100% de carga no es recomendable, como tampoco lo es mantenerlo con la batería completamente descargada durante semanas o ponerlo a cargar cuando está cerca del 0%. Ambos extremos aceleran la degradación de la batería y reducen su vida útil.
Guardar el equipo sin usarlo durante largos períodos también desgasta la batería y puede provocar que, al retomarlo, ni siquiera encienda. Lo recomendable es usarlo con cierta frecuencia y mantenerlo con algo de carga.
El uso de cargadores no originales suma otro riesgo, ya que no regulan correctamente el voltaje ni protegen contra picos de tensión, lo que puede derivar en fallos eléctricos irreversibles o en que la batería se hinche.
- Saturar el almacenamiento y descuidar el software
Llenar un disco de estado sólido (SSD) hasta casi su capacidad máxima desgasta el componente más rápido de lo habitual. Cuando no queda espacio libre, el disco pierde margen para procesos vitales como la recolección de basura o la nivelación del desgaste.
A esto se suma instalar programas de forma descontrolada, lo que consume almacenamiento, fragmenta las unidades y acumula aplicaciones que cargan automáticamente al inicio, afectando los tiempos de arranque y el consumo de memoria RAM.
No reiniciar el equipo con frecuencia también perjudica el rendimiento: la RAM acumula restos de microcódigo y se pueden generar fugas de memoria cuando los programas no se cierran correctamente. Reiniciar al menos una vez al día descarga la memoria y resuelve conflictos entre procesos.
Descuidar las actualizaciones del sistema operativo y los controladores le resta estabilidad al equipo y lo expone a amenazas de seguridad.
- Manipular el equipo sin cuidado y hacer clic sin pensar
Un computador portátil no está fabricado con estándares militares, por lo que los golpes o una manipulación descuidada pueden dañar sus componentes internos. Transportarlo sin protección adecuada puede averiar conectores o separar la tapa de la pantalla del resto del chasis.
Tomar el equipo únicamente por los bordes, sobre todo si es pesado o tiene una base flexible, puede combarlo y afectar piezas rígidas en su interior.
En el plano del software, hacer clic sin verificar el origen de una descarga puede instalar programas no deseados, modificar la página de inicio del navegador o anclar herramientas de terceros sin autorización. Aunque no se trate de un enlace malicioso, estas instalaciones ralentizan el sistema y consumen recursos de forma innecesaria.

articles.title: HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 Will Bring AI and HPC to the Moon on Astrolab FLIP
articles.text:
HPE has announced that its Spaceborne Computer-4 will power artificial intelligence workloads and, according to it, will be the first HPC benchmark on the lunar surface. The compute module is set to ride aboard Astrolab’s FLIP rover, which will land near the Moon’s South Pole as part of NASA’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) initiative. This moves HPE’s spaceborne program beyond the International Space Station and into an atmosphere-free environment with much higher radiation exposure.
The mission is intended to launch in late 2026 on Voyager Technologies’ Griffin-1 lander. Once deployed, Spaceborne Computer-4 will run large language model retrieval-augmented generation, vision inference, LiDAR data processing for mapping and navigation, and an AI services container designed to demonstrate reliable deployment of scalable AI applications at the lunar edge. AI is headed to the moon.
We first covered this hardware in June, when we looked inside the storage of Spaceborne Computer-4 at HPE Discover. The fourth iteration is a much smaller and lighter system than the HPE Spaceborne Computer-1 we covered years ago, which makes sense because mass is critical when sending payloads to the Moon. The idea is to build a small compute subsystem that can operate with low mass, low power, and that can make decisions locally, rather than having to transmit back to Earth.
Since there is no air on the Moon to move across a heatsink, the system uses a space radiator instead of fans. The housing has an intricate lattice structure that we saw in person at Discover 2026.
For storage, the system uses a Kioxia BG-series M.2 SSD, the same class of DRAM-less drive you might find in a low-cost TinyMiniMicro PC. Kioxia has been proving commercial NAND on the ISS for years, and this mission extends that work to the Moon’s harsher radiation environment.
HPE says the compute module is lightweight, self-contained, fanless, and equipped with both a low-power CPU and GPU. The company also assembled software to optimize interaction with Earth-based resources and securely deliver results back from the Moon.
HPE will also support Astrolab’s mission control in Hawthorne, California, using HPE Private Cloud and HPE CloudOps Software to manage and automate workloads from Earth.
NASA and Deloitte are joining the mission to deploy additional AI workloads. NASA will run its FLUID (Federated Learning for Unbounded and Intelligent Decentralization) experiment, coordinating three separate AI models trained on data from Earth, the Moon, and the International Space Station. NASA will also conduct a tuned LLM test with semantic processing abilities to search and interpret onboard documents. Deloitte’s Silent Shield system will provide near real-time predictive cyber-analytics and anomaly detection.
We missed an event in Hawthorne, CA last week due to OCP 2026, but we received a few photos from the event.
Final Words
If these benchmarks work as planned, they will provide useful data on whether off-the-shelf-class components can support the emerging lunar economy instead of requiring expensive custom space-grade silicon. We expect this compute mission to succeed, assuming it powers on on the lunar surface. Given the cost of lunar launches, everything is thoroughly tested before it gets loaded into a rocket.

articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.text:
Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. Their findings, published in Nature Physics, demonstrate how this combination could help scientists investigate fundamental interactions between matter and fields that are increasingly difficult to simulate using conventional computers.
A Strange Quantum Effect Predicted in 1959
In everyday physics, a charged particle responds to the electric and magnetic fields it encounters. Quantum mechanics, however, reveals that particles can behave in ways that have no straightforward counterpart in our ordinary experience.
In 1959, physicists Yakir Aharonov and David Bohm predicted that a charged particle could be affected by magnetic flux even if it traveled entirely outside the region containing the magnetic field. Rather than experiencing a conventional magnetic force along its path, the particle would undergo a change in its quantum phase.
Quantum phase describes an aspect of a particle's wave behavior that influences how different possible paths interfere with one another. Although the phase itself is not directly visible, differences in phase can produce measurable effects.
The prediction became known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect and was eventually verified in experiments involving real electrons. It remains one of the clearest demonstrations that the quantum world operates according to rules that go beyond the familiar laws of classical physics.
Researchers are now exploring how this phenomenon behaves in more complex theoretical systems known as lattice gauge theories.
These theories describe how matter interacts with fields associated with fundamental forces. They represent space as a grid, with matter located at individual points and fields associated with the connections between them. Such models are particularly important in particle physics and high-energy physics, where scientists study the basic particles and interactions that make up the universe.
The challenge is that the mathematics becomes extraordinarily demanding as these systems grow more complicated. Even powerful conventional computers can struggle to calculate how all the interacting components evolve.
Quantum computers offer a different approach. Instead of attempting to calculate every aspect of a quantum system using classical computing methods, scientists can construct another quantum system that follows the same underlying rules. They can then observe its behavior directly, an approach known as quantum simulation.
How Scientists Built the Quantum Experiment
The Oxford project began in 2022, when lead author Dr. Sebastian Saner, Dr. Oana Bazavan, and their colleagues started developing a way to simulate lattice gauge theories using a hybrid quantum system. They collaborated with Dr. Alejandro Bermudez of the Instituto de Física Teórica in Madrid.
Their experimental design relied on two different quantum components that performed separate functions.
The first consisted of qubits encoded in the internal states of trapped ions, which are electrically charged atoms held in place using electromagnetic fields. These qubits represented the gauge fields in the theoretical model.
The second component used quantum oscillators, created by the vibrations of those same trapped ions. These oscillators represented matter.
By combining the two, the researchers constructed a simple loop that served as a basic building block of a lattice gauge theory. Two oscillators represented matter at two different locations, while two qubits represented the fields connecting those locations.
Although the arrangement was small, it was sufficient to reproduce an important interaction between matter and magnetic flux.
Quantum Entanglement Creates a Surprising Solution
The researchers next placed the two qubits into an entangled quantum state. Entanglement is a phenomenon in which quantum systems become linked in ways that cannot be fully explained by classical physics.
Within the team's simulated lattice gauge theory, this entangled state represented magnetic flux passing through the center of the loop.
Initially, the researchers had planned to introduce the magnetic flux as a fixed background condition. However, creating the necessary interaction would have required capabilities that their quantum hardware did not possess.
Encoding the flux directly into the qubits provided a practical alternative. More importantly, it allowed the magnetic flux to become part of the evolving quantum system rather than remaining an unchanging external influence.
"For us, the exciting step was to encode the magnetic flux in a gauge field that was itself dynamical," says Dr. Saner. "Rather than having matter evolve in a fixed background, the matter and gauge field become part of the same quantum dynamics."
What began as a technical workaround ultimately enabled the researchers to explore a more interesting version of the phenomenon, one in which matter and the field could participate together in the quantum dynamics.
A Quantum Effect That Stops Particle Motion
With their simulated loop in place, the scientists examined how a matter particle moved between locations through a process known as quantum tunneling.
Quantum tunneling allows particles to move between states in ways that would not be possible under ordinary classical rules.
When the researchers ran their simulation without magnetic flux, the particle could tunnel freely around the loop.
Introducing the simulated flux produced a strikingly different result.
The particle had two possible paths around the loop, but the magnetic flux changed their relative quantum phases. As a result, the two paths interfered destructively, meaning their quantum contributions canceled each other out.
This interference completely suppressed the tunneling, leaving the simulated particle frozen in its original state.
The outcome demonstrated the Aharonov-Bohm effect within a lattice gauge theory containing a dynamical field. Rather than simply reproducing the familiar behavior of a particle moving around a fixed magnetic influence, the experiment showed how the phenomenon can emerge when matter and the field are both represented by interacting quantum components.
A New Tool for Exploring Fundamental Physics
The Oxford findings were published alongside a related study by researchers at the University of Maryland, led by Professor Norbert Linke.
The Maryland team also used a hybrid quantum system, but their experiment focused on simulating the Yukawa potential, a mathematical description of an interaction relevant to nuclear and particle physics.
Although the two research groups developed their methods independently, they later coordinated the submission of their studies to Nature Physics.
Together, the experiments demonstrate how hybrid quantum computers could become valuable tools for investigating fundamental interactions that are difficult to reproduce using classical simulations.
By combining different types of quantum components, researchers can build systems in which matter and fields are represented in ways that more closely reflect the physics they want to study.
The Oxford experiment provides an example of that potential. A phenomenon first predicted in 1959 and later observed with electrons has now been recreated in a quantum simulator where the field itself participates in the dynamics, offering scientists another way to explore the unusual rules governing the quantum world.

articles.title: Exclusive: Kantata's Expertise Insights answers services firms' business questions in plain English - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Kantata’s Expertise Insights answers services firms’ business questions in plain English
Professional services automation software company Kantata Inc. today added generative business intelligence to its Expertise Engine platform with the launch of Expertise Insights.
Users ask about the business in plain English, as in where margin pressure is showing up, and the software answers with an interactive chart, a calculation or an executive summary.
Kantata’s pitch rests on how long it takes services firms to get answers out of their own data. The company says a request often has to go through a business intelligence analyst or a services engagement, and the wait can run to a week.
Sarah Edwards, Kantata’s chief product and strategy officer, said the value of an insight in professional services “depends on how quickly you can act on it.” Reports often show up after the moment has passed, she said.
Expertise Insights runs on Amazon Web Services Inc.’s Amazon Quick. On top of it Kantata has added a semantic layer that translates database field names into the vocabulary staff at a particular firm use every day. Firm-specific terms are covered, down to distinctions such as “chargeable utilization” versus “billable utilization.”
Kantata ships the product with four ready-made dashboards. Finance teams get margin, revenue per head and cost leakage trends in one of them, and the rest are given over to delivery, time and resourcing. On the delivery dashboard, project health is broken out by schedule, scope, budget and client health.
Users who need something the stock dashboards don’t show can turn to Ask Insights for new analysis on demand. Kantata says a complete board deck can be assembled in minutes. Saved work goes into Bookmarks and Pinboards, so a filtered view or a one-off analysis can be kept without spawning another copy of a master dashboard. Kantata is pitching that as a cure for dashboard sprawl.
The software can also link capacity, margin, delivery risk and financial performance. Piecing those relationships together might otherwise take several reports, or a seasoned operator who knows where to look.
Vikas Nehru, Kantata’s chief technology officer, said artificial intelligence in professional services should make a firm’s “collective expertise available at the moment a decision needs to be made.” That requires clean data and context, he said, plus AI that understands how a business works.
Life sciences consultancy Lumanity Inc. is among the customers already running the product. Andy Newbill, its senior manager of professional services automation, recently put together a complex report using calculated fields in an hour, and by his estimate the job would have taken hours before. Most striking to him was the chance to describe what he needs “in natural language and have the system help me build it.”
Kantata announced Expertise Insights at the Technology & Services World conference in Las Vegas, and it is available now. The company’s previous launch, Agent Studio, came a month ago and lets firms build custom AI agents by describing them in plain language.

articles.title: NAS vs external hard drive: What are the differences?
articles.text:
NAS vs external hard drive: What are the differences?
We compare storage capacity, speed, pricing, and backup features
Network-attached storage (NAS) and external hard drives are effective ways to store and access large files on the go.
Yet, many sometimes need help when choosing between NAS systems and external hard drives. You’ve arrived at the right place if you fall into this category. We've tested the best NAS drives, NAS devices, and external hard drives.
So, I’ve written this guide explaining what you should know about NAS systems and external hard drives before deciding.
NAS vs. External Hard Drive: Design
Network-attached storage (NAS) utilizes hardware, software, and data transfer protocols to let users share files over a network. It uses a NAS box that houses storage disks, processors, and a random access memory (RAM) unit. This box has specialized software to manage file storage and user access.
NAS boxes can connect to a network and let users share files seamlessly. Suppose you work in a company with 50 staff. All 50 staff can connect to a single NAS box to access organizational files. Think of the NAS system as an online tree where everyone can pluck information. It provides an easy way to share massive files between employees.
In contrast, external hard drives are standalone devices that transfer files over USB ports rather than a network. Every file is stored locally, and the hard drive must be plugged into the PC that wants to retrieve information from it.
NAS systems offer substantially more storage space than external hard drives. You can always expand the storage capacity of your NAS system by adding more drives, unlike external hard drives with fixed storage capacities.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
External hard drives are portable and easy to move. Employees can quickly pass them around to retrieve relevant files, but this process gets cumbersome for large workforces. Picture a 100+ workforce sharing a single external hard drive; that’s inefficient and weakens productivity.
In contrast, you can keep a NAS box stationary, and employees can connect to this box from their respective PCs. Everyone can access files seamlessly without looking for hard drives to plug into their PC. A NAS system is the most convenient option for businesses that can afford it.
NAS vs. External Hard Drive: Price
NAS systems are more expensive than external hard drives, expectedly, because they use more sophisticated components. A NAS system includes a storage box, networking components, and a processor to run the software.
In contrast, an external hard drive’s main component is a simple magnetic disk (platter) that stores data. NAS systems are more expensive to produce.
A 4 TB external hard drive costs an average of $90. Meanwhile, a 4 TB NAS system costs upwards of $200. It gets costlier when more drives are added to the existing setup. When weighing both, expect to spend more on a NAS system, but the trade-off is bigger storage capacity and the convenience of accessing files.
NAS vs. External Hard Drive: Speed
NAS systems offer excellent speed, although they depend on bandwidth. Consumer-level NAS devices have average data transfer speeds of 3 to 20 MB per second (Mbps), but high-level NAS devices can reach 100 to 200 Mbps. Because they depend on network bandwidth, data transfer speeds can be slow when many people connect to the same NAS box.
External hard drives transfer data via USB ports. Data transfer speeds depend on the USB version of your external hard drive. USB 1 offers up to 12 Mbps, USB 2 offers up to 480 Mbps, USB 3 reaches up to 5 Gbps, and USB 4 has a maximum speed of 40 Gbps.
Some NAS systems offer gigabit speeds (over Ethernet cables) comparable to USB. On average, USB systems have faster data transfer speeds. However, I think this shouldn’t matter much because most users don’t transfer files at gigabit speeds. Both NAS and hard drives are sufficient for everyday use.
NAS vs. External Hard Drive: Backup and Redundancy
Many NAS systems have built-in data backup features. For instance, you can back up a Synology DS923+ NAS to Google Drive. You can schedule automatic backups, wherein all data stored on the Synology NAS box will be uploaded to Google Drive daily, weekly, or monthly. Automated backups keep your data safe even if the NAS device fails.
In contrast, external hard drives don’t have built-in backup software. To back up files, you need to manually connect the drive to a PC, which is cumbersome. People often forget to do manual backups, but automated NAS backups solve this issue. Your data is safer on a NAS than on a hard drive.
NAS vs. External Hard Drive: Verdict
NAS systems offer much larger storage and are expandable. They offer a more convenient way to access data, making it the best choice for enterprises. NAS systems cost more than external hard drives, but the higher cost is worth the convenience for business users.
External hard drives are ideal for casual users who frequently transfer files between PCs. They handle large file transfers without issues, although the process isn’t as smooth as using a NAS system. I think the hassle and expense of setting up a NAS system aren’t worth it for casual users.

articles.title: Microsoft profite de vos clics involontaires sur le bureau pour ouvrir Bing, et vous ne pouvez même plus l'en empêcher
articles.text:
Bing Wallpaper continue de transformer les clics malencontreux sur le bureau en visites sur Bing. Près d'un an après l'apparition de cette fonction, le réglage qui permettait de la désactiver semble avoir définitivement disparu.
Microsoft ne manque décidément pas d'imagination lorsqu'il s'agit de promouvoir son moteur de recherche. Pour rappel, il y a un peu moins d’un an, Bing Wallpaper, son application de renouvellement automatique des fonds d'écran, s'était découvert une nouvelle utilité : ouvrir Bing lorsqu'on cliquait sur une zone vide du bureau. À l'époque, un réglage permettait encore de désactiver cette fonction, bien que plusieurs utilisateurs et utilisatrices aient rapidement signalé son absence. On pensait alors à un bug. Près d'un an plus tard, pourtant, les redirections sont toujours actives et l'interrupteur a bel et bien disparu des paramètres de l'application.
Des clics détournés et plus aucun moyen de désactiver la fonction
L'alerte a une nouvelle fois été donnée par Windows Latest, qui, lors de ses derniers tests, a constaté qu'un clic gauche sur une zone vide du bureau déclenchait l'ouverture de Bing dans le navigateur par défaut, y compris lorsqu'il s'agissait de Chrome. La recherche porte sur la photographie affichée en arrière-plan et ne se lance qu'une fois toutes les 24 heures environ, ce qui peut donner l'impression d'un comportement aléatoire.
Plus gênant encore, nous avons également pu constater que la dernière version de Bing Wallpaper semble faire fi de l'option permettant de désactiver ces redirections, désormais introuvable dans les paramètres de l'application. Ce qui pouvait encore passer pour un bug il y a quelques mois prend donc une tournure plus discutable, à plus forte raison quand Bing Wallpaper dispose déjà d'un raccourci dédié pour consulter les informations relatives à la photographie du jour.
Bref, miser sur les clics involontaires pour générer du trafic vers Bing est déjà contestable, mais si Microsoft a effectivement supprimé ce réglage de manière délibérée, la manœuvre est franchement abusive. Heureusement qu’il était question de réduire les publicités sur Windows 11.
À toutes fins utiles, on rappellera que vous pouvez profiter de fonds d'écran renouvelés quotidiennement sans passer par Bing Wallpaper, et donc sans subir ces redirections, en activant Windows à la une depuis les Paramètres > Personnalisation > Arrière-plan.

articles.title: Ukraine rescues wounded soldier using drone in daring 'world's first' UAV evacuation of a human — heavy-lift hexacopter carried injured 176-pound soldier 11 miles back to safety from minefield
articles.text:
Ukraine rescues wounded soldier using drone in daring 'world's first' UAV evacuation of a human — heavy-lift hexacopter carried injured 176-pound soldier 11 miles back to safety from minefield
In heavily mined terrain and surrounded by Russian kamikaze drones, 'Kostya' was hoisted by a Gurzuf Defence heavy UAV and guarded to safety by a fleet of smaller drones.
The Ukrainian military is claiming a world’s first after using an unmanned drone to rescue an injured soldier on the eastern Kharkiv front. Ukraine’s United24 news shared a video of the historic first. It also explained that the wounded infantryman was stuck in a heavily mined area, guarded by Russian kamikaze drones.
The above video starts with the Ukrainian drone locating the soldier, callsign ‘Kostya,’ in enemy territory. Various media reports suggest he was 11 miles (18km) behind enemy lines, at the mercy of Russian kamikaze drones, and perilously located in a minefield. Traditional land-based rescue was therefore not possible, but Kostya bravely agreed to be part of the first-ever human drone-lift rescue plan.
After being located, the injured infantryman clipped himself into a harness. He said, “That’s it, we can take off,” when he was fully buckled into the rudimentary-looking harness. UAV operator, callsign ‘Black’ from the 20th Mechanized Battalion, 30th Infantry Brigade, then appeared in the video and explained: “We were constantly in touch with him."
Ukrainian drone rescue key facts:
- Drone used: Gurzuf Defense hexacopter
- Drone capable of carrying 130kg (~287 pounds)
- Drone’s known range: it has previously transported 90kg (~198 pounds) loads up to 25km (16 miles)
- Infantryman weight: 80kg (~176 pounds)
- Rescue distance: 8km (11 miles)
- Hazards: enemy kamikaze drones, mines, gravity, many more
Being in constant touch with the operations HQ would have been reassuring. However, the surrounding presence of a fleet of Ukrainian support drones, both kamikaze devices and UAVs with anti-drone nets, was probably most comforting.
Eventually dropping back into safe(r) territory, after what must have been an arduous, nerve-wracking journey, control said, “Congratulations, you’re on the ground,” to Kostya, as he touched down in a field. Then the control room erupted into applause. They got their man back safely, and he is now being treated and is in recovery.
UAV operator ‘Black’ was delighted with the concerted efforts that brought back this wounded soldier. “A lot of people were involved, and everything worked out for us,” he said. Importantly, this may be the start of a whole new system of personnel evacuations for wounded and/or stranded soldiers using drone technology, indicated brigade leader ‘Napalm’ toward the end of the video.

articles.title: Pourquoi la PS6 serait moins chère que la future Xbox — Frandroid
articles.text:
Kepler_L2 est un leaker connu pour ses fuites sur les puces AMD. Le fondeur devrait équiper à la fois la PS6 et la prochaine Xbox. Dans un message publié sur X ce mardi 20 octobre, il affirme que les composants de la PS6 coûteraient environ 200 dollars de moins que ceux de Magnus. Magnus est le nom de code de la puce de la future console de Microsoft. Sony aurait donc plus de marge pour vendre moins cher, mais la PS6 ne deviendrait pas bon marché pour autant.
Le même jour, le magazine américain Fortune a publié un long portrait d’Asha Sharma, CEO de Xbox depuis février. On y apprend que Microsoft estime en interne le prix de sa prochaine console de salon, prévue pour les fêtes 2028, entre 1 200 et 1 800 dollars. Cette fourchette vaut tant que Microsoft ne décide pas de vendre la machine à perte.
Sony a lui aussi des raisons de s’inquiéter. La mémoire vive et le stockage de la PS6 coûteraient déjà plus de 680 dollars (environ 605 euros) par console, toujours selon Kepler. De quoi faire craindre une PS6 à plus de 1 000 euros.
Microsoft a moins de marge pour vendre à perte
Il y a un an, Kepler pariait sur une PS6 à 600 dollars et une Xbox à 1 200 dollars. Il avançait trois raisons : une puce Xbox 42 % plus grande, 20 % de mémoire en plus et un refroidissement plus coûteux. Depuis, les centres de données de l’IA ont fait flamber le prix de la mémoire, et la facture des deux machines a grimpé.
Pourtant, l’écart en magasin pourrait dépasser les 200 dollars d’écart sur les composants. Sony peut vendre sa console à prix serré et se rattraper sur les commissions du PlayStation Store. Par contre, la prochaine Xbox fera aussi tourner les jeux PC et donc des boutiques concurrentes comme Steam. D’après Kepler, Microsoft touchera donc moins de commissions pour compenser une console vendue à perte.
Microsoft n’a pas commenté les chiffres de Fortune. Côté Sony, Hiroki Totoki, CEO du groupe, a récemment indiqué que la date de lancement de la PS6 n’était pas encore fixée.

articles.title: OVHcloud CLI releases backdoored on GitHub to steal developer secrets
articles.text:
French cloud and hosting provider OVHcloud is warning users that attackers compromised its open-source command-line interface (CLI) tool to distribute information-stealing malware.
The attacker hijacked a developer’s GitHub account to gain access to the OVHcloud CLI repository and modify versions 0.11.0 through 0.15.0 of the tool.
OVHcloud offers the CLI tool as an alternative for system administrators and developers to manage cloud and hosting services directly from a terminal, including for automating tasks.
OVHcloud CEO Octave Klaba disclosed that the company’s CLI repository on GitHub had been compromised, urging users who downloaded the latest version yesterday to update or remove the tool.
Klaba said that the compromised release appeared at 14:47 on October 19 and was detected and blocked at 16:21 after a customer reported it.
"The compromised versions are v0.11.0 v0.12.0 v0.13.0 v0.14.0 v0.15.0," the CEO said, adding that older version 0.10.0 and the latest release 0.16.0 were clean.
Despite the poor quality of the malware, its purpose was to "retrieve secrets from the disk," Klaba explained.
In a later update, Klaba shared that GitHub’s release immutability setting was disabled, allowing a sufficiently privileged account to modify existing releases without passing CI/CD checks.
"The entire set of CI/CD pipelines with unit tests, functional tests, CVE detection, etc., were not impacted."
OVHcloud has enabled GitHub’s release immutability feature and considers the incident resolved.
However, Klaba urges users who downloaded a compromised CLI package to perform a system cleanup and revoke all secrets.
"The quality of the binary is poor but it can go all the way. If you are affected, please change all the secrets on your disk."
GlassWorm connection
According to OpenSourceMalware, a community-driven threat intelligence platform, the attack was likely part of a new GlassWorm operation, known for campaigns since late 2025 that impacted the VSCode, OpenVSX, GitHub, and npm software development ecosystems.
The researchers confirmed that the attacker did not tamper with the CI/CD pipelines and uploaded malware-infected packages built locally.
The researchers note that the GitHub account used in the attack had been compromised for more than half a year.
"Its public repositories show a scripted history rewrite on 5 March 2026 and a hidden preinstall.js loader that decodes to a second stage using a Solana memo dead drop," OpenSourceMalware researchers found.
Although the associated wallet is a known GlassWorm indicator, the researchers did not analyze the malicious payload delivered through a trojanized version of the OVHcloud CLI.
According to OpenSourceMalware's report, affected platforms are macOS (Intel and ARM), Linux (x86_64 and ARM64), and Windows x86-64. Source builds and Docker images remained unaffected.
Anyone who ran an affected binary should treat all secrets on the machine as compromised.

articles.title: Spectrum costs squeeze African telecom investment and growth
articles.text:
Africa’s mobile networks have expanded significantly over the past decade, bringing coverage to more people. But wider coverage has not translated into widespread internet use or network quality on par with other regions.
A new report by the GSMA, Spectrum Policy in Africa: Enabling Investment and Empowering Consumers Through Effective Spectrum Pricing, identifies the high cost of accessing radio spectrum—the invisible radio frequencies that carry mobile calls and internet data—as a central bottleneck. African mobile operators pay significantly more for relatively less spectrum, leaving them with limited capacity to expand or improve service quality.
According to GSMA Intelligence, spectrum costs consume 0.82% of mobile operators’ revenue per 100 MHz in Africa, compared with 0.66% in the rest of the world. Meanwhile, African operators hold an average of about 570 MHz of spectrum below 7 GHz, 24% less than the global peer average of approximately 750 MHz.
The imbalance extends beyond price and availability to licence duration. Only nine African countries routinely grant spectrum licences lasting 20 years or more, while licences of 20 years or indefinite duration are standard across Europe, North America and developed Asian markets.
Lowering spectrum fees could free up vital capital for network expansion, but lower fees alone do not guarantee better connectivity. The crucial test for African regulators is whether more affordable access can be tied to measurable improvements in network quality and internet adoption, particularly in underserved communities where initial financial returns remain low.

articles.title: Oubliez PowerPoint : voici ChatGPT Slides
articles.text:
Le mois dernier, OpenAI officialisait l’arrivée de ChatGPT Space avec son lot d’outils bureautiques intégrant des pages et des feuilles de calcul, tout en précisant que les présentations arriveraient plus tard. C’est désormais chose faite avec le lancement de ChatGPT Slides. L’entreprise détaille les nouvelles possibilités offertes à ses abonnés pour générer rapidement des supports visuels directement à partir de documents existants ou de modèles prédéfinis. PowerPoint et Google Slides n’ont qu’à bien se tenir.
Collaboration en direct et options d’exportation
Une fois le diaporama généré par l’intelligence artificielle, il est possible de le partager avec des collaborateurs pour travailler simultanément sur le projet. Les membres invités peuvent donc apporter des modifications et laisser des commentaires en direct. De son côté, ChatGPT peut même appliquer automatiquement des changements en fonction des retours des membres de l’équipe.
Lorsque le résultat final vous convient, l’outil permet d’ouvrir directement le fichier dans des logiciels tiers comme PowerPoint ou Google Slides. Vous pourrez évidemment télécharger le document au format PDF ou l’exporter directement sous forme de fichier PowerPoint pour l’utiliser hors ligne.
Qui peut profiter de ChatGPT Slides ?
ChatGPT Slides est disponible dès maintenant pour les personnes abonnées aux formules Pro, Business et Enterprise d’OpenAI. Pour en profiter, il suffit de demander directement à l’IA de créer des diapositives à partir d’un fichier texte ou d’une conversation en cours.
À lire : Avec Atlas enterré, ChatGPT s’installe dans vos onglets Google Chrome
En revanche, les utilisateurs payants de la formule Plus ne peuvent malheureusement pas en profiter. On peut l’expliquer par le fait que ChatGPT Slides est intégré à l’écosystème ChatGPT Space, lequel est déjà réservé aux abonnements supérieurs. Une distinction qui n’est pas sans rappeler le retrait par Google de ses meilleurs modèles sur son abonnement payant Google AI Plus.

articles.title: Alibaba ya ha metido RISC-V en más de 6.000 millones de chips
articles.text:
Alibaba es una de las principales bazas de China en su pulso con EEUU en el terreno de la inteligencia artificial (IA). Es muy difícil cuantificar de una forma objetiva cuáles son las corporaciones que sostienen la estrategia del Gobierno liderado por Xi Jinping si pretendemos ponderar el peso de unas frente a otras. Aun así, es razonable atribuir a Alibaba una relevancia equiparable a la de Huawei, Cambricon Technologies o Baidu, entre otras empresas.
T-Head, la filial de semiconductores de Alibaba, ha presentado o lanzado durante 2026 varios de los chips más interesantes de la industria de la IA. Con su acelerador Zhenwu M890 presentado en mayo espera poder competir de tú a tú en términos de rendimiento con algunas de las GPU más avanzadas de Nvidia. No obstante, uno de los circuitos integrados más prometedores de T-Head es la CPU de alto rendimiento XuanTie C950.
Este chip con arquitectura RISC-V incorpora motores de cálculo vectorial y matricial que permiten ejecutar determinadas operaciones de IA directamente en la CPU. No suena nada mal. Además, trabaja a una frecuencia de reloj máxima de 3,2 GHz, implementa una microarquitectura con decodificación de ocho instrucciones y una ventana de ejecución superescalar de más de 1.000 instrucciones, y, según Alibaba, puede ejecutar modelos como Qwen3-235B-A22B o DeepSeek V3-671B.
UN VISTAZO A...
RISC-V lo es (casi) todo para China
La arquitectura RISC-V es muy importante para Alibaba. De hecho, la Academia DAMO, su brazo de investigación, ha anunciado que los procesadores basados en su arquitectura XuanTie ya han superado los 6.000 millones de unidades enviadas. Es una cifra impresionante incluso en el contexto de un mercado tan grande como el chino. No obstante, es importante que no pasemos por alto que la microarquitectura XuanTie es una implementación de RISC-V.
Tencent, Alibaba y la Academia de Ciencias de China son algunas de las organizaciones que están trabajando en el desarrollo de procesadores con arquitectura RISC-V
Y RISC-V es fundamental en el plan de China que persigue alcanzar la independencia tecnológica. Para el país liderado por Xi Jinping representa la oportunidad de sostener su desarrollo a pesar de las sanciones de la alianza liderada por EEUU. De hecho, el Gobierno chino ha creado un consorcio de empresas e institutos de investigación que persigue desarrollar chips con esta arquitectura.
Tencent, Alibaba y la Academia de Ciencias de China son algunas de las organizaciones que están trabajando en el desarrollo de procesadores con arquitectura RISC-V, y la Administración de EEUU está muy preocupada. Lo está debido a que esta tecnología puede utilizarse para poner a punto superordenadores extraordinariamente capaces. De hecho, Europa ya tiene listo EPAC (European Processor ACcelerator), su primer chip RISC-V, y precisamente ha sido diseñado para residir en el interior de los próximos superordenadores europeos.
En este escenario resulta sorprendente que una de las empresas que está trabajando codo con codo con las compañías y los centros de investigación chinos sea estadounidense. MIPS, una organización propiedad de GlobalFoundries que se dedica al diseño de procesadores RISC-V, está trabajando estrechamente con empresas chinas en la evolución y la estandarización de esta arquitectura. Sea como sea, el avance de RISC-V en China demuestra que la carrera por la soberanía tecnológica no consiste únicamente en fabricar chips más potentes, sino también en controlar las arquitecturas sobre las que se construyen.
